E) is incorrect because foot pedals are prone to accidental activation and create additional safety risks rather than reducing fire hazards.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old healthy person with gender dysphoria requests top surgery as part of their female-to-male gender transition. According to the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH) Standards of Care, what prerequisite must be fulfilled before this individual can receive approval for the surgery?
A) Individual must have reached 21 years of age
B) Individual must undergo 12 months of hormone therapy
C) Individual must possess health insurance coverage
D) Individual must spend 12 months living in male gender role
E) Individual must secure one referral letter from a qualified mental health provider
questions.answer:
E)

The correct answer is E because WPATH Standards of Care mandate one letter of recommendation from a qualified mental health provider for female-to-male top surgery. This documentation helps verify ongoing gender dysphoria and ensures appropriate assessment prior to surgical treatment. A is incorrect because the age criterion is legal majority in the respective country, not necessarily 21 years. B is incorrect because hormonal treatment is not a mandatory prerequisite for FTM top surgery under WPATH guidelines. C is incorrect because health insurance coverage is not included in WPATH Standards of Care requirements. D is incorrect because the 12-month real-life experience in male role is mandated for genital reconstruction surgery, not for chest surgery.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old man presents for management of a depressed, retracted scar following tracheostomy. Which treatment approach would best improve the aesthetic appearance of this scar?
A) Fat grafting combined with laser therapy
B) Tracheal cartilage reconstruction with adhesion release
C) Scar excision with acellular dermal matrix placement
D) Scar removal with strap muscle reapproximation
E) Basic scar revision procedure
questions.answer:
D)

The correct answer is D because contracted, depressed post-tracheostomy scars require reapproximation of the platysma muscle and proper alignment of the sternothyroid and sternohyoid muscles to eliminate the retraction and depression. This technique addresses the fundamental anatomical disruption causing the deformity. A is incorrect because fat injection alone cannot sufficiently correct the retraction element or completely resolve the depression. B is incorrect because reconstruction of tracheal rings is unnecessary for standard tracheostomy scar revision procedures. C is incorrect because although dermal matrices can provide support when tissue is deficient, they fail to address the core problem of separated muscles. E is incorrect because basic scar revision without correcting the underlying muscle disruption will not eliminate the retraction and depression.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old female patient is having breast reconstruction using abdominal tissue. During the operation, a perforator flap becomes impractical because of multiple small non-dominant perforators. The surgical approach is modified to a staged pedicled transverse rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap. Which blood vessel should be divided during this first phase to enhance tissue survival for the following operation?
A) Deep inferior epigastric
B) Hypogastric
C) Internal mammary
D) Superficial inferior epigastric
E) Superior epigastric
questions.answer:
A)
The correct choice is A because dividing the deep inferior epigastric vessels establishes a surgical delay that compels the tissue to depend on the superior epigastric circulation, which will serve as the vascular supply for the future pedicled TRAM flap. This delay technique improves tissue survival by promoting the development of collateral blood flow. B is wrong because the hypogastric vessels do not have a direct influence on pedicled TRAM tissue perfusion. C is wrong because dividing the internal mammary vessels could jeopardize the superior epigastric circulation that the flap will require. D is wrong because although cutting the superficial inferior epigastric vessels may provide some benefit, it is not as essential as deep inferior epigastric vessel ligation. E is wrong because dividing the superior epigastric circulation would destroy the vascular supply that the pedicled TRAM flap requires for survival.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old man comes to the clinic with ocular pain and double vision occurring two weeks after sustaining facial injuries from being hit. An orbital bone fracture is suspected. What represents the most common reason for requiring surgical repair in orbital floor fractures?
A) Accompanying naso-orbito-ethmoid fracture
B) Simultaneous opposite-side zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture
C) Orbital soft tissue prolapse resulting in diplopia
D) Single medial wall fracture without clinical signs
E) Undisplaced fracture
questions.answer:
C)
The correct answer is C because prolapse of orbital structures leading to diplopia indicates extraocular muscle impingement, which constitutes one of the three primary reasons for surgical correction of orbital fractures. This condition can result in lasting impairment if surgical treatment is not performed. A is wrong because accompanying NOE fractures are related trauma but do not constitute primary reasons for orbital floor surgical repair. B is wrong because opposite-side ZMC fractures are distinct injuries that do not dictate the necessity for orbital floor surgery. D is wrong because single medial wall fractures lacking symptoms usually do not warrant surgical treatment. E is wrong because undisplaced fractures typically do not fulfill requirements for surgical correction unless additional indications exist.

questions.question:
A cyclist sustained an 8-cm linear laceration on their forearm. When contrasting tissue adhesive (cyanoacrylate) closure with conventional suture repair, which adverse outcome is most likely to occur?
A) Wound dehiscence
B) Skin hyperpigmentation
C) Secondary infection
D) Hypertrophic scarring
E) Pain during treatment
questions.answer:
A)

The correct answer is A because research shows increased wound dehiscence rates with tissue adhesive closures, especially in longer wounds, with failure rates of 15-24% reported in clinical studies. The adhesive may lack sufficient tensile strength for larger wounds under mechanical stress. B is incorrect because skin discoloration is not a recognized increased complication with adhesive closures versus sutures. C is incorrect because infection rates do not differ significantly between adhesive and suture closures. D is incorrect because excessive scar tissue formation is not more frequent with adhesive closures compared to conventional suturing. E is incorrect because tissue adhesives generally produce less discomfort during application than needle-based suturing techniques.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of bite alignment issues. Clinical examination shows an open bite anteriorly, with maxillary incisors not showing when the lips are in repose. Radiographic analysis reveals a nasion (N) to anterior nasal spine (ANS) distance of 45 mm (standard range 52-57 mm), an ANS to menton (Me) distance of 63 mm (standard range 63-68 mm), and an N-ANS:ANS-Me proportion of 1:1.4 (standard 1:1.2). Other cephalometric values are within normal limits. Which surgical approach would be most appropriate for correcting this patient's skeletal abnormality?
A) Le Fort I maxillary osteotomy with downward repositioning
B) Le Fort II osteotomy with forward maxillary movement
C) Naso-orbito-maxillary osteotomy
D) Perinasal osteotomy
E) Sagittal split osteotomy with posterior mandibular positioning
questions.answer:
A)
Le Fort I osteotomy with downward repositioning is the appropriate treatment for this case of isolated maxillary vertical hypoplasia. This surgical technique effectively enhances maxillary vertical dimension by moving the maxilla inferiorly, which eliminates the anterior open bite and reestablishes normal facial balance, providing 3-4 mm of maxillary incisor display at rest. B) is incorrect because Le Fort II osteotomy is indicated for nasomaxillary hypoplasia with Class III skeletal pattern, not for isolated vertical underdevelopment. C) is incorrect because naso-orbito-maxillary osteotomy treats combined anteroposterior and vertical maxillary deficiencies with nasal abnormalities, making it overly extensive for this purely vertical issue. D) is incorrect because perinasal osteotomy only modifies nasal prominence and dimension without correcting maxillary vertical height or occlusal relationships. E) is incorrect because sagittal split osteotomy alters mandibular position rather than maxillary position, and would not correct the underlying maxillary vertical deficiency.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old man presents following a sharp, self-inflicted complete transection of his penis at the mid-shaft. After appropriate counseling, he elects to undergo penile replantation surgery. Which vascular anastomosis is most critical for successful penile reattachment and preservation of foreskin viability?
A) Cavernosal
B) Dorsal
C) External pudendal
D) Internal pudendal
E) Urethral
questions.answer:
B)
The dorsal artery anastomosis is most critical for successful penile reattachment and foreskin viability. This vessel supplies the glans and foreskin through its terminal branches and can perfuse the entire penile shaft through circumflex arterial connections. A) is incorrect because cavernosal artery anastomosis alone is insufficient for penile replantation and results in substantial skin necrosis. C) is incorrect because the external pudendal artery supplies the penile base and is not accessible at a mid-shaft amputation site. D) is incorrect because the internal pudendal artery also supplies the penile base and cannot be accessed at the mid-shaft level. E) is incorrect because the urethral artery does not contribute to penile skin blood supply.

questions.question:
Incomplete disappearance of the mammary ridge during embryonic development is most likely to result in which of the following abnormalities?
A) Absence of breast tissue
B) Male breast enlargement
C) Retracted nipple
D) Chest wall deformity syndrome
E) Supernumerary breast tissue
questions.answer:
E)

Supernumerary breast tissue (polymastia) occurs when the mammary ridge fails to completely regress during embryonic development. Normally, the mammary ridge undergoes apoptosis except at the thoracic sites, but incomplete regression can lead to accessory breast tissue or nipples forming along the embryonic milk line. A) is incorrect because absence of breast tissue occurs from either failed mammary ridge development or total ridge regression, not partial regression. B) is incorrect because male breast enlargement typically results from hormonal imbalances, not embryonic ridge developmental anomalies. C) is incorrect because retracted nipples arise from insufficient mesenchymal growth beneath the skin surface. D) is incorrect because chest wall deformity syndrome involves multiple thoracic and upper limb malformations believed to stem from vascular compromise, not mammary ridge development problems.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman with recurrent rectal cancer is scheduled for preoperative evaluation prior to pelvic exenteration, which will include total vaginectomy and reconstruction utilizing a vertical rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap. Which long-term complication is most likely to occur in this patient?
A) Ventral hernia
B) Pelvic infection
C) Rectovaginal communication
D) Intestinal obstruction
E) Narrowing of the vaginal canal
questions.answer:
E)
Narrowing of the vaginal canal represents the most common long-term complication after complete vaginal reconstruction, developing in 18-22% of patients. This complication necessitates continuous dilation using dilators and must be extensively discussed with patients before surgery. A) is incorrect because ventral hernia occurs less frequently as a long-term complication than vaginal narrowing. B) is incorrect because pelvic infection typically presents as an early postoperative complication rather than a delayed consequence. C) is incorrect because rectovaginal communication develops less commonly than stenosis as a chronic complication. D) is incorrect because intestinal obstruction also occurs less frequently than stenosis after vaginal reconstruction procedures.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old woman undergoes preoperative mammography prior to breast surgery. Her history includes symptomatic breast hypertrophy. Suspicious microcalcifications are identified, prompting core needle biopsy. Which biopsy result necessitates surgical excision prior to reduction mammoplasty?
A) Atypical lobular hyperplasia
B) Fibroadenoma
C) Papilloma without atypia
D) Pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia
E) Radial scar
questions.answer:
A)
Atypical lobular hyperplasia (ALH) necessitates excisional biopsy per NCCN recommendations since high-risk lesions such as ALH, atypical ductal hyperplasia, atypical papillomas, and DCIS may advance to malignancy in 10-39% of instances when first identified on core biopsy. B) is wrong because fibroadenoma represents a benign entity that does not mandate excision prior to reduction mammoplasty. C) is wrong because non-atypical papillomas are benign findings that do not require excisional biopsy. D) is wrong because pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia is benign and has not demonstrated increased breast malignancy risk. E) is wrong because a completely removed and definitively diagnosed radial scar does not warrant further excisional biopsy.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old female patient is having bilateral breast reduction surgery using the inferior pedicle method. During the deepithelialization process of the pedicle, the dermal layer is maintained to safeguard which of the following anatomical components?
A) Perforating vessels from the internal mammary artery
B) Perforating vessels from the lateral thoracic artery
C) Oil-producing glands
D) Subdermal vascular network
E) Superficial portion of the breast's superficial fascia
questions.answer:
D)
The subdermal vascular network requires protection during deepithelialization, which is why the dermis is preserved. The breast's blood supply originates from multiple sources including internal mammary perforators, intercostal perforators, and axillary artery branches. These vessels form concentrated vascular networks at the breast periphery (cutaneoglandular plexus), with major vessels located just beneath the skin surface, above the glandular tissue. This anatomical arrangement necessitates maintaining dermal thickness during flap elevation and preserving the dermis during deepithelialization to prevent damage to the subdermal plexus. A is incorrect because internal mammary perforators supply deeper breast tissue, not the subdermal layer that requires dermal preservation. B is incorrect because lateral thoracic perforators also supply deeper parenchymal tissue rather than the subdermal network. C is incorrect because sebaceous glands are not the primary concern requiring dermal preservation during this procedure. E is incorrect because the superficial fascia layer does not provide the critical vascularity that necessitates dermal preservation.

questions.question:
A patient presents with nasal breathing difficulty that is more severe on the right side. Clinical examination reveals the inferior turbinate demonstrates marked forward projection and tissue swelling with underlying bone enlargement. The patient also has a post-injury septal deflection and an internal nasal valve angle of 10 degrees. When planning surgical intervention to enhance nasal breathing, which of the following findings is the most critical factor in deciding whether submucous turbinate reduction is necessary?
A) Forward projection of the turbinate
B) Bone enlargement
C) Reduced internal nasal valve angle
D) Deflected septum
E) Tissue swelling
questions.answer:
B)
Bone enlargement is the most critical factor determining the need for submucous turbinate reduction because this procedure specifically addresses the underlying bony component that cannot be corrected by other means. Forward projection alone can often be managed without submucous resection. Tissue swelling without bone involvement can typically be treated with outfracture techniques. A deflected septum is corrected through septoplasty procedures. A reduced internal nasal valve angle can be addressed with techniques such as spreader graft placement.

questions.question:
A 73-year-old man is evaluated for a non-healing wound on the medial aspect of the calf. The wound has been present for 8 months, and he has undergone several months of serial debridements and moist wound care without improvement. A photograph is shown. Ten years ago, he was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the medial calf skin, and the condition was managed solely with radiation therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Hyperbaric oxygen therapy
B) Negative pressure wound therapy
C) Wound biopsy and culture
D) Wound debridement and skin graft
E) Continued observation and wound care
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Based on the clinical scenario described, wound biopsy and culture is the most appropriate management option. Despite wound debridement and moist wound care, the wound has not improved and is in the region of a previous malignancy. Wound biopsy would allow the diagnosis of recurrent malignancy and aid in the determination of further surgical intervention. Wound culture would allow the diagnosis of soft-tissue infection contributing to the wound‚Äos persistence.


Although wound debridement would be beneficial in this case, application of a skin graft in the face of possible recurrent malignancy and probable marked radiation injury would be associated with increased risk of delayed wound healing and may delay management of recurrent malignancy. If the wound was attributed only to radiation therapy, a better strategy would be to excise the irradiated soft tissues and cover the whole defect with a well-vascularized flap.


Hyperbaric oxygen therapy has been shown to be beneficial for the management of radiation soft-tissue injury. This therapeutic modality should only be instituted after a complete evaluation of the patient‚Äos wound, which would include soft-tissue biopsy because the patient previously had a malignancy in the region.


Complete evaluation of the wound would include pertinent history and physical examination, evaluation of the patient‚Äos nutritional status, examination of extremity vascular inflow and outflow, diagnosis and treatment of wound infection, and optimization of wound characteristics.
The patient has already undergone debridement and wound care for several months; therefore, continued observation and wound care would be an inadequate management option.


It is inappropriate to perform negative pressure wound therapy in an irradiated wound without diagnosis by tissue biopsy.


References
1. Janis JE, Kwon RK, Lalonde DH. A practical guide to wound healing. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Jun;125(6):230e-244e.
2. Thom SR. Hyperbaric oxygen: its mechanisms and efficacy. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2011 Jan;127 Suppl 1:131S-141S.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female patient seeks treatment for upper limb lymphedema that occurred following modified radical mastectomy and external beam radiotherapy for breast malignancy. Which of the following clinical findings would indicate that the patient is not a suitable candidate for vascularized lymph node transfer?
A) Dermal backflow observed on lymphoscintigraphy
B) Significant lipomatous tissue changes in the affected limb on MRI
C) Recurrent episodes of cellulitis
D) Marked pitting edema
E) Brief symptom duration
questions.answer:
B)
Vascularized lymph node transfers work best in the early stages of lymphedema before extensive fatty tissue accumulation occurs. When MRI shows significant lipomatous changes in the extremity, it indicates advanced disease with substantial fat deposition, making excisional procedures like liposuction more appropriate than physiologic reconstruction. A is incorrect because dermal backflow on lymphoscintigraphy indicates impaired lymphatic function but doesn't contraindicate vascularized lymph node transfer. C is incorrect because frequent cellulitis episodes may actually improve after lymph node transfer and can be considered an indication for surgery rather than a contraindication. D is incorrect because severe pitting edema suggests lymphatic fluid accumulation in tissues, indicating that physiologic procedures may still be effective. E is incorrect because short symptom duration actually favors vascularized lymph node transfer, as earlier intervention before fatty changes develop leads to better outcomes.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old female manicurist presents for left thumb reconstruction one year following an amputation at the metacarpophalangeal joint level. She seeks enhanced pinch and grasp function along with optimal cosmetic results. Which reconstruction method below would most likely provide functional improvement while minimizing donor site aesthetic compromise?
A) Z-plasty of the first web space
B) Great toe transfer
C) Great toe wraparound flap
D) Osteocutaneous radial forearm flap
E) Second toe transfer
questions.answer:
E)
The second toe transfer provides functional outcomes comparable to great toe transfer while creating a thumb that better matches the contralateral thumb in size. Additionally, harvesting the second toe preserves the aesthetic appearance of the great toe on the foot, which is important for this patient who may wear open-toe shoes. A) Z-plasty alone would be insufficient for reconstruction at the MCP joint level and wouldn't provide adequate length for functional pinch or grip. B) Great toe transfer, while functionally excellent, tends to create a thumb larger than the contralateral side and results in greater cosmetic impact on the foot compared to second toe harvest. C) Great toe wraparound flap requires existing skeletal support, which is absent in this MCP-level amputation case. D) Osteocutaneous radial forearm flap creates an insensate thumb with limited motion and poor aesthetic appearance compared to toe transfers.

questions.question:
A patient diagnosed with Möbius syndrome requires facial reanimation using free gracilis muscle transfers. Which donor nerve option provides the least morbidity and is most frequently utilized for this reconstructive procedure?
A) Contralateral facial nerve
B) Glossopharyngeal nerve
C) Hypoglossal nerve
D) Masseteric nerve
E) Spinal accessory nerve
questions.answer:
D)
The masseteric nerve is the optimal choice due to its anatomical proximity and minimal associated morbidity during harvest, making it the most frequently selected donor nerve for facial reanimation procedures when the facial nerve is unavailable. A) is incorrect because patients with Möbius syndrome have bilateral facial nerve agenesis, making contralateral facial nerve transfer impossible. B) is incorrect because bilateral glossopharyngeal nerve harvest would cause severe oropharyngeal dysfunction and is rarely used even in unilateral cases. C) is incorrect because hypoglossal nerve harvest causes significant tongue atrophy and oropharyngeal complications, and bilateral harvest would result in complete tongue paralysis. E) is incorrect because bilateral spinal accessory nerve harvest would create substantial shoulder and neck dysfunction.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with ongoing redness 2 weeks following complete facial CO2 laser resurfacing treatment. Which of the following topical medications would be most suitable for reducing this patient's post-surgical erythema?
A) Amoxicillin
B) Ascorbic acid
C) Hydroquinone
D) Prednisone
E) Valacyclovir
questions.answer:
B)

Ascorbic acid is the most appropriate topical treatment for reducing post-laser resurfacing erythema. Topical vitamin C application has been demonstrated to both shorten the duration and lessen the intensity of erythema following CO2 laser procedures, and should be initiated after re-epithelialization occurs. A) Amoxicillin is incorrect because antibiotics do not address erythema and are used for bacterial infections. C) Hydroquinone is incorrect as it functions as a depigmenting agent for hyperpigmentation rather than treating redness. D) Prednisone is incorrect because topical corticosteroids can impair wound healing by delaying re-epithelialization and have not proven effective for reducing post-laser erythema. E) Valacyclovir is incorrect since antiviral medications do not treat erythema and are indicated for viral infections.

questions.question:
A 2-month-old girl is presented by her caregivers for assessment of a 4-cm, growing infantile hemangioma located on her left cheek that does not interfere with her eyesight. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Intralesional steroid injection
B) Laser treatment
C) Oral propranolol treatment
D) Surgical removal
E) Watchful waiting
questions.answer:
C)
Oral propranolol treatment is the correct answer. Systemic propranolol has emerged as a safe and effective first-line medical therapy for infantile hemangiomas, demonstrating excellent tolerability with minimal adverse effects at most medical institutions. A) Intralesional steroid injection is incorrect because it has shown inferior efficacy compared to propranolol in multiple meta-analyses and randomized trials. B) Laser treatment is incorrect as it is also less effective than propranolol based on current evidence from systematic reviews. D) Surgical removal is incorrect because it is typically reserved for lesions that fail to respond to medical therapy or cause functional problems like vision obstruction. E) Watchful waiting is incorrect for this case because it is only appropriate for small, stable lesions in areas where cosmetic appearance is not a concern.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old girl is referred to the office because of a 7-month history of asymptomatic, rapid enlargement of the right breast. Physical examination shows a large, palpable mass occupying the lower half of the right breast. There is marked nipple-areola complex stretching and prominent dilated veins. Photographs are shown. Mammogram and ultrasound show a dense, circumscribed, homogeneous 15-cm mass in the right breast. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?


A) Carcinoma
B) Cyst
C) Giant fibroadenoma
D) Juvenile breast hypertrophy
E) Phyllodes tumor
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


This patient has a fibroadenoma, the most common breast neoplasm in adolescent females. Giant fibroadenoma are typically solitary, firm, nontender, and present as a rapid asymmetric breast enlargement with prominent overlying veins and occasional pressure-induced skin ulceration. These lesions are larger than 5 cm and present at or soon after the onset of puberty. These lesions are typically treated with enucleation using breast reduction techniques for optimal symmetry with the contralateral breast. Mastectomy is not indicated, and no other adjuvant therapy is necessary. Smaller fibroadenomas may be watched conservatively, with minimal risk for malignant transformation. Surgical intervention is indicated in cases of mastodynia, neck/back pain secondary to large size, difficulty with clothing due to asymmetry, and to alleviate patient concern.


The differential diagnosis would include phyllodes tumor, breast hypertrophy, or cystic enlargement. Carcinoma would be unlikely in this age demographic. Phyllodes tumors are large, benign tumors that typically occur in the perimenopausal patient. They are histologically distinct from fibroadenomas, and transformation of a fibroadenoma to a phyllodes tumor is exceptionally rare.


Juvenile breast hypertrophy may present as unilateral or bilateral breast enlargement. The enlargement is diffuse without evidence of a discrete mass or nodularity. Juvenile breast hypertrophy typically presents in early puberty, rarely regresses spontaneously, and is much more severe than simple breast hypertrophy. The underlying cause is attributed to estrogen stimulation at the onset of the first menses. Treatment is reduction mammoplasty.


ReferencesBeenken SW, Bland KI. Evaluation and treatment of benign breast disorders. In: Bland KI and Copeland EM, eds. The breast: comprehensive management of benign and malignant disorders. 3rd ed. Saunders; 2004: 232.Chang DS, McGrath MH. Management of benign tumors of the adolescent breast. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2007;120(1):13e-19e.Carlson GW. Breast cancer, high-risk breast disease, and prophylactic mastectomy. In: Glynn E. Jones, ed. Bostwick‚Äos Plastic and Reconstructive Breast Surgery. 3rd ed. Quality Medical Publishing; 2010: 831-837.McGrath MH. Benign tumors of the teenage breast. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2000;105(1):218-222.Rohrich RJ, Thorton JF, Sorokin ES. Recurrent mammary hyperplasia: current concepts. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2003;111(1):387-393.

questions.question:
An otherwise healthy 33-year-old woman comes to the office because of back pain, brassiere grooving, and an inframammary rash. She wears a size 42 L brassiere. She has one child and says she would like to have more children. BMI is 33 kg/m2. The distance from nipple to sternal notch is 37 cm bilaterally, and the distance from nipple to inframammary fold is 16 cm bilaterally. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate reduction mammaplasty technique for this patient? 


A ) Inferior pedicle with Wise skin pattern 
B ) Lower pole amputation with nipple grafting 
C ) Medial pedicle with vertical skin pattern 
D ) Superior pedicle with vertical skin pattern 
E ) Superior pedicle with Wise skin pattern and nipple grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


The patient described is a young, healthy woman, who may desire to have more children later in life, making nipple preservation an optimal choice. She is large in size and has ptosis, making an inferior pedicle with Wise pattern the best technique to ensure adequate tissue removal. This technique is also able to reduce the vertical dimension of the breast, which is more challenging with vertical skin pattern reduction mammaplasty. Inferior pedicle reduction mammaplasty can achieve significant reduction in breast volume and alleviate preoperative symptoms with a low risk of complications.


Nipple grafting techniques are unnecessary in this woman, whose nipple needs to be elevated only 13 to 16 cm, and who may desire to have another child in the future. Medial pedicle technique is not widely used. It has been described with limited incision techniques and in combination with Wise pattern for severe macromastia. Limited incision techniques might fail to achieve reliable reduction in breast volume and result in aesthetic dimensions as well. These vertical scar techniques are best reserved for smaller volume reductions.
References
1. Okoro SA, Barone C, Bohnenblust M, et al. Breast reduction trend among plastic surgeons: a national survey. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008 Nov;122(5):1312-1320.
2. Rohrich RJ, Gosman AA, Brown SA, et al. Current preferences for breast reduction techniques: a survey of board-certified plastic surgeons 2002. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2004 Dec;114(7):1724-1733.
3. Nahabedian MY, McGibbon BM, Manson PN. Medial pedicle reduction mammaplasty for severe mammary hypertrophy. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2000 Mar;105(3):896-904.
4. Hoffman S. Inferior pedicle techniques in breast reduction. In: Spear SL, ed. Surgery of the Breast: Principles and Art. 2nd ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2005:1119-1130.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old male patient with paraplegia and a Stage IV pressure ulcer over the ischial tuberosity receives comprehensive debridement of affected soft tissue and bone followed by reconstruction using a gluteal rotation flap. What is the minimum postoperative duration before permitting sitting to optimize flap survival and patient rehabilitation?
A) Restricted sitting after 48 hours
B) Restricted sitting after 1 week
C) Restricted sitting after 3 weeks
D) Full sitting privileges at 4 weeks
E) Full sitting privileges at 6 weeks
questions.answer:
C)
The appropriate answer is restricted sitting after 3 weeks. Successful prevention of pressure ulcer recurrence following flap reconstruction demands meticulous management throughout all phases of treatment, including patient selection, preoperative optimization, surgical technique, and postoperative protocols. Postoperative immobilization using pressure-redistribution surfaces like air-fluidized beds is crucial for adequate flap healing. Established protocols recommend avoiding sitting for 3 weeks, although limited research suggests comparable results at 2 weeks in uncomplicated cases. Given the high recurrence rates even with optimal care, premature weight-bearing on the surgical site before 2-3 weeks significantly increases the risk of wound dehiscence. A is incorrect because 48 hours is far too early and would likely cause flap failure. B is incorrect because 1 week provides insufficient time for initial healing and tissue integration. D is incorrect because unlimited sitting at 4 weeks is too aggressive and may compromise long-term outcomes. E is incorrect because while 6 weeks would be safe, it represents unnecessarily prolonged immobilization that delays rehabilitation without added benefit.

questions.question:
A patient had surgical repair with open reduction and internal fixation for naso-orbital-ethmoid fractures one year prior, and excessive tearing was observed during follow-up. Following 6 months of monitoring with continuing excessive tearing, what is the most suitable next approach to assess the patient's nasolacrimal system function?
A) Insertion of conjunctivorhinostomy tube
B) Further observation, as normal function will likely resume
C) Jones testing
D) Irrigation of the lacrimal system
E) Schirmer testing
questions.answer:
C)
Jones testing is the appropriate method for assessing lacrimal drainage function. This test has two components: Jones I evaluates lacrimal outflow under normal physiological conditions using fluorescein dye placement in the conjunctival fornix and checking for dye appearance in the nasal cavity at 2 and 5 minutes. Jones II test determines fluorescein presence after flushing residual dye from the conjunctival sac with saline to assess for reflux. NOE fractures frequently affect the lacrimal drainage system, either from direct surgical manipulation during transcanthal wiring or from the fractures themselves. Post-surgical excessive tearing occurs in at least 50% of NOE fracture patients after ORIF, with approximately half resolving after 3-6 months and the remaining 25% requiring further lacrimal drainage evaluation. A) is incorrect because conjunctivorhinostomy tube placement is a treatment procedure, not a diagnostic test. B) is incorrect because after 6 months of persistent symptoms, further observation is not appropriate and diagnostic evaluation is needed. D) is incorrect because lacrimal system irrigation is a treatment intervention rather than a functional assessment tool. E) is incorrect because Schirmer testing evaluates tear production for dry eye conditions, not lacrimal drainage function.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male presents for scalp restoration following thermal injury from a decade ago. Physical examination reveals irregular hair loss and thick scarring affecting the left temporoparietal region, encompassing roughly 35% of the entire scalp area. What represents the optimal reconstructive approach for this patient?
A) Free latissimus dorsi myocutaneous flap with skin grafting
B) Follicular hair transplantation
C) Orticochea three-flap technique
D) Sequential excision with primary closure
E) Controlled tissue expansion
questions.answer:
E)
Controlled tissue expansion provides the superior functional and aesthetic result for this patient. No other anatomical region can replicate the unique hair-bearing characteristics of native scalp tissue - essentially, optimal scalp replacement requires scalp tissue itself. Beyond achieving cranial coverage and wound healing, reconstructive goals must include cosmetic acceptability. For patients with approximately 40% scalp deficiency, tissue expansion delivers the best functional and cosmetic outcomes. This technique should be considered when local tissue rearrangement proves insufficient due to defect magnitude, traumatic damage, or unacceptable hairline distortion. Expansion increases available local tissue while preserving innervation and maintaining hair follicles with associated structures. Up to 50% scalp reconstruction is achievable with expanded tissue while maintaining acceptable hair density. A) Free latissimus dorsi flap is better reserved for total or near-total scalp defects, particularly following radiation or oncologic resection, not for this moderate-sized defect. B) Hair transplantation is inappropriate for defects of this magnitude and scarred recipient beds. C) Orticochea flaps are unsuitable for defects exceeding 30% scalp area and often produce inferior cosmetic results due to unnatural hair orientation. D) Serial excision works well for smaller defects but creates more scarring and deformity compared to tissue expansion for defects of this size.

questions.question:
A 13-year-old male patient with a history of surgical correction for left-sided unilateral cleft lip and palate presents to the clinic expressing concern about his "underbite." He denies any additional complaints. Cephalometric measurements reveal an SNA angle of 76 degrees (normal = 81 ± 3) and an SNB angle of 81 degrees (normal = 79 ± 3). Clinical examination demonstrates a negative overjet measuring 5 mm. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Bimaxillary surgical advancement
B) Le Fort I maxillary advancement with rigid internal fixation
C) Le Fort I osteotomy with distraction osteogenesis
D) Mandibular reduction surgery
E) Orthodontic treatment with annual monitoring
questions.answer:
E)
At 13 years old, facial skeletal development remains incomplete, requiring delay of definitive surgical intervention until skeletal maturity is achieved, typically around age 18 in males. During this period, regular monitoring by the craniofacial team is essential. Class III malocclusion frequently occurs following cleft palate reconstruction due to scar tissue formation that restricts maxillary development. Unless severe complications exist (like airway obstruction), orthognathic surgery should be postponed until growth completion. A) is incorrect because bimaxillary surgery is unnecessary given the normal SNB angle. B) is incorrect because immediate surgical correction is premature before skeletal maturity. C) is incorrect because distraction osteogenesis should be reserved for cases requiring advancement greater than 10mm and is inappropriate at this age. D) is incorrect because the SNB angle falls within normal parameters, making mandibular setback unwarranted.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old female patient presents with a fluid collection around her textured saline breast implants that were inserted a decade ago. Ultrasound-guided fluid aspiration is conducted and the sample undergoes Wright-Giemsa staining and immunohistochemical analysis with flow cytometry. Which laboratory finding pattern would establish the diagnosis of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma?
A) CD30 negative, ALK negative
B) CD30 negative, ALK positive
C) CD30 positive, ALK negative
D) CD30 positive, ALK positive
questions.answer:
C)
The diagnosis of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) is confirmed by the immunohistochemical pattern of CD30-positive and ALK-negative staining. BIA-ALCL represents a unique variant of T-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma that develops around breast implants following either reconstructive or aesthetic procedures. This malignancy characteristically expresses CD30 but lacks ALK expression, which distinguishes it from systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma that typically shows ALK positivity. Option A is incorrect because BIA-ALCL consistently demonstrates CD30 positivity, not negativity. Option B is incorrect as it shows CD30 negativity, which contradicts the defining characteristic of BIA-ALCL being CD30-positive. Option D is incorrect because while it correctly shows CD30 positivity, BIA-ALCL is characteristically ALK-negative, unlike systemic ALCL which tends to be ALK-positive.

questions.question:
A 69-year-old male patient is being assessed in the ICU on day 5 following abdominal wall reconstruction surgery for recurrent ventral hernia. He has no history of heart disease. Vital signs show fever of 103°F (39°C), pulse of 110 beats per minute, and mean arterial pressure of 50 mmHg. His airway is protected with mechanical ventilation, and oxygen therapy has been started. Laboratory results reveal hemoglobin of 9 g/dL. What is the most appropriate immediate management step?
A) Begin inotropic therapy
B) Start vasopressor therapy
C) Place a pulmonary artery catheter for wedge pressure monitoring
D) Administer crystalloid fluid resuscitation
E) Transfuse packed red blood cells
questions.answer:
D)

In this patient presenting with septic shock, after securing the airway and breathing, the most appropriate immediate intervention is crystalloid fluid resuscitation to restore adequate circulation and tissue perfusion. This patient demonstrates classic signs of septic shock including hypotension (MAP <70 mmHg), tachycardia (HR >100 bpm), and fever, requiring prompt volume expansion as first-line therapy. Crystalloid resuscitation should be guided by physiologic endpoints while monitoring for signs of fluid overload or pulmonary edema. A) is incorrect because inotropic agents like dobutamine are reserved for refractory shock with reduced cardiac output after adequate volume resuscitation. B) is incorrect because vasopressors such as norepinephrine are second-line treatments used only after fluid resuscitation has been attempted and found inadequate. C) is incorrect because pulmonary artery catheter placement has not demonstrated improved outcomes in septic shock management and carries additional procedural risks. E) is incorrect because current evidence supports restrictive transfusion strategies, with blood transfusion not recommended above hemoglobin levels of 7 g/dL in septic shock patients without active bleeding, cardiac disease, or myocardial ischemia.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female patient is undergoing tummy tuck surgery, diastasis recti repair, and correction of an incisional hernia. During the initial phase of surgery, the surgeon administers 20 mL of 1% lidocaine containing epinephrine 1:100,000 into the lower abdominal surgical site. Following completion of the hernia repair, the general surgeon intends to administer liposomal bupivacaine to the lower abdominal hernia repair area. What is the most appropriate guidance concerning the timing of liposomal bupivacaine administration following lidocaine injection?
A) Liposomal bupivacaine should not be administered following lidocaine use
B) Allow a minimum 20-minute interval before administering liposomal bupivacaine
C) Allow a minimum 60-minute interval before administering liposomal bupivacaine
D) Allow a minimum 90-minute interval before administering liposomal bupivacaine
E) No timing restrictions apply
questions.answer:
B)
Allow a minimum 20-minute interval before administering liposomal bupivacaine. Liposomal bupivacaine (Exparel) is an extended-release formulation that provides prolonged analgesia for approximately 72 hours and has demonstrated efficacy in reducing postoperative opioid requirements. When non-bupivacaine local anesthetics such as lidocaine are combined with liposomal bupivacaine, they can trigger immediate bupivacaine release from the liposomal carriers, potentially leading to toxic plasma concentrations. Therefore, these agents must not be mixed directly. However, sequential administration is permissible with a minimum 20-minute waiting period between lidocaine and liposomal bupivacaine injection. A) is incorrect because liposomal bupivacaine can be safely used after lidocaine with proper timing. C) is incorrect because a 60-minute delay exceeds the minimum required interval. D) is incorrect because a 90-minute delay is unnecessarily prolonged beyond clinical recommendations. E) is incorrect because specific timing restrictions do exist to prevent drug interaction complications.

questions.question:
A male patient arrives at the emergency department with a complex infection of his lower third molar. He exhibits restricted jaw opening (trismus) and localized pain when pressure is applied over the zygomatic arch. This infection has most likely spread to which anatomical space?
A) Buccal
B) Prevertebral
C) Pterygomandibular
D) Submasseteric
E) Temporal
questions.answer:
E)
The temporal space is the correct answer because the clinical presentation of trismus combined with point tenderness above the zygomatic arch is characteristic of temporal space involvement. The masticator space contains four interconnected compartments: masseteric (submasseteric), pterygomandibular, deep temporal, and superficial temporal spaces. When infection spreads to the temporal space, it causes the described symptoms due to inflammation affecting the temporalis muscle and surrounding structures. A) Buccal space infections typically present with facial swelling over the cheek rather than tenderness above the zygomatic arch. B) Prevertebral space infections would more commonly cause neck stiffness and swallowing difficulties rather than jaw restriction and zygomatic tenderness. C) Pterygomandibular space infections usually cause trismus but without the characteristic point tenderness above the zygomatic arch. D) Submasseteric space infections cause trismus but tenderness would be located along the mandibular angle rather than above the zygomatic arch.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman presents 18 years following placement of retropectoral smooth saline breast implants for cosmetic enhancement. She is unhappy with her current breast contour. Physical examination shows breast parenchyma sagging below the implants, with Grade I capsules noted. What is the optimal surgical management for this patient's complaint?
A) Implant exchange alone
B) Implant exchange with capsulectomy
C) Implant exchange with mastopexy
D) Implant exchange with suture repair of the stretched inferior pocket
E) Conversion to subglandular implant placement
questions.answer:
C)
This patient demonstrates a "snoopy nose" or "waterfall breast" deformity, characterized by ptotic breast parenchyma hanging over appropriately positioned implants. The implants have maintained their original position while the natural breast tissue has descended due to aging and gravity. This presentation does not involve pocket stretching or upward implant migration from capsular contracture, as indicated by the soft breast consistency. The ideal management involves implant exchange (given their 18-year duration) combined with a suitable mastopexy procedure. A is incorrect because it does not address the tissue ptosis. B is incorrect since the breasts are soft without significant capsule formation requiring removal. D is incorrect because the inframammary fold position remains appropriate without secondary fold development. E is incorrect as it would not resolve the substantial ptosis, although it might benefit cases with minimal drooping.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with severe pain and pressure in her right eye, beginning 12 hours after undergoing transcutaneous lower blepharoplasty at an outside facility. Her symptoms commenced shortly following the procedure, and when she contacted the surgical office, she was told to simply increase her analgesic dosage. Physical examination reveals right-sided periorbital ecchymosis, ocular protrusion, restricted ocular motility with diplopia, and decreased visual acuity relative to the left eye. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A) Acute angle-closure glaucoma
B) Extraocular muscle entrapment
C) Orbital cellulitis
D) Retrobulbar hematoma
E) Superior orbital fissure syndrome
questions.answer:
D)
This patient exhibits characteristic features of retrobulbar hematoma following blepharoplasty, representing a surgical emergency that demands urgent treatment. The combination of severe orbital pain and pressure, visual deterioration, limited extraocular movements causing diplopia, extensive bruising, and proptosis are diagnostic for this complication. Retrobulbar hemorrhage is the primary cause of visual loss following eyelid surgery, with 82% of cases occurring within 24 hours and more than half developing within 6 hours post-procedure. A is incorrect because acute angle-closure glaucoma, although causing painful visual loss in older patients, seldom develops immediately following blepharoplasty. B is incorrect since extraocular muscle entrapment typically results from orbital fractures during trauma rather than routine eyelid procedures. C is incorrect because orbital cellulitis usually presents with systemic signs like fever and develops 4-6 days after surgery, not within hours. E is incorrect as superior orbital fissure syndrome occurs with traumatic orbital fractures rather than elective cosmetic surgeries.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old healthy woman is being evaluated and prepared for breast enhancement surgery using silicone gel prostheses. Which statement is most correct regarding breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL)?
A) All late-developing fluid collections around breast prostheses need evaluation
B) BIA-ALCL usually demonstrates an aggressive clinical course
C) BIA-ALCL is most commonly seen with smooth-surfaced prostheses
D) BIA-ALCL information is not necessary in standard breast enhancement informed consent
E) BIA-ALCL etiology is established through strong evidence-based studies
questions.answer:
A)
Considering the potentially severe consequences of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) and its typical manifestation as late-onset fluid accumulation, appropriate diagnostic workup should be conducted for all delayed breast prosthesis-related fluid collections, incorporating cytologic examination and, when indicated, fine-needle sampling, flow cytometry, and CD30 immunohistochemical staining. B is incorrect because BIA-ALCL generally demonstrates a slow-growing pattern limited to peri-prosthesis fluid and has favorable outcomes with prosthesis and capsule excision, although aggressive forms can occur. C is incorrect since BIA-ALCL is primarily linked to textured, rather than smooth, prostheses. D is incorrect because BIA-ALCL constitutes an important potential adverse outcome that must be discussed during informed consent for all breast prosthesis surgeries. E is incorrect as existing data on BIA-ALCL causation relies on poor-quality research with insufficient evidence.

questions.question:
A 39-year-old woman presents for assessment of a facial growth that has been present for 6 months. A biopsy is under consideration. Which histopathologic finding would allow for safe management with monitoring only in this case?
A) Cylindroma
B) Eccrine poroma
C) Nevus sebaceous
D) Trichoepithelioma
questions.answer:
D)
Trichoepitheliomas represent benign hair follicle tumors that commonly manifest as multiple, pale yellow-pink, semi-transparent nodules distributed symmetrically across the cheeks, eyelids, and nasolabial folds, with a female predominance. Although they can mimic basal cell carcinomas both clinically and microscopically, these are benign growths that require only surveillance without active treatment. The exception is desmoplastic variants, which may necessitate complete surgical removal or Mohs micrographic surgery to distinguish them definitively from malignancy. A is incorrect because cylindromas, despite being generally benign, carry documented risk for malignant change and usually warrant removal through excision or electrocoagulation. B is incorrect since eccrine poromas possess rare potential for malignant progression to porocarcinoma and should undergo surgical removal. C is incorrect as nevus sebaceous carries roughly 20% likelihood of developing secondary tumors, particularly basal cell carcinoma, requiring preventive surgical removal, ideally prior to adolescence.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of superficial radial nerve entrapment in her left forearm comes for assessment. Non-operative management including NSAIDs, corticosteroid injections, bracing, and lifestyle changes over 7 months has failed to provide relief. Operative treatment is now being considered. Fascial release between which two muscle-tendon units would be most suitable for this condition?
A) Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
B) Brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus
C) Extensor carpi radialis longus and extensor carpi radialis brevis
D) Flexor carpi radialis and abductor pollicis longus
E) Flexor carpi radialis and brachioradialis
questions.answer:
B)
Superficial radial nerve entrapment, known as Wartenberg syndrome, typically develops at the dorsal border of the brachioradialis where the nerve emerges from its deep fascial compartment to become subcutaneous. Clinical manifestations include discomfort, paresthesias, or dysesthesias along the radial dorsal hand involving the thumb and index finger regions. Following failed conservative care, operative decompression requires fascial division between the brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus tendons, which corresponds to the anatomical zone of nerve entrapment as it transitions between tissue planes. A is wrong because this space is associated with de Quervain's disease, not radial nerve compression. C is wrong as this interval is not the site of superficial radial nerve entrapment. D is wrong because these structures are not located where the nerve becomes compressed. E is wrong as this anatomical relationship does not correspond to the typical compression site.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient presents to the clinic one month prior to a planned breast lift procedure. Her routine annual mammogram reveals a 1.5-cm lesion in the upper outer quadrant. A core needle biopsy is conducted. Histopathological analysis of the sampled tissue shows papilloma with no atypical features. What is the most appropriate subsequent management step?
A) Bilateral breast ultrasound examination
B) Surgical excision of the needle-localized region
C) Return to routine annual mammographic screening in 12 months
D) Follow-up mammography every 6 months for one year
E) Stereotactic vacuum-assisted core biopsy
questions.answer:
B)
Surgical excision of the needle-localized region is the most appropriate next step because this 65-year-old patient has a large (1.5-cm) peripherally located papilloma, which carries higher malignancy risk. Studies show that benign papillomas diagnosed on needle biopsy can harbor ductal carcinoma in situ in up to 11% of cases upon surgical excision. The size (>1.5 cm) and peripheral location are concerning features that distinguish this from typical benign papillomas, which are usually <1 cm and centrally located. A) Bilateral breast ultrasound is incorrect because sonographic evaluation would not provide meaningful additional information in a 65-year-old with mature breast tissue and a solid mammographically detected mass. C) Routine annual mammography is incorrect because the size and location characteristics warrant more definitive evaluation rather than observation. D) Short-interval mammographic follow-up is incorrect because imaging surveillance alone is insufficient given the high-risk features of this lesion. E) Repeat stereotactic biopsy is incorrect because additional needle sampling would not be more effective than the initial core biopsy and surgical excision is needed for definitive diagnosis.

questions.question:
Enhancement in which of the following represents a benefit of nipple-areolar complex reconstruction?
A) Ability to breastfeed
B) Contour of the breast mound
C) Tactile sensitivity
D) Patient contentment with reconstruction
E) Erotic sensation
questions.answer:
D)
Patient contentment with reconstruction, overall quality of life, and sense of wholeness following reconstruction have all been demonstrated to correlate with nipple and/or areolar reconstruction. The procedure does not restore nipple functionality; thus, breastfeeding capability, erotic sensation, and tactile sensitivity are not achieved through nipple and/or areolar reconstruction. A is incorrect because the reconstruction does not restore functional lactation ability. B is incorrect because nipple reconstruction using local tissue methods may actually cause flattening of the breast's anterior surface rather than improving mound contour. C is incorrect because tactile responsiveness is not restored by this reconstructive procedure. E is incorrect because erotic sensation is not regained through nipple-areolar reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old female patient, G3P3, seeks consultation for breast enhancement. She nursed each of her three children for 12 months. Physical examination reveals bilateral nipple-to-sternal notch measurements of 27 cm, diminished upper pole fullness, and visible stretch marks. Bilateral Grade 3 ptosis is present. The superior pole soft tissue measures 1 cm when pinched. Which of the following surgical approaches would most effectively restore upper pole fullness and improve breast contour in this case?
A) Dual-plane breast implant placement
B) Breast lift combined with dual-plane implant placement
C) Breast lift with subglandular implant placement
D) Subglandular breast implant placement
E) Vertical pattern breast lift
questions.answer:
B)
The optimal choice is breast lift combined with dual-plane implant placement. This approach addresses both the volume deficit and the significant ptosis present. The thin superior pole tissue (1 cm) makes subglandular placement inappropriate as it requires at least 2 cm of coverage. A) is incorrect because dual-plane implants alone would not correct the Grade 3 ptosis, leaving the nipple malpositioned. C) is incorrect because subglandular placement is contraindicated with insufficient tissue coverage. D) is incorrect for the same reason as C, plus it doesn't address the ptosis. E) is incorrect because vertical mastopexy alone would not restore the lost upper pole volume and may require additional skin excision modifications due to the extensive ptosis.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male presents to the emergency room 2 hours following trauma to his left leg after being struck by a car. Examination reveals soft tissue avulsion of the posterior thigh region. A femoral fracture has been stabilized with an intramedullary nail; the sciatic nerve appears continuous but shows bruising at the mid-posterior thigh level. Adequate soft tissue exists for reconstruction. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Immediate excision of the bruised nerve segment with nerve graft reconstruction
B) Nerve segment removal at 10 days post-injury followed by nerve graft repair
C) EMG testing at 3 weeks with nerve grafting if fibrillation potentials are present
D) Sequential nerve conduction studies at 3 weeks and 3 months with surgical repair if no recovery occurs
questions.answer:
D)
Sequential electrodiagnostic testing allows proper assessment of nerve recovery potential after crush injury. The 3-week study establishes a baseline and may show fibrillations indicating axonal damage, but cannot reliably predict recovery at this early stage. The 3-month evaluation can detect subtle recovery signs not apparent on clinical exam alone. If no improvement is demonstrated by 3 months on both clinical and electrodiagnostic assessment, surgical reconstruction is warranted. A is incorrect because immediate resection of a potentially viable nerve in continuity is contraindicated. B is incorrect because at 10 days post-trauma, nerve viability cannot be accurately determined intraoperatively when the nerve remains in continuity. C is incorrect because the presence of fibrillations at 3 weeks alone does not indicate need for immediate repair, as some recovery may still occur over the following months.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old female presents for assessment due to a 1-year duration of worsening mandibular retrusion and bilateral pain in the temporomandibular joints. No traumatic injury is reported. Physical examination reveals mildly restricted mouth opening without deviation of the chin point and an Angle class II dental misalignment with anterior open bite. What is the most probable etiology of this patient's condition?
A) Teeth grinding
B) Excessive condylar growth
C) Infectious process
D) Muscle-related pain disorder
E) Autoimmune joint inflammation
questions.answer:
E)
Autoimmune joint inflammation (rheumatoid arthritis) is the most likely cause. When rheumatoid arthritis occurs during childhood or adolescence (juvenile idiopathic arthritis), chronic inflammatory changes can erode the mandibular condyles, resulting in progressive backward positioning of the lower jaw and anterior open bite deformity. The temporomandibular joint is involved in approximately one-third of rheumatoid arthritis patients, and bilateral involvement with these specific skeletal changes is characteristic of this condition. A) Teeth grinding is incorrect because while it can cause jaw pain and dental wear, it does not alter facial skeletal structure or cause mandibular retrusion. B) Excessive condylar growth is incorrect because it typically occurs unilaterally, is usually painless, and would cause chin deviation rather than bilateral retrognathia. C) Infectious process is incorrect because TMJ infections are rarely bilateral and would typically present with systemic signs of illness. D) Muscle-related pain disorder is incorrect because while it can cause TMJ pain, it usually affects one side and does not cause joint destruction or changes in jaw position and bite alignment.

questions.question:
The use of oral contraceptives is associated with an increased occurrence of which histologic breast cancer risk factor?
A) Apocrine metaplasia
B) Atypical hyperplasia
C) Intraductal hyperplasia
D) Intraductal papilloma
E) Sclerosing adenosis
questions.answer:
B)
Atypical hyperplasia is the correct answer because it represents the only histologic finding among the options that shows increased incidence with oral contraceptive use, and it carries a 4.5- to 5-fold elevated risk for breast cancer development. A) is incorrect because apocrine metaplasia is a non-proliferative change that does not increase breast cancer risk and is not affected by oral contraceptive use. C) is incorrect because intraductal hyperplasia, while a proliferative lesion, actually decreases in occurrence with oral contraceptive use. D) is incorrect because intraductal papilloma incidence is reduced, not increased, by oral contraceptive use. E) is incorrect because sclerosing adenosis occurrence is also decreased with oral contraceptive use.

questions.question:
A 13-year-old female presents for evaluation of unilateral breast development abnormality. Physical examination reveals complete absence of mammary tissue on the left side, while the areola and nipple appear normal. The pectoral musculature is intact. No abnormalities of the hands, face, or other body regions are observed. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Amastia
B) Amazia
C) Athelia
D) Ectodermal dysplasia
E) Poland sequence
questions.answer:
B)
Amazia is the correct diagnosis as it describes the congenital absence of mammary gland tissue while the nipple and areola remain present, which matches this patient's presentation. A) Amastia is incorrect because it refers to complete absence of both breast tissue and nipple-areolar complex. C) Athelia is incorrect because it specifically describes absence of the nipple, which is present in this case. D) Ectodermal dysplasia is incorrect because it would require multiple abnormalities affecting ectodermal structures like hair, teeth, nails, or sweat glands, none of which are present. E) Poland sequence is incorrect because it involves absence of the pectoralis major muscle and associated chest wall deformities, but this patient has normal pectoral muscles.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female patient without any trauma history presents with a one-month duration of cephalgia and soft tissue edema overlying the frontal sinus and lateral frontal bone region. Currently, she exhibits pyrexia, altered mental state, and progressive swelling with erythema of the forehead. Computed tomography reveals a frontal epidural collection and opacification of the frontal sinuses. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Exostosis
B) Fibrous dysplasia
C) Frontal osteoma
D) Infected encephalocele
E) Pott puffy tumor
questions.answer:
E)
Pott puffy tumor represents the most likely diagnosis given the clinical presentation and imaging findings. This condition involves osteomyelitis with abscess formation secondary to chronic frontal sinusitis, which matches the patient's symptoms of headaches, soft tissue swelling, fever, mental status changes, and CT findings of epidural abscess with frontal sinus opacification. A) Exostosis is incorrect because it represents a benign bony outgrowth that develops gradually without infectious symptoms or mental status alterations. B) Fibrous dysplasia is incorrect as it is a non-infectious benign bone tumor characterized by slow growth without acute inflammatory signs. C) Frontal osteoma is incorrect because it is a benign bone lesion that grows slowly and does not cause fever, mental status changes, or soft tissue infection. D) Infected encephalocele is incorrect as this represents infection of a congenital skull defect with brain herniation, which would have different imaging characteristics and clinical history.

questions.question:
What is the leading cause of temporomandibular joint ankylosis?
A) Teeth grinding
B) Developmental defect
C) Infectious process
D) Radiation exposure
E) Traumatic injury
questions.answer:
E)
Traumatic injury is the leading cause of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) ankylosis. This typically develops following untreated or improperly managed mandibular fractures that damage the joint's articular surfaces. In pediatric patients, this can result in growth abnormalities requiring orthognathic correction, while adults may need joint replacement or repair procedures. A) Teeth grinding is incorrect because bruxism rarely leads to ankylosis, typically causing other TMJ disorders instead. B) Developmental defect is incorrect as congenital anomalies are uncommon causes of TMJ ankylosis. C) Infectious process is incorrect because infections causing TMJ ankylosis are rare in the modern antibiotic era. D) Radiation exposure is incorrect as it represents a less frequent cause compared to trauma.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male presents to the emergency room 4 months following right hand transplantation with complaints of a painful, burning rash affecting the transplanted hand. Physical examination reveals a maculopapular erythematous rash on the hand. What type of rejection is most likely occurring in this patient?
A) Hyperacute
B) Accelerated
C) Acute
D) Chronic
E) Graft-versus-host
questions.answer:
C)
This patient is experiencing acute rejection, which is mediated by T-cell activation and typically occurs after the fifth postoperative day, most commonly within the first 4-6 months post-transplantation. The clinical presentation of cutaneous manifestations on the transplanted hand at 4 months is characteristic of acute rejection. A) Hyperacute rejection is incorrect because it occurs within minutes to hours of transplantation due to preexisting antibodies and would have manifested immediately in the operating room. B) Accelerated rejection is incorrect because it typically occurs between days 2-5 post-transplantation, not at 4 months. D) Chronic rejection is incorrect because it develops over months to years and involves progressive arterial sclerosis and fibrosis rather than acute cutaneous manifestations. E) Graft-versus-host disease is incorrect because it involves the transplanted tissue's immune cells attacking the recipient and is most common after bone marrow transplantation, not hand transplantation.

questions.question:
In embryonic development, which structure originates from the same pharyngeal arch as the antihelix?
A) Mandible
B) Maxilla
C) Mylohyoid
D) Stapes
E) Tensor veli palatini
questions.answer:
D)

The stapes is the correct answer because both the stapes and antihelix develop from the second pharyngeal arch during embryogenesis. The antihelix forms from one of the three posterior hillocks of the second pharyngeal arch, while the stapes is among the bony structures derived from this same arch. A) is incorrect because the mandible develops from the first pharyngeal arch, not the second. B) is incorrect because the maxilla originates from the first pharyngeal arch. C) is incorrect because the mylohyoid muscle is a derivative of the first pharyngeal arch. E) is incorrect because the tensor veli palatini is also a first pharyngeal arch derivative.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient is undergoing tummy tuck surgery with lateral liposuction. A regional nerve block is being considered for anesthesia. What is the optimal anatomical plane for administering this anesthetic injection?
A) Between the external oblique and internal oblique muscles
B) Between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles
C) Between the skin and external oblique muscle
D) Between the transversalis fascia and peritoneum
E) Between the transversus abdominis muscle and transversalis fascia
questions.answer:
B)
The correct choice is B. The transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block targets the fascial plane between the internal oblique muscle and the transversus abdominis muscle, where the sensory nerve fibers supplying the anterolateral abdominal wall (T6-L1 dermatomes) travel. This anatomical location allows for effective blockade of pain sensation from the surgical site. Option A is incorrect because the plane between the external and internal oblique muscles does not contain the target sensory nerves for abdominal wall anesthesia. Option C is incorrect as the subcutaneous plane between skin and external oblique muscle would not provide adequate depth for nerve blockade. Option D is incorrect because injection between transversalis fascia and peritoneum would be too deep and risk intraperitoneal complications. Option E is incorrect as this plane is deeper than necessary and does not optimally target the sensory nerve fibers that run above the transversus abdominis muscle.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old child presents for assessment due to a 6-month duration of excessive tearing from both eyes. Physical examination reveals eyelashes making contact with the lower corneal surfaces on both sides. What is the most probable underlying cause of this patient's presentation?
A) Improper insertion of the orbital septum
B) Elevated tarsal plate position
C) Loosening of the lateral canthal ligaments
D) Weakness of the tarsal plate structure
E) Excess skin and muscle tissue around the eyelid
questions.answer:
E)
The most probable cause of epiblepharon is excessive pretarsal skin and orbicular muscle tissue at the lower eyelid border. This congenital condition involves a fold of skin and underlying orbicular muscle overriding the eyelid edge, frequently causing the eyelashes to contact the eyeball. The eyelid border and tarsal structure remain stable with proper positioning. Epiblepharon typically involves the lower eyelids, occurs more frequently in individuals of Asian heritage, and becomes more pronounced when looking downward. A is incorrect because improper orbital septum insertion is typically associated with traumatic causes rather than this congenital condition. B is incorrect because the tarsal plate position remains normal in epiblepharon. C is incorrect because lateral canthal ligament loosening is characteristic of age-related eyelid changes, not this pediatric condition. D is incorrect because tarsal plate weakness occurs with aging processes rather than this congenital anomaly.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old male presents to the emergency room with ongoing pain and discoloration beneath the nail of his left index finger occurring 6 hours following a crushing trauma. Clinical evaluation reveals a subungual hematoma localized to the area beyond the lunula. The overlying nail plate remains attached and undamaged. The nail plate shows no tearing or elevation. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Amputation
B) Digital nerve block using epinephrine
C) Elevation
D) Removal of nail plate and placement of sterile matrix graft
E) Trephination
questions.answer:
E)
Trephination is the correct treatment because subungual hematomas create pressure in the confined space beneath an intact nail plate, causing significant throbbing pain that requires drainage for relief. This procedure can be performed using a battery-powered electrocautery unit or heated sterile paper clip to create a hole large enough for sustained drainage. A) Amputation is incorrect because it represents excessive treatment for a simple nail bed hematoma. B) Digital block with epinephrine is incorrect because it only provides temporary pain relief without addressing the underlying pressure from the hematoma. C) Elevation is incorrect because it provides minimal pain reduction and does not resolve the primary problem of trapped blood beneath the nail. D) Nail plate removal and sterile matrix graft is incorrect because the nail plate is intact and undamaged, making exploration and grafting unnecessary for this condition.

questions.question:
A 64-year-old woman presents for evaluation of excessive tearing from her right eye. Physical examination reveals age-appropriate eyelid positioning. What is the most appropriate diagnostic test to assess for nasolacrimal duct blockage?
A) Goldmann applanation tonometry
B) Jones dye test
C) Optical coherence tomography
D) Seidel fluorescein test
E) Snap-back eyelid test
questions.answer:
B)
The Jones dye test is the optimal diagnostic procedure for evaluating nasolacrimal duct obstruction. The Jones I test assesses tear drainage under normal physiological conditions by placing fluorescein dye in the conjunctival fornix and checking for dye recovery from the nasal cavity after 5 minutes when the patient blows their nose. If no dye is recovered, this may indicate false-negative results, functional impairment, or structural blockage. The Jones II test follows a negative Jones I test, where remaining fluorescein is irrigated from the conjunctival sac with saline, and the patient expels drainage from the throat to check for fluorescein presence. Complete absence of fluorescein suggests total nasolacrimal duct or canalicular obstruction. A) Goldmann applanation tonometry is incorrect because it measures intraocular pressure using corneal flattening principles, not tear drainage. C) Optical coherence tomography is incorrect as it provides cross-sectional retinal imaging using light waves, unrelated to lacrimal system evaluation. D) The Seidel fluorescein test is incorrect because it detects aqueous humor leaks or vitreous exposure, not nasolacrimal obstruction. E) The snap-back eyelid test is incorrect as it evaluates horizontal lower eyelid laxity by assessing how quickly the displaced lid returns to normal position against the eye.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old female patient presents to the hospital following a motor vehicle accident with a fractured left mandibular angle. Surgical repair using open reduction and internal fixation is scheduled through a submandibular (Risdon) approach. Which anatomical plane of dissection would be most suitable for accessing the fracture site while protecting the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve?
A) Between the carotid sheath and posterior digastric muscle belly
B) Between the platysma muscle and investing layer of deep cervical fascia
C) Between the skin and platysma muscle
D) Between the submandibular gland and carotid sheath
E) Between the investing layer of deep cervical fascia and submandibular gland
questions.answer:
E)
The correct plane of dissection is between the investing layer of deep cervical fascia and the submandibular gland. This approach protects the marginal mandibular nerve, which consistently travels superficial to or within the investing fascia layer. The surgical technique involves making a skin incision 2cm below the mandibular border, dividing the platysma, then dissecting deep to the investing fascia just above the submandibular gland before proceeding superiorly to the mandibular border. A) is incorrect because this plane is too deep and lateral, not providing optimal access to mandibular fractures. B) is incorrect because dissecting between these layers would place the marginal mandibular nerve at risk since it travels within or superficial to the investing fascia. C) is incorrect because this superficial plane does not provide adequate access to the mandibular bone for fracture repair. D) is incorrect because this plane is too deep and does not follow the standard submandibular approach for mandibular fracture repair.

questions.question:
A 12-week-old baby is scheduled for surgical correction of a complete bilateral cleft lip. Which of the following represents a fundamental principle that applies to both bilateral and unilateral cleft lip reconstruction?
A) Repositioning the columella to the midline
B) Forming a rotation advancement flap
D) Restoring muscle continuity
C) Removing the prolabial vermillion tissue
E) Managing the protruding premaxilla
questions.answer:
D)
Restoring muscle continuity is an essential objective in both unilateral and bilateral cleft lip reconstruction procedures. Repositioning the columella to the midline is specific only to unilateral cleft lip repairs. The prolabium exists exclusively in bilateral cleft lip cases. Managing the protruding premaxilla is a technique used solely in bilateral cleft lip reconstructions. Forming a rotation advancement flap is a method employed only in unilateral cleft lip repairs.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old female athlete is planning to have liposuction for outer thigh contouring. She maintains good physical condition and has reduced her weight by 10 lb (4.5 kg) in the last 6 months. Her present weight is 145 lb (65.8 kg). Physical assessment revealed fat accumulation in the lateral thigh region. To minimize the likelihood of postoperative contour irregularities in this patient, special consideration should be given to which of the following adherence zones?
A) Gluteal fold
B) Iliotibial band
C) Lateral gluteal hollow
D) Medial mid-thigh
E) Dorsal thigh
