questions.answer:
C)

The lateral gluteal hollow is the correct answer because it represents a critical zone of adherence located just above the outer lateral thigh area. When performing liposuction in the outer thigh region, careful attention to this zone is essential to prevent contour deformities, as zones of adherence are areas where the superficial fascial system connects through the deep compartment to the underlying muscle fascia, creating natural boundaries that must be respected during fat removal. A) The gluteal fold is incorrect because it is not directly related to outer thigh liposuction and is located more posteriorly. B) The iliotibial band is incorrect because while it runs along the lateral thigh, the relevant portion for this procedure would be more distal to the primary area of concern. D) The medial mid-thigh is incorrect because it is on the opposite (inner) side of the thigh from the treatment area. E) The dorsal thigh is incorrect because it refers to the back of the thigh, which is not the target area for this outer thigh contouring procedure.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old male patient is planned for surgical removal of a melanoma on his leg under regional anesthesia. His current medications are lisinopril and intermittent ibuprofen. He has never smoked tobacco. Which of the following characteristics elevates his risk for experiencing postoperative nausea and vomiting?
A) Being older than 50 years
B) Being male
C) Never having smoked
D) Taking anti-inflammatory drugs
E) Receiving regional anesthesia
questions.answer:
C)

Non-smoking status is a well-established patient-related risk factor for postoperative nausea and vomiting. Patients who have never smoked or are non-smokers have a higher likelihood of developing PONV compared to smokers. A) is incorrect because age over 50 years is actually protective against PONV - younger patients (50 years or less) are at higher risk. B) is incorrect because male gender is protective against PONV, while female gender increases the risk. D) is incorrect because anti-inflammatory medications like ibuprofen are not established risk factors for PONV. E) is incorrect because regional anesthesia typically has a lower incidence of PONV compared to general anesthesia with inhalational agents.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient presents following significant weight reduction of 160 pounds (73 kg) through bariatric bypass surgery, requesting body contouring for a more sculpted midsection. Her current BMI measures 29 kg/m2. Clinical assessment reveals redundant skin in both the transverse and longitudinal planes of the abdominal region. Which of the following surgical interventions would most effectively address the aesthetic concerns of this deformity?
A) Belt lipectomy with circumferential excision
B) Corset trunkplasty technique
C) External laser-assisted lipolysis treatment
D) Anterior abdominal liposuction procedure
E) Bariatric bypass surgical revision
questions.answer:
B)
Corset trunkplasty is the optimal choice for addressing both horizontal and vertical skin redundancy following massive weight loss. This technique, developed by A.P. Moya, specifically targets upper abdominal skin laxity that traditional abdominoplasty procedures cannot adequately correct, making it ideal for patients with excess skin in multiple dimensions. A) Belt lipectomy is incorrect because while it provides vertical skin tightening, it fails to address horizontal skin excess adequately. C) External laser lipolysis is incorrect as it is not effective for managing significant skin laxity and redundancy. D) Anterior abdominal liposuction is incorrect because it removes fat but does not provide meaningful skin tightening in post-bariatric patients with substantial skin excess. E) Bariatric bypass revision is incorrect since the patient has achieved successful weight loss with an acceptable BMI of 29, indicating no need for further bariatric intervention.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman presents for cosmetic facial procedures. She is concerned about sagging brows and dynamic wrinkles in the glabellar region. Examination shows brow ptosis, both dynamic and static glabellar rhytids, a tall forehead, and thick hair. Which surgical approach is most appropriate for brow lifting in this patient?
A) Endoscopic
B) Endotemporal
C) Pretrichial
D) Transcoronal
E) Transpalpebral
questions.answer:
C)
The pretrichial technique is the most suitable approach for brow elevation while concurrently reducing forehead height. This is the only method among the choices that can effectively address an excessively tall forehead. A) Endoscopic approach is incorrect because it cannot reduce forehead height and is better suited for patients without forehead length concerns. B) Endotemporal technique is incorrect as it is primarily indicated for patients with thin hair or isolated lateral brow ptosis. D) Transcoronal approach is incorrect because it actually increases forehead height and is preferred for patients with low foreheads and significant rhytids. E) Transpalpebral method is incorrect as it provides limited brow elevation and cannot address forehead length issues.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old woman comes to the clinic after injuring her wrist when she fell on her outstretched hand. Physical examination shows tenderness over the radial aspect of her left wrist and pain in the anatomical snuffbox area. A fracture of the scaphoid bone is suspected. For anteroposterior radiographic views, what is the optimal wrist position to best demonstrate the entire scaphoid bone?
A) 20 degrees radial deviation with 20 degrees wrist extension
B) 20 degrees radial deviation with 20 degrees wrist flexion
C) 20 degrees ulnar deviation with 20 degrees wrist extension
D) 20 degrees ulnar deviation with 20 degrees wrist flexion
E) Neutral radial/ulnar positioning with neutral flexion/extension
questions.answer:
C)
Ulnar deviation paired with wrist extension offers the best positioning to display the scaphoid's long axis on radiographic images. This positioning enhances the diagnostic effectiveness of standard radiographs, which demonstrate roughly 85% sensitivity for identifying scaphoid fractures. A is incorrect because radial deviation blocks optimal scaphoid visualization. B is wrong since radial deviation combined with flexion further compromises scaphoid imaging. D is incorrect as flexion decreases the definition of the scaphoid's longitudinal axis. E is wrong because neutral positioning fails to enhance scaphoid visualization and could overlook subtle fractures.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old man underwent excision of a sarcoma from his chest wall with reconstruction using an anterolateral thigh flap. After receiving external beam radiotherapy, he presents with erythema, edema, and dry desquamation in the treated region. What is the optimal management strategy?
A) Diphenhydramine
B) Hyaluronic acid
C) Hydrocortisone
D) Salicylate
E) Vitamin E
questions.answer:
C)
Hydrocortisone 1% topical preparation, a mild to moderate strength corticosteroid, represents the standard treatment for these acute radiation dermatitis symptoms, along with appropriate skin care measures. This effectively manages the inflammatory cascade responsible for the skin redness, swelling, and peeling. A is wrong because antihistamines such as diphenhydramine lack demonstrated efficacy in treating radiation-induced skin reactions. B is incorrect since hyaluronic acid has been investigated and proven ineffective for radiation dermatitis. D is wrong because salicylate-based treatments provide no established benefit in managing radiation skin toxicity. E is incorrect as vitamin E has been studied and demonstrates no additional therapeutic value in this context.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old woman presents for consultation regarding breast implant removal due to concerns about malignancy. She has specifically researched anaplastic large cell lymphoma in patients with breast implants. She underwent saline breast augmentation 5 years ago. Physical exam reveals no capsular contracture and proper implant placement. What is the most appropriate management strategy?
A) Complete blood count
B) Hematology consultation
C) Breast MRI
D) Implant removal
E) Patient reassurance
questions.answer:
E)
Patient reassurance is the correct approach since breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma is exceedingly uncommon, and the FDA does not advocate for preventive implant removal in asymptomatic patients without clinical abnormalities. The incidence is minimal and most cases present with delayed symptoms such as chronic seroma, discomfort, or breast asymmetry. A is wrong because routine laboratory studies are not warranted for asymptomatic implant patients. B is incorrect since hematology evaluation is only necessary when ALCL is clinically suspected due to presenting symptoms. C is wrong because MRI surveillance is not recommended for asymptomatic patients concerning ALCL risk. D is incorrect as preventive explantation is not endorsed by the FDA for patients lacking symptoms or clinical findings.

questions.question:
According to the Tessier classification for craniofacial clefts, which anatomical region represents the central point of the most commonly encountered facial cleft?
A) Frontonasal junction
B) Frontozygomatic junction
C) Nasomaxillary pillar
D) Upper orbital area
E) Zygomaticotemporal junction
questions.answer:
E)
The Tessier No. 7 cleft, which centers around the zygomaticotemporal junction area, constitutes the most prevalent facial cleft and commonly manifests with different degrees of lateral oral commissure extension and underdevelopment of the zygomatic complex. This numbering system categorizes clefts according to their position relative to the orbital region, with classifications 0-7 affecting the lower facial structures and 9-14 involving the upper facial components. A is incorrect because the frontonasal junction area relates to different, rarer cleft classifications. B is incorrect since the frontozygomatic junction corresponds to a separate cleft category in the system. C is incorrect as the nasomaxillary pillar region pertains to other cleft classifications within the Tessier framework. D is incorrect because the upper orbital region involves cranial facial clefts that occur less frequently than the No. 7 variety.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old male presents for lower lip reconstruction following a blast trauma that resulted in complete destruction of his lower lip. He desires a lower lip that is symmetrical, functional, and provides adequate oral competence. Which of the following surgical approaches is most likely to fulfill the patient's objectives?
A) Innervated anterolateral thigh free flap
B) Innervated gracilis muscle free flap
C) Innervated regional advancement flaps (Karapandzic technique)
D) Prosthetic lower lip device
E) Radial forearm free flap with tendon reconstruction
questions.answer:
B)
The innervated gracilis muscle free flap is the optimal choice for achieving the patient's goals of symmetry, dynamic function, and oral competence in total lower lip reconstruction. This functional muscle flap can provide spontaneous, coordinated movement that closely mimics natural lip function. A) is incorrect because the anterolateral thigh flap, while innervated, would be excessively bulky and lacks the ability to provide dynamic lip movement. C) is incorrect because Karapandzic flaps are not suitable for complete lip loss and would result in severe microstomia (small mouth opening). D) is incorrect because while a prosthetic may provide acceptable static appearance, it cannot deliver functional competence or dynamic movement. E) is incorrect because although a radial forearm flap with tendon graft can achieve reasonable appearance and some competence, it cannot provide the spontaneous, symmetrical movement that a functional muscle flap offers.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman comes to the office for a second opinion because she is displeased with the results of a recent bilateral mastectomy and breast reconstruction with 800-mL high-profile silicone implants. A photograph is shown. BMI is 35 kg/m2. She repeatedly shows pictures of models with augmented breasts and says that she wants her breasts to be ‚Äuperkier.‚Äu She requests augmentation/mastopexy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Augmentation/mastopexy
B) Implant exchange
C) Mastopexy
D) Reassurance
E) Referral to a psychiatrist
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


The most reasonable approach in this patient is to offer reassurance and reset her expectations. A patient with a BMI of 35 kg/m2 who undergoes mastectomy and implant reconstruction will never look like a model with augmented breasts. This patient clearly has misguided expectations. Any surgical intervention is unlikely to produce the result she is looking for, when in fact she has a very acceptable result as is. Referral of this patient to a psychiatrist will likely upset the patient and undermine her trust.


References
1. Pusic AL, Klassen AF, Snell L, et al. Measuring and managing patient expectations for breast reconstruction: impact on quality of life and patient satisfaction. Expert Rev Pharmacoecon Outcomes Res. 2012 Apr;12(2):149-158.
2. Snell L, McCarthy C, Klassen A, et al. Clarifying the expectations of patients undergoing implant breast reconstruction: a qualitative study. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Dec;126(6):1825-1830.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient arrives with a fast-expanding, tender lesion on his left cheek accompanied by left-sided facial muscle weakness. Imaging reveals a left parotid neoplasm surrounding the facial nerve, with no enlarged lymph nodes detected. What is the most suitable surgical approach for managing this condition?
A) Simple tumor removal
B) Limited parotid gland resection
C) Complete parotidectomy with facial nerve sacrifice
D) Parotidectomy of superficial portion only
E) Complete parotid removal while preserving facial nerve
questions.answer:
C)
Radical parotidectomy is the appropriate treatment for this malignant parotid tumor with facial nerve invasion. The presence of pain, rapid growth, and facial weakness indicates malignancy with neural involvement, requiring complete gland removal and facial nerve sacrifice to achieve adequate oncologic resection. A) Simple tumor removal is incorrect because enucleation is contraindicated for malignant tumors and provides inadequate margins. B) Limited parotid gland resection is incorrect as partial parotidectomy would leave residual malignant tissue when the tumor involves the facial nerve. D) Parotidectomy of superficial portion only is incorrect because superficial parotidectomy cannot adequately address a tumor that encases the facial nerve, which runs between superficial and deep portions. E) Complete parotid removal while preserving facial nerve is incorrect because the tumor encases the facial nerve, making nerve preservation impossible while achieving clear margins.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old male patient has surgical removal of a peripheral nerve sheath mass from the median nerve at the left wrist. Meticulous dissection is carried out, and the well-encapsulated mass is successfully excised without complications while maintaining complete motor and sensory function. Histopathological examination reveals a benign neoplasm. Which of the following represents the most probable tumor type in this case?
A) Clear cell sarcoma
B) Fibroma
C) Intraneural perineurioma
D) Neurofibroma
E) Schwannoma
questions.answer:
E)
Schwannoma is the correct answer as it represents the most frequent benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor. These well-encapsulated, slowly progressive tumors originate from Schwann cells and typically allow for complete surgical removal without significant damage to surrounding nerve fascicles or loss of neurological function. A) Clear cell sarcoma is incorrect because it is a rare malignant soft tissue tumor that typically arises from tendons rather than nerve sheaths and would not present as an easily removable encapsulated mass. B) Fibroma is incorrect as these are uncommon benign hand tumors that usually present as dermal nodules rather than nerve sheath tumors. C) Intraneural perineurioma is incorrect because these benign tumors typically cause motor-predominant neuropathy in younger patients and often require nerve repair or grafting after removal. D) Neurofibroma is incorrect because these tumors involve nerve fascicles directly, making complete removal without nerve damage difficult and often requiring subsequent nerve reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 12-month-old infant presents with radial thumb duplication featuring a duplicated distal phalanx (Wassel Type II classification). The surgical plan involves removing the radial thumb and reconstructing the ulnar thumb. Which of the following techniques is most likely to restore thumb stability?
A) Beginning thumb movement 3 days postoperatively
B) Central tissue removal using the Bilhaut-Cloquet technique
C) Converting the index finger to a thumb (pollicization)
D) Reattaching the flexor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis brevis tendons
E) Creating a ligamentous and periosteal flap to reconstruct the radial collateral ligament
questions.answer:
E)
Proper radial collateral ligament reconstruction using a ligamentous and periosteal flap is essential for achieving thumb stability in Types II and IV duplications. The Manske technique involves carefully preserving the radial collateral ligament with its periosteal sleeve when removing the radial thumb, then using this tissue to reconstruct the ligament on the remaining thumb. The periosteal component provides additional length for secure repair. A) is incorrect because early mobilization at 3 days would compromise healing and destabilize the reconstruction - immobilization for 4-6 weeks is standard. B) is incorrect because the Bilhaut-Cloquet procedure involves combining parts of both thumbs rather than removing one completely as described in this case. C) is incorrect because pollicization is unnecessary for Type II duplications since an excellent thumb can be created without sacrificing the index finger. D) is incorrect because these muscles don't require reattachment in Type II duplications since the duplication occurs too distally at the distal phalanx level.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old female patient visits a plastic surgeon expressing dissatisfaction with her "angular jawline" and wants a gentler facial contour without undergoing surgery. Botulinum toxin treatment for her enlarged masseter muscles has been suggested. What should the patient be told regarding the most probable outcome from multiple treatments?
A) She can be reassured that botulinum toxin use for enlarged masseter muscles follows FDA-approved protocols
B) She should prepare to take anti-inflammatory medications for anticipated post-injection headaches
C) She will experience no difficulties with mastication or jaw function following botulinum toxin treatment
D) The size and mass of the masseter muscles will show substantial reduction with botulinum toxin treatments
questions.answer:
D)
Recent research (Shome et al.) showed that following multiple botulinum toxin treatments, masseter muscle volume reduction persisted for up to 4 years, indicating this therapy provides long-lasting rather than temporary effects. Studies measuring masseter volumes before and after treatment demonstrated significant muscle volume reduction (Chang et al.). A) is incorrect because botulinum toxin injection for masseter hypertrophy is currently an off-label application, not FDA-approved for this indication. B) is incorrect because headaches occur infrequently and typically resolve within 2-4 days without requiring preemptive medication. C) is incorrect because research (Peng et al.) found that 30% of patients experienced temporary reduction in chewing strength after botulinum injection.

questions.question:
At what minimum duration does elevated forearm compartment pressure exceeding 30 mmHg result in Volkmann ischemic contracture?
A) Under 2 hours
B) 3-5 hours
C) 6-12 hours
D) 18-24 hours
E) Over 24 hours
questions.answer:
C)
Irreversible neuromuscular damage develops at the 12-hour mark, resulting in Volkmann contracture formation. Experimental studies demonstrate that capillary endothelial injury begins at 3 hours, while muscle and nerve damage that may be partially reversible starts at 6 hours. A is incorrect because damage this early is minimal and reversible. B is incorrect because at 3-5 hours only endothelial damage occurs without permanent contracture. D is incorrect because permanent damage occurs much earlier than 18-24 hours. E is incorrect because contracture develops well before 24 hours of ischemia.

questions.question:
A 4-month-old male infant is brought to the office because of a rapidly enlarging mass in the eyebrow region. The patient‚Äos mother says she first noticed the lesion at 1 month of age and that it was not present at birth. A photograph is shown. Treatment with administration of propranolol is planned. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely in this patient?


A) Adrenal failure
B) Decrease in height
C) Hypertension
D) Hypoglycemia
E) Spastic diplegia
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


First-line treatment of a small problematic infantile hemangioma is intralesional corticosteroid (triamcinolone 3 mg/kg). If the tumor is too large to inject, then oral corticosteroid (prednisolone 3 mg/kg daily) or propranolol is initiated. Interferon is no longer used to treat infantile hemangioma because it may cause spastic diplegia when administered to infants.


The common side effects of propranolol include gastrointestinal effects (vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation), rash, fatigue, and hypersomnia. Severe side effects may include bradycardia, hypotension, chest pain, shortness of breath, bleeding, bronchospasm, and glaucoma. In pediatric patients, propranolol has been associated with hypoglycemia that may occur without the characteristic jitteriness.


Proliferating hemangiomas should not be treated with pulsed-dye laser therapy because accelerated involution does not occur, and patients are at risk for ulceration, pain, bleeding, hypopigmentation, and scarring. The pulsed-dye laser is indicated, however, to treat residual telangiectasias after the tumor has involuted.


Corticosteroid complications (e.g., adverse neurodevelopment, aseptic necrosis of the femoral head, diabetes mellitus, osteoporosis, adrenal insufficiency, cataracts, glaucoma, infection, gastric irritation) have not been observed in patients treated with corticosteroid for infantile hemangioma. Although increased blood pressure has been observed, the clinical significance of this is unclear, and no adverse effects have been reported. Twenty percent of infants develop a temporary cushingoid appearance that disappears during tapering of the medication. Approximately one third of infants exhibit decreased gain in height but return to their growth curve by 24 months of age.


References
1. Greene AK. Current concepts of vascular anomalies. J Craniofac Surg. 2012 Jan;23(1):220-224.
2. Lawley LP, Siegfried E, Todd JL. Propranolol treatment for hemangioma of infancy: risks and recommendations. Pediatr Dermatol. 2009 Sep-Oct;26(5):610-614.
3. Frieden IJ, Drolet BA. Propranolol for infantile hemangiomas: promise, peril, pathogenesis. Pediatr Dermatol. 2009 Sep-Oct;26(5):642-644.
4. Holland KE, Frieden IJ, Frommelt PC, et al. Hypoglycemia in children taking propranolol for the treatment of infantile hemangioma. Arch Dermatol. 2010 Jul;146(7):775-778.

questions.question:
What defines the lateral boundary of the breast footprint?
A) Anterior axillary line
B) Anterior edge of the latissimus dorsi muscle
C) Lateral clavicle
D) Midaxillary line
E) Posterior axillary line
questions.answer:
A)
The anterior axillary line correctly defines the lateral boundary of the breast footprint. The lateral breast tissue is mobile, unlike the fixed inframammary fold, so the footprint may vary slightly and can extend just posterior to the anterior axillary fold, but it does not reach the midaxillary line. B) is incorrect because the breast footprint boundaries are not described in relation to the latissimus dorsi muscle. C) is incorrect because the clavicle is not used to define the breast footprint boundaries. D) is incorrect because the breast footprint does not extend as far laterally as the midaxillary line. E) is incorrect because the posterior axillary line is too far posterior to represent the lateral breast boundary.

questions.question:
An otherwise healthy 32-year-old woman returns to the emergency department because she is unable to use her right hand 20 days after she underwent wound closure for management of a laceration to the hand. A photograph of the patient attempting to make a fist is shown. On examination, there is decreased sensation in the ulnar distribution, and the hand is warm. Which of the following tests is likely to provide the most pertinent information in developing a treatment plan for this patient‚Äos injury?


A) CT angiography
B) Electromyography/nerve conduction study
C) Magnetic resonance angiography
D) Ultrasonography
E) No testing is necessary; physical findings are sufficient
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


The patient described has a significant wrist injury until proven otherwise. Physical examination will be the most helpful in making a determination regarding what should be done next. Electromyography/nerve conduction study typically does not give actionable information until 3 weeks or more after injury. Ultrasonography may be helpful but would not give more information than one could get from a thorough physical examination and would likely be painful as the probe is pressed on the wound. CT angiography can be critical preoperatively if there was a concern regarding inflow. Magnetic resonance angiography would be revealing but would be expensive and unnecessary in this setting.


The patient was taken to the operating room for exploration. Intraoperative and postoperative images are shown.






References
1. Seiler JG III. Flexor tendon injury: acute injuires. In: Wolfe SW, Pederson WC, Hotchkiss RN, Kozin SH, eds. Green‚Äos Operative Hand Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Churchill-Livingstone; 2010:189-206.
2. Birch R. Nerve repair. In: Wolfe SW, Pederson WC, Hotchkiss RN, Kozin SH, eds. Green‚Äos Operative Hand Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Churchill-Livingstone; 2010:1035-1074.
3. Luria, S Bridgeman J, Trumble TE. Anatomy and examination of the hand, wrist, forearm, and elbow. In: Trumble TE, Rayan GM, Baratz M. Principles of Hand Surgery and Therapy. 2nd ed. Philadelphia, PA: Saunders; 2010:1-22.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old female patient is sent by her family doctor to assess a possible intracapsular breach of her left breast implant detected on routine mammographic screening. She had initial breast augmentation surgery with subglandular positioning of single-chamber silicone implants in 1990. Clinical examination reveals reduced volume of the left breast. MRI imaging is ordered. Which of the following MRI findings would most strongly support this diagnosis?
A) Double wall sign
B) Linguine sign
C) Multiple echogenic lines
D) Reverse double-lumen sign
E) Snowstorm sign
questions.answer:
B)

The linguine sign is the most characteristic MRI finding for intracapsular silicone implant rupture, representing the collapsed implant shell floating within leaked silicone gel. MRI demonstrates superior sensitivity and specificity compared to other imaging modalities for detecting silicone implant failure. A) Double wall sign is incorrect because this radiographic finding (Rigler sign) indicates pneumoperitoneum, not implant rupture. C) Multiple echogenic lines is incorrect because this is an ultrasound finding, not an MRI sign. D) Reverse double-lumen sign is incorrect because this would not occur in single-chamber devices and is associated with double-lumen implants. E) Snowstorm sign is incorrect because this appears on ultrasound examination, not MRI.

questions.question:
A patient seeks evaluation for reconstructing a saddle nose deformity after nasal injury. Structural framework for dorsal enhancement and nasal elongation is needed. Which of the following is most prone to causing secondary nasal asymmetry in the immediate postoperative phase?
A) Synthetic implant material
B) Cantilevered rib bone graft
C) Cantilevered skull bone graft
D) Sculpted rib cartilage graft
E) Minced cartilage graft
questions.answer:
D)
Sculpted rib cartilage graft is most likely to cause secondary nasal asymmetry due to its inherent tendency to warp postoperatively, despite providing excellent structural support for both dorsal augmentation and nasal lengthening. A) Synthetic implant material is incorrect because while it can cause complications like infection or extrusion, warping and asymmetry are not primary concerns. B) Cantilevered rib bone graft is incorrect as bone grafts are more susceptible to resorption rather than warping-related asymmetry. C) Cantilevered skull bone graft is incorrect for the same reason as rib bone - resorption is the main concern, not warping. E) Minced cartilage graft is incorrect because these grafts are malleable and actually allow for correction of minor asymmetries, plus they don't provide structural support for lengthening.

questions.question:
An 11-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a fingertip injury to his left middle finger during a baseball game. The middle fingertip remains in a bent position. The proximal portion of the nail is slightly visible above the cuticle fold, and there is a small collection of blood under the nail. Radiographic imaging is provided. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Closed reduction with splinting of the distal interphalangeal joint in extension for 6 to 8 weeks
B) Closed reduction with nail plate removal and percutaneous pin placement
C) Open reduction with nail bed repair and Kirschner wire stabilization
D) Surgical repair of zone I flexor tendon rupture
E) Wound closure with sutures and monitoring for 6 weeks
questions.answer:
C)
This patient presents with a Seymour fracture, which is an open growth plate or near-growth plate fracture of the terminal phalanx. These injuries appear similar to mallet finger deformities but are classified as open fractures. The optimal treatment involves open reduction, cleaning of the fracture area, repair of the associated nail bed tear, and Kirschner wire stabilization across the distal interphalangeal joint. This injury results from excessive bending and represents a Salter I or II fracture of the distal phalanx. The bent position occurs because the extensor tendon attaches to the back part of the growth plate, while the deep flexor tendon attaches to the bone fragment beyond the fracture. Nail bed tissue often becomes trapped between bone fragments, preventing proper closed reduction and requiring surgical repair. A) is incorrect because closed reduction and splinting alone cannot address the interposed nail bed tissue and open nature of this fracture. B) is incorrect because closed reduction techniques have high rates of infection and poor outcomes in Seymour fractures due to the open fracture pattern. D) is incorrect because zone I flexor tendon avulsion (jersey finger) would cause the finger to be stuck in extension, not flexion as seen here. E) is incorrect because simple wound repair without addressing the underlying fracture and nail bed injury would lead to poor healing and deformity.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old man needs total glossectomy for cancer treatment. A microvascular anterolateral thigh free flap reconstruction is planned. After making a vertical thigh incision, no perforating vessels are found between the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis muscles. When examining the medial thigh region, a large perforator is located between the rectus femoris and vastus medialis muscles. What is the most likely origin of this perforating vessel?
A) Ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery
B) Common femoral artery
C) Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery
D) Medial circumflex femoral artery
E) Profunda femoris artery
questions.answer:
C)
The descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery is the most probable origin of this anteromedial thigh perforator. In cases where typical ALT flap perforators are missing (which happens in roughly 5% of patients), anteromedial thigh perforators are present in approximately 50% of instances and usually arise from the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery via a branch that supplies the rectus femoris muscle. This enables surgeons to utilize an anteromedial thigh (AMT) flap as an alternative approach. A is wrong because the ascending branch provides blood supply to tensor fasciae latae flaps rather than anteromedial thigh perforators. B is wrong since the common femoral artery is not known to be a source for established cutaneous perforator flaps. D is wrong because the medial circumflex femoral artery does not provide blood supply to recognized perforator flaps. E is wrong as the profunda femoris artery is not an established source for cutaneous perforator flaps.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old right-handed man presents for management of a biopsy-proven subungual melanoma in situ affecting his right thumb. Which treatment option is most appropriate?
A) Amputation at the interphalangeal joint without reconstruction
B) Amputation at the metacarpophalangeal joint with toe-to-thumb reconstruction
C) Systemic chemotherapy
D) Radiotherapy
E) Wide local excision with split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
E)
Wide local excision with split-thickness skin graft represents the optimal treatment for subungual melanoma in situ. Current evidence demonstrates that melanoma in situ can be successfully treated with wide local excision alone, substantially decreasing morbidity when compared to amputation techniques. This finger-preserving method maintains hand function while providing appropriate oncologic margins. A is wrong because amputation represents excessive treatment for in situ melanoma and causes substantial functional impairment. B is wrong as it involves more extensive amputation with complicated reconstruction that is unjustified for non-invasive disease. C is wrong because systemic chemotherapy has no proven benefit in melanoma in situ treatment. D is wrong since radiation therapy is not a suitable primary intervention for this diagnosis.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old woman comes to the emergency department 5 days after sustaining a cat bite to the left index finger. A photograph is shown. Medical history includes diabetes mellitus type 1. Physical examination shows punctures to the dorsum and volar surfaces of the proximal phalanx, mild fusiform swelling of the digit with tenderness over the flexor tendon sheath, pain with passive extension, and partially flexed posture of the digit. The symptoms have worsened over the past 3 days. Temperature is 99¬∞F (37.2¬∞C). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Incision and drainage of the puncture sites
B) Inpatient intravenous antibiotics
C) Irrigation of the flexor sheath
D) Outpatient oral antibiotics
E) Splinting immobilization and elevation
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.




The most appropriate option for this patient is to proceed to the operating room for decompression/drainage of the flexor tendon sheath. This patient has all four of Kanavel‚Äos signs, specifically pain on passive extension, fusiform swelling, flexor tendon sheath tenderness, and flexion of the affected digit. These point towards a diagnosis of flexor tenosynovitis, with the cause being the cat bite she sustained several days prior. Although cat bites only reflect 5% of all animal bites, they represent 76% of all infected bites, thought to be because of the morphology of their long teeth, which simulate a deep puncture wound.


Outcomes studies demonstrate that because of this patient‚Äos diabetes, she is at risk for a poor outcome, specifically the need for amputation and/or decreased total active motion. Other risk factors that can lead to these outcomes include age greater than 43 years, presence of subcutaneous purulence, digital ischemia, and polymicrobial infection. Given that she is at risk and that she has all four Kanavel‚Äos signs, any intervention that is more conservative than operative decompression and drainage may lead to suboptimal outcomes.


Administration of antibiotics (orally or intravenously) is not a substitute for drainage of the flexor sheath, especially in a case that presents more than 48 hours out from initiation of symptoms. Drainage in the emergency department is not as optimal as in the operating room given that the infection may limit efficacy of local anesthesia as well as the need for possible conversion to an open drainage procedure if closed catheter irrigation is insufficient.


References
1. Pang HN, Teoh LC, Yam AK, et al. Factors affecting the prognosis of pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2007 Aug;89(8):1742-1748.
2. Kanavel AB. The symptoms, signs, and diagnosis of tenosynovitis and major fascial space abscesses. In: Kanavel AB, ed. Infections of the Hand. 6th ed. Philadelphia: Lea and Febiger; 1933:364-395.
3. Malahias M, Jordan D, Hughes O, et al. Bite injuries to the hand: microbiology, virology and management. Open Orthop J. 2014 Jun 27;8:157-161. eCollection 2014.
4. Gutowski KA, Ochoa O, Adams WP Jr. Closed-catheter irrigation is as effective as open drainage for treatment of pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis. Ann Plast Surg. 2002 Oct;49(4):350-354.

questions.question:
A 44-year-old man presents with a 20-degree extension contracture of the wrist secondary to burn scar formation. A Z-plasty procedure is planned to release the contracture. Which of the following options (A-D) shows the ideal placement of the central limb for this surgical approach?
A) (see image above)
B) (see image above)
C) (see image above)
D) (see image above)
questions.answer:
A)

The central limb of a Z-plasty must be aligned parallel to the direction of greatest tension for optimal contracture correction. With this extension deformity, the primary tension runs longitudinally, requiring the central limb to be positioned in a longitudinal orientation to maximize tissue elongation and scar release. The Z-plasty functions by redistributing forces through tissue transposition, using the central limb as the rotational axis for the triangular flap advancement. Option B is incorrect because it places the central limb perpendicular to the tension vector, reducing effectiveness. Option C is incorrect as it positions the central limb at an oblique angle that doesn't optimize tension release. Option D is incorrect because it fails to align with the primary direction of contracture forces, limiting the degree of correction achievable.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old girl with a complete unilateral cleft affecting the lip, alveolus, and palate is missing her lateral incisor on the cleft side. After secondary alveolar bone grafting has been completed, what is the most appropriate prosthetic treatment for restoring this missing tooth?
A) Nasoalveolar molding appliance
B) Dental implant with crown restoration
C) Palatal obturator prosthesis
D) Removable partial denture
E) Fixed bridge with three units
questions.answer:
B)
A dental implant with crown restoration is the ideal prosthetic solution for replacing a single missing tooth following alveolar bone grafting. The grafted bone provides sufficient support for placing a titanium implant, which delivers excellent aesthetics, function, and durability. This approach has emerged as the preferred standard for single tooth replacement in cleft patients because of its permanent nature and outstanding clinical results. A is wrong because nasoalveolar molding is performed in infancy prior to initial lip surgery, not for tooth replacement. C is wrong since palatal obturators are designed to close oronasal communications, not replace missing teeth. D is wrong because removable partial dentures cause tissue irritation, have poor retention, and serve only as temporary measures. E is wrong since fixed bridges require cutting down healthy neighboring teeth and need eventual replacement, making them less suitable for young patients.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old girl diagnosed with velocardiofacial syndrome exhibits severe velopharyngeal insufficiency. A superiorly based pharyngeal flap procedure is under consideration. What factor is most crucial for determining the optimal flap width?
A) Capacity to repair the pharyngeal donor site defect
B) Movement of the lateral pharyngeal walls
C) Soft palate length
D) Palatal mobility (coronal movement)
E) Location of carotid arteries in the posterior pharyngeal wall
questions.answer:
B)

Movement of the lateral pharyngeal walls is the most crucial factor for determining pharyngeal flap width. The flap establishes a static connection between the soft palate and posterior pharyngeal wall, so the extent of lateral wall movement dictates how much central blockage is required to achieve proper velopharyngeal closure while preserving adequate lateral openings for nasal airflow. Inadequate flap width combined with good lateral wall movement may lead to ongoing VPI, whereas excessive width paired with limited lateral wall movement may cause obstructive sleep apnea. A is incorrect because donor site repair, though advantageous for healing, is not essential and does not impact flap width determination. C is incorrect since soft palate length does not dictate the necessary flap width for this static reconstruction. D is incorrect because palatal mobility does not influence the width requirements for this static surgical approach. E is incorrect because although carotid artery location is important for surgical safety, it does not determine the functional width specifications.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old male patient presents with a complete scalp defect after melanoma excision. Histopathology confirms negative margins. Which of the following factors necessitates flap reconstruction rather than skin grafting for defect closure?
A) Hair loss in adjacent tissue
B) Visible bone surface
C) Granulating wound base
D) Preserved pericranial layer
E) Occipital positioning
questions.answer:
B)
Visible bone surface requires flap coverage because exposed bone lacks sufficient vascularity to support skin graft survival. A) Hair loss in adjacent tissue is incorrect because this actually reduces cosmetic concerns with reconstruction methods that don't restore hair growth. C) Granulating wound base is incorrect because granulation tissue indicates good vascularization that can support skin graft take. D) Preserved pericranial layer is incorrect because intact pericranium provides adequate blood supply for successful skin grafting. E) Occipital positioning is incorrect because anatomical location doesn't determine the requirement for vascularized tissue coverage.

questions.question:
A 3-year-old female patient with congenital right trigeminal nerve dysfunction presents with recurring corneal ulcers in the right eye. Clinical assessment reveals complete loss of sensation throughout the right V1 nerve distribution area. The right cornea lacks sensation and shows multiple regions of mild ulceration. Which procedure would be most effective in maintaining visual function in this patient's right eye?
A) Corneal reinnervation using sural nerve graft from contralateral supratrochlear nerve
B) Corneal grafting procedure
C) Same-side supratrochlear to ophthalmic nerve transfer
D) Laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) surgery
E) Surgical eyelid closure
questions.answer:
A)
Corneal reinnervation using sural nerve graft from the contralateral supratrochlear nerve is correct because neurotrophic keratitis from trigeminal dysfunction requires restoration of corneal sensation to prevent ongoing ulceration and preserve vision. This procedure redirects functioning nerve fibers from the unaffected side via a nerve graft to reestablish corneal innervation, which can reverse neurotrophic changes and restore normal corneal structure. B is incorrect because corneal grafting without restoring sensation typically fails as transplanted tissue becomes ulcerated due to continued lack of protective sensation. C is incorrect because using the ipsilateral supratrochlear nerve is ineffective when the entire trigeminal system on that side is non-functional. D is incorrect because LASIK only reshapes corneal tissue for refractive correction and does not address the underlying sensory deficit. E is incorrect because surgical eyelid closure in young children can cause deprivation amblyopia and permanent vision impairment.

questions.question:
When performing aesthetic facial analysis, the face is typically divided into which of the following proportional segments?
A) Equal horizontal thirds and vertical thirds
B) Equal horizontal fifths and vertical thirds
C) Equal horizontal thirds and vertical fifths
D) Equal horizontal fifths and vertical fifths
E) No standardized proportional divisions exist for facial analysis
questions.answer:
C)

Facial aesthetic analysis utilizes a systematic approach that divides the face into equal horizontal thirds and vertical fifths. The facial height is segmented into three equal horizontal divisions: the upper third spans from the hairline to the eyebrows/glabella, the middle third extends from the glabella to the base of the nose (subnasale), and the lower third reaches from the subnasale to the chin (menton). The facial width is partitioned into five equal vertical segments using vertical lines drawn through the medial and lateral canthi of both eyes, with each segment approximating the width of one eye opening. A is incorrect because it uses thirds for both dimensions rather than fifths for width. B is incorrect because it reverses the proportions, using fifths for height instead of thirds. D is incorrect because it applies fifths to both height and width rather than thirds for height. E is incorrect because standardized proportional analysis methods do exist and are widely used in aesthetic facial evaluation.

questions.question:
A newborn female presents with a large intraoral mass arising from alveolar mucosa of the lower jaw that does not cause any airway obstruction. Photographs are shown. Which of the following is the most likely pathology of the lesion?


A) Congenital epulis
B) Hemangiopericytoma
C) Odontogenic keratocyst
D) Rhabdomyosarcoma
E) Teratoma
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


Congenital epulis is a rare, benign tumor of the oral cavity that is found in newborns. They are considered a form of granular cell tumor that can lead to mechanical obstruction, resulting in respiratory distress or difficulty eating. Surgical excision is the treatment of choice and recurrence after excision is rare. The female-to-male ratio is 10:1. It is observed three times more frequently on the maxilla than the mandible. They are solitary in most cases, but can be large and multiple.

Teratomas and rhabdomyosarcomas of the mandible are even more rare and are usually seen in the older patient population; they are not seen in the neonatal population.

Hemangiopericytomas are rare, vascular neoplasms that originate from vascular pericytes. They can occur anywhere in the body, including the mandible. They are slow-growing and present in the older patient population. The likelihood of presentation in a neonate is exceedingly low.

Odontogenic keratocysts are rare and benign, but locally aggressive lesions of the posterior mandible. They most commonly present in the third decade of life. They make up 19% of jaw cysts.


ReferencesGoldblum JR, Folpe AL, Weiss SW, eds. Enzinger and Weiss's Soft Tissue Tumors. 6th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Elsevier Saunders; 2014:845.Husain AN, Stocker JT, Dehner LP, eds. Stocker and Dehner's Pediatric Pathology. 4th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Wolters Kluwer; 2016:1027.

questions.question:
What constitutes a Type I error in statistical hypothesis testing?
A) Accepting the alternative hypothesis when it is correct
B) Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is false
C) Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is true
D) Rejecting the alternative hypothesis when it is correct
E) Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true
questions.answer:
E)
A Type I error occurs when we reject the null hypothesis despite it being true. This represents a false positive result in hypothesis testing. A) is incorrect because accepting a true alternative hypothesis is the correct decision. B) is incorrect because this describes a Type II error (false negative). C) is incorrect because failing to reject a true null hypothesis is the correct decision. D) is incorrect because rejecting a true alternative hypothesis would be accepting a false null hypothesis, which is a Type II error scenario.

questions.question:
A 75-year-old female patient presents for assessment of a newly discovered skin growth on her right upper eyelid. Histopathological analysis of the biopsy specimen reveals a 1-cm Merkel cell carcinoma. Along with regional lymph node evaluation, what represents the most suitable surgical excision approach and adjuvant treatment for this patient?
A) 1-cm surgical margins with chemotherapy
B) 2-cm surgical margins with chemotherapy
C) 1-cm surgical margins with postoperative radiotherapy
D) 2-cm surgical margins with postoperative radiotherapy
E) 5-mm surgical margins with postoperative radiotherapy
questions.answer:
C)
Merkel cell carcinoma is an aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy that typically affects elderly, immunocompromised individuals in sun-exposed regions. For primary tumors less than 2 cm in diameter, the standard surgical margin recommendation is 1 cm for wide local excision. Given the radiosensitive nature of Merkel cell carcinoma, adjuvant radiation therapy following surgery has demonstrated efficacy in reducing local recurrence rates. A) is incorrect because chemotherapy is reserved for palliative care and metastatic disease, not primary treatment. B) is incorrect because 2-cm margins are excessive for tumors under 2 cm and chemotherapy is not indicated for primary treatment. D) is incorrect because 2-cm margins are unnecessarily wide for this tumor size. E) is incorrect because 5-mm margins are inadequate for proper oncologic resection of Merkel cell carcinoma.

questions.question:
Which patient has the greatest likelihood of being unsatisfied with their surgical results?
A) A 25-year-old male with significant loose skin after losing 100 pounds (45 kg) seeking body contouring procedures
B) A 35-year-old female seeking facial cosmetic surgery to help her career advancement as a television news reporter
C) A 42-year-old female presenting with a prominent nasal hump and wide nasal tip desiring aesthetic improvement
D) A 45-year-old mother of three children with severe breast deflation and sagging seeking enhanced appearance
E) A mother bringing her 3-year-old daughter for removal of a large birthmark
questions.answer:
B)
Patients who tie surgical success to achieving specific external goals like career advancement represent a psychological contraindication to cosmetic surgery and are at highest risk for dissatisfaction regardless of technical outcomes. A is incorrect because this patient has a clear, correctable anatomical problem with realistic expectations after significant weight loss. C is incorrect because this represents identifiable nasal deformities that can be surgically addressed with appropriate expectations. D is incorrect because post-pregnancy breast changes are well-defined problems with predictable surgical solutions. E is incorrect because congenital nevi removal addresses a legitimate medical and aesthetic concern in a pediatric patient.

questions.question:
What protein is produced by the gene that is altered in van der Woude syndrome and popliteal pterygium syndrome?
A) Fibroblast growth factor 10 (FGF10)
B) Fibroblast growth factor receptor 2b (FGFR2b)
C) Interferon regulatory factor 6 (IRF6)
D) Membrane-bound signaling molecule jagged 2 (JAG2)
E) Sonic hedgehog (SHH)
questions.answer:
C)
Interferon regulatory factor 6 (IRF6) is the correct answer because mutations in the IRF6 gene are directly responsible for causing both van der Woude syndrome and popliteal pterygium syndrome. IRF6 plays a crucial role in controlling periderm differentiation during palatal development and has been consistently linked to both syndromic and non-syndromic forms of cleft lip and palate across multiple populations and ethnic groups. A) FGF10 is incorrect because while it is involved in craniofacial development, it is not the gene mutated in these specific syndromes. B) FGFR2b is incorrect as it is associated with other craniosynostosis syndromes but not van der Woude or popliteal pterygium syndromes. D) JAG2 is incorrect because although it plays an important role in palatal shelf formation by controlling periderm differentiation, it is not the gene mutated in these syndromes. E) SHH is incorrect as it is involved in various developmental processes but is not the causative gene for van der Woude or popliteal pterygium syndromes.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents with drooping eyebrows and wrinkles around the eyes and receives botulinum toxin type A (BOTOX Cosmetic) treatment. Administration of BOTOX Cosmetic into which of the following muscles would most likely cause elevation of the outer portion of the eyebrow?
A) Corrugator supercilii
B) Depressor supercilii
C) Frontalis
D) Orbicularis oculi
E) Procerus
questions.answer:
D)
Administering BOTOX Cosmetic into the orbicularis oculi muscle is most likely to produce lateral eyebrow elevation. The orbicularis oculi functions as a lateral eyebrow depressor, opposing the elevating action of the frontalis muscle. When botulinum toxin weakens the orbicularis oculi, it eliminates this downward pull, allowing the frontalis muscle to elevate the lateral brow unopposed. A) Corrugator supercilii is incorrect because this muscle primarily depresses the medial brow, not the lateral brow. B) Depressor supercilii is incorrect as it also acts on the medial brow region rather than the lateral aspect. C) Frontalis is incorrect because injecting this muscle would weaken brow elevation rather than enhance it, since it is the primary brow elevator. E) Procerus is incorrect because it depresses the medial brow area and would not significantly affect lateral brow position.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with numbness and tingling sensations affecting the front outer portion of his tongue, which began following surgical extraction of his lower wisdom teeth 3 weeks prior. Which of the following nerve structures was most likely damaged?
A) Chorda tympani
B) Facial
C) Glossopharyngeal
D) Hypoglossal
E) Lingual
questions.answer:
E)
The lingual nerve provides general sensory innervation to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and is a branch of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve, making it susceptible to injury during mandibular third molar extraction. A) Chorda tympani is incorrect because it carries taste fibers rather than general sensation and travels with the lingual nerve. B) Facial nerve is incorrect because it provides motor innervation to facial muscles and taste sensation via the chorda tympani, not general sensation to the tongue. C) Glossopharyngeal nerve is incorrect because it innervates the posterior third of the tongue, not the anterior portion described. D) Hypoglossal nerve is incorrect because it provides motor innervation to the tongue muscles, not sensory innervation.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old individual, assigned female at birth, presents with male gender identity and seeks chest masculinization surgery. The patient has C-cup breast volume with moderate nipple ptosis (grade 2). What surgical approach would be most suitable?
A) Liposuction alone
B) Periareolar reduction technique
C) Vertical scar reduction method
D) Anchor-pattern reduction procedure
E) Complete mastectomy with nipple-areolar complex free graft
questions.answer:
E)
Complete mastectomy with nipple-areolar complex free graft is the optimal choice for this patient given the substantial breast volume and significant ptosis present. This technique provides the most masculine chest contour by removing all breast tissue and excess skin while repositioning the nipple-areolar complex to an appropriate male position. For transgender male patients with larger breasts and ptosis, this approach yields superior aesthetic outcomes compared to other methods. A) Liposuction alone is insufficient because it cannot address the excess skin envelope or achieve adequate tissue removal for masculinization. B) Periareolar reduction is inadequate for C-cup breasts with ptosis, as it has limited capacity for tissue and skin removal. C) Vertical scar reduction maintains breast projection and creates a feminine shape, which is inappropriate for masculinization goals. D) Anchor-pattern reduction similarly preserves breast mound shape and feminine contours, making it unsuitable for gender-affirming chest reconstruction.

questions.question:
An 11-year-old healthy boy presents to the emergency department with increasing erythema and discomfort at the site of a finger injury. He injured his left middle finger 3 weeks earlier during play-wrestling with his sibling. Initially there was swelling and tenderness of the digit, but the discomfort subsided rapidly and no medical attention was obtained. His mother notes that afterward she observed a small protrusion on the back of the finger. Two days ago the child developed redness and pain at the same location, which have progressively worsened. On examination, the distal phalanx is swollen and tender with a flexed posture of the fingertip, the proximal edge of the nail plate lies superficial to the eponychial fold, and purulent drainage is expressed from beneath the nail fold. Plain films of the digit demonstrate a transverse juxta-epiphyseal fracture at the base of the distal phalanx with dorsal apex angulation, along with periosteal reaction and lucency within the distal phalanx. What is the most probable etiology of this patient's current presentation?
A) Nail biting habits
B) Contact with Pasteurella organisms
C) Avulsion of the flexor tendon
D) Compromised immune system
E) Entrapped nail bed tissue
questions.answer:
E)
This patient has a Seymour fracture, a juxta-epiphyseal open fracture of the distal phalanx characterized by disruption of the eponychial fold with the nail plate displaced superficial to it, a mallet-like flexed fingertip posture, and a transverse physeal or juxta-physeal fracture at the base of the distal phalanx. These injuries are open fractures because the nail bed (germinal matrix) is lacerated and frequently becomes interposed within the fracture site. Because the injury was untreated, the interposed germinal matrix maintained a communication between the fracture and the external environment, leading to persistent contamination and secondary osteomyelitis, evidenced by periosteal reaction and bony lucency. Entrapped nail bed tissue is therefore the primary cause of the current infection and requires nail plate removal, irrigation and debridement, extraction of the interposed matrix, fracture reduction, nail bed repair, and antibiotics. A) Nail biting typically causes a nontraumatic paronychia rather than post-traumatic osteomyelitis following a fracture, and does not explain the fracture pattern. B) Pasteurella species are associated with animal bites, not with a wrestling injury; Staphylococcus aureus is the most common organism in infected Seymour fractures. C) Flexor digitorum profundus avulsion (jersey finger) is a closed injury that presents with inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and does not produce an open juxta-epiphyseal fracture with nail fold disruption. D) There is no evidence of immunocompromise; healthy children readily develop infection when an open physeal fracture with interposed soft tissue is left untreated.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old female patient is brought to the clinic by her family physician for evaluation of uneven breast development. She states that her right breast has been consistently smaller throughout development. Clinical assessment reveals slightly shortened digits on the right hand and a Tanner stage III right breast. The left breast demonstrates Tanner stage IV development with no palpable abnormalities. What is the Mathes and Nahai Classification for the muscle primarily affected in this congenital condition?
A) Type I
B) Type II
C) Type III
D) Type IV
E) Type V
questions.answer:
E)
The pectoralis major muscle receives blood supply from both a primary dominant vessel (pectoral branches from the thoracoacromial artery) and secondary segmental perforating vessels (internal mammary/thoracic perforators), making it a Type V muscle according to the Mathes and Nahai classification. The clinical presentation of pectoralis major absence combined with hand abnormalities is characteristic of Poland syndrome, which results from suspected vascular disruption during fetal development. Type I is incorrect because these muscles have only a single dominant blood supply. Type II is incorrect as these muscles have one dominant and one minor vascular pedicle. Type III is incorrect because these muscles have two dominant pedicles. Type IV is incorrect as these muscles rely solely on segmental blood supply without dominant vessels.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female presents to the clinic 10 years following subglandular placement of textured silicone breast implants for cosmetic breast enlargement. On examination, there is swelling of the left breast. She expresses concern about malignancy. Which of the following cancers has an increased association with breast implants?
A) Acute myelogenous leukemia
B) Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
C) Angiosarcoma
D) Invasive ductal carcinoma
E) Malignant fibrous histiocytoma
questions.answer:
B)
Anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) represents the correct answer as multiple studies have documented an association between breast implants and this rare malignancy. ALCL typically develops years after implant placement, presenting as breast swelling or a mass around the prosthesis, frequently accompanied by periprosthetic fluid collection. Treatment approaches include complete capsule removal with implant extraction and chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy, though standardized treatment protocols remain undefined. While the relative risk of ALCL is elevated in breast implant recipients, the absolute risk remains exceptionally low. Most reported cases have involved textured implants. A) is incorrect because acute myelogenous leukemia may be linked to breast radiation therapy but has no established connection to breast implants. C) is incorrect because angiosarcoma, while it can occur in breast tissue and may be radiation-induced, has not been associated with breast implants. D) is incorrect because large epidemiological studies show similar or reduced rates of invasive ductal carcinoma in patients with breast implants compared to those without. E) is incorrect because malignant fibrous histiocytoma, though it can arise in breast tissue, has no documented association with breast implants.

questions.question:
A patient undergoes breast reconstruction using a free TRAM flap procedure. The axillary vessels are exposed through dissection, and microsurgical anastomosis is completed under operating microscope visualization. While harvesting the flap, an umbilical hernia is discovered and surgically corrected. The TRAM flap is then shaped and positioned to create the reconstructed breast, followed by abdominal closure. Beyond code 19364 (breast reconstruction with free flap), what additional Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) coding is most appropriate for this case?
A) 15847 (abdominoplasty)
B) 49585 (repair of umbilical hernia, reducible)
C) 49585 (repair of umbilical hernia, reducible), 15847 (abdominoplasty), and 69990 (use of operating microscope)
D) 69990 (use of operating microscope)
E) No additional coding is necessary
questions.answer:
B)
The appropriate additional code is 49585 for umbilical hernia repair. The free TRAM flap reconstruction code 19364 is comprehensive and includes flap harvesting, microvascular transfer, donor site closure, and breast shaping/inset. However, repair of an incidentally discovered hernia is not included in this bundled code and can be reported separately. A) is incorrect because abdominoplasty is already included in the donor site closure component of 19364. C) is incorrect because while hernia repair can be coded separately, abdominoplasty and microscope use are already bundled into 19364. D) is incorrect because CPT specifically prohibits separate billing for operating microscope use with microvascular procedures like free flap reconstruction. E) is incorrect because the hernia repair represents additional work not included in the primary reconstruction code.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old female presents for evaluation of thoracic wall and mammary asymmetry. Her medical history includes pectus excavatum treated surgically in childhood with corrective bar placement, which was removed after 3 years. Following bar removal, she has observed gradual return of her chest wall abnormality accompanied by breast asymmetry. Clinical examination reveals a slender patient with a 4-cm deep depression at the lower sternal region and medial displacement of the right breast. The patient reports no dyspnea or thoracic discomfort. Which of the following therapeutic approaches would be the most suitable recommendation for aesthetic enhancement?
A) Autologous adipose tissue grafting to the sternal depression and right breast
B) Custom silicone elastomer implant placement with simultaneous breast augmentation
C) Injectable delivery of cultured autologous chondrocytes
D) Bilateral breast implant insertion using implants exceeding 550 cc
E) Corrective bar re-placement with sternal wire fixation
questions.answer:
B)
Custom silicone elastomer implant placement with simultaneous breast augmentation is the most appropriate treatment. In female patients with pectus excavatum, the primary aesthetic concern stems from the thoracic concavity rather than actual breast tissue deficiency. Custom sternal prostheses combined with breast augmentation provide reliable and consistent correction of both the chest wall deformity and associated breast asymmetry, with studies demonstrating this combined approach to be both safe and effective. A is incorrect because autologous fat grafting between the tight presternal adhesions is technically difficult and often unsuccessful. C is incorrect because injectable chondrocyte therapy remains experimental and unproven for soft tissue defects. D is incorrect because breast implants alone cannot address the underlying chest wall concavity, which is the primary source of the deformity. E is incorrect because corrective bar reinsertion is typically unsuccessful in post-adolescent patients with ossified bones and is reserved only for severe cases.

questions.question:
A 67-year-old man comes to the office because of a mass over his left palm that has grown rapidly during the past month. He reports that the mass has bled several times, although he does not recall trauma. Physical examination shows a 5 √o 8-mm, lobulated, reddish purple mass. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?


A) Hemangioma
B) Malignant melanoma
C) Merkel cell carcinoma
D) Pyogenic granuloma
E) Squamous cell carcinoma
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Pyogenic granulomas are benign vascular tumors of unknown etiology. These lesions grow rapidly and can easily bleed with little or no trauma. Because of these characteristics, they are often confused with a malignancy. Although trauma is sometimes associated with these lesions, over three quarters of cases have no history of trauma or any other predisposing factor. They have also been associated with pregnancy. Their differential diagnosis includes malignancies such as basal or squamous cell carcinoma or malignant melanoma, as well as other vascular-type anomalies.


Treatment of pyogenic granulomas often consists of a shave removal and cauterization. For recurrent or large lesions, surgical excision is recommended.


Hemangiomas are benign, vascular tumors that occur in children, usually in the limbs or trunk. Despite their vascular origin, hemangiomas do not metastasize or undergo malignant transformation. With age, growth of hemangiomas will slow and in many cases regress by age 5 to 7 years.


Malignant melanomas represent one of the most aggressive forms of skin cancers. Generally, these are pigmented, although an amelanotic or melanotic variance may occur.


Merkel cell carcinomas are a rare, aggressive skin cancer usually appearing as a flesh-colored or bluish red nodule on the face, head, or neck. These appear mostly in elderly patients. Merkel cell carcinoma is of a neuroendocrine origin in the skin.


Squamous cell carcinomas are the second most frequent type of skin cancer. This type of lesion can be present on the hand, especially in patients with a history of radiation exposure. They generally present as a broad, flat lesion with the appearance of a scab. The most common areas for these are sun-exposed areas, such as the face and the back of the hand.


References
Walsh JJ IV, Eady JL. Vascular tumors. Hand Clin. 2004 Aug;20(3):261-268, v-vi.
Pantanowitz L, Duke WH. Intravascular lesions of the hand. Diagn Pathol. 2008 May 30;3:24.
Quitkin HM, Rosenwasser MP, Strauch RJ. Efficacy of silver nitrate cauterization for pyogenic granuloma of the hand. J Hand Surg. 2003 May;28(3):435-438.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old woman presents 1 week following exchange of tissue expander for permanent implant, in which skin glue was used for closure. She reports an itchy rash around her incision. Medical history includes right breast cancer, for which she has undergone mastectomy and placement of a pre-pectoral textured tissue expander with acellular dermal allograft coverage. She is afebrile. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this rash?


A) Anaplastic large-cell lymphoma infiltration of the skin
B) Antiphospholipid antibody-mediated urticaria
C) Cyanoacrylate exposure and dermatitis
D) Lymphatic disruption leading to red breast syndrome
E) Staphylococcus aureus cellulitis
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


The patient has recently had surgery and is doing well except for her skin rash. The rash appears to be localized to the incision. Contact dermatitis to surgical adhesives is a common problem. There is growing recognition that surgical glues containing cyanoacrylate may be associated with a 10 to 15% rate of rashes secondary to Type IV allergic hypersensitivity reactions. These typically appear within 3 to 7 days and are treated by removal of the surgical glue and topical steroid cream. Patients who have previously been exposed to surgical glue are more at risk for developing sensitivity.


Surgical site infection is a concern following implant placement. However, a Staph cellulitis is typically more diffuse and has a different appearance more consistent with erythema rather than a rash. Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) may be associated with a rash and other systemic symptoms; however, there is no indication within the history that this patient suffers from that condition. Additionally, the timing and location of the rash along the incision point to other local causes rather than APS. Lymphatic disruption is one theory to explain red breast syndrome, which is a condition that has been reported in relation to acellular dermal matrix placement. This is typically more diffuse and usually occurs in the acute setting following acellular dermal matrix placement. Anaplastic large-cell lymphoma is a rare type of cancer that may be associated with breast implants and may present with swelling and a rash. There is a higher rate of this condition in patients who have had textured devices. The mean onset for this condition is 8 years after exposure to the breast implant. This patient‚Äos clinical course is not typical of anaplastic large cell lymphoma.


ReferencesNigro LC, Parkerson J, Nunley J, et al. Should we stick with surgical glues? the incidence of dermatitis after 2-octyl cyanoacrylate exposure in 102 consecutive breast cases. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2020;145(1):32-37.Nakagawa S, Uda H, Sarukawa S, et al. Contact dermatitis caused by Dermabond Advanced use. Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open. 2018;6(9):e1841.

questions.question:
A 2-year-old boy comes to the clinic for evaluation of a droopy eyelid on one side. Clinical examination shows 2-mm ptosis of the right upper eyelid with 7-mm levator function and no obstruction of the visual axis. The left eye examination is unremarkable. What is the best management strategy for this child?
A) Frontalis sling procedure
B) Upper eyelid skin excision
C) Levator muscle resection
D) Müller muscle-conjunctival resection (Fasanella-Servat procedure)
E) Observation with follow-up evaluation at age 3 years
questions.answer:
E)
The best management approach is observation with re-examination at 3 years of age. Surgical intervention for mild to moderate ptosis in very young children should be deferred until the child can cooperate with preoperative assessment and postoperative management, which is not possible in a 2-year-old. Surgery before age 3 is only indicated when there is substantial visual field compromise. A is incorrect because frontalis sling procedures are reserved for cases with poor levator function (less than 4 mm). B is incorrect because simple skin removal does not adequately address eyelid malposition. C is incorrect because although levator resection works well in pediatric cases with good levator function, it should be postponed until the child is more mature. D is incorrect because this technique is not the preferred initial approach for this degree of ptosis without visual impairment.

questions.question:
An 83-year-old woman comes to the office for repair of a deep sternal wound infection after undergoing open single-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting using the left inferior mammary artery. Medical history includes cancer of the left breast for which she underwent wide excision with oncoplastic reconstruction followed by adjuvant radiation therapy to the breast and axilla. She does not smoke cigarettes. The patient's infection resolves with aggressive debridement and culture-guided antibiotics. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate reconstructive option?


A) Left pectoralis turnover flap coverage with skin graft resurfacing
B) Left vertical rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap coverage
C) Right latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap coverage
D) Right pectoralis advancement flap with skin readvancement closure
E) Right vertical rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap coverage
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.



Deep sternal wound infections represent life-threatening infections whose most frequent etiology in contemporary cases is surgical site infection following open heart surgery, with a reported incidence of 0.2 to 3% of patients undergoing median sternotomy. Risk factors in adults include diabetes mellitus, obesity, peripheral arterial disease, tobacco use, reoperation, and other surgical complications such as prolonged operative time and postoperative bleeding. Published mortality rates range from 8.1 to 14.8%. Once a diagnosis is made, initial treatment in cases of deep infection typically involve a combination of antimicrobial therapy and staged surgical debridement followed by delayed closure.


Sternotomy wounds can be complex problems because of their proximity to heart and lungs and exposure of these vital organs following debridement. Principles of reconstruction once a healthy wound bed has been obtained include durable coverage of vital structures with obliteration of dead space with a view to retaining or restoring optimal form and function.


In the case scenario described, a right superiorly based rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap provides the most reliable, well vascularized and non-irradiated option for regional soft tissue reconstruction of the composite chest wall defect (shown). A left vertical rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap is suboptimal in the setting of a relatively compromised superior epigastric vascular pedicle in the setting of known sacrifice of its parent left internal mammary artery (IMA). Latissimus and pectoralis flaps in any form are less reliable in their ability to fully cover inferior third sternectomy defects. While a turnover pectoralis flap can reach the inferior sternum, a left pectoralis turnover flap is furthermore less reliable in the setting of known sacrifice of its inferior segmental internal mammary perforators in the setting of known IMA sacrifice. Skin re-advancement in the setting of prior radiation and distorted perfusion from prior reduction mammoplasty also invites further unnecessary risk.


References
Davison SP, Clemens MW, Armstrong D, Newton ED, Swartz W. Sternotomy wounds: rectus flap versus modified pectoral reconstruction. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2007;120(4):929-34.
Risnes I, Abdelnoor M, Almdahl SM, Svennevig JL. Mediastinitis after coronary artery bypass grafting risk factors and long-term survival. Ann Thorac Surg. 2010;89(5):1502-9.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old woman in good health with a family history of heart conditions has tumescent liposuction performed on her sides, legs, and belly. Six hours after being sent home, she arrives at the ER experiencing trouble speaking and restlessness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A) Embolism from fat particles
B) Anesthetic agent poisoning
C) Brain tissue death from lack of blood
D) Blockage in lung blood vessels
E) Body fluid shifting
questions.answer:
B)
The most probable diagnosis is toxicity from lidocaine. When using the tumescent method with epinephrine, lidocaine levels in the blood reach their highest point 10-14 hours following injection, making the 6-hour timeframe consistent with increasing drug concentrations in the bloodstream. Initial lidocaine poisoning manifests with nervous system symptoms such as difficulty speaking, restlessness, ear ringing, and metallic taste sensation. A is wrong because fat embolism syndrome usually develops 24-48 hours after surgery with characteristic skin petechiae, respiratory distress, and altered mental status. C is wrong because cerebral strokes typically cause sensory loss, perceptual disturbances, and spatial disorientation instead of speech problems and agitation. D is wrong because pulmonary embolism manifests with lower extremity symptoms, tachycardia, and hyperthermia.
