E is wrong because third-space fluid shifts result in edema, hypotension, and decreased cardiac output.

questions.question:
In which anatomical layer do scalp avulsions most commonly occur?
A) Aponeurotic galea
B) Loose areolar tissue
C) Pericranium
D) Skin and dermal layers
E) Subcutaneous fat layer
questions.answer:
B)
Scalp separations predominantly occur within the loose areolar connective tissue plane. The scalp's layered structure can be remembered by SCALP: skin, connective tissue (subcutaneous), aponeurosis (galea), loose areolar tissue, and pericranium. The first three layers function as a cohesive unit, while the loose areolar plane forms a natural cleavage point from the pericranium, facilitating scalp movement and creating space for hematoma formation. A is incorrect because the galea functions as a structural layer that moves with the overlying tissues. C is incorrect because the pericranium maintains firm attachment to the underlying bone. D is incorrect because the skin layers move as part of the unified superficial complex. E is incorrect because the subcutaneous tissue is integrated with the superficial moving unit.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman requests cosmetic breast enhancement. The decline in which hormone level is most directly responsible for breast tissue atrophy following menopause?
A) Estrogen
B) Growth hormone
C) Oxytocin
D) Prolactin
E) Testosterone
questions.answer:
A)
Estrogen is the key hormone whose reduction causes postmenopausal breast atrophy. Estrogen serves as the principal hormone driving breast ductal proliferation and epithelial development, collaborating with progesterone to control mammary growth. Following menopause, both estrogen and progesterone concentrations drop dramatically, resulting in involution and shrinkage of mammary glandular structures. B is incorrect because growth hormone does not play a central role in female mammary gland physiology. C is incorrect because oxytocin functions in milk letdown during nursing, not in mammary development or regression. D is incorrect because prolactin mainly controls lactogenesis during breastfeeding. E is incorrect because while testosterone may influence mammary tissue, it is not the dominant hormone controlling female breast physiology.

questions.question:
When coding evaluation and management services, what is the minimum number of months that must pass without professional services from a plastic surgeon in the same group practice for a patient to be classified as 'new'?
A) 6
B) 12
C) 18
D) 24
E) 36
questions.answer:
E)
Based on AMA CPT coding standards, a patient is classified as new when they have not received any professional services from a physician or qualified healthcare provider of the same specialty and subspecialty within the same group practice during the preceding 36 months (three years). When a patient has received professional services (including E/M visits or face-to-face procedures) within this three-year window from the same specialty provider in the practice, they must be coded as an established patient. A is wrong because 6 months falls far short of the three-year standard. B is wrong because 12 months represents only one year, not the required three. C is wrong because 18 months equals only one and a half years, insufficient for the three-year rule. D is wrong because 24 months represents two years, which still does not satisfy the three-year requirement.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old boy has had the lesion of the right index finger shown in the photograph since birth. The lesion has been growing in proportion to his overall growth. On physical examination, there is no thrill or bruit. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?


A) Arteriovenous malformation
B) Hemangioma
C) Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
D) Lymphatic malformation
E) Port-wine stain
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.






In 1982, Mulliken and Glowacki proposed a binary classification system for vascular anomalies based on pathologic features. This system divides vascular anomalies into two primary biological categories: 1) vasoproliferative or vascular neoplasms and 2) vascular malformations.


Vasoproliferative neoplasms, such as hemangioma and Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma, have increased endothelial cell turnover (i.e., they proliferate and undergo mitosis) because they are neoplasms. Vascular malformations do not have increased endothelial cell turnover. Instead, vascular malformations are structural abnormalities of the capillary, venous, lymphatic, and arterial systems that grow in proportion to the child.


The lesion shown in the photographs grew in proportion to the child; therefore, it is a malformation, not a vasoproliferative neoplasm. Given the absence of a bruit or thrill, it is unlikely to be an arteriovenous malformation; therefore, a slow-flow lesion such as a lymphatic malformation is the most likely diagnosis.


Although a port-wine stain is a type of venous malformation, it is characterized by its very superficial location, which causes the skin to be discolored red (hence the name). Such findings are not present in the photographs shown.


References
1. Lowe LH, Marchant TC, Rivard DC, Scherbel AJ. Vascular malformations: classification and terminology the radiologist needs to know. Semin Roentgenol. 2012 Apr;47(2):106-117.
2. Weibel L. Vascular anomalies in children. Vasa. 2011 Nov;40(6):439-447.

questions.question:
During which phase of wound healing does collagen production reach its peak?
A) Collagen production maintains steady levels across all healing phases
B) Collagen production does not occur during wound healing
C) Inflammatory phase
D) Proliferative phase
E) Maturation phase
questions.answer:
D)

The proliferative phase is characterized by peak collagen production during wound healing. This phase unfolds in two separate stages, beginning with fibrin and fibronectin deposition in the early proliferative period. By approximately day three of healing, fibroblasts arrive at the wound location and begin collagen synthesis. The proliferative phase ends at 2-4 weeks when collagen accumulation reaches its maximum and remodeling begins, leading into the maturation phase. A is incorrect because collagen deposition fluctuates dramatically across different phases, reaching maximum levels during proliferation. B is incorrect because collagen production is essential to wound healing and continues throughout the repair process. C is incorrect because the inflammatory phase is dominated by immune cell infiltration (neutrophils, macrophages, lymphocytes) rather than substantial collagen synthesis. E is incorrect because the maturation phase emphasizes transforming type III to type I collagen and enhancing cross-linking rather than maximum synthesis.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old patient exhibits a whistling abnormality after undergoing bilateral cleft lip reconstruction at 6 months of age. Physical examination shows interrupted orbicularis oris muscle continuity across the lip, dried encrusted tissue on the vermillion margin of the whistling defect, and nasolabial fistulous tracts. A revisional cleft lip surgery is planned to repair the musculature, close the nasolabial fistulas, and correct the whistling abnormality. Which Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code most accurately represents this operative intervention?
A) 40650 (Repair lip, full-thickness; vermillion only)
B) 40652 (Repair lip, up to half of vertical height)
C) 40654 (Repair lip, over one-half vertical height, or complex)
D) 40701 (Primary bilateral lip repair, one-stage procedure)
E) 40720 (Secondary lip repair, by recreation of the defect and reclosure)
questions.answer:
E)

Code 40720 is the most suitable choice because extensive revision of all lip structures requires recreating the defect and performing comprehensive reconstruction. This methodology enables concurrent repair of the nasolabial fistulous tracts, whistling abnormality, and orbicularis oris muscle continuity across the lip. A is wrong because repair limited to vermillion tissue would not correct the muscle disruption or nasolabial fistulas. B is wrong because partial lip reconstruction would be inadequate for the comprehensive repair needed. C is wrong because even complex repair involving more than half the vertical dimension would not cover all the required corrections. D is wrong because this case involves a secondary revision procedure rather than an initial bilateral repair.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old man with significant cranial injuries and extensive maxillofacial fractures sustained in a motor vehicle collision 14 days ago is intubated and receiving enteral nutrition via feeding tube. Indirect calorimetry shows a respiratory quotient (RQ) of 1.3. This finding most directly suggests which of the following metabolic activities?
A) Glucose oxidation
B) Ketogenesis
C) Lipid oxidation
D) Lipogenesis
E) Amino acid catabolism
questions.answer:
D)
An RQ of 1.3 signifies active lipogenesis (fat production from excess nutrients). Indirect calorimetry determines the ratio of carbon dioxide output (VCO2) to oxygen uptake (VO2), with typical RQ ranges of 0.8-0.9 reflecting normal mixed substrate utilization. When RQ exceeds 1.0, it indicates nutritional excess, and a value of 1.3 specifically demonstrates substantial overfeeding with conversion of surplus carbohydrates to fatty acids, warranting caloric reduction based on actual metabolic requirements. A is incorrect because glucose oxidation alone yields an RQ of 1.0, not 1.3. B is incorrect because ketone formation is not reflected in RQ measurements. C is incorrect because fat oxidation results in an RQ of approximately 0.7. E is incorrect because protein breakdown produces an RQ near 0.8.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old man comes to the clinic with enlargement of both breasts that began 7 years prior. Physical exam shows bilateral breast tissue growth with normal testicular examination. His body mass index is 27 kg/m². What is the most reliable approach for distinguishing genuine gynecomastia from pseudogynecomastia in this case?
A) Review of drug history
B) Blood work evaluation
C) Mammography
D) MRI scanning
E) Physical examination
questions.answer:
E)
Physical examination remains the most reliable method for distinguishing genuine gynecomastia from pseudogynecomastia. True gynecomastia involves palpable, dense glandular tissue located beneath the areolar region, whereas pseudogynecomastia consists only of soft adipose tissue distributed throughout the breast area without subareolar glandular tissue. Pseudogynecomastia commonly develops in patients with excess weight due to fat accumulation rather than actual glandular growth. A is incorrect because reviewing medications can identify potential triggers but cannot determine tissue composition. B is incorrect because blood tests may uncover underlying conditions but do not differentiate between glandular and fatty tissue. C is incorrect because mammography is not routinely used for gynecomastia assessment and cannot substitute for hands-on examination findings. D is incorrect because MRI is typically reserved for cases where malignancy is suspected, not for routine classification of gynecomastia subtypes.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old man sustained Zone II laceration to the left long finger, which severed both flexor tendons. A photograph is shown. Primary repair was performed with a 3-0 cruciate core suture within 2 weeks of injury. He is scheduled to undergo rehabilitation with active motion protocol. Compared with passive motion protocols, an active motion protocol is most likely to present which of the following risk factors and outcomes?


A) Equal risk of rupture and equal final range of motion
B) Higher risk of rupture and decreased final range of motion
C) Higher risk of rupture and increased final range of motion
D) Lower risk of rupture and decreased final range of motion
E) Lower risk of rupture and increased final range of motion
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Many techniques for primary flexor tendon repair have been described. All methods involve a core suture to bear the load of the repair with or without an epitendinous suture. Multiple studies have shown that more strands crossing the repair site and/or larger diameter of each strand increases the strength of the repair. Two-strand repairs cannot withstand early active rehabilitation protocols; repairs of four strands or greater, including a cruciate repair as done in the patient above, can tolerate an early active motion rehabilitation protocol.


Trumble and Seiler‚Äos studies compare passive motion protocols and active motion protocols to each other for risk of rupture and incidence of deceased range of motion at final measurement. Both studies identified active motion protocols incurred a higher occurrence of rupture but a lower incidence of decreased range of motion compared with the passive protocols.


References
Seiler JG 3rd. Flexor tendon Injuries: Acute Injuries. In: Wolfe SW, Hotchkiss RN, Pederson WC, Kozin SH, eds. Green‚Äos Operative Hand Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2011:189-207.
Starr HM, Snoddy M, Hammond KE, Seiler JG 3rd. Flexor tendon repair rehabilitation protocols: a systematic review. J Hand Surg. 2013;38A:1712-17.
Trumble TE, Vedder NB, Seiler JG 3rd, Hanel DP, Diao E, Pettrone S. Zone-II flexor tendon repair: a randomized prospective trial of active place-and-hold therapy compared with passive motion therapy. J Bone

questions.question:
What surgical technique for hypertrophic inferior turbinates best preserves mucosal function while achieving optimal clinical outcomes?
A) Electric cautery
B) Laser tissue ablation
C) Turbinectomy with partial resection
D) Submucous tissue excision
E) Lateral turbinate repositioning
questions.answer:
D)

Submucous tissue excision achieves excellent symptom resolution while maintaining mucosal integrity by excising the underlying bony and soft tissue structures while preserving the surface mucosa. This approach maximally improves nasal breathing while uniquely maintaining mucociliary transport and glandular secretion capabilities. The turbinate's essential functions of air conditioning and humidification are retained through mucosal preservation. A is incorrect because electric cautery damages tissue and creates scarring without durable results while compromising mucosal function. B is incorrect because laser tissue ablation also causes thermal injury and fibrosis without providing sustained benefit. C is incorrect because turbinectomy with partial resection achieves durable symptom control but eliminates mucosal function and carries increased morbidity. E is incorrect because lateral turbinate repositioning lacks robust evidence for sustained efficacy, with more than half of patients developing symptom recurrence within months.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male undergoes resection of the distal right femur due to osteosarcoma. A large allograft corticocancellous bone graft is used to reconstruct the 10-cm skeletal defect. An intramedullary vascularized fibular free flap is also integrated into the reconstruction. What is the most likely rationale for this additional procedure?
A) Decrease the allograft's immunogenic response
B) Lower the risk of infection
C) Improve creeping substitution within the allograft
D) Increase the immediate mechanical stability of the reconstruction
E) Accelerate bone healing time
questions.answer:
E)
The primary rationale for adding an intramedullary fibular free flap to the allograft reconstruction is to accelerate bone healing time. Vascularized fibular flaps contain living bone cells and maintain their blood supply, offering osteogenic potential through osteoinduction as an alternative to the allograft. This biological advantage significantly shortens healing time compared to allografts, which depend solely on the slow process of creeping substitution. Fibular flaps can achieve union in as little as 3 to 5 months, while large allografts typically heal slowly and incompletely with union times of 14 to 23 months for intercalary reconstructions. A is incorrect because the fibular flap does not alter the immunogenic characteristics of the allograft material. B is incorrect because infection risk is primarily related to the avascular nature of the allograft itself, not the medullary space. C is incorrect because the fibular flap does not modify the creeping substitution process occurring in the allograft. D is incorrect because although the fibula provides some structural support, mechanical reinforcement is not the main indication in this clinical context.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old man undergoes fasciectomy for Dupuytren disease affecting the left ring finger. During dissection, the ulnar digital nerve is noted to be centrally displaced on the ring finger by a Dupuytren cord. A photograph is shown. Which of the following palmar fascia structures contributes to the formation of this cord? 


A ) Central band
B ) Cleland ligament
C ) Lateral digital sheet
D ) Natatory ligament
E ) Septa of Legueu and Juvara
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Except for Cleland ligament, any of the above named structures can become involved in Dupuytren contracture. Once involved in a contracture, the name of the structure is changed to include ?cord? (e.g., natatory ligament becomes natatory cord).


A spiral cord is formed when Dupuytren disease affects the pretendinous band, spiral band, lateral digital sheet, and Grayson ligament. The normal palmar fascia structures pass around the neurovascular bundle in a spiral fashion. As the cord forms and contracts, it eventually becomes straight. The neurovascular bundle is then displaced centrally on the digit and is distorted to spiral around the cord.


References
1. Hettiaratchy S, Tonkin MA, Edmunds IA. Spiralling of the neurovascular bundle in Dupuytren‚Äos disease. J Hand Surg Eur Vol. 2010 Feb;35(2):103-108.
2. Rayan GM. Clinical presentation and types of Dupuytren‚Äos disease. Hand Clin. 1999 Feb;15(1):87-96, vii.

questions.question:
Based on systematic evidence analysis, what represents the most appropriate preoperative guidance for women with standard breast cancer risk who are having breast reduction surgery?
A) Annual mammographic screening for women aged 45 to 54 years
B) Biennial breast MRI screening for women above 55 years of age
C) BRCA gene mutation testing
D) Establish baseline mammography for women above 30 years of age
E) Screening using breast thermography
questions.answer:
A)

The American Cancer Society's 2015 evidence-based recommendations for women undergoing breast reduction include: 1) annual screening for women 45-54 years old; 2) biennial screening for women 55 and older; 3) women 40-44 may opt to start annual screening; 4) clinical breast examination is not advised for cancer detection and monitoring. B is wrong because biennial MRI screening is not advised for average-risk women over 55. C is wrong because BRCA testing is designated for high-risk hereditary cases, not standard-risk patients. D is wrong because obtaining baseline mammography at 30 is not included in evidence-based recommendations for average-risk women. E is wrong because thermography is not utilized for screening standard-risk patients.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old healthy woman receives tumescent liposuction for thigh contouring. The procedure involves administering lidocaine at a maximum dose of 55 mg/kg through tumescent infiltration, followed by fat removal using a 4-mm blunt cannula. What is the expected percentage of local anesthetic that will be removed in the aspirate?
A) 20%
B) 50%
C) 70%
D) 90%
questions.answer:
A)

While evidence indicates that lidocaine doses up to 55 mg/kg may be administered safely during liposuction procedures, the safety profile appears more related to tissue blood supply than to the amount of anesthetic removed during aspiration. Studies indicate that roughly 10 to 30% of the local anesthetic appears in the aspirated material, with research showing an average of 9.8% of the infiltrated solution being extracted. Recognizing that the majority of tumescent fluid remains in the tissues is important since lidocaine toxicity remains a concern after tumescent liposuction. B is incorrect because 50% substantially overestimates the anesthetic removal rate. C is incorrect because 70% dramatically overestimates the aspirated amount. D is incorrect because 90% extremely overestimates the local anesthetic percentage in the aspirate.

questions.question:
A 70-year-old man is recovering in the post-anesthesia care unit after undergoing radial forearm free flap reconstruction for squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue. His medical history includes a 30-pack-year tobacco use history, and he is currently on mechanical ventilation through a tracheostomy. On postoperative day 2, sedation is held for one hour to assess readiness for ventilator weaning. During this time, he develops agitation and confusion. Which drug should be contraindicated in this patient during his postoperative recovery?
A) Albuterol
B) Diphenhydramine
C) Neostigmine
D) Propranolol
E) Varenicline
questions.answer:
B)

Postoperative delirium represents an acute alteration in brain function marked by fluctuating consciousness, impaired attention, and cognitive disorganization. It may manifest as hyperactive symptoms (agitation, combativeness) or hypoactive features (withdrawal, reduced responsiveness). This complication occurs in 60-80% of critically ill ventilated patients and 20-50% of hospitalized patients with moderate illness severity. In patients susceptible to postoperative delirium, antihistamines and benzodiazepines should be avoided since these agents can precipitate or intensify delirious episodes. A is incorrect because albuterol is a beta-2 agonist bronchodilator that does not typically contribute to delirium development. C is incorrect because neostigmine is an anticholinesterase agent used for neuromuscular blockade reversal and is not known to worsen delirium. D is incorrect because propranolol is a non-selective beta-blocker that does not aggravate delirious states. E is incorrect because varenicline is a nicotinic receptor partial agonist for smoking cessation that is not particularly problematic in postoperative delirium.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old woman comes to the office with persistent right wrist pain that responds well to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications. Radiographic images are consistent with osteoid osteoma. What imaging modality would best establish the presumed diagnosis?
A) Nuclear bone scintigraphy
B) Computed tomography
C) Fluorescence laser angiography
D) MR arthrography
E) Ultrasound examination
questions.answer:
B)

Osteoid osteoma represents a benign osteoblastic bone neoplasm characterized by focal pain at the tumor location. Research demonstrates that computed tomography serves as the superior imaging modality for identifying this lesion. CT provides excellent visualization of the nidus, which appears as the typical radiolucent zone characteristic of this tumor. The radiolucent nidus frequently contains a central hyperdense focus, indicating calcified osteoid matrix. A is incorrect because nuclear bone scans can identify increased uptake but lack specificity and cannot definitively establish the diagnosis. C is incorrect because fluorescence laser angiography evaluates soft tissue blood flow and cannot reliably assess bone structures or deeper anatomical regions. D is incorrect because although MR arthrography might identify intra-articular osteoid osteomas, these locations are rare, and MRI demonstrates lower sensitivity compared to CT for nidus detection. E is incorrect because ultrasound cannot sufficiently penetrate cortical bone to visualize this intracortical pathology.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old female presents for discussion about left breast reconstruction following mastectomy for breast cancer treatment. Post-surgical chemotherapy and radiation are scheduled. She currently wears a 34D bra. Her height is 5 ft 6 in (168 cm) and weight is 160 lb (73 kg), with a BMI of 25.8 kg/m2. She prefers to avoid abdominal scarring. Autologous reconstruction using a transverse musculocutaneous gracilis (TMG) flap is being considered. What represents a limitation of the TMG flap for this patient's reconstruction?
A) Complex harvesting technique
B) Significant donor site complications
C) Elevated fat necrosis risk
D) Limited tissue volume
E) Inconsistent blood supply
questions.answer:
D)
The TMG flap's primary limitation is its restricted tissue volume, making it most suitable for small to medium-sized breast reconstruction. The largest reported flap weighed only 420g and measured 30 × 10 cm, which may be insufficient for reconstructing a 34D breast. A is incorrect because TMG flap harvest is actually straightforward and rapid, typically completed within 30 minutes. B is incorrect because functional donor site morbidity is low with this technique. C is incorrect because the TMG flap has reliable perfusion with low rates of fat necrosis. E is incorrect because the TMG flap is known for its constant and reliable vascular anatomy, which is one of its major advantages.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old male patient has revision ventral hernia repair surgery. His medical background includes inadequately managed type 1 diabetes and hepatic transplantation performed 3 years previously. The surgical procedure lasts 6 hours and involves complicated extensive adhesiolysis. On postoperative day 3, the patient develops oliguria and low blood pressure that persists despite fluid replacement with crystalloids and colloids. Intrinsic kidney failure is suspected. When examining serum and urine electrolyte values, which of the following parameters would be expected to remain normal in this patient with intrinsic renal failure?
A) BUN:serum creatinine ratio
B) Fractional excretion of sodium (FENa)
C) Urinalysis
D) Urinary sodium concentration
E) Urine osmolality
questions.answer:
A)
The BUN to serum creatinine ratio remains normal in intrinsic renal failure because both BUN and creatinine are elevated proportionally, maintaining their typical ratio. In intrinsic renal failure, the kidney's filtering and concentrating abilities are impaired at the parenchymal level, but the ratio between these two waste products stays within normal limits. B) is incorrect because FENa is typically elevated above 1% in intrinsic renal failure due to impaired tubular sodium reabsorption. C) is incorrect because the urinalysis shows abnormalities such as proteinuria, hematuria, or cellular casts in intrinsic renal failure. D) is incorrect because urinary sodium concentration is elevated above 40 mEq/L in intrinsic renal failure due to decreased tubular reabsorption capacity. E) is incorrect because urine osmolality is reduced below 350 mOsmol/kg H2O in intrinsic renal failure due to impaired concentrating ability.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient has right-sided breast carcinoma and is considering a nipple-preserving mastectomy with tissue expander insertion. She has expressed particular interest in a CO2-filled expander system. What represents a limitation of this type of device when compared to a saline-filled tissue expander?
A) Device extrusion
B) Cannot be deflated
C) Higher rate of wound separation
D) Elevated infection risk
E) Risk of implant displacement
questions.answer:
B)
The CO2-based tissue expander (AeroForm) represents a fixed-volume system that cannot be deflated once activated. In contrast to saline expanders which can be adjusted by removing fluid, the carbon dioxide system lacks this flexibility for volume reduction. A is incorrect because extrusion rates showed no significant difference between CO2 and saline expanders in clinical trials. C is incorrect because wound dehiscence rates were comparable between both expander types. D is incorrect because infection rates were statistically similar for both devices. E is incorrect because device displacement occurred at similar frequencies in both expander systems.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old female patient is sent by her speech pathologist due to ongoing nasal airflow during speech production. She had cleft palate reconstruction performed during her first year of life. Clinical assessment reveals an elongated, flexible soft palate. No opening or hole is observed. Nasal endoscopy demonstrates adequate midline closure but limited movement of the lateral pharyngeal walls. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Enhancement of Passavant's ridge
B) Ongoing speech pathology intervention
C) Placement of a palatal elevation device
D) Posterior pharyngeal wall flap procedure
E) Pharyngeal sphincter reconstruction
questions.answer:
E)
The patient presents with velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI), where inadequate closure between the soft palate and pharyngeal walls results in nasal air leakage during speech. At 4 years old, surgical intervention is warranted since speech therapy alone cannot resolve the anatomical deficiency. The endoscopic findings show good central closure with poor lateral wall movement, indicating lateral port gaps that are best addressed by sphincter pharyngoplasty. This procedure creates bilateral muscle-containing flaps from the posterior tonsillar pillars that are positioned on the posterior pharyngeal wall, effectively narrowing the lateral openings while preserving central airflow for breathing. A) Enhancement of Passavant's ridge is incorrect because it addresses central closure, but this patient already has adequate midline closure. B) Continued speech therapy is incorrect because anatomical VPI requires surgical correction, and speech therapy alone cannot overcome the structural deficiency. C) Palatal lift prosthesis is incorrect because it is primarily indicated for patients with minimal velopharyngeal movement, whereas this patient has good palatal mobility. D) Posterior pharyngeal flap is incorrect because it primarily addresses central gaps, but this patient's main problem is lateral port incompetence with adequate central closure.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old female patient is presented to the clinic by her parent due to the onset of breast development. The parent reports no significant medical history for the child. Her height measures 4 ft 2 in (127 cm, 50th percentile) and weight is 55 lb (25 kg, 50th percentile). Clinical examination reveals current breast development equivalent to a B cup. There is an absence of pubic hair growth or vaginal mucosal changes. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Benign premature thelarche
B) Cushing syndrome
C) Gynecomastia
D) McCune-Albright syndrome
E) Precocious puberty
questions.answer:
A)
Benign premature thelarche is the correct diagnosis because the patient shows isolated breast development without other signs of pubertal progression (no pubic hair or vaginal changes), which is characteristic of this benign condition that requires no treatment. B) Cushing syndrome is incorrect because this condition typically presents with weight gain, growth retardation, and other systemic features not present in this patient. C) Gynecomastia is incorrect because this term refers to breast tissue enlargement in males, not females. D) McCune-Albright syndrome is incorrect because this condition usually presents with precocious menstruation before breast development, along with bone abnormalities and café-au-lait spots that are not described here. E) Precocious puberty is incorrect because true precocious puberty involves multiple pubertal changes occurring simultaneously, whereas this patient only shows breast development without other pubertal signs.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male patient has undergone hemimandibulectomy with fibular flap reconstruction for treatment of oral squamous cell carcinoma. Four days after surgery, he develops a cough and malaise. His vital signs show: temperature 39.4°C (102°F), blood pressure 80/40 mmHg, pulse 120 bpm, and respirations 32/min. Physical examination reveals normal-appearing surgical sites. IV fluid resuscitation has been started immediately. Blood cultures have been obtained and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics have been given. What is the most appropriate next management step?
A) Providing additional fluid resuscitation using hydroxyethyl starch
B) Starting low-dose dopamine for kidney protection
C) Obtaining serum lactate measurement
D) Tailoring antibiotic therapy according to culture findings
E) Inserting a pulmonary artery catheter
questions.answer:
C)
Obtaining serum lactate measurement is the most appropriate next management step for this patient who is developing sepsis/septic shock postoperatively. According to the 2018 Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle guidelines, lactate measurement is a critical early intervention that should be performed immediately upon recognition of sepsis, as it serves as a surrogate marker for tissue hypoperfusion and guides resuscitation efforts. Studies have shown that lactate-guided resuscitation significantly reduces mortality. A is incorrect because hydroxyethyl starch is contraindicated in sepsis due to increased mortality risk compared to other fluids. B is incorrect because low-dose dopamine for renal protection is not recommended due to lack of evidence supporting its efficacy. D is incorrect because culture results would not be available during this early phase of management. E is incorrect because routine pulmonary artery catheter placement is not recommended as it lacks evidence for improving outcomes in septic patients.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old male presents for evaluation of complete high radial nerve paralysis 12 months following a gunshot injury to his upper arm that resulted in total radial nerve severance. Tendon transfer procedures are being planned to restore extension of the wrist and fingers. Which of the following transfer options would be most suitable for this patient?
A) Brachioradialis to extensor indicis proprius
B) Flexor carpi radialis to extensor digitorum communis
C) Palmaris longus to extensor pollicis brevis
D) Pronator quadratus to extensor carpi radialis brevis
questions.answer:
B)

Tendon transfer procedures for complete high radial nerve injuries are typically performed within weeks following injury to restore wrist and finger extension function. When available, the palmaris longus is transferred to the extensor pollicis longus to provide thumb extension capability. The flexor carpi radialis is transferred to the extensor digitorum communis to restore finger extension. The pronator teres is transferred to the extensor carpi radialis brevis to support wrist extension. Option A is incorrect because the brachioradialis typically has insufficient strength in high radial nerve palsy and the extensor indicis proprius does not require a separate transfer since the extensor digitorum communis will provide extension to all fingers including the index. Option C is incorrect because the extensor pollicis brevis does not typically receive a tendon transfer as thumb metacarpophalangeal joint extension is usually restored through transfer to the extensor pollicis longus. Option D is incorrect because the pronator quadratus is not utilized for wrist extension transfers and cannot reach the extensor carpi radialis brevis.

questions.question:
A 13-year-old male presents with his mother due to breast enlargement that has developed over the last 3 months. He is at the 50th percentile for both height and weight with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities other than moderately severe bilateral symmetric breast tissue enlargement. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A) Liposuction procedure
B) Hepatic function testing
C) Watchful waiting with reassessment in 12 months
D) Surgical removal
E) Ultrasound of the testicles
questions.answer:
C)
Watchful waiting with reassessment in 12 months is most appropriate because three months represents a relatively brief period for gynecomastia development, and pubertal gynecomastia commonly resolves spontaneously within the first year. Expert recommendations suggest waiting 12 months before considering surgical intervention when no other concerning findings are present. A is incorrect because liposuction is premature at this early stage when spontaneous resolution is likely. B is incorrect because liver function tests are not indicated without clinical history or physical findings suggesting hepatic disease. D is incorrect because surgical excision should be reserved for cases that persist beyond 12 months or have other concerning features. E is incorrect because testicular ultrasonography is unnecessary in typical pubertal gynecomastia without other clinical indicators of testicular pathology.

questions.question:
A 66-year-old male patient with paraplegia presents for assessment of a Grade IV pressure sore that has persisted for 6 months. His medical background includes several surgical debridements along with proper pressure relief and adequate wound management. The patient demonstrates no clinical progress. Chronic bone infection is suspected. What is the most suitable next diagnostic approach?
A) Bone biopsy
B) CT scan
C) Dual energy x-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scan
D) MRI
E) Triphasic technetium scan
questions.answer:
A)
Bone biopsy represents the gold standard for diagnosing chronic osteomyelitis in persistent wounds. This procedure provides both histopathologic and microbiologic information that offers high sensitivity and specificity for chronic bone infection. B) is incorrect because CT scans, while useful for detecting osteolysis and gas collections, lack specificity in chronic wounds and can be misleading due to previous surgical interventions. C) is incorrect because DEXA scanning measures bone density for osteoporosis assessment and has no diagnostic value for osteomyelitis. D) is incorrect because MRI, despite its anatomical detail, lacks specificity for osteomyelitis in the setting of chronic soft tissue injury and prior debridements. E) is incorrect because triphasic technetium bone scans assess bone metabolism but are not specific enough for osteomyelitis diagnosis in chronic wound situations.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic accompanied by her parents due to her intense worry about the cosmetic appearance of a forehead scar that has been present for 1 year. On examination, there is a well-healed scar that integrates well with the adjacent skin and is barely noticeable from a normal conversational distance. Her parents believe no treatment is necessary as they also find the scar nearly imperceptible. What criterion must be documented to establish a diagnosis of body dysmorphic disorder in this case?
A) Previous treatment history for an eating disorder
B) Intermittent social anxiety symptoms
C) Fixation on clearly visible appearance defects
D) Past history of nose surgery
E) Compulsive behaviors linked to her appearance worries
questions.answer:
E)
Body dysmorphic disorder requires the presence of repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns, such as mirror checking, excessive grooming, skin picking, seeking reassurance, or mentally comparing appearance to others. This behavioral component is essential for diagnosis according to DSM-5 criteria. A) is incorrect because while eating disorders may co-occur with body dysmorphic disorder, they are not required for diagnosis. B) is incorrect because occasional social anxiety alone does not meet the specific criteria for body dysmorphic disorder. C) is incorrect because the disorder involves preoccupation with perceived defects that are not observable or appear minor to others, not obvious flaws. D) is incorrect because prior cosmetic procedures are not part of the diagnostic criteria for body dysmorphic disorder.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old right-handed female sustains a full-thickness circumferential burn extending from shoulder to wrist on her dominant arm. After initial debridement and grafting procedures, she develops a significant elbow flexion contracture at 6 months post-injury (greater than 50% loss of range of motion) requiring surgical contracture release, which results in a large tissue defect. Which reconstructive method would be most appropriate for this defect?
A) Free fasciocutaneous flap
B) Full-thickness skin grafting
C) Local perforator flap
D) Split-thickness skin grafting
E) Z-plasty
questions.answer:
A)
Free fasciocutaneous flap represents the most appropriate reconstructive option for large defects created during severe burn contracture release. This technique is optimal because it introduces healthy, well-perfused tissue from an unaffected donor site, and intact perforator vessels are typically available to serve as recipient vessels for microsurgical anastomosis. B is incorrect because full-thickness skin grafts lack sufficient vascular supply for extensive defects and demonstrate high failure rates in this clinical scenario. C is incorrect because local perforator flaps require healthy adjacent tissue, which is not available in cases of circumferential burns. D is incorrect because split-thickness skin grafts are susceptible to re-contracture and insufficient for covering large defects following contracture release. E is incorrect because Z-plasty and similar local tissue rearrangement techniques cannot be performed when healthy surrounding tissue is absent.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient is being assessed for bilateral microsurgical breast reconstruction. When contrasting the superficial inferior epigastric artery (SIEA) flap with the deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap, which adverse outcome is more common with the SIEA technique?
A) Abdominal hernia
B) Wound separation at donor site
C) Adipose tissue necrosis
D) Complete flap loss
E) Umbilical tissue death
questions.answer:
D)
Complete flap loss is more common with SIEA flaps versus DIEP flaps, with documented failure rates of 7.35-14% for SIEA procedures, mainly caused by arterial anastomotic clotting. The reduced diameter and inconsistent anatomy of superficial blood vessels lead to increased clotting risk. A is wrong because SIEA flaps have reduced abdominal hernia rates since fascial cutting or muscle disturbance is avoided. B is wrong because evidence does not support higher wound separation rates with SIEA procedures. C is wrong because adipose tissue necrosis occurs at similar frequencies in both SIEA and DIEP techniques. E is wrong because umbilical tissue death shows no meaningful difference between these two methods.

questions.question:
An 82-year-old male patient needs nasal reconstruction after Mohs excision with negative margins. The surgical defect is 8mm × 8mm, penetrating all tissue layers at the alar margin and soft triangle region, affecting skin, cartilage, and internal nasal lining. The surgeon plans single-stage repair using an auricular composite graft with local anesthesia. Which auricular site offers the optimal donor tissue for this repair?
A) Bilobed flap for cutaneous coverage and anterior conchal bowl graft for cartilage and lining
B) Full-thickness tragal harvest
C) Full-thickness helical root composite graft with cartilaginous limb extensions
D) Full-thickness helical wedge with primary closure
E) Posterior auricular skin and conchal cartilage composite graft
questions.answer:
C)
The helical root composite graft with cartilaginous extensions represents the optimal choice as it delivers all three necessary tissue layers (skin, cartilage, internal lining) in one harvesting procedure, with the cartilaginous extensions preventing alar notching while providing structural integrity. The helical root skin texture and color closely approximate nasal alar characteristics, and the donor site allows primary closure with minimal aesthetic compromise. A is wrong because it requires two separate procedures instead of a single composite harvest. B is wrong because the tragus provides insufficient tissue volume and inappropriate skin characteristics for alar repair. D is wrong because a helical wedge cannot supply the required three-layer composite structure and may lack adequate lining tissue. E is wrong because posterior auricular skin has markedly different texture and thickness compared to nasal alar skin.

questions.question:
Which condition constitutes an absolute contraindication for administering finasteride to treat androgenetic alopecia in women of childbearing potential?
A) Absence of menstrual periods
B) Abnormal breast milk production
C) Excessive hair growth in male-pattern areas
D) Development of masculine facial characteristics
E) Gestational state
questions.answer:
E)
Gestational state represents an absolute contraindication for finasteride administration, as this medication holds FDA Pregnancy Category X status due to significant teratogenic potential, particularly causing malformation of external genital structures in male embryos. Expectant mothers must avoid taking or even touching finasteride tablets. A is incorrect because absence of menstrual periods does not contraindicate finasteride use and may occur with conditions that could benefit from this treatment. B is incorrect because abnormal breast milk production is unrelated to finasteride contraindications, although breast discomfort may occasionally develop as an adverse effect. C is incorrect because excessive hair growth in male-pattern areas actually represents one of the hyperandrogenic disorders for which finasteride might be prescribed off-label in women. D is incorrect because development of masculine facial characteristics does not contraindicate treatment but may instead indicate a need for anti-androgenic intervention.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old male child is brought in for assessment of drooping eyelids. Clinical examination shows bilateral incomplete eye closure, diminished eyelid muscle strength, and severe sagging of both upper eyelids. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A) Blepharophimosis syndrome
B) Congenital epiblepharon
C) Congenital euryblepharon
D) Fraser cryptophthalmos syndrome
E) Treacher Collins syndrome
questions.answer:
A)
Blepharophimosis syndrome is the most likely diagnosis because it is the only condition among the choices that characteristically presents with congenital ptosis, featuring the classic tetrad of ptosis, telecanthus, epicanthus inversus, and reduced horizontal palpebral fissure width. The bilateral severe upper eyelid drooping and impaired levator muscle function are defining characteristics of this syndrome. B is wrong because epiblepharon involves inward-turning eyelashes caused by excess skin and muscle tissue but does not produce ptosis. C is wrong because euryblepharon causes enlarged palpebral fissures rather than the narrowed openings seen here and lacks ptosis. D is wrong because Fraser cryptophthalmos involves absent eyelid formation with eyes covered by skin but not the ptosis pattern described. E is wrong because Treacher Collins syndrome predominantly affects the lower eyelids with notching and absent lashes, not upper eyelid drooping.

questions.question:
A 57-year-old female patient has surgical removal of vaginal squamous cell carcinoma, creating a defect involving the posterior two-thirds of the vaginal canal extending from the opening to the apex. A small rectal segment was also removed during resection and underwent primary reconstruction. Her medical history includes prior pelvic irradiation and smoking. What is the optimal reconstructive method for addressing this defect?
A) Bilateral gracilis muscle flaps
B) Deep inferior epigastric artery perforator flap
C) Primary repair of the vaginectomy defect
D) Split-thickness skin grafting with obturator
E) Vertical rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap
questions.answer:
E)
The vertical rectus abdominis musculocutaneous (VRAM) flap represents the optimal reconstructive choice for this clinical situation. This technique can deliver sufficient tissue volume to reconstruct the vaginal canal and eliminate dead space effectively. For posterior vaginal vault reconstruction, abdominally-based flaps are typically preferred due to their ability to provide substantial amounts of well-vascularized tissue that can be easily rotated into the defect site. A) is incorrect because bilateral gracilis muscle flaps would provide insufficient soft tissue coverage, and mucosal healing in an irradiated field is unreliable. B) is incorrect because a deep inferior epigastric artery perforator flap involves significantly greater technical complexity compared to a VRAM flap, and the donor site complications are concerning in patients with smoking history. C) is incorrect because primary closure of such an extensive vaginal defect would likely result in severe stenosis and compromised healing due to the patient's radiation exposure history. D) is incorrect because skin grafting with obturator would have poor success rates given her radiation exposure, tobacco use, and rectal involvement.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient with a medical history of high blood pressure presents for body sculpting surgery. Clinical examination reveals widespread abdominal fat deposits and a moderate skin fold below the navel. The patient receives a tummy tuck and extensive fat removal via suction following epidural anesthetic administration. A super-wet method is employed with 5500 mL total volume extracted. Which of the following elements presents the highest mortality risk for this patient?
A) Tummy tuck procedure
B) Epidural anesthetic
C) High blood pressure
D) Fat removal volume
E) Super-wet method
questions.answer:
A)
The combined impact of multiple surgical procedures performed simultaneously increases the likelihood of complications. Extensive fat removal by suction, when paired with additional operations like tummy tucks, can lead to severe adverse events. Mortality from fat suction alone is uncommon (0.0021%, or one in 47,415), but death rates rise substantially when fat suction is performed with other surgeries. Combined with non-tummy tuck procedures, fat suction mortality increases to one in 7314; when paired with tummy tuck procedures, with or without additional operations, mortality rises to one in 3281. B is incorrect because epidural anesthesia, while potentially causing vasodilation and hypotension, has been shown to be safe for liposuction procedures when properly managed. C is incorrect because controlled hypertension places this patient in ASA Class 2, which is appropriate for ambulatory surgery and does not significantly increase mortality risk. D is incorrect because while large-volume liposuction (≥5000 mL) requires careful consideration, no specific volume threshold has been scientifically established as unsafe. E is incorrect because the super-wet technique actually reduces blood loss to less than 1-2% of aspirate volume, making it safer than other infiltration methods.

questions.question:
When assessing evidence-based medicine, which type of study represents Level V evidence?
A) Case series
B) Individual case report
C) Prospective cohort study
D) Randomized clinical trial
E) Retrospective comparative study
questions.answer:
B)
Level V evidence consists of expert opinion, individual case reports, clinical examples, or evidence derived from physiology, laboratory research, or fundamental principles. A case report describes a single patient or clinical scenario and represents the lowest level of evidence in the hierarchy. A) is incorrect because case series are classified as Level IV evidence. C) is incorrect because prospective cohort studies are Level II evidence. D) is incorrect because randomized clinical trials represent Level I evidence, the highest quality. E) is incorrect because retrospective comparative studies are categorized as Level III evidence.

questions.question:
A 2-year-old boy is evaluated because of a soft, nontender, noncompressible glabellar mass that has progressively grown since birth. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management before scheduling surgery?


A) Corticosteroid injections
B) MRI
C) Plain film x-ray study
D) Propranolol trial
E) Observation
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


The differential diagnosis for a lesion in this location with the findings described include dermoid cyst, hemangioma, and encephalocele. Osteoma, which is a benign bony tumor, is unlikely because of patient age and examination findings. The noncompressible quality of the lesion makes hemangioma and encephalocele less likely. Propranolol therapy after 12 months of age is unlikely to help, even if the lesion is a hemangioma. If the lesion is a hemangioma, then observation would be appropriate, but because the lesion is still growing, this diagnosis is questionable. Corticosteroid injections are only moderately helpful in treating a hemangioma, but they are contraindicated for dermoid cysts and encephalocele. Diagnosis is the next step with a goal of ruling out intracranial communication, as it will impact the surgical approach. MRI is the best option. Plain x-rays films would not provide adequate information for management.


ReferencesAl-Muhaylib A, Alkatan HM, Al-Faky YH, Alsuhaibani AH. Periorbital lesions misdiagnosed as dermoid cysts. J AAPOS. 2017;21(6):509-511.Rezaei E, Shams Hojjati Y. Misdiagnosed extranasal mass: report of a 2-year old child with maltreated rare nasal neuroglial heterotopia. World J Plast Surg. 2019;8(1):122-124.Van Wyhe RD, Chamata ES, Hollier LH. Midline craniofacial masses in children. Semin Plast Surg. 2016;30(4):176-180.Vincent J, Baker P, Grischkan J, Fernandez Faith E. Subcutaneous midline nasal mass in an infant due to an intramuscular lipoma. Pediatr Dermatol. 2017;34(3):e135-e136.

questions.question:
A healthy 30-year-old male presents with left foot drop following a posterior knee dislocation. Surgical exploration of the common peroneal nerve at the knee level shortly after injury reveals the nerve remains intact. The patient fails to attend follow-up visits for one year. At 18 months post-injury, he returns showing no recovery from the foot drop. Full passive ankle range of motion is maintained. Which of the following transfer procedures would most effectively address this patient's foot drop condition?
A) Peroneus brevis tendon with graft to calcaneal bone
B) Peroneus longus tendon to calcaneal bone
C) Peroneus longus tendon to talar bone
D) Tibialis anterior nerve to tibialis posterior nerve
E) Tibialis posterior tendon to tibialis anterior tendon
questions.answer:
E)
Tibialis posterior to tibialis anterior tendon transfer will restore ankle dorsiflexion capability in this patient. The tibialis posterior muscle receives innervation from the tibial nerve, which typically remains unaffected during posterior knee dislocations. The tendon is detached from its tarsal insertion and rerouted through the medial aspect of the leg, then passed through the interosseous membrane to connect with the tibialis anterior tendon. A is incorrect because the peroneus brevis would also be paralyzed due to common peroneal nerve injury, making it unsuitable as a donor. B is incorrect because the peroneus longus is also affected by the same nerve injury and cannot function as a transfer donor. C is incorrect because the peroneus longus lacks function due to the nerve injury, and transfer to the talus would not restore dorsiflexion. D is incorrect because at 18 months post-injury, motor endplates have degenerated, making nerve transfers no longer viable options.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with a hard, purple-colored, 3-cm mass on her left cheek. Incisional biopsy reveals Merkel cell carcinoma with positive residual margins. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Systemic chemotherapy
B) Laser destruction
C) Mohs microsurgery
D) Combined radiation and chemotherapy
E) Extensive surgical resection with adjuvant radiation
questions.answer:
E)
Merkel cell carcinoma requires comprehensive treatment with both surgical removal and radiation therapy. This aggressive neuroendocrine skin malignancy has high rates of local recurrence and metastasis, making surgery alone inadequate. The combination of wide excision (or Mohs surgery) with postoperative radiation significantly improves local control and survival outcomes, with 5-year survival rates approaching 90% in node-negative patients without distant disease. A) is incorrect because chemotherapy alone is insufficient for local control of this aggressive tumor. B) is incorrect because laser ablation does not provide adequate tissue removal or histologic assessment for this high-risk malignancy. C) is incorrect because Mohs surgery alone, while an acceptable surgical technique, requires adjuvant radiation therapy for optimal outcomes. D) is incorrect because radiation and chemotherapy without surgical excision fails to address the primary tumor adequately.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old Asian woman presents requesting nasal bridge augmentation to achieve a more "Western" nasal profile. Autologous rib cartilage grafting is under consideration. What represents the most common complication of this procedure?
A) Graft displacement
B) Postoperative infection
C) Pneumothorax
D) Graft absorption
E) Contour irregularity
questions.answer:
E)
Contour irregularity (warping) is the most common complication with rib cartilage grafts. This develops because costal cartilage has an intrinsic tendency to deform over time, potentially due to retained perichondrial elements or uneven matrix structure that compromises long-term shape stability. A is incorrect because autologous cartilage demonstrates superior biocompatibility with very low displacement rates versus synthetic implants. B is incorrect because infection incidence is minimal with autologous cartilage due to excellent tissue compatibility. C is incorrect because although pleural breach may happen, it occurs infrequently and can be readily identified during surgery using methods like the Valsalva test. D is incorrect because viable autologous cartilage grafts show high survival rates and rarely undergo absorption processes.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old woman, G2P2, presents with loose abdominal skin and diastasis recti and is scheduled for tummy tuck surgery with fascial repair. Which regional anesthesia method performed during surgery would best manage post-surgical pain across the widest area of lower belly skin?
A) Local anesthetic infiltration directly into the repair area
B) Blocking the iliohypogastric nerve
C) Blocking the ilioinguinal nerve
D) Blocking the subcostal nerve
E) Transversus abdominis plane block
questions.answer:
E)

Transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block offers the most extensive coverage for lower abdominal skin sensation. The front and side abdominal wall gets nerve supply from spinal segments T7-L1, which run between the transversus abdominis and internal oblique muscle layers, allowing bilateral TAP blocks to effectively numb the T10-L1 skin areas. A is wrong because local infiltration at the midline only numbs the immediate injection area without wider coverage. B is wrong because iliohypogastric nerve block covers a smaller skin area compared to TAP block's broad coverage. C is wrong because ilioinguinal nerve block provides even more limited coverage than iliohypogastric block. D is wrong because subcostal nerve block only affects the T12 skin area, giving much less coverage than the comprehensive TAP technique.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old woman seeks evaluation for bothersome breast hypertrophy after failed non-surgical treatment. Her height is 5 ft 4 in (163 cm), weight is 245 lb (111 kg), resulting in a BMI of 42 kg/m². Physical examination shows Grade II breast sagging and bilateral breast enlargement. Expected tissue excision is 1200 g from each breast. An inferior pedicle breast reduction is planned. Which factor poses the greatest risk for postoperative hemorrhage complications in this patient?
A) Hypotensive anesthetic technique
B) Increased body mass index
C) Lack of surgical drains
D) Patient's age
E) Amount of tissue excised
questions.answer:
A)

Hypotensive anesthetic technique substantially elevates the risk of postoperative hematoma formation. Although this method aims to minimize bleeding during surgery, it paradoxically results in increased rates of bleeding complications afterward, making maintenance of normal blood pressure preferable throughout the operation. B is incorrect because although obesity presents various surgical challenges, BMI does not demonstrate a direct relationship with hematoma development in breast reduction procedures. C is incorrect because controlled trials show no meaningful difference in bleeding complications between patients who receive closed suction drains versus those who do not. D is incorrect because this patient's age of 37 years does not constitute a major risk factor for postoperative hemorrhage. E is incorrect because although greater resection volumes are associated with other complications such as wound healing problems, they do not specifically elevate hematoma risk.

questions.question:
A 6-month-old boy is brought for evaluation of a right-sided facial growth. This growth first appeared when he was 2 weeks old as a small 1-cm vascular mark and has quickly grown to 3 cm in size. Physical examination shows a raised, soft mass that can be compressed. What is the most appropriate management strategy at this time?
A) Oral steroid treatment
B) Laser therapy with pulsed-dye laser
C) Interferon injections
D) Surgical excision
E) Observation and monitoring
questions.answer:
E)
Observation and monitoring is the best management for this uncomplicated, non-ulcerated infantile hemangioma that is not causing obstruction. These vascular growths commonly develop in the first few months of life, experience rapid growth for 3-6 months, then begin a slow regression phase that can last up to 12 years (typically finishing by age 5-7), with most resolving completely without intervention. Given that this lesion is not interfering with function, careful observation with parental education is the appropriate approach. A is incorrect because oral steroids are only used for hemangiomas that cause functional problems or pose life-threatening risks. B is incorrect because pulsed-dye laser is not the primary treatment for simple hemangiomas that will likely disappear on their own. C is incorrect because interferon injections are only considered for severe, life-threatening cases due to significant potential adverse effects. D is incorrect because surgical removal is unnecessary for asymptomatic hemangiomas that have an excellent prognosis for natural resolution.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old man presents with a non-tender, firm, steadily growing unilateral mass in the mandibular body region. He denies any facial injury history and maintains superior oral hygiene. His dentist performed fine needle aspiration which showed multinucleated giant cells. CT imaging reveals a radiolucent bony lesion with cortical thinning. What is the most appropriate treatment strategy?
A) Incisional biopsy procedure
B) En bloc mandibular resection with wide margins
C) Radiotherapy
D) Total excision with thorough curettage
E) Sclerotherapy injection
questions.answer:
D)
Total excision with thorough curettage represents the ideal treatment for aneurysmal bone cysts (ABC). This method achieves a 91.8% success rate in extensive case studies, with recurrence seen in merely 11 out of 120 patients. These pseudocystic formations contain multinucleated giant cells, trabecular bone with cavities, and sinusoids without endothelial lining, necessitating complete removal due to their highly vascular characteristics. A is incorrect because incisional biopsy is contraindicated due to the lesion's substantial vascularity and challenges in achieving hemostasis once the lesion is opened. B is incorrect because en bloc mandibular resection with wide margins represents overtreatment for ABC and is reserved for more aggressive pathology such as ameloblastomas, considering the excellent success rate of conservative curettage. C is incorrect because radiotherapy has no role in treating aneurysmal bone cysts and introduces unnecessary complications. E is incorrect because sclerotherapy is suitable for vascular anomalies (arteriovenous, venous, or lymphatic malformations) but would be ineffective for this solid bony pathology.

questions.question:
An 88-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with a 2-cm pigmented growth on the top of her head as depicted. Physical examination reveals no palpable cervical or suboccipital lymph nodes. Punch biopsy analysis demonstrates a Breslow depth of 2.1 mm, Clark Level IV, two mitoses per high-power field, and absence of ulceration. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Resection with 1-cm margins and bilateral cervical lymph node dissection
B) Resection with 2-cm margins and delayed sentinel lymph node sampling
C) Resection with 3-cm margins and bilateral cervical lymph node dissection
D) Preoperative lymphatic mapping, resection with 1-cm margins, and concurrent sentinel lymph node sampling
E) Preoperative lymphatic mapping, resection with 2-cm margins, and concurrent sentinel lymph node sampling
questions.answer:
E)
For this patient with an intermediate-thickness melanoma (1-4 mm) and clinically negative regional lymph nodes, the optimal treatment involves wide resection with 2-cm margins combined with concurrent sentinel lymph node biopsy following preoperative lymphoscintigraphy. This approach is appropriate because lesions 2-4 mm thick require 2-cm margins for adequate local control, and patients with intermediate-thickness melanomas have a 20-25% risk of microscopic regional disease, making sentinel lymph node assessment valuable for staging and prognosis. A is incorrect because 1-cm margins are insufficient for a 2.1 mm thick lesion, and bilateral lymphadenectomy is unnecessarily aggressive without evidence of nodal involvement. B is incorrect because delayed sentinel lymph node biopsy is suboptimal due to potential alterations in lymphatic drainage patterns after wide excision and reconstruction. C is incorrect because 3-cm margins are excessive for intermediate-thickness melanomas and bilateral lymphadenectomy is not indicated without clinical evidence of nodal disease. D is incorrect because 1-cm margins are inadequate for a lesion of this thickness, which requires 2-cm margins for optimal local control.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old male experienced complete transection and paralysis of the right facial nerve following a circular saw injury 3 years prior. He now desires surgical intervention to restore facial symmetry at rest and enable dynamic smiling. What surgical approach would be most suitable to accomplish these objectives?
A) Cross-facial nerve graft with staged free functional muscle transfer
B) Fascial sling procedure
C) Hypoglossal-to-facial nerve transfer
D) Same-side nerve grafting
E) Direct nerve repair
questions.answer:
A)
Three years following complete facial nerve transection with paralysis, the facial musculature has become nonviable and cannot be successfully reinnervated. Cross-facial nerve grafting combined with staged free functional muscle transfer utilizing the gracilis muscle represents the optimal surgical approach in this clinical scenario. B is incorrect because fascial sling procedures provide only static support and would not be appropriate for a young patient when dynamic reanimation options are available. C is incorrect because hypoglossal-to-facial nerve transfer requires viable facial muscles, which are no longer present after three years. D is incorrect because ipsilateral nerve grafting also depends on viable facial muscles that have degenerated. E is incorrect because direct nerve repair requires viable distal muscle targets and is only feasible in acute injuries, not chronic cases like this one.

questions.question:
A 69-year-old man presents to the office with a large (5 x 7-cm) melanoma involving his right cheek. A photograph is shown. After resection with clear margins, which of the following methods of reconstruction will provide the best aesthetic result?


A) Cervicofacial flap
B) Immediate tissue expansion
C) Primary repair
D) Radial forearm free flap
E) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


Large defects of the cheek are best repaired with local skin when possible. Cervicofacial flaps can be used for moderate to large defects of the cheek with tension free repair (as shown in the photographs), which is vitally important to avoid eyelid-related complications, such as ectropion. Primary repair is useful for smaller cheek defects but would not be possible in this situation. A split-thickness skin graft would not provide optimal soft tissue match, and would undergo significant secondary contracture, resulting in eyelid malposition. They may be used in a temporary situation until definitive reconstruction. Full-thickness skin grafts may be an option; however, they tend to appear shiny and patch-like. Tissue expanders are useful in the head and neck, particularly in the scalp; however, in this particular case it is not advisable to use a tissue expander adjacent to an open wound. There is a significant risk of infection or extrusion. A radial forearm free flap could be an option if local tissue is not available, but would result in an unnecessarily long procedure with secondary donor site.


ReferencesBradley DT, Murakami CS. Reconstruction of the cheek. In: Baker SJ, ed. Local Flaps in Facial Reconstruction. Philadelphia, PA: Mosby Elsevier; 2007:526-556.Maciel-Miranda A, Morris SF, Hallock GG. Local flaps, including pedicled perforator flaps: anatomy, technique, and applications. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2013;131(6):896e-911e.Rogers-Vizena CR, Lalonde DH, Menick FJ, et al. Surgical treatment and reconstruction of nonmelanoma facial skin cancers. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2015;135(5):895e-908e.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of right nasal obstruction and cosmetic concerns regarding a dorsal hump and bulbous nasal tip. Her medical history reveals three previous untreated nasal fractures and periodic seasonal allergy symptoms. She undergoes functional septorhinoplasty with spreader graft placement and reduction of both the nasal tip and dorsal hump. At one week post-surgery, a fluid collection along the nasal bridge tests positive for MRSA and is treated with drainage and oral antibiotic therapy. At her 4-week postoperative visit, despite notable functional and aesthetic improvements, the patient expresses dissatisfaction with her nasal appearance. What is the most appropriate approach to prevent additional patient dissatisfaction?
A) Schedule weekly follow-up appointments for the following 6 weeks
B) Reassure the patient this represents typical postoperative healing and schedule return visit in 4 months
C) Propose surgical revision while informing her of responsibility for facility and anesthesia costs
D) Refer patient care to a different surgeon
questions.answer:
A)
Weekly follow-up visits for 6 weeks is the most appropriate strategy because frequent communication and contact are essential when managing dissatisfied patients, particularly those showing early signs of disappointment. This approach demonstrates empathy, validates the patient's concerns, and helps maintain the surgeon-patient relationship, which is crucial for preventing litigation that often stems from poor communication. B) is incorrect because waiting 4 months is too long and may make the patient feel abandoned, potentially increasing frustration and anger. C) is incorrect because offering revision surgery at 4 weeks postoperatively is premature, as most patient dissatisfaction is temporary and related to perioperative psychological changes rather than actual surgical outcomes. D) is incorrect because transferring care at this early stage is inappropriate and should only be considered after 3-4 months if a good relationship exists with the receiving surgeon.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old female patient seeks advice about facial laser treatment. Clinical assessment reveals Fitzpatrick skin type III with uneven facial pigmentation. What is the most probable adverse effect of fractional CO2 laser therapy in this individual?
A) Allergic contact reaction
B) Deep tissue scarring
C) Eyelid malposition
D) Increased pigmentation
E) Chronic facial flushing
questions.answer:
D)
Increased pigmentation is the most probable adverse effect in this patient with Fitzpatrick Type III skin. Darker skin types absorb approximately 40% more laser energy than lighter skin, leading to thermal damage that can extend beyond the treatment zone. Hyperpigmentation occurs in virtually all patients with darker skin types within 6 weeks to 6 months post-treatment, though it is typically temporary and resolves within 9-12 months with appropriate treatment like hydroquinone. A is incorrect because allergic contact reactions are secondary complications from topical medications like neomycin, not direct laser effects. B is incorrect because deep tissue scarring is a less common complication compared to pigmentary changes in darker skin types. C is incorrect because eyelid malposition (ectropion) is an uncommon side effect that occurs less frequently than pigmentation issues. E is incorrect because chronic facial flushing (rosacea-like symptoms) is not the primary concern in darker skin types undergoing CO2 laser treatment.

questions.question:
A 57-year-old man comes to the office 4 weeks after undergoing a free osseocutaneous fibula flap. He says he has pain with walking. A photograph is shown. X-ray studies show 6 cm of fibular bone remains proximally and distally. Sensation of the right foot shows no abnormalities; pain is noted on plantar flexion. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Cast immobilization of the lower extremity (above the knee)
B) Cast immobilization of the lower extremity (below the knee)
C) Operative exploration and bone grafting
D) Operative exploration and nerve grafting
E) Reassurance that the pain is self-limiting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


Vascularized bone flap is typically needed for defects >6 cm regardless of location in the body. The fibula is a common donor for vascularized bone. Understanding the postoperative course and complications is needed both in terms of discussions with the patient preoperatively and management of the patient‚Äos condition after surgery. Common sequelae of fibula harvest include pain in the leg (especially when walking). Four weeks is relatively early in the postoperative course and reassurance should be given.


Risks of fibula harvest include damage to the peroneal nerve (increased when <6 cm of bone is left behind or when the head of the fibula is included in the harvest); destabilization of the ankle (increased when <6 cm of bone is left behind); and damage to the posterior tibial nerve.


A free-fibular flap design with hash marks left intact is shown.






References
1. Lee JH, Chung CY, Myoung H, et al. Gait analysis of donor leg after free fibular flap transfer. Int J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 2008 Jul;37(7):625-629.
2. Sieg P, Taner C, Hakim SG, et al. Long-term evaluation of donor site morbidity after free fibula transfer. Br J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 2010 Jun;48(4):267-270.
3. Salgado CJ, Moran SL, Mardini S, et al. Fibula flap. In: Wei FC, Mardini S, eds. Flaps and Reconstructive Surgery. 1st ed. Philadelphia, PA: Saunders; 2009:439-456.

questions.question:
A 73-year-old male patient with a medical history of squamous cell carcinoma affecting the central area of his lower lip receives surgical excision followed by reconstruction using the Karapandzic method. The reconstructive flap has dimensions of 6 × 2 cm. Which Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code best describes this surgical procedure?
A) 12052 (Intermediate repair, lip 5.1 to 7.5 cm)
B) 13132 (Complex repair, lip 2.6 to 7.6 cm)
C) 14041 (Adjacent tissue transfer, head neck 10.1 to 30 cm2)
D) 15732 (Musculocutaneous flap)
questions.answer:
D)
The Karapandzic method represents an axial pattern musculocutaneous flap that relies on the facial artery and vein for its blood supply. This technique involves harvesting a composite flap containing skin and muscle along with its neurovascular bundle to provide functional restoration of lip defects. Option A (12052) is inappropriate because intermediate repair codes describe layered wound closures involving subcutaneous and superficial tissues without the muscle component that characterizes the Karapandzic procedure. Option B (13132) is incorrect as complex repair codes apply to wounds requiring advanced closure techniques like extensive debridement or undermining, but do not encompass musculocutaneous flap procedures. Option C (14041) is unsuitable because adjacent tissue transfer codes describe repairs using tissue rearrangement or rotation flaps that lack an axial vascular supply, unlike the Karapandzic technique which depends on a specific arterial system.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old male worker experiences a traumatic finger injury when his left index finger gets trapped in industrial equipment. He expresses urgency to resume his manual labor position. The proximal phalanx bone is visible through the wound. The torn-away portion encompasses the middle and distal phalanges plus surrounding tissues extending to the middle section of the proximal phalanx, including portions of tendons, nerves, and blood vessels. What represents the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Soft tissue reconstruction using a groin flap
B) Reconstruction with a reverse radial forearm flap
C) Microsurgical reattachment
D) Surgical amputation revision
E) Split-thickness skin graft application
questions.answer:
D)
Surgical amputation revision is the most suitable treatment approach. This injury involves extensive damage with avulsed tendons, nerves, and vessels creating a large zone of trauma. A properly executed amputation serves as a reconstructive procedure that can restore hand function, allowing rapid return to work activities. The goals include maintaining useful length, providing stable coverage, preserving sensation, avoiding painful neuromas, preventing joint stiffness, minimizing complications, enabling early prosthetic use, and facilitating quick return to daily tasks. For an index finger proximal phalanx amputation in a manual worker, the shortened digit will typically be bypassed in favor of using the middle finger for pinching activities. A) is incorrect because groin flap coverage requires prolonged hand attachment to the groin, causing stiffness in other fingers and necessitating multiple procedures. B) is incorrect because reverse radial forearm flap requires sacrificing a major hand vessel and would only preserve a non-functional bone segment.
