C) is incorrect because microsurgical reattachment faces significant challenges in avulsion injuries, with contraindications including the avulsion mechanism and single-digit amputation in Zone 2, leading to poor outcomes and delayed work return. E) is incorrect because skin grafting cannot succeed over exposed bone, and the absence of tendons and nerves would result in no movement and no sensation.

questions.question:
A newborn girl, 1 day old, requires evaluation following lumbar myelomeningocele repair. Following dural closure, examination reveals exposed spinal cord at the wound base with a 4 × 4-cm defect in soft tissue and skin. What is the most suitable approach for wound reconstruction?
A) Gluteal muscle flap combined with skin advancement flap
B) Paraspinous musculofascial flap combined with skin advancement flap
C) Skin advancement flap alone
D) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
B)
The optimal reconstruction approach involves using a local musculofascial flap combined with skin advancement flap. The fundamental principle in myelomeningocele reconstruction is establishing a well-perfused soft-tissue barrier between the dural closure and skin repair. The fascia covering the paraspinous muscles can be mobilized as flaps, with paraspinous muscle advancement flaps providing coverage over the dural repair. This vascularized tissue layer reduces the risk of cerebrospinal fluid exposure to skin bacteria and subsequent meningitis if either the dural or skin repair fails. A) is incorrect because regional gluteal muscle flaps are unnecessary when adequate local tissue is available and may cause significant donor site complications in a child already at risk for mobility issues. C) is incorrect because direct skin closure over dural repair increases meningitis risk if cerebrospinal fluid leakage or wound breakdown occurs along widely undermined skin flaps. D) is incorrect because split-thickness skin grafting directly over dura provides inadequate spinal cord protection.

questions.question:
A 68-year-old female patient has a partial tongue removal, excision of the front floor of mouth, and bilateral modified radical neck dissections for squamous cell cancer affecting the underside of the tongue and front mouth floor. The surgical defect is repaired using a 5 × 6-cm radial forearm free tissue transfer. The free tissue is connected to the left facial artery and left internal jugular vein. The forearm donor area is covered with a split-thickness skin graft harvested from the thigh. Along with Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code 15758 (free fascial flap with microvascular anastomosis), which of the following is most suitable?
A) 13152: Complex repair mouth 2.6–7.5 cm
B) 15100: Split thickness skin graft, arm; less than 100 cm2
C) 35761: Exploration of vessels without repair
D) 40840: Anterior vestibuloplasty
E) 69990: Use of operating microscope
questions.answer:
B)
The appropriate additional code is 15100 for split thickness skin graft to the arm donor site less than 100 cm2. Free flap codes are comprehensive and include flap elevation, vessel isolation, transfer, microvascular connections, and primary donor site closure. However, when donor site reconstruction requires more than primary closure (such as skin grafting), this represents additional work beyond the global procedure and should be coded separately. A) is incorrect because complex repair codes are not used when free flap reconstruction is performed at the recipient site. C) is incorrect because vessel exploration without repair is included in the global free flap procedure. D) is incorrect because vestibuloplasty was not performed in this case. E) is incorrect because operating microscope use is bundled into free flap codes and cannot be reported separately.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a vertical penetrating injury to the middle portion of his cheek, located just behind the lateral corner of his eye. Surgical repair is scheduled to occur within 72 hours. What is the main rationale for completing this procedure within this specific timeframe?
A) The anatomical position prevents surgical access and reconstruction
B) Motor endplates will undergo degeneration
C) Neural terminals will have significantly withdrawn
D) Neurotransmitter reserves will become permanently exhausted
E) The likelihood of facial soft-tissue infection dramatically escalates
questions.answer:
D)
After 72 hours, neurotransmitter stores necessary for motor endplate depolarization become permanently depleted, making nerve stimulation testing ineffective for identifying viable nerve stumps during repair. A is incorrect because the anatomical location does not prevent surgical access - facial nerve injuries in this region can be surgically approached and repaired. B is incorrect because motor endplate atrophy is a much slower process that takes 18-24 months to complete, not 72 hours. C is incorrect because while nerve endings do retract over time, this occurs more gradually and is not the primary concern within the 72-hour window. E is incorrect because infection risk, while a consideration, is not the primary driving factor for the 72-hour repair timeline - the main concern is preserving nerve function through timely repair before neurotransmitter depletion occurs.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with repetitive eyelid spasms and forceful eye closure. Physical examination reveals idiopathic blepharospasm. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
A) Prescribing benzodiazepine medication
B) Botulinum toxin type A injections
C) Surgical muscle removal (myectomy)
D) Nerve cutting procedure (neurectomy)
E) Wearing dark-tinted eyewear
questions.answer:
B)
Botulinum toxin type A injections represent the gold standard first-line therapy for idiopathic blepharospasm, providing effective symptom control through temporary muscle paralysis, though patients need regular re-treatment and monitoring. A is incorrect because benzodiazepines are not considered primary therapy for essential blepharospasm management. C is incorrect because myectomy is a surgical option reserved only for severe cases that have failed to respond to medical treatments. D is incorrect because neurectomy is also a last-resort surgical intervention used only when conservative treatments have been unsuccessful. E is incorrect because while tinted glasses may help reduce environmental triggers that worsen symptoms, they do not constitute definitive treatment for the underlying condition.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old healthy female comes to the emergency room for assessment of a small, non-healing wound on her right breast following breast augmentation with lift surgery performed 4 weeks prior in the Dominican Republic. The wound has shown no improvement despite local care and empirical oral antibiotic therapy. She denies fever, chills, or general illness. On examination, there is a 1-cm defect along the vertical surgical incision inferior to the nipple-areolar complex with minimal clear fluid drainage. What is the most appropriate next management step for this patient's condition?
A) Modify the topical wound care protocol and change oral antibiotics
B) Perform surgical debridement and implant removal in the operating room
C) Perform wound excision and primary closure at the bedside
D) Arrange for ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage
E) Initiate intravenous antibiotic therapy
questions.answer:
B)
Given the patient's history of undergoing surgery in Latin America, atypical mycobacterial infection such as Mycobacterium abscessus must be strongly suspected. The most appropriate management involves surgical exploration with thorough debridement and removal of the infected prosthetic device. Tissue specimens should be obtained for acid-fast bacilli staining, mycobacterial culture, and histopathologic examination. A) is incorrect because conservative wound care modifications will not address the underlying atypical mycobacterial infection and will delay proper treatment. C) is incorrect because bedside closure without addressing the infected implant will lead to treatment failure and recurrence. D) is incorrect because there is no evidence of fluid collection requiring drainage. E) is incorrect because intravenous antibiotics alone cannot effectively treat an open wound with prosthetic involvement from atypical mycobacteria.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old male presents to the clinic with a history of facial trauma resulting in nasal disfigurement, C-shaped septal break, and blocked nasal breathing. Following closed reduction of nasal fractures performed two weeks post-injury, considerable nasal blockage continues. Which of the following best explains his persistent nasal deformity and breathing obstruction?
A) Insufficient duration of nasal splinting
B) Failed healing of nasal bones
C) Coexisting septal fracture
D) Enlarged turbinates
E) Missed septal blood collection
questions.answer:
C)
The presence of a septal fracture is the primary reason for failed closed reduction outcomes. Research by Murray and colleagues demonstrated that 30-40% of patients experience ongoing nasal deformity following closed reduction procedures. Their cadaveric research revealed that failure was consistently linked to C-shaped nasal septal deviation and fracture when external nasal deviation exceeded half the nasal bridge width. The mechanism involves interlocking of the septal fracture creating tension that causes nasal bone displacement. A) is incorrect because standard nasal splinting for 7-10 days provides adequate time for reduction stabilization. B) is incorrect as nonunion rarely causes reduction failure and typically occurs only with severely fragmented or open nasal fractures. D) is incorrect because while turbinate enlargement can obstruct nasal breathing, it does not interfere with nasal bone reduction success. E) is incorrect because untreated septal hematoma leads to cartilage thickening and obstruction but does not cause reduction failure.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old male patient with chronic kidney disease requiring dialysis presents with asymmetric lower extremity edema and dyspnea occurring 48 hours following bilateral surgical removal of axillary hidradenitis suppurativa. His current therapy consists of aspirin. Room air pulse oximetry shows 88% saturation. While conducting the diagnostic workup, which medication should be initiated empirically?
A) Intravenous heparin
B) Oral clopidogrel
C) Oral rivaroxaban
D) Oral warfarin
E) Subcutaneous enoxaparin
questions.answer:
A)
This patient likely has developed venous thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism) following surgery. Intravenous heparin is the appropriate empiric treatment because it does not require renal clearance and can be safely used in patients with kidney failure. Option B is incorrect because clopidogrel is an antiplatelet agent used for arterial thrombosis prevention, not venous thromboembolism treatment. Option C is incorrect because rivaroxaban requires dose adjustment or is contraindicated in severe renal impairment. Option D is incorrect because warfarin is used for long-term anticoagulation after acute treatment is established, not for initial empiric therapy. Option E is incorrect because enoxaparin is renally cleared and contraindicated in patients with significant kidney dysfunction.

questions.question:
What histologic feature is most pathognomonic of tenosynovial giant cell tumor?
A) Mononuclear histiocytoid cells
B) Infiltrating lymphocytes
C) Myofibroblastic cells
D) Elongated spindle cells
E) Areas of tissue necrosis
questions.answer:
A)
Mononuclear histiocytoid cells represent the defining neoplastic element of tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TSGCT). This benign soft tissue lesion, which ranks as the second most frequent benign hand tumor after ganglion cysts, characteristically presents with multinucleated giant cells, histiocytes, fibrous tissue, and hemosiderin deposits. The histiocytoid mononuclear cells constitute the primary tumor component and must be identified during pathological examination. TSGCT typically affects adults aged 30-50 years with female predominance, presenting as a slow-growing, generally asymptomatic mass. While surgical excision remains the standard treatment, local recurrence is common, and repeated recurrences can lead to surrounding tissue damage. B is incorrect because lymphocytic infiltration is not a characteristic component of TSGCT histology. C is incorrect because myofibroblastic cells are not typical features of this tumor type. D is incorrect because spindle cells are not defining histologic elements of TSGCT. E is incorrect because necrotic zones are not characteristic findings in tenosynovial giant cell tumors.

questions.question:
A 19-year-old male presents with intense, progressively worsening pain in his arm and swelling of his fingers, along with numbness in the distal extremity. He suffered a complete circumferential burn injury to his arm 12 hours prior. The burned tissue appears thick and leather-like with no sensation. Physical examination reveals absent peripheral pulses. What is the most appropriate immediate intervention?
A) Arteriography
B) Computed tomography
C) Doppler ultrasound evaluation
D) Escharotomy
E) Fasciotomy
questions.answer:
D)

The most appropriate immediate intervention is escharotomy. This patient demonstrates classic signs of circulatory compromise secondary to constricting burn eschar from a circumferential full-thickness burn injury. Post-burn inflammation and fluid resuscitation lead to tissue edema, and when combined with inelastic circumferential eschar, creates a tourniquet-like effect that compromises vascular flow. Escharotomy involves making incisions through the burn eschar to release this constriction and restore circulation. A is incorrect because arteriography would provide vascular imaging but would unnecessarily delay urgent treatment and is not needed for diagnosis in this clear clinical scenario. B is incorrect because computed tomography would not provide useful information for this condition and would delay necessary intervention. C is incorrect because while Doppler ultrasound could assess vascular flow, the clinical presentation clearly indicates eschar-related vascular compromise that requires immediate surgical release rather than further diagnostic testing. E is incorrect because fasciotomy involves deeper incisions through muscle fascia to treat compartment syndrome, whereas this patient requires the more superficial escharotomy to release the constricting burn eschar.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old female patient carrying a BRCA gene mutation is undergoing preventive bilateral mastectomy with immediate reconstruction utilizing tissue expanders. What represents the optimal antibiotic prophylaxis timeframe for this surgical intervention?
A) No antibiotic administration
B) Single dose before surgery plus one additional dose during wound closure
C) Single preoperative dose with 24-hour postoperative antibiotic treatment
D) Single preoperative dose, 24-hour postoperative treatment, followed by oral antibiotics until drain extraction
E) Single preoperative dose, 24-hour postoperative treatment, followed by oral antibiotics until expander replacement
questions.answer:
C)
Option C represents the optimal approach. Breast reconstruction surgeries demonstrate complication rates up to 60% with infection rates over 20%, substantially exceeding those of typical clean surgical cases. CDC guidelines recommend perioperative antibiotic administration for 24 hours beginning 30 minutes prior to surgical incision. A 2013 meta-analysis evaluating no antibiotics versus less than 24 hours versus greater than 24 hours revealed infection rates of 14.4%, 5.8%, and 5.8% respectively, confirming antibiotic effectiveness while showing no benefit from prolonged administration beyond 24 hours. A 2013 randomized controlled study validated that 24-hour prophylaxis equals the efficacy of extended oral antibiotic regimens in tissue expander breast reconstruction. Option A is wrong because antibiotic prophylaxis substantially decreases infection rates versus no treatment. Option B is wrong because this shortened duration fails to provide optimal infection prevention. Options D and E are wrong because prolonged antibiotic regimens exceeding 24 hours offer no additional protective benefit while potentially increasing antibiotic resistance and side effects.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old patient with paraplegia presents with a 5×5-cm pressure sore over the ischial tuberosity that penetrates through skin, subcutaneous tissue, and into bone. After surgical debridement, reconstruction with a gluteal rotation flap is being considered. What is the main benefit of using a rotation flap versus a transposition flap for this wound?
A) Ability to reuse the flap for future operations
B) Reduced rates of ulcer recurrence
C) Improved distribution of pressure forces
D) More favorable scar placement
E) Increased vascular perfusion
questions.answer:
A)
The correct answer is A. Pressure ulcers over the ischial region pose complex reconstructive challenges with recurrence rates reaching up to 70% even with optimal management including pressure offloading, nutritional support, smoking cessation, and spasticity control. Given the high probability of recurrence, surgical planning must account for potential future reconstructive requirements. Large rotation or advancement flaps offer the advantage of being re-rotated or re-advanced for repeat procedures, whereas transposition flaps cannot be reused and may compromise future surgical options. B is incorrect because recurrence rates are comparable between both flap types when appropriately performed. C is incorrect because pressure distribution depends on flap design and positioning rather than the specific flap technique used. D is incorrect because scar aesthetics and positioning are similar between well-executed rotation and transposition flaps. E is incorrect because blood supply is equivalent between both flap types when properly planned and executed.

questions.question:
A 72-year-old male with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and a 40-pack-year tobacco use history arrives following a high-velocity motor vehicle collision as an unbelted occupant. Current vitals: pulse 88, respirations 18, blood pressure 115/70, oxygen saturation 98% with 6L face mask oxygen. Physical examination shows significant facial swelling, blood-tinged sputum, severe dental misalignment, and preserved teeth. Imaging demonstrates naso-orbital-ethmoid disruption, Le Fort III pattern fracture, hard palate fracture, and fragmented mandibular body and angle fractures. Which airway management strategy is most appropriate for operative intervention?
A) Surgical cricothyrotomy
B) Nasal endotracheal intubation
C) Oral endotracheal intubation
D) Surgical tracheostomy
E) Supraglottic airway device
questions.answer:
D)
Surgical tracheostomy is the optimal choice for this patient with complex panfacial trauma requiring extensive reconstructive surgery with probable intermaxillary fixation. His substantial smoking background and underlying COPD create significant postoperative respiratory risks that necessitate superior airway control and pulmonary care management. Tracheostomy allows unrestricted surgical access to all fracture locations while providing secure long-term airway management for this high-risk patient. A is incorrect because surgical cricothyrotomy is an emergency procedure for immediate airway compromise, but this patient is stable without acute respiratory failure. B is incorrect because nasal intubation is contraindicated with naso-orbital-ethmoid fractures since the endotracheal tube would interfere with proper fracture alignment and repair. C is incorrect because oral intubation tubes obstruct proper dental occlusion assessment during intermaxillary fixation procedures and fail to provide adequate postoperative respiratory support for this compromised patient. E is incorrect because supraglottic devices offer inadequate airway security and can become displaced during the extensive head positioning required for complex facial reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old female patient with a BMI of 36 kg/m² receives immediate bilateral tissue expander breast reconstruction. Ten days after surgery, she presents with bilateral breast redness and begins empirical antibiotic therapy. Apart from Staphylococcus organisms, which microorganism should be the next main focus for antimicrobial treatment?
A) Bacteroides fragilis
B) Enterococcus faecalis
C) Mycobacterium marinum
D) Pasteurella multocida
E) Pseudomonas aeruginosa
questions.answer:
E)
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the correct choice. After Staphylococcus aureus and S. epidermidis, P. aeruginosa represents one of the most common pathogens causing breast implant-related infections. This gram-negative bacterium frequently infects hospitalized patients, immunocompromised individuals, and those with prosthetic devices such as implants. Management usually requires advanced β-lactam antibiotics, carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, or aminoglycosides, often using combination therapy for serious infections. Breast implant infection incidence averages 6% in reconstruction procedures with 3% requiring device removal. A) is wrong because Bacteroides fragilis is an anaerobic intestinal bacterium that rarely causes breast infections. B) is wrong because Enterococcus faecalis mainly inhabits the gastrointestinal tract and is uncommon in breast surgical patients despite being a frequent hospital-acquired pathogen. C) is wrong because Mycobacterium marinum is an uncommon pathogen that causes hand infections following aquatic exposures. D) is wrong because Pasteurella multocida typically results from animal bite wounds, especially from felines and canines.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old child arrives 4 hours following traumatic loss of his left index finger at the middle portion of the proximal phalanx after being caught in a door. The family transported the amputated digit in a plastic bag placed on ice. What represents the strongest reason for pursuing replantation?
A) The amputation site is proximal to where the flexor digitorum superficialis attaches
B) The cold ischemia time is less than 6 hours
C) The affected digit is the index finger
D) This represents a single digit amputation
E) The patient is a pediatric case
questions.answer:
E)
The correct answer is pediatric age. Digital replantation should nearly always be pursued in children unless the severed part is severely damaged or life-threatening conditions prevent surgery. Despite technical difficulties from smaller blood vessels, pediatric replantations yield superior functional results compared to adults, including enhanced sensory restoration and normal developmental growth. Joint-level amputations show exceptional remodeling abilities in children. A is wrong because amputations proximal to FDS attachment typically result in poor motion and are usually contraindications in adults. B is wrong because fingers can withstand much longer ischemia periods (12-24 hours when cold) than presented here, so timing is not restrictive. C is wrong because index finger amputations at or proximal to PIP joint level are often better managed with amputation in adults due to possible stiffness and discomfort. D is wrong because single digit amputations, particularly proximal ones, are typically contraindications for replantation in adult patients.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old man and his 80-year-old father sustain injuries during an attack. Both present with fractures to the face. The elderly patient is more prone to experience which of the following?
A) Reduced likelihood of injuries outside the craniofacial region
B) Increased mortality rate
C) Minor injury severity
D) Fracture of the mandibular body
E) Reduced length of hospitalization
questions.answer:
B)
Elderly patients with facial fractures have significantly higher mortality rates compared to younger patients. Research demonstrates that geriatric patients (typically those over 60-65 years) experience worse outcomes across multiple parameters including prolonged hospitalizations, greater need for post-discharge assistance, more severe trauma, and most critically, substantially elevated death rates. A) is incorrect because elderly patients actually have increased likelihood of sustaining non-craniofacial injuries such as spinal and extremity fractures. C) is incorrect because geriatric patients typically sustain more severe injuries overall. D) is incorrect because mandibular body fractures are more prevalent in younger populations, while elderly patients more commonly experience midface, orbital, and condylar fractures. E) is incorrect because elderly patients require longer hospital stays, not shorter ones.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old man is evaluated because of the facial deformity shown in the photograph. Three years ago, he underwent resection of an infratemporal malignancy and intraoperative alloplastic reconstruction of bony defects. Postoperatively, he underwent extensive radiation therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate method for restoring facial volume in this patient?


A) Custom-fabricated alloplastic implantation
B) Dermal fat grafting
C) Implantation of layered acellular dermis
D) Parascapular free flap reconstruction
E) Serial fat grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.






The patient described has marked loss of facial soft-tissue volume related to the initial tumor resection and the adverse effects of postoperative radiation treatment. The best method for restoring soft-tissue volume is a scapular free flap. This method of reconstruction has advantages over the others listed. The free scapular flap does not rely on the damaged and scarred soft-tissue envelope for vascular support and, thus, it will retain its volume. In contrast, fat grafting, dermal fat graft, and layered acellular dermis all undergo some resorption, especially in this poorly vascularized recipient site. The scapular flap is of sufficient thickness to correct even a volume defect of this size. Although the other soft-tissue reconstructive options can improve contour, the volume required in this patient cannot be achieved with these modalities alone. The use of an alloplastic reconstruction alone can improve mid-facial volume, but will not address the lower third deficit. In addition, there is a moderate risk of extrusion and/or infection with this technique alone.
References
1. Haddock NT, Saadeh PB, Seibert JW. Achieving aesthetic results in facial reconstructive microsurgery: planning and executing secondary refinements. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2012 Dec;130(6):1236-1245.
2. Bourget A, Chang JT, Wu DB, et al. Free flap reconstruction in the head and neck region following radiotherapy: a cohort study indentifying negative outcome predictors. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2011 May;127(5):1901-1908.
3. Phulpin B, Gangloff P, Tran N, et al. Rehabilitation of irradiated head and neck tissues by autologous fat transplantation. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009 Apr;123(4):1187-1197.

questions.question:
A 41-year-old male patient is undergoing preoperative assessment for ventral hernia reconstruction. His medical history reveals a penetrating abdominal trauma with bowel exposure 4 years prior, which was managed with vacuum-assisted closure therapy and skin grafting. The surgical plan involves a components separation approach. During this operation, which of the following anatomical layer interfaces will most likely be preserved?
A) Intestine and fascial margin
B) External oblique and internal oblique
C) External oblique and subcutaneous tissue
D) Internal oblique and transversus abdominis
E) Rectus abdominis muscle and posterior rectus fascia
questions.answer:
D)
The components separation technique relies on mobilizing abdominal wall layers through strategic dissection planes while preserving certain anatomical connections. The internal oblique muscle typically remains attached to the transversus abdominis muscle because this plane contains the intercostal neurovascular bundles. Separating these layers would create a difficult, hemorrhagic dissection and risk denervation of the rectus abdominis muscle. A is incorrect because bowel adhesions to fascial edges are routinely lysed during hernia repair. B is incorrect because the external and internal oblique muscles are deliberately separated lateral to the rectus sheath as a key step in components separation. C is incorrect because extensive subcutaneous flaps are created, separating the external oblique from overlying tissues. E is incorrect because the posterior rectus sheath may be incised when additional mobilization is needed.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman undergoes composite resection of the right mandibular body and floor of the mouth. Closure with a fibular free flap is performed. A photograph is shown. Which of the following mechanisms best describes the healing process associated with vascularized bone transfers?


A) Endochondral ossification
B) Osteochondrosis
C) Osteoconduction
D) Osteogenesis
E) Osteoinduction
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Osteogenesis is the formation of new bone by cells in a flap/graft that survive the transfer. This is the primary mechanism by which a vascularized bone graft heals. The pedicle keeps the bone alive so that primary bone healing can occur between the graft and recipient site. Osteoblasts from both locations participate in the formation of new bone at the interface between graft and native bone. Advantages of a vascularized bone graft include the ability to place the graft into a hostile environment such as an irradiated wound bed and immediate structural support with shortened time to bony union compared with nonvascularized cortical grafts.


Osteoinduction refers to the direct stimulation of mesenchymal cells at the recipient site by bone morphogenetic protein to differentiate into osteoprogenitor cells. This mechanism of action is associated with the healing of cancellous bone grafts and demineralized bone matrix.


Endochondral ossification is the process by which the cartilaginous soft callus covering a fracture is transformed into bone.


Osteochondrosis refers to a family of ossification disorders in children.


Osteoconduction (creeping substitution) is the primary method by which cortical bone grafts heal. During osteoconduction, cells and blood vessels from the recipient bed grow into the graft. The bone graft becomes a template for the deposition of new bone and the graft resorbs. Neovascularization is complete by 6 to 8 weeks, but ultimate strength of cortical grafts is not seen until 6 to 12 months, at which time the graft is comparable to a vascularized bone graft.


References
Gosain AK, McCarthy JG, Staffenberg D, et al. The histomorphologic changes in vascularized bone transfer and their interrelationship with the recipient sites: a 1-year study. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1996 Apr;97(5):1001-1013.
Mehrara BJ, McCarthy JG. Repair and Grafting of Bone. In: Mathes SJ, ed. Plastic Surgery. Vol 1. Philadelphia: Elsevier-Saunders; 2006:639-718.
Finkemeier CG. Bone-grafting and bone-graft substitutes. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2002 Mar;84-A(3):454-464.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient presents to the clinic expressing significant dissatisfaction with her breast appearance after undergoing bilateral breast lift surgery 12 months prior. Her height is 5 ft 7 in (170 cm) and BMI is 26 kg/m2. Which of the following physical examination findings would present the greatest challenge for surgical correction?
A) Unequal breast volumes
B) Puckering at the lower end of the vertical incision
C) Distance from nipple to breast fold measuring 16 cm
D) Distance from nipple to suprasternal notch measuring 16 cm
E) Stretched scar around the areola
questions.answer:
D)
A suprasternal notch to nipple measurement of 16 cm indicates an elevated nipple position. Corrective surgery for a malpositioned high nipple is technically challenging and difficult to achieve satisfactory outcomes because both surgeons and patients prefer to avoid creating scars above the nipple-areolar complex. Additionally, the limited amount of available skin between the nipple and collarbone restricts surgical options. A) is incorrect because breast volume differences can be addressed through liposuction or revision lift/reduction procedures using existing incision sites. B) is incorrect because inferior vertical scar irregularities are easily corrected with minor transverse incisions in the breast crease, and many resolve spontaneously. C) is incorrect because increased nipple-to-fold distance (ptosis recurrence) can be improved by shortening the vertical scar with wedge excision at the breast fold. E) is incorrect because widened areolar scars can be successfully revised with permanent sutures to control areolar size and reduce tension.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old right-hand-dominant male construction worker is evaluated because of a right dorsal thumb abscess that is treated with debridement and administration of antibiotics. A photograph of the residual defect is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate method for reconstruction in this patient?


A ) Coverage with a muscle flap
B ) Coverage with a skin flap
C ) Full-thickness skin grafting
D ) Negative pressure wound therapy
E ) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.





The residual defect includes exposed extensor tendon without paratenon. This fact, combined with the need for flexion at the interphalangeal joint and avoidance of contracture, as well as the likely need for future tenolysis, makes a skin flap the most appropriate option for reconstruction. In the scenario described, a first dorsal metacarpal artery pedicled skin flap is used to reconstruct the thumb defect with the need for back grafting of the donor site. This provides the best combination of low donor-site morbidity, the ability to provide stable soft-tissue coverage over exposed tendon without paratenon, and the competitive advantage of being relatively easy to re-elevate for subsequent procedures, if needed.


A muscle flap could be used to reconstruct the defect but would not be optimal due to the increased donor site morbidity from muscle sacrifice, as well as the increased difficulty in re-elevation versus a skin flap over tendon.


Healing by secondary intention, with or without topical negative pressure wound therapy, will certainly result in extensive contracture as well as an increased time to heal. This will impact the patient‚Äos outcome both in terms of his ability to return to work as a construction worker as well as limitations on his functional range of motion.


Skin grafting, whether split- or full-thickness, is not a reliable option in this patient because of the exposed tendon without paratenon. It is important to note that this is a classic contraindication to skin grafting and therefore leads to a flap-based reconstruction.


Furthermore, skin grafts would lead to increased contraction versus flaps and would be difficult to re-elevate for subsequent procedures.


References
1. Carty MJ, Taghinia A, Upton J. Fascial flap reconstruction of the hand: a single surgeon's 30-year experience. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Mar;125(3):953-962.
2. Friedrich JB, Katolik LI, Vedder NB. Soft tissue reconstruction of the hand. J Hand Surg Am. 2009 Jul-Aug;34(6):1148-1155.
3. Taghinia AH, Carty M, Upton J. Fascial flaps for hand reconstruction. J Hand Surg Am. 2010 Aug; 35(8):1351-1355.
4. Gregory H, Heitmann C, Germann G. The evolution and refinements of the distally based dorsal metacarpal artery (DMCA) flaps. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2007;60(7):731-739. Epub 2007 May 18.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old male patient presents with septal deviation and enlarged inferior turbinates. He undergoes septal reconstruction, inferior turbinate reduction, and bilateral spreader graft insertion. His preoperative assessment revealed a constricted middle nasal vault and compromised internal nasal valve function. The Cottle test demonstrated enhanced nasal breathing. After the septal procedure, a 6-mm dorsal support and 10-mm caudal support are left intact. What is the most probable postoperative complication for this patient?
A) Collapse of the external nasal valve
B) Open roof abnormality
C) Pollybeak abnormality
D) Rocker abnormality
E) Saddle-nose abnormality
questions.answer:
E)
When conducting septal surgery involving cartilage removal, experts typically advise maintaining a 1-cm L-shaped support structure (1-cm caudal support and 1-cm dorsal support) to maintain structural integrity. In this case, only 6 mm of dorsal support remains. This inadequate support weakens the nasal bridge, making it susceptible to fracture, displacement from the bony septum, or collapse due to soft tissue contracture forces. A saddle-nose abnormality results from dorsal collapse. A) is incorrect because external nasal valve collapse typically occurs from procedures that compromise the lower lateral cartilages. B) is incorrect because an open roof abnormality happens when excessive dorsal hump reduction creates separation between the nasal sidewalls and septum. C) is incorrect because a pollybeak abnormality results from supratip fullness that depresses and under-projects the nasal tip, commonly from excessive scar tissue or inadequate lower dorsal septal resection. D) is incorrect because a rocker abnormality occurs after medial nasal bone osteotomy that extends beyond the thick radix bone, causing lateral rocking when the bone is repositioned medially.

questions.question:
A 14-year-old male patient presents with a childhood history of severe burns requiring skin grafts and now reports discomfort from multiple restrictive scars. Physical examination reveals elevated, thickened, and moderately contracted scarring across the scalp, back, abdomen, upper arms, and thighs. The treatment plan includes tissue expansion prior to scar excision. In which anatomical location is this patient most likely to experience the highest rate of tissue expander complications?
A) Abdomen
B) Back
C) Scalp
D) Thigh
E) Upper arm
questions.answer:
C)
The scalp represents the anatomical site with the highest likelihood of tissue expander complications. A longitudinal 10-year study tracking 256 pediatric burn survivors documented that 36 patients (14%) required expander removal secondary to extrusion, infection, or device rupture/port failure, with an additional 26 patients (10%) experiencing insufficient expansion or inability to complete the planned reconstruction. The scalp was identified as the predominant failure site (27/36 patients requiring implant removal, 18/26 cases of inadequate expansion). Research indicates that tissue expansion achieves superior outcomes in regions with greater tissue elasticity and compliance. A) Abdomen is incorrect because abdominal tissue demonstrates increased laxity and pliability, resulting in lower complication rates. B) Back is incorrect as the back region typically has better tissue compliance compared to the scalp, leading to fewer expansion failures. D) Thigh is incorrect since thigh tissue generally exhibits greater elasticity than scalp tissue, reducing the risk of expander complications. E) Upper arm is incorrect because the upper arm area typically has more pliable tissue characteristics compared to the scalp, resulting in lower failure rates.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old woman comes to the office because of fine rhytides and skin discoloration caused by photoaging. Topical application of 0.025% tretinoin is planned. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of topical retinoid therapy?


A) Decreased activation of skin appendages resulting in thinning of the stratum corneum
B) Decreased corneocyte cohesion resulting in increased desquamation
C) Increased free radical scavenging activity and synthesis of Types I and III collagen
D) Inhibition of AP-1 transcription factor binding to DNA resulting in diminished protease activity
E) Inhibition of tyrosinase resulting in diminished conversion of dopamine to melanin
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Tretinoin (all-trans-retinoic acid; Retin-A) is one of the best long-term topical therapies available for chronically photoaged skin. The mechanism of action of retinoids is regulated through specific nuclear receptors. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation activates a series of phosphokinases that stimulate c-Fos and c-Jun proto-oncogenes and thereby activate AP-1 transcription factor. AP-1 causes activation of metalloproteases such as collagenase, gelatinase, and stromelysin, which then break down collagen. Tretinoin results in a 70% inhibition of AP-1 transcription factor binding to DNA and a significant reduction in protease activity.


Long-term use of tretinoin is associated with improved skin texture, decreased sallowness, a reduction in fine rhytides and actinic keratosis, fading of pigmented macules, and an overall improvement in skin appearance. Histologic effects of tretinoin include increased epidermal and granular layer thickness; elimination of dysplasia, atypia, and microscopic actinic keratoses; uniform dispersion of melanin granules; increased collagen and glycosaminoglycan deposition in the papillary dermis; and diminished dermal elastosis, angiogenesis, and compaction/thinning of the stratum corneum.


Tretinoin side effects include erythema, photosensitivity, and desquamation. Patients are initially started on a low dose with nightly application until tolerance is achieved. Because tretinoin is a photosensitizer, sunscreen use is absolutely imperative. Topical retinoids should be used for a minimum of 3 to 4 months, with the greatest improvement after 1 year of use. Patients who use alpha-hydroxy acids concomitantly with topical retinoids will see a synergistic effect, and this combination is tolerated well in most patients.


Isotretinoin (13-cis retinoic acid; Accutane) impairs sebaceous gland activity, impairs epithelialization, and thins the stratum corneum. Alpha-hydroxy acids cause desquamation as a result of diminished corneocyte cohesion just above the granular cell layer. Dermal effects of these acids include increased collagen and glycosaminoglycan production. UV radiation-stimulated oxygen free radicals are the primary mediators of UV skin damage. Vitamin C has been shown to be the primary water-soluble nonenzymatic antioxidant that helps protect skin cells from UV radiation. Other functions of Vitamin C include increased Types I and III collagen production, decreased pigment synthesis, improved epidermal barrier function, and regeneration of oxidized Vitamin E. Hydroquinone impairs the conversion of dopamine to melanin. The result is decreased formation of melanin and increased degradation of melanosomes.


References
1. Saltz R, Borba T. Skin care and dermatologic treatments. In: Nahai F, ed. The Art of Aesthetic Surgery: Principles and Techniques. St. Louis: Quality Medical Publishing; 2005::170-193.
2. Bhawan J, Olsen E, Lufrano L, et al. Histologic evaluation of the long term effects of tretinoin on photodamaged skin. J Dermatol Sci. 1996 Mar;11(3):177-182.
3. Clark CP III. Office-based skin care and superficial peels: the scientific rationale. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1999 Sep;104(3):854-864.
4. Leyden JJ. Treatment of photodamaged skin with topical tretinoin: an update. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1998 Oct;102(5):1667-1671.
5. Kligman AM, Grove GL, Hirose R, et al. Topical tretinoin for photoaged skin. J Am Acad Dermatol. 1986 Oct;15(4 Pt 2):836-859.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old female patient receiving chemotherapy for lung cancer with metastases experiences discomfort at the injection site during her initial doxorubicin infusion. The next day, examination reveals hand edema and a 2 × 3 cm ulceration on the dorsal surface with surrounding ischemic tissue. What is the most appropriate initial management?
A) Hyperbaric oxygen therapy
B) Cold compress application
C) Warm compress application
D) Topical dimethyl sulfoxide application
E) Urgent surgical debridement with skin grafting
questions.answer:
D)
Topical dimethyl sulfoxide is the most appropriate initial treatment for doxorubicin extravasation injuries, as it has demonstrated efficacy in multiple clinical studies specifically for anthracycline-related tissue damage. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (A) lacks proven effectiveness for this indication. Cold compresses (B) are contraindicated as they cause vasoconstriction that concentrates the cytotoxic drug locally, worsening tissue damage. Warm compresses (C) promote vasodilation which can spread the extravasated medication to additional tissue areas. Immediate surgical excision with grafting (E) is premature at this stage and is typically reserved for cases with severe necrosis or intractable pain after conservative measures have failed.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male presents to the emergency department following a sharp traumatic amputation at the mid-humeral level. The severed limb is contained in a plastic bag. The patient is taken to the operating room for replantation attempt with 4 hours of warm ischemia time. His vital signs remain stable. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Arterial reconstruction to reestablish blood flow
B) Temporary arterial shunt to reestablish blood flow
C) Skeletal stabilization
D) Bone shortening procedure
E) Amputation revision with immediate targeted muscle reinnervation
questions.answer:
B)
The most appropriate initial step is placing a temporary arterial shunt to rapidly restore circulation. Upper extremity amputations above the wrist can tolerate 4-6 hours of warm ischemia before irreversible muscle death occurs. At 4 hours, this patient is at the upper limit of tolerance, making immediate perfusion restoration critical. A temporary shunt from the proximal arterial stump to the amputated part's artery quickly reestablishes blood flow, though venous bleeding will occur requiring transfusion. This venous outflow also removes accumulated lactic acid, preventing cardiovascular collapse from metabolic acidosis. A) is incorrect because formal arterial repair takes longer and delays perfusion restoration. C) is incorrect because bone fixation should occur after perfusion is restored. D) is incorrect because bone shortening, while eventually necessary, is not the immediate priority when ischemia time is critical. E) is incorrect because replantation remains viable at 4 hours and should be attempted before considering amputation with targeted muscle reinnervation.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with edema of her left arm 18 months following axillary radiation treatment for breast carcinoma. What is the most suitable diagnostic test to establish a diagnosis of lymphedema?
A) Computed tomography
B) Lymphatic scintigraphy
C) Magnetic resonance imaging
D) Tissue biopsy
E) Ultrasound examination
questions.answer:
B)
Lymphatic scintigraphy is the most suitable diagnostic test to establish a diagnosis of lymphedema. Axillary radiation leads to scarring of lymph nodes in the axilla, which disrupts normal lymphatic drainage from the arm and causes lymphedema. Lymphatic scintigraphy serves as the gold standard for lymphedema diagnosis. This test involves injecting a radioactive protein into the hands, which is absorbed by lymphatic vessels. Sequential imaging tracks the protein's movement toward the axillary nodes. Slow tracer movement and/or spillage into superficial lymphatics indicates lymphatic impairment and confirms lymphedema, with 96% sensitivity and 100% specificity. A) Computed tomography is incorrect because while it may detect subcutaneous fluid accumulation, it lacks the sensitivity and specificity needed for lymphedema diagnosis. C) Magnetic resonance imaging is incorrect because although it can visualize fluid in tissues, it cannot specifically diagnose lymphatic dysfunction. D) Tissue biopsy is incorrect because lymphedema cannot be diagnosed histologically, as tissue samples only reveal nonspecific inflammatory changes. E) Ultrasound examination is incorrect because while it may show fluid in subcutaneous tissues, it cannot specifically identify lymphatic system dysfunction.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old female patient will have surgical removal of a cerebellopontine angle mass on the left side requiring sacrifice of the facial nerve trunk. A two-stage cross-facial nerve graft procedure is being considered. Which of the following interventions would best reduce the likelihood of lasting facial asymmetry during the tumor removal surgery?
A) Free gracilis muscle flap to the left facial nerve remnant
B) Hypoglossal-to-facial nerve transfer combined with cross-facial nerve grafting
C) Implantation of a 1.2-g gold weight into the left upper eyelid
D) Transcutaneous stimulation of distal facial nerve branches
E) Installation of an extended temporalis fascia static suspension
questions.answer:
B)
Hypoglossal-to-facial nerve transfer combined with cross-facial nerve grafting provides the optimal approach for maintaining facial muscle function and minimizing asymmetry. When cerebellopontine angle tumors require facial nerve sacrifice, cross-facial nerve grafting alone often produces delayed and weakened muscle reinnervation. The addition of hypoglossal-to-facial transfer (babysitter procedure) helps prevent muscle atrophy and strengthens facial muscle function while the cross-facial graft matures. A is incorrect because free gracilis transfer would be a secondary reconstructive option rather than immediate reinnervation. C is incorrect because gold weight insertion only addresses eyelid closure but doesn't restore facial muscle movement. D is incorrect because percutaneous stimulation cannot maintain long-term muscle viability after nerve sacrifice. E is incorrect because static sling procedures provide support but no dynamic muscle function.

questions.question:
A 67-year-old male patient with a documented history of Dupuytren's disease affecting his right fifth digit presents for assessment one week following the development of numbness and tingling sensations along the lateral border of his right fifth finger. The sensory symptoms began two days after he received a collagenase Clostridium histolyticum injection into the affected digit. Current physical examination reveals minimal swelling of the finger. Digital extension has markedly improved, and flexor tendon integrity remains intact. Nevertheless, sensation is absent in the ulnar digital nerve territory; two-point discrimination exceeds 10 mm. Neurological function was normal before the injection procedure. What represents the most suitable management approach?
A) Electromyography and nerve conduction studies
B) Urgent surgical exploration with direct ulnar digital nerve repair
C) Urgent surgical exploration with ulnar digital nerve reconstruction using nerve conduit
D) Conservative management with observation
questions.answer:
D)
Observation is the most appropriate management strategy in this scenario. Collagenase Clostridium histolyticum treatment for Dupuytren's contracture has extensive clinical documentation regarding its safety profile. While flexor tendon ruptures and pulley injuries have been documented, no cases of digital nerve transection during cord disruption with collagenase have been reported in the medical literature. The patient's symptoms are most consistent with neurapraxia rather than complete nerve severing. A) is incorrect because electromyography and nerve conduction studies cannot definitively determine if the nerve has been completely severed. B) is incorrect because immediate surgical exploration is not warranted only one week post-injury when neurapraxia is the likely diagnosis. C) is incorrect because urgent nerve reconstruction is premature; surgical exploration for suspected neurapraxia should be delayed until 8 weeks post-injury to allow for potential spontaneous recovery.

questions.question:
A 10-month-old male child diagnosed with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and normal preoperative electrolyte panel is undergoing cleft palate repair surgery. Following the procedure, which laboratory test should be prioritized during the initial 6-hour postoperative period?
A) Fluorescent in situ hybridization analysis
B) Serum phosphate level assessment
C) Serum calcium level assessment
D) Serum potassium level assessment
E) Serum sodium level assessment
questions.answer:
C)
Patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome are predisposed to various complications including cardiac defects, kidney problems, immunodeficiency, developmental delays, speech difficulties, psychiatric conditions, cleft palate, and disorders of calcium homeostasis. Following surgical procedures, individuals with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome face an elevated risk of developing hypocalcemia compared to patients without this genetic condition, necessitating calcium level monitoring within 6 hours post-surgery to detect and treat any abnormalities promptly. Early identification and correction of hypocalcemia is crucial to prevent increased complications and potential fatal outcomes. A is incorrect because fluorescent in situ hybridization is a diagnostic genetic test that serves no purpose in a patient with an established 22q11.2 deletion diagnosis. B is incorrect because phosphate levels are not part of standard early postoperative monitoring protocols. D is incorrect because potassium measurements are not typically required in the immediate postoperative period unless specifically indicated. E is incorrect because sodium levels are not routinely assessed in early postoperative care.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old woman seeks consultation for nipple-areolar complex reconstruction following mastectomy and silicone implant-based breast reconstruction. While discussing the advantages and disadvantages of a C-V flap procedure, she inquires about the long-term outcomes of various reconstruction methods. What is the most probable long-term complication associated with single-pedicle nipple-areolar reconstruction?
A) Atrophic scarring
B) Delayed nipple necrosis
C) Hypertrophic scarring
D) Implant exposure
E) Loss of projection
questions.answer:
E)

Loss of projection is the most common long-term complication of single-pedicle nipple reconstructions because these flaps rely on random-pattern blood supply from the subdermal plexus and tend to flatten over time due to tissue contraction and remodeling. A) Atrophic scarring is incorrect because while it can occur, it is not the predominant long-term issue and depends more on individual patient factors than the reconstruction technique itself. B) Delayed nipple necrosis is incorrect because the original nipple is absent after mastectomy, and if flap necrosis occurs, it typically happens in the early postoperative period rather than as a late complication. C) Hypertrophic scarring is incorrect because although possible, it is not the most frequent long-term problem and is more related to patient healing characteristics than the specific flap technique. D) Implant exposure is incorrect because this represents an early complication associated with wound breakdown rather than a late sequela of the nipple reconstruction itself.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male patient is planned for mandibular resection with floor of mouth excision due to malignancy. An osteocutaneous radial forearm free flap is under consideration. Which of the following represents the most significant contraindication for this flap procedure?
A) Positive Allen test result
B) Tumor located in the anterior mandible
C) Reconstructive defect measuring 8 cm in length
D) Previous radiation therapy exposure
E) Absence of ipsilateral neck vessels suitable as recipients
questions.answer:
A)
A positive Allen test result is the most significant contraindication because the osteocutaneous radial forearm free flap depends on the radial artery as its blood supply, which is a primary source of circulation to the hand. A positive Allen test indicates inadequate ulnar artery circulation, making harvest of the radial artery dangerous as it could compromise hand perfusion. B is incorrect because anterior mandibular location is actually well-suited for this flap type due to its ability to be contoured with osteotomies. C is incorrect because defects up to 10 cm or more can be safely reconstructed with this flap according to multiple studies. D is incorrect because the well-vascularized bone component tolerates irradiated recipient sites well. E is incorrect because the flap's long pedicle length typically allows anastomosis to ipsilateral transverse cervical vessels or even contralateral neck vessels without requiring vein grafts.

questions.question:
A 75-year-old male patient with dilated cardiomyopathy is being managed in the intensive care unit. He was originally hospitalized for sepsis 6 weeks ago and has remained in the ICU since admission. The medical team observed loss of appetite, fatigue, a widespread non-itchy perifollicular rash, and impaired healing of minor cuts and contusions. The ascorbic acid (vitamin C) concentration is 5 μmol/L (normal range 45 to 90 μmol/L). This deficient ascorbic acid concentration is most likely to compromise lysyl oxidase function and which of the following processes in wound repair?
A) Collagen cross-linking
B) Collagen degradation
C) Collagen protein translation
D) Procollagen cleavage
E) Procollagen trafficking
questions.answer:
A)
The correct answer is A because lysyl oxidase is a crucial enzyme in wound healing that specifically requires vitamin C as a cofactor for catalyzing collagen cross-linking, which stabilizes collagen fibrils and is essential for proper wound repair. B is incorrect because collagen degradation is primarily mediated by collagenase enzymes, not lysyl oxidase. C is incorrect because collagen protein translation occurs through standard ribosomal mechanisms and does not depend on lysyl oxidase. D is incorrect because procollagen cleavage is performed by specific procollagen C- and N-proteinases, not lysyl oxidase. E is incorrect because procollagen trafficking is thought to be mediated by COP-I and COP-II transport complexes, not lysyl oxidase.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old female comes for surgical correction of an underdeveloped left breast. Physical examination reveals a concave left chest wall, missing anterior axillary fold, and a small, superiorly positioned nipple. Which of the following findings would most likely be observed in the left upper limb of this patient?
A) Acrosyndactyly
B) Arachnodactyly
C) Macrodactyly
D) Polydactyly
E) Symbrachydactyly
questions.answer:
E)
This patient has Poland syndrome, which is characterized by breast and/or nipple-areola hypoplasia, absence of the pectoralis major's sternal portion, rib deformities, and symbrachydactyly (webbed and shortened fingers). A) Acrosyndactyly is incorrect because it involves only distal digit fusion and is not typically part of Poland syndrome. B) Arachnodactyly is incorrect as it refers to abnormally long fingers and is not associated with this condition. C) Macrodactyly is incorrect because it involves digit enlargement and overgrowth, which is not a feature of Poland syndrome. D) Polydactyly is incorrect as it involves extra digits and is not commonly seen in Poland syndrome.

questions.question:
A 67-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with facial asymmetry one week following facelift and neck lift surgery. On examination, during a complete smile, the left corner of the mouth sits lower than the right corner. Which nerve has most likely sustained damage?
A) Left cervical branch
B) Left marginal mandibular branch
C) Mental nerve
D) Right cervical branch
E) Right marginal mandibular branch
questions.answer:
E)
The right marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve is the most likely injured structure. This nerve controls the ipsilateral lower lip depressor muscles, mentalis muscle, and portions of the orbicularis oris. When damaged, it causes weakness on the affected side, making the opposite (left) lower lip appear to droop during smiling. The marginal mandibular nerve runs beneath the platysma and SMAS layers but becomes vulnerable near the mandibular notch where these protective layers thin out, making it susceptible to surgical trauma and electrocautery injury during facelift procedures. A) Left cervical branch is incorrect because injury here would affect the same side as the apparent weakness, not cause contralateral drooping. B) Left marginal mandibular branch is incorrect as this would cause right-sided lip drooping, opposite to what is observed. C) Mental nerve is incorrect because this is purely a sensory nerve providing sensation to the lower lip and chin, not motor function. D) Right cervical branch is incorrect because while it innervates some lower lip depressors, it does not control the mentalis or orbicularis oris muscles that contribute to the complete clinical picture.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old female patient seeks consultation for aesthetic nose surgery. She continuously tells the physician that her appearance is "hideous" and she "cannot tolerate" her nasal structure. Clinical examination reveals no objective findings supporting her complaints. Her history reveals five consultations with various plastic surgeons over the previous 4 months, with all practitioners declining to operate. The physician declines the procedure and directs her to a mental health professional. This physician's action exemplifies which of the following ethical principles?
A) Beneficence
B) Iniquity
C) Justice
D) Maleficence
E) Noxiousness
questions.answer:
A)
By declining to operate on a patient showing signs of body dysmorphic disorder and instead directing her to a mental health professional, the physician demonstrates beneficence—the ethical duty to act in the patient's best interest and promote wellbeing. B) Iniquity is incorrect because it refers to unfairness or wrongdoing, which does not apply here. C) Justice is incorrect because while it involves fair distribution of healthcare resources, this scenario focuses on individual patient care rather than resource allocation. D) Maleficence is incorrect because it means causing harm, whereas the physician is preventing potential harm. E) Noxiousness is incorrect because it refers to causing damage or harm, opposite to what the physician is doing.

questions.question:
A 6-year-old female patient with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is evaluated in the clinic by her caregivers. The caregivers express difficulty comprehending the child's speech. Velopharyngeal insufficiency is being considered. Which of the following findings would most strongly suggest this dysfunction?
A) Missing consonant sounds
B) Glottal substitution
C) Reduced nasal resonance
D) Air escape through the nose
E) Lateral production of sibilants
questions.answer:
D)
Air escape through the nose, together with excessive nasal resonance and facial muscle tension, represents typical manifestations seen in individuals with velopharyngeal insufficiency or velopharyngeal dysfunction. Missing consonant sounds and glottal substitutions are frequent abnormal compensatory speech behaviors that these individuals develop, but they result from the patient's attempts to adapt rather than being direct consequences of the velopharyngeal problem. While some individuals with velopharyngeal dysfunction may demonstrate reduced nasal resonance or lateral sibilant production, these features are not related to the velopharyngeal insufficiency itself or represent compensatory mechanisms for this condition.

questions.question:
A 2-year-old child with cleft palate and repeated serous otitis media episodes due to compromised eustachian tube function is planned for palatal reconstruction. During palate repair, restoration of which muscle is most likely to enhance eustachian tube function?
A) Levator veli palatini
B) Palatopharyngeus
C) Salpingopharyngeus
D) Superior constrictor
E) Tensor veli palatini
questions.answer:
A)
Restoring the levator veli palatini muscle during cleft palate reconstruction is most likely to improve eustachian tube function. In normal anatomy, contraction of the levator veli palatini with superior and posterior movement of the levator sling opens the eustachian tube. In unrepaired cleft palate, this muscle's abnormal insertion on the posterior hard palate prevents proper eustachian tube opening. Surgical repositioning of this muscle during repair restores the levator sling mechanism, allowing proper tube dilation. B) Palatopharyngeus is incorrect because it primarily functions in velopharyngeal closure and medial pharyngeal wall displacement, not eustachian tube opening. C) Salpingopharyngeus is incorrect because despite its role in tube function, it is the smallest and least functionally significant of the paratubal muscles. D) Superior constrictor is incorrect because it forms the Passavant ridge and causes medial pharyngeal wall displacement through sphincteric action, not eustachian tube opening. E) Tensor veli palatini is incorrect because its function is typically unaffected by clefting, and its ability to open the tube may actually be reduced during surgical repair through hamular fracture or tendon division.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old female patient presents for evaluation of lower eyelid surgery. Physical examination reveals the presence of a negative vector. Following the procedure, this individual faces heightened risk for developing which of the following complications?
A) Dystopia
B) Ectropion
C) Enophthalmos
D) Lagophthalmos
E) Proptosis
questions.answer:
B)
The presence of a negative vector significantly increases the patient's risk for developing lower eyelid malposition and ectropion following surgery. A negative vector describes the anatomical relationship seen on lateral examination where the most prominent point of the eyeball projects less than the most prominent point of the infraorbital-malar region. This anatomical configuration suggests inadequate globe and eyelid support from the underlying skeletal structure, often presenting with subtle scleral show or lateral eyelid lag preoperatively. Recognition of this finding is crucial before surgery to implement preventive measures such as primary lid suspension during the blepharoplasty procedure. A) Dystopia is incorrect because it refers to globe malposition due to orbital skeletal changes, typically resulting from trauma or tumor resection rather than blepharoplasty complications. C) Enophthalmos is incorrect as it involves inward displacement of the globe due to increased orbital volume and is unrelated to lower blepharoplasty procedures. D) Lagophthalmos is incorrect because it represents incomplete upper eyelid closure, which is a complication of upper blepharoplasty from excessive tissue removal or scarring, not lower lid surgery. E) Proptosis is incorrect as it involves forward displacement of the globe, commonly associated with thyroid eye disease, trauma, or increased intracranial pressure, not typical lower blepharoplasty complications.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female patient desires facial enhancement using dermal fillers. Her aesthetic treatment plan involves using a highly cross-linked hyaluronic acid-based injectable product in the midface region to address volume depletion. For optimal volumization and rejuvenation of this anatomical area, into which tissue plane should the filler be placed?
A) Intradermal
B) Preperiosteal
C) Subdermal
D) Subperiosteal
E) Throughout multiple layers of soft tissue from deep to superficial
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is preperiosteal placement. For midface volume restoration, highly cross-linked hyaluronic acid fillers should be injected at the preperiosteal level to achieve optimal aesthetic outcomes while minimizing complications. These dense, stable fillers have enhanced cohesivity and longevity due to cross-linking, creating larger molecules with viscoelastic properties similar to fat. Preperiosteal placement provides the ideal depth for volume restoration while reducing risks of vascular compromise or visible irregularities. A) Intradermal injection is incorrect because it is too superficial for midface volume restoration and would not address the underlying volume loss. C) Subdermal placement is incorrect as it lacks the depth needed for significant volume enhancement in the midface region. D) Subperiosteal injection is incorrect because it places the filler too deep, directly against bone, which may not provide optimal aesthetic results. E) Multi-layer injection is incorrect as it increases complexity and potential complications without providing superior results compared to proper preperiosteal placement.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male presents for evaluation of a 1-cm metacarpal bone gap following a gunshot injury to his hand. Along with surgical stabilization of the fracture, which of the following graft materials inserted into the defect would be most effective at stimulating new bone formation?
A) Hydroxyapatite calcium phosphate
B) Autogenous cancellous bone
C) Allogeneic cortical bone
D) Demineralized bone matrix
E) Polymethylmethacrylate
questions.answer:
B)
Autogenous cancellous bone is the material most likely to stimulate osteogenesis. Osteogenesis requires viable cells within the graft material that can survive transplantation and directly produce new bone tissue. Cancellous autograft contains living osteoblasts and osteocytes that maintain viability after transfer, making it superior for true bone formation. A) is incorrect because hydroxyapatite calcium phosphate provides only osteoconduction (scaffold for bone ingrowth) without viable cells for osteogenesis. C) is incorrect because allogeneic cortical bone lacks living cells due to processing and sterilization, limiting it to osteoconductive properties. D) is incorrect because demineralized bone matrix provides osteoinduction through growth factors but contains no viable cells for direct osteogenesis. E) is incorrect because polymethylmethacrylate is a non-biodegradable cement that provides structural support but has no capacity for bone formation or replacement.

questions.question:
A 4-month-old male infant is brought to the office with the multiple extremity findings shown in the photographs. Which of the following additional clinical findings is most commonly seen with this condition?


A) Absence of the sternocostal head of the pectoralis major
B) Bilateral symmetric anomalies
C) Clubfoot
D) Craniosynostosis
E) Hematopoietic changes
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


This child has constriction ring syndrome (CRS). CRS is a rare occurrence, with the incidence reported from 1 in 1200 to 15,000 births. CRS frequently affects multiple extremities asymmetrically, with an average of three extremities involved, most often at the distal aspect of the extremity. Several characteristics are most often seen in the affected extremities including constriction rings, amputations, lymphedema distal to the ring, and acrosyndactyly (digits are fused distally, but proximally have fenestrations as fusion occurred after apoptosis in utero). Amputation or hypoplasia is usually seen distal to the ring, whereas the proximal aspect is intact and usually well-formed. CRS affecting the hands most frequently affects the index, middle, and ring fingers. Associated anomalies include syndactyly, oligodactyly, clubfoot, limb absences, body-wall defects (e.g., gastroschisis), and craniofacial anomalies, particularly facial clefts.


Symbrachydactyly, which is associated with Poland syndrome, is usually present in one limb. There is true hypoplasia of the affected extremity with absent or rudimentary digits with nubbins and frequent syndactyly. Symbrachydactyly usually impacts the central digits. Poland syndrome is defined by the absence of the sternocostal head of the pectoralis major.


Hematopoietic changes can be seen in radial hypoplasia. Fanconi anemia and thrombocytopenia (thrombocytopenia absent radius syndrome) are both associated with radial hypoplasia.


Children with Apert syndrome (acrocephalosyndactyly) have bilateral relatively symmetric complex syndactyly, symphalangism, and craniosynostosis.


ReferencesKawamura K, Chung KC. Constriction band syndrome. Hand Clin. 2009;25(2):257-264.Netscher DT, Baumholtz MA. Treatment of congenital upper extremity problems. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2007;119(5):101e-129e.Oda T, Pushman AG, Chung KC. Treatment of common congenital hand conditions. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010;126(3):121e-133e.Kay SP, McCombe DB, Kozin SH. Constriction ring syndrome (amniotic disruption sequence or amniotic band syndrome). In: Wolfe SW, Hotchkiss RN, Pederson WC, Kozin SH, Cohen MS, Eds. Green's Operative Hand Surgery. 7th ed. Elsevier; 2017, 36: 1217-1288.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old male arrives with a deep cut on the palm side of his lower forearm after hitting glass. He requires immediate surgery to fix several severed flexor tendons, nerves, and arteries. Which statement correctly describes how the flexor digitorum superficialis tendons are positioned so that the cut ends can be properly identified and sutured together?
A) The index and middle superficialis tendons lie in front of the ring and little finger superficialis tendons
B) The index and little finger superficialis tendons lie in front of the middle and ring superficialis tendons
C) The index, middle, ring, and little finger superficialis tendons are positioned next to each other
D) The middle and ring superficialis tendons lie in front of the index and little finger superficialis tendons
E) The ring and little finger superficialis tendons lie in front of the index and middle superficialis tendons
questions.answer:
D)
The middle and ring superficialis tendons are positioned superficially (anteriorly) relative to the index and little finger superficialis tendons in the distal forearm region. This anatomical arrangement is crucial for surgeons to properly identify and align the severed tendon ends during repair of complex "spaghetti wrist" injuries. A is incorrect because it reverses the actual positioning - the index and middle tendons are deeper, not more superficial. B is incorrect as it places the index and little finger tendons superficially when they are actually positioned deeper. C is incorrect because the superficialis tendons are not arranged in a single plane side-by-side; they have a layered configuration. E is incorrect as it positions the ring and little finger tendons superficially, when only the ring tendon (along with the middle) is in the superficial layer.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old male patient received one cryolipolysis treatment session. His BMI prior to treatment was 28.5 kg/m2. The treatment duration was 60 minutes using a large applicator positioned on the lower abdominal area below the umbilicus. Following treatment, minor swelling accompanied by skin redness was observed. Two months post-cryolipolysis, the treatment site gradually enlarged in dimensions. The region remained non-tender but demonstrated increased firmness and thickness compared to adjacent abdominal tissue. These clinical findings most likely indicate which condition?
A) Hematoma formation
B) Lymphocele development
C) Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia
D) Seroma collection
E) Overall weight increase
questions.answer:
C)
Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia (PAH) is the correct diagnosis. This represents a recognized adverse effect of cryolipolysis characterized by localized fat tissue enlargement in the treated region rather than the expected fat reduction. The patient exhibits classic features: male gender, large applicator use, abdominal location, and progressive tissue thickening months after treatment - all established risk factors for PAH development. A) Hematoma is incorrect because hematomas typically present acutely with pain and discoloration, not progressive enlargement months later. B) Lymphocele is incorrect as these fluid collections would be softer and fluctuant rather than firm and thick. D) Seroma is incorrect because seromas are fluid-filled cavities that would feel soft and mobile, not firm tissue thickening. E) Weight gain is incorrect as this would cause generalized rather than localized tissue changes in the specific treatment area.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male patient with spinal cord injury resulting in paraplegia and diabetes is being assessed for a stage 4 ischial pressure sore. After optimizing nutritional status and glycemic management, extensive debridement of the wound and affected bone with regional flap reconstruction is being considered. Which of the following factors increases this patient's likelihood of ulcer recurrence in the future?
A) Patient age exceeding 45 years
B) Wound area larger than 20 cm2
C) Glycated hemoglobin level below 6%
D) Anatomical site of the pressure sore
E) Bone infection verified through biopsy
questions.answer:
D)
The anatomical location of this ischial pressure ulcer represents the most significant risk factor for future recurrence in this patient. Ischial pressure sores have particularly high recurrence rates due to the excessive pressure forces experienced over the ischial tuberosities during sitting, with pressures often exceeding 80-100 mmHg compared to 60 mmHg over the sacrum when lying down. A) is incorrect because advanced age (over 45 years) is actually associated with dehiscence risk rather than recurrence, and younger age (under 45) poses greater risk for complications. B) is incorrect because defect size greater than 20 cm2 has not been shown to correlate with increased recurrence rates in clinical studies. C) is incorrect because excellent glycemic control (HbA1c <6%) is protective rather than harmful, while poor diabetic control (HbA1c >6%) increases recurrence risk. E) is incorrect because the presence of osteomyelitis confirmed by bone biopsy has not been demonstrated to increase recurrence rates in research studies.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old male presents with persistent right wrist discomfort following a car accident. Radiographic imaging reveals no bone breaks and proper carpal alignment. The Watson scaphoid shift maneuver yields a positive result. Which diagnostic approach provides the greatest sensitivity and specificity for identifying this condition?
A) Standard posteroanterior radiograph
B) Wrist arthroscopy
C) Grip compression radiograph
D) Computed tomography
E) Magnetic resonance arthrography
questions.answer:
B)
Wrist arthroscopy represents the gold standard for diagnosing scapholunate and other intercarpal ligament injuries because it allows direct visualization of the damaged structures. The scapholunate ligament is optimally viewed through the 3,4 portal, with midcarpal arthroscopy also recommended for comprehensive evaluation. This procedure serves as the benchmark against which all other diagnostic methods are measured. A) is incorrect because standard radiographs often appear normal in dynamic scapholunate instability and may not show changes for months.
