A 36-year-old expectant mother receives standard prenatal ultrasound imaging. Assessment of the developing fetus reveals limb buds are present but digits have not yet separated. Considering the developmental timeline of upper limb formation, at which gestational age has the fetus most likely arrived?
A) 2 Weeks
B) 5 Weeks
C) 8 Weeks
D) 11 Weeks
E) 14 Weeks
questions.answer:
B)
Embryonic upper limb development follows a well-established timeline. At 5 weeks of gestation, limb buds are clearly formed but digital separation has not yet occurred, which matches the ultrasound findings described. A) is incorrect because at 2 weeks gestation, limb buds have not yet developed. C) is incorrect because by 8 weeks, digital separation is nearly complete and individual fingers would be visible. D) and E) are incorrect because at 11 and 14 weeks respectively, the digits would be fully separated and well-developed, far beyond the stage described in the question.

questions.question:
What complication is most commonly observed in patients following superficial parotidectomy performed for sialadenitis management?
A) Frey syndrome developing 3 months after surgery
B) Hematoma formation beyond the initial 24-hour period
C) Irreversible facial nerve impairment
D) Formation of salivary fistulae
E) Development of tinnitus
questions.answer:
D)
Patients with sialadenitis have an elevated risk for developing salivary fistulae following superficial parotidectomy. A) is incorrect because Frey syndrome typically presents much later (median 11 months) due to auriculotemporal nerve injury and abnormal regeneration. B) is incorrect because hematoma is an early complication occurring within the first 24 hours, not after. C) is incorrect because while facial nerve dysfunction affects up to 60% of patients, approximately 90% experience resolution without surgical intervention, making permanent dysfunction uncommon. E) is incorrect because tinnitus is not a recognized complication associated with superficial parotidectomy procedures.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old male presents for reconstruction of a 4 × 3-cm soft-tissue defect in the middle third of the lower leg with exposed mid-tibial fracture. A proximally based medial hemisoleus muscle flap is being considered for coverage. Which of the following vessels is the primary blood supply source for this flap?
A) Anterior tibial
B) Dorsalis pedis
C) Medial sural
D) Peroneal
E) Posterior tibial
questions.answer:
E)
The posterior tibial artery provides the primary vascular supply to the medial hemisoleus muscle flap. The soleus is a bipennate muscle situated in the superficial posterior compartment beneath the gastrocnemius, with medial fibers originating from the posterior tibia and lateral fibers from the posterior fibula. When harvested as a medial hemisoleus flap for middle-third lower leg defects, it receives its dominant blood supply from posterior tibial artery branches, making it most reliable when based proximally. A is incorrect because the anterior tibial artery does not supply the medial hemisoleus. B is incorrect because the dorsalis pedis artery (continuation of anterior tibial) does not contribute to this flap's blood supply. C is incorrect because the medial sural artery primarily supplies the medial gastrocnemius muscle, not the hemisoleus. D is incorrect because the peroneal artery supplies the lateral hemisoleus portion, not the medial hemisoleus used in this flap.

questions.question:
Which patient below would be considered suitable for organ donation?
A) 30-year-old individual with HIV infection
B) 10-year-old child whose parents refuse donation
C) 42-year-old person diagnosed with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
D) 49-year-old individual recently diagnosed with metastatic melanoma
questions.answer:
A)
The 30-year-old HIV-positive individual is eligible for organ donation. Current guidelines allow HIV-positive donors to donate organs to HIV-positive recipients, making HIV status no longer an absolute contraindication. B is incorrect because minors cannot donate organs without parental or guardian consent, and the family has explicitly refused. C is incorrect because Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and other prion diseases are absolute contraindications to organ donation due to transmission risk. D is incorrect because stage IV melanoma represents metastatic cancer, which is a contraindication for organ donation due to risk of transmitting malignancy to recipients.

questions.question:
Which cranial nerve provides motor innervation to the inferior oblique muscle of the eye?
A) Oculomotor (III)
B) Trochlear (IV)
C) Trigeminal (V)
D) Abducens (VI)
E) Facial (VII)
questions.answer:
A)
The inferior oblique muscle is supplied by the oculomotor nerve (cranial nerve III). This nerve also innervates several other extraocular muscles including the levator palpebrae superioris, superior rectus, medial rectus, and inferior rectus muscles. The inferior oblique uniquely originates from the medial orbital floor near the infraorbital rim rather than the orbital apex, travels laterally and posteriorly beneath the inferior rectus, and inserts on the posterior globe under the lateral rectus. Its primary function is ocular elevation. B) is incorrect because the trochlear nerve (IV) innervates only the superior oblique muscle. C) is incorrect because the trigeminal nerve (V) provides sensory innervation to orbital structures but does not supply motor function to extraocular muscles. D) is incorrect because the abducens nerve (VI) specifically innervates the lateral rectus muscle. E) is incorrect because the facial nerve (VII) controls facial expression muscles and some parasympathetic functions but does not innervate extraocular muscles.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male presents for evaluation of a traumatic heel wound on the plantar surface after sustaining a calcaneal fracture to his left foot. A pedicled fasciocutaneous flap from the plantar arch area is planned for reconstruction. Which of the following most accurately describes where the vascular pedicle of this flap is anatomically positioned?
A) Located between the abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis muscles
B) Positioned between the flexor digitorum brevis and abductor digiti minimi muscles
C) Situated between the flexor hallucis brevis and adductor hallucis muscles
D) Found between the flexor hallucis longus and quadratus plantae muscles
E) Running between the extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus tendons
questions.answer:
A)
The medial plantar artery flap is the appropriate choice for plantar heel reconstruction as it provides sensate, glabrous tissue similar to the weight-bearing plantar surface. This artery, which is a terminal division of the posterior tibial artery, travels in the fascial plane between the abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis muscles, making option A correct. The flap can include medial plantar nerve fibers for sensation and provides reliable coverage with appropriate tissue characteristics including fibro-fatty tissue and plantar fascia. Option B is incorrect because the lateral plantar artery, not the medial plantar artery, runs between the flexor digitorum brevis and abductor digiti minimi. Option C is incorrect as no major reconstructive arterial pedicle is found in this muscle interval. Option D is incorrect because this anatomical space does not contain a primary arterial supply suitable for flap reconstruction. Option E is incorrect because this describes the location of the dorsalis pedis artery on the dorsal foot, which is not relevant to plantar reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old female presents with a 12-month history of discomfort and swelling in the right supraorbital region. Her medical history includes café-au-lait macules, early onset puberty, and a recent spontaneous rib fracture. What is the most probable pathological diagnosis for this lesion?
A) Epidermoid cyst
B) Fibrous dysplasia
C) Schwannoma
D) Osteosarcoma
E) Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma
questions.answer:
B)
This patient demonstrates the characteristic triad of McCune-Albright syndrome: polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, early puberty, and café-au-lait skin pigmentation. McCune-Albright syndrome may also involve hyperactive endocrine disorders such as excessive growth hormone production. When accompanied by intramuscular myxomas, this condition is termed Mazabraud syndrome. Malignant transformation of fibrous dysplasia occurs in approximately 4% of McCune-Albright cases. Treatment is tailored to symptom severity and functional impairment, typically requiring surgical intervention. A) is incorrect because epidermoid cysts typically present without pain and are usually diagnosed much earlier in childhood. C) is incorrect because while schwannomas may be associated with café-au-lait spots in neurofibromatosis, they do not cause precocious puberty or pathologic fractures. D) is incorrect because osteosarcoma would not present with the endocrine features or skin pigmentation seen in this case. E) is incorrect because embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma does not cause the constellation of findings including café-au-lait spots, precocious puberty, and pathologic fractures.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old man comes to the office 1 week after he sustained an avulsion injury to the soft tissue of the dorsal aspect of the left thumb while firing his crossbow. Moist dressing changes have not resulted in granulation tissue over the tendon. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate definitive treatment of the defect?


A) Alginate dressing changes
B) Cross-finger flap transfer
C) First dorsal metacarpal artery flap transfer
D) Full-thickness skin grafting
E) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.







In this patient with exposed tendon denuded of tenosynovium (as evidenced by the photo and failure to granulate) flap coverage with the first dorsal metacarpal artery flap, or ‚Äukite‚Äu flap, will provide closure of the wound with similar skin to what has been lost with minimal morbidity. Apart from reaching the thumb dorsal surface, this flap has been successfully used to resurface palmar wounds of the thumb. Photographs of the flap are shown.


Alginate dressings would keep the wound moist but would not add to the conservative management of dressing changes the patient has already tried.


Skin-graft take relies on adequate granulation tissue in the recipient site to survive. Here neither split- nor full-thickness grafts would be likely to take. Furthermore, grafts directly to tenosynovium can limit tendon excursion after healing.


Cross-finger flaps are useful for resurfacing the palmar defects of adjacent digits. Reversed/turnover cross-finger flaps, or cross-finger fascial flaps, can resurface adjacent digits. Wound closure then requires skin grafting of the fascial flap at the recipient site.


References
1. Delikonstantinou IP, Gravvanis AI, Dimitriou V, et al. Foucher first dorsal metacarpal artery flap versus littler heterodigital neurovascular flap in resurfacing thumb pulp loss defects. Ann Plast Surg. 2011 Aug;67(2):119-22.
2. Muyldermans T, Hierner R. First dorsal metacarpal artery flap for thumb reconstruction: a retrospective clinical study. Strategies Trauma Limb Reconstr. 2009 Apr;4(1):27-33.

questions.question:
Following acoustic neuroma removal requiring facial nerve sacrifice, which reconstructive approach offers the most rapid return of spontaneous reflexive eyelid closure?
A) Contralateral facial nerve grafting
B) Free muscle flap transfer
C) Eyelid weight implantation
D) Same-side nerve grafting
E) Regional nerve transfer
questions.answer:
E)
Regional nerve transfer provides the fastest restoration of reflexive blinking. Transferring a nearby motor nerve, such as the masseter nerve, allows for rapid reinnervation of the orbicularis oculi muscle since the distance for nerve regeneration is minimal. A) Contralateral facial nerve grafting is incorrect because it requires extensive regeneration across a long distance, significantly delaying functional recovery. B) Free muscle flap transfer is incorrect as these procedures use non-facial nerve innervation, preventing coordinated reflexive movements. C) Eyelid weight implantation is incorrect because it provides only passive, gravity-dependent closure without true reflexive function. D) Same-side nerve grafting is incorrect as it still requires time for nerve regeneration at 1mm per day across the graft length, making it slower than direct nerve transfer.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old female presents to the clinic with a 6-cm fast-growing mass in her left breast. She typically wears a 36C bra. The lesion appears bluish in color with prominent superficial veins. Following diagnosis of a phyllodes tumor, surgical removal is recommended. What is the most suitable surgical approach for this patient?
A) Removal with 1-cm clear margin
B) Removal with 2-cm clear margin
C) Diagnostic excisional biopsy
D) Modified radical mastectomy
E) Radical mastectomy
questions.answer:
A)
Phyllodes tumors are typically large benign masses that predominantly affect women in the perimenopausal period. Historically called cystosarcoma phyllodes due to their fleshy appearance and leaf-like growth pattern, this terminology is misleading since these lesions rarely exhibit malignant behavior. These tumors are essentially large fibroadenomas with increased stromal cellularity compared to typical fibroadenomas. The distinction between benign and malignant phyllodes tumors is often unclear, with borderline lesions showing increased mitotic activity and nuclear abnormalities that may recur locally but don't demonstrate true malignant characteristics. True metastases are rare and typically contain obvious sarcomatous components. Current surgical management has evolved from the previously recommended mastectomy to more conservative approaches. Contemporary practice favors excision with 1-cm negative margins, with mastectomy reserved only when breast-conserving surgery is not feasible. B is incorrect because 2-cm margins are unnecessarily wide for phyllodes tumors and current guidelines recommend 1-cm margins. C is incorrect because excisional biopsy alone without adequate margins would lead to high recurrence rates. D is incorrect because modified radical mastectomy is overly aggressive for benign phyllodes tumors when breast conservation is possible. E is incorrect because radical mastectomy is unnecessarily extensive and is no longer recommended for phyllodes tumors.

questions.question: A 75-year-old woman with a history of right mastectomy and irradiation therapy presents with a sarcoma that requires radical resection and partial sternectomy. A photograph is shown. A pedicled flap is planned to repair the defect. Which of the following arteries supplies the most appropriate flap in this situation?A) Deep inferior epigastricB) Internal mammaryC) Lateral thoracicD) ThoracoacromialE) Thoracodorsal
questions.answer: The correct response is Option E.The most appropriate pedicled flap for this particular defect is a latissimus flap, shown in the photograph, supplied by the thoracodorsal artery. The latissimus flap is a Mathes/Nahai type V flap that can be transferred on its dominant pedicle (thoracodorsal artery) or on multiple segmental paraspinal perforators. The internal mammary artery terminates as the superior epigastric artery, which would provide blood supply for a superiorly based vertical rectus flap. The rectus flap is a Mathes/Nahai type III flap, with two dominant pedicles. However, this pedicle is not available because of the radical resection and prior irradiation. The lateral thoracic artery is one of two dominant pedicles supplying the serratus anterior muscle (Mathes/Nahai type III). This flap is an option, but it would not provide enough bulk necessary for the defect in this situation. The deep inferior epigastric artery (DIEA) supplies the DIEA perforator flap, which would be an option as a free tissue transfer but not as a pedicle flap for this situation.ReferencesLatissimus Dorsi Flap. In: Zenn MR, Jones G, ed. Reconstructive Surgery. St. Louis, MO: Quality Medical Publishing; 2012:727-757.Veronesi G, Scanagatta P, Goldhirsch A, et al. Results of chest wall resection for recurrent or locally advanced breast malignancies. Breast. 2007 Jun;16(3):297-302.Netscher DT, Baumholtz MA. Chest reconstruction: I. Anterior and anterolateral chest wall and wounds affecting respiratory function. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009 Nov;124(5):240e-52e.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old female patient presents for evaluation of transverse wrinkles located at the nasal root and in the area between her brows. Which muscle would be most precisely addressed by treatment?
A) Corrugator supercilii
B) Depressor septi nasi
C) Frontalis
D) Orbicularis oculi
E) Procerus
questions.answer:
E)
The procerus muscle extends from the nasal bones to the glabellar skin, and its contraction creates transverse wrinkles in the glabellar area. A) Corrugator supercilii is incorrect because it primarily causes vertical glabellar lines rather than horizontal ones. B) Depressor septi nasi is incorrect because it affects nasal tip position and does not influence forehead wrinkles. C) Frontalis is incorrect because it creates horizontal wrinkles across the upper forehead above the eyebrows, not at the nasal root. D) Orbicularis oculi is incorrect because it functions as an eyelid sphincter and contributes to vertical glabellar lines, not horizontal ones.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old pregnant woman seeks counseling about the probability that her upcoming second baby will develop cleft lip and palate. She herself was born with cleft lip and palate, and her firstborn child also has this condition. The baby's father has no personal or family history of orofacial clefts. What is the most accurate estimate of the recurrence risk for cleft lip and palate in this pregnancy?
A) 2%
B) 4%
C) 5%
D) 10%
E) 14%
questions.answer:
E)
When a parent has cleft lip and palate and already has one affected child, the recurrence risk for subsequent pregnancies is 14%. A) 2% is incorrect because this represents the baseline risk when neither parent is affected and the first child has a unilateral cleft. B) 4% is incorrect as it underestimates the risk given both parental and sibling history. C) 5% is incorrect because this would apply when neither parent is affected and the first child has a bilateral cleft. D) 10% is incorrect as this risk applies when both parents are unaffected but have already had two children with clefts.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old male child presents to the clinic for assessment of cranial morphology abnormalities. Clinical examination reveals an asymmetric head configuration, decreased frontal hairline position, drooping upper eyelids, and an enlarged helical crus. Which syndrome most likely accounts for this patient's presentation?
A) Apert
B) Crouzon
C) Muenke
D) Pfeiffer
E) Saethre-Chotzen
questions.answer:
E)
Saethre-Chotzen syndrome is the correct diagnosis as it presents with the characteristic features observed in this patient: asymmetric brachycephaly, low frontal hairline, eyelid ptosis, and prominent helical crus, caused by TWIST1 gene mutations. A) Apert syndrome is incorrect because it typically presents with complex hand and foot syndactyly, turribrachycephaly, and enlarged anterior fontanelle rather than the asymmetric features seen here. B) Crouzon syndrome is incorrect as it commonly involves exorbitism, midface hypoplasia, and hydrocephalus without the low hairline and helical abnormalities. C) Muenke syndrome is incorrect because it primarily causes coronal synostosis with hearing loss and middle phalange abnormalities, lacking the distinctive facial features present. D) Pfeiffer syndrome is incorrect as it typically presents with broad thumbs/great toes, hypertelorism, and down-slanting palpebral fissures rather than the specific combination of findings in this case.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old man who is right-handed comes to the clinic with a 4-month history of weakness in his right arm. He describes the sudden appearance of shoulder pain that occurred without any injury. Although the pain has lessened, he now has trouble lifting his arm away from his body, rotating his shoulder outward, and bending his elbow. MRI reveals hourglass-shaped narrowings of the brachial plexus. Nerve conduction studies show involvement of several peripheral nerves. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Brachial plexus tear
B) Guillain-Barré syndrome
C) Parsonage-Turner syndrome
D) Rotator cuff tear
E) Transverse myelitis
questions.answer:
C)
Parsonage-Turner syndrome, also called acute brachial neuritis or neuralgic amyotrophy, is a rare but well-documented condition. Patients typically experience sudden, severe unilateral shoulder and arm pain that spreads, followed by progressive weakness and muscle wasting in the shoulder and arm region. Pain is the presenting symptom in 90% of cases. While the cause is usually unknown, it can occur after surgery, infections, pregnancy, intense exercise, trauma, or vaccinations. The condition shows variable presentation in terms of nerve and muscle involvement, recovery extent, and recurrence. Diagnosis relies on clinical examination supported by nerve studies and imaging. Electrodiagnostic testing reveals multiple peripheral nerve lesions rather than brachial plexus localization. MRI demonstrates characteristic hourglass constrictions. The syndrome is generally self-limiting but recovery can be prolonged and incomplete, with 30% of patients never fully recovering. A) is incorrect because brachial plexus tears typically follow significant trauma and show root involvement rather than distal nerve pathology. B) is incorrect because Guillain-Barré syndrome usually follows infection or immune stimulation, presents with symmetric ascending paralysis that can progress to respiratory failure, not unilateral shoulder-focused symptoms. D) is incorrect because rotator cuff injuries maintain full shoulder range of motion and imaging findings don't match rotator cuff pathology. E) is incorrect because transverse myelitis involves bilateral motor, sensory, and autonomic spinal cord dysfunction, not unilateral peripheral nerve involvement.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old child presents to the emergency room following a crushing trauma to the index finger of his dominant right hand, causing amputation at the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint level. Radiographic imaging reveals a fragmented fracture of the proximal phalanx. What represents the most important CONTRAINDICATION to replantation in this case?
A) Pediatric patients struggle with accommodating functional limitations
B) The index digit is considered dispensable
C) The injury pattern and multi-level damage prevent achieving functional outcomes
D) Microsurgical vessel repair is improbable in a pediatric patient this young
E) Reattachment procedures will negatively impact growth plate development
questions.answer:
C)
The injury pattern and multi-level damage prevent achieving functional outcomes because crush mechanisms create extensive tissue damage and zones of injury that make successful replantation highly unlikely, and the combination of proximal phalanx fracture with DIP joint involvement makes functional restoration improbable. A is incorrect because children actually adapt remarkably well to hand function deficits. B is incorrect because while the index finger may be expendable in adults, children generally achieve better replantation outcomes than adults, making attempts worthwhile when feasible. D is incorrect because microsurgical techniques in children, though technically demanding, have demonstrated very high success rates when performed by experienced microsurgeons. E is incorrect because replantation procedures do not negatively affect growth plate function in pediatric patients.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old male presents for assessment of a 2-year history of progressive swelling in his right lower leg. He reports that the symptoms began after he returned from a year of work in Africa. Physical examination reveals pitting edema extending up to the knee level. The skin overlying the toes is non-tenting. Thyroid function tests are normal. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Venous thromboembolism
B) Lymphatic obstruction
C) Hypothyroid edema
D) Chronic venous disease
questions.answer:
B)
The most probable diagnosis is lymphatic obstruction (lymphedema). This condition results from impaired lymphatic drainage, leading to accumulation of protein-rich fluid in tissues. Key clinical features include progressive pitting edema starting distally, inability to pinch the skin over the toes (positive Stemmer sign), and unilateral presentation. The patient's history of residing in Africa raises suspicion for filarial lymphedema, which accounts for most cases worldwide. The gradual 2-year onset and characteristic physical findings support this diagnosis. A) Venous thromboembolism is incorrect because it typically presents with acute onset rather than gradual progression over years. C) Hypothyroid edema is incorrect because thyroid function tests are normal, and myxedema typically presents with bilateral involvement and characteristic skin changes. D) Chronic venous disease is incorrect because it usually presents with skin discoloration, varicosities, and a negative Stemmer sign.

questions.question:
A 68-year-old female presents with tingling and numbness affecting her right hand. Electrodiagnostic testing confirms the diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome. She wishes to attempt conservative treatment before considering surgery. The treatment plan includes nocturnal wrist splinting and steroid injection into the carpal tunnel. Which of the following most accurately describes the expected long-term results of this conservative approach?
A) Permanent elimination of all symptoms
B) Complete lack of symptomatic benefit
C) Initial absence of improvement with delayed benefit occurring over 6 to 12 months
D) Temporary symptom relief with return of symptoms within 6 to 12 months
E) Progressive deterioration of both sensory and motor function
questions.answer:
D)
Conservative treatment for carpal tunnel syndrome typically provides temporary symptom improvement lasting 3 to 6 months, but symptoms commonly recur within 6 to 12 months, with approximately 70% of patients eventually requiring surgical intervention. A is incorrect because complete permanent resolution rarely occurs with nonsurgical treatment alone. B is incorrect because conservative measures do provide initial symptomatic benefit in most cases. C is incorrect because improvement typically occurs early rather than being delayed for months. E is incorrect because conservative treatment rarely causes symptom deterioration, though it may not prevent natural disease progression in severe cases.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old male experiences traumatic loss of his right thumb at the metacarpal base level. During pollicization reconstruction, osteosynthesis should involve which of the following structures?
A) Index finger metacarpal base with trapezium bone
B) Index finger metacarpal with thumb metacarpal
C) Index finger middle phalanx with thumb metacarpal
D) Index finger proximal phalanx with thumb metacarpal
E) Index finger proximal phalanx with trapezium bone
questions.answer:
D)
Pollicization reconstruction involves transferring the index finger's proximal phalanx to the remaining thumb metacarpal when the metacarpal base is intact. This approach creates an appropriately sized and positioned neo-thumb. A is incorrect because fusing the index metacarpal base to the trapezium would eliminate the carpometacarpal joint's crucial abduction and opposition movements. B is incorrect because connecting the entire index metacarpal would result in an excessively large thumb reconstruction. C is incorrect because using only the middle phalanx would produce a thumb that is too short for adequate function. E is incorrect because attaching the proximal phalanx directly to the trapezium bypasses the preserved thumb metacarpal and compromises optimal positioning.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male arrives at the emergency department following high-velocity ejection from a motor vehicle. Clinical assessment reveals extensive bleeding from the nose and mouth along with maxillary instability. The patient demonstrates hemodynamic compromise, and alternative sources of significant hemorrhage have been ruled out. Endotracheal tube placement has been completed. What represents the most suitable immediate management approach?
A) Implementation of intermaxillary fixation
B) Nasal endoscopy with electrocautery
C) Surgical ligation of external carotid vessels
D) Installation of anterior and posterior nasal tampons
E) Catheter-directed arterial embolization
questions.answer:
D)
Following airway securement, the optimal initial approach for managing severe oronasal bleeding involves nasal tamponade. This procedure can be rapidly executed by inflating Foley balloon catheters within the posterior nasal passages, subsequently followed by anterior packing using nasal tampons or gauze strips. Studies demonstrate that nasal packing successfully stops hemorrhage in 29% of cases and significantly reduces bleeding in an additional 44% of patients. A) is incorrect because intermaxillary fixation in the emergency setting is often impractical due to equipment limitations and complications from the endotracheal tube. B) is incorrect because nasal endoscopy has limited effectiveness during active heavy bleeding due to poor visualization and difficulty identifying bleeding sources. C) is incorrect because external carotid artery ligation is rarely successful for controlling oronasal hemorrhage due to extensive collateral circulation in the head and neck region. E) is incorrect because transcatheter embolization, while highly effective, is typically reserved for cases where packing has failed and requires specialized availability.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old male baseball pitcher receives a facial injury from a baseball during training and develops an isolated medial orbital wall blowout fracture. A transcaruncular surgical approach is selected for access. Following incision of the medial conjunctiva, what is the optimal dissection plane between which two anatomical structures to access the posterior lacrimal crest?
A) Capsulopalpebral fascia and inferior rectus muscle
B) Inferior oblique muscle and Lockwood ligament
C) Lacrimal duct and medial canthal ligament
D) Horner muscle and medial orbital septum
E) Medial rectus muscle and Whitnall ligament
questions.answer:
D)
The correct dissection plane lies between the Horner muscle and medial orbital septum to expose the periosteum just posterior to the posterior lacrimal crest. This technique helps protect the more inferiorly located Lockwood ligament and the more anteriorly positioned lacrimal sac from injury. Maintaining the integrity of the septum prevents orbital fat from entering the operative field. A is incorrect because this plane is too inferior and doesn't provide proper access to the posterior lacrimal crest. B is incorrect as this dissection plane is located too far inferiorly from the target area. C is incorrect because dissection in this plane risks damage to the lacrimal drainage system and doesn't reach the appropriate surgical target. E is incorrect as this plane is positioned too far laterally and superiorly from the required access point.

questions.question:
A 9-year-old child presents with intense, progressive arm pain, digital edema, and paresthesias occurring 2 days following cast application for a bone fracture. After cast removal, a fasciotomy procedure is carried out. Which muscle below is most susceptible to injury?
A) Extensor carpi radialis brevis
B) Extensor digitorum communis
C) Extensor pollicis longus
D) Flexor digitorum profundus
E) Flexor digitorum superficialis
questions.answer:
D)

The flexor digitorum profundus is the muscle most susceptible to injury in this scenario. This patient exhibits classic signs of compartment syndrome following cast application, where increased pressure within muscle compartments compromises blood circulation and nutrient delivery. The deep flexor muscles of the forearm, particularly the flexor digitorum profundus and flexor pollicis longus, are initially affected due to their location in the deepest compartment where pressure builds first. Without prompt intervention, this leads to Volkmann's ischemic contracture with permanent muscle shortening and functional impairment. A) Extensor carpi radialis brevis is incorrect because extensor muscles are among the last to be affected in compartment syndrome. B) Extensor digitorum communis is incorrect as it is also an extensor muscle that becomes involved only in advanced cases. C) Extensor pollicis longus is incorrect since extensor compartment involvement occurs later in the progression. E) Flexor digitorum superficialis is incorrect because superficial flexor muscles are less vulnerable than deep flexor muscles due to their more superficial location with better vascular supply.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old man is referred for evaluation of a flexion deformity of the left long finger. Physical examination shows a thickened cord from the mid palm to the volar proximal phalanx of the long finger. The metacarpophalangeal joint cannot be extended beyond 30 degrees. A photograph is shown. Which of the following cells is most directly responsible for the contraction of the cord shown?


A) Macrophage
B) Merkel cell
C) Myofibroblast
D) Stem cell
E) Striated myocyte
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Myofibroblasts act on the collagen bundles deposited by fibroblasts to cause alignment into a cord and shortening of the cord. These cells also secrete extracellular matrix components that remodel in a shorter configuration, creating durability of the contracture. More mature cords are believed to be less cellular.


Macrophages are believed to act on the extracellular matrix but do not produce contracture. Striated myocytes are in skeletal muscle and are not involved in Dupuytren disease. Merkel cells are a sensory end-organ and are not involved in Dupuytren disease. Stem cells including adipocyte progenitors are known to exist in Dupuytren cords. They are hypothesized to develop into cells that affect the cord. There is no evidence that these cells act on Dupuytren cords while they are still stem cells.


References
1. Hindocha S, Iqbal SA, Farhatullah S, et al. Characterization of stem cells in Dupuytren‚Äos disease. Br J Surg. 2011 Feb;98(2):308-315.
2. Hurst L. Dupuytren‚Äos contracture. In: Wolfe SW, Pederson WC, Hotchkiss RN, Kozin SH, eds. Green's Operative Hand Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Churchill Livingstone; 2010:141-158.
3. Verjee LS, Midwood K, Davidson D, et al. Myofibroblast distribution in Dupuytren's cords: correlation with digital contracture. J Hand Surg Am. 2009 Dec;34(10):1785-1794.

questions.question:
A plastic surgeon receives a request from a community charity to provide complimentary medical services for their yearly benefit event. According to the ethical guidelines established by the American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS), which of the following treatments may be donated?
A) Breast augmentation surgery
B) Liposuction procedure
C) Botulinum toxin type A injections
D) Facelift surgery
E) None of these treatments are allowed
questions.answer:
C)
Botulinum toxin type A injections are permissible donations because they do not involve making an incision, which means they fall outside the ASPS definition of a "procedure." According to ASPS ethical guidelines (Section 2, Article I [K]), a "procedure" is specifically defined as any medical service requiring an incision. Non-incisional treatments such as botulinum toxin injections, hyaluronic acid fillers, microdermabrasion, and other surface skin treatments are not classified as procedures under this definition and may therefore be donated. A is incorrect because breast augmentation requires surgical incisions and is prohibited from donation. B is incorrect because liposuction involves incisions for cannula insertion and falls under the prohibited procedure category. D is incorrect because facelift surgery requires extensive incisions and is explicitly prohibited as a donation. E is incorrect because non-incisional treatments like botulinum toxin injections are permitted for charitable donation.

questions.question:
A 72-year-old male patient presents for assessment due to a 3-month duration of skin lesions affecting the bridge of his nose and facial cheek area (illustrated). Given his status as a high-risk surgical candidate, he receives treatment with imiquimod (Aldara). What is the most probable mechanism by which this therapy works?
A) Blocking the cyclooxygenase enzymatic pathway
B) Preventing DNA replication
C) Altering genetic transcription processes
D) Regulating cellular maturation
E) Enhancing proinflammatory cytokine release
questions.answer:
E)
Imiquimod (Aldara) functions as an immune response modifier that enhances host cytokine production and triggers programmed cell death in malignant cells, making it effective for treating actinic keratoses, viral warts, and non-melanoma skin cancers. A is incorrect because cyclooxygenase pathway inhibition is the mechanism of topical diclofenac, not imiquimod. B is incorrect because DNA synthesis inhibition describes the action of topical 5-fluorouracil. C is incorrect because gene transcription modification is how interferons work. D is incorrect because cell differentiation regulation is the mechanism of retinoids.

questions.question:
Which cranial nerve is associated with the development of the first pharyngeal arch?
A) Hypoglossal (XII)
B) Vagus (X)
C) Trigeminal (V)
D) Facial (VII)
E) Glossopharyngeal (IX)
questions.answer:
C)
The trigeminal nerve (V) is the cranial nerve that develops in association with the first pharyngeal arch. Each pharyngeal arch has a specific cranial nerve association: the first arch corresponds to the trigeminal nerve (V), the second arch to the facial nerve (VII), and the third arch to the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX). A is incorrect because the hypoglossal nerve (XII) is not associated with pharyngeal arch development. B is incorrect because the vagus nerve (X) is associated with the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches, not the first. D is incorrect because the facial nerve (VII) develops with the second pharyngeal arch. E is incorrect because the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) is associated with the third pharyngeal arch.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient is having liposuction performed on her abdomen and flanks. Using the superwet liposuction method, the anticipated blood loss most closely approximates what percentage of the total aspirated volume?
A) 0.1%
B) 1%
C) 15%
D) 30%
E) 50%
questions.answer:
B)
The most accurate estimate for blood loss during superwet or tumescent liposuction procedures is approximately 1% of the total lipoaspirate volume. This low percentage reflects the effectiveness of these techniques in minimizing bleeding through vasoconstriction and tissue infiltration. A) 0.1% is incorrect because it underestimates the actual blood loss that occurs during liposuction. C) 15% is incorrect as this percentage is too high for superwet technique, which uses adequate tumescent solution to minimize bleeding. D) 30% is incorrect because such high blood loss percentages are associated with techniques using lower ratios of tumescent infiltration, not the superwet method. E) 50% is incorrect as this represents an extremely high blood loss that would occur with inadequate tumescent technique or dry liposuction methods.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old woman presents to the clinic expressing concern about the drooping appearance of her breasts. On physical examination, both nipples are positioned 1 cm above the inframammary crease. Most of the breast parenchyma is located below this crease. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Grade 1 ptosis
B) Grade 2 ptosis
C) Grade 3 ptosis
D) Pseudoptosis
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is pseudoptosis. According to Regnault's classification system for breast ptosis, pseudoptosis occurs when the nipple remains at or above the level of the inframammary crease while the bulk of breast tissue hangs below this landmark, creating an appearance of drooping without true nipple descent. A) Grade 1 ptosis is incorrect because it involves the nipple being positioned within 1 cm below (not above) the inframammary fold while remaining above the breast's lower border. B) Grade 2 ptosis is incorrect as it describes nipple positioning 1-3 cm below the inframammary fold but still above the breast's lower contour. C) Grade 3 ptosis is incorrect because it involves the nipple being more than 3 cm below the inframammary fold and below the breast's lower border.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female presents to the clinic with a 1-year history of clicking sounds during jaw opening. She sustained facial trauma when her face hit the steering wheel in a car accident 1 year prior. On examination, her dental midline appears normal without any deviation. What is the most probable etiology of her symptoms?
A) Lateral pterygoid muscle injury
B) Intra-articular foreign material
C) Improperly healed coronoid process fracture
D) Ununited mandibular condyle fracture
E) Displaced articular disc
questions.answer:
E)
The clicking sensation during jaw movement is most commonly attributed to displaced articular disc. The disc typically sits centrally between the joint compartments of the temporomandibular joint. TMJ motion can be assessed by palpating with fingers placed in or just anterior to the external auditory canal. Initial management includes bite adjustment using splints, anti-inflammatory medications, and physiotherapy, with surgery reserved for conservative treatment failures. A) Lateral pterygoid muscle injury would more likely cause muscle dysfunction rather than clicking sounds. B) Intra-articular foreign material typically causes pain and restricted movement rather than clicking. C) Improperly healed coronoid process fracture would affect jaw opening mechanics differently. D) Ununited mandibular condyle fracture would present with different symptoms including malocclusion and limited function.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old female presents to the clinic with significant thenar muscle wasting 3 years following unsuccessful reconstruction of a distal median nerve injury. A tendon transfer procedure is being considered to restore thumb opposition. Which of the following thumb movements would an ideal transfer procedure restore?
A) Palmar abduction, extension, supination
B) Palmar abduction, flexion, pronation
C) Palmar abduction, flexion, supination
D) Radial abduction, extension, pronation
E) Radial abduction, flexion, supination
questions.answer:
B)

Median nerve injury, whether from trauma or compression, leads to thenar muscle wasting and impaired thumb opposition. When severe, chronic atrophy is present, tendon transfer represents the most dependable method for restoring thumb function. Opposition is a complex motion consisting of three components: palmar abduction, flexion, and pronation. This movement enables the thumb to position properly for grasping activities, though opposition itself is distinct from grip function. Various transfer techniques exist to enhance thumb opposition (including palmaris longus, abductor digiti minimi, and flexor digitorum superficialis transfers), with the most successful procedures addressing all three movement components. A is incorrect because extension and supination are not components of opposition. C is incorrect because supination is not part of opposition movement. D is incorrect because radial abduction, extension, and pronation do not constitute the proper combination for opposition. E is incorrect because radial abduction and supination are not involved in opposition.

questions.question:
A 70-year-old female patient presents with an 18 cm circular scalp defect on the parietal region following resection of squamous cell carcinoma. The pericranium was excised along with the scalp tissue. Postoperative radiation treatment is scheduled to begin 4 to 6 weeks following the procedure. What is the most suitable option for reconstructing this defect?
A) Free latissimus dorsi muscle flap combined with split-thickness skin grafting
B) Direct closure following galeal scoring techniques
C) Application of split-thickness skin graft alone
D) Initial reconstruction using split-thickness skin graft followed by rotation-advancement flap after tissue expansion of scalp
questions.answer:
A)
The free latissimus dorsi muscle flap combined with split-thickness skin grafting provides optimal single-stage reconstruction for extensive scalp defects, enabling the patient to receive planned radiation therapy following surgical recovery. This vascularized tissue transfer offers reliable coverage over exposed calvarium lacking pericranium and can withstand subsequent radiation treatment. B is incorrect because primary closure is typically only possible for scalp defects smaller than 3 cm, even with galeal scoring to reduce tension. C is incorrect because split-thickness grafts have poor survival rates on bare bone without pericranium, especially when followed by radiation therapy. D is incorrect because skin grafts demonstrate poor adherence to exposed calvarium without pericranium, and tissue expansion becomes more challenging and complication-prone in previously irradiated tissues.

questions.question:
An elderly 89-year-old frail male patient presents to the clinic with a large sacral pressure ulcer that has been present for 2 months. His past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and multi-infarct dementia. The patient experiences both bowel and bladder incontinence. What is the primary factor responsible for the formation of this pressure ulcer?
A) Bowel and bladder incontinence
B) Insufficient wheelchair padding
C) Poor nutritional status
D) Suboptimal diabetes management
E) Extended periods of immobilization
questions.answer:
E)
Extended periods of immobilization is the primary factor in pressure ulcer development. Pressure ulcers form when sustained pressure exceeds capillary closing pressure (32 mmHg), with pressures above 70 mmHg for 2 hours causing irreversible tissue damage. Sacral pressure ulcers develop from supine positioning where pressures reach 40-60 mmHg. Prevention requires position changes every 2 hours and pressure-redistributing surfaces for patients with impaired mobility or awareness. A) is incorrect because incontinence causes skin maceration and delayed healing but is secondary to pressure as the primary cause. B) is incorrect because inadequate cushioning contributes to ischial ulcers from sitting but the sacral location indicates prolonged recumbency as the main issue. C) is incorrect because malnutrition impairs wound healing and is a contributing factor but not the primary cause of ulcer formation. D) is incorrect because poorly controlled diabetes delays healing and increases infection risk but does not directly cause the initial tissue breakdown from pressure.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female presents to the clinic one week following bilateral breast reduction surgery. Her past medical history is unremarkable. A preoperative pregnancy test was negative. Physical examination reveals bilateral breast swelling and edema, with thick, white discharge expressible from both nipples. The patient reports no fever or general malaise. Which laboratory parameter is most likely to be elevated?
A) C-reactive protein
B) Estrogen
C) Human chorionic gonadotropin
D) Prolactin
E) White blood cells
questions.answer:
D)
The presence of bilateral milky nipple discharge following breast surgery indicates galactorrhea, an uncommon but recognized postoperative complication. This condition results from increased prolactin secretion triggered by surgical manipulation of breast tissue, periareolar incisions, or irritation of intercostal nerves that send signals to the pituitary gland. A) C-reactive protein would be incorrect as there are no signs of infection or systemic inflammation. B) Estrogen levels would be incorrect since they are typically elevated during pregnancy, which was ruled out preoperatively. C) Human chorionic gonadotropin is incorrect as this hormone is associated with pregnancy, and the preoperative test was negative. E) White blood cells would be incorrect because the absence of fever and signs of infection make leukocytosis unlikely.

questions.question:
A 14-year-old male presents to the emergency department after a fall. He has pain with eye movement, nausea, and limited abduction of the left eye. CT of the orbits shows an isolated left medial orbital wall (lamina papyracea) fracture with incarceration of the medial rectus muscle in the fracture; the orbital floor, rim, and lateral wall are intact. Urgent operative release and reconstruction are planned. Which incision provides the most suitable surgical approach?
A) Bicoronal
B) Lateral brow
C) Orbital rim
D) Subciliary
E) Transcaruncular
questions.answer:
E)
The transcaruncular approach is optimal for an isolated medial orbital wall fracture with medial rectus entrapment. It gives direct, scar-free access to the lamina papyracea and posterior medial wall, allows release of the incarcerated muscle and placement of an implant, and can be extended with a transconjunctival incision if floor involvement is present. A) A bicoronal incision provides far more exposure than needed, with greater morbidity (blood loss, alopecia, scarring, and risk to the supraorbital and frontal branch nerves), and is reserved for extensive craniofacial or naso-orbito-ethmoid injuries. B) A lateral brow incision accesses the lateral orbital rim and frontozygomatic region and does not expose the medial wall. C) An orbital rim (infraorbital skin) incision leaves a visible scar and gives limited access to the posterior medial wall, so it cannot adequately address the entrapped medial rectus. D) A subciliary incision is directed at the orbital floor and inferior rim; medial wall exposure through it is poor, and it carries the highest risk of lower lid retraction and ectropion among transcutaneous lower lid approaches.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female patient comes in with increased depth in her nasolabial and nasojugal creases and decreased midface volume. She desires dermal fillers to restore volume in these regions. A hyaluronic acid filler with an elevated elastic modulus (G') is most suitable for this patient because which of the following properties is enhanced?
A) Injection flow resistance
B) Duration of effect
C) Material rigidity
D) Hydration capacity
E) Tissue spreading
questions.answer:
C)
The elastic modulus (G') indicates a hyaluronic acid filler's capacity to withstand deforming forces and recover its initial form. Higher G' values correspond to increased material rigidity and enhanced structural support capability. A) is incorrect because injection flow resistance relates to viscous modulus (G''), not elastic modulus. B) is incorrect because duration of effect is not directly measured by G' values. D) is incorrect because hydration capacity (swelling factor) typically has an inverse relationship with G' - stiffer gels generally have lower swelling factors. E) is incorrect because materials with higher elastic modulus (greater rigidity) actually spread less through tissues when injected, not more.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a motor vehicle accident with trauma to his left lower leg. Clinical examination reveals extensive crush damage, significant soft tissue loss, and an open tibial fracture with bone exposure. The lower extremity appears cold and pallid. Distal pulses cannot be detected. Angiographic imaging demonstrates complete disruption of the popliteal artery. What is the most appropriate Gustilo classification for this patient's fracture?
A) Type I
B) Type II
C) Type IIIA
D) Type IIIB
E) Type IIIC
questions.answer:
E)
The correct classification for this injury is Gustilo Type IIIC.

The Gustilo classification system is the standard method for categorizing open lower extremity fractures. The system divides injuries into three main categories. Type I fractures feature soft-tissue wounds less than 1 cm in size. Type II fractures have wounds measuring 1 to 10 cm with moderate soft-tissue injury. Type III fractures exceed 10 cm and involve severe soft-tissue trauma, creating challenges for bone coverage or hardware placement. Type III fractures are further categorized into subtypes A, B, and C. Type IIIA fractures retain adequate soft tissue for bone coverage. Type IIIB fractures show periosteal stripping and extensive tissue loss, making local soft-tissue coverage impossible and typically resulting from high-energy trauma like gunshot wounds or severe crush injuries. Type IIIC fractures are distinguished by associated vascular damage requiring surgical repair. The presence of vascular compromise substantially elevates amputation risk.

A is incorrect because Type I fractures have minimal soft tissue damage (<1 cm wounds) without vascular injury. B is incorrect because Type II fractures have moderate soft tissue damage (1-10 cm wounds) without vascular compromise. C is incorrect because Type IIIA fractures, while having extensive soft tissue damage, maintain adequate tissue for bone coverage and lack vascular injury. D is incorrect because Type IIIB fractures have extensive soft tissue loss requiring coverage procedures but do not involve vascular injury requiring repair.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old male presents to the emergency room following complete penile amputation at the shaft base. The severed portion has been properly preserved and transported. Successful replantation is most likely achieved by revascularizing which of the following vascular structures?
A) Bulbar artery and vein
B) Cavernosal artery and vein
C) Deep dorsal arteries and vein
D) Internal pudendal artery and vein
questions.answer:
C)

The deep dorsal arteries and vein are the most critical vessels to reconnect for successful penile replantation. This vascular network consists of two deep dorsal arteries and one deep dorsal vein, which can adequately supply blood flow to the entire penile structure. These vessels are optimally positioned for microsurgical anastomosis and provide sufficient circulation for tissue viability. Option A is incorrect because the bulbar vessels are too small and less accessible for effective replantation surgery. Option B is incorrect because the cavernosal vessels, while important for erectile function, are inadequate alone for complete penile revascularization and are technically challenging to access. Option D is incorrect because the internal pudendal vessels are located too proximally from the amputation site, making surgical anastomosis impractical for replantation at the shaft base.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female presents to the clinic reporting a 2-day onset of impaired left thumb mobility. Two months prior, she experienced a non-displaced fracture of the distal radius. Her cast was removed 2 weeks ago. Physical examination reveals loss of thumb retropulsion. What is the most suitable definitive management?
A) Arthrodesis of the thumb carpometacarpal joint
B) Arthrodesis of the thumb interphalangeal joint
C) Neurotization from the anterior interosseous nerve to the median nerve recurrent branch
D) Tendon transfer from extensor indicis proprius to abductor pollicis brevis
E) Tendon transfer from extensor indicis proprius to extensor pollicis longus
questions.answer:
E)
This case represents a typical extensor pollicis longus (EPL) tendon rupture complicating a distal radius fracture, with reported occurrence rates of 0.2-3%. The rupture results from tendon impingement against hardware or ischemic changes from compartment swelling. Transfer of the extensor indicis proprius to the EPL tendon effectively restores thumb retropulsion and extension function. A) is incorrect because CMC joint fusion treats arthritis but would further limit thumb mobility rather than restore extension. B) is incorrect because IP joint fusion addresses flexor pollicis longus injuries but does not restore retropulsion. C) is incorrect because this nerve transfer addresses median nerve palsy affecting thumb opposition, not extension deficits. D) is incorrect because transferring EIP to abductor pollicis brevis restores thumb abduction/opposition but not retropulsion or extension.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old girl presents with a tender and erythematous right pretragal abscess. Upon inquiring about the pit inferior to it, her parents report only recent drainage, despite presence since birth. They deny hearing deficits but report a family history of a similar defect. Facial cellulitis and excess granulation tissue are also noted on physical examination. Photographs are shown. Malformation of which of the following embryological structures most likely accounts for these findings?


A) Hillocks
B) Meatal plug
C) Otic capsule
D) Otic vesicle
E) Tubotympanic recess
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


Auricular hillocks are ectodermal derivatives of the first pharyngeal groove and are responsible for the formation of external ear structures (e.g., auricle and external auditory canal [EAC]). Incomplete fusion of the auricular hillocks (defective closure of the dorsal 1st pharyngeal groove) results in preauricular sinus. This is the only answer choice that contributes to the development of the external ear.


The meatal plug is an ectodermal derivative of the first pharyngeal groove (extends from the medial end of the EAC), which largely degenerates/canalizes, but is responsible for formation of the surface layer of the tympanic membrane. Persistence of the meatal plug results in conductive congenital deafness.


The otic vesicle is an ectodermal derivative of the developing brain that is responsible for formation of inner ear structures (e.g., saccule, utricle, semicircular and cochlear ducts, and membranous cochlea including the spiral organ of Corti). Abnormal development of the membranous labyrinth results in sensorineural congenital deafness.


The otic capsule is derived from mesenchyme of the first and second pharyngeal arches, surrounds/is induced by the otic vesicle, and is responsible for formation of inner ear structures (e.g., bony labyrinth). Abnormal development of the bony labyrinth results in sensorineural congenital deafness.


The tubotympanic recess is an endodermal derivative of the first pharyngeal pouch, responsible for the formation of middle ear structures (e.g., auditory tube, tympanic cavity, etc.). Abnormal/under-development of the middle ear structures increases the risk for chronic otitis media and can have an effect on conductive hearing.


ReferencesHonda M, Anda T, Mori H. Surgical site infection due to a preauricular sinus: A rare complication after craniotomy. Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open. 2014;2(10):e223.Kuczkowski J, Brzoznowski W, Kobierska-Gulida G, et al. Rozpoznawanie i leczenie przetok przedusznych u dzieci [Diagnosis and treatment preauricular fistulas in children]. Otolaryngol Pol. 2011;65(3):194-198.Kumar Chowdary KV, Sateesh Chandra N, Karthik Madesh R. Preauricular sinus: a novel approach. Indian J Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2013;65(3):234-236.Leopardi G, Chiarella G, Conti S, et al. Surgical treatment of recurring preauricular sinus: supra-auricular approach. Acta Otorhinolaryngol Ital. 2008;28(6):302-305.Yoo H, Park DH, Lee IJ, et al. A surgical technique for congenital preauricular sinus. Arch Craniofac Surg. 2015;16(2):63-66.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old female presents to the clinic seeking consultation for a tummy tuck procedure one year following the birth of her first baby. After assessment, she is determined to be an appropriate candidate for surgery. The patient is wed, but attended the appointment without her spouse. What is the most suitable next course of action?
A) Secure authorization from her spouse
B) Secure authorization from one of her parents
C) Secure authorization from the patient herself
D) Reassess the patient when she turns 18 years old
E) Reassess the patient when she turns 21 years old
questions.answer:
C)
The most suitable next course of action is to secure authorization from the patient herself. Since the patient is wed and has given birth to a child, she qualifies as an emancipated minor and possesses the legal capacity to provide consent for medical treatments. The standards for emancipated minor status typically encompass: matrimony, armed forces enrollment, economic self-sufficiency, residential independence from parents, and having children. A) is incorrect because spousal consent is not required for an emancipated minor's medical decisions. B) is incorrect because parental consent is not needed when a minor is legally emancipated through marriage and parenthood. D) is incorrect because waiting until age 18 is unnecessary since she already has legal capacity to consent as an emancipated minor. E) is incorrect because age 21 has no special legal significance for medical consent, and the patient already qualifies for emancipated status.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old male child presents to the clinic for assessment. His medical background includes a congenital heart defect that required surgical intervention, submucous cleft palate, hypernasal speech, and delayed development. His family mentions he has yearly cardiology appointments. Additional testing will most likely reveal an abnormality requiring referral to which of the following medical specialties?
A) Endocrinology
B) Gastroenterology
C) Immunology
D) Nephrology
E) Psychiatry
questions.answer:
C)
This patient presents with classic features of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (previously called DiGeorge syndrome or velocardiofacial syndrome). This chromosomal deletion disorder affects 1 in 3000-6000 live births and is the most frequent chromosomal deletion in fetuses. The combination of congenital heart disease and hypernasal speech should prompt evaluation for this syndrome. Immunology consultation is most likely needed because up to 75% of patients with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome develop thymic hypoplasia leading to reduced T-cell production, making them susceptible to recurrent infections and poor vaccine responses. A) Endocrinology is incorrect because while hypocalcemia from hypoparathyroidism occurs in 50-65% of patients, immunologic problems are more frequent at 75%. B) Gastroenterology is incorrect as GI issues like feeding problems and reflux occur in only about 30% of patients. D) Nephrology is incorrect since genitourinary abnormalities affect approximately 33% of patients, less common than immune defects. E) Psychiatry is incorrect because while psychiatric disorders do occur, they typically manifest later in childhood or adulthood, whereas immune problems require immediate attention.

questions.question:
A 2-month-old girl presents for assessment of a pigmented cutaneous lesion located on the central lower back region. Clinical examination reveals a dark brown patch measuring 10 cm across with an uneven texture and thick hair growth. What complication is this patient most likely to develop?
A) Basal cell carcinoma
B) Occult spina bifida
C) Precocious puberty
D) Renal anomalies
E) Vascular malformations
questions.answer:
B)
This describes a congenital melanocytic nevus (CMN), which when located over the spine is associated with vertebral column abnormalities including occult spina bifida and neurocutaneous melanosis. A) is incorrect because basal cell carcinomas are linked to nevus sebaceous, not CMN. C) is incorrect because precocious puberty occurs with congenital adrenal hyperplasia, which presents with generalized hyperpigmentation in areolas and genitalia, not localized hairy nevi. D) is incorrect because renal anomalies are not associated with congenital melanocytic nevi. E) is incorrect because vascular malformations are not a recognized complication of CMN.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient presents with a decade-long history of unilateral facial paralysis and is being considered for dynamic lower facial reanimation. A single-stage free gracilis muscle transfer is being planned to restore smile function. The proximal portion of the ipsilateral facial nerve cannot be used as a donor nerve. Which of the following nerve options would be most suitable for this patient due to its association with minimal donor site complications and functional loss?
A) Cross-facial nerve graft
B) Ipsilateral glossopharyngeal nerve
C) Ipsilateral hypoglossal nerve
D) Ipsilateral masseteric nerve
E) Ipsilateral spinal accessory nerve
questions.answer:
D)
The masseteric nerve represents the optimal choice among the available options due to its favorable location and minimal associated morbidity during harvesting. This nerve transfer technique has demonstrated reliable outcomes, with spontaneous smile function achieved consistently in 59% of patients and intermittently in 29% of cases according to research studies. A) Cross-facial nerve graft is incorrect because it necessitates a two-stage surgical approach rather than the desired single-stage reconstruction. B) Ipsilateral glossopharyngeal nerve is incorrect as its use results in substantial oropharyngeal functional deficits, making it an uncommon choice. C) Ipsilateral hypoglossal nerve is incorrect because harvesting this nerve leads to significant oropharyngeal complications due to unilateral tongue muscle wasting. E) Ipsilateral spinal accessory nerve is incorrect since it requires uncoordinated movement patterns for activation and is seldom utilized compared to the superior masseteric nerve option.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old male patient arrives with an 18-cm wide central ventral hernia one year following a midline exploratory laparotomy for bowel resection and right terminal ileostomy creation. His medical background includes substantial weight reduction via dietary changes and physical activity. His body weight has remained constant for the past 2 years. Current BMI is 29 kg/m2. He receives bilateral component separation repair with biological mesh positioned between the rectus muscles along with simultaneous panniculectomy. Which of the following patient factors will most probably elevate the risk of hernia recurrence?
A) BMI exceeding 24.9 kg/m2
B) Biological mesh repair with bridging technique
C) Simultaneous panniculectomy procedure
D) Existing terminal ileostomy
E) Previous abdominal surgical intervention
questions.answer:
B)
The bridging technique with biological mesh is the strongest predictor of hernia recurrence in this scenario. When bilateral component separation with biological mesh repair is performed, the critical factor determining recurrence risk is whether complete fascial closure at the midline can be achieved (total submuscular repair) versus requiring a bridged repair. Bridged repairs carry a 33% recurrence rate at 3 years compared to only 6.2% when total muscle coverage with midline fascial closure is possible. A) is incorrect because while BMI >24.9 kg/m2 increases surgical site complications and wound dehiscence, it does not significantly affect hernia recurrence rates (11.4% vs 7.7%). C) is incorrect because concomitant panniculectomy increases wound complications but does not impact hernia recurrence rates. D) is incorrect because existing ileostomies increase surgical site occurrences but do not affect hernia recurrence rates. E) is incorrect because prior abdominal surgery is present in virtually all incisional hernia patients and is not a specific risk factor for recurrence.

questions.question:
What is most commonly included in a durable power of attorney for healthcare document?
A) Consent for organ and tissue donation
B) Designation of a healthcare agent
C) Do not resuscitate (DNR) directives
D) Authorization for ventilator support
E) Instructions to withhold tube feeding and hydration
questions.answer:
B)

A durable power of attorney for healthcare is a legal document that enables an individual to designate another person, called a healthcare agent or proxy, to make medical decisions on their behalf when they become unable to do so themselves. This is the primary and most characteristic feature of this type of advance directive. A) is incorrect because organ donation preferences are typically specified in a living will rather than a power of attorney document. C) is incorrect because DNR orders are usually part of a living will that outlines specific treatment preferences. D) is incorrect because ventilator authorization decisions are generally included in living wills that detail preferences for life-sustaining treatments. E) is incorrect because instructions about artificial nutrition and hydration are commonly found in living wills rather than power of attorney documents.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female patient undergoes assessment for nasal surgery. During the examination, the Cottle test is conducted. This maneuver is primarily used to assess which of the following?
A) External nasal valve collapse
B) Inferior turbinate enlargement
C) Internal nasal valve function
D) Septal defects or holes
E) Nasal mucosal swelling
questions.answer:
C)
The Cottle test is specifically designed to evaluate the function and patency of the internal nasal valves by laterally displacing the cheek to open the valve area and assess improvement in airflow. A is incorrect because external nasal valve collapse is assessed by observing nostril movement during inspiration, not with the Cottle maneuver. B is incorrect because inferior turbinate hypertrophy is evaluated through direct visualization with a nasal speculum, not the Cottle test. D is incorrect because septal perforations are identified through direct examination of the nasal septum, not functional testing. E is incorrect because mucosal thickening is assessed visually and may be aided by decongestant sprays, but not by the Cottle maneuver.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient receives intravenous doxorubicin chemotherapy via a subcutaneous chest port on the left side for breast cancer treatment. Five minutes into the infusion, she develops severe pain at the port site, prompting discontinuation of the treatment. Physical examination reveals significant swelling (8 × 6 cm) and skin redness in the area. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Irrigating the port with normal saline
B) Administering intravenous dexrazoxane
C) Surgically removing the port
D) Injecting dimethyl sulfoxide subcutaneously
E) Administering subcutaneous saline injection
questions.answer:
B)
The most appropriate immediate management is intravenous dexrazoxane administration. Current evidence supports dexrazoxane as an effective antidote for anthracycline extravasation injuries, including doxorubicin. This agent reduces the frequency and severity of tissue damage through two proposed mechanisms: chelating metal ions to reduce oxidative stress from metal-anthracycline complexes, and inhibiting topoisomerase II catalytically to block topoisomerase II toxicity. The standard protocol involves dexrazoxane 1000 mg/m² IV on days 1 and 2, followed by 500 mg/m² on day 3, administered in the contralateral arm within 6 hours of extravasation. A) is incorrect because port irrigation could worsen extravasation if the port is malfunctioning and may introduce additional fluid into already compromised tissue. C) is incorrect because port removal should only be considered after confirming malfunction, not as immediate management. D) is incorrect because DMSO is applied topically, not injected subcutaneously, and should not be used concurrently with dexrazoxane as it reduces dexrazoxane efficacy. E) is incorrect because additional subcutaneous fluid would increase tissue pressure and worsen skin damage.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male patient is scheduled for removal of a soft tissue tumor from his left thigh. During his previous surgical attempt six months ago, he experienced malignant hyperthermia following anesthesia induction, which led to procedure cancellation and successful treatment. For this rescheduled surgery, which anesthetic agent would be the safest choice?
A) Ether
B) Halothane
C) Propofol
D) Sevoflurane
E) Succinylcholine
questions.answer:
C)
Propofol is the correct choice because it is an intravenous anesthetic that does not trigger malignant hyperthermia and is considered safe for patients with known susceptibility to this condition. A) Ether is incorrect because it is a volatile anesthetic agent that can trigger malignant hyperthermia episodes. B) Halothane is incorrect because it is a halogenated volatile anesthetic known to be a potent trigger for malignant hyperthermia. D) Sevoflurane is incorrect because it is a volatile anesthetic agent that poses a risk for triggering malignant hyperthermia in susceptible individuals. E) Succinylcholine is incorrect because it is a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent that is a well-known trigger for malignant hyperthermia.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female patient receives autologous fat transfer to the upper right breast region to address a contour depression following implant-based reconstruction. Which of the following variables will most likely enhance the effectiveness of fat transplantation?
A) Harvesting from the abdominal region
B) Immediate transplantation following collection
C) Washing the adipose tissue with lactated Ringer's solution
D) Harvesting using ultrasound-assisted liposuction
E) Processing fat through centrifugation
questions.answer:
B)
Immediate transplantation following collection maximizes adipocyte viability, as prolonged exposure to room temperature significantly reduces cell survival. Research demonstrates that stem cell viability may be completely lost within 4 hours at room temperature and within 24 hours when stored at 4°C. A) is incorrect because no evidence supports superior fat survival based on specific donor sites like the abdomen versus other locations. C) is incorrect because high-level evidence does not demonstrate that rinsing fat with solutions improves viability. D) is incorrect because ultrasound-assisted liposuction is specifically designed to disrupt fat cells, which would likely impair graft survival. E) is incorrect because there is insufficient high-quality evidence showing that centrifugation enhances fat viability.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 5 hours after being involved in a motorcycle collision. The patient reports worsening pain of the left forearm despite previous opioid administration. On physical examination, the left radial pulse is easily palpable. Hypoesthesia in a median nerve distribution is noted in the left hand. Active motion of wrist and fingers is present but is minimal and limited by pain. Passive wrist motion produces intense pain in the left forearm. X-ray study of the left upper extremity shows no fracture, and remaining trauma workup is negative. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Carpal tunnel release
B) Forearm fasciotomy
C) Local wound care until demarcation of tissue loss
D) Splinting and observation
E) Wound debridement and skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


This patient presents with acute compartment syndrome (ACS) in the left forearm after blunt soft tissue trauma. The most appropriate next step in management is emergent forearm fasciotomy for decompression.


The diagnosis of ACS in the extremities should be based on clinical presentation and progress. Signs and symptoms commonly evolve over a few hours after the initial traumatic event, especially after fluid resuscitation. Occasionally, the patient‚Äos initial presentation may raise strong suspicion and warrant immediate decompression. ACS in the extremities may develop from soft tissue injury without a fracture in up to 30% of cases.


The commonly accepted clinical findings suggestive of ACS (rest pain, pain on passive motion, paresthesia, and paresis) have been shown to have high specificity but low sensitivity, rendering them a poor predictive value. Paresis/paralysis and other signs of arterial obstruction (pulselessness, pallor, pain out of proportion) are thought to be particularly late findings. Therefore, physicians should have a high level of suspicion for ACS in any case of limb trauma associated with excessive pain and paresthesia. Measurement of compartment pressures may be of diagnostic assistance in equivocal cases, especially when the patient is unable to communicate.


Carpal tunnel release is an important component of a forearm fasciotomy; however, it is not sufficient decompression alone. Emergent decompressive fasciotomy should precede wound debridement, demarcation of tissue loss, and splinting of the extremity. Skin grafting of the wounds (including the skin incisions for fasciotomy) may or may not be needed after resolution of limb edema.


References
Friedrich JB, Shin AY. Management of forearm compartment syndrome. Hand Clin. 2007 May;23(2):245-54, vii.
von Keudell AG, Weaver MJ, Appelton PT, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute extremity compartment syndrome. Lancet. 2015 Sep 26;386(10000):1299-310.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male patient is planned for gracilis muscle transfer surgery to restore finger flexion function. For optimal functional outcomes, at what tension should the muscle be positioned during inset?
A) Reduced tension compared to its original position in the leg
B) Identical tension to its original position in the leg
C) Increased tension compared to its original position in the leg
D) Zero tension
questions.answer:
B)
The optimal approach is to inset the gracilis muscle at identical tension to its original position in the leg. This preserves the muscle's natural length-tension relationship, which is critical for optimal contractile function. Muscle fibers perform most effectively at their physiologic resting length where actin and myosin filaments have optimal overlap for force generation. A) is incorrect because reduced tension leads to suboptimal actin-myosin interaction and decreased contractile strength. C) is incorrect because excessive tension overstretches the muscle fibers, reducing filament overlap and weakening contraction force. D) is incorrect because zero tension, like reduced tension, prevents optimal filament positioning and results in poor functional outcomes.

questions.question:
A 79-year-old agricultural worker comes to the clinic with a growth on the posterior aspect of his neck. Physical examination reveals the growth is flat, has a pink coloration, and feels rough when palpated. What is the approximate percentage of malignant transformation risk for actinic keratoses?
A) 1%
B) 10%
C) 25%
D) 50%
E) 75%
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is B (10%).
