It is also used in the treatment of some squamous cell cancers, but its efficacy is lower and would not be indicated for a T2 cancer. In curettage and electrodessication, small tumors are scraped off with a curette and electrocautery destroys residual tumor and controls bleeding. It is used for superficial squamous cell cancers without high-risk characteristics in noncosmetically sensitive sites and would not be appropriate for this lesion. Also, surgical margins cannot be evaluated with this technique. Photodynamic therapy involves application of a photosensitizing agent, such as 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA), that is taken up by the cancer cells. The next day, the medicated areas are activated by a strong light. The treatment selectively destroys cancer cells while causing minimal damage to the surrounding tissue. It is used to treat actinic keratosis and is not approved by the Food and Drug Administration for treatment of squamous cell carcinoma, although experience suggests that it is effective for small, superficial cancers. Radiation therapy alone can be used in cosmetically and functionally important sites such as the lip or in patients who are poor candidates for surgery because of medial comorbidities. Given the good functional and cosmetic prognosis of surgical resection and reconstruction in this patient, irradiation would likely be reserved for a recurrent cancer. Combined surgery and irradiation is usually reserved for T4-stage cancers or those with nodal metastases.


References
1. Patel SG, Shah JP. TNM staging of cancers of the head and neck: striving for uniformity among diversity. CA Cancer J Clin. 2005 Jul-Aug;55(4):242-258.
2. Lai SY, Weber RS. High-risk non-melanoma skin cancer of the head and neck. Curr Oncol Rep. 2005 Mar;7(2):154-158.
3. Ruldolph R, Zelac DE. Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2004 Nov;114(5):82e-94e.

questions.question:
An 8-month follow-up evaluation is conducted for a 10-year-old male patient who previously had surgical treatment for an almost complete dorsal fingertip avulsion injury at the middle nail bed level. The patient now presents with a hook-nail abnormality affecting the middle finger. During planning for surgical correction, which anatomical component is most likely inadequate?
A) Terminal phalanx tuft
B) Nail root matrix
C) Non-growing nail matrix
D) Palmar skin layer
E) Fingertip pad tissue
questions.answer:
A)
Hook-nail abnormality results from inadequate bony foundation supporting the non-growing nail matrix, causing the nail to curve in a palmar direction. This condition typically develops following traumatic injury. The terminal phalanx tuft provides essential structural support for proper nail growth and shape. Without sufficient bony support from the distal tuft, the nail lacks the framework needed to maintain its normal contour. B is incorrect because the nail root matrix generates new nail tissue but doesn't provide structural support for nail shape. C is incorrect because the non-growing nail matrix itself isn't deficient - it lacks proper underlying bony support. D is incorrect because palmar skin layer deficiency doesn't cause hook-nail deformity. E is incorrect because fingertip pad tissue problems don't result in nail curvature abnormalities.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old female seeks correction of a prominent nasal bridge hump, drooping columella, and rounded tip with vertically positioned lower lateral cartilages. The patient declines septal cartilage graft procedures. Which of the following techniques will most effectively prevent a dorsal inverted V deformity?
A) Internal silicone splinting
B) Lateral crus mattress suturing
C) Subdomal grafting
D) Tongue-in-groove tip stabilization
E) Upper lateral spanning sutures
questions.answer:
E)
Upper lateral spanning sutures are the optimal choice for preventing inverted V deformity by reestablishing the proper anatomical relationship between the dorsal medial borders of the upper lateral cartilages and the septum after hump reduction. When the dorsal hump is removed, the structural connection between the dorsal septum and upper lateral cartilages is disrupted, causing the cartilages to collapse and splay outward, creating the visible inverted V appearance and potentially narrowing the nasal airway. The spanning sutures restore this critical anatomical relationship without requiring septal cartilage harvesting. A is incorrect because internal silicone splints provide temporary septal support after septoplasty but do not address upper lateral cartilage positioning. B is incorrect because lateral crus mattress sutures are used to reshape curved lateral crura, not prevent dorsal collapse. C is incorrect because subdomal grafts control tip shape but do not prevent upper lateral cartilage collapse or inverted V deformity. D is incorrect because tongue-in-groove technique involves overlapping medial crura with the caudal septum for tip support but does not address dorsal structural issues.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old right-handed male patient arrives with Volkmann contractures affecting finger flexion in his right hand following a serious burn to the right ventral forearm. A functional reconstruction using a neurovascularized gracilis free muscle-skin flap is being considered. When harvesting this flap, the feeding blood vessels are located roughly 7 cm below the pubic symphysis positioned between which anatomical structures?
A) Adductor longus and adductor magnus muscles
B) Adductor magnus and vastus medialis muscles
C) Sartorius and adductor longus muscles
D) Semimembranosus and sartorius muscles
E) Vastus medialis and semimembranosus muscles
questions.answer:
A)
The neurovascularized gracilis muscle flap serves as an excellent option for functional reconstruction procedures. Its tendinous lower portion makes it particularly suitable for reconstructing finger flexor or extensor tendons. The primary blood supply originates from the profunda femoris artery, while the obturator nerve provides innervation. During flap harvest, surgeons can consistently locate the neurovascular bundle positioned between the adductor longus and adductor magnus muscles, situated about 7 cm below the pubic symphysis. B is incorrect because the adductor magnus and vastus medialis do not form the anatomical boundaries where the gracilis pedicle is found. C is incorrect because while the sartorius is nearby, the pedicle lies between the adductor longus and adductor magnus, not between sartorius and adductor longus. D is incorrect because the semimembranosus and sartorius muscles are not the correct anatomical landmarks for locating the gracilis vascular pedicle. E is incorrect because the vastus medialis and semimembranosus do not define the location where the gracilis neurovascular bundle can be identified.

questions.question:
A patient with significant weight reduction presents for consultation regarding body contouring surgery. The surgeon concludes that a circumferential body lift would be most beneficial. To optimize flap mobilization during this procedure, which zone of adherence should be released?
A) Distal posterior thigh region
B) Gluteal fold
C) Inferolateral aspect of the iliotibial band
D) Lateral gluteal depression
E) Central medial thigh area
questions.answer:
D)
Releasing the lateral gluteal depression, either completely or partially, provides the most effective means of facilitating flap advancement during a circumferential body lift procedure. A is incorrect because the distal posterior thigh is too remote from the operative site to significantly impact flap mobility. B is incorrect because releasing the gluteal fold would compromise this important anatomical landmark and create an undesirable aesthetic outcome. C is incorrect because the inferolateral iliotibial tract is not positioned to meaningfully affect flap advancement in this procedure. E is incorrect because the central medial thigh location is too distant from the primary surgical field to influence flap mobilization effectively.

questions.question:
Compared to younger patients, elderly patients have a higher likelihood of sustaining which type of facial fracture?
A) Conservative Le Fort fracture resulting from bicycle trauma
B) Conservative mandibular fracture resulting from vehicular accident
C) Conservative maxillary fracture resulting from a fall
D) Surgical nasal fracture resulting from assault
E) Surgical orbital fracture resulting from occupational trauma
questions.answer:
C)
Elderly patients have an increased propensity for fall-related injuries compared to younger individuals and are less frequently involved in altercations. Conservative management of maxillary fractures and nasal bone injuries occurs more frequently in the elderly population, while mandibular fractures are more prevalent in younger age groups. A is incorrect because Le Fort fractures from bicycle accidents are more common in younger, more active patients. B is incorrect because mandibular fractures are typically more frequent in younger patients who are more likely to be involved in motor vehicle accidents. D is incorrect because interpersonal violence leading to nasal fractures is more common in younger populations. E is incorrect because workplace injuries requiring surgical orbital fracture repair are more typical in younger working-age adults.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female patient receives breast reconstruction using a pedicled TRAM flap procedure. Her weight is 185 lb (84 kg) with a BMI of 32 kg/m2. Mesh is used for donor site reconstruction. After 6 months, she presents with donor site bulging. What constitutes the most posterior component of the anterior rectus sheath below the arcuate line?
A) External oblique aponeurosis
B) Internal oblique aponeurosis
C) Rectus abdominis fascia
D) Transversalis fascia
E) Transversus abdominis aponeurosis
questions.answer:
E)
The transversus abdominis aponeurosis forms the deepest layer of the anterior rectus sheath below the arcuate line. At this anatomical level, both the posterior leaf of the internal oblique aponeurosis and the transversus abdominis aponeurosis migrate anteriorly to join the anterior sheath, leaving the posterior sheath significantly weakened. This anatomical change creates vulnerability for herniation when the anterior sheath is compromised. A) is incorrect because the external oblique aponeurosis forms the most superficial layer of the anterior sheath at all levels. B) is incorrect because while the internal oblique aponeurosis contributes to the anterior sheath below the arcuate line, it is not the deepest component. C) is incorrect because rectus abdominis fascia is not a distinct layer of the rectus sheath but rather refers to the muscle's own fascial covering. D) is incorrect because transversalis fascia lies deep to the rectus sheath and does not contribute to the anterior sheath composition.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old female patient whose family practices the Jehovah's Witness faith is undergoing major cranial reconstruction surgery. The procedure is being performed at a medical center with a blood conservation protocol to avoid transfusions. During the operation, the child develops cardiovascular instability due to significant ongoing surgical bleeding, with laboratory results showing a hemoglobin concentration of 6.0 g/dL. The child's parents decline to authorize blood transfusion therapy. What is the most appropriate next management decision?
A) Provide blood transfusion products
B) Give erythropoietin therapy
C) Begin vasopressor medications
D) Fluid resuscitation using albumin
E) Fluid resuscitation using hypertonic saline solution
questions.answer:
A)
The appropriate action is to provide blood transfusion products. When a pediatric patient faces life-threatening circumstances, medical professionals have the ethical and legal obligation to act in the child's best interest, even when this conflicts with parental religious convictions. The severe anemia (hemoglobin 6.0 g/dL) combined with hemodynamic instability and active bleeding creates an immediate threat to life that requires urgent blood replacement. International medical ethics and legal precedent support overriding parental objections when a minor's survival is at stake. Blood conservation programs typically include provisions allowing emergency transfusions despite religious objections when medically necessary. B is incorrect because erythropoietin works over days to weeks and cannot address acute severe blood loss. C is incorrect because vasopressors alone cannot correct the underlying problem of severe anemia and hypovolemia from blood loss. D is incorrect because albumin provides volume expansion but lacks oxygen-carrying capacity needed for severe anemia. E is incorrect because hypertonic saline addresses volume but not the critical oxygen delivery deficit from severe anemia.

questions.question:
A 39-year-old male patient receives rhinoplasty at your clinic. Six months post-operatively, he expresses dissatisfaction with the results and reports minor ongoing nasal tip asymmetry. Despite obtaining three consultations from community plastic surgeons who all agreed to treat him, he returns to your practice demanding that the original surgeon perform revision surgery because he believes that surgeon is "the best." Which psychological condition does this patient most likely exhibit?
A) Bipolar disorder
B) Body dysmorphic disorder
C) Histrionic personality disorder
D) Narcissistic personality disorder
questions.answer:
D)
Recognizing psychiatric and personality conditions before providing cosmetic procedures can help prevent complications in the doctor-patient relationship. Narcissistic personality disorder (NPD) involves an inflated sense of self-worth and preoccupation with fantasies of unlimited achievement, power, intelligence, beauty, or perfect love. These individuals demonstrate entitlement, expecting unusually favorable treatment and automatic compliance with their demands. A characteristic feature of NPD patients is their tendency to return for additional cosmetic procedures despite being unsatisfied with previous outcomes. Body dysmorphic disorder is incorrect because it involves obsessive, intrusive thoughts about perceived physical flaws that consume hours daily and cause significant distress, typically visible only to the patient. Histrionic personality disorder is incorrect because it features excessive attention-seeking behavior, inappropriate seductive conduct, and excessive need for approval, along with dramatic and flirtatious presentation. Bipolar disorder is incorrect because it involves extreme mood swings between manic episodes (elevated mood, increased energy) and depressive episodes (sadness, hopelessness, low energy).

questions.question:
A 38-year-old African American male comes to the clinic with numerous pus-filled tunneling wounds in both armpits and the right inguinal area. Which surgical approach below has the smallest chance of disease recurrence?
A) Unroofing procedure
B) Electrocautery ablation
C) Drainage with incision
D) Tissue-preserving removal
E) Extensive surgical excision
questions.answer:
E)

Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) represents a chronic inflammatory condition affecting skin in areas rich in apocrine glands, characterized by recurring painful, pus-producing lesions. Wide excision demonstrates the lowest recurrence rates among surgical options, with studies showing overall recurrence of 13% (15% with primary closure, 8% with flaps, 6% with grafting) compared to higher rates with other techniques. A) Unroofing procedure is incorrect because it shows higher recurrence rates of approximately 27%. B) Electrocautery ablation is incorrect as it has limited effectiveness for deep tunneling disease and higher recurrence potential. C) Drainage with incision is incorrect because it only addresses acute symptoms without removing the diseased tissue, leading to very high recurrence rates. D) Tissue-preserving removal is incorrect as it shows recurrence rates around 22%, higher than wide excision due to incomplete removal of affected tissue.

questions.question:
Regarding thumb carpometacarpal (CMC) joint dislocations, which statement correctly matches the injured stabilizing ligament with its corresponding dislocation direction?
A) Dorsal intercarpal - radial
B) Dorsoradial - dorsal
C) Intermetacarpal - ulnar
D) Radiocarpal - dorsal
questions.answer:
B)
The dorsoradial ligament injury results in dorsal dislocation. The thumb CMC joint is crucial for hand function, particularly in pinch and grasp activities. Its saddle-shaped biconcave articular surface provides inherent stability while allowing extensive motion including flexion, extension, adduction, abduction, and circumduction. Five primary ligaments stabilize this joint: anterior oblique, ulnar collateral, intermetacarpal, dorsoradial, and posterior oblique. While the volar oblique ligament was previously considered most important, current research demonstrates that the dorsal complex (including dorsoradial and posterior oblique ligaments) provides the most critical restraint against dislocation. Traumatic thumb CMC dislocations typically occur in a dorsal direction when these dorsal stabilizing structures are compromised. A is incorrect because the dorsal intercarpal ligament stabilizes the wrist, not the thumb CMC joint, and does not cause radial dislocation when injured. C is incorrect because intermetacarpal ligament injury does not typically result in ulnar dislocation patterns. D is incorrect because the radiocarpal ligament is a wrist stabilizer rather than a thumb CMC joint stabilizer.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old female patient experiences complete dermal tissue death in a 4 × 4 × 2-cm region of her lower breast after undergoing breast reduction surgery. Following surgical removal of dead tissue down to viable tissue, she begins daily wound care using calcium alginate fiber dressings. What is the primary benefit of calcium alginate compared to saline gauze dressings?
A) Reduced frequency of dressing changes
B) Faster wound healing
C) Lower risk of hypertrophic scar formation
D) Lower overall treatment expenses
E) Reduced rate of wound contamination
questions.answer:
A)
Calcium alginate dressings require less frequent changing compared to saline gauze, which is their main advantage. Traditional saline wet-to-dry gauze dressings need replacement 2-3 times daily due to rapid saturation, while calcium alginate's superior absorbent capacity (holding over ten times its weight in fluid) allows for once-daily changes. This reduced frequency provides greater patient convenience and may decrease overall care costs through fewer nursing visits. B is incorrect because studies show no significant difference in healing times between these dressing types. C is incorrect as no evidence demonstrates reduced keloid or hypertrophic scarring with alginate dressings. D is incorrect because alginate dressings have higher material costs than traditional gauze, though they may reduce total treatment expenses through decreased visit frequency. E is incorrect since research shows no difference in infection rates between these dressing materials.

questions.question:
A patient undergoes thyroid cartilage reduction surgery as part of gender-affirming facial feminization one month ago. She now complains that her voice has become deeper in pitch compared to before the procedure, though she denies any voice roughness. Which anatomical structure was most likely damaged during the operation?
A) Anterior commissure tendon
B) Arytenoid cartilage
C) Cricothyroid membrane
D) Hyoepiglottic ligament
E) Recurrent laryngeal nerve
questions.answer:
A)
The anterior commissure tendon was most likely injured. During chondrolaryngoplasty, surgeons reduce the prominent thyroid cartilage (Adam's apple) by carefully removing excess cartilage superior to the vocal cords and anterior commissure. If the anterior commissure tendon is inadvertently damaged during this procedure, it results in a lowered voice pitch, which matches this patient's presentation. B) is incorrect because arytenoid cartilages are located posteriorly and should not be encountered during anterior thyroid cartilage reduction. C) is incorrect because the cricothyroid membrane is positioned below the vocal cord structures and is used for emergency airway access, not involved in voice pitch changes from this surgery. D) is incorrect because the hyoepiglottic ligament connects the epiglottis to the hyoid bone and assists with epiglottic elevation, having no role in voice pitch control. E) is incorrect because recurrent laryngeal nerve injury would cause hoarseness and voice quality changes, not the isolated pitch lowering without hoarseness described in this case.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female presents to the clinic one week following an uneventful facelift procedure. She states that sensation is absent in her left earlobe. Injury to a sensory nerve is presumed. During surgery, this nerve was most probably damaged at which of the following anatomical sites?
A) Following a path from the external acoustic meatus to the lateral margin of the lower orbital rim
B) At the front edge of the sternocleidomastoid muscle
C) Midway between the mastoid process and where the sternocleidomastoid attaches to the clavicle
D) One centimeter below the external jugular vein where it traverses the sternocleidomastoid muscle
E) At one-third the span from the external acoustic meatus to the clavicular attachment of the sternocleidomastoid muscle
questions.answer:
E)
The great auricular nerve represents the most frequently damaged nerve during facelift surgery, with injury rates around 6.5%. This nerve damage can cause complete loss of feeling, partial numbness, or painful nerve growths in the affected area. Complete permanent numbness occurs in up to 5% of cases, potentially interfering with earring use, phone conversations, shaving, or hair styling. While less severe than facial nerve damage, this complication creates functional problems and frustration for both patient and surgeon. The great auricular nerve becomes most vulnerable after emerging onto the front surface of the sternocleidomastoid muscle, where it lies superficially and risks injury during facial flap elevation. Its most exposed position occurs approximately one-third the distance from the external acoustic meatus to the clavicular attachment of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. A) is incorrect because this describes the Frankfort line, which runs too high (cranially) to locate the great auricular nerve. B) is incorrect because this location is too general and doesn't specify the precise vulnerable point along the muscle's anterior border. C) is incorrect because the midpoint between mastoid and clavicular attachment places the nerve deeper and less susceptible to injury. D) is incorrect because the nerve actually lies about one centimeter above (cranial to) the external jugular vein, not below it.

questions.question:
Among the following surgical procedures, which carries the highest risk for developing venous thromboembolism (VTE)?
A) Abdominoplasty
B) Bilateral reduction mammaplasty
C) Implant-based calf augmentation
D) Liposuction of the trunk
questions.answer:
A)
Abdominoplasty carries the highest VTE risk among these procedures. Level II evidence from Winocour et al. (2017) analyzing over 129,000 patients in the Cosmetassure database demonstrated that body contouring procedures like abdominoplasty and lower body lifts pose greater VTE risk compared to breast, liposuction, or facial surgeries. Additional Level II evidence from Keyes et al. (2018) using the Internet Based Quality Assurance Program database specifically identified BMI >25 kg/m² and age >40 as independent VTE risk factors in abdominoplasty patients. B) is incorrect because bilateral breast reduction has lower VTE risk than body contouring procedures according to large database studies. C) is incorrect because despite the anatomical location near calf muscles, there is no literature or database evidence linking calf implants to increased VTE risk. D) is incorrect because liposuction procedures demonstrate lower VTE rates compared to body contouring surgeries in large-scale analyses.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old electrical worker sustains an electrical injury to the right hand. Among the following tissue types, which one demonstrates the lowest electrical resistance?
A) Bone
B) Fat
C) Muscle
D) Skin
E) Tendon
questions.answer:
C)
Muscle tissue exhibits the lowest electrical resistance among the listed options. According to Ohm's Law (V=IR), electrical current flow through tissue is directly related to voltage and inversely related to resistance. Consequently, tissues with lower resistance will conduct more electrical current when other factors remain constant. Additional variables affecting current conduction include tissue volume and moisture content. The hierarchy of tissue resistance from highest to lowest is: cortical bone, cancellous bone, fat, tendon, skin, muscle, blood vessels, then nerve tissue. A) Bone is incorrect because it has the highest resistance among body tissues. B) Fat is incorrect as it has significantly higher resistance than muscle tissue. D) Skin is incorrect because its resistance is greater than that of muscle. E) Tendon is incorrect since it demonstrates higher electrical resistance compared to muscle tissue. This resistance pattern explains why high-voltage electrical injuries often cause more extensive internal damage than what appears on surface examination, necessitating comprehensive evaluation including ECG monitoring and laboratory studies.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female patient is planned for oncoplastic breast reduction surgery to treat ductal carcinoma in situ. She desires preservation of her natural nipple-areolar complex, so the surgical approach will be designed to preserve vascular supply to this region. Which of the following vessels most frequently provides the primary blood supply to the nipple-areolar complex?
A) Internal thoracic
B) Musculophrenic
C) Posterior intercostal
D) Superior intercostal
E) Thoracoacromial
questions.answer:
A)
The internal thoracic artery represents the most frequent dominant vascular supply to the nipple-areolar complex (NAC) based on multiple anatomical investigations. Cadaveric studies consistently demonstrate that this vessel provides the primary perfusion, forming anastomotic connections with other arteries within the anterior breast fat. MRI studies of patients with BI-RADS I classifications revealed medial blood supply (primarily from internal thoracic) in 53.9% of cases, with an additional 42.30% showing combined medial and lateral supply patterns. Fresh cadaver research confirms the dominance of internal and external thoracic arterial branches, with the internal thoracic being the principal NAC perfusion source. B) Musculophrenic is incorrect because it is not a major contributor to NAC blood supply. C) Posterior intercostal is incorrect because while intercostal arteries do supply breast tissue, they have not been demonstrated as dominant NAC suppliers. D) Superior intercostal is incorrect as it does not provide significant NAC perfusion. E) Thoracoacromial is incorrect because although its pectoral branch contributes to breast blood supply and forms anastomoses with other vessels, it is not the primary NAC blood supply.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old female presents for assessment due to a 4-month duration of finger pain in her right hand. The discomfort is most intense in the fourth digit and worsens when exposed to cold conditions. Clinical examination reveals blue-colored discoloration beneath the nail of the fourth finger. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Malignant melanoma of the skin
B) Epidermal inclusion cyst
C) Giant cell tumor
D) Glomus tumor
E) Mucous cyst
questions.answer:
D)
Glomus tumors are benign vascular-neural neoplasms that function as temperature regulation mechanisms. These lesions typically occur in the hand, particularly in the digits and fingertips, and are characterized by intense pain that worsens with cold exposure. The cold sensitivity can be demonstrated by immersing the digit in cold water. These tumors are well-visualized on MRI with T1 and T2 sequences, and ultrasound can also aid in diagnosis. Complete surgical removal is the treatment of choice, with up to 25% having multiple lesions. A) Malignant melanoma is incorrect because while it can occur subungually as a pigmented streak, it is typically painless and lacks the characteristic cold sensitivity. B) Epidermal inclusion cyst is incorrect because these present as painless masses without the severe pain or cold sensitivity seen here. C) Giant cell tumor is incorrect because these benign soft tissue masses typically occur on the palm side of fingers as firm, non-tender nodules without cold sensitivity. E) Mucous cyst is incorrect because these are ganglion cysts of the DIP joint that may cause nail changes but pain is related to underlying arthritis, not cold sensitivity.

questions.question:
Following nipple-sparing mastectomy, which intercostal nerve branch is the primary source of residual sensation to the nipple-areola complex?
A) Anterior division of the fourth
B) Anterior division of the fifth
C) Lateral division of the fourth
D) Lateral division of the fifth
E) Lateral division of the third
questions.answer:
A)
The anterior division of the fourth intercostal nerve is the primary source of residual nipple-areola sensation after nipple-sparing mastectomy. While the nipple-areola complex receives innervation from both lateral and anterior branches of the third through fifth intercostal nerves, the fourth intercostal nerve demonstrates the most consistent anatomical pattern. Crucially, the anterior branches travel superficially through subcutaneous tissue in the medial breast, while lateral branches course deeply through pectoral fascia and breast parenchyma. During mastectomy, the lateral branches are typically severed due to their deep location within the breast tissue, making them unlikely contributors to postoperative sensation. B is incorrect because the fifth intercostal nerve's anterior branch is less consistent than the fourth. C is incorrect because the lateral branch of the fourth intercostal nerve travels deeply and is usually transected during mastectomy. D is incorrect because the lateral branch of the fifth intercostal nerve also courses deeply and is typically removed. E is incorrect because the lateral branch of the third intercostal nerve follows the same deep pathway and is generally resected during the procedure.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after sustaining a knife wound to the left cheek. Physical examination shows a wound just anterior to the left ear that extends intraorally. A photograph is shown. He is able to elevate the brow, close the eyes, smile, and evert the lower lip. The laceration is irrigated thoroughly. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Application of wet-to-dry dressings
B) Cannulation of Stensen duct
C) Closure of the facial wound and administration of sialogogues
D) Starch-iodine test
E) Testing of the distal branches of the facial nerve with a stimulator
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


After ruling out facial nerve injury, the next priority in management of a cheek laceration is to rule out injury to the parotid (Stensen) duct. Failure to repair a parotid duct laceration can result in a salivary fistula or sialocele. A small amount of methylene blue dye injected via an intravenous catheter, introduced through the ductal papilla in the mouth opposite the maxillary second molar, may be effective in identifying lacerations. Whenever possible, it is best to repair lacerations primarily using fine suture (eg, 8-0 nylon) over a stent. If the duct cannot be repaired because of extensive damage, ligation of the duct can be considered.


Wet-to-dry dressing changes and healing by secondary intention are not indicated in an early, uninfected facial wound. If a ductal injury can be ruled out, the wound should be closed primarily. It is not necessary to explore the facial nerve when the patient has clinically intact facial motor function. Such exploration risks inadvertent injury to the nerve. Anticholinergic medications, such as glycopyrrolate, can be administered to limit salivary secretion during healing and to help prevent salivary fistula or sialocele formation from an unrecognized ductal injury or glandular laceration. Sialogogues increase salivary secretion and are not effective in limiting complications. The starch-iodine test is used to assess gustatory sweating thought to occur because of inappropriate sympathetic reinnervation of the facial sweat glands after parotid surgery and is not indicated in the initial management of the patient described.


References
Lewkowicz AA, Hasson O, Nahlieli O. Traumatic injuries to the parotid gland and duct. J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 2002 Jun;60(6):676-680.
Steinberg MJ, Herrera AF. Management of parotid duct injuries. Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol Endod. 2005 Feb;99(2):136-141.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with numbness and discomfort around the elbow region occurring 1 year following bilateral brachioplasty surgery after losing 150 pounds (68 kg). His current weight is 200 pounds (90 kg) with a BMI of 32 kg/m². Electrodiagnostic nerve conduction testing would most likely reveal damage to which of the following sensory nerves?
A) Lateral antebrachial cutaneous
B) Medial antebrachial cutaneous
C) Posterior antebrachial cutaneous
D) Radial dorsal cutaneous
E) Ulnar dorsal cutaneous
questions.answer:
B)
The medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve is most susceptible to injury during brachioplasty procedures due to its superficial location along the medial arm where the surgical incision is typically made. This nerve provides sensation to the medial forearm and elbow region, explaining the patient's symptoms. A) is incorrect because the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve runs more laterally and is less likely to be injured during medial arm surgery. C) is incorrect because the posterior antebrachial cutaneous nerve is located posteriorly and would not typically be affected by standard brachioplasty incisions. D) is incorrect because the radial dorsal cutaneous nerve innervates the dorsal hand, not the elbow region. E) is incorrect because the ulnar dorsal cutaneous nerve also supplies the dorsal hand rather than the elbow area where symptoms are occurring.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old male patient has parotid gland and Stensen duct reconstruction following trauma from a glass bottle assault. After 10 days, saliva is leaking from the surgical site. What is the most appropriate initial management?
A) Compression bandages and restricted oral feeding
B) Radiotherapy
C) Surgical re-exploration and duct reconstruction
D) Tympanic nerve section
E) Watchful waiting alone
questions.answer:
A)
Compression bandages and restricted oral feeding represent the standard initial approach for managing sialocele and salivary fistula complications following parotid injury or repair. Conservative treatment including pressure dressings, serial aspirations, dietary restrictions, and antisialagogue medications to reduce saliva production typically resolves most cases within 2-3 weeks. B) is incorrect because radiotherapy has poor success rates for ductal injuries, requires over 6 weeks for gland atrophy, and carries malignancy risk, leading to its abandonment for this indication. C) is incorrect because secondary duct repair is technically challenging due to scar tissue and granulation, with increased risks of poor healing and facial nerve damage. D) is incorrect because tympanic neurectomy has high failure rates and does not accelerate recovery. E) is incorrect because observation alone without supportive measures is inadequate - active conservative management with pressure dressings and dietary modification is required.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old man comes to the emergency department after sustaining an injury to the right thumb. A photograph is shown. The patient declines revision amputation and states that he does not want to lose thumb length or the nail. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Complete the amputation of the thumb proximal to the germinal matrix
B) Obliterate the germinal matrix and remaining nail bed, followed by skin grafting
C) Transplant germinal matrix from the great toe
D) Transplant sterile matrix from the great toe
E) Continue to observe
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


The patient described has lost the sterile matrix of the nail bed. The germinal matrix is intact, as the nail continues to grow. The nail bed consists of the germinal matrix proximally and the sterile matrix distally. The sterile matrix allows the nail to adhere to the bed. Observation, amputation, and obliteration of the nail bed do not seem to be good options for a patient who has stated that appearance is paramount. The issue here is that the nail continues to grow, but cannot adhere to the full-thickness skin graft. The best option would be to harvest a split-thickness sterile matrix graft from the big toe. No additional germinal matrix is necessary as the germinal matrix is intact and producing nail.


References
1. De Berker D, Mawhinney B, Sviland L. Quantification of regional matrix nail production. Br J Dermatol. 1996 Jun;134(6):1083-1086.
2. Zook EG. Reconstruction of a functional and aesthetic nail. Hand Clin. 2002 Nov;18(4):577-594.

questions.question:
A previously healthy 28-year-old female patient requires urgent splenectomy following isolated splenic injury from blunt abdominal trauma. Physical examination reveals hemodynamic compromise. Following surgery, the patient has persistent hypotensive episodes that are challenging to control. Urine production totals 200 mL during a 12-hour period. Complete tertiary evaluation confirms no active bleeding or additional trauma. Laboratory results demonstrate:

What value best approximates the fractional excretion of sodium (FENa) for this patient?
A) 0.3%
B) 1.2%
C) 2.3%
D) 3.1%
E) 4.1%
questions.answer:
D)

Acute renal dysfunction (ARF, previously termed acute renal failure) involves a sudden decline in kidney function. The diagnostic workup can be organized into prerenal, intrarenal, and postrenal etiologies. Among these categories, reduced kidney perfusion (prerenal pathology) and acute tubular damage (ATN) constitute the two primary causes, representing 65-75% of all instances. The fractional sodium excretion (FENa) has been demonstrated across multiple research studies to better distinguish prerenal pathology from ATN compared to other laboratory markers and inform clinical decision-making when considered alongside patient history and examination findings. FENa quantifies the percentage of filtered sodium using the formula:

FENa = [(UNa × PCr) / (PNa × UCr)] × 100%
where UNa and PNa denote urinary and serum sodium levels, while UCr and PCr represent urinary and serum creatinine levels, respectively.

Generally, FENa values under 1% indicate prerenal pathology, reflecting proper sodium reabsorption in response to diminished kidney perfusion. FENa values exceeding 2% suggest inappropriate sodium loss characteristic of ATN. Notable exceptions that limit the diagnostic accuracy of elevated FENa include diuretic use and existing kidney disease, which disrupt normal sodium regulation.

Using the provided laboratory values: FENa = [(35 × 4.5) / (145 × 35)] × 100% = 3.1%. A is incorrect because 0.3% would suggest prerenal azotemia with preserved tubular function. B is incorrect because 1.2% falls in the intermediate range and would be less definitive for ATN. C is incorrect because 2.3% is at the lower threshold for ATN but doesn't match the calculated value. E is incorrect because 4.1% exceeds the calculated result from the given laboratory data.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male presents to the clinic 2 months following a severe facial laceration extending from his forehead to his cheek with medial canthal degloving sustained in an automobile accident. His initial evaluation included computed tomography imaging that revealed no facial bone fractures; the wound was closed with primary repair in the emergency room. Currently, his visual acuity remains unchanged from before the injury. What triad of clinical complications is this patient most likely to experience at this time?
A) Proptosis, eyelid drooping, and impaired eye movement
B) Inability to close eyelids, drooping eyelid, and nocturnal eye exposure
C) Constricted pupil, drooping eyelid, and decreased sweating
D) Double vision and eyelid drooping that become worse in the evening
E) Widened intercanthal distance, drooping eyelid, and excessive tearing
questions.answer:
E)
The correct answer is E because medial canthal degloving injuries typically result in the classic triad of telecanthus (widened intercanthal distance due to disruption of the medial canthal tendon, particularly the weaker posterior limb), ptosis (eyelid drooping from upper eyelid avulsion or injury), and epiphora (excessive tearing from damage to the lacrimal system or canaliculi). A is incorrect because proptosis, ptosis, and ophthalmoplegia characterize superior orbital fissure syndrome. B is incorrect because lagophthalmos, ptosis, and nocturnal exposure are more typical of congenital ptosis conditions. C is incorrect because miosis, ptosis, and anhidrosis represent the classic triad of Horner syndrome. D is incorrect because strabismus and ptosis that worsen at night are characteristic findings in myasthenia gravis.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male presents to the clinic with bilateral, slowly enlarging, asymptomatic masses in both parotid glands. He has a 25-year history of smoking 10 cigarettes per day. Following bilateral superficial parotidectomies, histopathological analysis reveals papillary cystic structures containing mucoid material and collections of lymphoid tissue in both surgical specimens. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Adenoid cystic carcinoma
B) Hemangioma
C) Pleomorphic adenoma
D) Squamous cell carcinoma
E) Warthin tumor
questions.answer:
E)
Warthin tumor is the correct diagnosis based on the characteristic histological findings of papillary cysts with mucoid fluid and lymphoid tissue nodules, combined with the patient's demographics (elderly male smoker) and bilateral presentation. This benign neoplasm is the second most frequent parotid tumor and shows a strong association with smoking and male gender, particularly affecting men aged 50-70 years. A) Adenoid cystic carcinoma is incorrect because it typically shows a cribriform "swiss cheese" pattern with perineural invasion rather than papillary cysts with lymphoid tissue. B) Hemangioma is incorrect as it primarily affects children and consists of proliferating endothelial-lined capillaries, not the described cystic and lymphoid architecture. C) Pleomorphic adenoma is incorrect because it demonstrates mixed epithelial and mesenchymal components with stellate cells in a myxoid matrix, lacking the specific papillary cystic and lymphoid features described. D) Squamous cell carcinoma is incorrect as it rarely involves parotid glands and would show invasive sheets of squamous epithelium with possible keratinous pearls, not the benign cystic lymphoid pattern observed.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old child presents with cerebrospinal fluid leakage and a 3 × 3-cm area of wound separation along the posterior back following surgical correction of spinal cord tethering. What is the optimal reconstructive approach for this defect?
A) Buttock muscle flap combined with skin advancement flap
B) Latissimus dorsi muscle flap combined with skin advancement flap
C) Regional fascial flap combined with skin advancement flap
D) Skin advancement flap alone
E) Partial-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
C)
The optimal reconstructive approach is a regional fascial flap combined with skin advancement flap. The fundamental principle in spinal cord tethering and neural tube defect repairs is establishing a well-perfused soft tissue barrier between the dural closure and skin closure. The fascia covering the paraspinal muscles can be mobilized as turnover flaps to provide coverage over the repaired dura. This vascularized tissue layer reduces cerebrospinal fluid leakage risk by strengthening the dural repair and creates a protective barrier against bacterial contamination and potential meningitis if either the dural or skin repair fails. A) is incorrect because gluteal muscle harvest creates unnecessary donor site complications when local tissue is available. B) is incorrect because latissimus dorsi muscle flap involves excessive donor site morbidity in a child already at risk for mobility issues. D) is incorrect because direct skin closure over dural repair increases infection risk if cerebrospinal fluid leak or wound breakdown occurs. E) is incorrect because partial-thickness skin grafts provide inadequate protection for the spinal cord and dural repair.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient presents with Stage T2 invasive ductal carcinoma and is planned for skin-preserving complete mastectomy on the right side and nipple-preserving prophylactic mastectomy on the left side. Final pathology results will determine whether adjuvant radiotherapy to the right breast is necessary. Her medical history includes tobacco use. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2. She currently wears a D-cup bra and desires to maintain similar breast volume postoperatively. What immediate bilateral reconstruction approach would be most suitable for this patient?
A) Free tissue transfer using abdominal donor sites
B) Free tissue transfer using gluteal donor sites
C) Latissimus dorsi muscle flaps combined with silicone breast implants
D) Direct placement of silicone implants with acellular dermal matrix
E) Placement of tissue expansion devices with acellular dermal matrix
questions.answer:
E)
The most appropriate choice is tissue expansion devices with acellular dermal matrix placement. Given the potential need for postoperative radiation therapy, immediate autologous tissue reconstruction could be negatively affected by radiation and should be postponed until after radiotherapy completion. While direct-to-implant reconstruction with acellular dermal matrix can achieve successful and cost-effective results, this patient presents with risk factors including large breast size and smoking history that increase the likelihood of early complications and implant failure. A is incorrect because abdominal free flaps would be compromised by potential radiation therapy. B is incorrect because gluteal free flaps would similarly be affected by radiation if needed. C is incorrect because latissimus dorsi flaps with implants still involve autologous tissue that could be negatively impacted by radiation. D is incorrect because direct-to-implant placement carries higher risk of complications in this patient due to her smoking history and large breast size.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old female presents with a 2.5-year history of painful, draining lesions in the axillary and inguinal regions. Physical examination reveals multiple nodules and abscesses. Conservative management including loose-fitting garments, topical antimicrobials, and antibacterial cleansers has failed. These clinical findings are most suggestive of which of the following pathological processes?
A) Candida infection of intertriginous regions
B) Follicular obstruction in apocrine gland-bearing areas
C) Follicular obstruction in eccrine gland-bearing areas
D) Neutrophil-mediated inflammatory and ulcerative dermatologic condition
E) Sexually transmitted disease caused by Klebsiella granulomatis
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is B because this presentation is characteristic of hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), which results from follicular occlusion in apocrine gland-bearing regions. HS involves blockage of hair follicles due to excessive ductal keratinocyte proliferation, leading to follicular rupture, re-epithelialization, and formation of chronic draining sinus tracts with recurrent inflammation and scarring in areas like the axillae and groin. A is incorrect because candidal infections typically present as erythematous, scaling patches with satellite lesions rather than deep nodules and abscesses with sinus tract formation. C is incorrect because eccrine glands are distributed throughout the body with highest concentrations in palms and soles, areas typically unaffected by HS. D is incorrect because pyoderma gangrenosum presents as rapidly expanding ulcers with undermined borders rather than the nodular, abscess-forming pattern seen here. E is incorrect because granuloma inguinale (donovanosis) presents as painless, progressive ulcerative lesions rather than the painful nodules and abscesses described in this case.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female patient has sustained a Zone II injury to her left index finger involving both the flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) and flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendons. The surgical plan includes repair of the FDP and only one slip of the FDS. When compared to repairing both slips of the FDS, what parameter will be reduced by repairing only one FDS slip?
A) Range of motion
B) Rate of tendon healing
C) Resistance
D) Risk for infection
E) Strength of FDP repair
questions.answer:
C)
Repairing only one slip of the FDS tendon creates more space within Camper chiasm during finger movement, which reduces resistance and enhances tendon gliding. The close anatomical relationship between FDS and FDP tendons in Zone II makes adhesion formation a common complication. By repairing fewer tendon structures, there is improved glide mechanics and decreased resistance during flexion, leading to fewer adhesions and reduced need for secondary tenolysis procedures. A is incorrect because active range of motion is not compromised when repairing only one FDS slip compared to both slips. B is incorrect because the rate of tendon healing remains unchanged regardless of whether one or both FDS slips are repaired. D is incorrect because infection risk is not altered by the number of FDS slips repaired. E is incorrect because the strength of the FDP repair is not affected by the decision to repair one versus both FDS slips.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female presents to the clinic with inability to bend the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of her right middle finger. Radiographic imaging is provided. She states the injury occurred 2 days prior while trying to control her dog. Clinical examination reveals absence of active DIP joint flexion; the DIP joint demonstrates passive range of motion from 0 to 80 degrees. During operative intervention, the distal portion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon will most likely be located at which of the following anatomical structures?
A) A4 pulley
B) Camper chiasm
C) Central slip
D) Sagittal band
E) Terminal tendon
questions.answer:
A)
This patient has sustained a "jersey finger" injury, characterized by sudden loss of fingertip grasping ability, similar to a football player grabbing an opponent's jersey during a tackle. The injury can involve isolated soft tissue rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendon or avulsion of a bone fragment from the volar base of the distal phalanx along with the tendon. Classification depends on fracture pattern and degree of proximal FDP tendon retraction. In this case, a large distal phalanx base fragment remained attached to the FDP tendon, with the tendon and fragment being restrained at the A4 pulley level. B is incorrect because Camper chiasm is the location where the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon divides to pass behind the FDP tendon toward its middle phalanx insertion, and it does not exist distal to the PIP joint. C is incorrect because the central slip is part of the extensor mechanism and has no contact with the FDP tendon. D is incorrect because the sagittal band stabilizes extensor tendons at the MCP joint dorsally and does not interact with the FDP tendon. E is incorrect because the terminal tendon is an extensor mechanism component that does not contact the FDP tendon.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old male presents to the clinic with a growing tumor in his humerus. Biopsy examination reveals osteosarcoma. Which of the following sites is the most common location for metastasis in this patient?
A) Brain
B) Colon
C) Digit
D) Liver
E) Lung
questions.answer:
E)
The lungs represent the most frequent site of osteosarcoma metastasis. This malignancy typically affects the proximal humerus in the upper limb and is the most prevalent primary malignant bone neoplasm. It predominantly occurs during childhood, with hand involvement being extremely rare at 0.18% incidence. In patients beyond 40 years, the proximal phalanges and metacarpals may be affected. Clinical presentation usually develops 3-12 months before diagnosis, featuring pain and swelling. Imaging demonstrates characteristic sunburst appearance with Codman's triangle periosteal reaction. Management involves wide surgical resection or amputation combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Primary bone malignancies are uncommon, representing 1 in 5000 tumors. A is incorrect because brain metastases are uncommon in osteosarcoma. B is incorrect because colon metastases are not typical for osteosarcoma. C is incorrect because digit involvement is extremely rare in osteosarcoma, especially in young patients. D is incorrect because liver metastases are not the primary metastatic pattern for osteosarcoma.

questions.question:
A 67-year-old woman with Fitzpatrick Type I skin comes to the office because of deep rhytides and signs of photoaging. Which of the following chemical peels will penetrate to the reticular dermis?


A) Alpha-hydroxy acid
B) Beta-hydroxy acid
C) Jessner solution
D) Phenol-croton oil
E) 20% Trichloroacetic acid
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Croton oil is mixed with phenol to create a deeper peel. These are part of the ingredients in the Baker-Gordon and Hetter solutions. Hetter's studies demonstrated that it was the croton oil that controlled the depth of the peel. The deeper the chemical peel, the greater the risk of scarring and hyperpigmentation. Because of this increased risk of hyperpigmentation, deep chemical peels are best suited for patients that have Fitzpatrick Type I skin.


Chemical peels vary in their depth of penetration into the dermis. Superficial peels penetrate to the epidermis. Alpha-hydroxyl acids (glycolic and lactic acid) and beta-hydroxy acid peels (salicylic acid) are superficial peeling agents. Jessner solution (14 g resorcinol, 14 g salicylic acid, 14 mL of lactic acid, and 100 mL of 95% ethanol) is also a superficial peel that can be used in conjunction with a trichloroacetic acid peel to achieve a deeper and more uniform peel. Superficial peels affect the epidermis and dermal-epidermal interface. 


Twenty percent trichloroacetic acid is a medium-depth peel that penetrates into the papillary dermis.


References
1. Baumann, L. Saghari, S. Chemical peels. In: Baumann L, ed. Cosmetic Dermatology and Medicine: Principles and Practice. 2nd ed. New York, NY: McGraw-Hill; 2009:148-162.
2. Perrotti, J. Cutaneous resurfacing: chemical peeling, dermabrasion, and laser resurfacing. In: Thorne CH, Beasley RW, Aston SJ, et al., eds. Grabb and Smith's Plastic Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2007:459-467.
3. Herbig K, Trussler AP, Khosla RK, et al. Combination Jessner's solution and trichloroacetic acid chemical peel: technique and outcomes. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009 Sep;124(3):955-964.
4. Nguyen AT, Ahmad J, Fagien S, et al. Cosmetic medicine. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2012 Jan;129(1):142e-153e.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old male patient has a 1-centimeter invasive squamous cell carcinoma on the skin of his penis. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Topical 5-Fluorouracil treatment
B) Mohs micrographic surgical excision
C) Penile transplantation
D) Radiotherapy
E) Complete penile amputation
questions.answer:
B)
Mohs micrographic surgical excision is the optimal treatment choice. This specialized technique removes skin cancers while simultaneously examining tissue margins microscopically, allowing for maximal preservation of healthy tissue with minimal recurrence rates. It is particularly indicated for aggressive tumors, high-risk lesions for recurrence, and anatomical sites where tissue conservation is crucial for function and appearance, including genital areas. Professional dermatologic societies have established guidelines categorizing squamous cell carcinoma of the genitalia as appropriate for Mohs surgery regardless of aggressiveness. Research demonstrates excellent outcomes with penile Mohs surgery, showing low recurrence rates while better maintaining sexual and urinary function compared to traditional partial or complete amputation procedures. A) is incorrect because topical 5-Fluorouracil is only suitable for superficial lesions like actinic keratoses or carcinoma in situ, not invasive squamous cell carcinoma. C) is incorrect because penile transplantation is experimental, requires lifelong immunosuppression, and is not a cancer treatment. D) is incorrect because radiation therapy, while sometimes used when surgery is contraindicated, would be less effective than Mohs surgery and cause greater morbidity in this case. E) is incorrect because total amputation, though potentially curative, causes severe functional and psychological morbidity and is not appropriate as first-line therapy for this localized lesion.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old woman with hypertension and diabetes comes to the office because of a large mid-palatal cancer. She undergoes a total palatectomy. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate method of reconstruction?


A) Anterolateral thigh free flap
B) Bilateral temporalis muscle flaps
C) Fibula osteocutaneous free flap
D) Iliac crest bone grafting
E) Rehabilitation with a palatal obturator
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


This patient has a bilateral maxillectomy defect following resection via a Le Fort I osteotomy. While small defects can be successfully addressed with prosthetic palatal obturators that fit through the wound margins and clasp to the remaining teeth, larger defects can rarely be obturated because of their weight and instability due to lack of dentition and an alveolar ridge. Bone grafting is also not an option for such a large defect, particularly one resulting from a malignancy where postoperative radiation therapy is likely. In general, bone grafts are only indicated in benign conditions with bone loss less than 5 cm in length. Even when these conditions are met, they require coverage with well-vascularized tissue. Temporalis muscle flaps can be used to reconstruct palatal defects, but in this case, the skeletal elements of the mid face have been removed. Temporalis muscle flaps alone will result in loss of mid face projection. Similarly, the anterolateral thigh free and rectus abdominis myocutaneous free flaps are frequently used to reconstruct posterior maxillary defects but, though bulkier than temporalis muscle flaps, will not maintain midfacial projection in this patient with loss of the entire palate and premaxilla.


The most appropriate reconstruction for this patient is the fibula osteocutaneous free flap. This flap will restore midfacial height, width, and projection. It has adequate bone stock for osseointegrated implant placement dental restoration as well. The skin paddle is used to close the palatal defect, separating the oral cavity from the nasal cavity.



Several other osteocutaneous free flaps, including the iliac crest and scapular osteocutaneous free flaps, have also been used for similar reconstructions.


References
1. Cordeiro PG, Santamaria E. A classification system and algorithm for reconstruction of the maxillectomy and midfacial defects. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2000 Jun;105(7):2331-2346; discussion 2347-2348.
2. Hanasono MM, Silva AK, Yu P, et al. A comprehensive algorithm for oncologic maxillary reconstruction. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2013 Jan;131(1):47-60.
3. Okay DJ, Genden E, Buchbinder D, et al. Prosthodontic guidelines for surgical reconstruction of the maxilla: a classification system of defects. J Prosthet Dent. 2001 Oct;86(4):352-363.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old male arrives at the emergency room with the depicted infection. His medical background includes diabetes mellitus type 2, elevated blood pressure, renal transplant 5 years prior, and a previous smoking habit of 10 pack-years (quit smoking). His temperature reads 39.7°C (103.5°F) with blood pressure at 80/45 mmHg, and white blood cell count at 25,000/μL. He is moved to the surgical ICU for fluid replacement and IV antibiotic therapy before scheduled surgical debridement in 6 hours. What represents the most significant mortality risk factor for this patient?
A) Patient's age
B) Postponement of surgical debridement
C) Previous renal transplantation
D) Former smoking habit
E) Diabetes mellitus type 2
questions.answer:
B)
Delayed surgical intervention is the most critical mortality risk factor in necrotizing fasciitis. This aggressive soft tissue infection requires immediate surgical debridement, and studies consistently demonstrate that mortality increases significantly with each hour of delay in operative treatment. Time to surgical intervention is directly correlated with patient survival outcomes. A) Patient's age is incorrect because while extremes of age (under 1 year or over 60 years) are associated with increased mortality, this 40-year-old patient falls outside these high-risk age ranges and age is not the strongest predictor among the listed factors. C) Previous renal transplantation is incorrect because although immunosuppression from transplant medications does increase mortality risk and represents the second most important factor after surgical delay, it is not the primary determinant of outcome. D) Former smoking habit is incorrect because while smoking can impair wound healing, there is no evidence that previous tobacco use significantly impacts the progression or mortality of necrotizing fasciitis. E) Diabetes mellitus type 2 is incorrect because although diabetic patients have higher morbidity and mortality rates with necrotizing fasciitis compared to non-diabetics, diabetes is not the most powerful predictor of death among the options provided.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old male presents for evaluation following a fall onto his extended hand. Clinical examination reveals anatomical snuffbox tenderness. Wrist radiographs demonstrate no visible fracture. What is the most appropriate initial management approach?
A) Apply a sugar-tong splint
B) Apply a thumb spica splint
C) Apply a volar wrist splint
D) Apply an ulnar gutter splint
E) No intervention required
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is B because the patient likely has a scaphoid fracture that is not visible on initial radiographs. Appropriate management requires thumb spica splinting until a definitive diagnosis can be established through repeat imaging in 2 weeks or advanced studies like CT. A is incorrect because a sugar-tong splint does not provide adequate scaphoid immobilization. C is incorrect because a volar wrist splint fails to properly immobilize the scaphoid bone. D is incorrect because an ulnar gutter splint is designed for fourth and fifth metacarpal injuries, not scaphoid fractures. E is incorrect because occult scaphoid fractures require immobilization to prevent complications like nonunion or avascular necrosis.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old female presents with painless swelling of the left mandible. A panoramic radiograph is provided. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Cherubism
B) Dentigerous cyst
C) Desmoid tumor
D) Giant cell tumor
E) Tuberous sclerosis
questions.answer:
B)
The panoramic radiographic findings are most characteristic of a dentigerous cyst, which is also known as a follicular cyst. These are developmental cystic lesions, not neoplasms, that form when the dental follicle separates from an unerupted tooth crown. Dentigerous cysts develop during odontogenesis and have an odontogenic origin. The cyst wall is composed of reduced enamel epithelium that normally participates in enamel formation. When this epithelium fails to integrate with the gingiva after enamel completion, fluid can collect between the epithelium and the unerupted tooth crown, forming a cyst. These lesions most frequently occur around impacted mandibular third molars and typically affect adolescents and young adults. They manifest as painless jaw expansion and radiographically appear as well-defined, unilocular radiolucent areas, commonly with a sclerotic border. The spatial relationship between the cyst and associated tooth can vary. A) Cherubism is incorrect because it is a rare hereditary condition affecting children where jaw bones are replaced by fibrous tissue and multiple cysts, causing bilateral facial swelling. C) Desmoid tumor is incorrect because these are solid fibrous masses that appear more aggressive and erosive radiographically. D) Giant cell tumor is incorrect because it presents as a solid lesion with more destructive radiographic features rather than a well-circumscribed cystic appearance. E) Tuberous sclerosis is incorrect because associated jaw lesions are typically solid bony growths, not cystic lesions.

questions.question:
A 51-year-old individual seeks male-to-female gender affirmation surgery. The World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH) criteria have been satisfied, and the patient is considered an appropriate candidate for penile inversion vaginoplasty. What is the most probable long-term complication following this surgical procedure?
A) Neovaginal narrowing
B) Incomplete prolapse
C) Rectovaginal communication
D) Urethrovaginal communication
E) Urological impairment
questions.answer:
A)
Neovaginal narrowing (stenosis) represents the most frequent long-term complication following male-to-female gender affirmation surgery, particularly with penile inversion vaginoplasty. This contrasts with female-to-male procedures where urological reconstruction complications predominate. Literature reviews confirm stenosis as the primary concern for both penile inversion and intestinal vaginoplasty techniques. B) is incorrect because incomplete prolapse occurs less frequently than stenosis. C) is incorrect because rectovaginal communications are rare complications. D) is incorrect because urethrovaginal communications are uncommon compared to stenosis. E) is incorrect because while urological dysfunction can occur, it is not the most common long-term complication in male-to-female procedures.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being involved in a high-speed motorcycle collision. Physical examination shows comminuted fractures of the left radius and ulna. A photograph of his wounds is shown. After debridement of the necrotic tissue, the brachial vessels and median nerve are exposed. Microsurgical techniques are not available. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice for tissue coverage in this patient?


A ) Groin flap
B ) Lateral arm flap
C ) Posterior interosseous artery flap
D ) Radial forearm flap
E ) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


The vascular supply of the lateral arm flap is from the posterior radial collateral artery, a terminal branch of the deep brachial artery. This artery communicates distally with the ulnar artery, allowing the flap to be raised in a distally based fashion, as it was for the patient in this item. For most adult patients, a 12 √o 6-cm flap can be harvested and still allow for primary donor site closure. The major extremity vessels are not disturbed with the harvest of this flap.






A groin flap would be difficult to mobilize sufficiently to reach the defect shown. It would also require leaving the arm attached to the torso for several weeks for vascular ingrowth prior to division and inset.
The posterior interosseous artery flap is based on the communication between the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries just proximal to the distal radioulnar joint. Its pedicle can be used in a distally based fashion to allow for coverage of defects of the hand and wrist. It cannot reach to cover defects at the elbow.


A radial forearm flap has two major disadvantages. It will remove a major vessel to a wrist and hand that is needed to heal a severe injury. It will also expose the radius fracture, requiring secondary flap reconstruction of the donor site. Split-thickness skin grafting is inappropriate to place over an exposed nerve, as sensitivity and pain would be expected to persist after healing. In addition, a skin graft would suffer secondary contraction, which would impair elbow extension.


References
1. Prantl L, Schreml S, Schwarze H, et al. A safe and simple technique using the distal pedicled reversed upper arm flap to cover large elbow defects. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2008;61(5):546-551.
2. Sauerbier M, Unglaub F. Perforator flaps in the upper extremity. Clin Plast Surg. 2010 Oct;37(4):667-676.

questions.question: A 51-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo needle aponeurotomy for Dupuytren disease of the small finger. A photograph is shown. The addition of lipografting after needle aponeurotomy is most likely to decrease the rate and severity of recurrence in this patient by which of the following mechanisms?A) Decreasing the proximity of residual cord tissue to the skinB) Increasing the density of myofibroblast cell-to-cell contactC) Increasing the density of the residual cord tissueD) Inhibiting myofibroblast proliferationE) Providing stem cells to promote collagen production
questions.answer: The correct response is Option D.Fat grafting (also called lipofilling) has shown promise as a means to improve outcomes after percutaneous needle aponeurotomy for Dupuytren disease. It is believed to work by several mechanisms:Reducing the density of cell-to-cell myofibroblast contactInhibiting myofibroblast proliferation via adipose-derived stem cellsActing as an interposed tissue graftProviding passing over the cords to replace native subdermal fat displaced by the nodules and cordsA randomized prospective trial by Kan and colleagues showed that aponeurotomy with lipofilling showed equivalent results at one year out from treatment with a much faster recovery compared with limited fasciectomy.ReferencesHovius SER, Kan HJ, Smit X, et al. Extensive percutaneous aponeurotomy and lipografting: a new treatment for Dupuytren's disease. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2011.128:221-8.Kan HJ, Selles RW, van Nieuwenhoven CA, et al. Percutaneous aponeurotomy and lipofilling (PALF) versus limited fasciectomy in patients with primary Dupuytren‚Äos contracture: a prospective, randomized, controlled trial. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2016. 137:1800-12.Murphy A, Lalonde DH, Eaton C, et al. Minimally invasive options in Dupuytren's contracture: aponeurotomy, enzymes, stretching, and fat grafting. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2014. 134:822e-829e.Verhoekz JSN, Mudera V, Walbeehm ET, Hovius SER. Adipose-derived stem cells inhibit the contractile myofibroblast in Dupuytren‚Äos disease. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2013.132:1139-48.

questions.question:
A 16-month-old male child presents to the clinic 2 months following surgical repair of a complete unilateral cleft lip. His mother expresses worry about how the surgical scar looks. On examination, the repaired upper lip demonstrates excellent shape and projection. The scar appears flat, somewhat broad, and shows moderate redness. What is the most suitable approach to management at this point?
A) Continue with optimal scar care protocols
B) Perform immediate surgical scar revision
C) Initiate laser resurfacing treatment for the scar
D) Schedule scar revision surgery in 4 months
questions.answer:
A)
The most appropriate management is continued optimal scar care protocols. This patient shows an excellent surgical outcome following unilateral cleft lip repair, with good lip shape and projection. The scar characteristics described (flat, slightly widened, moderately red) are normal for this early postoperative period. The mother requires reassurance and education about proper scar management, including sun protection and scar massage. Scars continue to mature and improve for up to 12 months postoperatively. B) is incorrect because immediate revision is not indicated for a normal-appearing scar at 2 months post-surgery, and early revision can lead to worse outcomes. C) is incorrect because laser resurfacing has not demonstrated effectiveness as an early intervention for scar modification and is not appropriate at this stage. D) is incorrect because surgical revision at 6 months post-repair is still too early, as scars typically continue improving throughout the first year.

questions.question:
How many aesthetic subunits make up the surface anatomy of the nose?
A) Six
B) Seven
C) Eight
D) Nine
E) Ten
questions.answer:
D)
The nose consists of nine topographic subunits: the nasal dorsum, tip, columella, and the paired sidewalls, ala, and soft triangle subunits. This classification system facilitates reconstruction by allowing scars to be placed between subunits where they are less noticeable, and helps surgeons select replacement tissue with appropriate contour and thickness. When a defect involves more than half of an aesthetic subunit, reconstructing the entire subunit yields better results than attempting partial coverage. A is incorrect because six subunits would not account for all the distinct anatomical regions. B is incorrect as seven subunits underestimates the total number. C is incorrect since eight subunits falls short of the actual count. E is incorrect because ten subunits exceeds the established anatomical divisions.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a right congenital ear anomaly that affects his interaction with his peers. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?


A) Ear molding
B) Multiple stages of surgery for rib cartilage construct, elevation of construct, and soft-tissue reconstruction
C) Surgery with cadaveric cartilage
D) Surgery with distant rib cartilage
E) Surgery with local cartilage
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.







The photographs show Stahl ear, a congenital ear anomaly that is characterized by an abnormal third crus of the antihelix. This is a fairly uncommon deformity, and multiple surgical methods have been described. Compared with other ear anomalies, there is usually enough local cartilage in Stahl ear, so most authors recommend local cartilage flaps or grafts, and otoplasty techniques, to remove the third crus and reconstruct a more normal antihelical fold.


Ear anomalies that lack significant cartilage may require larger cartilage grafts, such as rib. Multi-stage surgery is for reconstruction of microtia, which has a severe paucity of normal cartilage and soft-tissue structures.


References
Liu L, Pan B, Lin L, et al. A new method to correct Stahl's ear. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2011 Jan;64(1):48-52.
Ogawa R, Hyakusoku H. Crucial incision method for Stahl's ear reconstruction. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2007;60(8):961-3.
Thorne CH, Wilkes G. Ear deformities, otoplasty, and ear reconstruction. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2012 Apr;129(4):701e-16e.
Weinfeld AB. Stahl's ear correction: synergistic use of cartilage abrading, strategic Mustarde suture placement, and anterior anticonvexity suture. J Craniofac Surg. 2012 May;23(3):901-5.
Rodriguez ED, Dorafshar AH, Manson PN. Facial Fractures. In: Neligan P, ed. Plastic surgery. Elsevier Saunders, London; New York, 2003;1.

questions.question:
A 66-year-old male presents for assessment of a persistent left lower leg ulcer. He states the lesion has existed for 15 years. Physical exam reveals an 8 × 10-cm ulceration on the lateral left calf. What is the most appropriate initial diagnostic step?
A) Arteriography
B) Tissue biopsy
C) Nuclear bone imaging
D) Computed tomography
E) Magnetic resonance imaging
questions.answer:
B)
Tissue biopsy is the most critical initial diagnostic step for this patient. The clinical presentation and prolonged duration of this chronic ulcer strongly suggests a Marjolin ulcer developing within a chronic venous stasis wound. Marjolin ulcers represent malignant transformation occurring in chronic burn wounds or other persistent inflammatory conditions. While burn injuries are the most frequent cause, malignancies can arise in chronic ulcerations from pressure sores, trauma, venous insufficiency, and other etiologies. Well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma is the predominant histologic type, though basal cell carcinoma and various sarcomas have been documented. These ulcers represent aggressive squamous cell carcinomas with metastatic capability correlating with tumor grade, showing metastasis rates of 10% for Grade 1, 59% for Grade 2, and 86% for Grade 3 lesions. Definitive diagnosis requires clinical assessment, history, and crucially, histopathologic examination. A) Arteriography is incorrect because while it assesses extremity blood flow and may assist in surgical planning, it cannot establish malignancy. C) Nuclear bone imaging is incorrect as it evaluates for bone involvement but cannot diagnose the primary lesion. D) Computed tomography is incorrect because although useful for staging and detecting metastases, it cannot provide histologic diagnosis. E) Magnetic resonance imaging is incorrect as it helps evaluate tumor extent but cannot definitively diagnose malignancy without tissue sampling.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old male presents to the clinic following trauma to his left index finger (non-dominant hand) during a baseball game 2 days prior. He reports persistent pain since the injury. On examination, the left index finger appears shortened with radial deviation. Radiographic imaging reveals a well-circumscribed radiolucent area in the shaft of the proximal phalanx accompanied by a displaced fracture with volar angulation. What is the most suitable initial management?
A) Finger amputation at the metacarpophalangeal joint level
B) Closed fracture reduction with percutaneous pinning alone
C) Lesion curettage, bone grafting, and percutaneous pin stabilization
D) Sequential radiographic monitoring every 3 months
E) Extensive mass excision with bone grafting
questions.answer:
B)
The appropriate initial approach is closed reduction with percutaneous pin fixation only. Enchondromas represent benign cartilaginous tumors and constitute the most frequent primary bone neoplasms in hand bones. About 35% of enchondromas develop in the hand, representing up to 90% of hand bone tumors. The proximal phalanx is most commonly affected, followed by metacarpals and middle phalanges.
