C) Musculocutaneous nerve injury would result in biceps weakness and elbow flexion loss. E) Ulnar nerve damage would present with intrinsic hand muscle weakness and hypothenar sensory loss.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with a back lesion that has been slowly growing over the past 2 years. He reports that pressing on it sometimes causes white substance to emerge. On examination, there is a movable, solid 2 × 1.5-cm mass with a central pore and white material plugging it located on the middle back. The lesion is non-tender to touch. What is the most appropriate first management approach?
A) Complete surgical removal
B) Making an incision to drain contents
C) Taking a small tissue sample for testing
D) Extensive removal with wide margins
questions.answer:
A)
The patient presents with an epidermal inclusion cyst (sebaceous cyst), which is a benign lesion formed by epidermal cell growth within the skin layers. These cysts have a characteristic appearance with a central punctum and can express keratinous material when compressed. Complete surgical excision is the appropriate treatment because it removes the entire cyst wall, preventing recurrence that would occur if epithelial remnants were left behind. Incision and drainage (B) is incorrect because it only empties the cyst contents without removing the cyst wall, leading to high recurrence rates. Punch biopsy (C) is incorrect because the clinical presentation is classic for a benign epidermal cyst and doesn't require tissue sampling for diagnosis. Wide local resection (D) is incorrect because this technique is reserved for malignant lesions requiring negative margins, not benign cysts.

questions.question:
What represents the most reliable characteristic observed in skin that has undergone aging?
A) Reduced number of sweat glands
B) Enhanced melanocyte count
C) Disappearance of dermal papillae
D) Increased dermal thickness
E) Enhanced epidermal thickness
questions.answer:
C)
The disappearance of dermal papillae represents the most reliable characteristic in aging skin. This structural change leads to flattening of the dermo-epidermal junction by over one-third, which can be detected through scanning electron microscopy starting in the sixth decade of life. This flattening reduces the skin's ability to resist shearing forces and increases susceptibility to damage. A is incorrect because sweat gland numbers remain unchanged with age, though sebum production decreases. B is incorrect because melanocytes actually decrease by 8-20% per decade, not increase. D is incorrect because dermal thickness decreases with aging due to reduced vascularity and cellularity. E is incorrect because epidermal thickness decreases by approximately 6.4% per decade.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male with a significant history of chronic alcohol use presents for assessment of left upper extremity and forearm discomfort that started one week following a traumatic fall. Volkmann ischemic contracture is being considered. Which of the following anatomical structures would most likely be affected first?
A) Extensor digitorum communis
B) Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
C) Flexor digitorum profundus
D) Supinator, brachioradialis, and extensor carpi radialis
E) Volar wrist ligaments and capsule
questions.answer:
C)
The flexor digitorum profundus is the correct answer because it represents the muscle group with the highest susceptibility to ischemic injury in Volkmann contracture, being located in the deepest compartment where pressure effects are most pronounced. The Tsuge classification system demonstrates that mild contractures initially affect the flexor digitorum profundus due to its position in the deep flexor compartment, which experiences the greatest pressure during compartment syndrome. A) is incorrect because the extensor digitorum communis is in the extensor compartment and is typically affected only in severe cases. B) is incorrect because the flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus are superficial flexor muscles that are involved later in moderate cases. D) is incorrect because the supinator, brachioradialis, and extensor carpi radialis are part of the mobile wad and extensor compartments, which are affected only in advanced contractures. E) is incorrect because the volar wrist ligaments and capsule are not muscle groups and are not part of the typical progression pattern of Volkmann contracture.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents to the clinic 6 weeks following lipoabdominoplasty. While satisfied with her body contour and the low scar positioning, she reports ongoing discomfort along the lower aspect of the incision accompanied by thigh numbness. Physical examination reveals tenderness with gentle compression or touch over the affected region along the incision's lower border, and a positive Tinel sign is noted at the anterior superior iliac spine. Nerve compression is suspected. Which nerve is most likely affected?
A) Anterior femoral cutaneous
B) Genitofemoral
C) Ilioinguinal
D) Lateral femoral cutaneous
E) Lateral thoracic
questions.answer:
D)
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) is the most likely nerve involved in this case. Compression of this nerve causes meralgia paresthetica, which presents as numbness and pain in the lateral upper thigh region. Literature review by Ducic et al. identified the LFCN as the most frequently injured nerve following abdominoplasty procedures, with a pooled injury risk of 1.36%. The nerve's anatomical relationship to the anterior superior iliac spine and the clinical presentation with positive Tinel sign at this location strongly support LFCN involvement. A) Anterior femoral cutaneous nerve injury would not typically present with symptoms localized to the lateral thigh or positive Tinel sign at the ASIS. B) Genitofemoral nerve compression would cause different symptom distribution, typically affecting the genital region and medial thigh. C) Ilioinguinal nerve entrapment would produce pain and numbness in the inguinal region and medial thigh, not the lateral thigh. E) Lateral thoracic nerve injury would affect the lateral chest wall sensation, not the thigh region described in this case.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient has bilateral arm liposuction performed using tumescent anesthesia. The procedure yields 500 mL of removed tissue. She goes home the same day but presents to the emergency room 8 hours later. Lidocaine poisoning is being considered. Which of the following clinical manifestations is most probable in this case?
A) Unequal pupil sizes
B) Small hemorrhagic spots on neck and underarms
C) Fast heart rhythm originating above the ventricles
D) Rapid breathing
E) Ringing in the ears
questions.answer:
E)
Lidocaine toxicity commonly presents with early neurological symptoms, and tinnitus (ringing in the ears) is a characteristic early sign along with slurred speech, restlessness, and metallic taste. Peak lidocaine levels occur 10-14 hours after tumescent injection, making this timeline consistent with toxicity. A) is incorrect because unequal pupils suggest neurological conditions like Horner syndrome rather than lidocaine toxicity. B) is incorrect because small hemorrhagic spots indicate fat embolism, not lidocaine poisoning. C) is incorrect because supraventricular tachycardia is not a typical early manifestation of lidocaine toxicity. D) is incorrect because rapid breathing suggests pulmonary embolism rather than lidocaine toxicity.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old male patient with abdominal and flank lipodystrophy is scheduled for suction-assisted lipectomy under general anesthesia. The surgeon expects to remove 3 L of lipoaspirate. When using the superwet technique, what is the most appropriate volume of subcutaneous infiltration fluid for this patient?
A) 0 mL
B) 900 mL
C) 1500 mL
D) 3000 mL
E) 6000 mL
questions.answer:
D)

The superwet technique requires a 1:1 ratio of infiltration solution to anticipated lipoaspirate volume. Since 3 L of lipoaspirate is expected, 3000 mL (3 L) of infiltration fluid is appropriate. This technique uses wetting solutions containing normal saline or lactated Ringer's with epinephrine and lidocaine to enhance hemostasis and provide pain control. A) is incorrect because 0 mL represents the dry technique with no infiltration solution. B) is incorrect because 900 mL corresponds to the wet technique, which uses 200-300 mL per anatomic area regardless of expected aspirate volume. C) is incorrect because 1500 mL doesn't correspond to any established technique ratio. E) is incorrect because 6000 mL represents the tumescent technique, which uses a 2:1 to 3:1 ratio of solution to expected aspirate.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old male patient is scheduled for a facelift procedure lasting 90 minutes under IV sedation. He has a smoking habit of 10 cigarettes per day but is otherwise in good health. Which of the following risk factors is most likely to increase this patient's susceptibility to postoperative nausea and vomiting?
A) Length of surgical procedure
B) Patient's sex
C) Tobacco use history
D) Previous episodes of postoperative nausea and vomiting
E) Anesthetic technique used
questions.answer:
D)
The most significant risk factor is a previous history of postoperative nausea and vomiting. Known risk factors for PONV include female sex, non-smoking status, previous history of PONV or motion sickness, use of volatile anesthetics or general anesthesia, opioid administration, facial cosmetic procedures, and prolonged surgical duration. A) is incorrect because while procedure length can contribute to PONV risk, it is not the most significant factor among the choices given. B) is incorrect because male gender actually reduces PONV risk compared to female gender. C) is incorrect because smoking actually decreases the risk of PONV, while non-smoking status increases it. E) is incorrect because IV sedation typically carries lower PONV risk compared to general anesthesia with volatile agents.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old male presents to the clinic with white papular lesions on his oral mucosa occurring 3 weeks following successful facial transplantation that included the maxilla, palate, oral mucosa, and overlying skin. Physical examination reveals the patient is without fever and shows no elevated white blood cell count. The original acute post-surgical immunosuppressive regimen remains unchanged. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment for this patient?
A) Administer topical nystatin
B) Perform biopsy to assess for transplant rejection
C) Escalate tacrolimus dosage
D) Begin oral amoxicillin treatment
E) Schedule follow-up examination in 4 weeks
questions.answer:
A)
The most appropriate initial management is topical nystatin application. Post-transplant infections occur in distinct timeframes: early postoperative (0-2 months), intermediate (2-9 months), and late (>9 months). Facial transplantation uniquely involves oral and sinus cavities with resident microbial flora, with Candida being the most prevalent organism. The whitish papules described are characteristic of oral candidiasis, which is effectively treated with topical antifungal agents like nystatin and clotrimazole. B is incorrect because acute rejection rarely occurs in the immediate postoperative period, and biopsy would only be considered if antifungal therapy fails. C is incorrect because there are no clinical signs suggesting acute rejection that would warrant increasing immunosuppression. D is incorrect because amoxicillin is a bacterial antibiotic and would be ineffective against this fungal infection. E is incorrect because the patient requires immediate treatment rather than observation, as untreated oral candidiasis can worsen in immunocompromised patients.

questions.question:
A 2-week-old preterm male twin presents with an erythematous, rapidly expanding lesion on the posterior torso. Which of the following represents the most significant factor indicating a diagnosis of infantile hemangioma?
A) Rapid expansion of the lesion
B) Anatomical location of the lesion
C) Male sex of the patient
D) Preterm delivery
E) Multiple gestation birth
questions.answer:
A)
The rapid expansion of the lesion is the most significant diagnostic factor for infantile hemangioma. These vascular tumors characteristically appear between 2 weeks and 2 months of age and undergo rapid proliferation during the first 9 months of life, making the growth pattern pathognomonic for this condition. B) is incorrect because while hemangiomas can occur anywhere, location alone is not the most important diagnostic criterion. C) is incorrect because although hemangiomas are 3-4 times more common in females, male sex does not suggest the diagnosis. D) is incorrect because while prematurity is a risk factor, it is not the most important diagnostic feature. E) is incorrect because twin gestation is a risk factor but not the primary diagnostic indicator.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient comes to the clinic with a chest wall ulceration on the right side. She had a right mastectomy followed by adjuvant radiation treatment for advanced breast carcinoma 5 years previously. On examination, there is a 2-cm ulcerative lesion with adjacent radiation-induced skin changes and no evidence of active infection. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Tissue biopsy of the lesion
B) Complete resection of all radiation-affected tissue with vascularized reconstruction
C) Ulcer excision with vascularized tissue coverage
D) Hyperbaric oxygen treatment
E) Vacuum-assisted closure therapy
questions.answer:
A)
The appropriate initial step is tissue biopsy of the lesion. Radiation exposure generates reactive oxygen species that damage tissues and stem cells, leading to cytokine-mediated chronic inflammation and continued tissue injury. Radiation can result in soft tissue ulcerations, bone radionecrosis, and radiation-associated malignancies. When patients develop late-onset ulcers following radiation treatment, excluding malignancy is essential, requiring biopsy of the ulcer margin. B is incorrect because complete excision should only be performed after ruling out malignancy through biopsy. C is incorrect because partial excision without first obtaining tissue diagnosis could miss malignancy and may not address all damaged tissue. D is incorrect because hyperbaric oxygen is an adjunctive treatment used after malignancy exclusion and is not the primary initial step. E is incorrect because negative pressure therapy is contraindicated when malignancy is suspected and should not be used until cancer has been ruled out.

questions.question:
A healthy 60-year-old woman had right free TRAM flap breast reconstruction yesterday. Her cardiac rhythm strip reveals absent P waves with an irregular QRS pattern. She has no symptoms. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg with a heart rate ranging from 130-139 bpm. What is the most appropriate initial treatment for this patient?
A) Amiodarone
B) Digoxin
C) Diltiazem
D) Metoprolol
E) Propafenone
questions.answer:
D)

This patient has developed postoperative atrial fibrillation, characterized by the absence of P waves and irregularly irregular QRS complexes on ECG. Rate control is the preferred initial management strategy for postoperative atrial fibrillation, with a target heart rate of 80-100 bpm. Metoprolol is the first-line beta-blocker of choice due to its ease of conversion between intravenous and oral forms, cost-effectiveness, and widespread clinical familiarity. A) Amiodarone is incorrect because it is typically reserved for rhythm control or patients with reduced ejection fraction, and carries risks of pulmonary toxicity. B) Digoxin is incorrect because it is considered a third-line option due to its narrow therapeutic window and is only used when other agents are ineffective or contraindicated. C) Diltiazem is incorrect because it serves as a second-line rate control agent, used only when beta-blockers are ineffective at maximum doses or contraindicated. E) Propafenone is incorrect because it is an antiarrhythmic agent used for rhythm control rather than the preferred rate control strategy.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old female presents to the clinic complaining of excessive fullness in her upper arms. On examination, there is significant subcutaneous adipose tissue with minor skin looseness. Circumferential fat removal via suction is being considered. What is the most probable adverse outcome following liposuction in the bicipital groove area?
A) Compartment syndrome
B) Contour deformity
C) Paresthesia
D) Seroma
E) Skin necrosis
questions.answer:
B)
Contour deformity is the most likely complication when performing liposuction in the bicipital groove region because the adipose layer is extremely thin in this area, making it prone to irregular contours, skin wrinkling, and poor skin retraction. A) Compartment syndrome is incorrect as it typically occurs with more aggressive procedures or in areas with tight fascial compartments. C) Paresthesia is incorrect as nerve injury is less common in this specific region compared to contour irregularities. D) Seroma is incorrect as fluid collections are not the primary concern in the thin-fat bicipital groove area. E) Skin necrosis is incorrect as vascular compromise is not the main risk factor in this particular anatomical location.

questions.question:
An 8-month-old girl is presented to the clinic by her caregivers. Clinical examination reveals a triangular-shaped cranium with ridge formation along the forehead, narrowly spaced eyes, and bilateral temporal region depression. Early fusion of cranial sutures at which location would most likely result in this patient's presentation?
A) Bicoronal
B) Lambdoid
C) Metopic
D) Sagittal
E) Unicoronal
questions.answer:
C)
This infant presents with trigonocephaly, which results from premature fusion of the metopic suture. Early closure of this suture restricts bilateral frontal bone growth, creating the characteristic triangular skull shape when viewed from above, along with bitemporal narrowing and hypotelorism (close-set eyes). A) Bicoronal synostosis would cause brachycephaly with a shortened anterior-posterior skull dimension and turricephaly. B) Lambdoid synostosis produces posterior skull flattening with mastoid prominence and posterior ear displacement. D) Sagittal synostosis results in scaphocephaly with a boat-shaped skull that is long and narrow. E) Unicoronal synostosis leads to plagiocephaly with unilateral frontal flattening and compensatory contralateral bulging.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old male presents to the emergency department 30 minutes following a self-inflicted facial shotgun injury. Clinical examination reveals significant mid-facial soft tissue destruction with visible mandible and maxilla, noisy breathing, and intermittent breathing cessation. Vital signs show pulse 100 bpm and blood pressure 65/30 mmHg. What represents the most appropriate management approach?
A) Secure airway patency, manage hemorrhage, conduct secondary assessment, immobilize cervical spine
B) Secure airway patency, immobilize cervical spine, manage hemorrhage, conduct secondary assessment
C) Secure airway patency, immobilize cervical spine, conduct secondary assessment, manage hemorrhage
D) Immobilize cervical spine, manage hemorrhage, secure airway patency, conduct secondary assessment
E) Transport patient immediately to surgery for facial wound debridement and reconstructive procedures
questions.answer:
B)
The correct management sequence follows ATLS protocol: secure airway patency, immobilize cervical spine, manage hemorrhage, then conduct secondary assessment. This systematic approach ensures life-threatening issues are addressed in proper priority order before proceeding to definitive surgical care. The dramatic facial injury should not distract from following established trauma protocols that prioritize airway management while maintaining spinal precautions. A) is incorrect because cervical spine stabilization should occur simultaneously with airway management, not after bleeding control. C) is incorrect because hemorrhage control takes priority over secondary survey in this hypotensive patient. D) is incorrect because airway assessment and management is the highest priority in trauma care. E) is incorrect because immediate surgery bypasses critical primary survey steps needed to stabilize this unstable patient.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old female patient presents to the office one year following breast augmentation surgery with 325-mL textured implants. She reports that her breasts appear uneven and have become rigid. Clinical examination reveals firm, asymmetrical breasts with detectable capsular tissue. There is no evidence of pain, cutaneous infection, hematoma, or fluid collection. Raised scarring is noted along the inframammary crease bilaterally. What is the most probable contributing factor to the development of capsular contracture in this case?
A) Size of the implant
B) Patient's predisposition to excessive scar formation
C) Occult bacterial infection with biofilm development
D) Placement of implants beneath the pectoral muscle
E) Use of textured surface implants
questions.answer:
C)
This patient demonstrates Baker Grade III capsular contracture based on her clinical findings. Capsular contracture represents the most frequent complication following breast implant surgery. While this condition has multiple contributing factors, only occult bacterial infection with biofilm development shows a definitive correlation with more severe degrees of capsular contracture. A) is incorrect because implant volume does not have a direct relationship with clinically significant capsular contracture risk. B) is incorrect because there is no established connection between an individual's scarring tendency and increased capsular contracture risk. D) is incorrect because submuscular implant placement actually results in lower capsular contracture rates compared to subglandular positioning. E) is incorrect because textured implants are actually associated with reduced capsular contracture risk.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old man is brought to the emergency department for frostbite injury of the right thumb. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the inciting mechanism of the injury?


A) Failure of DNA repair mechanisms
B) Formation of extracellular ice crystals
C) Osteonecrosis secondary to vasoconstriction
D) Polymerization of intracellular amino acids
E) Vascular endothelial damage
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


Frostbite occurs by the formation of ice crystals in the intracellular and extracellular spaces. During the cooling process, the extracellular ice crystals form, and osmotic pressure increases, dragging water out of the cells. This leads to intracellular dehydration and an increase in intracellular electrolytes, proteins, and enzymes that lead to cell death. Additionally, there is vascular endothelial damage leading to intravascular thrombosis and decreased blood flow. Arteriovenous shunting occurs at the capillary level, and end-organ tissue damage is compounded.


During the warming process, there is an influx of fluid back into the cells, causing intracellular swelling. The warming process also allows reflow, vasodilation, and reactive hyperemia to occur, leading to increased inflammatory mediators causing further cell death.


Frostbitten extremities should be rapidly rewarmed in water at a temperature of 104.0¬∞F (40.0¬∞C). Typically, rewarming can be completed in 20 to 30 minutes. Adjunctive use of anti-inflammatory medications and anticoagulants also has been described. Patience is required in determining which areas need debridement.


References
1. Klein MW. Thermal, chemical, and electrical injuries. In: Thorne CH, Beasley RW, Aston SJ, et al, eds. Grabb and Smith‚Äos Plastic Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2007:147.
2. Lee CK, Hansen SL. Management of acute wounds. Clin Plast Surg. 2007 Oct;34(4):685-96.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents for evaluation of cutaneous changes that have persisted for one year. On physical examination, there are regions of skin thickening affecting her hands and forearms. Dilated capillaries are observed on her face and within her mouth. Her symptom review reveals gastroesophageal reflux and difficulty swallowing. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Amyloidosis
B) Dermatomyositis
C) Hypothyroidism
D) Scleroderma
E) Systemic lupus erythematosus
questions.answer:
D)
Scleroderma (systemic sclerosis) is the correct diagnosis. This condition encompasses a spectrum of disorders characterized by skin sclerosis and thickening. The limited cutaneous form affects the hands, distal forearms, face, and neck, and is associated with CREST syndrome features including calcinosis, Raynaud phenomenon, esophageal dysfunction, sclerodactyly, and telangiectasias. Gastrointestinal manifestations, particularly gastroesophageal reflux causing heartburn and dysphagia, occur in most patients with systemic sclerosis. The combination of skin thickening on hands/forearms, facial and oral telangiectasias, and esophageal symptoms strongly suggests this diagnosis. A) Amyloidosis is incorrect because while it can cause skin thickening, it does not typically present with telangiectasias or gastroesophageal reflux symptoms. B) Dermatomyositis is incorrect because it presents with characteristic rashes (heliotrope, Gottron sign, shawl sign) rather than skin thickening and telangiectasias. C) Hypothyroidism is incorrect because it causes myxedema (cutaneous edema) rather than skin thickening and is not associated with telangiectasias. E) Systemic lupus erythematosus is incorrect because it typically presents with butterfly rash and discoid lesions rather than skin thickening and telangiectasias.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old male patient with a past medical history of a self-inflicted gunshot injury presents for assessment due to severe facial disfigurement that persists after numerous complex reconstructive surgeries. The patient undergoes composite tissue allotransplantation. A single rejection episode is effectively managed at 4 weeks following the operation. At 3 months post-surgery, the patient presents with recurring edema and erythema of the facial tissue. What is the most probable etiology of this clinical presentation?
A) ABO blood group mismatch
B) Acute transplant rejection
C) Antibody-mediated incompatibility
D) Chronic transplant rejection
E) Hyperacute transplant rejection
questions.answer:
B)
The most probable diagnosis is acute transplant rejection, as this patient remains within the early post-transplant timeframe when acute rejection episodes are most commonly observed (within the first 0-3 months post-transplantation). A) ABO blood group mismatch is incorrect because it would lead to hyperacute rejection occurring within minutes of transplantation. C) Antibody-mediated incompatibility is incorrect as it would also result in hyperacute rejection mediated by pre-existing antibodies within minutes to hours. D) Chronic transplant rejection is incorrect because it typically develops over years and presents with characteristic features of vasculopathy and tissue fibrosis. E) Hyperacute transplant rejection is incorrect since it occurs immediately (within minutes) after transplantation due to pre-formed antibodies, not months later.

questions.question:
A male newborn is evaluated in the newborn nursery because of limited movement of the right arm. Maternal history includes gestational diabetes, but routine prenatal monitoring and ultrasound examinations were normal. The patient's delivery was difficult, and he weighed 10.5 lb (4.8 kg) at birth. He was noted to have no spontaneous movement of the right arm. The right upper extremity was warm, pink, and supple. Pulsations of the radial and ulnar arteries were palpable at the wrist. X-ray studies of the affected shoulder show no obvious fractures. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Angiography of the extremity
B) Anticoagulation
C) CT scanning of the extremity
D) Measurement of compartment pressures
E) Observation
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


This patient has an obstetrical palsy of the right upper extremity. The likelihood of recovery depends on the severity of the injury, but statistically over 70% of patients have complete or near complete recovery of upper extremity function without any surgical intervention. Thus the most appropriate next step for this newborn is observation. MRI of the shoulder and neck are helpful to discern evidence of anatomical injury to the cervical roots and/or portions of the brachial plexus, but CT scanning is unnecessary and of little use in this regard. Angiography and anticoagulation would be appropriate steps if there was clinical evidence of subclavian or brachial artery thrombosis, but the physical examination does not support this diagnosis. Similarly, the examination is inconsistent with neonatal compartment syndrome, a rare condition that usually presents with arm swelling, immobility, reduced arm perfusion, and purple cutaneous areas. Therefore, measurement of compartment pressures is unnecessary.


ReferencesBorschel GH, Clarke HM. Obstetrical brachial plexus palsy. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009;124(suppl 1):144e-155e. doi:10.1097/PRS.0b013e3181a80798Hulleberg G, Elvrum AK, Brandal M, Vik T. Outcome in adolescence of brachial plexus birth palsy. 69 individuals re-examined after 10‚Äi20 years. Acta Orthop. 2014;85(6):633-640. doi:10.3109/17453674.2014Michelow BJ, Clarke HM, Curtis CG, Zuker RM, Seifu Y, Andrews DF. The natural history of obstetrical brachial plexus palsy. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1994;93(4):675-680;discussion 681.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old healthy female comes for consultation regarding breast reduction surgery. Breast examination reveals palpable fibrocystic tissue in the left axillary region. She reports this tissue has existed since her first menstrual period and frequently becomes enlarged and mildly painful during her menstrual cycle. What is the most probable embryological source of this tissue?
A) Incomplete involution of the mammary ridge
B) Excessive development of milk duct formation
C) Inadequate mesodermal absorption
D) Excessive growth of apocrine and sebaceous glands
questions.answer:
A)
Accessory breast tissue, also known as polymastia, occurs due to incomplete involution of the ectodermal ridge beyond the primary mammary buds. During embryonic development, paired ectodermal ridges form the breast tissue. Initially, 15-20 buds appear but most undergo programmed cell death, leaving only the main mammary buds at the 4th-5th intercostal space level to develop into breasts. Accessory breast tissue develops when portions of these ectodermal ridges fail to involute during the 7th gestational week. B is incorrect because lactiferous duct hypertrophy does not explain the embryological origin of accessory breast tissue. C is incorrect because mesodermal resorption is not involved in mammary ridge development. D is incorrect because apocrine and sebaceous gland overdevelopment does not account for the formation of accessory mammary tissue.

questions.question:
A 57-year-old female patient receives microsurgical breast reconstruction utilizing a muscle-sparing transverse rectus abdominis musculocutaneous (MS-TRAM) flap. Postoperatively, near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is employed for flap monitoring. Which parameter does NIRS measure?
A) Arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2)
B) Mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2)
C) Partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2)
D) Peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2)
E) Tissue oxygen saturation (StO2)
questions.answer:
E)
Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is a non-invasive technique that enables continuous assessment of tissue oxygenation and perfusion by measuring relative changes in oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin concentrations. Tissue oxygen saturation (StO2) represents the proportion of hemoglobin within tissue that carries oxygen. Since StO2 evaluates oxygen saturation in the tissue's vascular bed, it encompasses both arterial and venous saturation, thereby reflecting oxygen delivery and utilization, making it an excellent indicator of tissue perfusion. A) is incorrect because arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2) is obtained directly from arterial blood and indicates systemic rather than local tissue oxygenation. B) is incorrect because mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) is measured from mixed venous blood and reflects systemic oxygen consumption, not local tissue perfusion. C) is incorrect because partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2) is a direct blood measurement that indicates systemic oxygenation status rather than tissue-specific perfusion. D) is incorrect because peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) measured by pulse oximetry reflects arterial saturation and may not accurately represent tissue perfusion status.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with concerns about excessive volume in the upper posterior arm region. Physical examination reveals a pinch test measurement exceeding 2 cm thickness, with minimal skin redundancy noted. Liposuction procedure is being considered. What represents the most probable adverse outcome following upper extremity liposuction?
A) Surface contour deformities
B) Skin darkening
C) Ulnar nerve damage
D) Lymphatic swelling
E) Fluid collection
questions.answer:
A)
Surface contour deformities represent the most frequent complication following arm liposuction, typically resulting from areas of excessive fat removal. These irregularities may be related to postoperative edema and should be managed conservatively for a minimum of 6 months post-procedure. Persistent contour abnormalities after this period may require fat grafting for correction, while early management can include lymphatic drainage massage. B) Skin darkening is uncommon in arm liposuction and occurs more frequently in medial thigh procedures with ultrasound-assisted techniques. C) Ulnar nerve damage at the elbow is theoretically possible but has not been documented in the literature, though careful cannula placement is essential to avoid nerve injury. D) Lymphatic swelling can be prevented by limiting liposuction to the posterior arm area, avoiding major lymphatic pathways. E) Fluid collections are uncommon in upper extremity procedures, though temporary postoperative swelling is normal.

questions.question:
Based on the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care recommendations, which gender-affirming surgical intervention mandates two official referral letters from mental health clinicians prior to surgical planning?
A) Chest masculinization surgery
B) Chest implant placement
C) Nasal reshaping surgery
D) Scrotal prosthetic insertion
E) Adam's apple enhancement
questions.answer:
D)
Testicular prosthesis implantation (scrotal prosthetic insertion) is correct because the WPATH Standards of Care specify that genital surgical procedures require two formal referral letters from mental health professionals before proceeding. A) is incorrect because mastectomy (chest masculinization) requires only one referral letter, not two. B) is incorrect because pectoral implant surgery (chest implant placement) requires only one referral letter from a mental health professional. C) is incorrect because rhinoplasty (nasal reshaping) is classified as facial surgery and does not require any referral letters from mental health professionals. E) is incorrect because thyroid cartilage grafting (Adam's apple enhancement) is also considered facial surgery and does not require mental health referral letters.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female patient measuring 5 ft 7 in (170 cm) in height and weighing 135 lbs (61 kg) presents for evaluation one year after undergoing bilateral nipple-sparing mastectomy with immediate reconstruction using 350-mL smooth, round silicone gel implants positioned under the pectoralis major muscle. Following surgery, she has developed hyperdynamic breast deformity. Physical examination reveals natural-appearing breast reconstruction with notable breast movement during chest muscle flexion. What is the most appropriate treatment approach for this patient?
A) Administer botulinum toxin injections into the pectoralis major muscle
B) Perform ultrasound-guided triamcinolone-40 injections into tender areas
C) Relocate the implants to a prepectoral position with complete acellular dermal matrix coverage
D) Order breast MRI to evaluate for implant rupture
E) Provide physical therapy referral for range of motion exercises, massage, and ultrasound therapy
questions.answer:
C)
This patient's significant breast movement results from implant placement beneath the pectoralis major muscles. Given that she is a thin, healthy patient who is not suitable for fat grafting or tissue transfer procedures, repositioning the implants above the pectoralis major muscles with complete acellular dermal matrix coverage represents the most effective approach to address her hyperdynamic deformity concerns. A) is incorrect because botulinum toxin injections are unlikely to provide lasting significant improvement compared to surgical revision. B) is incorrect because triamcinolone injections would not effectively treat hyperdynamic deformity. D) is incorrect because MRI would likely be non-diagnostic, and prepectoral conversion remains the indicated treatment regardless of implant integrity. E) is incorrect because physical therapy and muscle relaxants are unlikely to achieve long-term resolution of this problem.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with the ventral hernia depicted. His medical history reveals a sigmoid resection for diverticular disease performed through a midline approach 7 years prior. Following surgery, he developed an incisional hernia that was treated with mesh repair, but the repair failed. On examination, there is a palpable fascial defect measuring 28 cm horizontally at the umbilical level and 25 cm vertically. What is the most suitable approach for abdominal wall reconstruction?
A) Component separation technique alone
B) Component separation technique combined with mesh repair
C) Mesh repair alone
D) Tissue expansion and component separation technique combined with mesh repair
E) Utilization of a pedicled tensor fascia lata flap
questions.answer:
B)

The component separation technique combined with mesh repair is the most appropriate choice for this large fascial defect. Component separation, first described by Ramirez and colleagues in 1990, involves dividing the external oblique fascia lateral to the rectus muscle and elevating it from the internal oblique in a relatively avascular plane. This technique preserves the intercostal neurovascular supply to the rectus muscle, maintaining its function and innervation. The procedure can achieve closure of defects up to 10 cm at the epigastrium, 20 cm at the mid-abdomen, and 6 cm at the lower abdomen under optimal conditions. However, given the 28 cm horizontal dimension of this defect, component separation alone would be inadequate, necessitating supplemental mesh reinforcement to achieve complete closure while restoring functional abdominal wall integrity.

A) is incorrect because component separation alone cannot adequately close a 28 cm defect, leaving a persistent fascial gap. C) is incorrect because mesh repair alone fails to restore abdominal wall functionality and may lead to recurrence and bulging in large defects. D) is incorrect because tissue expansion is unnecessary when skin coverage is adequate, as in this case. E) is incorrect because while tensor fascia lata flaps can provide vascularized fascia, they tend to lose muscular tone over time, leading to fascial attenuation and eventual bulging.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old male patient has an acute injury to the flexor pollicis longus tendon at the interphalangeal joint that requires surgical repair. During the procedure, the surgeon cannot access the proximal portion of the severed tendon through the original wound. A secondary incision is made in the distal forearm region. When the flexor pollicis longus is located at this proximal level, initial attempts to mobilize the proximal tendon stump are hindered by an abnormal connection between the flexor pollicis longus and a neighboring tendon. Which tendon is most commonly associated with this anatomical variant?
A) Abductor pollicis longus
B) Brachioradialis
C) Flexor carpi radialis
D) Flexor digitorum profundus index
E) Flexor digitorum superficialis index
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is D. This describes the Linburg-Comstock anomaly, which is an abnormal tendinous connection between the flexor pollicis longus and the flexor digitorum profundus tendon to the index finger. This anatomical variant was first documented by Linburg and Comstock in 1979 and occurs in approximately 31% of individuals in at least one hand. The connection typically exists in the distal forearm region, before the tendons enter the carpal tunnel. This anomalous link can cause complications during flexor pollicis longus repairs by creating unintended tension at the repair site, and it may also be a source of tenosynovitis that requires surgical division. A is incorrect because the abductor pollicis longus is located on the radial side of the forearm and does not have documented anomalous connections with the flexor pollicis longus. B is incorrect because the brachioradialis is a more superficial muscle that inserts at the radial styloid and is not known to have tendinous connections with the flexor pollicis longus. C is incorrect because while the flexor carpi radialis runs in the same compartment, there are no well-documented anomalous connections between it and the flexor pollicis longus. E is incorrect because the flexor digitorum superficialis to the index finger does not have established anomalous connections with the flexor pollicis longus; the connection specifically involves the profundus tendon.

questions.question:
A 3-month-old baby shows left frontal flattening with orbital and facial asymmetry. The child demonstrates early right-sided astigmatism and compensatory head positioning. CT imaging is provided. The family is weighing two treatment approaches: endoscopic strip craniectomy with helmet molding at 3 months versus fronto-orbital reconstruction at 9 months. When comparing endoscopic strip craniectomy with helmet therapy to fronto-orbital reconstruction, which surgical outcome is more probable with fronto-orbital reconstruction?
A) Higher revision rate
B) Improved postoperative facial balance
C) Reduced surgical complications
D) Decreased total treatment expense
E) Worsened eye muscle imbalance
questions.answer:
E)
Fronto-orbital advancement is more likely to result in more severe strabismus compared to endoscopic suturectomy with helmet therapy. Early endoscopic intervention better addresses the orbital asymmetry that causes strabismus and ocular torticollis, leading to superior ophthalmologic outcomes. Multiple studies demonstrate significantly better eye alignment following early endoscopic treatment versus delayed fronto-orbital advancement. A is incorrect because FOA actually has similar revision rates to endoscopic techniques. B is incorrect because endoscopic approaches achieve better facial symmetry when performed early. C is incorrect because FOA is more invasive with greater operative morbidity than endoscopic techniques. D is incorrect because FOA is more expensive than endoscopic suturectomy with helmet therapy.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old male presents to the emergency room following trauma from an ATV accident. Physical findings include telecanthus and bruising around the eyes. Fracture displacement of which structure most likely accounts for the telecanthus?
A) Inferior rectus muscle tendon
B) Lateral canthal tendon
C) Lateral rectus muscle tendon
D) Medial canthal tendon
E) Medial rectus muscle tendon
questions.answer:
D)
The medial canthal tendon is a fibrous structure that connects to the medial orbital wall at the frontal bone and lacrimal crest. When severe trauma affects the frontal and midface areas, fractures can occur in the medial orbital wall, nasomaxillary buttress, and lateral nasal bones, leading to naso-orbital-ethmoid fractures. When these fractures are displaced, the medial canthal tendon gets pulled laterally, causing telecanthus - an abnormal widening of the distance between the inner corners of the eyes. A) is incorrect because the inferior rectus muscle tendon is located at the orbital floor and its injury would cause vertical eye movement problems rather than telecanthus. B) is incorrect because the lateral canthal tendon attaches to the lateral orbital wall and is not involved in traumatic telecanthus formation. C) is incorrect because the lateral rectus muscle tendon controls horizontal eye movement and its disruption would cause horizontal diplopia, not telecanthus. E) is incorrect because the medial rectus muscle tendon controls inward eye movement and its injury would result in horizontal strabismus rather than telecanthus.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old Asian American child presents to the clinic with congenital cryptotia. What is the most probable pathophysiologic mechanism underlying this condition?
A) Abnormal positioning of the intrinsic transverse and oblique ear muscles
B) Developmental failure of antihelix folding between gestational weeks 12-16
C) Absence of hillocks 3 and 4 formation from the first and second branchial arches
D) Defective fusion of the six auricular hillocks
E) Structural abnormality of the conchal bowl
questions.answer:
A)
Cryptotia represents a congenital ear anomaly where the upper portion of the ear appears embedded under the mastoid skin, commonly seen in Asian populations. Children typically present during school age when unable to properly wear eyeglasses. This condition results from abnormal positioning of the intrinsic ear muscles. B is incorrect because antihelix folding failure leads to scaphal protrusion, not cryptotia. C is incorrect as hillock formation failure from branchial arches does not cause cryptotia. D is incorrect since incomplete hillock fusion does not result in this specific deformity. E is incorrect because conchal bowl malformation causes ear prominence from the head, not the buried appearance characteristic of cryptotia.

questions.question:
A 64-year-old male patient presents with a T3N2 oropharyngeal carcinoma involving the tongue and tonsillar region and receives transoral robotic surgery (TORS). What is the primary benefit of TORS compared to conventional treatment modalities?
A) TORS patients experience reduced swallowing difficulties
B) TORS patients demonstrate lower bleeding complications versus open surgical methods
C) TORS results in reduced postoperative infectious complications
D) TORS eliminates the requirement for free flap reconstruction
E) TORS provides substantially better disease-free survival outcomes
questions.answer:
E)
TORS demonstrates substantially better disease-free survival outcomes compared to open surgical approaches, as shown in meta-analysis studies, while maintaining comparable overall survival and quality of life to nonsurgical treatments. A is incorrect because dysphagia rates are not significantly different between TORS and traditional treatments. B is incorrect because TORS actually has a higher hemorrhage risk (6%) compared to open approaches (<2%). C is incorrect because infection rates show no significant difference between TORS and conventional treatments. D is incorrect because reconstruction with free flaps is still required for TORS patients depending on defect size, though the incidence may be lower than open approaches.

questions.question:
A 10-year-old child has surgical correction of microtia affecting the right ear. While harvesting rib cartilage, the right chest wall is inadvertently injured with exposure of lung tissue. Following pleural repair, a Valsalva maneuver shows no air leak. An operative chest radiograph reveals no pneumothorax. Minutes later in the recovery room, the child develops low blood pressure and rapid breathing, with oxygen saturation dropping to the mid-80s despite high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather mask. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Obtain arterial blood gas analysis
B) Endotracheal intubation
C) Needle thoracostomy of the right chest
D) Reopen the surgical incision
E) Order portable chest radiograph
questions.answer:
C)
The patient demonstrates classic signs of tension pneumothorax requiring immediate decompression. Needle thoracostomy at the second intercostal space is the standard emergency treatment to rapidly decompress tension pneumothorax and restore hemodynamic stability. A is incorrect because arterial blood gas analysis would delay necessary intervention without providing diagnostic benefit. B is incorrect because intubation alone will not relieve the tension and may worsen the condition by increasing intrathoracic pressure. D is incorrect because reopening the surgical incision requires anesthesia and surgical equipment, causing dangerous delays. E is incorrect because obtaining a chest radiograph would waste critical time when immediate decompression is needed.

questions.question:
What is the primary function of estrogen in mammary tissue development?
A) Reduces cellular proliferation
B) Minimizes fibrocystic alterations
C) Promotes ductal proliferation
D) Promotes alveolar development
E) Promotes stromal tissue expansion around ducts
questions.answer:
C)
Estrogen's primary role in breast tissue is to stimulate ductal proliferation and branching throughout the mammary gland. A is incorrect because estrogen actually increases, rather than reduces, cellular proliferation in breast tissue. B is incorrect because estrogen is associated with increased, not decreased, fibrocystic changes. D is incorrect because alveolar (glandular) development is primarily driven by progesterone, not estrogen. E is incorrect because periductal stromal development is also primarily mediated by progesterone rather than estrogen.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old white female comes to the clinic with numerous (>50) pigmented spots on her forearms and shins. These lesions are located in sun-exposed regions. Physical examination reveals many well-defined, uniformly colored spots measuring under 5 mm. The patient reports a family history of melanoma. Due to the large number of lesions, complete excision is not feasible. Which of the following characteristics in one of these spots would indicate the need for excisional biopsy?
A) Asymmetry
B) Clearly demarcated borders
C) Dark coloration
D) Waxy surface
questions.answer:
A)
In this patient with numerous melanocytic nevi, lesions warrant excisional biopsy when there is high concern for melanoma. Given the presence of over 50 lesions, complete removal of all spots is impractical. These lesions should be assessed for asymmetry, irregular borders, color variation, diameter exceeding 6 mm, and changes over time. Any of these warning signs in a lesion should prompt excisional biopsy due to melanoma suspicion, particularly considering the patient's family history. B) is incorrect because well-demarcated borders are actually a reassuring feature of benign nevi. C) is incorrect because dark pigmentation alone does not indicate malignancy. D) is incorrect because waxy surfaces are characteristic of seborrheic keratoses, benign lesions commonly seen in older patients in sun-exposed areas.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male patient has developed a ventral incisional hernia in his abdomen. His BMI is 32 kg/m2. His past medical history includes an exploratory laparotomy performed after traumatic injury one year prior. The abdominal fascia was closed using primary closure at the conclusion of that operation. On physical examination, there is a fascial defect measuring 10 cm in width. CT imaging reveals that both rectus muscles remain intact and are separated by 12 cm in the periumbilical area. During hernia repair surgery, primary closure of the fascia at the midline is not achievable. Which of the following surgical approaches would most likely provide the lowest risk of recurrent hernia formation in this patient?
A) Bilateral component separation
B) Bilateral component separation with onlay mesh reconstruction
C) Bilateral component separation with underlay mesh reconstruction
D) Inlay mesh reconstruction
E) Unilateral component separation
questions.answer:
C)
The optimal approach for minimizing long-term hernia recurrence involves achieving primary fascial closure combined with mesh placement in the retrorectus or underlay position. This technique provides the strongest repair by combining tissue approximation with mesh reinforcement in an optimal anatomical plane. A) Bilateral component separation alone, while allowing primary closure, lacks mesh reinforcement and has higher recurrence rates. B) Bilateral component separation with onlay mesh has increased failure rates in obese patients due to the superficial mesh position being more prone to complications. D) Inlay mesh reconstruction acts as a bridging repair without primary fascial closure, resulting in the highest hernia recurrence rates. E) Unilateral component separation provides insufficient mobilization for this large defect and lacks mesh augmentation.

questions.question:
A healthy 3-day-old full-term female newborn presents to the office for assessment of a noticeable ear malformation. The family is exploring non-operative treatment options and wishes to consider ear molding therapy but has concerns regarding potential adverse effects from molding apparatus. What should the family be informed is the most frequent complication associated with these devices?
A) Chondritis
B) Otitis media
C) Overcorrection
D) Sensorineural hearing loss
E) Skin ulceration
questions.answer:
E)
Skin ulceration represents the most frequently encountered complication with ear molding devices, occurring in approximately 7.6% of cases according to recent research, with other studies reporting rates around 3%. While chondritis can occur, it affects fewer than 3% of patients, making it less common than skin breakdown. Otitis media is incorrect because external molding systems do not interfere with eustachian tube function or predispose to middle ear infections. Sensorineural hearing loss is wrong as ear molding is an external treatment that does not affect inner ear structures or auditory pathways. Overcorrection is incorrect because molding devices alone typically do not produce excessive correction of ear deformities.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old male presents to the clinic seeking advice regarding his protruding ears. He demonstrates noticeable self-consciousness about his ear appearance and grows his hair long to conceal them. During the assessment, he frequently checks his reflection in the mirror. Physical examination reveals postauricular measurements with helical rim-to-scalp distances of 12 mm at the upper pole, 17 mm at the middle section, and 23 mm at the earlobe on both sides. What is the most suitable initial management approach?
A) Psychiatric consultation referral
B) Follow-up assessment in 12 months
C) Conchal bowl excision
D) Anterior cartilage scoring technique
E) Conchal-mastoid suture placement
questions.answer:
A)
This patient demonstrates characteristics suggestive of body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), warranting psychiatric evaluation before any surgical intervention. His excessive self-consciousness, mirror-checking behavior, and social avoidance (hiding ears with hair) indicate psychological distress disproportionate to the physical findings. The measured ear protrusion values (12mm, 17mm, 23mm) fall within or very close to normal ranges (10-12mm, 16-18mm, 20-22mm respectively), suggesting his distress is primarily psychological rather than based on significant anatomical abnormality. B is incorrect because delaying evaluation doesn't address the underlying psychological concerns that require immediate attention. C is incorrect as conchal bowl resection is a surgical technique that wouldn't be appropriate without first addressing the psychological component and confirming surgical candidacy. D is incorrect because anterior cartilage scoring is another surgical approach that should not be considered until psychological evaluation is completed. E is incorrect as conchal-mastoid suturing is a surgical procedure that would be premature given the likely presence of BDD and near-normal ear measurements.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old woman presents with lower lip impairment following a facelift procedure. The surgeon instructs the patient to demonstrate a broad smile showing her teeth and then to purse her lips, pulling down and turning out the lower lip. Asymmetrical movement is noted during both maneuvers, with reduced lower dental exposure on the left during the broad smile, and absence of left lower lip turning outward during pursing. Which of the following facial nerve branches is most likely damaged?
A) Left cervical
B) Left marginal mandibular
C) Right cervical
D) Right marginal mandibular
questions.answer:
B)
The left marginal mandibular branch is the correct answer because it uniquely innervates the mentalis muscle, which is essential for lip eversion (turning the lip outward). Damage to this branch would cause both decreased lower tooth visibility during smiling and inability to evert the lower lip when pursing, matching the patient's presentation on the left side. A) Left cervical is incorrect because cervical branch injury affects lip depression but not eversion, so it wouldn't cause the absence of lip turning outward. C) Right cervical is incorrect because the symptoms are on the left side, not the right. D) Right marginal mandibular is incorrect because the functional deficits are occurring on the left side, not the right side of the face.

questions.question:
A 51-year-old female patient is receiving free flap breast reconstruction surgery. After completing the anastomosis, the patient develops a venous clot, and the surgical team decides to irrigate the flap with tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). What is the principal mechanism by which tPA functions in this clinical situation?
A) Activation of antithrombin III
B) Breakdown of fibrin clots
C) Prevention of platelet clumping
D) Activation of protein C
E) Splitting of prothrombin
questions.answer:
B)
Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) works primarily through fibrinolysis, converting plasminogen into its active form plasmin, which directly dissolves fibrin clots. This makes it particularly effective for breaking down existing thrombi that may compromise flap perfusion. A is incorrect because antithrombin III activation is the mechanism of heparin, not tPA. C is incorrect because platelet aggregation inhibition is the mechanism of aspirin and similar antiplatelet agents. D is incorrect because protein C activation is an anticoagulant mechanism that inhibits clotting factors but does not actively dissolve existing clots. E is incorrect because prothrombin cleavage actually promotes clot formation by generating thrombin, which is opposite to tPA's fibrinolytic action.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old healthy female patient is planned for bilateral arm lift surgery combined with upper arm liposuction. What is the most frequent adverse result associated with this dual procedure?
A) Blood collection under the skin
B) Excessive scar tissue formation
C) Bacterial contamination
D) Loss of feeling in nerves
E) Separation of wound edges
questions.answer:
B)
Excessive scar tissue formation is the most prevalent complication following arm lift procedures and may require additional surgical correction in certain patients. Upper arm liposuction performed simultaneously with brachioplasty is an established and secure technique. Current research demonstrates that along with fluid collections, abnormal scar development represents the most frequent adverse result of this combination surgery. A) is incorrect because blood collections occur less commonly than scarring issues. C) is incorrect because bacterial contamination happens less frequently than scar problems. D) is incorrect because nerve sensation loss, particularly affecting the medial antebrachial nerve, occurs much less often than hypertrophic scarring. E) is incorrect because wound separation is encountered less frequently than excessive scar formation.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old female patient, G1P1, who previously underwent cesarean section presents with an asymptomatic, hard, 6-cm subcutaneous lesion that is adherent to the anterior abdominal wall. The lesion appeared following her pregnancy. Laboratory tumor markers are normal. She has a family history of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
B) Desmoid
C) Lipoma
D) Lymphoma
E) Neurofibroma
questions.answer:
B)
Desmoid tumor is the correct diagnosis. These tumors, also called aggressive fibromatosis, are characterized by unpredictable growth patterns or spontaneous regression without metastatic capability. Most desmoid tumors result from sporadic CTNNB1 mutations, while 10% are associated with APC mutations in FAP syndrome. Abdominal wall desmoids show increased frequency in women of reproductive age, making this diagnosis highly likely given the patient's demographics, FAP history, and clinical presentation. A) Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is incorrect because it typically presents as smaller lesions (<5 cm) with characteristic purple or blue coloration and remains confined to superficial cutaneous structures. C) Lipoma is incorrect because these benign adipose tumors typically present as soft, rubbery masses rather than firm, fixed lesions, and lack association with FAP syndrome. D) Lymphoma is incorrect because primary abdominal wall lymphoma is rare, more common in males over 50 years, and would typically show elevated LDH tumor markers. E) Neurofibroma is incorrect because these present as soft, skin-colored lesions and are associated with neurofibromatosis syndromes (NF1/NF2), not FAP.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents with T2 N0 M0 invasive ductal breast cancer located in the lower pole of her left breast and is planned for partial mastectomy with subsequent radiotherapy. She currently uses a 36E bra size and desires to achieve a cup size between C and D. Following tumor excision via segmental resection, which procedure would most likely provide the optimal aesthetic outcome for this patient?
A) Bilateral breast reduction surgery
B) Direct closure of the left breast with contralateral breast reduction
C) Left breast reconstruction using latissimus dorsi myocutaneous flap combined with right breast reduction
D) Left breast reconstruction with TRAM flap and right breast mastopexy
E) Single-stage reconstruction with silicone implant placement in the left breast and right breast reduction
questions.answer:
A)
Bilateral breast reduction surgery represents the optimal approach for this patient with macromastia undergoing partial mastectomy. This technique addresses her symptoms related to large breast size, reduces tissue volume in both breasts proportionally, and achieves the most favorable cosmetic result with symmetry. Option B is suboptimal because primary closure alone after significant tissue removal will likely result in breast deformity and asymmetry. Option C is inappropriate as latissimus dorsi flap reconstruction is better suited for delayed reconstruction and may limit future reconstructive options. Option D is not ideal since TRAM flap reconstruction is typically reserved for delayed reconstruction of partial mastectomy defects rather than immediate reconstruction. Option E is contraindicated because implant placement in tissue that will receive radiation therapy significantly increases complication rates and typically produces inferior aesthetic results with poor symmetry.

questions.question: A 50-year-old woman comes to the emergency department after sustaining an avulsion injury of the right ring finger proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint. A photograph is shown. Examination shows the central slip is disrupted, and the inside of the PIP joint is visible through the dorsal wound. The patient is able to actively extend the PIP joint. Which of the following anatomical structures allows the patient to extend the PIP joint?A) Extrinsic extensor tendonB) Interosseous muscle tendonC) Lateral conjoined tendonD) Oblique retinacular ligamentE) Sagittal band
questions.answer: The correct response is Option B. The central slip of the extensor mechanism is the terminal direct extension of the extrinsic extensor tendon (extensor digitorum communis and extensor digiti quinti) and is the primary extensor of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint. Injury to the central slip will normally produce flexion of the PIP joint due to unopposed action of the flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) and flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendons and is called a boutonniere deformity.The intrinsic extensor mechanism, via the middle band of the interosseous muscles, also inserts on the dorsal base of the middle phalanx and causes extension of the PIP joint. In an open injury, the central slip may be injured without concurrent injury to the interosseous muscle tendon, allowing the patient to still actively extend the PIP joint even in the presence of a disruption of the central slip.The oblique retinacular ligament connects the flexor tendon sheath volarly to the terminal extensor tendon dorsally. When a patient sustains a laceration to the extensor mechanism over the body of the middle phalanx bone, the oblique retinacular ligament may prevent the occurrence of an extensor lag and a mallet deformity.The lateral conjoined tendon is formed by the lateral bands of the interosseous muscles and the lateral slips of the extrinsic extensor and produces extension of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint.The sagittal band keeps the extrinsic extensor tendon centralized over the dorsal metacarpophalangeal (MP) joint by connecting to the volar plate. Disruption of the sagittal band on one side of a finger would allow the extrinsic extensor tendon to dislocate and impair its ability to extend the MP joint.ReferencesAmirtharajah M, Lattanza L. Open extensor tendon injuries. J Hand Surg Am. 2015; 40(2):391-397.Grau L, Baydoun H, Chen K, et al. Biomechanics of the acute boutonniere deformity. J Hand Surg Am. 2018 Jan;43(1):80.e1-80.e6.Hanz KR, Saint-Cyr M, Semmler, MJ, Rohrich RJ. Extensor tendon injuries: acute management and secondary reconstruction. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008 121:109e-120e.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old child with a documented history of severe allergic reactions to bee venom presents to the clinic 45 minutes following accidental epinephrine injection into the fingertip from his auto-injector device. Examination of the affected digit reveals edema, pain, and poor capillary refill. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Use ice application
B) Use heat application
C) Raise the affected limb
D) Create drainage incisions with saline washout
E) Inject a reversal agent subcutaneously
questions.answer:
C)
Raising the affected limb is the most appropriate initial management step. Elevation promotes venous drainage of the infiltrated medication, reduces edema, and decreases the likelihood of tissue death. The vasoconstricting properties of epinephrine persist for only 60 to 90 minutes, and significantly longer periods of reduced blood flow are required to cause tissue death. A is incorrect because ice application may worsen tissue damage through additional vasoconstriction and potential frostbite injury. B is incorrect because heat application risks thermal burns and may convert partial-thickness injury to full-thickness damage. D is incorrect because surgical drainage with saline irrigation is typically reserved for chemotherapy extravasations and would be considered only after conservative measures like elevation. E is incorrect because injecting antidotes like phentolamine adds additional fluid volume that can worsen pressure-related tissue damage, and the epinephrine effects usually resolve before treatment can be implemented.

questions.question:
A 2-month-old female infant is brought to the office because her parents are concerned about the flat appearance of her forehead that they first noticed 2 weeks ago. Physical examination shows flattening of the right side of the forehead and left side of the occiput, and the left ear is positioned farther forward than the right. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?


A ) Calvarial vault remodeling
B ) CT scan
C ) MRI
D ) Placement of a molding helmet
E ) Repositioning exercises
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


The physical findings described are consistent with deformational (positional) plagiocephaly. In contradistinction to craniosynostosis, deformational plagiocephaly will demonstrate deviation of the nasal root away from the side of the forehead with flattening, and the supraorbital rim will be depressed or lowered. Physical findings are sufficient in the scenario described to diagnose the child without CT scan. Occupational and physical therapy should be instituted to encourage behaviors such as head-turning to the right and tipping the top of the head to the left shoulder. In cases that are either severe or are diagnosed late, molding helmets may be advisable.


References
1. Huang MH, Gruss JS, Clarren SK, et al. The differential diagnosis of posterior plagiocephaly: true lambdoid synostosis versus positional molding. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1996 Oct;98(5):765-774.
2. Hansen M, Mulliken JB. Analysis of posterior plagiocephaly: Deformational versus synostotic. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1999 Feb;103(2):371-380.
3. Ellenbogen RG, Gruss JS, Cunningham ML. Update on craniofacial surgery: the differential diagnosis of lambdoid synostosis/posterior plagiocephaly. Clin Neurosurg. 2000;47:303-318.

questions.question:
A plastic surgeon is participating in an international surgical mission to perform primary cleft reconstructions in a resource-limited setting. For which of the following patients would it be most suitable to conduct a combined single-stage primary cleft lip and palate reconstruction?
A) Normally developing 1-year-old child, weighing 4 kg (8.8 lb), with hemoglobin level of 8 g/dL
B) Normally developing 2-year-old child, weighing 8 kg (17.6 lb), with hemoglobin level of 7 g/dL
C) Normally developing 4-year-old child, weighing 17 kg (37.5 lb), with hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL
D) Syndromic 2-year-old with global developmental delays, weighing 10 kg (22 lb), with hemoglobin level of 10 g/dL
E) 67-year-old female patient, weighing 55 kg (121.2 lb), with hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL
questions.answer:
C)
The 4-year-old child with normal development, adequate weight, and hemoglobin of 11 g/dL is the optimal candidate for combined surgery because they meet all safety criteria: sufficient hemoglobin (>10 g/dL recommended for palate surgery), appropriate weight for age, normal development to tolerate longer anesthesia, and age where combined repair can provide both functional and aesthetic benefits. Option A is incorrect because the hemoglobin of 8 g/dL is below the recommended 10 g/dL threshold for safe palate surgery. Option B is incorrect due to the critically low hemoglobin of 7 g/dL, making any palate surgery unsafe. Option D is incorrect because syndromic patients with global delays have increased anesthetic risks and may not tolerate the prolonged surgical time required for combined procedures. Option E is incorrect because elderly patients are unlikely to achieve meaningful speech improvement from palate repair and have increased risks of bleeding and healing complications.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient weighing 154 pounds (70 kg) receives surgical debridement and skin grafting following severe burns covering more than 40% of his total body surface area. What is this patient's complete daily caloric requirement according to the Curreri formula?
A) 2250 kCal/day
B) 3350 kCal/day
C) 4450 kCal/day
D) 5550 kCal/day
E) 6650 kCal/day
questions.answer:
B)
The Curreri formula calculates daily caloric requirements as: 25 kCal/kg/day + 40 kCal/%TBSA/day. For this patient: 25 × 70 + 40 × 40 = 1750 + 1600 = 3350 kCal/day. A) is incorrect because it underestimates the burn component of the calculation. C) is incorrect because it overestimates by adding too much to the base metabolic needs. D) is incorrect as it significantly overestimates the total caloric requirement. E) is incorrect because it grossly overestimates the patient's nutritional needs.

questions.question:
Researchers are investigating the relationship between diabetes mellitus and surgical site infections in patients receiving implant-based breast reconstruction using acellular dermal matrix. Which statistical method would be most suitable for analyzing the data in this investigation?
A) Analysis of variance (ANOVA)
B) Linear regression analysis
C) Pearson's chi-squared test
D) Unpaired T test
E) Wilcoxon rank-sum test
questions.answer:
C)

Choosing the correct statistical method is essential for valid data interpretation. The selection process must consider the nature and distribution characteristics of the variables being examined.

Statistical variables are classified as either categorical or numerical. Categorical variables represent qualitative characteristics (such as surgical site infection, diabetes mellitus, obesity) while numerical variables represent quantitative measurements (such as body mass index, HgbA1c levels). It's also crucial to differentiate between independent (explanatory) and dependent (outcome) variables, which can be either categorical or numerical. Dependent variables are the study outcomes being measured (like surgical site infections - categorical, or surgery duration - numerical) while independent variables are factors believed to influence these outcomes (like diabetes/obesity - categorical, or HgbA1c/BMI - numerical).

Investigations like this one that examine exclusively categorical variables (diabetes mellitus and surgical site infections) are most appropriately analyzed using Pearson's chi-squared test. Conversely, studies involving only numerical variables are best analyzed through regression methods.

A) Analysis of variance (ANOVA) is incorrect because it's designed for comparing means across groups when the dependent variable is numerical, not for analyzing relationships between categorical variables. B) Linear regression analysis is incorrect because it's used when examining relationships involving numerical variables, particularly with a numerical dependent variable. D) Unpaired T test is incorrect because it compares means between two groups with a numerical outcome variable, not for analyzing associations between categorical variables. E) Wilcoxon rank-sum test is incorrect because it's a non-parametric alternative to the t-test for comparing distributions of numerical data between groups, not for categorical variable associations.

questions.question:
A 64-year-old woman who has gone through menopause presents for assessment and management of jaw bone death in the lower jaw. Which medication below should potentially be stopped?
A) Alendronate
B) Calcitonin
C) Estrogen
D) Raloxifene
E) Teriparatide
questions.answer:
A)
Alendronate is the correct answer because it is a bisphosphonate medication that can cause osteonecrosis of the jaw, a serious condition where jaw bone tissue dies due to impaired blood supply and healing capacity. Discontinuing bisphosphonate therapy is a key component of managing this condition. B) Calcitonin is wrong because it is a synthetic hormone used for osteoporosis treatment that does not cause jaw osteonecrosis. C) Estrogen is incorrect as it is used for osteoporosis prevention in postmenopausal women and is not associated with jaw bone death. D) Raloxifene is wrong because it is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that provides estrogen benefits without causing osteonecrosis complications. E) Teriparatide is incorrect since it is a parathyroid hormone analog used for osteoporosis treatment that does not lead to jaw osteonecrosis.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old male cycling enthusiast presents with a 5-week duration of paresthesias affecting the fourth and fifth digits of his left hand. Non-operative treatment has been unsuccessful. Clinical examination reveals diminished grip strength. Dorsal ulnar hand sensation remains normal, and cubital tunnel provocative tests are negative. Which anatomical structures should be surgically decompressed?
A) Osborne ligament and arcade of Struthers
B) Osborne ligament and volar carpal ligament
C) Pisohamate ligament and volar carpal ligament
D) Transverse carpal ligament and arcade of Struthers
E) Transverse carpal ligament and pisohamate ligament
questions.answer:
C)
This patient presents with ulnar tunnel syndrome, characterized by ulnar nerve compression within Guyon's canal. The preserved dorsal ulnar sensation indicates the compression occurs distal to where the dorsal cutaneous branch originates. Surgical decompression requires release of both the pisohamate ligament and volar carpal ligament, which form the boundaries of the ulnar tunnel where the nerve becomes entrapped. A is incorrect because the Osborne ligament and arcade of Struthers are sites of ulnar nerve compression at the elbow (cubital tunnel syndrome), not at the wrist. B is incorrect because while the volar carpal ligament is part of the ulnar tunnel, the Osborne ligament is located at the elbow, not the wrist. D is incorrect because the transverse carpal ligament is involved in median nerve compression (carpal tunnel syndrome), and the arcade of Struthers is an elbow structure. E is incorrect because the transverse carpal ligament is associated with carpal tunnel syndrome affecting the median nerve, not ulnar nerve compression.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old boy develops a severe left first web space contracture 8 months after undergoing skin grafting for a soft-tissue avulsion injury. At the time of contracture release, a pedicled fasciocutaneous flap is planned for coverage of the soft-tissue defect. On the basis of the preoperative markings for the flap in the photographs shown, the flap pedicle is located between which of the following muscles?


A) Brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus
B) Brachioradialis and flexor carpi radialis
C) Extensor digiti minimi and extensor carpi ulnaris
D) Extensor digiti minimi and the extensor digitorum communis
E) Extensor digitorum communis and extensor carpi radialis brevis
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


The photograph illustrates the markings for a reverse posterior interosseous artery (PIA) flap. The reverse PIA flap is a thin, pliable fasciocutaneous flap that can provide reliable coverage of soft-tissue defects involving the dorsal hand, metacarpophalangeal joints, and first web space.
