She previously had bilateral mastectomies with reconstruction using deep inferior epigastric perforator flaps 6 months prior. The patient has no breast implants and does not want them. What percentage range best represents the expected fat graft retention rate in this case?
A) 10%
B) 35%
C) 60%
D) 85%
questions.answer:
C)
Autologous fat grafting has become increasingly popular for correcting aesthetic contour issues following breast reconstruction due to demonstrated safety and effectiveness, along with improved harvesting and processing techniques. The primary concern with fat injection remains the absorption of transplanted fat tissue. Radiologic volumetric studies of fat grafting in both cosmetic and reconstructive breast procedures show retention rates of 50-80%, which may vary based on timing and volume factors. C) 60% is correct as it falls within the established range of 50-80% fat graft survival documented in clinical studies. A) 10% is incorrect because this represents an extremely low survival rate not supported by current literature. B) 35% is incorrect as this falls below the documented range of fat graft retention. D) 85% is incorrect because this exceeds the upper limit of the established 50-80% retention range.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old woman of Korean heritage receives bilateral upper eyelid blepharoplasty to establish a supratarsal fold. The surgeon employs a partial incision approach. What is the most probable complication following this operation?
A) Uneven results
B) Epicanthal web formation
C) Loss of the created fold
D) Inability to close eyelids completely
E) Visible suture material
questions.answer:
A)
Uneven results represent the most frequent complication following Asian blepharoplasty procedures. Asian eyelid surgery differs significantly from Caucasian blepharoplasty as its primary objective is establishing a supratarsal fold rather than rejuvenation. Asian eyelids typically lack or have minimal lid creases, possess shorter tarsal plates, contain descending pre-aponeurotic fat, and have limited connections between the levator aponeurosis and upper lid skin. The surgical technique involves creating permanent attachment points between the levator muscle and supratarsal skin layers. Since patients are usually younger and seeking fold creation or correction of existing asymmetries, even minor differences in crease positioning become highly noticeable. Pre-existing asymmetry should be thoroughly documented and discussed before surgery, and immediate revision should be considered when asymmetry is detected post-operatively. B is incorrect because epicanthal webbing, while a potential complication of epicanthoplasty, is not the most common issue with standard blepharoplasty. C is incorrect because fold loss, though possible from technical errors or insufficient sutures, occurs less frequently than asymmetry. D is incorrect because lagophthalmos typically results from excessive skin removal, which is uncommon in Asian blepharoplasty due to more conservative skin excision, especially with partial incision techniques in younger patients. E is incorrect because suture extrusion, while not uncommon given the use of permanent sutures, is still less frequent than asymmetry issues.

questions.question:
A 49-year-old male presents to the clinic with inability to extend his right wrist, digits, and thumb following a humeral fracture 16 months prior. He had open reduction with internal fixation performed at the time of injury. The fracture union was successful. His functional deficit has remained unchanged since the surgical procedure. Clinical evaluation demonstrates the patient cannot actively extend the wrist, digits, and thumb. Tendon transfer surgery is being considered. Which of the following muscles would be most suitable for transfer to restore digital extension?
A) Brachioradialis
B) Extensor carpi radialis longus
C) Flexor carpi ulnaris
D) Palmaris longus
E) Pronator teres
questions.answer:
C)

The flexor carpi ulnaris is the most suitable muscle for transfer to restore digital extension. This patient has radial nerve palsy from humeral fracture, causing loss of wrist, finger, and thumb extension. Since 16 months have passed, nerve repair is no longer viable, making tendon transfer the best option. The flexor carpi ulnaris provides adequate strength and excursion for finger extension and takes advantage of the natural tenodesis effect between wrist flexion and finger extension. A) Brachioradialis is incorrect because it is innervated by the radial nerve and would be non-functional in high radial nerve palsy. B) Extensor carpi radialis longus is incorrect because it is also affected by the radial nerve palsy and would not be functioning. D) Palmaris longus is incorrect because it lacks sufficient power to provide effective finger extension, though it can be used for thumb extension. E) Pronator teres is incorrect because while it has adequate power, it has limited excursion and is typically reserved for wrist extension restoration rather than finger extension.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old female patient receives smooth round silicone breast implants placed in the subglandular position. After 6 months, she reports breast rippling and noticeable implant edge visibility. What represents the most significant risk factor for developing this complication?
A) Selection of textured implant surface
B) Placement in submuscular pocket
C) Insufficient preoperative breast tissue coverage
D) Oversized implant selection
E) Inframammary approach for insertion
questions.answer:
C)
Insufficient preoperative breast tissue coverage is the primary risk factor for visible implant rippling, particularly in the superior breast region. Subglandular positioning combined with minimal soft tissue thickness significantly elevates this complication risk. A) is incorrect because textured surfaces may contribute to rippling but are not the strongest predictor. B) is incorrect because submuscular placement actually decreases rippling risk by providing additional tissue coverage. D) is incorrect because implant volume has less impact on rippling than tissue thickness. E) is incorrect because the surgical approach has minimal influence on rippling development.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female patient presents to the office with sensory loss affecting her right upper extremity, spanning from the middle portion of her arm along the medial forearm down to her wrist, occurring 5 weeks following bilateral arm lift surgery. Which surgical approach would be most effective in minimizing the likelihood of this sensory deficit while still achieving appropriate aesthetic correction?
A) Performing dissection immediately adjacent to the muscular fascia along the entire arm length
B) Conducting dissection beneath the muscular fascia throughout the complete arm length
C) Preserving a 1-centimeter layer of adipose tissue above the deep fascial plane along the full arm length
D) Executing only cutaneous tissue removal
questions.answer:
C)
The optimal approach involves preserving a 1-centimeter layer of adipose tissue above the deep fascial plane to protect the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, which consistently penetrates the deep fascia approximately 14 cm above the medial epicondyle and travels alongside the basilic vein. This protective fat layer prevents inadvertent nerve injury during the dissection process. Option A is incorrect because dissecting directly adjacent to the muscle fascia places the nerve at high risk due to its anatomical location. Option B is incorrect as dissection beneath the muscle fascia creates an excessively deep plane that endangers the nerve structure. Option D is incorrect because skin-only excision fails to address the underlying tissue excess and would not provide adequate aesthetic improvement in most brachioplasty cases.

questions.question:
A healthy 13-year-old female presents to the office with a tender, progressively growing mass in her axilla. Histologic examination of a previously obtained biopsy specimen revealed proliferative glandular tissue without cellular atypia located in the reticular dermis and subcutaneous layers. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Ectopic breast tissue
B) Fibroadenoma
C) Juvenile mammary hypertrophy
D) Juvenile papillomatosis
E) Lipoma
questions.answer:
A)
Ectopic breast tissue commonly develops along the embryologic milk line and frequently undergoes enlargement during hormonal changes like puberty. This rapid growth may cause discomfort. Microscopic examination demonstrates glandular elements with positive estrogen and progesterone receptor staining. B) is incorrect because fibroadenomas appear as firm, rubbery masses typically within ectopic breast tissue and show both epithelial and stromal proliferation histologically. C) is incorrect because juvenile mammary hypertrophy involves progressive breast enlargement during puberty exceeding 3% of body weight or 1500g, with histology resembling gynecomastia showing increased stromal collagen and adipose tissue. D) is incorrect because juvenile papillomatosis presents similarly to fibroadenoma but shows characteristic papillomatosis, epithelial hyperplasia, sclerosing adenosis, and cysts on microscopy, and actually occurs more frequently in adults despite its name. E) is incorrect because lipomas may appear similar clinically but would demonstrate mature fat cells on histologic examination rather than glandular tissue.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old female presents to the clinic 8 months following circumareolar mastopexy with breast augmentation. She expresses concern regarding asymmetrical areolas, which were symmetrical before surgery. On examination, the right areolar diameter measures 7 cm while the left measures 4 cm. What is the most probable cause of this asymmetry due to failure of which of the following?
A) Breast pillar coaptation
B) Circumareolar epithelial removal
C) Implant pocket creation
D) Circular suture technique
E) Skin envelope fine-tuning
questions.answer:
D)
The most probable cause of nipple-areolar asymmetry in this case is failure of the circular suture technique. Circumareolar mastopexy with augmentation has been associated with inconsistent nipple-areolar complex diameter control. This lift procedure involves concentric periareolar epithelial removal to elevate the nipple-areolar complex and tighten the skin envelope. The underlying cause of areolar widening is the inherent tension created by this closure technique. Utilizing a permanent suture for the circular closure helps prevent postoperative areolar diameter expansion. The introduction of interlocking polytetrafluoroethylene sutures has provided better control over areolar shape and size. When a circular suture fails or pulls through tissue, that areola becomes subject to tension forces and enlarges in diameter. In this patient, surgical correction would involve either replacing the circular suture on the enlarged side or removing it from the smaller areola. A) Breast pillar coaptation is incorrect because it relates to parenchymal shaping rather than areolar diameter control. B) Circumareolar epithelial removal is incorrect as this creates the tension but is a necessary component of the procedure. C) Implant pocket creation is incorrect because pocket formation doesn't directly affect areolar diameter in this context. E) Skin envelope fine-tuning is incorrect as this refers to final periareolar adjustments rather than the primary cause of diameter asymmetry.

questions.question:
A 19-year-old male with no prior medical records comes for his first assessment of enlarged breast tissue. What should be prioritized in the diagnostic evaluation of this patient?
A) Chest radiograph
B) Hand radiograph
C) Breast imaging
D) Examination of the testicles
questions.answer:
D)
Testicular examination is essential because gynecomastia may result from hormonal imbalances between estrogen and testosterone, and can be linked to testicular malignancies that require early detection. A) Chest radiograph is unnecessary for an otherwise healthy 19-year-old without respiratory symptoms. B) Hand radiograph to assess growth plate fusion is typically not needed at age 19 when puberty is likely complete. C) Breast imaging is not routinely required when physical examination reveals no concerning masses or abnormalities.

questions.question:
Which of the following approaches best reduces fat necrosis and enhances fat graft survival?
A) Preventing pressure on transplanted areas after surgery
B) Excluding placement of grafts in previously irradiated tissue
C) Centrifugation of the fat grafts
D) Distributing the graft in numerous small portions using a grid-like pattern
E) Employing ultrasound-assisted liposuction for graft harvesting
questions.answer:
D)
Distributing fat grafts in numerous small portions using a grid-like pattern maximizes contact with surrounding vasculature and promotes revascularization while preventing large deposits that lead to central necrosis. A is incorrect because while avoiding pressure helps, it doesn't address the fundamental issue of graft placement technique. B is incorrect because although irradiated tissue poses challenges, this doesn't directly minimize fat necrosis in viable tissue. C is incorrect because centrifugation alone doesn't address optimal placement methodology. E is incorrect because the harvesting method, while important for graft quality, doesn't determine viability as much as proper placement technique.

questions.question:
A 64-year-old male presents to the emergency department following a collapse at his residence. Physical examination reveals a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm with hemodynamic compromise. The patient undergoes emergent open aneurysm repair. Following surgery, urinary output diminishes despite intensive fluid replacement, and bladder pressure exceeds 30 mmHg. Elevated peak inspiratory pressures are observed. What is the pathophysiologic consequence of elevated intra-abdominal pressure in this case?
A) Direct compression of organs results in reduced systemic afterload
B) Diaphragmatic displacement results in reduced preload
C) Diaphragmatic displacement results in enhanced inferior vena cava flow
D) Vessel compression results in enhanced inferior vena cava flow
E) Vessel compression results in reduced renal vascular resistance
questions.answer:
B)
Abdominal compartment syndrome develops when intra-abdominal pressure rises acutely. Diaphragmatic elevation from increased abdominal pressure causes decreased venous return to the heart and increased intrathoracic pressure, ultimately reducing cardiac preload. A is incorrect because direct organ compression actually increases systemic afterload, not decreases it. C is incorrect because diaphragmatic elevation impedes rather than enhances inferior vena cava flow. D is incorrect because vascular compression reduces rather than increases inferior vena cava flow. E is incorrect because vessel compression increases rather than decreases renal vascular resistance.

questions.question:
A 10-year-old boy presents with an ear injury sustained after a picture frame fell onto his head. The injury is shown in the photograph. He never lost consciousness and has no other injury. Microsurgical reattachment is not an option. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?


A) Debridement and closure
B) Dressing with petroleum gauze
C) Immediate flap reconstruction
D) Reattach as a composite graft
E) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


While composite grafting of large ear avulsions has a globally poor outcome, the avulsed fragment in this patient is a thin piece of the helical rim that includes only a small piece of the helical rim cartilage. The shape of the defect, minimal cartilage involvement, and the fact that this was a clean injury in a young patient, makes an initial attempt to replace the tissue as a composite graft the best initial option. At worst, the tissue acts to cover the wound until a definitive reconstruction can be planned. At best, the tissue survives to some degree and salvages some of the delicate and very hard to replace helical rim contour. This patient described in the clinical scenario had 80% survival of the tissue with this technique and required no further reconstruction.


The exposed cartilage is at risk for infection and may dessicate, so a simple dressing change with petroleum is ill advised. Debridement and closure might be possible if more cartilage was removed, but this further compounds the tissue loss. A split-thickness skin graft contracts and may not take well on exposed cartilage. Immediate flap reconstruction is possible, but a flap can always be done at a later time if the composite graft does not survive.


ReferencesKalus R. Successful bilateral composite ear reattachment. Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open. 2014 Jun; 2(6): e174.Steffen A, Katzbach R, Klaiber S. A comparison of ear reattachment methods: a review of 25 years since Pennington. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2006 Nov;118(6):1358-1364.Thorne CH. Ear reconstruction. In: Thorne CH, Chung KCC, Gosain AK, et al, eds. Grabb and Smith's Plastic Surgery. 7th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2013:283-294.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old woman comes to the office because of a firm, mildly tender, well-circumscribed mass of the abdomen. A photograph is shown. The mass has been slowly increasing in size for the past 6 months. CT scan shows a mass that occupies the left musculofascial abdominal wall, including the rectus, external, and internal oblique muscles, and penetrates through the anterior rectus sheath. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?


A) Neoadjuvant chemotherapy
B) Radiation therapy
C) Wide local excision, bilateral component separation, adjuvant chemotherapy
D) Wide local excision, mesh placement, radiation therapy
E) Wide local excision, right component separation, mesh reinforcement
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.






The lesion in this patient is a desmoid tumor, also known as aggressive fibromatosis. It is a benign tumor, usually found in younger patients between 10 and 40 years old, and is locally aggressive. It is oftentimes associated with pregnancy and prior surgery, and can frequently recur. Treatment is en bloc full-thickness wide local excision (usually with frozen section confirmation of negative margins). As aggressive full-thickness abdominal wall resection is standard of care, reconstruction is more challenging.
If midline fascia can be reapproximated, it should be, as primary fascial closure is associated with the lowest hernia recurrence rates. Reinforcement with mesh has been prospectively demonstrated to reduce recurrence rates even further, especially in defects over 4 cm. If midline fascial reapproximation is not possible, reduction in the size of the defect is crucial to decrease recurrence rates. This is done by component separation. However, in this case, only a right component separation is possible, given that the tumor has invaded the left rectus muscle and obliques, precluding their use for myofascial advancement. If the obliques had been spared, a component separation could still have been attempted even if there were violation of the rectus. The most durable reconstruction would be achieved if midline fascial reapproximation were possible with mesh reinforcement. Second best would be reduction in the size of the defect with a right component separation and placement of mesh as a bridging underlay.


There is no role for neoadjuvant chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the treatment of these tumors.


References
1. Catania G, Ruggeri L, Iuppa G, et al. Abdominal wall reconstruction with intraperitoneal prosthesis in desmoid tumors surgery. Updates Surg. 2012 Mar;64(1):43-48.
2. Yezhelyev MV, Deigni O, Losken A. Management of full-thickness abdominal wall defects following tumor resection. Ann Plast Surg. 2012 Aug;69(2):186-191.
3. Bertani E, Chiappa A, Testori A, et al. Desmoid tumors of the anterior abdominal wall: results from a monocentric surgical experience and review of the literature. Ann Surg Oncol. 2009 Jun;16(6):1642-1649.
4. Luijendijk RW, Hop WC, van den Tol MP, et al. A comparison of suture repair with mesh repair for incisional hernia. N Engl J Med. 2000 Aug 10;343(6):392-398.
5. Itani KM, Rosen M, Vargo D, et al. Prospective study of single-stage repair of contaminated hernias using a biologic porcine tissue matrix: the RICH Study. Surgery. 2012 Sep;152(3):498-505.
6. Garvey PB, Bailey CM, Baumann DP, et al. Violation of the rectus complex is not a contraindication to component separation for abdominal wall reconstruction. J Am Coll Surg. 2012 Feb;214(2):131-139. Epub 2011 Dec 9.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old woman presents with a basal cell carcinoma of the lower nasal dorsum. A photograph is shown. Mohs micrographic surgery is performed, and the patient is left with a 2 √o 2-cm defect with exposed cartilage. The patient desires the best cosmetic outcome but refuses more than one procedure. Which of the following is the most appropriate option to accommodate the patient‚Äos wishes?


A) Dorsal nasal flap
B) Full-thickness skin graft
C) Healing by secondary intention
D) Paramedian forehead flap
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


The correct option for this particular patient is an axial frontonasal or dorsal nasal flap as demonstrated in the photographs. When immediate local tissue is insufficient for primary repair of nasal defects, one is forced to look for additional tissue for a proper reconstruction. The ideal reconstruction would utilize the remaining nasal skin if possible, in order to match the texture and color of nasal skin. This is especially true in the middle and lower third of the nose. The axial frontonasal flap is a modification of the original flap described by Rieger and is based on a branch of the angular artery near the medial canthus. Because of the axial nature, the flap can be mobilized through both a wide or narrow skin bridge, or even as an island flap if necessary. The flap provides a sizable amount of skin with similar color and texture for the dorsum and in some cases the nasal tip as well. Limitations of the flap include a maximal defect diameter of 2.0 to 2.5 cm, possible nasal ala or tip retraction, and possible skin thickness mismatch where the thicker glabellar skin that has been mobilized inferiorly meets the thinner medial canthal skin.


Healing by secondary intention would be difficult with exposed cartilage and would be cosmetically and functionally unacceptable with this particular wound. In some cases, a full-thickness skin graft for a small superficial defect can provide excellent results; however, graft take is unpredictable with prolonged healing and in some cases leave a patch-like result. In this situation, a full-thickness skin graft would have difficulty healing with exposed cartilage. Even if perichondrium were intact to allow for proper healing, the discrepancy in skin thickness would be cosmetically unacceptable to this patient. Paramedian forehead flaps are the gold standard for large, complex defects of the nasal tip and ala, but require at least two to three stages and would not be an option for this patient.


ReferencesBaker SR. Reconstruction of the nose. In: Baker SR, ed. Local Flaps in Facial Reconstruction. 2nd ed. Mosby-Elsevier; 2007:415-474.Guo L, Pribaz JR, Pribaz JJ. Nasal reconstruction with local flaps: a simple algorithm for management of small defects. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008;122(5):130e-139e.Marchac D, Toth B. The axial frontonasal flap revisited. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1985;76(5):686-694.Scheufler O. Variations in frontonasal flap design for single-stage reconstruction of the nasal tip. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2016;138(6):1032e-1042e.

questions.question:
After undergoing a skin-preserving mastectomy, a 39-year-old patient receives breast reconstruction using a deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap. To enhance sensory function of the flap, the anterior sensory branch of the fourth intercostal nerve is connected to which nerve found within the DIEP flap?
A) Genitofemoral
B) Iliohypogastric
C) Ilioinguinal
D) Intercostal
E) Lateral femoral cutaneous
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is D because intercostal nerves provide segmental cutaneous innervation to the lower abdominal region and travel through the rectus abdominis muscle, making them the appropriate target for coaptation with the fourth intercostal nerve to restore breast sensation. The T10 intercostal nerve branch is most commonly utilized as it supplies the periumbilical dermatome. A is incorrect because the genitofemoral nerve innervates the upper anterior thigh and mons pubis, not the abdominal flap tissue. B is incorrect because the iliohypogastric nerve supplies sensation to the lateral gluteal area rather than the abdominal region used in DIEP reconstruction. C is incorrect because the ilioinguinal nerve provides sensation to the upper medial thigh, not the abdominal donor site. E is incorrect because the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve innervates the lateral thigh and is not involved in abdominal flap sensation.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old female patient receives bilateral breast reconstruction utilizing free microvascular tissue transfer from the abdominal region. Eight hours postoperatively, the right breast flap demonstrates a mottled appearance with engorgement. Which of the following treatments should NOT be administered to this patient?
A) Local heparin irrigation of flap vasculature
B) Papaverine administration to flap vessels
C) Systemic heparin therapy
D) Systemic thrombolytic therapy
E) Local thrombolytic treatment to flap vessels
questions.answer:
D)
Systemic thrombolytic therapy is contraindicated because it poses significant risk of systemic bleeding complications and hemorrhage throughout the body. Local heparin irrigation is appropriate as it helps prevent further clot formation and can flush existing thrombus from flap vessels. Papaverine administration to flap vessels is correct as it provides vasodilation to improve blood flow locally. Systemic heparin is acceptable as it can help prevent additional thrombosis while having manageable anticoagulation effects. Local thrombolytic treatment to flap vessels is appropriate as it can dissolve clots directly at the site without systemic risks.

questions.question:
A doctor is planning to investigate how well a novel analgesic works in their patient population. They are designing a prospective randomized trial with one group receiving the experimental pain reliever and another group getting a placebo. Information from both groups will be collected and examined to assess the statistical significance of pain reduction from the experimental drug. Which of the following statistical methods would most appropriately help establish the required sample size for this investigation?
A) ANOVA
B) Chi-square
C) Fisher exact test
D) Statistical power
E) Student t-test
questions.answer:
D)
Statistical power represents the probability of detecting a clinically meaningful difference when one truly exists. Power analysis examines the relationships between effect size, sample size, significance level, and the power of the statistical test. Statistical power can be utilized to calculate appropriate sample sizes during study planning or to evaluate non-significant findings after data has been collected. A statistical power of 80% is considered optimal for research studies. A) ANOVA is incorrect because it compares means across multiple groups rather than determining sample size. B) Chi-square is incorrect because it tests associations between categorical variables, not sample size calculations. C) Fisher exact test is incorrect because it analyzes contingency tables with small sample sizes, not for determining sample size requirements. E) Student t-test is incorrect because it compares means between groups rather than calculating needed sample sizes.

questions.question:
A healthy 25-year-old female presents with an extensive, microcystic lymphatic malformation affecting her pelvis and perineum. The lesion extends through the skin and subcutaneous tissue of the area, with widespread involvement of the pelvic musculature. What would be the most appropriate treatment approach for this condition?
A) Intralesional corticosteroid injection
B) Propranolol treatment
C) Sclerotherapy
D) Sirolimus treatment
E) Surgical resection
questions.answer:
D)
Systemic sirolimus treatment represents the most appropriate and effective therapeutic option for this patient. Recent research demonstrates that sirolimus shows remarkable efficacy in treating and clinically reducing venous malformations (90% response rate) and lymphatic malformations (95% response rate). It proves particularly beneficial for vascular tumors complicated by Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon (96% response rate with 93% coagulopathy normalization). A) is incorrect because intralesional corticosteroid injections are indicated for hemangiomas rather than vascular malformations. B) is incorrect because propranolol therapy is specifically used for treating hemangiomas, not malformations. C) is incorrect because sclerotherapy is effective for macrocystic lymphatic malformations but not suitable for microcystic variants. E) is incorrect because surgical resection would be excessively destructive given the anatomical location, extensive distribution, and critical structures involved in this case.

questions.question:
What type of joint classification describes the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint of the thumb?
A) Ball-and-socket
B) Condyloid
C) Hinge
D) Pivot
E) Saddle
questions.answer:
C)
The thumb's metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint is classified as a hinge joint, permitting only flexion and extension movements. This joint structure makes it susceptible to collateral ligament injuries when subjected to lateral stress forces. A) Ball-and-socket joints are incorrect as they allow multiple planes of motion including rotation, found in shoulders and hips. B) Condyloid joints are wrong because they permit flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, and circumduction, seen in the MCP joints of fingers 2-5. D) Pivot joints are incorrect as they only allow rotational movement, exemplified by the atlantoaxial joint. E) Saddle joints are wrong because they allow multiple movements including circumduction and are found at the thumb's carpometacarpal joint, not the MCP joint.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old male presents to the clinic with a 12-year history of recurring painful lumps in his inguinal area, gluteal region, and perineum. Clinical examination reveals deep subcutaneous collections of pus. Several have burst open and created multiple draining tunnels. Along with careful hygiene practices, which of the following represents the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Hormonal blockade therapy
B) TNF-alpha inhibitor treatment
C) Surgical removal
D) Radiation treatment
E) Routine antiseptic washes
questions.answer:
C)
This patient presents with hidradenitis suppurativa, and given the extensive nature with multiple interconnected sinus tracts and abscesses throughout the region, wide surgical excision of all affected tissue and underlying sinus tracts is the most effective treatment option. The severity and chronicity of this case with established tract formation requires definitive surgical management for optimal symptom control. A) Antiandrogen therapy is incorrect because while it may help in some cases, it is not the most appropriate first-line treatment for this severe, established disease with extensive sinus tract formation. B) Anti-TNF therapy is incorrect because although it has shown benefit in some studies, surgical excision remains the most definitive treatment for this advanced stage of disease. D) Radiotherapy is incorrect because it was used historically but is associated with poor tissue healing and is not considered appropriate modern management. E) Chlorhexidine baths are incorrect because while good hygiene is important as an adjunct, antiseptic washes alone are insufficient for treating this advanced stage of hidradenitis suppurativa with established sinus tracts.

questions.question:
A 69-year-old female patient with breast carcinoma receives bilateral breast reconstruction utilizing free deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flaps. Intraoperatively, she develops hypotension that fails to respond to conventional crystalloid and colloid fluid therapy. The anesthesiology team decides to give norepinephrine to manage her blood pressure. What flap-related complication is most probable?
A) Flap failure
B) Bleeding collection
C) Return to operating room
D) Wound separation
E) No adverse effect
questions.answer:
E)
The correct answer is E because vasopressor medications do not increase flap complications, and studies have actually demonstrated decreased intraoperative flap complications with agents like ephedrine. While traditional teaching suggested avoiding vasopressors during free tissue transfer due to concerns about vasoconstriction and compromised flap perfusion, extensive research has proven the safety of these medications in this setting. The lack of complications likely results from sympathetic denervation following flap transfer, adventitial stripping causing sympathectomy, and topical vasodilator use. Any potential vasoconstrictive effects are outweighed by improved flap perfusion from elevated systemic blood pressure. A is incorrect because flap failure does not occur with appropriate vasopressor use during free tissue transfer. B is incorrect because hematoma formation is not associated with vasopressor administration in this context. C is incorrect because reoperation rates are not increased with vasopressor use during flap surgery. D is incorrect because wound dehiscence is not a recognized complication of vasopressor use during free flap procedures.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with a congenital mucus-secreting cutaneous sinus tract positioned in the lower portion of the neck, situated over the anterior margin of the left sternocleidomastoid muscle. Physical examination reveals that the act of swallowing produces visible dimpling of the sinus opening. Operative probing demonstrates communication with the left tonsillar fossa. During surgical dissection, what is the most probable upward pathway of this sinus tract?
A) Deep to the hypoglossal nerve
B) Deep to the internal carotid artery
C) Superficial to the posterior belly of the digastric muscle
D) Superficial to the stylohyoid muscle
E) Superficial to the stylopharyngeal muscle
questions.answer:
E)

The correct answer is E because this second pharyngeal cleft and pouch fistula follows an embryologically determined pathway that runs superficial to structures derived from the third pharyngeal arch, including the stylopharyngeal muscle. Second pharyngeal apparatus anomalies course deep to second arch derivatives and superficial to third through sixth arch derivatives. A is incorrect because the hypoglossal nerve develops from occipital somites, not pharyngeal apparatus mesenchyme, and pharyngeal fistulas run superficial to it. B is incorrect because the internal carotid artery is a third pharyngeal arch derivative, so the fistula runs superficial to it, not deep. C is incorrect because the posterior belly of the digastric muscle is a second pharyngeal arch structure, so the fistula runs deep to it. D is incorrect because the stylohyoid muscle is also a second pharyngeal arch derivative, making the fistula course deep to this structure.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male presents to the clinic seeking counseling about breast cancer risk following genetic testing that revealed he carries a BRCA2 gene mutation. His family history is significant for breast, prostate, and ovarian malignancies. What is his approximate lifetime risk of developing breast cancer?
A) 6%
B) 15%
C) 30%
D) 60%
E) 85%
questions.answer:
A)

The correct answer is A) 6%. Male carriers of BRCA2 mutations have an approximately 6-7% lifetime risk of developing breast cancer, which represents a significantly elevated risk compared to the general male population but is much lower than the risk for female carriers. This risk is highest during the 30s and 40s and decreases with advancing age. B) 15% is incorrect as it overestimates the risk for male BRCA2 carriers. C) 30% is incorrect as this substantially overestimates the lifetime risk. D) 60% is incorrect as this risk level is more associated with female carriers of certain mutations. E) 85% is incorrect as this represents the lifetime breast cancer risk for female BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers, not males.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old female comes to the office 3 years following the development of a right-sided unilateral Bell's palsy complaining of lack of corner-of-mouth elevation and nasolabial fold asymmetry during smiling. No prior interventions have been performed. Which of the following surgical options is most likely to achieve natural smile animation triggered by emotion on the paralyzed side?
A) Cross-facial nerve grafting from the normal left side to the peripheral facial nerve branches on the paralyzed right side
B) Direct temporalis muscle transfer
C) Single-stage gracilis free tissue transfer with nerve connection to the right masseteric nerve
D) Two-phase reconstruction using cross-facial nerve grafting from the normal left side followed by functional gracilis muscle free flap to the right side
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is D because after 3 years of facial paralysis, the native facial muscles have undergone irreversible atrophy, making muscle transfer necessary, and a two-stage approach using contralateral facial nerve input provides the best chance for spontaneous emotional smile activation. Cross-facial nerve grafting followed by gracilis free flap allows for facial nerve-powered reconstruction, which is superior for generating natural emotional responses compared to other cranial nerve sources. A is incorrect because direct reinnervation of native muscles fails after 24 months due to irreversible muscle atrophy. B is incorrect because temporalis transfer is powered by the trigeminal nerve, requiring jaw clenching for activation and rarely achieving spontaneous emotional smiling. C is incorrect because single-stage gracilis with masseteric nerve also uses trigeminal nerve power, requiring conscious jaw movement rather than providing natural emotional smile activation.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old male patient with ASA Physical Status 2 presents for consultation regarding autologous fat transfer to address HIV-related lipodystrophy. His current CD4+ T-cell count is 100 cells/mm³. Which of the following variables most significantly elevates his risk for postoperative adverse events?
A) ASA Physical Status classification
B) CD4+ T-cell count
C) HIV infection status
D) Minimally invasive surgical approach
questions.answer:
B)

The CD4+ T-cell count of 100 cells/mm³ represents the most significant risk factor for postoperative complications in this patient. A CD4 count below 200 cells/mm³ indicates AIDS and is strongly associated with increased risk of wound infections and other postoperative complications due to severe immunocompromise. A) ASA Physical Status 2 indicates only mild systemic disease and represents lower surgical risk compared to higher ASA classes. C) HIV seropositivity by itself has not been demonstrated to be an independent predictor of postoperative complications when other factors are controlled. D) Minimally invasive procedures like percutaneous fat grafting have not been shown to increase infection risk in HIV patients, unlike transoral mucosal surgeries which do carry higher risk.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old female patient receiving breast cancer therapy experiences discomfort at her port location 6 hours following paclitaxel leakage from a subcutaneously tunneled subclavian central line. The patient maintains stable vital signs and has no respiratory distress. Moderate edema and pain are noted in the area between the port and clavicle. What represents the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Use of calcium gluconate gel application
B) Use of topical collagenase treatment
C) Catheter exchange using guidewire technique
D) Catheter removal with monitoring
E) Surgical debridement procedure
questions.answer:
D)
This patient presents with paclitaxel leakage from a compromised or displaced catheter with mild manifestations; thus, catheter removal with monitoring is the appropriate intervention. D is correct because the patient has minimal symptoms from the extravasation and no signs of severe tissue damage, making conservative management with line removal and observation the standard approach. A is incorrect because calcium gluconate gel is specifically used for hydrofluoric acid exposure to neutralize fluoride ions, not for chemotherapy extravasation. B is incorrect because topical collagenase is reserved for wounds with established tissue death and has no indication in this acute extravasation scenario. C is incorrect because wire-guided catheter exchange is contraindicated when the existing catheter is compromised or improperly positioned. E is incorrect because surgical intervention is rarely needed for extravasation injuries and is reserved for cases with compartment syndrome or significant tissue necrosis, which this patient does not exhibit.

questions.question:
What is the most frequent indication for secondary surgery following arm lift procedures in patients with massive weight reduction?
A) Blood collection under the skin
B) Excessive scar tissue formation
C) Bacterial contamination
D) Fluid accumulation
E) Separation of wound edges
questions.answer:
B)
Excessive scar tissue formation is the primary reason patients require additional procedures after arm lift surgery. While patients generally report satisfaction with brachioplasty outcomes, complications occur frequently with some studies documenting rates up to 50%. Most complications are minor and manageable conservatively. The most common indication for reoperation is scar revision due to unfavorable scarring that becomes thickened or widened, which can be addressed through revision surgery, laser therapy, or steroid injections. A) is incorrect because hematomas are typically managed conservatively with observation or drainage rather than requiring reoperation. C) is incorrect because infections are usually treated successfully with oral antibiotics without need for surgery. D) is incorrect because seromas are generally managed with observation or aspiration rather than surgical intervention. E) is incorrect because wound separation is typically managed with dressing changes and conservative care.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old male presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of discomfort and enlargement affecting the proximal phalanx of his right index finger. There is no reported history of injury. Radiographic imaging and MRI of the affected finger reveal an expanding osteolytic lesion within the proximal phalanx. Histopathological analysis of a biopsy specimen establishes the diagnosis of giant cell tumor of bone. What is the most appropriate staging evaluation for this patient?
A) Cervical spine CT scan
B) Chest CT scan
C) Wrist MR arthrography
D) Brain MRI
E) Pulmonary function studies
questions.answer:
B)
Chest CT scan is the most appropriate staging test because giant cell tumors of bone, while benign, can metastasize to the lungs in 1-5% of cases, making pulmonary evaluation essential for proper staging and management planning. A) Cervical spine CT is incorrect as giant cell tumors rarely metastasize to the spine and this would not be part of routine staging. C) Wrist MR arthrography is incorrect because it evaluates joint structures rather than staging for metastatic disease, and the tumor is in the proximal phalanx, not the wrist joint. D) Brain MRI is incorrect since giant cell tumors do not typically metastasize to the brain. E) Pulmonary function studies are incorrect as they assess lung function rather than detect metastatic lesions.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient presents with a unilateral fixed, dilated, and unresponsive pupil occurring 1 day following prophylactic mastectomy with immediate reconstruction using a superior gluteal artery perforator free flap. Her postoperative course was complicated by significant nausea. Multiple antiemetic agents were used prophylactically during the surgical procedure. Which of the following medications is the most probable cause of the fixed dilated pupil?
A) Intravenous dexamethasone
B) Intravenous droperidol
C) Intravenous ondansetron
D) Oral metoclopramide
E) Scopolamine patch
questions.answer:
E)

The scopolamine patch is the most likely cause of the fixed dilated pupil. Scopolamine is a centrally-acting anticholinergic medication delivered transdermally via a patch placed behind the ear for prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting. Unilateral mydriasis can occur when patients inadvertently contaminate their eye by touching the patch and then rubbing their eye without proper hand hygiene. This pharmacologic mydriasis results in a fixed, dilated pupil that will not respond to light or constrict with pilocarpine testing. A) Intravenous dexamethasone is incorrect because it is a corticosteroid antiemetic that does not have anticholinergic properties and would not cause mydriasis. B) Intravenous droperidol is incorrect because it is a dopamine antagonist antiemetic without anticholinergic effects that could cause pupillary dilation. C) Intravenous ondansetron is incorrect because it is a serotonin receptor antagonist that lacks anticholinergic activity and does not affect pupil size. D) Oral metoclopramide is incorrect because it is a dopamine receptor antagonist and prokinetic agent that does not possess anticholinergic properties that would lead to mydriasis.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male experienced multiple internal organ injuries, extended unconsciousness, and an orbital floor fracture during an accident 3 months prior. He postponed surgical repair of the orbital floor fracture initially but now presents seeking treatment for fracture-related symptoms. The patient demonstrates normal mental status and orientation. Which of the following clinical findings would most likely be improved by orbital floor fracture reconstruction in this patient?
A) Loss of vision
B) Lower eyelid eversion
C) Posterior globe displacement
D) Eyeball size
E) Upward gaze limitation
questions.answer:
C)
Posterior globe displacement (enophthalmos) is the finding most likely to be corrected by delayed orbital floor fracture repair. Orbital floor fractures alter the orbital cavity volume, which affects globe positioning and can trap the inferior rectus muscle, restricting eye movement. Surgical repair reduces orbital volume back toward normal, restoring proper globe position and correcting the retro-displacement that occurs from increased orbital space.

A is incorrect because vision loss typically results from optic nerve damage, which cannot be restored through orbital floor reconstruction. B is incorrect because lower eyelid eversion usually stems from eyelid contracture rather than orbital floor defects and would not improve with floor repair. D is incorrect because eyeball size refers to the actual globe dimensions, not orbital volume, and remains unchanged by orbital floor surgery. E is incorrect because upward gaze restriction from muscle entrapment requires immediate repair to prevent permanent muscle damage; after 3 months, the entrapped muscle would likely have sustained irreversible injury that delayed repair cannot correct.

questions.question:
A 14-year-old male patient comes to the clinic with a fast-growing, non-tender swelling on the left maxillary region. Radiographic studies show an expanding, radiolucent area with cortical bone thinning but no extension into surrounding soft tissues. Histopathological examination reveals immature woven bone formation within a fibroblastic matrix, with no cellular atypia present. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Osteosarcoma
B) Fibrous dysplasia
C) Ossifying fibroma
D) Juvenile ossifying fibroma
E) Giant cell granuloma
questions.answer:
D)

Juvenile ossifying fibroma represents a benign yet locally invasive fibro-osseous tumor that predominantly occurs in children and adolescents, particularly involving the maxillary bones. Radiographically, it appears as an expanding radiolucent mass with cortical thinning, while microscopic examination reveals immature woven bone within a fibroblastic matrix. A) Osteosarcoma is incorrect because it is a malignant tumor that would show cellular atypia and aggressive features. B) Fibrous dysplasia is incorrect as it typically shows irregular bony trabeculae in a more cellular stroma without the expansile growth pattern. C) Ossifying fibroma is incorrect because it occurs in adults and demonstrates slower growth characteristics. E) Giant cell granuloma is incorrect as it primarily consists of multinucleated giant cells and lacks the immature bone formation seen in this case.

questions.question:
A 6-year-old boy presents with a congenital absence of the radius, resulting in marked radial deviation of the hand and hypoplasia of the thumb. Which syndrome is most commonly associated with congenital radial deficiency and should be screened for due to its significant hematologic implications?

A) Fanconi anemia
B) Klippel-Feil syndrome
C) Poland syndrome
D) VATER association
E) Crouzon syndrome
questions.answer:
A)

Fanconi anemia (A) is the correct answer because it is a genetic disorder frequently associated with congenital radial deficiency (radial club hand) and carries significant risk for bone marrow failure and malignancy. Children with radial deficiency should always be screened for Fanconi anemia due to these hematologic risks. 

Option B (Klippel-Feil syndrome) is incorrect because while it involves cervical vertebral fusion and can be associated with limb anomalies, it does not have a strong association with radial deficiency or hematologic disease. 
Option C (Poland syndrome) is incorrect as this syndrome is characterized by absence of the pectoralis muscle and syndactyly, not radial deficiency. 
Option D (VATER association) is incorrect; although it includes vertebral, anal, tracheoesophageal, and renal anomalies, radial deficiency is not the most classic feature and VATER does not carry significant hematologic risks. 
Option E (Crouzon syndrome) is incorrect because it is associated with craniosynostosis, not congenital hand anomalies such as radial deficiency.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old female presents to the emergency room following a traumatic injury to her right thumb and index finger caused by an industrial ink press. Clinical examination reveals complete amputation of the right thumb at the carpometacarpal joint level, along with amputation of the index finger at the middle phalangeal head. The severed thumb was immediately wrapped in wet gauze but shows extensive crushing damage. What is the optimal definitive treatment for the thumb amputation?
A) Wound debridement and primary closure
B) Microsurgical great toe transfer to thumb
C) Osteoplastic reconstruction of the thumb
D) Thumb replantation surgery
E) Pollicization using the remaining index finger
questions.answer:
E)
Pollicization using the remaining index finger is the optimal choice because the thumb provides approximately 40% of total hand function, making reconstruction essential. Pollicization involves transferring a finger with its neurovascular supply to create a functional thumb, and it works exceptionally well for carpometacarpal joint level amputations. Since the index finger is already traumatized with limited future mobility, converting it into a thumb provides excellent aesthetic outcomes, preserved joint motion, and reliable sensation while maintaining normal foot anatomy. A) is incorrect because simple wound closure would severely compromise hand function without thumb reconstruction. B) is incorrect because great toe transfer is better suited for amputations between the MCP and IP joints, and the damaged index finger provides a superior reconstruction option while preserving foot integrity. C) is incorrect because osteoplastic reconstruction is rarely used today due to poor outcomes including stiffness, poor aesthetics, limited sensation, and requiring multiple surgical stages. D) is incorrect because the thumb was severely mangled, making successful replantation unlikely or impossible.

questions.question:
A 41-year-old female patient presents for evaluation regarding tummy tuck and fat removal procedures in an ambulatory care facility. The anticipated surgical duration is 2 hours. Her Caprini risk assessment score is 2. What is the estimated probability of venous thromboembolism development in this patient?
A) 1%
B) 10%
C) 15%
D) 20%
E) 25%
questions.answer:
A)
The correct answer is A) 1%. Multiple research studies have focused on venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk assessment in aesthetic surgery patients, though consensus remains elusive. While no specific guidelines exist for tummy tuck and liposuction procedures, clinical management approaches are individualized and differ among surgeons. Abdominoplasty is recognized to carry elevated VTE risk compared to other surgical procedures. Although reported VTE rates vary across studies, the mean risk approximates 1%, with some research showing rates as low as 0.15%. Importantly, studies have not demonstrated increased VTE incidence with combined procedures. Regardless, Caprini scoring and individualized patient assessment remain essential. At minimum, pneumatic compression devices should be utilized for all abdominoplasty patients, with consideration of anticoagulation therapy for higher-risk cases. B) 10% is incorrect because this rate significantly overestimates the actual VTE risk for abdominoplasty procedures. C) 15% is incorrect as it represents a much higher incidence than documented in clinical studies. D) 20% is incorrect because it exceeds the established risk profile for these procedures. E) 25% is incorrect as it grossly overestimates the VTE probability for abdominoplasty patients.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male patient presents to the clinic reporting a clicking sound when opening his mouth. He experienced trauma to the right facial region 12 months prior during a snowmobile accident. Initial assessment at that time revealed no fracture. Current examination demonstrates normal mandibular range of motion. What is the most probable etiology of this patient's symptoms?
A) Hemarthrosis of the temporomandibular joint
B) Condylar head impingement on the articular eminence
C) Mandibular condyle striking the glenoid fossa
D) Intra-articular foreign material in the temporomandibular joint
E) Anterior displacement of the articular disc
questions.answer:
E)
Anterior displacement of the articular disc is the most likely cause of the clicking sensation during jaw opening. The temporomandibular joint contains an articular disc that divides the joint into superior and inferior compartments. When the posterior disc attachments become stretched or torn, the disc can sublux anteriorly and then relocate during jaw movement, producing the characteristic clicking sound. This condition commonly develops following trauma and may initially be painless. A) is incorrect because hemarthrosis would typically cause joint stiffness and pain rather than isolated clicking. B) is incorrect because normal condylar contact with the articular eminence during jaw opening does not produce pathological clicking. C) is incorrect because the condyle normally articulates with the glenoid fossa without producing clicking sounds. D) is incorrect because foreign bodies in the TMJ are extremely rare and would likely cause additional symptoms beyond clicking.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman undergoes a breast reduction surgery and experiences postoperative complications, including a hematoma formation. On examination, the hematoma is found to be located within the breast tissue, and she is experiencing significant pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this complication?

A) Observation and reassurance
B) Drainage of the hematoma
C) Immediate reoperation
D) Administering anticoagulants
E) Application of compressive dressings
questions.answer:
B)
Drainage of the hematoma is the most appropriate management in this case, especially given the significant pain and the location of the hematoma within the breast tissue. Observation may be appropriate for small, asymptomatic hematomas, but in this situation, intervention is warranted to relieve pain and prevent further complications. Immediate reoperation may not be necessary unless there are other indications. Anticoagulants are not indicated in the setting of a hematoma, and compressive dressings would not adequately address the issue.

questions.question:
A 70-year-old male patient with a smoking history and oromandibular malignancy is planned for tumor resection, computer-guided fibular mandibular reconstruction, and adjuvant radiotherapy. The patient has a strong desire for dental rehabilitation. Which of the following most accurately describes when dental implants can be most safely inserted?
A) At the time of initial surgery
B) Following completion of radiation treatment
C) After unsuccessful prosthetic attempts
D) Twelve months after the operation
E) Not recommended under any circumstances
questions.answer:
A)
Immediate dental implant placement is the safest and most appropriate timing for this patient. Contemporary advances in virtual surgical planning and coordinated multidisciplinary care involving ablative surgeons, reconstructive surgeons, oral surgeons, and radiation oncologists have enabled successful immediate dental restoration with high success rates. This approach allows for timely restoration of oral function including feeding and speech, which is particularly important given the often limited prognosis of these patients. B is incorrect because waiting until after radiation therapy increases the risk of complications and delays functional restoration unnecessarily. C is incorrect because denture failure is not a prerequisite for implant consideration in this reconstructive scenario. D is incorrect because delaying implant placement for one year is outdated practice that unnecessarily postpones functional restoration. E is incorrect because modern techniques have demonstrated that dental implants can be successfully placed in appropriately selected patients undergoing mandibular reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 64-year-old male patient has a confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue via biopsy. Surgical removal and reconstruction are being planned. Allen testing bilaterally demonstrates complete radial artery dominance, which is verified using non-invasive ultrasound imaging. The surgical plan involves using an ulnar artery perforator flap from the non-dominant hand. When contrasting the ulnar artery perforator flap with the radial forearm flap, which of the following represents a significant advantage of the ulnar artery flap?
A) It provides a greater pedicle vessel diameter
B) It offers an extended pedicle length
C) It demonstrates reduced flap thrombosis rates
D) It serves as a superior option for incorporating bone in osteocutaneous reconstruction
E) It reduces the likelihood of tendon exposure at the harvest site
questions.answer:
E)
The ulnar artery perforator flap's more proximal anatomical position allows for primary closure of the donor site more frequently than the radial forearm flap. When primary closure is not achievable, the exposed deeper structures are typically muscle bellies rather than peritenon or tendons, which are more commonly exposed in the more distally positioned radial forearm flap. A is incorrect because the radial artery typically has similar or larger diameter compared to the ulnar artery. B is incorrect because the radial forearm flap actually provides a longer pedicle length. C is incorrect because thrombosis rates have been demonstrated to be equivalent between both flaps. D is incorrect because the radial forearm flap has better reported outcomes for osteocutaneous reconstruction when bone incorporation is needed.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient receives immediate unilateral breast reconstruction using a free deep inferior epigastric artery perforator (DIEP) flap. Following completion of the surgery, the flap skin paddle demonstrates venous congestion. During reexploration, the venous anastomosis appears intact with detectable venous outflow using handheld pencil Doppler assessment, yet the flap exhibits persistent venous congestion with rapid capillary refill. What is the most suitable next management step?
A) Initiate postoperative leech therapy
B) Loosely reposition the flap and observe carefully
C) Create a second venous anastomosis utilizing the superficial inferior epigastric vein
D) Create a second venous anastomosis utilizing the vena comitans
E) Revise the existing venous anastomosis with hand-sewn technique
questions.answer:
C)
The superficial inferior epigastric vein (SIEV) serves as a crucial backup vessel for venous drainage when the primary deep venous system is insufficient. When a DIEP flap shows venous congestion despite patent deep venous anastomosis, the SIEV should be assessed and connected to a recipient vessel to provide additional venous outflow, as the flap may be dependent on superficial venous drainage. A) is incorrect because leeches are not appropriate for global venous congestion in free flaps and would not address the underlying drainage issue. B) is incorrect because loose reinsertion alone will not resolve inadequate venous outflow when the primary drainage system is insufficient. D) is incorrect because using another vena comitans does not address the potential need for superficial venous drainage that the SIEV provides. E) is incorrect because the anastomosis is already patent, so revision would not solve the underlying problem of inadequate total venous outflow capacity.

questions.question:
Which of the following fracture types is most commonly associated with an open wound?
A) Barton fracture
B) Colles fracture
C) Epiphyseal fracture
D) Salter-Harris III fracture
E) Seymour fracture
questions.answer:
E)
The Seymour fracture consistently presents as an open injury in pediatric patients. This fracture occurs when displacement happens through the epiphysis with nail matrix tissue becoming trapped between the bone fragments, creating an inherently open wound pattern. A) Barton fractures are closed injuries of the distal radius involving the radiocarpal joint. B) Colles fractures are typically closed distal radius fractures with dorsal angulation. C) Epiphyseal fractures can be either open or closed depending on the specific injury pattern. D) Salter-Harris III fractures involve the epiphysis and metaphysis but are not inherently open injuries.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old tennis player with right-hand dominance presents with a 6-month history of lateral elbow discomfort. He experiences pain during object lifting that extends into the forearm. On examination, there is tenderness located just distal and anterior to the lateral epicondyle. Which muscle is most likely involved?
A) Brachioradialis
B) Extensor carpi radialis brevis
C) Extensor carpi radialis longus
D) Extensor carpi ulnaris
E) Extensor digiti minimi
questions.answer:
B)
The extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB) is the primary muscle implicated in lateral epicondylitis, as its origin at the lateral epicondyle has a poorly vascularized undersurface that predisposes it to degenerative changes and partial tearing. A) Brachioradialis is incorrect because while it originates from the lateral epicondyle region, it is not the primary site of pathology in tennis elbow. C) Extensor carpi radialis longus is incorrect because although it shares a common origin, it is less frequently involved than the ECRB. D) Extensor carpi ulnaris is incorrect because despite originating from the lateral epicondyle, it is not the predominant muscle affected in lateral epicondylitis. E) Extensor digiti minimi is incorrect because while it can occasionally be involved in lateral epicondylitis, it is much less commonly affected than the ECRB.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old female patient sustains a traumatic injury to the proximal third of her tibia and receives open reduction with internal fixation using an intramedullary nail. Soft tissue reconstruction using a gastrocnemius muscle flap is being considered. Which of the following vessels serves as the primary vascular supply to this flap?
A) Anterior tibial artery
B) Peroneal artery
C) Popliteal artery
D) Posterior tibial artery
E) Sural artery
questions.answer:
E)
The sural artery is the primary blood supply to the gastrocnemius muscle flap. The medial and lateral sural arteries branch from the popliteal artery approximately 3-4 cm proximal to the fibular head and supply the respective heads of the gastrocnemius muscle at the level of the fibular head. This muscle flap can be rotated to reconstruct soft tissue defects in the anterior distal knee region, measuring 5-9 cm in width and 13-20 cm in length, while providing vascularized coverage for skin grafts and enhancing oxygen and antibiotic delivery. A) is incorrect because the anterior tibial artery does not supply the gastrocnemius muscle. B) is incorrect because the peroneal artery does not provide blood supply to the gastrocnemius. C) is incorrect because while the popliteal artery gives rise to the sural arteries, it is not the direct supply to the gastrocnemius muscle. D) is incorrect because the posterior tibial artery does not vascularize the gastrocnemius muscle.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old morbidly obese female patient presents to the burn center with second-degree burns covering 40% of her total body surface area, affecting her torso and legs. Which of the following parameters should be primarily monitored to ensure appropriate fluid resuscitation management?
A) Systolic blood pressure maintained above 90 mmHg
B) Cardiac output maintained above 5 L/min
C) Mean arterial pressure maintained above 55 mmHg
D) Heart rate maintained below 120 bpm
E) Urine production of 0.5 mL/kg/h
questions.answer:
E)
Urine production of 0.5 mL/kg/h is the most reliable indicator for guiding fluid resuscitation in burn patients. Hourly urine output serves as an established marker of adequate tissue perfusion and intravascular volume status, with the target being approximately 30-50 mL/h in adults. This parameter remains accurate even when other vital signs are unreliable due to the physiologic stress response following major burns. A is incorrect because systolic blood pressure can be misleading in burn patients due to catecholamine release that may maintain blood pressure despite significant volume depletion. B is incorrect because measuring cardiac output requires invasive monitoring that poses additional risks in morbidly obese patients and may not be necessary unless burns involve the upper body. C is incorrect because mean arterial pressure measurements can be inaccurate due to peripheral vasospasm from the hyperadrenergic state and edema formation affecting noninvasive monitoring. D is incorrect because tachycardia is nearly universal in burn patients due to pain and catecholamine release, making heart rate an unreliable indicator of volume status.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male presents for evaluation of progressive nasal enlargement. He seeks cosmetic improvement due to the psychological impact of his appearance. Physical examination reveals thickened nasal skin with enlarged glands at the tip and a bulbous configuration. Surgical debulking of the nose is being considered. Which of the following risk factors is this patient most likely to have in his medical history?
A) Chronic alcohol consumption
B) Prolonged ultraviolet light exposure
C) Psoriatic skin disease
D) Radiotherapy for adolescent acne
E) Rosacea
questions.answer:
E)
This patient presents with rhinophyma, which is characterized by progressive enlargement of sebaceous glands in the nasal region, creating a bulbous, disfiguring appearance that can cause significant psychological distress. Rhinophyma represents the advanced stage of rosacea. Management includes topical and systemic antibiotics for mild cases and underlying rosacea, while surgical debulking and laser treatments are used for severe cases. A) is incorrect because although alcohol abuse was historically thought to be linked to this condition due to the reddish facial appearance, no scientific evidence supports an association between alcohol consumption and rhinophyma development. B) is incorrect because there is no established evidence that ultraviolet exposure causes rhinophyma, though malignant lesions have occasionally been discovered incidentally within rhinophyma tissue. C) is incorrect because psoriasis has no known association with rosacea or rhinophyma. D) is incorrect because rhinophyma is not related to radiation exposure.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old female patient is having endoscopic breast augmentation through a transaxillary approach. What is the most important measure to maintain feeling in the inner portion of the arm?
A) Staying superficial and avoiding entry into axillary adipose tissue
B) Using gentle dissection techniques around the collarbone area
C) Locating and identifying sensory nerve branches in the armpit
D) Placing the implant beneath the pectoral muscle
E) Protecting the lateral pectoral nerve during surgery
questions.answer:
A)
To prevent sensory loss in the medial arm during transaxillary breast augmentation, the surgeon must maintain a subdermal plane and avoid dissecting into the axillary fat pad. The intercostobrachial and medial brachial cutaneous nerves supply sensation to the inner arm and travel superficially through the axillary fat behind the lateral edge of the pectoralis major. Entering the axillary fat risks damaging these nerves, causing numbness or abnormal sensations in the inner arm. B is incorrect because clavicular dissection does not affect medial arm sensation. C is incorrect because nerve identification requires dissecting into axillary fat, increasing injury risk. D is incorrect because implant placement (subpectoral vs subglandular) does not influence medial arm sensation. E is incorrect because the lateral pectoral nerve provides motor function to the lower pectoralis major, not sensory innervation to the medial arm.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old woman presents to the clinic expressing concern about a noticeable step-off deformity between her chest wall and the upper portion of her breast 6 months following immediate tissue expander reconstruction of her left breast. No additional adjuvant treatment was required. Following complete expansion, the tissue expander was exchanged for a permanent smooth, round silicone implant. Her current BMI is 28 kg/m2. Physical examination reveals a well-defined inframammary crease with volume symmetry to the opposite breast. Which of the following surgical interventions would be most appropriate to address this patient's contour irregularity?
A) Replacing the silicone implant with a larger volume and dimension silicone implant
B) Replacing the silicone implant with a saline implant of identical volume and dimension
C) Autologous fat transfer to the upper pole and chest wall region
D) Insertion of acellular dermal matrix as an inferolateral support
E) Implant removal and reconstruction using a deep inferior epigastric perforator flap
questions.answer:
C)
Autologous fat transfer effectively corrects acquired contour irregularities in breast reconstruction patients. A) is incorrect because increasing implant size would not resolve the step-off deformity caused by insufficient soft tissue coverage and would compromise symmetry with the contralateral breast. B) is incorrect because switching to a saline implant of the same dimensions would not address the underlying problem of inadequate superior pole soft tissue coverage. D) is incorrect because acellular dermal matrix placement as an inferolateral sling is typically performed during the initial reconstruction phase to establish the inframammary fold, which this patient already has well-defined. E) is incorrect because this patient lacks the excess abdominal tissue required for a DIEP flap reconstruction, making her an unsuitable candidate for this procedure.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old male develops hardware infection 4 weeks following spinal fusion surgery. After the neurosurgeon performs wound debridement and seeks plastic surgery consultation for defect coverage, the plastic surgeon observes in the operating room that paraspinous muscle flap coverage is not feasible due to extensive muscle debridement by the neurosurgeon. A reverse latissimus dorsi flap is selected for reconstruction. Which artery provides the common vascular supply for both of these flaps?
A) Circumflex scapular
B) Posterior intercostal
C) Superior gluteal
D) Thoracodorsal
E) Transverse cervical
questions.answer:
B)
The posterior intercostal artery provides blood supply to both the paraspinous muscle and the reverse latissimus dorsi flap, making it the shared vascular source for these reconstructive options. In midline spinal defects, these vessels typically remain intact unless compromised by extensive oncologic resections or major trauma. A) is incorrect because the circumflex scapular artery supplies scapular and parascapular flaps, not these two flaps. C) is incorrect because the superior gluteal artery supplies the gluteus maximus muscle. D) is incorrect because the thoracodorsal artery is the primary blood supply for the standard latissimus dorsi muscle, not the reverse flap or paraspinous muscle. E) is incorrect because the transverse cervical artery supplies the trapezius muscle flap.

questions.question:
A 2-year-old boy is brought to the office because of an infantile hemangioma of the right lower lip. His parents say that he frequently drools and has difficulty in phonation. On examination, the lesion measures 1 cm in width and distorts the surrounding tissues. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most definitive treatment?


A) Bleomycin
B) Oral prednisolone
C) Propranolol
D) Pulsed-dye laser therapy
E) Surgical resection
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.






The lip is a favorable area for early surgical intervention for infantile hemangiomas and vascular malformations. The amount of lip tissue that can safely be resected allows for primary closure in the majority of cases. The tumors often distort the local tissues and are ‚Äuadditive‚Äu to the amount of available tissue, so resection typically allows for safe linear closure along the vertical resting tension lines. Reconstruction of other facial areas, such as the cheek and eyelids, is usually more complicated, and nonoperative measures may be a better first line of treatment. Surgical treatment is further warranted in this case by the functional impact of the lesion.


Pulsed-dye lasers are effective treatment for thin vascular lesions. Multiple treatments are needed, they can be painful, and some residual scarring is usually left after resolution.


Intralesional bleomycin is another option for local control, though multiple treatments, often with anesthesia, are required.


Propranolol therapy has recently come to the forefront of hemangioma treatment. Oral treatment is preferred at 1 mg/kg three times daily. Dramatic responses are seen within 24 hours of starting treatment, and significant resolution occurs over a course of weeks. Contraindications may include bronchospasm, significant cardiac abnormalities, or cerebrovascular abnormalities. Pretreatment MRI and pediatric medical management may help determine suitability for treatment. Propranolol is most effective for early lesions that are in a proliferative growth phase. In this case, by 2 years, the lesion is likely done with growth and in a stable to involuting phase.


Oral prednisolone is also effective at treating hemangiomas and is a common treatment option. Hyperglycemia and cushingoid features are temporary drawbacks. Given the symptoms in this case and the relative ease of surgical resection, medical therapies such as steroids and beta blockers would be secondary choices. In asymptomatic patients with minimal disfigurement, observation alone may be the preferred first line of treatment.


References
1. Li WY, Chaudhry O, Reinisch JF. Guide to early surgical management of lip hemangiomas based on our experience of 214 cases. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2011 Nov;128(5):1117-1124.
2. Pienaar C, Graham R, Geldenhuys S, et al. Intralesional bleomycin for the treatment of hemangiomas. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2006 Jan;117(1):221-226.
3. L√©aut√©-Labr√®ze C, Dumas de la Roque E, Hubiche T, et al. Propranolol for severe hemangiomas of infancy. N Engl J Med. 2008 Jun 12;358(24):2649-2651.
4. Constantinides J, Prowse P, Gorst C, et al. Adrenal suppression following steroid treatment of infantile hemangiomas: expediting the move toward propranolol? Plast Reconstr Surg. 2012 Feb;129(2):377e-378e.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old man presents to the emergency department because of spontaneous progressive pain, swelling, cyanosis, and edema of the left lower extremity for the past 24 hours. A photograph is shown. Medical history includes prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter placement in the setting of prolonged immobilization secondary to traumatic closed head injury sustained 2 years ago. Physical examination shows no dyspnea. Oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Venous ultrasonography and CT scan show total left deep femoral thrombosis extending into the lower IVC at the indwelling filter. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Catheter-directed thrombolysis
B) Femoral vein to IVC vascular bypass
C) Isolated extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support to the affected extremity
D) Open thrombectomy
E) Oral anticoagulation
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


The patient is presenting with extensive acute thrombotic occlusion resulting in clinically evident symptomatic venous insufficiency of the extremity. If the occlusion is left untreated, progressive cyanosis and secondary ischemia followed by gangrene develop. Locally delivered thrombolytic agents via catheter-directed thrombolysis with or without percutaneous transluminal angioplasty is an effective first line of treatment in this scenario where the patient presents within a few days of symptom onset (ie, prior to clot fibrosis) and is not high-risk for bleeding. In patients who are high-risk for bleeding (eg, acute intracerebral hemorrhage, gastrointestinal bleeding), alternative methods of restoring venous outflow include clot retrieval through other percutaneous or open techniques (eg, transluminal aspiration thrombectomy, open inferior vena cava (IVC) thrombectomy with or without temporizing groin arteriovenous fistula creation).
