Systemic thrombolysis can be considered when other first line therapies are not available but has been associated with high frequency of major bleeding complications in several randomized trials (14% for streptokinase).


Systemic anticoagulation infusion helps prevent progression but does not restore acute compromised ischemic limb secondary to venous outflow obstruction. Oral anticoagulation is not indicated for acute management of a limb-threatening thrombosis. Femoral vein to IVC vascular bypass is not a described procedure for venous insufficiency. Limb-threatening thrombo-occlusive venous insufficiency resulting in a painful swollen blue leg, such as that pictured (also known as "phlegmasia cerulea dolens," literally "painful blue edema") was first described with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. It has also been associated with cancer or life-threatening critical illness. More recently, a growing population of patients are at risk due to unretrieved IVC filters. While IVC filter placement may protect the pulmonary vascular bed, it does not lessen thrombotic predisposition or incidence in the lower extremities, and IVC thrombosis with or without phlegmasia cerulea dolens has been reported to occur in 3 to 30% of patients following IVC filter placement. Filter retrieval following its initial indicated need can lessen secondary thrombotic complications, but data suggest that only a fraction of retrievable filters are later removed. In a systemic review, overall retrieval was 34% with a high percentage of nonretrieval occurring for a variety of reasons, including loss to follow up (particularly in trauma centers), limited life expectancy, and/or unresolved underlying conditions.


ReferencesAlkhouli M, Morad M, Narins CR, Raza F, Bashir R. Inferior vena cava thrombosis. JACC Cardiovasc Interv. 2016;9(7):629-643. Angel LF, Tapson V, Galgon RE, et al. Systematic review of the use of retrievable inferior vena cava filters. J Vasc Interv Radiol. 2011; 22:1522.Fedullo PF, Roberts A. Placement of vena cava filters and their complications. UpToDate website. https://www.uptodate.com/contents/placement-of-vena-cava-filters-and-their-complications. Updated October 5, 2017. Accessed January 8, 2019.Heilman J. Phlegmasia cerulea dolens. In: WikiMedia website. https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=49299938. Created June 7, 2016. Accessed January 8, 2019. Courtesy J Heilman.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient visits the clinic seeking advice about his hair loss issues. He mentions that an acquaintance had a hair restoration surgery that appears artificial, particularly along the anterior hairline. When employing the minigraft and micrograft technique, what is the appropriate number of follicles that should be included in a minigraft?
A) 1 to 2
B) 3 to 4
C) 5 to 6
D) 7 to 8
E) 9 to 10
questions.answer:
B)
Minigrafts contain 3 to 4 follicular units and are typically utilized alongside micrografts that hold 1 to 2 follicular units. This combination helps achieve natural-looking results in hair restoration procedures. A) is incorrect because 1 to 2 follicular units define micrografts, not minigrafts. C) is incorrect because 5 to 6 follicular units exceed the standard minigraft size and may contribute to unnatural appearance. D) is incorrect because 7 to 8 follicular units are too large for minigrafts and increase the risk of artificial-looking outcomes. E) is incorrect because 9 to 10 follicular units represent excessive graft size that commonly results in the undesirable "plug look" appearance.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old unconscious and intoxicated female patient arrives at the emergency department following a motor vehicle collision. She has sustained multiple trauma, including a right thigh laceration measuring 12 × 18 cm with visible fat and muscle tissue. The wound contains debris and dirt particles. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics
B) Tetanus toxoid immunization
C) Application of negative pressure wound therapy
D) Placement of split-thickness skin graft
E) Surgical irrigation and tissue debridement
questions.answer:
B)
Tetanus immunization is the most appropriate initial step for this patient with a contaminated wound. Tetanus, also called lockjaw, results from prolonged skeletal muscle contractions caused by tetanospasmin, a neurotoxin from Clostridium tetani, an anaerobic gram-positive bacterium. Contaminated wounds, particularly those with dirt and debris, create ideal conditions for tetanus infection. A) is incorrect because prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics have not proven effective in reducing wound infection rates and may promote antibiotic-resistant organisms. C) is incorrect because negative pressure therapy is a temporary measure and would not be appropriate as initial management for such a large contaminated wound. D) is incorrect because skin grafting cannot be performed until the wound bed is clean and viable after proper debridement. E) is incorrect as the immediate priority, though debridement will be necessary after tetanus prophylaxis is administered.

questions.question:
A 3-month-old male infant presents to the clinic with his parents due to concerns about head shape irregularity that has progressively worsened since delivery. The birth history reveals a difficult labor requiring surgical delivery via cesarean section. On physical examination, there is notable flattening of the right posterior skull region accompanied by prominence of the right forehead on the same side. When viewed from above, the right ear appears positioned 1 cm further forward compared to the left ear, and the anterior fontanelle remains open without evidence of increased pressure. The infant demonstrates rightward head positioning with limited ability to turn left. The left cervical region feels more tense and restricted than the right side. What represents the most suitable first-line treatment approach for this patient?
A) Assessment for cerebral palsy
B) Physical therapy targeting cervical muscles
C) Surgical expansion of posterior skull vault
D) Custom-fitted repositioning helmet treatment
E) Surgical division of sternocleidomastoid muscle
questions.answer:
B)
This infant exhibits the characteristic features of positional plagiocephaly, showing posterior skull flattening with compensatory forehead prominence and ear displacement on the affected side. The head positioning preference and restricted neck movement indicate concurrent torticollis. The primary treatment approach should focus on addressing the underlying neck muscle imbalance through targeted physical therapy and stretching exercises to restore normal cervical function and muscle balance. A) is incorrect because there are no neurological signs suggesting cerebral palsy in this case. C) is incorrect as surgical intervention is not indicated for positional deformities that can be managed conservatively. D) is incorrect because helmet therapy should not be the initial approach when torticollis is present and conservative measures have not been attempted first. E) is incorrect as surgical muscle release is reserved for severe cases that fail conservative management and is not appropriate as initial treatment.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old female presents to the clinic seeking consultation for surgical treatment of tuberous breast anomaly. During physical assessment, which of the following findings would most likely be observed in this patient?
A) Missing sternal portion of the pectoralis major muscle
B) Loss of definition of the inframammary crease
C) Severe grade III drooping of the nipple-areolar region
D) Protrusion of mammary tissue through the nipple-areolar area
E) Enlarged breast size
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is D because tuberous breast deformity characteristically presents with herniation or protrusion of breast tissue through the nipple-areolar complex, creating a distinctive appearance. A is incorrect because absence of the sternal head of the pectoralis major muscle is a hallmark feature of Poland syndrome, not tuberous breast deformity. B is incorrect because tuberous breasts typically show a constricted or tight inframammary fold rather than an effaced one. C is incorrect because severe nipple-areolar ptosis is not a defining characteristic of tuberous breast deformity. E is incorrect because tuberous breasts are not associated with macromastia or excessive breast enlargement.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male patient requires surgical intervention for a large subtotal squamous cell carcinoma located in the posterior larynx. His medical history reveals prior chemoradiation therapy followed by bilateral selective neck dissections for residual disease 9 months previously. An anterolateral thigh free flap has been selected for reconstruction, however the surgical records indicate that both external carotid arterial systems were removed. Which recipient vessel would be most suitable for this patient?
A) Facial
B) Internal mammary
C) Occipital
D) Subclavian
E) Transverse cervical
questions.answer:
E)
The transverse cervical vessels represent the optimal recipient choice in this scenario. In head and neck microsurgical reconstruction, comprehensive knowledge of regional vascular anatomy is essential. With the increasing use of chemotherapy protocols for laryngopharyngeal malignancies, surgical salvage cases have become more frequent, presenting elevated complication risks including fistula formation, stenosis, and carotid artery damage. This case illustrates the growing challenge of the "vessel-depleted neck" following extensive prior treatment. The facial artery is incorrect because it originates from the external carotid system which was previously sacrificed. The occipital artery is also incorrect as it too is a branch of the external carotid system and would be unavailable. The subclavian artery is incorrect due to its large caliber, challenging anatomical location, and significant potential complications during surgical exposure. The internal mammary system is incorrect because while technically feasible, it requires extensive dissection through intercostal spaces, carries substantial morbidity, and often necessitates vein grafts for adequate length. The transverse cervical vessels are typically preserved even during radical neck dissections as they commonly serve as the inferior surgical margin, making them reliable recipient vessels in previously treated patients.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female patient is planning to have an elective cosmetic surgery at an outpatient surgical facility. She expresses worry about mortality risk during her operation. Which of the following procedures performed at an outpatient surgical center would place this patient at the greatest postoperative risk of death due to pulmonary embolism?
A) Tummy tuck
B) Breast augmentation
C) Nose reshaping surgery
D) Facelift
E) Liposuction
questions.answer:
A)
Tummy tuck carries the highest risk of postoperative death from pulmonary embolism among cosmetic procedures performed in outpatient surgical centers. Data from the American Association for Accreditation of Ambulatory Surgery Facilities shows that of 13 pulmonary embolism deaths between 2001-2006, 12 were associated with abdominoplasty procedures either alone or combined with other operations. B) is incorrect because breast augmentation has a much lower association with fatal pulmonary embolism. C) is incorrect because rhinoplasty involves minimal tissue manipulation and shorter operative times, reducing thromboembolism risk. D) is incorrect because facelift procedures have significantly lower rates of pulmonary embolism-related mortality. E) is incorrect because while liposuction can cause complications, it is not as strongly associated with fatal pulmonary embolism as abdominoplasty.

questions.question:
A 74-year-old male patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus is diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the mandible. His medical history includes bilateral distal fibular fractures from a motor vehicle accident 10 years prior, which required open reduction and internal fixation. The patient emphasizes that maintaining his ability to eat and chew is a priority. Which of the following statements about mandibular reconstruction options is accurate?
A) Scapular flap bone quality exceeds that of iliac crest flaps
B) Implant-based dental restoration is more reliable with osteocutaneous radial forearm flaps compared to iliac crest flaps
C) Fibular free flaps result in greater donor site complications than iliac crest flaps
D) Previous distal fibular fractures do not represent an absolute contraindication for free fibular flap use
E) Iliac crest bone flaps demonstrate lower complication rates than osteocutaneous radial forearm flaps
questions.answer:
D)
Previous fibular fractures do not constitute an absolute contraindication for utilizing free fibular flaps in mandibular reconstruction. The literature demonstrates that fibular flaps can still be successfully harvested even after previous fracture repair. A) is incorrect because scapular flaps actually provide inferior bone quality compared to both fibular and iliac crest flaps. B) is incorrect because dental implant placement is actually less predictable and less frequently performed in radial forearm bone flap reconstructions compared to iliac crest flaps. C) is incorrect because fibular flaps actually have more reported donor site morbidities than iliac crest flaps, not fewer. E) is incorrect because systematic reviews show that iliac crest flaps actually have higher failure rates compared to other reconstruction methods, including radial forearm flaps.

questions.question:
The main vascular supply to a free anterolateral thigh fasciocutaneous flap originates from vessels that pierce through which of the following muscles?
A) Gluteus maximus
B) Rectus femoris
C) Sartorius
D) Tensor fascia lata
E) Vastus lateralis
questions.answer:
E)
The anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap represents one of the most adaptable free tissue transfers in reconstructive procedures. The flap relies on perforating vessels from the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery that pass through the vastus lateralis muscle in approximately 80% of cases, or through the intermuscular septum between the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis in 18-20% of cases. This flap can be designed up to 10 cm in width and 25 cm in length. When no major perforator is found during exploration, the flap can be sustained by multiple smaller perforators along with the vastus lateralis muscle. A) Gluteus maximus is incorrect because its blood supply comes from the superior and inferior gluteal arteries, not the lateral circumflex femoral system. B) Rectus femoris is incorrect because while it receives supply from the lateral circumflex femoral artery's descending branch, the perforators for the ALT flap pass through the vastus lateralis, not the rectus femoris itself. C) Sartorius is incorrect because it has segmental vascular supply and is not the muscle through which ALT flap perforators traverse. D) Tensor fascia lata is incorrect because it is supplied by the ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery, not the descending branch that provides the ALT flap perforators.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female presents for evaluation of a progressively growing mass on the right side of her face over the past 2 years. Physical examination reveals an approximately 4-cm indurated lesion in the right parotid area and an enlarged lymph node in the ipsilateral neck zone III. Cross-sectional imaging excludes distant metastatic spread. Fine-needle biopsy of the lesion indicates high-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma originating from the parotid gland. What is the optimal therapeutic approach for this patient?
A) Primary chemoradiotherapy followed by evaluation of treatment response prior to further intervention
B) Partial parotidectomy combined with same-side neck lymph node removal
C) Partial parotidectomy combined with same-side neck lymph node removal followed by postoperative radiation therapy
D) Complete parotidectomy combined with same-side neck lymph node removal
E) Complete parotidectomy combined with same-side neck lymph node removal followed by postoperative radiation therapy
questions.answer:
E)
This patient presents with T2N1M0 (Stage II) high-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma, requiring complete parotidectomy with ipsilateral neck dissection as the standard surgical approach. Given the presence of lymph node involvement, both ipsilateral cervical lymphadenectomy and postoperative adjuvant radiation are necessary components of treatment. The combination of nodal positivity and high tumor grade mandates adjuvant radiotherapy to optimize local-regional control. A) is incorrect because neoadjuvant chemoradiation is not standard care for resectable parotid malignancies and chemotherapy remains controversial in mucoepidermoid carcinoma treatment. B) is incorrect because partial parotidectomy is inadequate for high-grade lesions and omits necessary adjuvant radiation. C) is incorrect because partial parotidectomy provides insufficient surgical margins for high-grade tumors. D) is incorrect because it omits postoperative radiotherapy, which is essential given the high-grade histology and nodal involvement.

questions.question:
An 89-year-old male patient has a 5 x 5-cm ulcerated squamous cell carcinoma of the skin confirmed by biopsy, located on the right ear pinna. Physical examination reveals no palpable lymphadenopathy. Radiation therapy is being considered for treatment. What is the most important factor for predicting local control rates with radiation therapy in this case?
A) Patient's age
B) Tumor histologic type
C) Anatomical location of the lesion
D) Ulcerative characteristics
E) Tumor dimensions
questions.answer:
E)
Tumor size is the primary determinant of local control rates for radiation therapy in squamous cell carcinoma. According to NCCN guidelines, local control rates decrease significantly with increasing tumor size: lesions <1 cm achieve 91% control, 1-5 cm lesions achieve 76% control, and lesions >5 cm achieve only 56% control. A) Patient age is incorrect because it is a secondary predictor that does not primarily determine local control rates. B) Tumor histology is incorrect as it is also a secondary factor compared to size in predicting radiation therapy outcomes. C) Anatomical location is incorrect because while ear involvement increases metastatic risk, size remains the primary predictor of local control. D) Ulcerative characteristics are incorrect as ulceration is a secondary predictor rather than the primary determinant of local control rates.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female patient presents for surgical repair of a nasal bridge deformity resulting from childhood nasal injury. The treatment plan involves using autologous costal cartilage grafts to reconstruct the dorsal contour. What complication is most commonly associated with this procedure?
A) Graft extrusion
B) Tissue necrosis
C) Cartilage ossification
D) Graft resorption
E) Shape distortion
questions.answer:
E)
Shape distortion (warping) represents the most frequent complication when using cartilage grafts for nasal reconstruction. This occurs due to the natural tendency of cartilage to change configuration over time, particularly when perichondrium is present or when the cartilage matrix has non-uniform composition. The perichondrial layer can cause significant curling and unpredictable shape changes, making proper harvesting technique crucial for maintaining graft stability. A) Graft extrusion is uncommon with autologous cartilage due to excellent biocompatibility. B) Tissue necrosis rarely occurs with fresh autologous grafts as they have reliable blood supply integration. C) Cartilage ossification is not a typical complication of nasal cartilage grafting procedures. D) Graft resorption is minimal with autologous cartilage grafts, which maintain their volume well over time.

questions.question:
A 51-year-old female patient is preparing for a surgical reduction of her lower lip. A mental nerve block is intended to provide local anesthesia. Where should the mental foramen block be administered in the oral mucosa in relation to the teeth?
A) Canine
B) Central incisor
C) Lateral incisor
D) Second premolar
E) Second molar
questions.answer:
D)
The mental foramen is anatomically positioned adjacent to the second premolar or first molar tooth along the mandibular border, making this the optimal injection site for mental nerve anesthesia to achieve lower lip numbness. A is incorrect because the canine is located too far forward (mesial) from the mental foramen. B is incorrect because the central incisor is positioned too mesially for effective mental nerve blockade. C is incorrect because the lateral incisor is also too far mesial to the mental foramen location. E is incorrect because the second molar is positioned too far back (distal) from the mental foramen.

questions.question:
What is the approximate probability that a patient presenting with a frontal sinus fracture will also have an associated intracranial injury?
A) 1%
B) 15%
C) 30%
D) 55%
E) 90%
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is D (55%). Frontal sinus fractures require extremely high impact forces (800-1600 lbs) to occur, and due to their location high on the craniofacial skeleton, these forces are efficiently transmitted to intracranial structures. Studies demonstrate that frontal sinus fractures carry a 45-65% risk of concurrent intracranial injury, making 55% the most accurate estimate. A) 1% is incorrect because it vastly underestimates the risk associated with high-energy frontal bone trauma. B) 15% is incorrect as it represents a low probability that doesn't reflect the significant force required to fracture the frontal bone. C) 30% is incorrect because it falls below the established range of 45-65% for frontal sinus fracture-associated brain injuries. E) 90% is incorrect as it overestimates the risk, exceeding the documented prevalence range for this injury pattern.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient is planned for functional septorhinoplasty to address nasal breathing difficulties. For this patient, what is the most probable impact of perioperative corticosteroid use on swelling and bruising?

  Swelling   Bruising
A) Reduced   Reduced
B) Reduced   Unchanged
C) Enhanced   Enhanced
D) Unchanged   Reduced
E) Unchanged   Unchanged
questions.answer:
A)

Perioperative corticosteroid administration significantly reduces both postoperative swelling and bruising following rhinoplasty procedures. Multiple prospective randomized controlled trials and meta-analysis have demonstrated that steroids effectively minimize both upper and lower eyelid edema and ecchymosis at 1 day and 7 days postoperatively. The anti-inflammatory properties of corticosteroids help control the inflammatory response that leads to tissue swelling and vascular leakage causing bruising. B) is incorrect because steroids do reduce bruising, not just swelling. C) is incorrect because steroids have anti-inflammatory effects that decrease rather than increase these complications. D) is incorrect because steroids reduce swelling in addition to bruising. E) is incorrect because evidence clearly shows steroids have beneficial effects on both parameters.

questions.question:
For patients with breast ptosis, what benefit does simultaneous augmentation mammoplasty with mastopexy offer over mastopexy performed alone?
A) Greater predictability of aesthetic results
B) Reduced complication rates
C) Lower revision rates
D) Enhanced upper pole fullness
E) Reduced surgical costs
questions.answer:
D)
The benefit of concurrent implant placement is the enhanced upper pole fullness that mastopexy alone cannot provide. A is incorrect because aesthetic outcomes are actually less predictable with the combined one-stage procedure compared to mastopexy alone. B is incorrect because complication rates are higher, not lower, with the simultaneous approach. C is incorrect because revision rates are increased with the combined procedure. E is incorrect because operative costs are higher due to longer surgical time and implant expenses.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old male presents for evaluation of a 2-cm lesion located on the anterior floor of his mouth. Physical examination reveals no palpable cervical lymphadenopathy. Besides excision of the primary tumor, what is the most appropriate next management step?
A) Radiotherapy alone
B) Comprehensive neck dissection
C) Comprehensive neck dissection with radiotherapy
D) Limited neck dissection
E) Watchful waiting
questions.answer:
D)
For a 2-cm oral cavity tumor with clinically negative neck examination (pT2cN0), a supraomohyoid neck dissection is indicated due to the significant risk of microscopic nodal metastases in the regional drainage areas. This procedure addresses lymph node levels I, II, and III where occult disease is most likely to occur. A) Radiotherapy alone is insufficient as it doesn't provide pathologic staging of the neck or adequate local control for this tumor size. B) Comprehensive neck dissection is unnecessarily extensive for a clinically node-negative neck and carries higher morbidity. C) Adding radiotherapy to comprehensive neck dissection represents overtreatment for N0 disease. E) Observation alone is inappropriate given the substantial risk of occult cervical metastases with a T2 floor of mouth primary tumor.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female presents for evaluation of breast asymmetry that occurs during physical exercise. Her past medical history is significant for bilateral breast augmentation with silicone gel implants performed 10 years prior. She has recently started an intensive fitness program involving marathon training and resistance exercises. Her primary cosmetic complaint is that her breast implants create an unnatural appearance when she performs weightlifting movements. What is the most appropriate treatment approach for this patient?
A) Exchange current implants for higher cohesivity silicone gel implants
B) Replace existing implants with saline-filled implants
C) Relocate the implants from subpectoral to subglandular position
D) Move the implants from subglandular to subpectoral position
E) Perform complete capsulectomy with placement of new silicone implants
questions.answer:
C)
The optimal treatment involves relocating the implants from the subpectoral position to the subglandular plane. This addresses the animation deformity caused by repeated pectoralis major muscle contractions during weightlifting exercises. Moving the implants superficial to the muscle eliminates the distortion that occurs when the pectoralis contracts, while compression of the previous subpectoral pocket prevents implant migration back to the original location. A) is incorrect because using more cohesive gel implants may reduce rippling but does not eliminate muscle-induced animation deformity. B) is incorrect because switching to saline implants will not resolve the fundamental problem of muscle contraction affecting implant position. D) is incorrect because this patient's implants are already in the subpectoral plane, which is causing the animation deformity. E) is incorrect because capsulectomy addresses capsular contracture but does not solve the animation deformity caused by pectoralis muscle activation.

questions.question:
A 10-month-old boy underwent cranial vault reconstruction for sagittal craniosynostosis. The infant has no additional medical conditions. Two days after surgery, his serum sodium level drops from 140 to 129 mEq/L. Lab results reveal decreased plasma aldosterone levels. Cerebral salt wasting (CSW) is the presumed diagnosis. Which of the following findings would most strongly confirm this diagnosis?
A) Elevated plasma antidiuretic hormone levels
B) Increased plasma sodium levels
C) Expanded plasma volume
D) Elevated serum uric acid levels
E) Increased urine production
questions.answer:
E)
Cerebral salt wasting involves excessive renal sodium and fluid losses following brain injury, resulting in negative sodium balance and volume depletion. The condition is characterized by increased urine output as the kidneys inappropriately waste sodium and water. This increased urinary losses help distinguish CSW from SIADH. A) is incorrect because elevated ADH is characteristic of SIADH, not CSW. B) is incorrect because plasma sodium would be decreased, not increased, in CSW. C) is incorrect because CSW causes volume contraction, not expansion. D) is incorrect because serum uric acid is typically low in CSW due to increased renal clearance from volume depletion.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old manual worker reports thumb-side wrist pain and inflammation during work activities. Conservative management including bracing, lifestyle changes, and anti-inflammatory medications over 6 months has not provided symptom relief. Radiographic imaging of the wrist is provided. What is the most suitable surgical procedure for lasting reconstruction in this case?
A) Scaphocapitate fusion
B) Four-corner fusion with scaphoid removal
C) Open scaphoid fracture repair with internal fixation
D) Scapholunate ligament repair
E) Scaphotrapeziotrapezoid joint fusion
questions.answer:
B)
This case demonstrates scaphoid nonunion advanced collapse (SNAC) arthritis. The degenerative pattern mirrors scapholunate advanced collapse (SLAC) arthritis. Four-corner arthrodesis involving the capitate, lunate, triquetrum, and hamate bones with scaphoid excision represents the optimal treatment for this condition, providing reliable pain relief and functional improvement while preserving wrist motion. A) is incorrect because scaphocapitate fusion is used for advanced Kienböck disease and would not address the radioscaphoid arthritis present in SNAC. C) is incorrect because the chronic nonunion has progressed to advanced arthritis, making fracture repair no longer viable. D) is incorrect because the arthritis results from chronic scaphoid nonunion rather than primary scapholunate ligament injury, making ligament reconstruction ineffective. E) is incorrect because the primary pathology involves the radiocarpal joint rather than the scaphotrapeziotrapezoid joint, so STT fusion would not address the main source of symptoms.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old transfeminine patient presents for consultation regarding breast augmentation as part of gender-affirming surgery. She has been on estrogen therapy for 2 years but reports minimal breast development (Tanner stage II). Which of the following is the MOST appropriate next step in the surgical management of her chest feminization?

A) Recommend waiting an additional year for possible spontaneous breast growth before considering augmentation
B) Advise direct placement of large-volume implants to achieve desired size in a single stage
C) Recommend staged tissue expander placement prior to final implant placement
D) Suggest reduction mammaplasty to improve chest contour
E) Perform subglandular fat grafting only without implants
questions.answer:
C)

Option C is correct because transfeminine patients with minimal native breast tissue after sufficient hormone therapy may have tight chest skin envelopes, making single-stage large-volume implant placement unsafe due to risk of complications (e.g., implant malposition, wound dehiscence). Staged tissue expander placement allows for gradual skin expansion and safer definitive augmentation.

Option A is incorrect because after 2 years of hormone therapy, further significant breast growth is unlikely; waiting longer will not provide clinical benefit.

Option B is incorrect as direct placement of large implants in tight tissues increases surgical risks and does not allow proper expansion or aesthetic results.

Option D is incorrect because reduction mammaplasty is not indicated; this patient desires breast enlargement, not reduction.

Option E is incorrect since subglandular fat grafting alone typically does not provide sufficient volume or projection for chest feminization in patients with minimal native tissue.

questions.question:
A plastic surgery consultation is sought for a 7-year-old female patient due to chemotherapy drug extravasation into the dorsal aspect of her forearm. Clinical findings include tissue firmness, forearm edema, and discomfort during passive wrist flexion. What represents the most suitable first-line management approach?
A) Providing a specific antidote medication
B) Performing Doppler ultrasound of the forearm
C) Conducting liposuction with saline irrigation of the involved region
D) Obtaining compartment pressure measurements
E) Performing surgical debridement with skin grafting
questions.answer:
D)

Measuring compartment pressures is the most appropriate initial step because extravasation injuries can lead to compartment syndrome, which must be promptly identified through clinical evaluation or direct pressure monitoring to prevent permanent tissue damage including skin, muscle, tendon, nerve, and vascular structures. A) is incorrect because antidote administration is not the primary initial concern when compartment syndrome is suspected. B) is incorrect because Doppler sonography does not assess for compartment syndrome, which is the immediate threat requiring evaluation. C) is incorrect because liposuction and irrigation are treatment options that come after ruling out compartment syndrome, not initial diagnostic measures. E) is incorrect because surgical excision and grafting are definitive treatments performed after initial assessment and stabilization, not as the first management step.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old male presents to the clinic seeking advice regarding reconstruction after removal of a squamous cell carcinoma from the right mandibular angle and oral floor. The procedure involved resection of the right hemimandible and right cervical lymph node dissection. Which of the following represents the most suitable reconstructive approach?
A) Osteocutaneous fibular flap
B) Osteocutaneous radial forearm flap
C) Osteocutaneous scapular flap
D) Rectus abdominis flap with titanium reconstruction plate
questions.answer:
A)
The osteocutaneous fibular flap is the optimal choice for this extensive mandibular reconstruction. This flap provides excellent bone length and quality for hemimandibular reconstruction, with reliable vascular anatomy that allows for straightforward microvascular anastomosis to ipsilateral recipient vessels in the neck. B) is incorrect because the radial forearm flap offers insufficient bone length for such an extensive mandibular defect. C) is incorrect because the scapular flap lacks adequate bone stock for this large reconstruction requirement. D) is incorrect because soft tissue flaps with reconstruction plates have high failure rates due to plate exposure, particularly following post-operative radiation therapy.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old man comes to the office because of facial asymmetry and pain in the left mid face. He says that he first started noticing the asymmetry at 14 years of age. The pain began 3 years ago. Physical examination shows atrophy of the temporal and mid facial soft tissue and bone. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?


A) Bell palsy
B) Hemifacial microsomia
C) Parry-Romberg syndrome
D) Torticollis
E) Treacher Collins syndrome
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Acquired facial asymmetry, as demonstrated in the photograph, is known as Parry-Romberg syndrome, or hemifacial atrophy. It involves both skeletal and soft tissue, and it is characterized by slow atrophy of the tissues of half of the face. It typically appears between the ages of 5 and 15 years, and it can be associated with neurologic symptoms such as seizures and trigeminal neuralgia. Facial atrophy usually begins in the temporal and/or nasolabial fold region and progresses to involve the mouth, the area around the eye, and the brow. Many patients go on to develop atrophy of half of the upper lip and tongue and exposure or damage to the roots of teeth on the affected side. The skin overlying the affected areas may become hyperpigmented. The atrophy may progress slowly and plateau, or it may progress indefinitely. The etiology of Parry-Romberg syndrome is unknown and occurs sporadically.


Bell palsy is a mononeuropathy involving cranial nerve VII and the facial nerve; it results in unilateral facial nerve paralysis. It is not usually self-limiting but may result in residual weakness in rare cases.


Hemifacial microsomia is a congenital anomaly involving an underdevelopment of either one or both sides of the face. It more commonly affects the lower half of the face, resulting in mandibular hypoplasia, microtia, and vestigial remnants. Hemifacial microsomia is the second most common facial congenital difference, after cleft lip and palate.


Torticollis involves tightness of the sternocleidomastoid muscle of the neck resulting in a head tilt toward the affected muscle. Patients may have a mild underdevelopment of the lower half of the face on the affected side secondary to deformational pressure. Torticollis is generally congenital, thought to be secondary to intrauterine positioning, and is treated with physical therapy.


References
Terenzi V, Leonardi A, Covelli E, et al. Parry-Romberg syndrome. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2005 Oct;116(5):97e-102e.
Buonaccorsi S, Leonardi A, Covelli E, et al. Parry-Romberg syndrome. J Craniofac Surg. 2005 Nov;16(6):1132-1135.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old female patient comes to the clinic with a 2-year history of increasing breast asymmetry and a palpable lesion in her right breast. Radiological examination shows a well-defined, multilobulated mass containing internal calcifications. Core biopsy results confirm a phyllodes tumor diagnosis. What is the most suitable next management approach?
A) Watchful waiting
B) Breast-conserving surgery
C) Complete breast removal
D) Systemic chemotherapy
E) External beam radiation
questions.answer:
C)
Complete breast removal is the most suitable management for phyllodes tumors, particularly for large or high-grade lesions. These neoplasms have a significant tendency for local recurrence and are resistant to both chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Complete surgical removal with negative margins is essential given their aggressive behavior. A) Watchful waiting is incorrect because phyllodes tumors require active surgical intervention due to their growth potential and recurrence risk. B) Breast-conserving surgery is incorrect as it may not achieve adequate margins for these tumors that tend to recur locally. D) Systemic chemotherapy is incorrect because phyllodes tumors are not chemosensitive. E) External beam radiation is incorrect as these tumors do not respond well to radiation therapy.

questions.question:
Among pediatric patients, which mandibular fracture configuration is most likely to cause subsequent growth disturbances?
A) Displaced bilateral parasymphyseal fractures
B) Displaced mandibular body fractures
C) Nondisplaced bilateral condylar fractures
D) Nondisplaced bilateral parasymphyseal fractures
E) Nondisplaced mandibular symphyseal fractures
questions.answer:
C)
Nondisplaced bilateral condylar fractures are most likely to cause future growth complications because the mandibular growth centers are primarily located in the condylar regions, and even nondisplaced fractures in this area can disrupt the growth potential of these critical anatomical structures. A) is incorrect because parasymphyseal fractures, even when displaced bilaterally, do not directly involve the primary growth centers. B) is incorrect because mandibular body fractures do not affect the condylar growth centers where mandibular development occurs. D) is incorrect because nondisplaced parasymphyseal fractures are away from the condylar growth centers and less likely to impact future growth. E) is incorrect because symphyseal fractures do not involve the posterior condylar regions where the main growth centers are located.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old woman undergoes a facelift. Postoperatively, she develops a hematoma that requires evacuation. Which of the following factors is most likely to contribute to hematoma formation after facial surgery?
A) Use of local anesthetic with epinephrine
B) Intraoperative blood loss
C) Use of anticoagulants
D) Surgical technique employed
E) Duration of the procedure
questions.answer:
C)
The use of anticoagulants is a significant risk factor for hematoma formation after facial surgery. Anticoagulants can increase the risk of bleeding during and after surgery, leading to hematoma development. While other factors can also contribute, anticoagulant use is particularly impactful.

questions.question:
A healthy 20-year-old male presents to the emergency department following thermal injuries to his right forearm and upper arm sustained during an attempt to ignite a backyard barbecue. Physical examination of the injured limb reveals erythematous, vesicular, painful regions alongside areas that appear white and lack sensation upon touch. The thermal injuries are not circumferential. The patient demonstrates comfortable respirations with oxygen saturation of 99% on ambient air. Transfer to a specialized burn facility should be recommended based on which of the following factors?
A) Patient's age
B) Depth of thermal injury
C) Anatomical location of burns
D) Mechanism of injury
E) Percentage of total body surface area affected
questions.answer:
B)
The severity of this patient's thermal injuries, specifically the presence of full-thickness burns (characterized by white appearance and absence of pain sensation), meets the criteria for transfer to a specialized burn center. The affected arm accounts for approximately 9% of total body surface area in this patient. Given his young age and good health status, age alone does not justify transfer. The burns do not affect critical anatomical regions such as face, hands, feet, or genital/perineal areas. Additionally, since this was not an electrical or chemical injury and occurred outdoors, inhalation injury is improbable. A is incorrect because the patient's young age and healthy status do not meet transfer criteria. C is incorrect because the burns do not involve critical areas like face, hands, feet, or genitals. D is incorrect because thermal burns from grilling do not constitute a high-risk mechanism requiring transfer. E is incorrect because 9% body surface area alone, without other factors, does not mandate transfer to a burn center.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic seeking breast augmentation surgery. She measures 5 ft 4 in (163 cm) tall and weighs 120 lb (54 kg). Clinical examination reveals underdeveloped breast tissue. She presently uses a 34B bra size and desires to achieve a C cup size. What is the most suitable choice for breast enlargement?
A) Fat grafting using patient's own tissue
B) External breast expansion device (BRAVA)
C) Saline-filled implants
D) Cohesive gel implants with smooth surface
E) Cohesive gel implants with textured surface
questions.answer:
C)
Saline-filled implants are the most appropriate choice for this patient. FDA regulations require patients to be at least 22 years old to receive silicone gel breast implants, making saline the only viable implant option for this 20-year-old patient. Saline implants provide reliable volume enhancement and have a well-established safety profile, with rupture easily detectable as the saline is harmlessly absorbed by the body. A) Fat grafting is incorrect because this thin patient lacks sufficient donor fat to achieve the desired cup size increase. B) The BRAVA system is incorrect as it provides only minimal volume enhancement, insufficient to reach her goal of C cup size. D) Smooth gel implants are incorrect due to the patient's age being below the FDA requirement of 22 years for silicone gel devices. E) Textured gel implants are incorrect for the same age restriction as smooth gel implants.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with discomfort at the base of her right thumb. Which radiographic view is most suitable for demonstrating subluxation of the thumb's basal joint?
A) Bett view
B) Brewerton view
C) Eaton stress view
D) Roberts view
E) Standard lateral view of the thumb
questions.answer:
C)
The Eaton stress view is the optimal radiographic technique for assessing basal joint subluxation. This posteroanterior projection is performed with the radial aspects of both thumb distal phalanges pressed together, creating stress that reveals laxity of the trapeziometacarpal joint by demonstrating subluxation of the thumb metacarpal relative to the trapezium. A) The Bett view is incorrect because it provides a true lateral perspective of the trapeziometacarpal joint and is primarily used for evaluating metacarpal base fractures like Bennett fractures, not subluxation. B) The Brewerton view is incorrect because it focuses on the metacarpal heads with fingers positioned flat and metacarpophalangeal joints flexed at 65 degrees, making it useful for detecting degenerative changes or occult fractures rather than joint subluxation. D) The Roberts view is incorrect because although it can show trapeziometacarpal joint degeneration through hyperprotonation positioning, it does not demonstrate subluxation as effectively as the stress view. E) The standard lateral thumb view is incorrect because it does not provide the stress component necessary to reveal joint laxity and subluxation.

questions.question:
A 41-year-old woman undergoes mastectomy for breast cancer and wishes to have immediate reconstruction. She has a BMI of 33, past medical history of poorly controlled diabetes, and is an active smoker. Which reconstruction option carries the lowest postoperative complication risk for her?

A) Immediate microvascular free TRAM flap reconstruction
B) Delayed autologous latissimus dorsi flap with implant
C) Immediate prepectoral tissue expander placement with ADM
D) Immediate subpectoral direct-to-implant reconstruction
E) Immediate pedicled transverse rectus abdominis musculocutaneous (TRAM) flap reconstruction
questions.answer:
C)

In a patient with obesity, poorly controlled diabetes, and active smoking, autologous reconstruction carries significant risks of wound healing complications, infection, and flap loss—especially microvascular free and pedicled TRAM flaps (Options A and E). The latissimus dorsi flap with implant (Option B) still involves donor-site morbidity and is not ideal in this comorbidity profile. Immediate subpectoral direct-to-implant (Option D) has higher complication rates compared to a staged approach. Prepectoral tissue expander with ADM (Option C) offers the lowest surgical risk, is less invasive, and allows time for patient optimization prior to definitive reconstructive steps. Using ADM supports soft tissue coverage and expansion in a controlled way, minimizing complication risk.

questions.question:
A 6-year-old male child comes to the clinic with a non-tender, gradually growing mass on the left frontal region. Computed tomography shows a clearly defined, expanding, low-density lesion with ground-glass characteristics affecting the skull and orbital area, resulting in slight eye protrusion. The patient has no hormonal disorders or additional bone abnormalities. What is the best treatment approach for this condition?
A) Watchful waiting with follow-up scans
B) Complete surgical removal with immediate repair
C) Scraping procedure with bone transplantation
D) Radiotherapy treatment
E) Anticancer drug therapy
questions.answer:
B)

This clinical picture is characteristic of craniofacial fibrous dysplasia. When there is cosmetic deformity, eye displacement, or potential for functional impairment, complete surgical excision with immediate reconstructive repair is the treatment of choice. A) is incorrect because watchful waiting is only appropriate for asymptomatic lesions without progression. C) is incorrect because scraping procedures have high rates of lesion recurrence. D) is incorrect because radiation treatment can lead to malignant transformation and is therefore not recommended. E) is incorrect because chemotherapy has no efficacy against this benign, slow-growing fibrous condition.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female presents with invasive carcinoma of the right breast. What is the most accurate estimate of the probability that this patient's malignancy is linked to BRCA1 or BRCA2 genetic mutations?
A) 1%
B) 10%
C) 25%
D) 40%
E) 75%
questions.answer:
B)

The correct answer is B) 10%. Hereditary breast cancers account for approximately 5-10% of all familial breast cancer cases and are associated with mutations in cancer susceptibility genes, particularly BRCA1 and BRCA2. These genes function as tumor suppressors that maintain DNA stability and prevent uncontrolled cellular proliferation in healthy cells. Women carrying BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations have significantly elevated lifetime risks for developing breast and/or ovarian cancers, with these hereditary cancers typically presenting at younger ages and frequently being estrogen receptor-negative. A) 1% is too low as it underestimates the actual prevalence of BRCA-associated breast cancers. C) 25% overestimates the frequency, as hereditary forms represent only a small subset of breast cancers. D) 40% and E) 75% are both significantly higher than the established prevalence rates for BRCA-related breast malignancies.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old male presents to the emergency room following electrical injury to his right arm from high-voltage power line contact. Clinical assessment reveals deep burns covering the right palmar forearm, representing 3% total body surface area. The injured region demonstrates temperature instability and pale coloration. No pulses can be detected. Oxygen therapy has been started and intravenous fluid replacement begun. What represents the most suitable immediate management approach?
A) Arm elevation
B) Eschar removal from the palmar forearm
C) Fascial release of the palmar forearm alone
D) Fascial release of the palmar forearm with carpal tunnel decompression alone
E) Fascial release of the palmar forearm with pronator quadratus exploration and carpal tunnel decompression
questions.answer:
E)
The appropriate management is fascial release of the palmar forearm with pronator quadratus exploration and carpal tunnel decompression. High-voltage electrical injuries frequently cause compartment syndrome requiring urgent surgical decompression. The clinical presentation includes the classic five signs: pain, numbness, pallor, temperature changes, and absent pulses. Complete decompression must include fascial release, carpal tunnel decompression to protect the median nerve and palmar circulation, and deep compartment exploration including the pronator quadratus muscle, as electrical current generates significant heat near bone structures like the radius and ulna, causing deeper tissue damage. A is incorrect because elevation alone will not address compartment syndrome. B is incorrect because escharotomy without fasciotomy is insufficient for compartment decompression. C is incorrect because it fails to address carpal tunnel compression and deep compartment involvement. D is incorrect because it does not include exploration of the deep compartment where significant injury may occur near the bones.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female patient presents for consultation regarding buttock fat transfer surgery. Her BMI is 27.5 kg/m2. She has no other medical issues. Which of the following operative approaches will best reduce this patient's likelihood of developing fatal fat embolism to the lungs?
A) Prevent injection of fat into muscle tissue
B) Process fat through centrifugation before transplantation
C) Only inject fat while keeping the cannula motionless
D) Utilize a transplantation cannula with diameter of 2 mm or larger
E) Employ an extended cannula to minimize the number of incision sites
questions.answer:
A)
Preventing injection of fat into muscle tissue is the most critical factor in reducing fatal pulmonary fat embolism risk. The primary mechanism causing death involves mechanical injury to large gluteal veins followed by either direct intravascular fat injection or extravascular fat migration into damaged vessels due to pressure gradients. Avoiding intramuscular injection significantly decreases this risk. B is incorrect because centrifugation versus decantation of harvested fat does not substantially impact mortality risk. C is incorrect because fat should only be injected while the cannula is moving, not stationary, to prevent vessel injury. D is incorrect because the recommended cannula diameter is greater than 4.1 mm, not 2 mm. E is incorrect because longer cannulas narrower than 4 mm may bend and inadvertently penetrate muscle tissue, increasing risk.

questions.question:
A 12-month-old boy comes to the office for evaluation of a congenital thumb deformity. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate management of the thumb?


A) First metacarpal distraction osteogenesis
B) First web space deepening
C) Flexor digitorum superficialis opponensplasty
D) Free great toe transfer
E) Index finger pollicization
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


This patient has a type IV (floating thumb or pouce flottant) thumb hypoplasia best managed with thumb ablation and index finger pollicization. Thumb hypoplasia can range from a minor decrease in size to complete absence. Thumb hypoplasia may also be associated with VACTERL (vertebral abnormalities, anal atresia, cardiac abnormalities, tracheoesophageal fistula or esophageal atresia, renal agenesis and dysplasia, and limb defects), TAR syndrome, Fanconi anemia, and Holt-Oram syndrome. Given the possible association with these conditions, a workup of all potentially affected organ systems should be performed. This includes a renal ultrasound, an echocardiogram, spine x-ray studies, a complete blood count, and a chromosomal challenge test.


Thumb hypoplasia may occur in an isolated fashion or in combination with radial hypoplasia, as seen in this case. The most important and difficult distinction is between types IIIa and IIIb hypoplastic thumbs. A type IIIa thumb has a stable thumb carpometacarpal (CMC) joint, whereas a type IIIb thumb does not. If the child uses the thumb for integrated pinch, the CMC joint is deemed stable. If the thumb is bypassed in favor of scissor pinch between the index and middle fingers, the CMC joint is either unstable or absent; in this case, a pollicization is recommended.


A free great toe transfer is not indicated in children with thumb hypoplasia because the existing thumb CMC is not stable and pollicization would provide a better functional outcome. Flexor digitorum superficialis or abductor digiti minimi opponensplasty are both options for thumb hypoplasia reconstruction in the presence of a stable CMC joint. A first webspace deepening is typically combined with opponensplasty and metacarpophalangeal joint stabilization in children with reconstructible hypoplastic thumbs, but not for children undergoing pollicization. The patient in the image does not have a first metacarpal, and therefore cannot undergo distraction osteogenesis.


ReferencesKozin SH, Zlotolow DA. Common pediatric congenital conditions of the hand. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2015;136(2):241e-257e.Soldado F, Zlotolow DA, Kozin SH. Thumb hypoplasia. J Hand Surg Am. 2013;38(7):1435-1444.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male presents to the emergency department following a severe traumatic injury to his right hand and wrist requiring soft-tissue repair. Physical examination reveals exposed tendons and bone on the dorsal aspect of the right hand and wrist. The injury zone reaches the elbow level. The Allen test shows abnormal results. What is the most suitable reconstruction approach?
A) Groin flap coverage
B) Reverse radial forearm flap coverage
C) Full-thickness skin graft
D) Negative pressure wound therapy
E) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
A)
Groin flap coverage is the most appropriate reconstruction method. This patient has a severe injury with exposed extensor tendons and bone on the dorsal hand and wrist, creating an unsuitable bed for skin grafting. Skin grafts require a vascularized wound bed for survival through plasmatic imbibition and subsequent inosculation, which exposed tendons cannot provide adequately. B) is incorrect because the reverse radial forearm flap is contraindicated due to the abnormal Allen test, indicating compromised palmar arch circulation that would risk arterial insufficiency if the radial artery is sacrificed. C) and E) are incorrect because both full-thickness and split-thickness skin grafts will fail on exposed tendons lacking adequate vascular supply for graft take. D) is incorrect because while negative pressure wound therapy may serve as temporary management, it does not provide definitive reconstruction for this complex defect.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old female patient suffered thermal burns covering 50% of her total body surface area and was successfully stabilized hemodynamically and pulmonarily. On the fourth day post-injury, she underwent complete tangential debridement and temporary xenograft placement of all burned regions. Post-operatively, she was returned to the intensive care unit on mechanical ventilation with an endotracheal tube in place. She exhibits viscous respiratory secretions. During the procedure, she received 2 units of packed erythrocytes. Current vital parameters are:

Temperature 99.5°F (37.5°C)
Heart Rate 130 bpm
Respiratory Rate 22/min
Blood Pressure 80/50 mmHg

Oxygen saturation measures 96% on 40% FiO2. Cardiac output is 6 L/min, and urinary output is 0.1 mL/kg/h. What is the most probable cause of these abnormal clinical findings?

A) Acute lung injury syndrome
B) Volume depletion shock
C) Pulmonary infection
D) Venous thromboembolism
E) Systemic inflammatory response syndrome
questions.answer:
B)

The most probable explanation for this patient's abnormal physiology is volume depletion shock. The patient recently underwent tangential debridement of a 50% total body surface area burn, which typically results in significant hemorrhage. Although she received 2 units of packed erythrocytes, this transfusion volume is likely insufficient for such extensive burn excision. Additionally, her vital signs are characteristic of hypovolemic shock with hypotension, tachycardia, and oliguria. A) Acute lung injury syndrome is incorrect because it typically occurs later in the clinical course and would present with more severe hypoxemia rather than isolated hypotension. C) Pulmonary infection is incorrect because it usually develops later in burn patients and would cause more pronounced oxygen desaturation than observed. D) Venous thromboembolism is incorrect because it typically presents later in the hospital stay and would cause more severe hypoxemia. E) Systemic inflammatory response syndrome is incorrect because it characteristically presents with hyperthermia and elevated cardiac output, whereas this patient has normal temperature and appropriate cardiac output for her hemodynamic state.

questions.question:
In a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled study, 84% of participants receiving migraine surgery versus 58% of participants receiving sham surgery experienced more than 50% improvement in migraine symptoms (p < 0.05). What does a p value of <0.05 signify?
A) The observed difference is probably due to random variation (accept null hypothesis)
B) The observed difference is probably due to random variation (reject null hypothesis)
C) The observed difference is probably not due to random variation (accept null hypothesis)
D) The observed difference is probably not due to random variation (reject null hypothesis)
E) No conclusion can be drawn about the null hypothesis
questions.answer:
D)
The p value represents the probability of obtaining a difference at least as large as the one observed assuming the null hypothesis is true. When the p value is small (< 0.05), it indicates the observed difference is unlikely to be due to random sampling variation, leading us to reject the null hypothesis of no difference between groups. A) is incorrect because a small p value suggests the difference is not due to sampling variation and we should reject, not accept, the null hypothesis. B) is incorrect because while we reject the null hypothesis with a small p value, it's because the difference is unlikely due to sampling variation, not likely. C) is incorrect because although the difference is not likely due to sampling variation, we reject rather than accept the null hypothesis. E) is incorrect because a p value < 0.05 provides sufficient evidence to make a determination about the null hypothesis.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female patient presents for assessment of several hard, raised, pink-toned growths on her scalp, measuring 2 to 4 mm in diameter. Histopathological analysis of a biopsy sample reveals benign cylindroma. What is the most suitable treatment approach for these growths?
A) Cryotherapy
B) Electrodessication and curettage
C) Imiquimod therapy
D) Radiotherapy
E) Surgical excision
questions.answer:
E)
Surgical excision is the most appropriate treatment for benign cylindromas because these adnexal tumors have the potential for malignant transformation and high recurrence rates, making complete removal with close follow-up essential. A) Cryotherapy is incorrect as it is not an established treatment modality for cylindromas. B) Electrodessication and curettage is incorrect because these techniques are inadequate for complete removal of cylindromas and do not address the risk of malignant transformation. C) Imiquimod therapy is incorrect as topical immunomodulators are not effective treatments for cylindromas. D) Radiotherapy is incorrect for benign cylindromas, as radiation therapy is reserved for malignant cylindromas (cylindrocarcinomas) rather than benign lesions.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old female patient with a past medical history of Stage I T1N0 infiltrating ductal breast carcinoma of the right breast comes to clinic 15 years following bilateral mastectomy, negative right sentinel lymph node sampling, and staged tissue expander to permanent implant breast reconstruction. During the last 3 months, her left reconstructed breast has grown noticeably larger compared to her right side. Physical examination reveals no cutaneous abnormalities, palpable lumps, or enlarged axillary lymph nodes. What is the most suitable initial diagnostic step for evaluating this patient?
A) Ultrasonography
B) Mammographic imaging
C) Positron emission tomography-computed tomography
D) Magnetic resonance imaging
questions.answer:
A)
Ultrasonography is the most appropriate initial diagnostic step. This patient presents with late-onset enlargement of her reconstructed breast 15 years post-reconstruction, which raises concern for a periprosthetic fluid collection that could represent breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL). Ultrasound can effectively differentiate between fluid collections and capsular contracture as causes of apparent breast enlargement, identify capsular masses, and allow for fluid aspiration for cytological analysis and flow cytometry to evaluate for BIA-ALCL markers (CD30 positivity, ALK negativity). B) is incorrect because mammography is a breast cancer screening modality that has no utility in post-mastectomy patients for evaluating implant-related complications. C) is incorrect because PET-CT is typically used for staging after BIA-ALCL diagnosis is confirmed, not as an initial diagnostic tool. D) is incorrect because while MRI is recommended for routine silicone implant surveillance to assess shell integrity, it does not play a role in the initial evaluation of suspected BIA-ALCL.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old female patient presents to discuss circumferential body contouring surgery. Her medical background includes significant weight reduction after undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass procedure 3 years prior. She currently takes a daily multivitamin supplement. The patient has been inconsistent with follow-up visits to her bariatric surgery team and admits to poor compliance with dietary guidelines and supplementation protocols. Which nutrient deficiency is most probable in this patient?
A) Folate
B) Iron
C) Magnesium
D) Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine)
E) Vitamin E
questions.answer:
B)
Iron deficiency frequently occurs following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass procedures and is challenging to remedy with multivitamin supplementation alone. Folate deficiencies post-gastric bypass are typically resolved through standard multivitamin supplementation. Although other B-vitamin deficiencies may occur after bariatric surgery, vitamin B6 deficiency has not been specifically associated with gastric bypass procedures. Magnesium deficiency is not commonly observed as a consequence of gastric bypass surgery. Vitamin E, despite being fat-soluble, is not regularly found to be deficient after gastric bypass, unlike other fat-soluble vitamins.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient seeking breast lift surgery presents with C-cup breasts, grade 3 ptosis, bilateral breast skin stretch marks, 5-mm upper pole pinch test measurement, and areolae measuring 7 cm in diameter. Which of the following represents the most significant CONTRAINDICATION to using a periareolar-only technique for mastopexy?
A) Stretch marks on breast skin
B) C-cup breast volume
C) Grade 3 ptosis
D) 5-mm upper pole pinch test
E) 7-cm areolar diameter
questions.answer:
C)
Periareolar-only mastopexy techniques are not suitable for severe ptosis such as grade 3 ptosis and are typically reserved for patients with mild to moderate ptosis. A) is incorrect because stretch marks, while indicating compromised skin quality that may predispose to ptosis recurrence, do not specifically contraindicate the periareolar approach. B) is incorrect because moderate breast size (C-cup) does not negatively impact the success of this surgical technique. D) is incorrect because the thin upper pole pinch measurement primarily affects implant-related surgical decisions rather than mastopexy approach selection. E) is incorrect because large areolae (7 cm) are actually well-suited for periareolar surgical techniques.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old woman with right-hand dominance presents to the clinic with a loose nail at the middle portion of the nail bed on her right ring finger. The nail occasionally detaches when she places her hand in her pocket. She has a history of injury to the nail bed of this finger. Physical examination reveals normal finger range of motion. Radiographic imaging demonstrates a dorsal bony exostosis. Besides nail plate removal, what is the most appropriate treatment for this nail detachment?
A) Removal of the distal phalanx bony growth
B) Excision of the exostosis with sterile matrix transplantation
C) Nail bed destruction followed by split-thickness skin transplantation
D) Patient education that natural nail regrowth will occur
questions.answer:
B)
Nail detachment represents the most frequent nail abnormality following injury and typically occurs distal to nail bed scarring or bony irregularities. Scar tissue in the nail bed is the primary cause of nail detachment. This scarring disrupts the continuous addition of nail cells from the sterile matrix to the nail plate's undersurface, resulting in nail separation. The detached nail cannot properly adhere to the distal nail bed. This condition can cause hygiene difficulties beneath the nail, nail instability during fine motor tasks, and pain when the nail catches on objects. Treatment involves nail plate removal and excision of the underlying scar tissue. The resulting defect can be closed directly or reconstructed with a sterile matrix graft if too large for primary closure. The bony exostosis must also be removed to create a smooth surface for proper sterile matrix function and subsequent nail attachment. A is incorrect because removing only the exostosis without addressing the scarred nail bed and providing matrix grafting will not solve the adherence problem. C is incorrect because nail bed ablation with skin grafting would eliminate nail growth entirely rather than restore normal nail function. D is incorrect because without surgical intervention to address the underlying scar tissue and bony irregularity, the nail will continue to have adherence problems.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old, right-hand‚Äidominant man is brought to the emergency department 3 hours after sustaining an avulsion injury to the left thumb. The avulsed digit was immediately placed on ice and transported with the patient. Photographs are shown. Replantation fails; the necrotic digit is removed and the wound closed. The carpometacarpal (CMC) joint is disarticulated. Which of the following is the most appropriate method of reconstruction in this patient?


A) Great toe to thumb transfer
B) Metacarpal lengthening
C) Osteoplastic reconstruction
D) Pollicization of index finger
E) Web deepening
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


This patient has a proximal thumb avulsion with disruption of the carpometacarpal (CMC) joint. In this scenario, the best reconstructive option (besides successful replantation) is pollicization of the index finger. Reconstruction after thumb amputation, as with congenital deficiencies, depends largely on the length of the remaining skeletal structure. One can lose most of the distal phalanx and still retain good overall thumb function. Amputations that involve the proximal phalanx or the metacarpal suffer from deficient bone length and procedures that add length, like distraction, toe to thumb, or osteoplastic reconstruction. When the entire metacarpal is absent, the aforementioned procedures will not be effective. Pollicization will restore thumb length and provide very good function.


References
Friedrich JB, Vedder NB. Thumb reconstruction. Clin Plast Surg. 2011 Oct;38(4):697-712.
Heitman C, Levin LS. Alternatives to thumb replantation. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2002 Nov;110(6):1492-503.
Pet MA, Ko JH, Vedder NB. Reconstruction of the traumatized thumb. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2014 Dec;134(6):1235-45.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old woman who underwent repair of unilateral cleft lip and palate in infancy comes to the office for consultation regarding facial aesthetics. Cephalometric analysis shows an SNA angle of 75 degrees (N 81.2), an SNB angle of 81 degrees (N 77.3), and an SNPg angle of 81 degrees (N 80). A negative overjet of 1.5 mm is noted. A photograph is shown. After orthodontic preparation, which of the following is the most appropriate surgical management?


A) Maxillary advancement
B) Maxillary advancement and mandibular setback
C) Maxillary advancement, mandibular setback, and advancement genioplasty
D) Maxillary setback
E) Maxillary setback, mandibular advancement, and advancement genioplasty
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


The cephalogram is a standardized x-ray study used for analyzing facial disharmony and asymmetry. Labeled landmarks help establish the relationship of the maxilla, mandible, and skull base to other facial structures. The sella (S) point marks the center of the hypophyseal fossa. The nasion (N) is the junction of the nasal and frontal bones at the most posterior point of the curve of the nose. Point ?A? marks the innermost curvature from the maxillary anterior nasal spine to the alveolar process. The angle created by these points (SNA) establishes the maxillary position in relation to the skull base. Point ?B? is located at the innermost curvature from the chin to the alveolar process of the mandible. The SNA angle similarly establishes the mandibular relationship to the skull base.


The prominence of the chin is often an important consideration in orthognathic surgery. The pogonion is the most anterior chin point. SNPg angle is representative of the degree of chin prominence relative to the cranial base (mandible position).


Normal angle values are given in the text. The patient described is in a dramatic Angle class III malocclusion. The SNA is less than normal, and the SNB is greater than normal. The chin position is appropriate. In order to establish a class I dental relationship, the maxilla must advance, and the mandible must be set back. Doing so will also move the chin back. Therefore, to maintain the preoperative chin position, a compensatory advancement genioplasty should also be performed.


References
McCarthy JG, Grayson B. Orthognathic surgery. In: McCarthy JG, Galiano RD, Boutros SG, eds. Current Therapy in Plastic Surgery. Philadelphia: WB Saunders; 2006:151-164.
Schendel S. Orthognathic surgery. In: Achauer BM, Eriksson E, Guyuron B, et al, eds. Plastic Surgery: Indications, Operations, and Outcomes. Vol 2. St. Louis: Mosby; 2000:871-896.
Zoldos J, Sotereanos G. Pediatric orthognathic surgery syndromes. In: Bentz ML, ed. Pediatric Plastic Surgery. McGraw-Hill Professional; 1997: 227-257.

questions.question:
A 79-year-old female patient has surgical removal and prophylactic neck dissection performed for a 2.5-cm infiltrating squamous cell carcinoma located on the right lateral tongue surface. She has no prior history of head and neck malignancy, and imaging and physical examination show no evidence of lymph node involvement or distant spread. Complete resection with clear margins and ipsilateral modified radical neck dissection are completed. What is the most probable outcome of prophylactic neck dissection in this patient?
A) Reduced local tumor recurrence
B) Lower rate of surgical complications
C) Higher risk of distant metastatic spread
D) Greater lymph node recurrence rate
E) Improved overall survival
questions.answer:
E)
This patient will experience improved overall survival compared to a patient who does not receive prophylactic neck dissection. The described patient has Stage II (T2 N0 M0) oral malignancy (measuring greater than 2 cm but less than 4 cm, without lymph node spread and no distant metastases). There has been considerable discussion about neck management in patients with early-stage oral malignancies. The two main approaches include prophylactic neck dissection (performed simultaneously with primary tumor removal) versus therapeutic neck dissection when lymph node recurrence occurs. In a prospective, randomized, controlled study of patients with T1 or T2 node-negative oral squamous cell carcinoma, patients received either prophylactic neck dissection during primary tumor removal or therapeutic neck dissection following lymph node recurrence. At 3 years, patients who had prophylactic neck dissection showed higher survival rates compared to the therapeutic surgery group (69.5 vs. 45.9%, P<0.001). A is incorrect because elective neck dissection primarily affects regional control rather than local recurrence at the primary site. B is incorrect because patients who undergo elective neck dissection actually experience more postoperative complications due to the additional surgical procedure. C is incorrect because distant metastasis rates were similar between elective and therapeutic neck dissection groups. D is incorrect because elective neck dissection actually decreases nodal recurrence by removing potentially involved lymph nodes before they become clinically apparent.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old previously healthy woman presents to the burn center following extensive thermal injury affecting 50% of her body surface area. Clinical assessment reveals complete circumferential deep burns of the right arm with loss of peripheral pulses. Digital capillary refill exceeds 3 seconds. After establishing proper airway management and beginning fluid replacement therapy, urgent escharotomies are completed on the right upper limb. Following the procedure, perfusion to the distal arm continues to be compromised as evidenced by prolonged capillary refill and poor Doppler signals. What represents the most suitable subsequent intervention?
A) Performing additional escharotomy incisions
B) Providing intravenous fluid supplementation
C) Obtaining arterial imaging studies
D) Positioning the limb in elevation and reassessing after 45 minutes
E) Performing compartment release surgery of the upper limb
questions.answer:
E)
Compartment release surgery (fasciotomy) of the upper extremity is the most appropriate next intervention. When standard escharotomy procedures fail to restore adequate circulation despite proper technique, the underlying muscle compartments may require surgical decompression. This scenario indicates compartment syndrome developing beneath the burned tissue, where increased pressure within fascial compartments compromises blood flow even after eschar release. Fasciotomy involves incising the deep fascial layers to relieve this pressure and restore perfusion. Carpal tunnel decompression should also be performed during upper extremity fasciotomy. A) Additional escharotomies would be ineffective since standard escharotomy has already been performed and failed to improve circulation. B) Further fluid administration would not address the mechanical compression causing poor perfusion and could worsen edema. C) Angiography would delay necessary treatment and is not indicated when compartment syndrome is the likely cause of continued ischemia. D) Limb elevation and observation would waste critical time when immediate surgical decompression is needed to prevent irreversible tissue damage.

questions.question:
A healthy 41-year-old woman plans to undergo bilateral prophylactic nipple-sparing mastectomy due to a BRCA1 mutation. What is a benefit of prepectoral implant reconstruction compared to subpectoral implant reconstruction?
A) Significantly increased acute postoperative complications occur
B) Higher revision rates are observed
C) Reduced animation deformity occurs
D) Decreased upper pole rippling and implant visibility result
E) Greater pain and functional limitations are present
questions.answer:
C)
Prepectoral implant placement results in reduced animation deformity compared to subpectoral placement. When implants are placed beneath the pectoralis muscle, muscle contraction can cause visible implant movement and distortion (animation deformity). Prepectoral placement avoids this issue since the implant is not covered by contracting muscle. Additionally, studies show prepectoral reconstruction leads to less postoperative pain and faster functional recovery. A) is incorrect because multiple patient series demonstrate no significant difference in acute complications between the two techniques. B) is incorrect as revision rates are comparable between prepectoral and subpectoral approaches. D) is incorrect because prepectoral placement actually increases the risk of upper pole rippling and implant palpability due to less soft tissue coverage, particularly in thin patients. E) is incorrect since prepectoral reconstruction typically results in less pain and better functional outcomes compared to subpectoral placement.

questions.question:
