C) is incorrect because this patient has a small surface area exposure to low-concentration acid, making systemic toxicity unlikely and serial lab monitoring less critical. D) is incorrect because mafenide acetate is used for thermal burns but does not neutralize hydrofluoric acid. E) is incorrect because while pain control is necessary, it alone does not address the ongoing chemical burn process that requires specific neutralization.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male presents for assessment 8 weeks following a right knee dislocation that occurred when he stumbled over a railroad tie during work. Physical examination reveals right foot drop and abnormal sensation over the lateral aspect of the lower leg and dorsolateral portion of the foot. Electromyography and nerve conduction studies would most likely demonstrate damage to which of the following nerves?
A) Femoral
B) Peroneal
C) Plantar
D) Sural
E) Tibial
questions.answer:
B)
The peroneal nerve supplies the tibialis anterior muscle and the extrinsic toe extensors, which are responsible for dorsiflexing the ankle. When these muscles are paralyzed, foot drop occurs. A) Femoral nerve is incorrect because it travels through the anterior thigh and innervates the knee extensors, making it unlikely to be injured in a knee dislocation. C) Plantar nerves are incorrect because they are terminal branches of the tibial nerve that supply intrinsic foot muscles and plantar sensation. D) Sural nerve is incorrect because it is purely sensory, providing cutaneous innervation around the lateral ankle area. E) Tibial nerve is incorrect because it innervates the ankle and toe flexors, and its injury would not result in foot drop.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old female patient with breast carcinoma receives bilateral mastectomies followed by immediate breast reconstruction using deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flaps. Her postoperative course is uncomplicated, and she is released from the hospital on the fourth day after surgery. Which of the following most accurately characterizes the anticipated postoperative alterations in the lower limb venous circulation throughout her hospitalization?
A) Reduction in the caliber of the common femoral vein occurs
B) Enhancement of flow velocity in the common femoral vein develops
C) The venous circulation remains unaltered
D) Venous stasis continues until hospital discharge
E) Venous stasis occurs, with differences based on unilateral versus bilateral flap procedures
questions.answer:
D)
Venous stasis continues until hospital discharge. Autologous breast reconstruction carries an elevated risk for deep vein thrombosis development. Research has demonstrated correlations between autologous breast reconstruction and impaired venous return with resulting stasis. Compared to preoperative measurements, the common femoral veins demonstrate enlarged diameter and reduced flow velocity, with these alterations continuing through discharge day. A is incorrect because the common femoral vein diameter actually increases rather than decreases. B is incorrect because flow velocity decreases, not increases, in the common femoral vein. C is incorrect because significant changes do occur in the venous circulation following this procedure. E is incorrect because harvesting lower abdominal tissue and performing tight abdominal closure occurs in both unilateral and bilateral reconstructions, resulting in similar venous stasis patterns regardless of whether one or both sides are reconstructed.

questions.question:
The periodontal ligament secures teeth to the adjacent alveolar bone by connecting to which of the following anatomical components?
A) Cementum
B) Dentin
C) Enamel
D) Gingiva
E) Neurovascular bundle
questions.answer:
A)
The correct answer is A) Cementum. The tooth root is encased by a calcified tissue called cementum, which serves as the attachment site for the periodontal ligament. This ligament, containing Sharpey fibers and sensory components, creates a secure connection between the cementum and the surrounding alveolar bone, enabling the periodontal ligament to provide tooth stability, shock absorption, and proprioceptive feedback. B) is incorrect because while dentin forms the main structure of the tooth root, it does not serve as the direct attachment point for the periodontal ligament to bone. C) is incorrect because enamel covers only the tooth crown and has no direct connection to the periodontal ligament or bone attachment. D) is incorrect because the gingiva does not provide direct mechanical attachment to the alveolar bone. E) is incorrect because neurovascular bundles supply sensation and blood flow to the tooth but do not contribute to mechanical anchorage to the bone.

questions.question:
Which nerve provides innervation to the nipple-areolar region?
A) Intercostal
B) Lateral pectoral
C) Long thoracic
D) Supraclavicular
E) Thoracodorsal
questions.answer:
A)
The intercostal nerve is correct. Traditional anatomical knowledge attributes nipple innervation to the fourth intercostal nerve, though contemporary anatomical research has demonstrated that the nipple receives innervation from a complex subdermal nerve network that delivers both tactile and pressure sensations. This network is supplied by the lateral and anterior cutaneous branches of the second through fifth intercostal nerves, which explains how nipple sensation can be preserved even after extensive surgical interventions. B) is incorrect because the lateral pectoral nerve supplies the pectoralis major muscle, not the nipple-areolar skin. C) is incorrect because the long thoracic nerve innervates the serratus anterior muscle rather than breast skin. D) is incorrect because the supraclavicular nerve provides sensation to the upper breast skin, not specifically the nipple-areolar complex. E) is incorrect because the thoracodorsal nerve supplies the latissimus dorsi muscle, not breast tissue.

questions.question:
An 8-month-old male infant presents to the clinic for assessment of a vascular birthmark affecting the right chest wall and right facial area. Clinical examination reveals red skin discoloration following a dermatomal pattern. Which laser system would be the optimal choice for managing this lesion?
A) CO2 laser (10,200 nm)
B) Neodymium:YAG (1064 nm)
C) Pulsed-dye (585 nm)
D) Q-switched alexandrite (755 nm)
E) Q-switched ruby (694 nm)
questions.answer:
C)
The pulsed-dye laser with epidermal cooling continues to be the gold standard for treating port-wine stains in children. Intense pulsed-light systems have also shown some efficacy. The concept of selective photothermolysis is fundamental to successful port-wine stain treatment. Oxyhemoglobin acts as the target chromophore, with three distinct absorption peaks at 418, 542, and 577 nm. The 585-nm and 595-nm pulsed-dye lasers are currently the preferred options due to their wavelength proximity to an absorption peak and superior tissue penetration. Penetration depth can be further improved by utilizing larger spot sizes (10 mm). A) CO2 laser is incorrect because it targets water and is used for tissue ablation rather than vascular lesions. B) Nd:YAG laser is incorrect as it is primarily effective for deeper venous malformations, not superficial capillary malformations. D) Q-switched alexandrite laser is incorrect because it is designed for tattoo removal, specifically targeting black, blue, and green pigments. E) Q-switched ruby laser is incorrect as it is also used for tattoo removal and targets similar pigments as the alexandrite laser.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old female patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus is scheduled for lower limb angiography to assess her candidacy for forefoot surgical repair. What is the most suitable intervention for preventing contrast-associated acute kidney injury in this patient?
A) Vitamin C
B) Normal saline infusion
C) N-acetylcysteine
D) Statin medication
E) Bicarbonate solution
questions.answer:
B)

Normal saline infusion is the most appropriate preventive measure for contrast-associated acute kidney injury (AKI). This condition represents the third leading cause of hospital-acquired kidney dysfunction and occurs through ischemic damage to the kidney's inner medulla. Intravenous normal saline hydration serves as the cornerstone of prevention because it expands blood volume, enhances urine production, reduces contrast concentration in blood vessels, and promotes kidney blood vessel dilation. This approach is safe, economical, and consistently proven effective in clinical trials. A) Vitamin C is incorrect because ascorbic acid supplementation has not demonstrated efficacy in preventing contrast-induced kidney injury. C) N-acetylcysteine is incorrect as current evidence does not support its use for contrast nephropathy prevention. D) Statin medication is incorrect because these cholesterol-lowering drugs are not recommended for this indication. E) Bicarbonate solution is incorrect because while it has been studied, recent research shows inconsistent results compared to normal saline.

questions.question:
A 2-year-old girl is referred for evaluation of a congenital hand anomaly. On exam, she is found to have complete absence of the central three digits with preservation of the thumb and fifth finger. There is a deep median cleft and syndactyly between the remaining digits. Which of the following is the MOST likely diagnosis?

A) Radial longitudinal deficiency
B) Ulnar longitudinal deficiency
C) Polydactyly
D) Cleft hand (ectrodactyly)
E) Camptodactyly
questions.answer:
D)

Correct Answer (D): Cleft hand, also known as ectrodactyly or split hand, is characterized by absence of the central digits (usually the index, middle, and ring fingers), preservation of the thumb and fifth digit, and a deep median cleft. Syndactyly may also be present.

A (Radial longitudinal deficiency): Incorrect. This presents as absence or hypoplasia of the radius and radial-sided digits, often with the thumb missing. The scenario describes preservation of thumb and little finger with a central cleft, not radial deficiency.

B (Ulnar longitudinal deficiency): Incorrect. This manifests as absence or hypoplasia of the ulnar-sided digits and the ulna, often affecting the fifth finger. In this vignette, the fifth digit is present; it is the central digits that are missing.

C (Polydactyly): Incorrect. Polydactyly refers to extra digits, not absent digits or a cleft hand.

E (Camptodactyly): Incorrect. Camptodactyly refers to congenital flexion contracture of a finger, usually the little finger, and does not cause absence of digits or a median cleft.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient experiences an ulnar nerve injury above the elbow level with complete loss of hand intrinsic muscle function. During operative exploration, a 1-cm defect is identified in the nerve. What represents the optimal treatment approach for this condition?
A) Nerve conduit interposition
B) Nerve graft interposition
C) Direct primary repair alone
D) Direct primary repair combined with anterior nerve transposition
E) Direct primary repair combined with distal nerve transfer
questions.answer:
E)
The optimal treatment approach combines direct primary repair with distal nerve transfer. The ulnar nerve provides motor innervation to critical hand intrinsic muscles including the interossei, hypothenar muscles, ulnar lumbricals, and adductor pollicis. These small muscles are highly susceptible to denervation and undergo irreversible atrophy within 9-12 months. Given the proximal location of this injury (approximately 18 inches from the target muscles), nerve regeneration at 1 inch per month would take too long to prevent muscle atrophy. A distal nerve transfer, typically using the terminal anterior interosseous nerve branch, provides immediate "babysitting" innervation to preserve muscle viability while the primary repair regenerates. A) is incorrect because nerve conduits are unnecessary for a 1-cm gap that can be primarily repaired. B) is incorrect because nerve grafts are not needed when primary repair is feasible after mobilization. C) is incorrect because primary repair alone would result in muscle atrophy before reinnervation occurs. D) is incorrect because anterior transposition alone, while providing additional length, does not address the timing issue of muscle denervation.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male patient requires surgical removal of a squamous cell carcinoma located in the right floor of mouth with extension into the mandibular body. The surgical plan includes composite resection of the right mandibular segment and a 2-cm excision of the floor of mouth tissue, followed by immediate reconstruction using a fibula flap, which will require an osteocutaneous flap approach. Which of the following most accurately describes the vascular supply pathway for the cutaneous component of this flap?
A) Musculocutaneous and septocutaneous perforating vessels from the peroneus longus and brevis muscles
B) Musculocutaneous perforating vessels from the flexor hallucis brevis muscle
C) Septocutaneous and musculocutaneous perforating vessels from the anterior tibialis muscle
D) Septocutaneous perforating vessels from the posterior intermuscular septum
E) Septocutaneous perforating vessels from the posterior tibialis muscle
questions.answer:
D)
The vascular supply to the cutaneous portion of the fibula flap originates from septocutaneous perforating vessels of the peroneal artery that pass through the posterior intermuscular septum. These vessels can be preoperatively identified using pencil Doppler examination and provide dependable perfusion for microsurgical reconstruction in most patients. A is incorrect because while musculocutaneous perforators exist from peroneal muscles, the primary reliable supply comes from septocutaneous perforators through the posterior septum. B is incorrect because the flexor hallucis brevis does not contribute to fibula flap skin paddle vascularization. C is incorrect because the anterior tibialis muscle does not supply the fibula flap skin paddle. E is incorrect because the posterior tibialis muscle does not provide blood supply to the fibula flap cutaneous component.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old transgender male (assigned female at birth) seeks evaluation for chest reconstruction surgery as part of gender-affirming care. Based on the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH) Standards of Care, this surgical intervention is deemed medically necessary, suitable, and warranted when which of the following criteria is satisfied?
A) The patient possesses the ability to provide fully informed consent
B) The patient has completed 6 months of uninterrupted hormonal treatment
C) The patient has a single healthcare provider documenting gender dysphoria
D) The patient has recently begun antidepressant medication
E) The patient must have reached 21 years of age
questions.answer:
A)
The correct answer is A because WPATH guidelines require that patients have the capacity to make fully informed decisions and provide consent for gender-affirming surgeries. For minors under 18, this includes patient assent combined with parental consent for mastectomy procedures. B is incorrect because WPATH actually requires at least 12 months of hormone therapy, not 6 months. C is incorrect because documentation of gender dysphoria must come from at least two healthcare providers, not just one. D is incorrect because while psychiatric conditions must be stable and well-controlled, recently starting depression treatment suggests instability rather than the required stable mental health status. E is incorrect because there is no minimum age requirement of 21 years; minors can undergo mastectomy with appropriate consent processes.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of weakness and difficulty fully straightening her right dominant thumb at the interphalangeal joint. Her medical history reveals a Colles fracture of the right wrist that occurred 6 months prior. The fracture was treated with cast immobilization. Physical examination shows the patient's thumb positioned at 30 degrees of flexion. Active extension at the finger metacarpophalangeal joints is normal. The patient is unable to extend or lift her thumb when her hand is placed flat on a table. When the thumb is held in adduction, she can extend it to a neutral position. All thumb joints demonstrate normal flexibility with complete passive range of motion. What is the most probable cause of this patient's thumb extension deficit?
A) Intersection syndrome
B) Radial nerve palsy
C) Rupture of the extensor pollicis longus
D) Saddle deformity of the basal joint
E) Trigger thumb with locking
questions.answer:
C)
Extensor pollicis longus (EPL) tendon rupture is the most likely diagnosis given the clinical presentation and history of distal radius fracture. EPL rupture commonly occurs as a delayed complication following Colles fractures due to tendon devascularization and subsequent attritional rupture. The timeline of 6 months post-fracture fits the typical presentation window of 2 weeks to 11 months. The patient's ability to extend the thumb when adducted occurs because intrinsic muscles can still contribute to extension through their connections to the dorsal apparatus. A) Intersection syndrome is incorrect because it presents with pain and tenderness along the radial forearm where muscle bellies cross, not isolated thumb extension loss. B) Radial nerve palsy is incorrect because it would cause more widespread deficits affecting wrist and finger extension, not just the thumb interphalangeal joint. D) Saddle deformity is incorrect because it involves basal joint arthritis with characteristic zigzag collapse and metacarpophalangeal hyperextension, which is not described here. E) Trigger thumb is incorrect because it typically presents with pain, tenderness along the flexor sheath, and would not allow the passive range of motion or extension with adduction seen in this case.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old male presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of numerous light-red, scaly patches on his scalp and forehead. Physical examination reveals significant solar damage to the face and scalp, with multiple flat patches ranging from 3 to 10 mm in diameter. Histological examination of a shave biopsy specimen demonstrates actinic keratosis with no evidence of invasive carcinoma. Along with daily sunscreen use and protective clothing, which of the following represents the most appropriate treatment?
A) Topical 5-fluorouracil application
B) Surgical excision with 2-mm margins
C) Follow-up biopsy in 6 months
D) Shave removal of the patches
E) Watchful waiting only
questions.answer:
A)
Topical 5-fluorouracil is the most appropriate treatment for multiple actinic keratoses because it can effectively treat numerous lesions simultaneously without causing extensive scarring, and it addresses both visible and subclinical lesions to prevent progression to malignancy. B is incorrect because surgical excision is unnecessarily invasive for superficial premalignant lesions and would result in significant scarring when treating multiple lesions. C is incorrect because delaying treatment of confirmed actinic keratoses increases the risk of malignant transformation, which can occur at rates of 1-25% per year per lesion. D is incorrect because shave excision is also unnecessarily invasive for multiple superficial lesions and would cause more scarring than topical therapy. E is incorrect because observation alone is inappropriate for multiple actinic keratoses in a healthy patient due to the significant risk of progression to squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.question:
A 51-year-old male comes for assessment of neurological damage after surgical removal of varicose veins from his left lower extremity. What clinical finding would most likely be observed with saphenous nerve damage in this patient?
A) Loss of sensation around the left medial malleolus
B) Heightened sensitivity over the dorsal aspect of the left foot
C) Loss of ability to lift the left foot upward
D) Elevated insertional activity in the tibialis anterior muscle
E) Sensory loss near the left lateral heel area
questions.answer:
A)
Saphenous nerve damage results in sensory loss over the medial calf and medial malleolus region, making this the expected finding. B is incorrect because heightened sensitivity over the dorsal foot would indicate superficial peroneal nerve involvement. C is incorrect because inability to dorsiflex the foot suggests deep peroneal nerve injury, not saphenous nerve damage. D is incorrect because increased insertional activity in the tibialis anterior would occur with deep peroneal nerve injury affecting motor function. E is incorrect because sensory loss near the lateral heel would result from sural nerve injury, not saphenous nerve damage.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old male presents for evaluation of a large grade IV left ischial pressure sore. His medical background includes traumatic T12 paraplegia for 6 months. The surgical plan involves debridement of the pressure sore and coverage with a left inferior gluteal thigh flap. During anesthetic induction, the patient develops cardiac dysrhythmia with peaked T waves and rapid heart rate. Oxygen saturation remains 100% with normal end-tidal CO2. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F). It is noted that succinylcholine was administered for rapid-sequence intubation by the anesthesia resident. What is the most appropriate initial treatment for this patient's condition?
A) Intravenous adenosine
B) Intravenous amiodarone
C) Intravenous calcium chloride
D) Intravenous dantrolene
E) Synchronized cardioversion
questions.answer:
C)
The patient has developed acute hyperkalemia secondary to succinylcholine administration, which is a known complication in paraplegic patients due to upregulation of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in denervated muscle. Intravenous calcium chloride is the correct initial treatment as it directly antagonizes hyperkalemia-induced cardiac membrane depolarization by stabilizing the membrane potential, providing immediate cardiac protection. A) Adenosine is incorrect because it treats supraventricular tachycardia, not hyperkalemia-induced arrhythmias. B) Amiodarone is incorrect as it is an antiarrhythmic for various tachyarrhythmias but does not address the underlying hyperkalemia. D) Dantrolene is incorrect because it treats malignant hyperthermia, which would present with elevated end-tidal CO2 and hyperthermia, neither of which are present. E) Synchronized cardioversion is incorrect as it treats unstable tachycardia but does not address the metabolic cause of this patient's arrhythmia.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient presents for evaluation of intense pain in the anatomical snuffbox region of her right hand, which developed following first dorsal compartment surgical decompression performed 8 months previously. Clinical examination reveals localized tenderness in the first dorsal compartment area, positive Tinel sign at the operative site, and sensory loss beyond the surgical incision. Current treatment includes gabapentin initiated when symptoms began, and she has undergone desensitization therapy. What is the most appropriate next management approach?
A) Surgical exploration with silicone nerve capping of the palmar cutaneous branch
B) Commencement of oral pregabalin treatment
C) Dexamethasone iontophoresis therapy
D) Nerve release with intramuscular transposition of the superficial radial nerve
E) Scar phenol injection combined with compression glove treatment
questions.answer:
D)
The appropriate treatment involves nerve release with intramuscular transposition of the superficial radial nerve. Radial sensory nerve branch injury is a recognized complication following de Quervain disease surgical treatment. When nerve injury is identified, management should include surgical exploration and nerve repair when feasible. If direct repair is not possible, various surgical approaches are available, with transposition of the damaged radial sensory nerve into the brachioradialis muscle being a frequently utilized technique. Other options include nerve transposition into bone or vein, nerve stripping, and covering the injured nerve with vascularized tissue. Since the patient has undergone 6 months of gabapentin therapy without improvement, surgical intervention is indicated. A is incorrect because silicone nerve capping has been abandoned due to poor pain relief outcomes and problems with cap displacement or migration. B is incorrect because both gabapentin and pregabalin are similar medications for neuropathic pain, and switching between them after 6 months of failed medical therapy is not the next appropriate step when surgical intervention is indicated. C is incorrect because corticosteroid iontophoresis lacks proven effectiveness for neuroma management. E is incorrect because phenol injection is used for stump neuromas and Morton's neuromas but has no evidence supporting its use in non-amputation neuroma cases.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old office worker presents for assessment of his left non-dominant wrist following trauma from a fall that occurred 2 days prior. CT imaging demonstrates an undisplaced fracture of the distal scaphoid tubercle. Physical examination shows no additional abnormal findings. What is the most appropriate initial management approach?
A) Autologous bone graft with internal fixation and immobilization for 3 to 6 months
B) Cast immobilization for 6 to 8 weeks
C) Compression screw fixation with immobilization for 6 to 12 weeks
D) Physical therapy for 6 weeks
E) Observation until wrist tenderness resolves
questions.answer:
B)
Undisplaced scaphoid fractures can be difficult to detect on standard X-rays but are clearly visible on CT scans. While treatment options for undisplaced scaphoid fractures include both conservative immobilization and surgical intervention, undisplaced distal pole and tubercle fractures are considered more stable injuries that can be effectively managed with immobilization alone for 6 to 12 weeks. These fractures typically involve small bone fragments that are not well-suited for compression screw placement. A) is incorrect because autologous bone grafting with internal fixation is typically reserved for established scaphoid nonunions, not acute fractures. C) is incorrect because compression screw fixation is generally unnecessary for stable tubercle fractures and may not be technically feasible due to the small fragment size. D) is incorrect because physical therapy allows wrist mobility which could impair healing and increase risk of delayed union or nonunion. E) is incorrect because simple observation without immobilization carries significant risk of poor healing outcomes or nonunion development.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male patient seeks treatment for his sagging right upper eyelid. His past medical history reveals a traumatic eye injury that occurred two years prior. Clinical examination demonstrates ptosis affecting the right upper eyelid. The levator muscle demonstrates functionality of less than 5 mm. No additional abnormalities are observed. What is the primary mechanism by which the most suitable surgical procedure for correcting this ptosis operates?
A) Stimulation of the frontalis muscle
B) Complete excision of a segment of the posterior lamella
C) Folding of the levator aponeurosis
D) Liberation of muscular fibrosis
E) Relocation of the levator aponeurosis
questions.answer:
A)
The appropriate treatment requires utilizing muscle tissue external to the eyelid to provide lifting power for the desired elevation. This procedure involves connecting the eyelid, specifically the tarsal plate, to the frontalis muscle using either synthetic materials, the patient's own fascia, or biological products. Stimulation of the frontalis muscle will subsequently lift the eyelid independently of the levator mechanism. B) is incorrect because en bloc removal of posterior lamella would not address the poor levator function and could worsen the condition. C) is incorrect because plication of a poorly functioning levator aponeurosis would not provide adequate lift given the minimal function. D) is incorrect because simply releasing fibrosis would not restore adequate function to a severely compromised levator. E) is incorrect because repositioning a dysfunctional levator aponeurosis would not improve its poor contractile ability.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female patient presents to the clinic 4 days following a sub-SMAS facelift procedure. Physical examination reveals an uneven full-denture smile pattern. Right-sided lip depressor activity is intact while left-sided function is absent. Lip eversion remains normal bilaterally. What is the most suitable initial treatment approach?
A) Nerve conduction studies
B) Surgical exploration for cervical nerve division
C) Surgical exploration for marginal mandibular nerve division
D) Injection of botulinum toxin type A to paralyze right lip depressors
E) Conservative management with monitoring
questions.answer:
E)
The appropriate initial approach is conservative management with monitoring. This patient demonstrates marginal mandibular branch pseudoparalysis, a temporary condition following SMAS rhytidectomy. Even with actual nerve injury, observation remains the preferred initial management as patients can retrain their smile for improved symmetry. Depressor function typically recovers within 3 weeks to 6 months. This pseudoparalysis occurs when SMAS/platysma flaps are elevated in the mandibular area, causing transient lip depression dysfunction in patients with preoperative full-denture smiles. A is incorrect because nerve conduction studies provide no therapeutic benefit in this scenario. B is incorrect because surgical exploration for cervical nerve injury is not warranted as initial management. C is incorrect because operative exploration for marginal mandibular nerve injury is premature and unnecessary at this early stage. D is incorrect because botulinum toxin injection should only be considered if asymmetry persists beyond 6 months.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male patient requires surgical repair of a large midline abdominal hernia. The surgical plan includes component separation using a posterior technique with mesh placement in the retrorectus space. Which anatomical layer can be incised to achieve additional mobilization while maintaining nerve supply to the rectus abdominis muscle?
A) Anterior rectus fascia
B) External oblique muscle
C) Internal oblique muscle
D) Transversalis fascia
E) Transversus abdominis muscle
questions.answer:
E)
The transversus abdominis muscle release (TAR) is the correct choice for achieving additional mobilization in posterior component separation while preserving rectus muscle innervation. This technique allows lateral extension of dissection beyond the linea semilunaris without compromising the segmental nerves that supply the rectus abdominis. The TAR approach maintains the integrity of the anterior rectus sheath, external oblique, and transversalis fascia. A) Anterior rectus fascia division would not provide the needed lateral release and could compromise structural integrity. B) External oblique division is not part of the posterior approach and would not achieve the desired mobilization. C) Internal oblique division would sever the segmental nerves to the rectus muscle, which is precisely what this technique aims to avoid. D) Transversalis fascia division alone would not provide sufficient release for large defect repair.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old female presents for assessment of a traumatic injury to her left heel sustained during a shark attack 6 days prior. Clinical examination reveals a 5 × 5-cm soft-tissue loss with bone exposure. A sensate flap from the instep area is being considered for reconstruction. Which nerve supplies sensation to this flap?
A) Calcaneal
B) Lateral femoral
C) Medial plantar
D) Superficial peroneal
E) Sural
questions.answer:
C)
The medial plantar nerve supplies sensation to the medial plantar artery flap from the instep region. This sensate flap utilizes tissue from the non-weight-bearing medial instep area and can be transposed to cover heel defects while preserving sensation through incorporation of a medial plantar nerve branch. The flap provides durable plantar skin suitable for weight-bearing reconstruction. A) is incorrect because the calcaneal nerve supplies native heel sensation, not the instep donor site. B) is incorrect because the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve innervates the anterolateral thigh, not the foot. D) is incorrect because the superficial peroneal nerve provides motor function to lateral leg muscles, not sensory innervation to the instep. E) is incorrect because the sural nerve supplies sensation to the lateral foot, not the medial instep region.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old male presents to the clinic with recurring and locally invasive rectal carcinoma occurring 2 years following low anterior resection with adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy. A surgical resection encompassing the external perianal tissue, anal canal, rectum, and pelvic floor musculature is carried out. Which of the following represents the most suitable approach for perineal reconstruction in this case?
A) Gracilis flap
B) Local propeller flap
C) Omental flap
D) Rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap
E) Rectus femoris flap
questions.answer:
D)
The vertical rectus abdominis myocutaneous (VRAM) flap is the most evidence-based reconstruction method for this clinical scenario. This patient requires reconstruction of a large composite defect following extensive resection, and the VRAM flap provides both substantial tissue volume and a reliable cutaneous component necessary for such defects. A) Gracilis flaps are incorrect because they provide insufficient volume for large defects, though bilateral gracilis flaps may suffice for moderate-sized defects. B) Local propeller flaps are incorrect due to the high risk of wound healing complications in previously irradiated tissue. C) Omental flaps are incorrect as they are better suited for smaller defects primarily involving internal structures rather than large composite defects requiring cutaneous coverage. E) Rectus femoris flaps are incorrect as they are not the standard of care for perineal reconstruction and lack the proven reliability of VRAM flaps for this indication.

questions.question:
What represents the most frequent histological change observed in skin following tretinoin therapy?
A) Reduced blood vessel formation
B) Decreased mucin content
C) Enhanced collagen production
D) Elevated melanin levels
E) Epidermal atrophy
questions.answer:
C)
Tretinoin therapy primarily results in enhanced collagen production, which is the most characteristic histological finding. Retinoids penetrate cells through non-receptor-mediated endocytosis and are transported to the nucleus by cellular retinoic acid-binding proteins. They bind to retinoic acid receptors and retinoid X receptors, forming complexes that interact with promoter genes at retinoid response elements, leading to protein synthesis responsible for the observed histological changes. In photodamaged skin, tretinoin increases collagen types I, III, and VII, improves collagen organization, enhances elastic tissue arrangement, causes epidermal thickening, increases mucin deposition, and reduces melanin content. A) is incorrect because tretinoin actually promotes angiogenesis rather than reducing it. B) is incorrect because tretinoin increases mucin deposition in both epidermis and dermis. D) is incorrect because tretinoin decreases melanin content, helping correct pigmentation irregularities. E) is incorrect because tretinoin causes epidermal hyperplasia, not thinning.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female presents to the clinic seeking advice about mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction due to recurring right breast cancer. She previously received breast-conserving surgery and radiotherapy 5 years prior. Her BMI is 23 kg/m2. The patient has no other medical issues and is a non-smoker. Physical examination reveals a soft breast with evident radiation fibrosis. Which of the following reconstruction options carries the greatest risk of failure in this patient?
A) Deep inferior epigastric artery perforator (DIEP) flap
B) Free transverse rectus abdominis musculocutaneous (TRAM) flap
C) Latissimus flap with prosthesis
D) Pedicled TRAM flap
E) Tissue expander and prosthesis
questions.answer:
E)
Tissue expander and prosthesis reconstruction has the highest failure rate in previously irradiated patients, with complication rates reaching up to 70% and failure or conversion to flap reconstruction occurring in 40% of cases. The prior radiation therapy creates a hostile environment with compromised tissue quality, poor vascularity, and increased fibrosis, making implant-based reconstruction particularly challenging. A) DIEP flap is incorrect because autologous tissue reconstructions like DIEP flaps generally perform better in irradiated fields due to their own blood supply. B) Free TRAM flap is incorrect as free tissue transfers typically have lower failure rates in radiated patients compared to implant-based methods. C) Latissimus flap with prosthesis is incorrect because while it involves an implant, the addition of well-vascularized muscle coverage improves outcomes compared to tissue expander/prosthesis alone. D) Pedicled TRAM flap is incorrect as this autologous reconstruction option generally has better success rates than implant-based reconstruction in previously irradiated patients.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old male presents to the emergency room following trauma to his right eye. Physical examination reveals sunken eye appearance, blood in the anterior chamber, and loss of sensation across the cheek area. Visual field defects are absent. Imaging demonstrates a significant break in the orbital floor with tissue prolapse into the maxillary cavity. Which of the following clinical findings demands immediate intervention?
A) Loss of cheek sensation
B) Sunken eye appearance
C) Blood in anterior chamber
D) Maxillary cavity inflammation
E) Break in orbital floor
questions.answer:
C)
Blood in the anterior chamber represents an ophthalmologic emergency that requires immediate treatment to prevent irreversible vision loss and elevated intraocular pressure complications. A) is incorrect because sensory loss from infraorbital nerve damage, while concerning, is not immediately sight-threatening. B) is incorrect because sunken eye appearance from fat pad herniation can be managed on a delayed basis. D) is incorrect because sinus inflammation is a secondary concern that does not require urgent intervention. E) is incorrect because orbital floor reconstruction can typically be performed within days to weeks without compromising outcomes.

questions.question:
Which virus among the following is associated with the development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
A) EBV
B) HCV
C) HHV8
D) HIV
E) HPV
questions.answer:
A)
Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is strongly linked to nasopharyngeal carcinoma development. All stages of EBV's lifecycle contribute to human pathology. In patients with compromised immune systems, EBV-infected cells proliferate and eventually trigger B-cell growth control mechanisms, resulting in cellular transformation that leads to various malignancies including nasopharyngeal carcinoma, Burkitt lymphoma, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorders, and gastric cancers. B) is incorrect because while HCV has been associated with oral verrucous and squamous cell carcinomas and is more common in oral lichen planus patients, it is not linked to nasopharyngeal carcinoma. C) is incorrect because HHV8 (Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus) is specifically associated with Kaposi sarcoma, not nasopharyngeal carcinoma. D) is incorrect because HIV does not directly cause malignant transformation but rather increases susceptibility to opportunistic infections and viral-induced cancers. E) is incorrect because HPV is primarily associated with oropharyngeal cancers, not nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

questions.question:
A 21-month-old boy requires reconstruction of a 12-cm² skull defect following cranial vault remodeling surgery. Which material would be most suitable for cranioplasty in this child?
A) Bone dust
B) Hydroxyapatite
C) Particulate bone
D) Split calvarium
E) Split rib
questions.answer:
C)

Particulate bone is the most appropriate choice for cranioplasty in this young patient. Autogenous bone remains the gold standard for cranial reconstruction because it provides osteogenic, osteoinductive, and osteoconductive properties, leading to rapid osseointegration and resulting in tissue with native bone characteristics including strength, growth potential, stability, and infection resistance. Particulate cranial bone graft, consisting of small bone fragments harvested using a low-speed hand-driven bit, can be obtained at any age and has demonstrated equivalent effectiveness to split calvarial grafts in both animal studies and clinical practice for repairing full-thickness cranial defects.

A) Bone dust is incorrect because this powdered bone material from high-speed burr use is ineffective and undergoes resorption when used for cranioplasty, likely due to smaller particle size and thermal damage during collection. B) Hydroxyapatite is incorrect because while synthetic materials have been used in pediatric cranial reconstruction, they lack the biological advantages of autogenous bone and do not provide the same integration and growth potential. D) Split calvarium is incorrect because calvarial bone cannot be effectively split until the diploic space develops, typically after age 4 years, making this technique unsuitable for a 21-month-old patient. E) Split rib is incorrect because extracranial autologous bone sources provide insufficient volume in toddlers, have higher resorption rates compared to cranial bone, and cause additional donor site morbidity.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female presents to your clinic with her partner seeking consultation for breast augmentation surgery. She currently wears a 34B bra and desires to increase to a D cup size. She reports being content with her appearance when clothed, but her partner expresses wanting to see more cleavage when she wears swimwear. Her medical history reveals liposuction of her outer thighs performed 6 months prior by a dermatologist with satisfactory results. She has also received botulinum toxin injections to her forehead area three times within the past year. What is the most compelling reason to decline performing this procedure on this patient?
A) The patient may be coerced into the surgery
B) The patient may be addicted to cosmetic procedures
C) The patient may suffer from body dysmorphic disorder
D) The patient may have an underlying personality disorder
E) The patient may hold unreasonable outcome expectations
questions.answer:
A)
The most appropriate reason to refuse surgery is that the patient may be coerced into the procedure. When a partner or family member is the primary driving force behind a patient's desire for cosmetic surgery rather than the patient's own motivation, this represents a significant red flag. Patients who are pressured by others into aesthetic procedures often experience poor psychological outcomes and dissatisfaction regardless of surgical results. A is correct because external pressure from her boyfriend is the primary concern here. B is incorrect because having two previous minor aesthetic procedures does not constitute surgical addiction. C is incorrect because there are no signs of distorted body image or obsessive focus on perceived flaws. D is incorrect because no specific personality disorder symptoms are evident from the presentation. E is incorrect because her expectations appear realistic - she simply wants to increase her cup size by two sizes.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female patient presents with severe breast ptosis (Grade 3) and is planning to have breast augmentation combined with a breast lift. Which surgical approach below would most likely result in complications or poor outcomes?
A) Breast augmentation combined with a vertical lift technique
B) Breast augmentation combined with an anchor-pattern lift technique
C) Breast lift with insertion of 450-mL saline implants using dual-plane positioning
D) Breast lift with insertion of 200-mL silicone implants in a submuscular position
E) Completing the surgery in two separate procedures
questions.answer:
C)

Combining breast augmentation with mastopexy creates competing surgical goals that can compromise outcomes, particularly when large implants are used. The 450-mL saline prostheses represent a large volume that significantly compromises blood supply to the breast tissues and skin flaps created during the lift procedure. Large implants (generally considered >350 mL) place excessive tension on the surgical closure, increase risk of wound healing problems, nipple-areola complex necrosis, implant exposure, and infection. The substantial volume also counteracts the tissue tightening achieved by the lift, leading to long-term complications like tissue stretching, thinning, rippling, and recurrent sagging. A) is incorrect because vertical mastopexy is an established technique suitable for Grade 3 ptosis when combined with appropriately sized implants. B) is incorrect because the Wise-pattern (anchor) technique is also a well-accepted approach for severe ptosis cases. D) is incorrect because 200-mL implants are considered modest in size and less likely to compromise tissue vascularity or cause long-term stretching problems. E) is incorrect because staged procedures actually reduce complications by allowing better control of results and healing between operations.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female patient visits the clinic for botulinum toxin type A treatment of her corrugator and procerus muscles. One week following the procedure, she returns distressed about drooping of both upper eyelids. Clinical evaluation reveals bilateral ptosis. What is the most suitable intervention to ameliorate this patient's symptoms while awaiting resolution of the botulinum toxin type A effects?
A) Apraclonidine
B) Artificial tears
C) Botulinum toxin type A to the lateral orbicularis oculi
D) Ophthalmic tobramycin and dexamethasone
E) Tetracaine
questions.answer:
A)
This patient has developed eyelid ptosis due to botulinum toxin type A inadvertently affecting the levator palpebrae superioris muscle. Apraclonidine, an alpha-adrenergic agonist, stimulates the Müller muscle (located beneath the levator) to contract, potentially lifting the eyelid 1-3 mm and reducing ptosis severity until natural levator function returns. The typical dosing is 1-2 drops three times daily until resolution. B) is incorrect because artificial tears only provide lubrication and have no effect on muscle function or ptosis. C) is incorrect because additional botulinum toxin injections would worsen the muscle paralysis rather than improve ptosis. D) is incorrect because this antibiotic-steroid combination treats infection and inflammation but has no impact on eyelid position or muscle function. E) is incorrect because tetracaine is a topical anesthetic used for corneal numbing and does not affect eyelid muscles or ptosis.

questions.question:
A 2-day-old male infant is being assessed in the NICU due to facial abnormalities and respiratory distress. The baby was delivered at full term after a normal pregnancy and birth. He shows appropriate responses to stimuli. Physical examination reveals a small lower jaw, posterior displacement of the tongue, and an opening in the roof of the mouth. The baby shows signs of labored breathing with chest wall retractions. Oxygen saturation measurement indicates 92%. What is the most suitable first-line treatment approach?
A) Three-dimensional CT imaging of the skull
B) Bronchoscopic airway assessment
C) Placing the infant face-down
D) Surgical attachment of tongue to lip
E) Creation of a breathing opening in the neck
questions.answer:
C)
This infant presents with Pierre Robin sequence, characterized by mandibular hypoplasia and tongue displacement, often accompanied by cleft palate. The primary concern is airway management due to obstruction caused by the relatively large tongue in the context of the underdeveloped jaw. Prone positioning allows gravity to pull the tongue and mandible forward, often resolving the airway compromise and is the safest initial intervention. A) is incorrect because imaging is not the immediate priority when airway obstruction is present. B) is incorrect because endoscopic evaluation, while potentially useful later, is not the first-line management for acute airway issues in Pierre Robin sequence. D) is incorrect because tongue-lip adhesion is a surgical procedure reserved for cases where conservative positioning fails. E) is incorrect because tracheostomy is only considered when other measures fail or when additional lower airway abnormalities are present.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents for body contouring consultation 2 years following bariatric gastric bypass surgery. She has achieved a weight reduction of 120 lb (54 kg) since her initial procedure. Her height is 5 ft 5 in (165 cm), and her weight has remained steady at 160 lb (72 kg) for the past 11 months. The patient wishes to minimize the number of surgical stages required. A combined lower body lift with bilateral mastopexy is planned as a single-stage procedure. What postoperative complication is most likely to develop in this patient?
A) Wound dehiscence
B) Hematoma formation
C) Surgical site infection
D) Pulmonary thromboembolism
E) Seroma development
questions.answer:
A)
Wound dehiscence is the most frequent complication following combined body contouring procedures performed in a single stage, occurring in approximately 15% of cases due to the extensive nature of the surgery and healing challenges in post-bariatric patients. B is incorrect because hematoma formation occurs in less than 5% of cases. C is incorrect because surgical site infection rates are below 5% in these procedures. D is incorrect because pulmonary thromboembolism occurs in fewer than 5% of patients. E is incorrect because while seroma is the second most common complication, it occurs in only about 10% of cases, making it less likely than dehiscence.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient has a 4 x 4-cm oval-shaped tissue loss on the top of her head following removal of a sebaceous cyst. Local tissue rearrangement flaps with extensive tissue release are being considered for reconstruction. Incision of which anatomical layer below is crucial for successful scalp flap mobilization?
A) Dermal layer
B) Epicranial aponeurosis
C) Subaponeurotic fascia
D) Periosteal layer
E) Loose areolar tissue
questions.answer:
B)
The epicranial aponeurosis must be divided because this fibrous layer creates the primary resistance to scalp tissue advancement. Surgeons commonly perform parallel scoring of this aponeurotic layer at 1-cm spacing to achieve sufficient tissue release. The scalp anatomy consists of five layers: skin, subcutaneous connective tissue, epicranial/galeal aponeurosis, loose connective tissue, and periosteum. Dividing the other listed structures is ineffective since they do not contribute significant resistance to flap advancement. A is incorrect because the dermis does not limit scalp mobility. C is incorrect because the subaponeurotic fascia (loose areolar layer) provides minimal resistance. D is incorrect because the periosteal layer does not restrict scalp advancement. E is incorrect because loose areolar tissue offers no appreciable resistance to flap movement.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient presents with a 1.25-cm alar rim defect following Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell carcinoma. The defect involves both skin and cartilage. What is the most suitable reconstructive approach?
A) Composite grafting
B) Full-thickness skin grafting
C) Healing by secondary intention
D) Primary closure
E) Use of an alar advancement rotation flap
questions.answer:
A)
Composite grafting is the most appropriate reconstruction method for this 1.25-cm alar rim defect involving both skin and cartilage. For alar rim defects measuring 1 to 1.5 cm, composite grafts provide the best option as they can address both the skin and cartilage components of the three-dimensional defect. B) Full-thickness skin grafting is incorrect because it cannot reconstruct the three-dimensional structure and fails to address the cartilage loss. C) Healing by secondary intention is incorrect because it is only suitable for defects smaller than 0.25 cm and not located near the rim. D) Primary closure is incorrect because it can only be used for very small defects (less than 0.25 cm) away from the rim area. E) Alar advancement rotation flap is incorrect because it is typically reserved for smaller defects (less than 1 cm) and would be inadequate for a defect of this size.

questions.question:
An 8-month-old male infant is evaluated for a lip mass. A photograph is shown. Treatment with propranolol is initiated. Which of the following adverse effects is most important to monitor?


A) Drooling
B) Hypertension
C) Hypoglycemia
D) Lethargy
E) Tachycardia
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Vascular anomalies are a common source of pediatric morbidity, potentially resulting in cosmetic and functional abnormalities. Two main categories of lesions are hemangiomas and vascular malformations. Vascular malformations are generally named after the vessel types that are involved and are further subdivided into low-flow and high-flow lesions. Low-flow lesions include capillary, lymphatic, venous, and mixed lesions. High-flow lesions include arteriovenous malformations. Both high- and low-flow vascular malformations are almost always present at birth and either grow commensurately with the child or slowly enlarge over a period of years.


Treatment is guided by the degree of functional impairment, and many require surgical therapy.


Hemangiomas are rarely present at birth. They tend to appear between 2 and 8 weeks of life and grow rapidly. These lesions comprise of rapidly proliferating endothelial cells and follow a predictable clinical course. They usually undergo an aggressive proliferative phase that lasts several months before reaching a plateau phase, when they grow very little. Finally, at about 1 year of life, hemangiomas begin a process of spontaneous involution which may last for up to 4 years. Completion of involution does not mean complete involution, and many hemangiomas may leave cosmetically unacceptable residua. Hemangiomas found in inconspicuous areas can be observed. Those noted in cosmetically or functionally sensitive areas require more aggressive treatment. Treatment options have included topical, intralesional, and systemic corticosteroids, laser treatment, interferon-alfa, and surgical resection. However, each of these treatments carries marked risks and still does not provide consistent, reliable success.


In June 2008, a French group reported rapid resolution of hemangiomas in children treated with propranolol for pediatric cardiomyopathy. This serendipitous finding led to a landmark paper and has resulted in a paradigm shift in the clinical care of these patients. Many groups have now confirmed their findings with very promising results. The use of propranolol for hemangiomas remains off-label, but there are centers of excellence with institutional review board protocols in place to further study its clinical effects. Recommended doses vary but frequently start at 0.5 mg/kg/day divided three times daily and slowly titrated over 1 to 2 weeks to 2 mg/kg/day. Most centers recommend obtaining pretreatment electrocardiography (ECG); if normal, then therapy can be initiated on an outpatient basis. If the ECG is abnormal, then pretreatment cardiology evaluation is warranted. Dose titration, blood pressure, and heart rate are checked regularly. The most common adverse effect is lethargy. Other adverse effects include hypoglycemia, hypotension, and bradycardia. All children drool, and this has not been reported as a complication of propranolol administration. Hypoglycemia can be a potentially life-threatening complication that can also cause seizures. Parents are counseled to give food with medication. Many centers regularly check blood glucose.


An image of a child with upper lip hemangioma treated with propranolol for 14 months is shown.






References
1. Mulliken JB, Glowacki J. Hemangiomas and vascular malformations in infants and children: a classification based on endothelial characteristics. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1982 Mar;69(3):412-422.
2. L√©aut√©-Labr√®ze C, Dumas de la Roque E, Hubiche T, et al. Propranolol for severe hemangiomas of infancy. N Engl J Med. 2008 Jun 12;358(24):2649-2651.

questions.question:
Which viral pathogen is associated with the development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
A) Epstein-Barr virus
B) Hepatitis C virus
C) Human herpesvirus 8
D) Human immunodeficiency virus
E) Human papillomavirus
questions.answer:
A)
Epstein-Barr virus is strongly linked to nasopharyngeal carcinoma development. The virus disrupts B-cell growth control mechanisms in immunocompromised patients, leading to cellular transformation and various malignancies including nasopharyngeal carcinoma, Burkitt lymphoma, post-transplant lymphomas, and gastric carcinomas. B) is incorrect because hepatitis C virus is associated with oral verrucous and squamous cell carcinomas, not nasopharyngeal carcinoma. C) is incorrect because human herpesvirus 8 (Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus) is primarily linked to Kaposi sarcoma tumors. D) is incorrect because HIV does not directly cause malignant transformation but rather increases susceptibility to opportunistic infections and viral-induced cancers. E) is incorrect because human papillomavirus is primarily associated with oropharyngeal cancers, not nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old woman presents 2 months postpartum with complaints of right breast pain, swelling, and asymmetry. Her history is significant for breast augmentation surgery performed 4 years prior. She reports no fever or chills and discontinued breastfeeding 1 month ago. On examination, the right breast appears markedly enlarged compared to the left. A healed periareolar surgical scar is visible with no signs of active infection. Ultrasonography reveals a complex cystic lesion from which 150 cc of milk-like fluid is aspirated and a drainage tube is inserted. What medication should be prescribed as the most appropriate next intervention?
A) Bromocriptine
B) Cephalexin
C) Fluconazole
D) Prolactin
E) Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
questions.answer:
A)
This patient has developed a galactocele, which is a benign milk-containing cyst that commonly occurs in lactating or recently lactating women. Bromocriptine is the correct treatment as it acts as a dopamine receptor agonist that suppresses prolactin release, thereby reducing milk production and helping resolve the galactocele. The periareolar incision from her previous augmentation may have contributed to ductal obstruction leading to this condition. B) Cephalexin is incorrect because this antibiotic is not needed since there are no clinical signs of bacterial infection. C) Fluconazole is incorrect as this antifungal medication has no role in treating galactoceles. D) Prolactin is incorrect because administering this hormone would actually increase milk production and worsen the patient's condition. E) Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is incorrect as this antibiotic is unnecessary given the absence of infectious symptoms.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a motorcycle accident with a grade IIIB open fracture of the right distal tibia and fibula. Following initial debridement and external fixation, plastic surgery consultation is obtained. Physical examination reveals a 10-cm open medial ankle wound with complete tibial nerve transection. The tibial fracture shows comminution but minimal bone loss. The foot maintains good perfusion with single-vessel runoff via the anterior tibial artery. What is the most appropriate treatment approach for this patient?
A) Debridement and free muscle flap reconstruction without nerve repair
B) Debridement, tibial nerve reconstruction, and coverage using bilaminar acellular dermal regeneration template
C) Debridement, tibial nerve reconstruction, and coverage using free fasciocutaneous flap
D) Debridement, tibial nerve reconstruction, and coverage using pedicled reverse sural fasciocutaneous flap
E) Primary below-knee amputation
questions.answer:
C)
Debridement with tibial nerve reconstruction and coverage using a free fasciocutaneous flap represents the optimal treatment approach. While historically an insensate plantar foot was considered grounds for amputation, current evidence demonstrates that tibial nerve injury alone should not preclude limb salvage attempts when repair is feasible. Research shows comparable long-term outcomes between limb salvage and primary amputation, with approximately 50% of patients recovering plantar sensation within two years following tibial nerve repair. The wound size and location make it ideally suited for microvascular free flap coverage, which provides excellent soft-tissue reconstruction with minimal donor site morbidity and superior outcomes for potential future procedures like bone grafting or hardware revision. A) is incorrect because nerve repair should be attempted given the potential for sensory recovery in half of patients. B) is incorrect because bilaminar templates are better suited for smaller wounds, and this large defect over a major nerve repair and comminuted fracture requires more robust coverage. D) is incorrect because the reverse sural flap's pedicle lies within the zone of injury where the peroneal artery was damaged, making it unreliable. E) is incorrect because current evidence supports limb salvage attempts in cases with isolated tibial nerve injury when other factors favor reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female patient seeks body contouring procedures following childbirth. Her BMI is 34 kg/m2. When performed simultaneously with tummy tuck surgery, liposuction of which anatomical region carries the highest risk for impaired wound healing?
A) Flank region
B) Lateral hip area
C) Lateral thigh region
D) Mons pubis area
E) Upper abdominal region above the umbilicus
questions.answer:
E)
The upper abdominal region above the umbilicus is correct because this area's vascular supply is already compromised by the extensive tissue undermining performed during abdominoplasty, making additional liposuction particularly risky for wound healing complications. A) Flank region is incorrect because its blood supply remains largely intact during abdominoplasty procedures. B) Lateral hip area is incorrect as this region's vascular network is not significantly disrupted by tummy tuck undermining. C) Lateral thigh region is incorrect since its circulation is independent of the abdominal surgical field. D) Mons pubis area is incorrect because while adjacent to the surgical site, its blood supply is generally preserved during standard abdominoplasty techniques.

questions.question:
A 67-year-old female presents to the clinic for assessment of facial abscesses occurring 5 weeks following autologous fat transfer for cheek enhancement. Clinical examination reveals numerous red nodules, areas of tissue hardening, and small abscesses on bilateral cheeks. Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C). The liposuction harvest sites appear normal. A 1-week treatment with ciprofloxacin from her primary care physician did not improve the condition. Gram staining and standard bacterial culture with antibiotic sensitivity testing show no growth. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Atypical mycobacterial infection
B) Herpes zoster infection
C) MRSA infection
D) Mucocutaneous candidiasis
E) Staphylococcus epidermidis infection
questions.answer:
A)
Atypical mycobacterial infection is the most likely diagnosis. Nontuberculous mycobacteria are commonly found in environmental sources like soil and water, and can cause complications following cosmetic liposuction and fat grafting procedures. These infections typically present with cellulitis, abscess formation, draining wounds, and postoperative infections. Patients frequently lack fever, chills, or systemic symptoms. Even immunocompetent individuals can develop these infections. More than half of cases will have negative acid-fast bacilli tests and negative routine cultures, making diagnosis challenging. PCR testing is now available for common nontuberculous mycobacterial species and serves as an effective rapid screening tool. B is incorrect because herpes zoster typically presents with painful fluid-filled vesicles earlier in the postoperative period. C is incorrect because MRSA infections usually appear sooner after surgery, cause systemic symptoms, and grow readily on standard cultures. D is incorrect because mucocutaneous candidiasis is a chronic condition affecting skin, nails, and mucous membranes, not typically associated with surgical procedures. E is incorrect because while S. epidermidis can cause biofilm infections, there is no history of previous fillers or implants to suggest this etiology.

questions.question:
A 9-month-old child presents for assessment of webbed fingers. In which of the following conditions would surgical correction be most strongly discouraged?
A) Complicated finger fusion associated with amniotic band sequence
B) Complicated finger fusion associated with Poland anomaly
C) Thumb web fusion associated with Apert syndrome
D) Uncomplicated fusion of fourth and fifth fingers
E) Finger webbing associated with Type I supernumerary digit
questions.answer:
E)
The correct answer is E because supernumerary digits represent a contraindication to web release surgery. These extra digits typically develop complications such as overgrowth and stunted development as they mature, making successful reconstruction into normally functioning digits unlikely. A is incorrect because constriction band syndrome, while potentially complex, can often be surgically addressed depending on severity. B is incorrect because Poland syndrome-associated syndactyly, despite accompanying hypoplasia, is not typically considered a contraindication to surgical intervention. C is incorrect because first web syndactyly in Apert syndrome, while challenging, is generally amenable to surgical correction. D is incorrect because simple syndactyly between the ring and little fingers is typically straightforward to surgically separate and represents an ideal candidate for intervention.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old man presents with the rapidly growing, painful dorsal hand lesion shown in the photographs. It is not fixed to the underlying structures and the tendon and bone are not involved. He is a kidney transplant recipient and has been on immunosuppression for the past 10 years. Eighteen months ago, he was treated for a previous squamous cell carcinoma on the contralateral hand. Which of the following are the most appropriate surgical margins and depth of excision for this lesion?


A) 1-cm peripheral margins, excision to the deep dermal level
B) 1-cm peripheral margins, excision to the deep subcutaneous level
C) 1-mm peripheral margins, excision to the deep dermal level
D) 1-mm peripheral margins, excision to the deep subcutaneous level
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


Squamous cell carcinoma that arises in immunocompromised patients tends to behave more aggressively than tumors in immunocompetent patients. Resection with at least 6-mm margins (some recommend up to 10-mm margins), extending into the subcutaneous tissue, is recommended. Cure rates with Mohs surgery and with frozen section margin control are similar to those for wide local excision.

One-mm surgical margins are too narrow for squamous cell carcinoma, and would lead to a high rate of reoperations for positive microscopic margins. Furthermore, the entire dermis must be completely excised, along with at least part of the subcutaneous tissue, as lesions like this are likely to penetrate to that depth.


ReferencesHepper DM, Hepper CT, Anadkat M. Treatment options for squamous cell carcinoma of the dorsal hand including Mohs micrographic surgery. J Hand Surg Am. 2009;34(7):1337-1339.Martin DE, English JC III, Goitz RJ. Squamous cell carcinoma of the hand. J Hand Surg Am. 2011;36(8):1377-1381;quiz 1382.Webber T, Wolf JM. Squamous cell carcinoma of the hand in solid organ transplant patients. J Hand Surg Am. 2014;39(3):567-570.Nahhas AF, Scarbrough CA, Trotter S. A Review of the Global Guidelines on Surgical Margins for Nonmelanoma Skin Cancers. J Clin Aesthet Dermatol. 2017;10(4):37?46.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents for breast augmentation consultation. She currently wears a 32B bra; her height is 5 ft 3 in (160 cm) and weight is 130 lb (59 kg). Subglandular placement of saline implants is being considered. What is the main benefit of choosing saline over silicone implants for this patient?
A) More straightforward rupture identification
B) Reduced capsule development
C) Decreased rippling
D) Lower implant weight
E) Reduced leakage probability
questions.answer:
A)
Saline and silicone implants have comparable rupture rates, but saline ruptures are much more readily identified since the saline gets absorbed by the body, resulting in noticeable breast volume reduction. In contrast, silicone ruptures may only present with subtle signs like diminished upper breast fullness or increased softness on examination, often requiring ultrasound or MRI for confirmation. B is incorrect because both implant types produce similar rates of capsular contracture. C is incorrect because saline implants actually have a higher tendency for visible wrinkling compared to silicone. D is incorrect because weight differences between the two implant types are minimal and not clinically significant. E is incorrect because both implant types have similar leakage rates over time.

questions.question:
A healthy 38-year-old female patient with a BMI of 34 kg/m2 is planned for tumescent liposuction of the abdomen, hips, and thighs with an anticipated 5000-mL aspirate volume. The infiltration solution includes lidocaine and epinephrine. Which of the following modifications to the surgical plan would be most suitable for reducing intraoperative complication risk?
A) Reducing the infiltration rate of the wetting solution
B) Simultaneous infiltration of all treatment areas
C) Eliminating epinephrine from the infiltration solution
D) Replacing lidocaine with bupivacaine
E) Utilizing a superwet technique rather than tumescent
questions.answer:
E)
The superwet technique is the most appropriate modification for large-volume liposuction cases to reduce lidocaine toxicity risk. The superwet technique uses a 1:1 ratio of infiltrate to lipoaspirate compared to the tumescent technique's 3:1 ratio, significantly reducing the total lidocaine dose administered while maintaining surgical efficacy. A is incorrect because infiltration rate does not affect lidocaine absorption kinetics. B is incorrect because simultaneous infiltration of multiple areas increases total lidocaine exposure and is counterproductive for safety. C is incorrect because epinephrine is essential for vasoconstriction, improved hemostasis, delayed anesthetic absorption, and reduced lidocaine toxicity risk. D is incorrect because bupivacaine has not been adequately studied in wetting solutions and poses greater risks due to slower elimination and potential for severe cardiovascular, neurologic, and hematologic complications.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female patient is planning to have a transcutaneous lower lid blepharoplasty procedure for age-related periorbital changes. What is the most probable complication at 3 months following surgery?
A) Conjunctival swelling
B) Surgical site infection
C) Tear duct malfunction
D) Inability to close eyelids completely
E) Abnormal lower eyelid positioning
questions.answer:
E)
Abnormal lower eyelid positioning is the most frequent complication after lower blepharoplasty surgery. This malposition can vary from subtle scleral exposure to significant scarring-induced ectropion. The condition develops due to excessive downward tension on the eyelid caused by factors such as excessive scar formation, removal of too much skin, orbital septum folding, muscle weakness, swelling, and bleeding. Risk factors that should be assessed before surgery include underdeveloped cheekbones, protruding eyes, severe nearsightedness, loose lower eyelid support, and thyroid eye disease. Mild cases with slight scleral show may improve with massage and eye drops, while severe ectropion cases might need scar removal, skin grafts, or eyelid tightening procedures like canthoplasty. A is incorrect because conjunctival swelling typically resolves within 6 weeks postoperatively. B is incorrect because surgical site infections are uncommon due to the excellent blood supply to the eyelid area. C is incorrect because tear duct problems are rare and usually resolve spontaneously without surgical treatment. D is incorrect because incomplete eyelid closure primarily occurs after upper blepharoplasty and is typically temporary, improving with lubrication and massage.

questions.question:
A cosmetic surgeon encounters a woman at a charity gala who inquires about having a tummy tuck operation, and they engage in a detailed conversation about the procedure. The woman later contacts the clinic to schedule a consultation. Upon her visit, she provides a comprehensive medical history to the nursing staff and undergoes evaluation by the cosmetic surgeon. The surgery is arranged and completed three weeks thereafter. At what point in this sequence was a physician-patient relationship formed?
A) During the conversation at the charity event
B) When the woman scheduled her consultation
C) When the nursing staff documented her medical history
D) When the cosmetic surgeon conducted the evaluation
E) When the surgery was completed
questions.answer:
A)
The physician-patient relationship was established during the charity event conversation when specific medical advice was provided. Professional negligence requires four components: an existing obligation (duty owed), failure to meet that obligation (duty breached), a connection between the failure and harm (causation), and resulting patient harm (damages). The duty component arises once the doctor-patient relationship begins. Simply holding a medical license does not create an automatic obligation to treat everyone. This professional relationship forms when a physician engages in professional contact with a patient, which can occur without physical examination. Any individual under the physician's supervision and authority can also establish this relationship on behalf of the doctor. When the surgeon offered specific medical guidance at the event, a doctor-patient relationship was created. B) is incorrect because the relationship was already formed before the appointment was made. C) is incorrect because the nurse taking history occurred after the relationship was established. D) is incorrect because the physical examination happened subsequent to the relationship formation. E) is incorrect because performing the procedure occurred well after the relationship was already in place.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old female presents to the clinic with a small portion of titanium protruding through the skin over her sacral region 12 months following successful posterior spinal fusion with autologous bone grafting for myelodysplasia and lumbosacral kyphotic deformity. On examination, there is a midline surgical scar with a 2 × 2-cm defect at the L4 vertebral level showing an exposed screw. What is the most appropriate initial management?
A) Bilateral advancement flaps of skin
B) Free rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap
C) Gluteus maximus myocutaneous flap
D) Vacuum-assisted closure therapy followed by skin grafting
E) Hardware extraction
questions.answer:
E)
Hardware extraction is the most appropriate initial management for this exposed titanium implant. The titanium rod or screw has likely become loose and migrated to protrude through the skin. At 12 months post-procedure, the spinal fusion is adequately consolidated. Orthopedic consultation should be obtained for hardware removal, after which the wound can be managed with delayed primary closure or secondary healing. A) is incorrect because bilateral skin advancement flaps will ultimately fail as the rigid hardware will re-extrude through any soft tissue coverage. B) is incorrect because a free rectus abdominis flap, while providing vascularized coverage, cannot withstand the mechanical forces from the protruding hardware. C) is incorrect because gluteus maximus muscle flaps will also fail due to the superior strength of the titanium hardware compared to soft tissue. D) is incorrect because negative pressure therapy and skin grafting do not address the underlying cause of hardware malposition and will result in recurrent exposure.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old man who works as a pipe fitter sustains amputation of the radial three digits of the nondominant left hand. Replantation of the thumb and long finger is performed. Three weeks later, the replanted thumb becomes necrotic. Photographs are shown. Which of the following methods of reconstruction is most likely to provide the best functional outcome? 


A ) Amputation and web space deepening 
B ) Debridement and coverage with a radial forearm flap 
C ) Distraction lengthening of the remaining thumb
D ) Pollicization of the long finger
E ) Toe-to-thumb transfer
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


Toe-to-thumb transfer has become the standard of care for thumb reconstruction when the level of loss occurs at or around the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint. The functional outcomes from the transfer are excellent and the donor defect, while not completely free from morbidity, is acceptable. Wound and nerve complications, such as neuroma, can be successfully managed through traditional techniques.


Revision amputation of the thumb in the patient described would be at or proximal to the MCP joint level. Even with web space deepening, there would be insufficient length of the thumb against which the other fingers could oppose.


Distraction lengthening requires a higher-quality skin envelope than exists in the patient described to tolerate the increased space that would be occupied by the thumb metacarpal. In addition, the only remaining mobile joint in this patient would be the carpometacarpal (CMC) joint. Also, the distal end of a thumb created by this technique would have poor sensation and poor durability.
