Debridement and coverage with a radial forearm flap would provide high-quality tissue that could even be made sensate with coaptation of the medial and lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerves to the digital nerve stumps. However, there would still be inadequate length of the thumb with this method.


Pollicization, while less commonly used in adult than in pediatric reconstruction, can still be useful when the level of amputation occurs at the CMC joint, or when the patient cannot tolerate or will not accept microsurgical transfer of a toe. Pollicization generally moves the index finger to the thumb position; pollicizing the long finger is technically very difficult to do because of the vascular pedicle. Given that the index finger is already lost in this patient, sacrifice of the long finger would leave only two mobile fingers on this hand.

questions.question:
A 44-year-old female presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of painful bluish discoloration beneath her nail. She describes excruciating pain when direct pressure is applied to the region, and immersion in cold water triggers intense discomfort. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Glomus tumor
B) Hemangioma
C) Hematoma
D) Melanoma
E) Pyogenic granuloma
questions.answer:
A)
Glomerus tumors account for roughly 1-5% of hand soft tissue neoplasms, with most occurring in the subungual location. These typically manifest as elevated blue or pink nodules that may cause nail discoloration or deformation. The Love's pin test, which involves applying pinpoint pressure to elicit severe pain, is characteristic. Diagnostic workup may include plain radiographs and MRI imaging. Complete surgical removal is the treatment of choice. B) Hemangioma is incorrect because it rarely causes the characteristic point tenderness and cold sensitivity seen with glomus tumors. C) Hematoma is incorrect because it would not typically produce the chronic pain pattern or positive cold water test. D) Melanoma is incorrect because while it can appear as subungual discoloration, it does not characteristically cause the exquisite point tenderness or cold sensitivity. E) Pyogenic granuloma is incorrect because it typically presents as a rapidly growing, friable lesion without the specific pain pattern of glomus tumors.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old female patient with abdominal and waist lipodystrophy is scheduled for suction-assisted lipectomy under general anesthesia. The surgeon expects to remove 1.5 L of lipoaspirate. Using the superwet technique, what volume of fluid will most likely be infiltrated into the subcutaneous tissue?
A) 0 mL
B) 375 mL
C) 750 mL
D) 1500 mL
E) 3000 mL
questions.answer:
D)
The superwet technique uses a 1:1 ratio of infiltration solution to expected lipoaspirate volume. Since 1.5 L of lipoaspirate is anticipated, 1500 mL of wetting solution would be infiltrated. This technique involves injecting saline or lactated Ringer's solution with epinephrine and lidocaine to improve hemostasis and provide anesthesia. A) is incorrect because 0 mL represents the dry technique with no infiltration. B) is incorrect because 375 mL corresponds to the wet technique, which uses a fixed volume of 200-300 mL per anatomic area regardless of expected aspirate. C) is incorrect because 750 mL doesn't correspond to any established wetting technique ratio. E) is incorrect because 3000 mL represents the tumescent technique, which uses a 2-3:1 ratio of solution to expected aspirate.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old male patient returns 2 years following extensive full-thickness thermal injuries to the front of his neck. He has previously received tissue expansion therapy and regional flap coverage for the burn wound. He reports banding and tightness at the edge of one of his previous flap repairs. Three matching 60-degree Z-plasty procedures are being considered across a combined distance of 12 cm. What is the anticipated increase in scar length?
A) 3 cm
B) 4 cm
C) 6 cm
D) 8 cm
E) 9 cm
questions.answer:
E)
A 60-degree Z-plasty increases scar length by 75%. With each Z-plasty spanning 4 cm of scar tissue, each procedure will add 3 cm of length, resulting in a total lengthening of 9 cm. A is incorrect because 3 cm represents the gain from only one Z-plasty, not all three. B is incorrect because 4 cm is the length each Z-plasty covers, not the gain achieved. C is incorrect because 6 cm would represent only a 50% increase (equivalent to a 45-degree Z-plasty). D is incorrect because 8 cm does not correspond to the 75% lengthening provided by 60-degree Z-plasties.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old male sustained an injury to his extended right wrist during a snowboarding accident 12 months prior. The injury pattern is visible in the posteroanterior radiograph of the right wrist provided. Given the presence of dorsal intercalated segment instability, what position would the lunate bone most likely demonstrate in relation to the surrounding carpal bones on a lateral wrist radiograph?
A) Lunate in normal position, scaphoid in extension
B) Lunate in extension, scaphoid in flexion
C) Lunate in flexion, scaphoid in extension
D) Lunate in flexion, triquetrum in normal position
E) Lunate in flexion, triquetrum in extension
questions.answer:
B)
The posteroanterior radiograph demonstrates static scapholunate dissociation with greater than 3 mm separation between the scaphoid and lunate bones. In dorsal intercalated segment instability (DISI), complete disruption of the scapholunate ligament and secondary stabilizers occurs. This results in the scaphoid falling into flexion and pronation, while the intact lunotriquetral ligament causes the triquetrum to pull the lunate into extension. The lunate's anatomical configuration with its narrower dorsal aspect and volar inclination of the radial joint surface contributes to this positioning. A is incorrect because the lunate is not in anatomical position in DISI - it extends abnormally. C is incorrect because in DISI the lunate extends rather than flexes, and the scaphoid flexes rather than extends. D is incorrect because the triquetrum is not in anatomical position but rather extends in DISI. E is incorrect because while both bones may be in abnormal positions, the lunate extends rather than flexes in DISI pattern.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old female patient presents to the clinic seeking advice regarding upper lip reconstruction one week following excision of an upper lip adnexal neoplasm with clear surgical margins. Physical examination reveals a central full-thickness upper lip defect involving 75% of the lip width. Which of the following represents the most suitable approach for functional reconstruction?
A) Abbe flap alone
B) Bilateral Estlander flaps combined with an Abbe flap
C) Bilateral Karapandzic flaps combined with an Abbe flap
D) Radial forearm flap alone
E) Radial forearm flap combined with a palmaris longus sling
questions.answer:
C)
The optimal reconstruction approach for this patient is bilateral Karapandzic flaps combined with a central Abbe flap for philtral restoration. Karapandzic flaps allow mobilization of the remaining upper lip tissue while preserving muscle innervation, unlike alternative techniques such as the Gilles flap. While bilateral Karapandzic flaps can address defects up to 80% of upper lip width, using them alone in this case would sacrifice the philtrum, creating a significant aesthetic deformity. Option A is incorrect because an Abbe flap alone cannot adequately close such an extensive 75% defect. Option B is incorrect because Estlander flaps are designed for commissural reconstruction rather than central defects. Options D and E are incorrect because radial forearm flaps, whether used alone or with palmaris sling reinforcement, provide suboptimal results due to poor color matching, lack of appropriate innervation, and inability to reconstruct the vermillion border effectively.

questions.question:
A 76-year-old female patient with rheumatoid arthritis presents to the clinic with a 2-month history of trouble bending her left index finger. She reports experiencing a painful clicking feeling when attempting to flex the digit. On examination, there is swelling of the flexor tendon at the A1 pulley location. What is the most suitable surgical intervention?
A) A1 pulley release only
B) A1 pulley release with stair-step pulley reconstruction
C) Complete excision of the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon
D) Rerouting the A1 pulley beneath the flexor tendons
E) Flexor tendon synovectomy and debridement
questions.answer:
E)
This patient's presentation is characteristic of trigger finger, which frequently occurs in rheumatoid arthritis patients due to intratendinous nodules and synovial inflammation. In rheumatoid arthritis patients, the A1 pulley serves as a crucial structure preventing ulnar drift of tendons and joints, so it should never be divided. The appropriate surgical treatment is flexor tenosynovectomy with removal of intratendinous nodules. A is incorrect because A1 pulley release would compromise joint stability in rheumatoid patients. B is incorrect because stair-step reconstruction is not an established treatment for this condition. C is incorrect because complete superficialis tendon removal is too aggressive as an initial surgical approach. D is incorrect because tendon rerouting is not a recognized treatment for trigger finger in rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.question:
The absence of which anatomical structure is the most defining feature of Poland syndrome?
A) Clavicular portion of the pectoralis major muscle
B) Ribs on the affected side
C) Pectoralis minor muscle
D) Serratus anterior muscle
E) Sternocostal portion of the pectoralis major muscle
questions.answer:
E)
The sternocostal portion of the pectoralis major muscle is characteristically absent in Poland syndrome, representing the most common and defining feature of this condition. This unilateral absence creates the typical chest wall deformity seen in patients with this syndrome. A) is incorrect because the clavicular head of the pectoralis major is typically preserved in Poland syndrome patients. B) is incorrect because rib absence may occur in complex cases but is not the most characteristic feature. C) is incorrect because pectoralis minor absence is variable and not the primary defining characteristic. D) is incorrect because serratus anterior involvement is inconsistent and not the hallmark feature of Poland syndrome.

questions.question:
A 44-year-old female presents with a 6-month history of right upper chest and back discomfort, occasional coldness in her right hand, and paresthesias affecting her right fourth and fifth digits. Physical examination reveals a diminished radial pulse on the right side during the Adson maneuver, and the Roos test elicits her symptoms on the affected side. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Ulnar nerve decompression at the cubital tunnel
B) Non-invasive vascular assessment and nerve conduction studies
C) Anterior and middle scalenectomy
D) First rib excision via transaxillary approach
E) Conservative management with observation
questions.answer:
B)
Non-invasive vascular assessment and nerve conduction studies represent the most appropriate initial step. Since thoracic outlet syndrome can manifest with both vascular and neurological symptoms, comprehensive diagnostic evaluation is essential before determining the optimal treatment approach. These studies will help characterize the extent of vascular compromise and nerve involvement, guiding subsequent management decisions.

A) is incorrect because isolated ulnar nerve decompression at the elbow would not address the thoracic outlet compression that is causing the patient's constellation of symptoms. B) is correct as diagnostic workup should precede surgical intervention. C) is incorrect because scalenectomy is a surgical treatment that should only be considered after proper diagnostic evaluation and failed conservative management. D) is incorrect because first rib resection is also a surgical option that requires prior diagnostic confirmation and conservative treatment failure. E) is incorrect because while conservative management may be appropriate eventually, diagnostic evaluation should be performed first to confirm the diagnosis and assess the severity of compression.

questions.question:
During a cranioplasty procedure on a 6-year-old patient, the plastic surgeon inadvertently allows the bone graft to fall onto the operating room floor. What is the most appropriate course of action?
A) Modify the wound classification from clean to dirty-infected
B) Cleanse with triple antibiotic solution irrigation and utilize the graft
C) Dispose of the graft and substitute with synthetic material
D) Autoclave sterilize and employ the graft
E) Cleanse with chlorhexidine solution and utilize the graft
questions.answer:
B)
The appropriate action is to irrigate the graft with sterile triple antibiotic solution (containing 0.1% gentamicin, 0.1% clindamycin, 0.05% polymyxin) and proceed with its use. Since this graft cannot be easily re-harvested, salvaging it through proper decontamination is reasonable. Triple antibiotic solution is both available and safe for bone grafts, unlike iodine and chlorhexidine which can be harmful. Research demonstrates that iodine lacks superior antimicrobial efficacy compared to other agents. While chlorhexidine effectively eliminates microorganisms, studies show it damages corticocancellous bone, making it unsuitable for this application. A) is incorrect because the wound classification should change from 1 to 3, not 4. C) is incorrect because discarding the graft is unnecessary given the minimal infection risk with proper decontamination, and alloplastic materials are contraindicated in pediatric patients. D) is incorrect because steam sterilization is not appropriate for acute graft salvage and could damage the bone. E) is incorrect because chlorhexidine, while effective antimicrobially, has detrimental effects on bone tissue.

questions.question:
In rhinoplasty, the intercartilaginous incision is made along the caudal margin of which structure?
A) Lateral crus of the alar cartilage
B) Caudal nasal septum
C) Lower lateral nasal cartilage
D) Middle crus
E) Upper lateral nasal cartilage
questions.answer:
E)
The intercartilaginous incision is positioned along the caudal margin of the upper lateral nasal cartilage, situated between this cartilage and the cephalic edge of the lateral crus of the alar cartilage. This incision often connects with a transfixion incision at the septal angle where the caudal septum meets. A) is incorrect because the lateral crus of the alar cartilage forms the cephalic border of the incision, not the structure being followed. B) is incorrect because while the caudal septum may connect via transfixion incision, it is not the primary structure defining the intercartilaginous incision path. C) is incorrect because this is another term for the alar cartilage, which forms the lower border rather than the structure being followed. D) is incorrect because the middle crus is not the anatomical landmark used for this specific incision placement.

questions.question:
An 11-year-old child comes to the clinic following trauma from falling off his scooter. A panoramic radiograph reveals a displaced fracture of the mandibular body on the left side at the level of the first premolar. Clinical evaluation shows that the permanent lateral incisor appears elongated compared to the contralateral lateral incisor. The permanent second molars have not yet emerged. Which of the following statements about treating this patient's injury is most correct?
A) Circummandibular wiring should be avoided in children with mandible fractures due to potential harm to developing tooth buds
B) Intermaxillary fixation using arch bars should not be used in children during primary and mixed dentition phases
C) Rigid internal fixation with plates should never be utilized for mandibular fractures in mixed dentition
D) A tooth located within the fracture site requires extraction
E) A tooth that has been displaced from its alveolar socket requires extraction
questions.answer:
E)
The elongated appearance of the lateral incisor indicates an extrusive luxation injury, where the tooth has been displaced from its socket. According to established guidelines, luxated teeth that have been displaced from their sockets are indicated for removal as they pose risks for complications and interfere with proper healing. A) is incorrect because circummandibular wiring can safely be used in pediatric mandible fractures without damaging tooth buds. B) is incorrect because recent studies have shown that arch bars can be safely used in primary and mixed dentition without causing disturbances to permanent teeth. C) is incorrect because plate fixation can be performed in mixed dentition depending on the location and timing relative to permanent tooth eruption. D) is incorrect because simply being in the fracture line alone is not an indication for tooth removal unless other specific criteria are met.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old male presents to the clinic with wound dehiscence occurring 2 weeks following a calcaneal fracture. Emergency department orthopedic fixation was completed at the time of initial trauma. Current examination reveals a 3 × 4-cm defect overlying the lateral calcaneus. Reconstruction using a propeller fasciocutaneous flap from the lateral lower leg is being considered. Which of the following vessels provides the perforating branches for this flap?
A) Anterior tibial artery
B) Lateral plantar artery
C) Lateral sural artery
D) Peroneal artery
E) Posterior tibial artery
questions.answer:
D)
The peroneal artery supplies the perforators for laterally-based propeller flaps used in lower extremity reconstruction. These versatile flaps utilize perforating vessels from the peroneal artery for lateral defect coverage and from the posterior tibial artery for medial leg defects. They often eliminate the need for sural artery flaps or free tissue transfer procedures. A) The anterior tibial artery is incorrect because it lacks perforators in the appropriate location for a distally-based propeller flap reconstruction. B) The lateral plantar artery is incorrect because laterally-based plantar flaps are only suitable for small weight-bearing foot defects, not larger lateral defects. C) The lateral sural artery is incorrect because these vessels are positioned too proximally to provide adequate coverage for heel reconstruction. E) The posterior tibial artery is incorrect because its perforators are used for medial leg defects, not lateral calcaneal coverage.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old male patient has a persistent lower leg ulcer. He is currently taking prednisone to treat his rheumatoid arthritis. Along with conventional local wound management, which treatment option would be most suitable?
A) Folic acid
B) Hyperbaric oxygen treatment (HBOT)
C) Extended-release insulin
D) Vitamin A
E) Vitamin C
questions.answer:
D)
Vitamin A is the most appropriate treatment because it has been demonstrated in numerous studies to counteract the negative impact of corticosteroids on the wound healing process. Poor nutrition is a recognized risk factor for chronic wound development, and vitamin A supplementation specifically helps mitigate steroid-induced healing impairment. A) Folic acid is incorrect because while it may help with hyperhomocysteinemia, its benefit for chronic wounds is not well-established, particularly in the context of corticosteroid use. B) Hyperbaric oxygen treatment is incorrect because although it can improve wound healing through various cellular mechanisms, it has not shown proven benefits specifically for wounds complicated by chronic corticosteroid therapy. C) Extended-release insulin is incorrect because proper glucose control is only relevant for diabetic ulcers, and there is no indication this patient has uncontrolled diabetes. E) Vitamin C is incorrect because while it serves as a cofactor in collagen synthesis and may benefit nutritionally deficient patients, it has not been proven to specifically help wound healing in the setting of chronic corticosteroid use.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male presents to the clinic following a deep cut to his elbow region. Clinical assessment reveals impaired ulnar nerve function, prompting surgical exploration and reconstruction. After mobilizing both proximal and distal nerve segments, a 1-cm defect remains between the nerve ends. What is the most suitable next management approach?
A) Nerve transfer procedure
B) Nerve transposition
C) Polyglycolic acid conduit placement
D) Direct primary repair
E) Sural nerve graft reconstruction
questions.answer:
B)
Nerve transposition is the most appropriate choice because it can eliminate the 1-cm gap by repositioning the ulnar nerve anteriorly, thereby shortening the distance between nerve ends and enabling tension-free primary repair. A) Nerve transfer is incorrect because it is reserved for very proximal injuries with unavailable proximal stumps or extremely long gaps where muscle denervation is a concern before regeneration occurs. C) Polyglycolic acid conduit is incorrect because while it could bridge the gap, transposition offers a better solution by allowing primary repair without foreign material. D) Direct primary repair is incorrect because attempting repair with a 1-cm gap would create excessive tension, compromising perfusion and healing at the repair site. E) Sural nerve grafting is incorrect because while it could bridge the defect, transposition provides a superior option by enabling direct repair without donor site morbidity.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old female patient is scheduled for breast enhancement surgery combined with abdominal contouring with liposuction and an overnight hospital stay. She has no prior history of complex or antibiotic-resistant infections and reports no known medication allergies. To minimize the risk of postoperative wound infection, which of the following represents the most suitable antibiotic selection, timing, and treatment duration for this patient?
A) Cefazolin, single dose administered within 60 minutes before skin incision
B) Cefazolin, initial dose given within 60 minutes of surgical start, followed by continued therapy for 23 hours after surgery
C) Cefuroxime, single dose given within 60 minutes before skin incision
D) Cefuroxime, initial dose administered within 60 minutes of incision, followed by continued treatment for 23 hours postoperatively
E) Antibiotic prophylaxis is not required
questions.answer:
A)
The appropriate choice is a single preoperative dose of cefazolin given within one hour of incision. Evidence-based guidelines from plastic surgery consensus statements demonstrate that single-dose antibiotic prophylaxis significantly reduces surgical site infection rates in clean breast surgery procedures, with cefazolin being the preferred first-line agent for clean plastic surgery cases. Current data do not support extending antibiotic therapy beyond the single preoperative dose. B) is incorrect because prolonged antibiotic courses beyond 24 hours are not supported by evidence and contribute to antibiotic resistance. C) is incorrect because cefuroxime is not the preferred first-line prophylactic antibiotic for clean plastic surgery procedures when cefazolin is available. D) is incorrect because it combines the wrong antibiotic choice with unnecessary prolonged duration. E) is incorrect because meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials shows significant reduction in surgical site infections with prophylactic antibiotics versus no treatment in clean breast surgery.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old male presents to the emergency department with complete transection of all extensor tendons in Zone VII of his right arm. During surgical repair, which tendon will demonstrate the most distally located muscle belly when attempting to approximate the severed ends?
A) Extensor carpi radialis longus
B) Extensor carpi ulnaris
C) Extensor digitorum communis to middle finger
D) Extensor indicis proprius
E) Extensor pollicis longus
questions.answer:
D)
The extensor indicis proprius possesses the most distally positioned muscle belly among the extensor tendons in Zone VII, making it readily identifiable during surgical repair. Zone VII encompasses extensor tendon injuries occurring at the dorsal aspect of the wrist region. This anatomical characteristic of the extensor indicis proprius serves as a reliable landmark for surgeons during tendon identification and repair procedures. A) is incorrect because the extensor carpi radialis longus has a more proximally located muscle belly. B) is incorrect because the extensor carpi ulnaris muscle belly is positioned more proximally than the extensor indicis proprius. C) is incorrect because the extensor digitorum communis has muscle bellies located more proximally in the forearm. E) is incorrect because the extensor pollicis longus muscle belly is situated more proximally compared to the extensor indicis proprius.

questions.question:
A 72-year-old male patient receives a composite mandibular resection with fibula osteocutaneous free flap reconstruction. His medical history reveals oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. On the first postoperative day, signs of flap ischemia are observed. Emergency revision of the microvascular connections is undertaken. Which of the following complications causing flap compromise has the highest likelihood of unsuccessful salvage procedures?
A) Arterial clot formation
B) Blood collection
C) Vessel kinking
D) Venous clot formation
questions.answer:
A)
Arterial clot formation has the poorest salvage success rates compared to venous clotting or mechanical complications. Research by Bui and colleagues showed salvage success rates of 40% for arterial clots, 71% for venous clots, and 90% for blood collections. Similar findings were reported by Selber and team, who also found 92% salvage rates for mechanical complications versus 64.9% for vessel clotting issues. B) is incorrect because blood collections have much higher salvage rates (90%) due to easier correction. C) is incorrect because vessel kinking represents a mechanical cause with excellent salvage rates (92%) since it's readily reversible without vessel damage. D) is incorrect because venous clots have better salvage outcomes (71%) than arterial clots, likely due to less severe endothelial damage.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old female patient receives bilateral hand transplants. Within 12 hours post-operatively, the grafted tissues demonstrate signs of rejection. Despite intensive medical and surgical interventions, the transplants are unsuccessful. What is the most probable form of tissue rejection occurring in this case?
A) Acute cellular rejection
B) Acute antibody-mediated rejection
C) Chronic rejection
D) Hyperacute rejection
questions.answer:
D)
Hyperacute rejection is the most likely form of tissue rejection in this scenario. This type of rejection occurs within minutes to hours due to pre-existing antibodies in the recipient that react immediately with the donor tissue. These antibodies typically develop from prior blood transfusions, multiple pregnancies, or previous transplants. The antigen-antibody reactions trigger complement activation, leading to extensive microvascular thrombosis that prevents graft vascularization. Without prompt graft removal, serious systemic complications like systemic inflammatory response syndrome can occur.

A) Acute cellular rejection is incorrect because it is T-cell mediated and typically develops over the first 3-6 months post-transplant, not within hours. B) Acute antibody-mediated rejection is incorrect because while it involves antibodies and complement like hyperacute rejection, these antibodies are newly formed after graft exposure and the process takes several days (3-7 days) rather than hours. C) Chronic rejection is incorrect because it develops months to years after transplantation, involving both cellular and humoral mechanisms in a gradual process.

questions.question:
A healthy 26-year-old female patient receives zone 2 wide-awake flexor tendon reconstruction of her right index finger. Local injection of 1% lidocaine containing 1:100,000 epinephrine is administered to the hand and digit. Following surgical reconstruction of the flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendon, the patient's digit remains blanched with absent capillary refill. Which of the following medication classes would most effectively counteract the epinephrine effects in this case?
A) Alpha-adrenergic receptor agonist
B) Alpha-adrenergic receptor antagonist
C) Beta-adrenergic receptor antagonist
D) Potassium channel opener
E) Sodium channel antagonist
questions.answer:
B)
The appropriate medication to counteract epinephrine effects is phentolamine, an alpha-adrenergic receptor antagonist. This drug effectively reverses the vasoconstriction caused by epinephrine in wide-awake hand surgery procedures. A is incorrect because alpha-adrenergic receptor agonists like epinephrine would worsen vasoconstriction rather than reverse it. C is incorrect because beta-adrenergic receptor antagonists do not address the alpha-mediated vasoconstriction and could potentially worsen the situation. D is incorrect because potassium channel openers are not the standard treatment for epinephrine-induced vasoconstriction. E is incorrect because sodium channel antagonists are not indicated for reversing epinephrine's vasoconstrictive effects.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old commercial fisherman from Florida presents to the emergency room one day after sustaining a laceration to his palm from a knife used for fish scaling. Vital signs reveal hypotension (90/50 mmHg) and tachycardia (120 bpm). Clinical examination demonstrates marked edema of the hand, blood-filled blisters on the hand, and redness extending to the middle of the forearm. Radiographic imaging reveals no evidence of gas in the soft tissues. Gram staining of fluid from a blister shows gram-negative rod-shaped bacteria. What is the most probable infectious organism responsible for this patient's condition?
A) Clostridium perfringens
B) Mycobacterium marinum
C) Pseudomonas aeruginosa
D) Staphylococcus aureus
E) Vibrio vulnificus
questions.answer:
E)
This patient presents with necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock. Vibrio vulnificus is a gram-negative rod that causes aggressive necrotizing fasciitis and is characteristically found in warm marine waters (consistent with Florida). This organism typically produces hemorrhagic bullae as seen in this case. A) Clostridium perfringens is incorrect because it is a gram-positive, gas-producing bacillus that would show gas on X-ray, which is absent here. B) Mycobacterium marinum is incorrect because it typically causes chronic, indolent granulomatous infections in aquarium handlers, not acute necrotizing fasciitis. C) Pseudomonas aeruginosa is incorrect because while it is a gram-negative rod found in moist environments, it usually causes less severe soft tissue infections. D) Staphylococcus aureus is incorrect because it is a gram-positive coccus that typically produces pustular rather than hemorrhagic lesions and is not specifically associated with marine environments.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female patient presents with significant photodamage and facial rhytides seeking laser resurfacing treatment. What is the most appropriate approach for protecting against inhalation hazards from laser-generated smoke?
A) High-efficiency smoke evacuation system positioned 20 to 25 cm from the laser plume source
B) High-efficiency smoke evacuation system positioned within 1 to 2 cm of the laser plume source
C) Standard surgical mask only
D) Standard wall suction system
E) No special protective measures or equipment required
questions.answer:
B)

High-efficiency smoke evacuation systems must be positioned within 1 to 2 cm of the laser plume source to effectively capture hazardous particles and pathogens. Laser smoke contains numerous toxic substances including carcinogens, mutagens, viable bacteria, and viral DNA particles, with 77% of particles being 1 micron or smaller. The evacuation system's effectiveness drops dramatically from 99% to 50% when distance increases from 1 to 2 cm from the source. A) is incorrect because positioning the evacuator 20 to 25 cm away renders it ineffective due to the significant distance from the plume source. C) is incorrect because standard surgical masks only filter particles 5 microns or larger, while most laser plume particles are smaller than 1 micron. D) is incorrect because standard wall suction lacks the specialized filtration and proximity needed for laser plume capture. E) is incorrect because laser smoke poses documented occupational hazards requiring specific protective equipment.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old female patient who is not emancipated presents to your clinic seeking breast reduction surgery. What is the most appropriate next step in her care?
A) Proceed with the breast reduction after securing consent from both parents
B) Proceed with the breast reduction after securing consent from one parent
C) Proceed with the breast reduction without requiring parental consent
D) Postpone the breast reduction until the patient reaches 18 years of age
E) Postpone the breast reduction until the patient reaches 21 years of age
questions.answer:
B)
The most appropriate next step is to proceed with the breast reduction surgery after obtaining consent from one parent. In nearly all jurisdictions, patients under 18 years of age must have parental consent from at least one parent before undergoing surgical procedures. Since this patient is not emancipated, she cannot provide independent consent for surgery. A) is incorrect because consent from both parents is not required - one parent's consent is sufficient. C) is incorrect because non-emancipated minors cannot consent to surgery independently. D) is incorrect because waiting until 18 is unnecessary when proper parental consent can be obtained. E) is incorrect because 21 is not the legal age of medical consent, and waiting is unnecessary with appropriate parental permission.

questions.question: A 75-year-old man with a history of renal transplantation presents with a rapidly growing squamous cell carcinoma involving his anterior scalp and forehead. A photograph is shown. Wide excision results in a 20 √o 20-cm defect with exposed calvarium. Which of the following flaps is most appropriate for coverage of this wound?A) Anterolateral thigh free flapB) Gracilis free flapC) Lateral arm free flapD) Radial forearm free flapE) Rectus abdominis free flap
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.

The anterolateral thigh (ALT) free flap (shown) is the only option listed with the requisite tissue characteristics, size, and pedicle length necessary to repair a defect of this size and location. The ALT flap has rapidly become a first-line option for covering large or irregular head and neck defects. It is an extremely versatile flap with chimeric options allowing for multiple skin paddles, muscle bulk (vastus lateralis) if needed for dead space obliteration, as well as bone (iliac crest) for midface or small mandibular defects. The tissue thickness is well suited for large scalp defects. Flaps as large as 35 √o 25 cm have been described, although defects larger than 10 to 12 cm in width generally require skin grafting the donor site. Pedicle lengths of 12 to 16 cm have been described, which is often long enough to reach the upper neck if necessary.The radial forearm free flap is an excellent option in many cases, providing a pedicle length up to 18 to 20 cm with maximal dimensions up to 12 √o 30 cm. A major criticism of this flap is the poor cosmesis of the donor site and lack of subcutaneous tissue necessary to match the surrounding cutaneous defect. The lateral arm flap based on the radial collateral artery is useful for smaller defects in the head and neck but is limited in this situation by a short pedicle (6 cm) and smaller skin paddle (6 √o 12 cm).Muscle flaps covered with skin grafts have also been described for scalp coverage. When necessary, a latissimus dorsi flap is a great option for near total scalp coverage. With the examples listed here, the gracilis flap is too narrow (5 to 6 cm) with too short a pedicle (medial femoral circumflex, 7 cm). While the pedicle for the rectus free flap (deep inferior epigastric, 8 to 10 cm) might be long enough in this situation, the muscle is not big enough (6 cm wide) to cover the defect.ReferencesNasajpour H, Steele MH. Anterolateral thigh free flap for "head-to-toe" reconstruction. Ann Plast Surg. 2011 May;66(5):530-3.Wei FC, Dayan JH. Scalp, skull, orbit, and maxilla reconstruction and hair transplantation. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2013 Mar;131(3):411e-24e.Chana JS, Wei FC. A review of the advantages of the anterolateral thigh flap in head and neck reconstruction. Br J Plast Surg. 2004 Oct;57(7):603-9.Rectus Abdominis and TRAM/DIEP Flaps. In: Zenn MR, Jones G, eds. Reconstructive Surgery. St. Louis, MO: Quality Medical Publishing;2012:1138-1191.Gracilis and TUG/TMG Flaps. In: Zenn MR, Jones G, eds. Reconstructive Surgery. St. Louis, MO: Quality Medical Publishing;2012:1420-1465.Ninkovic M, Dornseifer U. Lateral arm flap. In: Wei FC, Mardini S, eds. Flaps and Reconstructive Surgery. Philadelphia, PA: Saunders-Elsevier;2009:305-319.Soutar DS. Radial forearm flap. In: Wei FC, Mardini S, eds. Flaps and Reconstructive Surgery. Philadelphia, PA: Saunders-Elsevier;2009:321-338

questions.question:
A 12-year-old male presents to the clinic with lymphatic swelling of the penis and scrotum. He has experienced multiple infections and is unhappy with the cosmetic appearance of his external genitalia. What is the most suitable initial management approach?
A) Charles operation
B) Suction-assisted lipectomy
C) Vascularized lymph node transplantation
D) Microsurgical lymphaticovenous bypass
E) Surgical excision with skin reconstruction
questions.answer:
E)
Surgical excision with skin reconstruction is the primary surgical treatment for penile and scrotal lymphedema, involving removal of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue. A) Charles operation is incorrect because this extensive procedure removing skin, subcutaneous tissue, and fascia is rarely used and reserved for extremity lymphedema, not genital disease. B) Suction-assisted lipectomy is incorrect because while it may be effective for limb lymphedema, it lacks proven benefit for genital lymphatic disorders. C) Vascularized lymph node transplantation is incorrect because this microsurgical technique is designed for early-stage extremity lymphedema and has no established role in treating genital lymphatic conditions. D) Microsurgical lymphaticovenous bypass is incorrect because this procedure is indicated for early extremity lymphedema and does not provide therapeutic benefit for penile or scrotal lymphatic disease.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old male presents to the clinic following a workplace accident where his dominant right hand's middle finger was caught in machinery. Examination reveals a 1.3-cm defect of fingertip soft tissue without bone exposure. What is the best treatment approach to maintain digit function and sensation?
A) Distal interphalangeal joint amputation
B) Cross-finger flap reconstruction
C) Wet-to-dry dressing changes
D) Thenar flap coverage
E) Palmar V-to-Y advancement flap
questions.answer:
C)
Wet-to-dry dressing changes provide optimal outcomes for fingertip injuries without bone exposure. This conservative approach avoids donor site complications, minimizes scarring, and typically restores excellent sensation, though patients must understand the extended healing period of 3-6 weeks with regular dressing changes. A) Distal interphalangeal joint amputation is incorrect because it would eliminate profundus tendon function and weaken grip strength unnecessarily. B) Cross-finger flap reconstruction is incorrect as it risks digit stiffness and contractures, particularly in older patients, when simpler treatment suffices. D) Thenar flap coverage is incorrect because it may cause contractures and stiffness in older individuals and is unnecessary without significant bone exposure. E) Palmar V-to-Y advancement flap is incorrect as it creates a donor defect and reduces sensation while being overly complex for this injury pattern.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old female patient with rheumatoid arthritis history develops a boutonnière deformity affecting her middle finger. What is the most probable underlying cause of this deformity?
A) Cartilage deterioration within the proximal interphalangeal joint
B) Posterior displacement of the lateral bands at the proximal interphalangeal joint
C) Subluxation of the metacarpophalangeal joint
D) Tear of the terminal extensor tendon
E) Inflammatory synovitis affecting the proximal interphalangeal joint
questions.answer:
E)
Synovitis at the proximal interphalangeal joint causes weakening and stretching of the central slip tendon, which is the primary mechanism leading to boutonnière deformity in rheumatoid arthritis patients. This inflammatory process results in loss of active extension at the PIP joint, allowing the lateral bands to migrate palmarly and create the characteristic flexion at the PIP joint with hyperextension at the DIP joint. A is incorrect because cartilage destruction alone does not cause the specific tendon imbalance seen in boutonnière deformity. B is incorrect because the lateral bands actually move volarly (palmarly), not dorsally. C is incorrect because MCP joint subluxation is a separate rheumatoid manifestation that does not directly cause boutonnière deformity. D is incorrect because boutonnière deformity involves central slip rupture or attenuation, not the distal extensor tendon.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old male develops a contracture at the proximal interphalangeal joint following secondary wound healing of a palmar burn injury to his right hand. Which cell type is primarily responsible for the contraction of this scarred tissue?
A) Keratinocyte
B) Langerhans cell
C) Melanocyte
D) Merkel cell
E) Myofibroblast
questions.answer:
E)
Myofibroblasts are the primary cells responsible for scar contraction during secondary wound healing. These specialized cells are terminally differentiated fibroblasts that express alpha-smooth muscle actin, allowing them to function like smooth muscle cells. They contract their cell length and pull on the attached extracellular matrix, leading to tissue contraction that can result in joint contractures when excessive. Myofibroblasts are particularly abundant in hypertrophic scars, produce increased collagen while decreasing collagenase production, and resist programmed cell death signals. A) Keratinocytes are incorrect because they are epithelial cells that produce keratin for skin barrier function, not involved in scar contraction. B) Langerhans cells are incorrect because they are immune cells specialized for antigen presentation, not contractile function. C) Melanocytes are incorrect because they produce melanin pigment and are not involved in tissue contraction. D) Merkel cells are incorrect because they function as mechanoreceptors for touch sensation, not in scar formation or contraction.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old male patient presents to the clinic 24 hours following liposuction procedures on his arms, chest, and breast area. He displays signs of disorientation and mental confusion. Physical examination reveals petechial lesions distributed across the front of his torso and underarm areas. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Drug hypersensitivity reaction
B) Fat embolism
C) Local anesthetic toxicity
D) Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
E) Transient ischemic attack
questions.answer:
B)
Fat embolism syndrome represents the correct diagnosis as it classically presents with the characteristic triad of neurological changes, respiratory symptoms, and petechial rash appearing within 24-72 hours post-procedure, particularly after liposuction involving significant fat manipulation. A) is incorrect because allergic drug reactions typically don't present with this specific pattern of upper truncal petechiae and neurological symptoms in this timeframe. C) is incorrect because lidocaine toxicity manifests earlier with perioral numbness, visual changes, and muscle twitching, without the characteristic petechial rash pattern. D) is incorrect because TTP more commonly presents with headache and gastrointestinal symptoms rather than this specific post-procedural presentation. E) is incorrect because transient ischemic attacks present with focal neurological deficits like vision loss or weakness, not the diffuse confusion and petechial rash seen here.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old female patient has moderately sized breasts with slight sagging, and the treatment plan involves bilateral circumareolar breast lift surgery to reduce scar visibility. What postoperative complication occurs most frequently with this surgical approach?
A) Areolar widening
B) Lower breast pole constriction
C) Nipple-areolar sensory loss
D) Nipple-areolar complex pseudoherniation
E) Symmastia
questions.answer:
A)
Areolar widening represents the most frequent complication following this surgical technique. Breast lift procedures aim to enhance the appearance of drooping breasts while keeping scars minimal. The circumareolar approach works best for very mild breast sagging, but when used for moderate to severe drooping, various complications may develop including central breast flattening, areolar diameter expansion, and circumareolar scar irregularities or widening. B) is incorrect because lower pole constriction is characteristic of tuberous breast abnormality rather than periareolar mastopexy complications. C) is incorrect as nipple-areolar sensory loss typically occurs with breast tissue removal procedures rather than this lifting technique. D) is incorrect since pseudoherniation of the nipple-areolar complex is associated with tuberous breast deformity, not periareolar mastopexy. E) is incorrect because symmastia results from oversized breast implants, not from this particular lifting procedure.

questions.question:
A newborn male infant, 8 hours old, is being evaluated in the NICU and found to have epibulbar dermoids. Radiographic imaging reveals cervical vertebral fusion. Which of the following accompanying features would be most characteristic of this condition?
A) Cleft palate
B) Lower lip pits
C) Microtia
D) Syndactyly
E) Telecanthus
questions.answer:
C)
The correct answer is microtia. This clinical presentation is consistent with oculoauricular dysplasia (Goldenhar syndrome), which characteristically includes ear malformations (microtia), epibulbar dermoids, facial and mandibular underdevelopment, and spinal vertebral abnormalities. A) Cleft palate is incorrect because while it can occur in Goldenhar syndrome, it is not considered a hallmark feature and occurs less frequently than ear anomalies. B) Lower lip pits is incorrect because this finding is characteristic of van der Woude syndrome, the most prevalent orofacial clefting condition, not Goldenhar syndrome. D) Syndactyly is incorrect because finger webbing is not typically associated with Goldenhar syndrome. E) Telecanthus is incorrect because increased distance between the inner canthi is not a classic manifestation of Goldenhar syndrome.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a severe laceration on the inner aspect of his right arm near the elbow. Assessment reveals total loss of ulnar nerve function affecting the right hand. During surgical exploration, complete severing of the ulnar nerve at the elbow is discovered with a 3-cm gap remaining after tissue debridement. Which of the following surgical approaches is most likely to provide the quickest restoration of intrinsic hand muscle function in this patient?
A) Anterior interosseous nerve transfer
B) Cable grafting using nerve allograft
C) Cable grafting using sural nerve graft
D) Direct repair with elbow positioned in flexion
E) Ulnar nerve transposition with direct repair
questions.answer:
A)
Anterior interosseous nerve transfer is the optimal choice for achieving the fastest recovery of intrinsic hand muscle function. This technique involves transferring the expendable anterior interosseous nerve to the motor branch of the ulnar nerve in the distal forearm, creating an anastomosis only 8-10 cm from the target muscles rather than the full 30-35 cm distance from the elbow injury site. This dramatically reduces regeneration time and stays within the critical 18-month window for meaningful motor recovery. B is incorrect because cable grafting with allograft, while effective, requires regeneration across the full distance from elbow to hand, exceeding the optimal timeframe for motor recovery. C is incorrect because sural nerve grafting also requires the same lengthy regeneration distance as option B, making recovery slower than nerve transfer. D is incorrect because primary repair under tension with extreme joint positioning leads to poor outcomes, internal scarring, and potential contractures. E is incorrect because ulnar nerve transposition only gains approximately 1 cm of length, insufficient to bridge the 3-cm gap without tension.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old healthcare worker is planning to have elective breast surgery without implants on her left side. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she reports no drug allergies. She currently smokes one pack of cigarettes per day. What perioperative intervention would be most effective in reducing her risk of surgical site infection?
A) Give intravenous cefazolin 5 minutes before making the skin incision
B) Start continuous insulin infusion to maintain blood glucose below 100 mg/dL
C) Instruct the patient to stop smoking completely for one week before the procedure
D) Order intranasal mupirocin and chlorhexidine body washes for 5 days before surgery
E) Choose povidone-iodine for skin antisepsis instead of chlorhexidine with isopropyl alcohol
questions.answer:
D)
The most effective strategy is prescribing intranasal mupirocin and chlorhexidine body washes for 5 days preoperatively. A landmark 2010 randomized controlled trial involving over 6,700 patients showed that this decolonization protocol reduced Staphylococcus aureus infections by approximately 60% and decreased hospital length of stay by nearly 2 days. Meta-analyses have confirmed these findings, demonstrating roughly 45% reduction in surgical site infections. A) is incorrect because cefazolin should be given 30-59 minutes before incision, not 5 minutes, to achieve adequate tissue penetration and optimal infection prevention. B) is incorrect because this healthy, non-diabetic patient does not require insulin therapy, and maintaining glucose below 100 mg/dL could cause harmful hypoglycemia. C) is incorrect because smoking cessation requires 4 weeks before and after surgery to significantly reduce infection rates, not just 7 days. E) is incorrect because chlorhexidine-alcohol preparations are actually more effective than povidone-iodine alone for reducing surgical site infections.

questions.question:
A 20-month-old female child presents to the clinic with midface underdevelopment, premature fusion of skull sutures, and malformations of the hands and feet. These clinical features are most likely due to a genetic mutation in which of the following?
A) 22q.11
B) FGFR2
C) IRF6
D) TCOF1
questions.answer:
B)

This patient presents with Apert syndrome, an autosomal dominant condition characterized by bicoronal synostosis resulting in turribrachycephaly, midface underdevelopment, and complex syndactyly of hands and feet. This syndrome is caused by mutations in the Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor-2 (FGFR2) gene. A) is incorrect because 22q11 deletion syndrome (DiGeorge/velocardiofacial syndrome) primarily causes congenital heart defects, cleft palate, learning difficulties, and facial elongation, not the hand/foot syndactyly seen here. C) is incorrect because IRF6 mutations cause van der Woude syndrome, which presents with cleft lip/palate and lip pits, not craniosynostosis or limb anomalies. D) is incorrect because TCOF1 mutations cause Treacher Collins syndrome (mandibular dysostosis), which involves facial bone hypoplasia and ear defects but does not include craniosynostosis or hand/foot malformations.

questions.question:
A healthy 20-year-old transgender female (designated male at birth) has undergone proper psychological evaluation and puberty suppression treatment since childhood. She is currently being evaluated for male-to-female gender confirmation surgery. What is the most suitable surgical approach if the ability to engage in penetrative sexual activity is a priority?
A) Intestinal vaginoplasty
B) Metoidioplasty
C) Penile inversion vaginoplasty
D) Radial forearm free flap
E) Surgery is contraindicated for this patient
questions.answer:
A)
Intestinal vaginoplasty is the most suitable approach in this case. When patients have undergone early hormone suppression therapy, there may be insufficient penile-scrotal tissue available for traditional penile inversion techniques. Intestinal vaginoplasty using sigmoid colon provides adequate vaginal depth and function regardless of original genital size, making it ideal for patients with limited penile tissue or those requiring revision procedures. B) Metoidioplasty is incorrect because it is a female-to-male procedure used to create a phallus, not applicable for male-to-female surgery. C) Penile inversion vaginoplasty is incorrect because early hormone suppression may have limited penile tissue development, making this approach less feasible. D) Radial forearm free flap is incorrect as this technique is used for phalloplasty in female-to-male patients, not for creating a vagina. E) Surgery is not contraindicated is incorrect because the patient meets appropriate criteria including age, health status, and proper preparation.

questions.question:
During transnasal canthal wiring for medial canthal ligament reattachment, what is the optimal positioning of drill holes relative to the lacrimal fossa?
A) Anterior and inferior
B) Anterior and posterior
C) Posterior and inferior
D) Posterior and superior
questions.answer:
D)
The optimal drill hole placement is posterior and superior to the posterior crest of the bony lacrimal fossa. This positioning is crucial when reconstructing naso-orbital-ethmoid deformities to ensure proper medial canthal tendon reattachment. Since overcorrection is virtually impossible with this technique, maximum effort must be made to prevent relapse and recurring telecanthus by securing the transnasal wires through drill holes in this posterior-superior location. A is incorrect because anterior and inferior placement would not provide adequate support and could lead to relapse. B is incorrect because anterior and posterior describes a horizontal relationship rather than the needed vertical component. C is incorrect because posterior and inferior positioning lacks the superior component necessary for optimal canthal support and prevention of telecanthus recurrence.

questions.question:
A 59-year-old male with diabetes type 2 presents to the clinic with edema, discomfort, and impaired mobility of his right fifth digit following minor trauma 2 weeks prior. He describes comparable manifestations in his right thumb, despite no precipitating injury to that digit. Physical examination of both fingers reveals findings consistent with bacterial flexor tenosynovitis. Beyond irrigating the affected tendon sheaths, which additional anatomical location requires surgical exploration?
A) First web space
B) Flexor carpi radialis tendon sheath
C) Hypothenar compartment
D) Ring finger flexor tendon sheath
E) Space of Parona
questions.answer:
E)
The space of Parona is the correct answer because bacterial flexor tenosynovitis can propagate from the fifth digit's tendon sheath to the thumb's flexor tendon sheath through this anatomical space. The space of Parona represents a potential cavity located in the palmar aspect of the wrist, positioned deep to the flexor tendons yet superficial to the pronator quadratus muscle. Within this region, the proximal portions of both the small finger and thumb tendon sheaths are anatomically adjacent, creating what is known as the "horseshoe abscess" pattern in the upper limb. A is incorrect because the first web space is not involved in the communication pathway between these specific tendon sheaths. B is incorrect because the flexor carpi radialis tendon sheath does not connect the thumb and small finger flexor sheaths. C is incorrect because the hypothenar compartment, while related to small finger anatomy, is not the communication route to the thumb. D is incorrect because the ring finger flexor tendon sheath is not part of the pathway connecting the thumb and small finger infections.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with swelling of both lower eyelids. Clinical examination reveals minimal excess lower eyelid skin but noticeable protruding fat compartments. Eyelid tension, recoil testing, and pull-away examination demonstrate normal findings. The lid-cheek transition appears intact. A posterior septal transconjunctival technique for the lower eyelid is being considered. Which of the following statements regarding this surgical method is most correct?
A) Adipose tissue modification is accomplished without breaching the orbital septum
B) Concurrent lower eyelid skin rejuvenation using laser or chemical treatments is contraindicated with a posterior septal technique
C) The surgical incision should be positioned 1 to 2 mm inferior to the tarsal margin
D) The inferior oblique muscle is located between the middle and outer fat compartments
E) The dissection plane lies beneath the orbicularis muscle but above the orbital septum
questions.answer:
A)
The posterior septal approach allows for fat compartment modification without penetrating the orbital septum since the fat pads are already located behind the septum, making septal violation unnecessary. The surgical incision is typically positioned 4 to 5 mm below the tarsal margin, not 1-2 mm as stated in option C. Option D is incorrect because the inferior oblique muscle is situated between the central and medial fat compartments, not the central and lateral ones. Option E is wrong since the posterior septal dissection plane extends deep to both the orbicularis muscle and the orbital septum by definition. Option B is incorrect as multiple studies have demonstrated the safety of performing simultaneous skin resurfacing procedures with transconjunctival blepharoplasty.

questions.question:
A 41-year-old female dental professional presents to the clinic with severe burning sensation and itching of her primary index finger lasting 6 days. She describes an initial small vesicular eruption on the digit that has now developed into a small blister. She reports episodes of fever and general malaise. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Surgical incision and drainage of the blisters
B) Intravenous cefazolin therapy
C) Oral acyclovir treatment
D) Topical silver sulfadiazine application
E) Conservative observation
questions.answer:
E)
This patient presents with clinical features characteristic of herpetic whitlow, a herpes simplex virus infection commonly seen in healthcare workers, particularly those in dental and medical fields. The optimal management approach is conservative observation, as this viral condition is self-resolving and typically clears within 1-3 weeks without intervention. A) Surgical incision and drainage is contraindicated because it can promote bacterial superinfection and facilitate systemic spread of the herpes simplex virus. B) Intravenous cefazolin is inappropriate since this is a viral rather than bacterial infection, making antibiotics ineffective. C) Oral acyclovir could potentially reduce symptom duration but is only beneficial when initiated within 2-3 days of symptom onset, making it too late in this case. D) Topical silver sulfadiazine would provide no therapeutic benefit for this viral infection.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old male patient with high blood pressure and inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis) presents to the clinic with a painful wound on his right lower extremity. He reports that he accidentally dropped a heavy office machine on his leg approximately 12 months ago, resulting in a minor injury that has progressively enlarged despite conservative management with dressings and topical antimicrobial agents. Histopathological examination of tissue obtained via incisional biopsy reveals neutrophilic dermatosis. Bacterial cultures yield Staphylococcus aureus. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Leishmaniasis
B) Marjolin ulcer
C) Necrotizing fasciitis
D) Pyoderma gangrenosum
E) Scleroderma
questions.answer:
D)
The patient has pyoderma gangrenosum, a neutrophilic dermatosis strongly associated with inflammatory bowel diseases like ulcerative colitis. The condition typically develops after minor trauma on the lower extremities and presents as painful, rapidly expanding ulcerative lesions. The neutrophilic infiltrate on biopsy and association with ulcerative colitis are characteristic features. Treatment is primarily immunosuppressive rather than surgical, as surgery may worsen the condition.

A) Leishmaniasis is incorrect because it is caused by protozoan parasites transmitted by sandfly bites and requires travel history to endemic areas, which is not mentioned in this case.

B) Marjolin ulcer is incorrect because it represents malignant transformation (usually squamous cell carcinoma) of chronic wounds after many years (5-30 years), and the biopsy would show malignant cells rather than neutrophilic dermatosis.

C) Necrotizing fasciitis is incorrect because it presents as a rapidly spreading, life-threatening soft tissue infection with systemic toxicity, not a slowly expanding chronic ulcer over one year.

E) Scleroderma is incorrect because it is an autoimmune connective tissue disorder characterized by skin fibrosis and tightening, not neutrophilic dermatosis with ulceration.

questions.question:
A healthy 45-year-old female patient seeks consultation about autologous breast reconstruction after mastectomy. Her past surgical history includes a tummy tuck performed after her final pregnancy. Following clinical assessment, the plastic surgeon concludes she would be an appropriate candidate for bilateral lumbar artery perforator flaps. During preoperative counseling, the surgeon discusses the advantages, disadvantages, and anticipated results comparing lumbar artery perforator flaps with deep inferior epigastric artery perforator (DIEP) flaps, which represent the surgeon's standard first option for autologous tissue reconstruction. Which of the following adverse outcomes is more frequently seen with lumbar artery perforator flaps compared to DIEP flaps?
A) Increased patient dissatisfaction with breast appearance
B) Elevated hematoma incidence
C) Greater need for secondary procedures
D) Increased complete flap failure rate
questions.answer:
D)
Lumbar artery perforator (LAP) flaps represent a viable alternative for autologous breast reconstruction when DIEP flaps are unavailable. However, LAP flaps demonstrate a significantly higher complete flap failure rate, with studies reporting 6.6-9% compared to less than 2% for DIEP flaps. The increased microvascular complications, predominantly venous rather than arterial, also result in higher reoperation rates for LAP flaps. A) is incorrect because BREAST-Q data shows similar breast satisfaction rates between LAP and DIEP flaps. B) is incorrect because hematoma rates are comparable between the two procedures. C) is incorrect because secondary revision rates are similar for both flap types.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old female presents to the clinic with worsening discomfort in her right ring finger that has developed over 4 months. On examination, the ring finger remains in a bent position with both the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints flexed at 45 degrees. There is pain over the palm during active finger flexion. The patient describes that upon awakening each morning, her ring finger is typically locked in flexion and requires manual straightening using her opposite hand. During the last month, the finger has stayed continuously flexed. Her past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. What is the most probable diagnosis for this patient?
A) Central slip tear
B) de Quervain tenosynovitis
C) Trigger finger
D) Dupuytren disease
E) Cubital tunnel syndrome
questions.answer:
C)
Trigger finger, also known as digital stenosing tenosynovitis, is an inflammatory condition affecting the flexor tendons of the fingers. It typically presents with pain, stiffness, and sometimes a palpable nodule in the palm. Chronic cases can result in finger contracture when appropriate treatment is delayed. A) Central slip tear is incorrect because it would cause a boutonnière deformity with PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension, not the described flexion pattern. B) de Quervain tenosynovitis is incorrect as it affects the first dorsal compartment tendons causing pain at the wrist and thumb base, not finger flexion contracture. D) Dupuytren disease is incorrect because it involves palmar fascial contracture that would prevent passive finger extension, whereas this patient can manually straighten her finger. E) Cubital tunnel syndrome is incorrect as it would typically cause clawing of both ring and little fingers with associated numbness and tingling in the ulnar nerve distribution.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male presents with a 4-cm bone gap in the middle section of his middle finger metacarpal following a gunshot injury to his left hand. What is the most suitable management for this skeletal defect?
A) Application of a free vascularized bone transfer
B) Bone transport using distraction techniques
C) Administration of calcium phosphate cement injection
D) Insertion of an autogenous bone graft
E) Application of demineralized bone matrix
questions.answer:
D)
For a patient presenting with a non-critical bone defect (under 6-8 cm) in the hand, reconstruction using an autogenous bone graft offers the optimal balance of maximum healing potential with minimum associated complications. The graft should permit stable fixation for optimal healing outcomes. Corticocancellous grafts harvested from the iliac crest represent the standard donor site. A) is incorrect because free vascularized bone transfers are reserved for critical defects exceeding 6-8 cm and introduce substantial surgical morbidity unnecessary for smaller defects. B) is incorrect because distraction osteogenesis requires adequate bone stock for pin fixation, which a 4-cm metacarpal defect would not provide at the base and head regions. C) is incorrect because calcium phosphate cement serves as an osteoconductive material only in already-stabilized defects and is contraindicated in infected or potentially contaminated wounds. E) is incorrect because demineralized bone matrix, while osteoinductive, provides no structural support or stability.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old man has a 1.7-cm-diameter defect of the nasal tip and ala after undergoing Mohs micrographic surgery for resection of basal cell carcinoma. There is exposed cartilage with no perichondrium. A photograph of the nose is shown. Which of the following is most appropriate for this defect?


A) Closure by secondary intention
B) Composite graft
C) Locoregional flap
D) Primary closure
E) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


A locoregional flap is the most appropriate option, with preferences dependent on the surgeon. In general, however, nasolabial flaps are useful for reconstructions of small- to medium-sized defects of the nasal tip, ala, and lateral nose. They can be superiorly or inferiorly based and usually require at least two stages, with the second stage being the division and inset. When placed close to the alar margin, they are frequently combined with a nonanatomically placed conchal cartilage graft to prevent notching. Paramedian forehead flaps also are commonly used for nasal lobular defects, especially larger ones.


A dorsal nasal flap is used for defects in the lower half of the nose that are less than 2 cm in diameter, are at least 1 cm from the alar rim, and lie above the tip defining points. This defect lies directly adjacent to the alar rim and is below the tip defining points. Bilobed flaps generally are used for defects less than 1.5 cm in the thicker skin zones of the nasal tip/ala.


The defect described is too large for primary closure and would yield a suboptimal aesthetic outcome if allowed to heal by secondary intention.


There is no need for a composite graft in this location with intact lower lateral cartilage. Split-thickness skin grafting, with its thickness discrepancy versus the thicker nasal lobular skin and higher intrinsic secondary contracture, is not the most appropriate option. Furthermore, there is exposed cartilage without perichondrium, which would not lend itself to skin grafting.


References
Elliot RA Jr. Rotation flaps of the nose. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1969;44:147.
Zitelli JA. The bilobed flap for nasal reconstruction. Arch Dermatol. 1989;125:957-959.
Rohrich RJ, Muzaffar AR, Adams WP Jr, et al. The aesthetic unit dorsal nasal flap: rationale for avoiding a glabellar incision. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1999;104:1289-1294.
Guerrerosantos J, Dicksheet S. Nasolabial flap with simultaneous cartilage graft in nasal alar reconstruction. Clin Plast Surg. 1981;8:599-602.

questions.question:
What is the main function of adipose-derived stem cells (ADSC) in the wound repair process?
A) Aid in the recruitment of platelets and inflammatory cells
B) Transform directly into fibroblasts and epithelial cells
C) Stimulate formation of hair follicles and sebaceous glands
D) Serve as structural support for granulation tissue formation
E) Align and arrange pro-collagen molecules
questions.answer:
B)

Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSC) primarily function by directly differentiating into essential wound healing cell types including keratinocytes, endothelial cells, and dermal fibroblasts. This direct transformation capability, combined with their paracrine signaling effects, makes them valuable therapeutic agents in wound repair. A) is incorrect because ADSCs do not participate in the immediate inflammatory response or chemotaxis of immune cells during early wound healing phases. C) is incorrect because hair follicle and sebaceous gland development occurs during embryonic stages through ectoderm-mesenchyme interactions via specific signaling pathways, not through ADSC activity. D) is incorrect because ADSCs do not function as structural scaffolding during the proliferative phase of healing. E) is incorrect because lysyl oxidase, not ADSCs, is the enzyme responsible for the final organization and cross-linking of collagen fibrils.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old female patient with a body mass index of 35 kg/m2 receives liposuction treatment on her anterior torso, posterior torso, and bilateral thighs in a circumferential manner. What is the threshold lipoaspirate volume that defines "large volume" liposuction?
A) 1000 mL
B) 2500 mL
C) 5000 mL
D) 7500 mL
questions.answer:
C)
Lipoaspirate volumes exceeding 5000 mL are universally recognized as the threshold for defining "large volume" liposuction procedures. This classification is clinically significant because it influences postoperative management decisions, with patients undergoing large volume liposuction typically requiring overnight hospital observation and inpatient monitoring. A) 1000 mL is incorrect because this volume is well below the established threshold and would be considered routine liposuction. B) 2500 mL is incorrect as this amount falls short of the 5000 mL cutoff used to classify large volume procedures. D) 7500 mL is incorrect because while this exceeds the large volume threshold, it is not the minimum defining volume - 5000 mL remains the established cutoff point.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old female with no international travel history presents to the clinic due to progressive enlargement of her feet, leg swelling, and loss of calf muscle definition. Her parents report initially observing ankle soft tissue compression from footwear approximately 2 years prior. There is a family history of lower extremity and ankle edema. Physical examination reveals blunted knee-calf and calf-ankle contours. Non-pitting edema is present. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Filariasis
B) Lymphedema praecox
C) Lymphedema tarda
D) Milroy disease
E) Secondary lymphedema
questions.answer:
B)
Lymphedema praecox represents the most probable form of inherited lymphatic dysfunction. This condition characteristically develops during adolescence and follows a progressive pattern. The clinical presentation demonstrates typical features of lymphedema praecox—bilateral involvement beginning around pubertal age. A is incorrect because filariasis, while globally the leading lymphedema cause, does not occur in non-tropical regions and requires parasitic exposure. C is incorrect because lymphedema tarda by definition develops during middle age, not adolescence. D is incorrect because Milroy disease is a congenital lymphatic disorder present at birth or early infancy, often with asymmetric presentation, which does not match this timeline. E is incorrect because secondary lymphedema in a 16-year-old would typically have identifiable underlying causes like malignancy, trauma, or infection, and the strong family history points toward primary lymphedema.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old male patient receives microdermabrasion treatment for irregular scarring after facial skin cancer therapy. Which of the following operative observations indicates the proper termination point for the procedure?
A) Yellow, cobblestone-textured fat tissue
B) Continuous bleeding pools against a yellow tissue backdrop
C) Sparse dermal tissue with exposed subdermal vessel network
D) Small, dot-like bleeding points on a white tissue surface
E) Reduced but intact epidermal layer
questions.answer:
D)
The appropriate endpoint for microdermabrasion is achieving removal into the papillary dermis, which appears as punctate bleeding spots against a white dermal background. This depth allows for optimal healing while preserving adnexal structures necessary for re-epithelialization. A is incorrect because yellow cobblestone fat indicates excessive depth into subcutaneous tissue, risking significant deformity. B is incorrect because confluent bleeding pools on yellow background suggests removal into reticular dermis, increasing scarring risk. C is incorrect because visible subdermal plexus indicates near-complete dermal removal, which is too deep and compromises healing. E is incorrect because intact epidermis means insufficient treatment depth for effective scar revision.

questions.question:
A 9-month-old infant undergoes repair of the palatal defect shown in the photograph using a Furlow palatoplasty. Which of the following best represents this patient's risk for developing a palatal fistula postoperatively?


A) 5%
B) 10%
C) 15%
D) 20%
E) 25%
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


This cleft involves both the soft and posterior hard palate, but does not extend into the alveolus or primary palate (Veau class II). Based on several recent studies, including a large systematic review, the rate of fistula formation following a Furlow repair of a Veau class II palatal cleft is 5% or less.


ReferencesHardwicke JT, Landini G, Richard BM. Fistula incidence after primary cleft palate repair: a systematic review of the literature. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2014;134(4):618e-627e.Jackson O, Stransky CA, Jawad AF, et al. The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia modification of the Furlow double-opposing Z-palatoplasty: 30-year experience and long-term speech outcomes. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2013;132(3):613-622.Losken HW, van Aalst JA, Teotia SS, Dean SB, Hultman S, Uhrich KS. Achieving low cleft palate fistula rates: surgical results and techniques. Cleft Palate Craniofac J. 2011;48(3):312-320.Bykowski MR, Naran S, Winger DG, Losee JE. The rate of oronasal fistula following primary cleft palate surgery: a meta-analysis. Cleft Palate Craniofac J. 2015 Jul;52(4):e81-7. doi: 10.1597/14-127. Epub 2014 Oct 16.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old construction worker presents for evaluation 12 days following surgical reconstruction of both the flexor digitorum profundus and superficialis tendons (FDP and FDS) in his fifth digit of the non-dominant hand after sustaining a laceration from a sharp object. Early mobilization therapy was started during rehabilitation, but he experienced abrupt loss of both distal and proximal joint flexion the previous day. What is the most appropriate management?
A) Wait 10 weeks before treatment, then insert a silicone rod
B) Stop rehabilitation therapy for 2 weeks, then restart using a Duran passive motion protocol
C) Perform arthrodesis of both the proximal and distal joints of the fifth digit
D) Surgically repair both the FDS and FDP tendons
E) Perform tendon transfer using the FDS from the fourth digit to the FDP of the fifth digit
questions.answer:
D)
Surgical repair of both the FDS and FDP tendons is correct because tendon rupture commonly occurs within the first 6-7 weeks post-repair (most frequently days 7-10), and immediate re-repair yields results comparable to primary repair while maintaining the optimal tissue bed for healing. A is incorrect because delaying treatment for 10 weeks would result in significant tendon retraction and require more complex reconstruction. B is incorrect because passive motion alone will not address the ruptured tendons that require surgical intervention. C is incorrect because joint fusion is reserved as a salvage procedure after failed tendon repairs, not as initial treatment for tendon rupture. E is incorrect because tendon transfer is unnecessary when direct repair is still feasible and will provide superior function with independent finger motion and greater strength.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a fall down stairs where he landed with his hand extended. Radiographic imaging reveals a perilunate dislocation. Along with the scapholunate ligament, which additional ligament must be torn for this injury pattern to develop?
A) Dorsal intercarpal
B) Dorsal radiotriquetral
C) Lunotriquetral
D) Radioscaphocapitate
E) Ulnotriquetral
questions.answer:
C)
Perilunate dislocation represents the most frequent type of carpal dislocation and involves disruption of the ligamentous attachments between the lunate and adjacent carpal bones as well as the radius. For this injury pattern to occur, both the scapholunate and lunotriquetral ligaments must be disrupted, as these are the primary stabilizing structures connecting the lunate to its neighboring bones.
