Treatment typically involves repair of these torn ligaments combined with open reduction and internal fixation. A is incorrect because the dorsal intercarpal ligament does not directly attach to the lunate bone. B is incorrect because the dorsal radiotriquetral ligament connects the radius to the triquetrum, not the lunate. D is incorrect because the radioscaphocapitate ligament connects the radius to the scaphoid and capitate, bypassing the lunate. E is incorrect because the ulnotriquetral ligament connects the ulna to the triquetrum and does not involve the lunate.

questions.question:
Which approach is most successful for enhancing the long-term survival of adipose tissue transplants?
A) Obtain fat from the abdomen as the donor location
B) Extract fat using a manual syringe instead of suction equipment
C) Deliver fat using a gentle, low-trauma injection device
D) Prepare fat using the telfa gauze rolling method
E) Apply tumescent fluid that does not contain lidocaine
questions.answer:
C)
The most effective strategy for improving long-term fat graft survival is using low-shear injection devices, which minimize trauma to adipocytes during placement and thereby enhance cell viability. A is incorrect because the anatomical location of fat harvest does not significantly impact graft survival rates. B is incorrect because studies have not demonstrated that manual syringe harvesting provides superior outcomes compared to suction-based extraction methods. D is incorrect because while some practitioners avoid centrifugation to reduce cellular damage, there is no conclusive evidence that alternative processing techniques like gauze rolling improve fat cell survival. E is incorrect because although lidocaine can temporarily affect adipocyte metabolism, these effects resolve once the anesthetic is cleared from the harvested tissue and do not influence long-term graft viability.

questions.question:
Which statement aligns with The Joint Commission and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services guidelines for provider orders and patient communication?
A) Electronic provider order entry (EPOE) is not recommended for order placement since it permits clinicians to input orders directly into the electronic medical record (EMR)
B) Healthcare facilities should permit unsecured text messaging—specifically, SMS texting from personal mobile phones—for sharing protected health information
C) HIPAA requirements are violated when all data is de-identified prior to transmission
D) Verbal order transmission must include immediate, real-time verification and acknowledgment of the order during delivery by the prescribing provider
questions.answer:
D)
Verbal orders require immediate, synchronous verification and confirmation as they are communicated by the ordering provider, ensuring accuracy and compliance with safety standards. A) is incorrect because electronic provider order entry is actually the preferred method for order submission as it enhances accuracy and provides clinical decision support. B) is incorrect because healthcare organizations must prohibit unsecured text messaging for protected health information to maintain privacy standards. C) is incorrect because HIPAA compliance is actually maintained when information is properly de-identified using methods like the Safe Harbor approach before transmission.

questions.question:
A 59-year-old female patient presents to the clinic seeking assessment for a facelift procedure due to facial aging concerns. The surgical plan includes the application of fibrin adhesive during the rhytidectomy. Which of the following outcomes is most frequently observed with the use of tissue adhesives following facelift surgery?
A) Reduced bruising
B) Shortened duration of tissue firmness
C) Diminished scarring
D) Enhanced fluid drainage
E) Heightened swelling
questions.answer:
A)
Tissue adhesives, including fibrin-based sealants and platelet-rich plasma preparations, have been employed to influence post-rhytidectomy complications such as fluid collection, bruising, and swelling. Clinical studies conducted prospectively have shown reduced rates of bruising, swelling, fluid collection, and extended tissue firmness. While tissue sealants show a tendency toward reducing drainage, this effect is not statistically significant compared to other benefits. These adhesives have not demonstrated any impact on the formation of scars. B) is incorrect because tissue sealants actually help reduce the period of induration rather than having no effect on it. C) is incorrect because research has not shown tissue sealants to influence scar formation outcomes. D) is incorrect because while there may be a trend toward reduced drainage, increased drainage is not associated with tissue sealant use. E) is incorrect because tissue sealants are associated with decreased rather than increased edema.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old female patient receives breast reconstruction utilizing a deep inferior epigastric artery perforator (DIEP) flap. Following the microanastomosis procedure, arterial thrombosis is observed. Which of the following outcomes is more probable when tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) is administered locally as an adjunctive treatment to revision microanastomosis compared to revision microanastomosis performed without tPA?
A) Reduced flap salvage rate
B) Reduced occurrence of fat necrosis
C) Enhanced flap salvage rate
D) Enhanced occurrence of fat necrosis
E) Enhanced occurrence of surgical hematoma
questions.answer:
B)
Local tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) administration during microanastomotic revision results in a reduced rate of subsequent fat necrosis. The proposed mechanism involves thrombolysis of distant microemboli within the microvasculature that can compromise tissue perfusion. A is incorrect because tPA administration does not negatively impact flap salvage rates. C is incorrect because tPA does not improve overall flap salvage rates when used as an adjunct to revision. D is incorrect because tPA actually decreases rather than increases fat necrosis incidence. E is incorrect because the low dose (2 mg) administered locally into the flap artery does not increase hematoma risk, unlike higher systemic doses.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old female patient seeks consultation regarding her breast aesthetics. Physical examination reveals unilateral protrusion of the nipple-areolar complex with constriction of the inferior breast pole. Which of the following surgical techniques would most effectively resolve this patient's aesthetic concerns?
A) Repositioning of the inframammary crease
B) Radial division of constricting tissue bands
C) Nipple-areolar complex skin transplantation
D) Vertical breast lift procedure
E) Wise-pattern breast reduction surgery
questions.answer:
B)
This clinical presentation is characteristic of tuberous breast anomaly. The optimal surgical approach typically involves addressing the periareolar protrusion through periareolar incisions combined with radial division of constricting tissue bands. Option A is incorrect because repositioning the inframammary crease would not resolve the fundamental tuberous deformity and could potentially worsen it. Option C is incorrect because skin transplantation of the nipple-areolar complex would not correct the underlying tissue protrusion. Option D is incorrect because a standard vertical breast lift alone could further restrict the already constricted lower breast pole. Option E is incorrect because reduction mammaplasty would not address the specific anatomical issues characteristic of tuberous breast deformity.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old male patient comes to the clinic with a tender subungual glomus tumor affecting his index finger. What should be the definitive management approach?
A) Chemotherapeutic treatment
B) Total surgical removal
C) External radiation therapy
D) Immunologic therapy
E) Steroid injection into the lesion
questions.answer:
B)
Complete surgical removal is the definitive treatment for subungual glomus tumors. These benign vascular tumors require total excision to prevent recurrence and provide symptom relief. A) Chemotherapy is incorrect because glomus tumors are benign lesions that do not respond to cytotoxic agents. C) External radiation therapy is incorrect as it has no established role in treating these benign vascular tumors. D) Immunotherapy is incorrect since glomus tumors are not malignant and do not require immune system modulation. E) Intralesional steroid injection is incorrect as it does not provide definitive treatment and will not eliminate the tumor.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old female patient with prior breast cancer history arrives for delayed bilateral latissimus dorsi flap reconstruction. Her medical background includes cardiac artery disease, elevated blood pressure, and rheumatoid arthritis. She currently takes aspirin, propranolol, and prednisone, which has been used for 8 years. Before the operation, prednisone is stopped 6 weeks prior and aspirin is halted 1 week beforehand. The surgery proceeds without complications. In the recovery room, her pulse is 115 bpm and blood pressure reads 80/40 mmHg. Clinical assessment reveals no hematoma evidence. Following 3 L of IV fluid resuscitation, hemodynamic status shows no improvement. Chest radiograph, electrocardiogram, hematocrit, serum electrolytes, and cardiac enzymes are within normal limits. Over the following 2 hours, despite escalating vasopressor therapy, hypotension persists. What medication should be given as the most suitable next management step?
A) Dantrolene
B) Desmopressin (DDAVP)
C) Hydrocortisone
D) Insulin and dextrose
E) Labetalol
questions.answer:
C)
The most suitable next management step for this patient with unexplained resistant hypotension and recent prolonged corticosteroid use history is intravenous hydrocortisone administration, presuming adrenal crisis as the diagnosis. This patient demonstrates classic signs of acute adrenal insufficiency following surgical stress in the setting of chronic steroid therapy that suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. The 8-year prednisone use places her at significant risk for adrenal crisis when subjected to surgical stress, and prompt steroid replacement is life-saving. A) Dantrolene is incorrect because it treats malignant hyperthermia, which this patient does not exhibit. B) Desmopressin is incorrect because it addresses bleeding disorders by releasing von Willebrand factor, not hypotension from adrenal insufficiency. D) Insulin and dextrose is incorrect because this combination treats hyperkalemia by shifting potassium intracellularly, not adrenal crisis. E) Labetalol is incorrect because this beta-blocker would further worsen the patient's existing hypotension.

questions.question:
What is the most frequently occurring hyperplastic breast abnormality in pediatric patients?
A) Massive fibroadenoma
B) Male breast enlargement
C) Adolescent breast overgrowth
D) Supernumerary breast tissue
E) Accessory nipples
questions.answer:
B)
Male breast enlargement (gynecomastia) represents the most prevalent hyperplastic breast anomaly in children. Studies demonstrate that hyperplastic conditions constitute the largest category of pediatric breast abnormalities, with gynecomastia being the leading diagnosis, followed by adolescent breast overgrowth. A) Massive fibroadenoma is incorrect because while it can occur in children, it is less common than gynecomastia and patients with this condition are more likely to need revision surgery. C) Adolescent breast overgrowth is incorrect because although it is the second most common hyperplastic anomaly, it occurs less frequently than gynecomastia. D) Supernumerary breast tissue is incorrect because this represents an accessory breast condition rather than a hyperplastic anomaly of existing breast tissue. E) Accessory nipples is incorrect because this is a congenital anomaly involving extra nipples rather than hyperplastic enlargement of breast tissue.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old female presents to the clinic with a newly discovered mass in her right breast occurring 6 weeks following bilateral breast reduction surgery performed using the inferior pedicle method. Her preoperative breast examination revealed no abnormal findings. Physical examination now reveals a firm, painless mass located in the lateral portion of the right upper breast. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Abscess
B) Fat necrosis
C) Fibroadenoma
D) Hematoma
E) Seroma
questions.answer:
B)
A patient who develops a firm, painless mass 6 weeks following breast reduction surgery most likely has fat necrosis. This condition typically results from compromised blood supply to breast tissue areas, leading to hemorrhagic tissue death. Fat liquefaction drainage often represents the initial indication of infection, which may progress to cellulitis and fever. Limited fat necrosis areas can be treated conservatively, with secondary revision procedures performed after 6 months to 1 year. Extensive skin and fat necrosis with associated infection requires surgical removal of dead tissue and antibiotic treatment, followed by secondary closure and grafting once infection resolves. A) Abscess is incorrect because while it would be firm, it would typically be tender and associated with signs of infection. C) Fibroadenoma is incorrect because it would be unlikely to be detectable so soon after surgery. D) Hematoma is incorrect because although it would be firm, it would usually be tender to palpation. E) Seroma is incorrect because it would typically have a softer, more fluctuant consistency rather than being hard.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old mail carrier presents to the emergency room 2 hours following a crushing trauma to his right lower extremity when his delivery vehicle rolled down an incline and trapped him against a barrier. He describes worsening, severe burning pain in his right leg. Physical examination reveals a swollen extremity with a firm, indurated sensation anterolaterally and marked tenderness during passive ankle movement. Numbness is present between the great and second toes. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are palpable. The delta pressure (difference between diastolic blood pressure and anterior compartment pressure) measures 15 mmHg. Radiographic imaging demonstrates no fractures. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Execute immediate fasciotomy
B) Reassess anterior compartment pressure after 1 hour
C) Evaluate electromyographic function of the tibialis anterior
D) Measure serum creatine kinase levels
E) Reduce pain medications to minimize interference with subsequent evaluations
questions.answer:
A)
This patient demonstrates classic findings of developing acute compartment syndrome (ACS), which constitutes a surgical emergency requiring immediate fasciotomy to decompress all affected compartments. The combination of severe pain, tense woody compartment feel, pain with passive motion, sensory changes in the deep peroneal nerve distribution, and a delta pressure of 15 mmHg (well below the critical threshold of 20-30 mmHg) mandates urgent surgical intervention to prevent irreversible tissue damage, muscle necrosis, and permanent functional impairment. B is incorrect because delaying treatment when ACS is clinically evident risks irreversible tissue damage and functional loss. C is incorrect because EMG changes are late findings in compartment syndrome and waiting for these abnormalities would delay necessary treatment. D is incorrect because elevated creatine kinase levels are a late consequence of muscle breakdown and should not delay immediate surgical intervention. E is incorrect because withholding analgesics has no diagnostic value in extremity trauma and may cause unnecessary patient suffering.

questions.question:
A 79-year-old woman comes to the office because of a large scalp defect following Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell carcinoma. A photograph of the defect (left) and a rotation flap designed to cover the defect (right) are shown. At the completion of the procedure, a large ‚Äudog ear‚Äu is noted at the pivot point of the flap. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Burrow triangle
B) Compression
C) Direct excision
D) Staged advancement
E) Observation
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


The most appropriate next step in management is observation. A Burrow triangle would not sufficiently address this deformity and is not necessary. Compression and staged advancement are not necessary, as the deformity resolves spontaneously. The temptation to excise should be resisted, as most of these ?dog ears? resolve over time. Photographs immediately after the procedure (left) and 5 months later (right) are shown.


Excision would only increase the length-to-width ratio and compromise blood supply to the flap. If the contour abnormality is unacceptable to the patient after some time has passed, then excision at a later time can be performed. The need for this is exceedingly rare.

questions.question:
In which of the following surgical procedures is prophylactic systemic antibiotic administration routinely recommended?
A) Tummy tuck surgery
B) Carpal tunnel decompression
C) Removal of skin squamous cell carcinoma
D) Breast reduction surgery
E) Facelift procedure
questions.answer:
D)
Prophylactic systemic antibiotics are routinely recommended for clean breast surgical procedures. Research demonstrates that antibiotic prophylaxis in patients undergoing breast operations (whether with or without implants) substantially decreases surgical site infection rates. While the prophylactic benefit is most pronounced in patients receiving tissue expanders or breast implants during reconstruction, patients having breast augmentation or reduction mammaplasty also derive benefit from antibiotic prophylaxis. Except for cosmetic breast procedures, clean surgical cases have not demonstrated benefit from routine antibiotic prophylaxis. A is incorrect because abdominoplasty is a clean procedure that does not require routine prophylaxis. B is incorrect because carpal tunnel release is a clean hand procedure that does not benefit from routine antibiotic prophylaxis. C is incorrect because excision of skin cancer is a clean procedure that does not require routine prophylaxis. E is incorrect because rhytidectomy is a clean head and neck procedure that does not benefit from routine antibiotic prophylaxis.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male patient comes to the clinic with bruxism and associated pain. Which medication would be the best choice for managing this condition?
A) Amitriptyline
B) Botulinum toxin type A
C) Clonidine
D) Escitalopram
E) Fluoxetine
questions.answer:
B)
Botulinum toxin type A is the most appropriate treatment as it has demonstrated effectiveness in reducing pain associated with bruxism, with benefits extending beyond just addressing masseter muscle hypertrophy. Clinical studies have shown it to be as effective as occlusal splints and superior to placebo in decreasing bruxism-related pain based on visual analogue scale measurements. A) Amitriptyline is incorrect because studies have not shown it to provide pain relief superior to placebo for bruxism. C) Clonidine is incorrect as research has demonstrated no significant improvement in pain relief compared to placebo. D) Escitalopram is incorrect because SSRIs like escitalopram can actually cause bruxism as a side effect. E) Fluoxetine is incorrect since this SSRI is known to potentially induce bruxism rather than treat it.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female patient comes in with symptomatic breast enlargement. Her family history reveals breast cancer in her aunt before menopause. The patient is planned for bilateral breast reduction surgery (utilizing an inferior pedicle technique with Wise pattern incision), and informed consent has been obtained. During the operation, a 3 × 3-cm region of concerning tissue is identified in the left upper outer area. Frozen section analysis reveals a 5-mm invasive ductal carcinoma with clear margins. What is the most appropriate next management step for this patient?
A) Complete bilateral breast reduction surgery with concurrent left axillary sentinel lymph node biopsy
B) Complete bilateral breast reduction surgery with proper specimen orientation, suture marking of the cancer location, and placement of surgical clips
C) Complete bilateral breast reduction surgery, then arrange for immediate adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation treatment
D) Complete bilateral breast reduction surgery while removing an additional 3-cm margin around the cancer area
E) Complete breast reduction on the right side only, then perform left mastectomy
questions.answer:
B)
Option B is correct because when occult breast cancer is discovered during reduction mammaplasty, the appropriate immediate management includes completing the planned bilateral reduction while ensuring proper specimen orientation with suture marking of the cancer site and clip placement for future reference. This allows for appropriate pathological evaluation while maintaining the original surgical plan until multidisciplinary evaluation can be completed. A is incorrect because sentinel lymph node biopsy requires separate consent and multidisciplinary planning that cannot be performed without prior patient consent and oncologic consultation. C is incorrect because adjuvant therapy decisions require comprehensive staging, multidisciplinary team evaluation, and separate patient counseling before implementation. D is incorrect because taking additional 3-cm margins is not the standard approach for a 5-mm invasive cancer and would compromise the reduction mammaplasty results unnecessarily. E is incorrect because immediate mastectomy requires separate informed consent and multidisciplinary oncologic evaluation, which cannot be performed during the same procedure without prior patient agreement.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old male presents with right wrist pain and post-traumatic degenerative changes following a chronic, untreated scapholunate ligament rupture. A salvage proximal row carpectomy is being considered. Which articular surface must remain undamaged for this procedure to be viable?
A) Capitolunate
B) Lunotriquetral
C) Radioscaphoid
D) Scaphotrapezial
E) Trapeziotrapezoid
questions.answer:
A)
The capitolunate joint surface must be preserved and free of arthritis for proximal row carpectomy to be successful. This procedure removes the proximal carpal row (scaphoid, lunate, and triquetrum), allowing the capitate head to articulate directly with the lunate fossa of the radius. The integrity of the capitate head cartilage and radial lunate fossa is essential for the new joint articulation to function properly. B is incorrect because the lunotriquetral joint is removed during the procedure and its condition is not relevant to success. C is incorrect because the radioscaphoid joint is typically already arthritic in SLAC wrist and the scaphoid is excised during surgery. D is incorrect because the scaphotrapezial joint is not involved in the new articulation created by proximal row carpectomy. E is incorrect because the trapeziotrapezoid joint is not part of the radiocarpal articulation that results from this salvage procedure.

questions.question:
A patient presenting with facial hyperkinesia seeks office-based botulinum toxin type A therapy for temporary cosmetic enhancement of moderate to severe glabellar wrinkles. What is the FDA-recommended dosage of botulinum toxin type A for this patient?
A) 1
B) 10
C) 20
D) 50
E) 100
questions.answer:
C)

The FDA-approved dosage for treating moderate to severe glabellar lines is 20 units of botulinum toxin type A, administered as 4 units per injection site across five locations: one injection in the procerus muscle and two injections in each corrugator supercilii muscle. This dosing protocol was established through two identical phase 3 randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. A is incorrect because 1 unit would be therapeutically insufficient for treating glabellar lines. B is incorrect because 10 units falls short of the established effective dose for this indication. D is incorrect because 50 units exceeds the recommended dose and could increase the risk of adverse effects. E is incorrect because 100 units represents a significant overdose that could lead to serious complications including muscle weakness and systemic effects.

questions.question:
Which peeling agent would require neutralization with 1% sodium bicarbonate solution?
A) Glycolic acid
B) Jessner solution
C) Phenol-croton oil
D) Salicylic acid
E) Trichloroacetic acid (TCA)
questions.answer:
A)
Glycolic acid is the correct answer because it is one of the specific acids that requires neutralization with a basic solution like 1% sodium bicarbonate to halt the peeling process and prevent overtreatment. B) Jessner solution is incorrect because it cannot be neutralized and the peeling process must be allowed to run its course. C) Phenol-croton oil is incorrect because these deep peels cannot be neutralized once applied. D) Salicylic acid is incorrect because it is self-neutralizing and does not require external neutralization. E) TCA is incorrect because it penetrates deeply into the dermal-epidermal junction and cannot be neutralized; instead, it is counteracted through dilution with saline solution.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male presents for evaluation of a large tumor in a previously radiated area of the posterolateral thorax. Preoperative ventilation-perfusion imaging and pulmonary function studies show normal results. The surgical plan involves full-thickness chest wall excision including three ribs with at least 10 cm removal of each rib. The anticipated soft-tissue defect measures 20 cm in diameter. Which of the following characteristics in this patient would most likely require rigid chest wall reconstruction?
A) Posterolateral location of the defect
B) History of chest wall radiation treatment
C) Overall size of the chest wall defect
D) Number of ribs being removed
questions.answer:
C)
The overall size of the chest wall defect is the most significant factor determining the need for rigid reconstruction in this extensive anticipated defect. Reconstruction of the lateral bony chest wall is typically required when four or more consecutive ribs are removed or when the total defect diameter exceeds 5 cm. A is incorrect because posterolateral defects are actually better tolerated than lateral defects and less likely to require rigid reconstruction. B is incorrect because patients with prior radiation therapy can often tolerate larger defects without rigid stabilization due to radiation-induced fibrosis that increases chest wall stiffness. D is incorrect because while the number of ribs matters, three ribs alone would not necessarily mandate rigid reconstruction - it is the combination of rib number and total defect size that determines the need for reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 19-year-old collegiate baseball athlete presents for assessment 4 weeks following a jamming injury and dislocation of his middle finger on his dominant right hand that occurred during a slide into home base. The team coach performed field reduction of the dislocation. The patient reports escalating discomfort at the injury location over the previous 2 days. Clinical examination reveals swelling of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint of the middle finger. Lateral stress testing demonstrates 30 degrees of angulation. Radiographic imaging reveals a congruent joint with 1 mm of radial-sided widening. What represents the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Buddy strapping of the middle finger to the index finger
B) Splinting with a dorsal extension blocking device at 30 degrees
C) Casting with a volar forearm splint
D) Percutaneous pin stabilization of the PIP joint for 3 weeks
E) Surgical reconstruction of the radial collateral ligament
questions.answer:
E)
This patient has sustained a complete rupture of the radial collateral ligament at the PIP joint of the middle finger, evidenced by the significant angulation (30 degrees) and joint space widening on imaging, which suggests ligamentous tissue interposition. Complete ligament tears with subluxation and tissue interposition require surgical intervention to restore stability and prevent long-term complications such as chronic pain, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis. A) Buddy strapping is insufficient for complete ligament tears with instability. B) Extension block splinting is appropriate for partial tears but inadequate for complete ruptures with interposition. C) Volar splinting provides insufficient stabilization for this degree of instability. D) Kirschner wire fixation alone does not address the torn ligament and would not restore proper joint mechanics.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient with breast cancer presents for evaluation of bilateral breast reconstruction options. Autologous abdominal tissue reconstruction is being considered. During discussion of potential abdominal complications, which of the following flap procedures is most likely to produce the minimal overall abdominal morbidity?
A) Deep inferior epigastric artery perforator
B) Free muscle-sparing transverse rectus abdominis musculocutaneous (TRAM)
C) Free TRAM
D) Pedicled TRAM
E) Superficial inferior epigastric artery flap
questions.answer:
E)
The superficial inferior epigastric artery (SIEA) flap produces the minimal overall abdominal morbidity because the harvesting technique preserves the abdominal fascia completely intact. However, these vessels are present in fewer than one-third of patients, and only half of those have adequate vessel caliber for free tissue transfer. The SIEA flap also has increased rates of complete flap failure and fat necrosis. A is incorrect because DIEP flap harvesting requires perforator dissection through the rectus muscle, causing moderate trauma and potential abdominal wall complications. B is incorrect because muscle-sparing free TRAM still requires removal of some rectus muscle and fascia for safe perforator transfer. C is incorrect because free TRAM involves taking a portion of the rectus muscle with the flap. D is incorrect because pedicled TRAM requires elevation of the entire rectus muscle (unilateral or bilateral) from its abdominal wall position, resulting in the highest abdominal morbidity.

questions.question:
In which scenario would topical skin adhesive (cyanoacrylate polymer) be most appropriately utilized for wound closure?
A) Stellate tear along the eyebrow region
B) Applied over subcuticular sutures for a vertical forehead wound
C) Covering sutured canine bite injury to the ear
D) Linear laceration on facial cheek with 4 mm gap between edges
E) Approximated lip wound that crosses the vermilion-skin junction
questions.answer:
B)
Cyanoacrylate adhesives are monomeric compounds that undergo polymerization through an exothermic process when exposed to air and moisture. They function effectively as adjuncts to other closure methods like sutures or as standalone closure agents. Research demonstrates their time-saving benefits across various surgical disciplines, with cosmetic outcomes equivalent to or superior to external suturing. Laboratory studies indicate antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, with clinical reports suggesting reduced infection rates. However, using adhesive as the sole closure method increases dehiscence risk, and inadvertent application beneath the skin surface can impede healing and worsen scarring. FDA labeling specifically contraindicates use on mucosal surfaces and contaminated wounds like animal bites. Option A is incorrect because stellate tears lack the smooth epithelial alignment required for adhesive application. Option C is incorrect as FDA guidelines prohibit adhesive use over animal bite repairs. Option D is incorrect since the 4 mm separation prevents proper edge approximation necessary for adhesive effectiveness. Option E is incorrect because vermilion border involvement is specifically contraindicated per manufacturer guidelines.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male patient arrives at the emergency room following a pedestrian-motor vehicle collision. Clinical assessment reveals a Gustilo Type IIIB open tibial fracture. An anterolateral thigh flap reconstruction is being considered. To access the posterior tibial vessels, which anatomical interval would be the most suitable surgical approach?
A) Between the lateral malleolus and Achilles tendon
B) Between the lateral malleolus and extensor hallucis longus tendon
C) Between the medial malleolus and Achilles tendon
D) Between the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus tendons
questions.answer:
C)
The posterior tibial vessels are anatomically positioned in the interval between the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon, making this the correct surgical approach for vessel access. A) is incorrect because this interval contains the sural nerve, not the posterior tibial vessels. B) is incorrect because the greater saphenous vein runs in this location between the lateral malleolus and extensor hallucis longus tendon. D) is incorrect because the dorsalis pedis artery is found between the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus tendons, not the posterior tibial vessels.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female patient is having Stage II alloplastic breast reconstruction surgery. The surgeon accesses the breast pocket by removing the mastectomy scar tissue, separates the muscle and expander capsule, extracts the tissue expanders from both sides, inserts silicone high-profile implants, and sutures the 7-cm incision in multiple layers. The surgeon subsequently performs autologous fat transfer to address medial contour deficiency. What is the most appropriate CPT coding for this surgical procedure?

A) 19380 Revision of reconstructed breast
B) 11970, 19370, 20926, 13102 Replacement of tissue expander with permanent prosthesis, Capsulotomy, Fat grafting, Complex repair
C) 11970, 20926, 13102 Replacement of tissue expander with permanent prosthesis, Fat grafting, Complex repair
D) 11970, 20926 Replacement of tissue expander with permanent prosthesis, Fat grafting
E) 11970, 19370 Replacement of tissue expander with permanent prosthesis, Capsulotomy
questions.answer:
D)

This patient's surgical procedure should be coded using replacement of tissue expander with permanent prosthesis (11970) and autologous fat transfer (20926). The removal of mastectomy scar tissue, typically done before closure, is included within code 11970. In this case, the periprosthetic capsule division does not warrant a separate code since the capsule was opened as part of the surgical approach to access the implant. Code 19380 for revision of reconstructed breast should only be applied when a patient is having revision of an existing reconstruction, not during Stage II alloplastic reconstruction. Option A is incorrect because 19380 applies to revision of existing reconstruction, not Stage II reconstruction. Option B is incorrect because it includes unnecessary codes for capsulotomy (19370) and complex repair (13102) that are bundled into the primary procedure. Option C is incorrect because the complex repair code (13102) is included in the primary procedure and should not be coded separately. Option E is incorrect because capsulotomy (19370) is part of the surgical approach and not separately billable in this context.

questions.question:
Which anatomical region provides the greatest contribution to overall nasal airway resistance?
A) Posterior nasal apertures
B) Internal nasal valve area
C) Keystone region
D) Middle nasal passage
E) Nostril wings
questions.answer:
B)
The internal nasal valve area represents the most constricted part of the nasal passage and contributes roughly 50% of total nasal airway resistance. This region is formed by the nasal septum, the lower edge of the upper lateral cartilage, the pyriform opening, and the front margin of the inferior turbinate. A) is incorrect because the posterior nasal apertures (choanae) typically only cause resistance when blocked by congenital abnormalities like choanal atresia. C) is incorrect because the keystone region is primarily a structural landmark at the junction of bony and cartilaginous components rather than a site of airflow resistance. D) is incorrect because while the middle nasal passage carries most airflow, it is not the primary source of resistance. E) is incorrect because the nostril wings (nasal alae) contribute to external nasal valve function but do not account for the majority of nasal resistance.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male patient receives leuprolide acetate therapy for prostate cancer treatment. What is the most probable breast-related effect this medication will produce?
A) Nipple-areolar complex hyperpigmentation
B) Breast tissue reduction
C) Milk production
D) Breast pain and tenderness
E) Small hemorrhagic spots
questions.answer:
D)
Leuprolide acetate is a synthetic GnRH analog that initially stimulates then suppresses pituitary gonadotropin release, ultimately reducing testosterone and estradiol levels. Despite lowering overall hormone levels, gynecomastia and mastodynia (breast pain/tenderness) are well-documented adverse effects of leuprolide therapy in prostate cancer patients. This occurs due to the complex hormonal changes during treatment initiation. A) is incorrect because nipple-areolar darkening typically occurs during pregnancy or hormonal states not associated with leuprolide. B) is incorrect because leuprolide causes breast enlargement (gynecomastia), not reduction. C) is incorrect because galactorrhea is associated with prolactin-elevating medications or pituitary disorders, not GnRH analogs. E) is incorrect because petechiae are not a recognized breast-related side effect of leuprolide treatment.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old male presents for evaluation of excessive overjet. Cephalometric measurements reveal an SNA angle of 83 degrees (normal 82 ± 3) and an SNB angle of 74 degrees (normal 80 ± 3). What is the most probable underlying etiology of this malocclusion?
A) Protruding maxilla
B) Retrusive maxilla
C) Protruding mandible
D) Retrusive mandible
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is retrusive mandible because the patient demonstrates isolated mandibular deficiency characterized by a reduced SNB angle (74 degrees, below normal range of 80 ± 3) while maintaining a normal SNA angle (83 degrees, within normal range of 82 ± 3). This pattern indicates the mandible is positioned posteriorly relative to the cranial base while the maxilla maintains normal positioning. A) is incorrect because a protruding maxilla would show an elevated SNA angle above normal range. B) is incorrect because a retrusive maxilla would demonstrate a decreased SNA angle below normal range. C) is incorrect because a protruding mandible would present with an increased SNB angle above normal range.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient returns for a follow-up visit 3 months following surgical correction of a complete laceration through his left cheek. During the operation, damage to the parotid duct was identified and surgically repaired. The patient reports feeling well overall, but now experiences trouble playing his trumpet due to his inability to generate adequate air pressure within his oral cavity. Which of the following muscles was most likely transected during the injury?
A) Buccinator
B) Levator labii superioris
C) Masseter
D) Risorius
E) Zygomaticus major
questions.answer:
A)
The buccinator muscle is the sole facial expression muscle responsible for cheek compression, which is crucial for playing wind instruments like the trumpet. Together with the orbicularis oris, the buccinator compresses the lips, both functions being essential for trumpet performance. The buccinator normally assists in forming food boluses during chewing. Anatomically, the parotid duct exits the parotid gland's anterior margin, travels superficial to the masseter muscle toward the middle cheek region, then penetrates through the buccinator muscle substance to reach the oral mucosa at the level of the upper second molar. B is incorrect because the levator labii superioris elevates the upper lip, which would separate rather than compress the lips and release oral pressure. C is incorrect because the masseter is a muscle of mastication that elevates the jaw but plays no role in maintaining intraoral or lip pressure. D is incorrect because the risorius retracts the corner of the mouth laterally, contributing to lip separation and pressure release. E is incorrect because the zygomaticus major elevates and retracts the corner of the mouth, also contributing to lip separation rather than compression.

questions.question:
Which cephalometric reference point forms part of the Frankfort horizontal plane?
A) Nasion
B) Pogonion
C) Point B
D) Porion
E) Sella turcica
questions.answer:
D)

The Frankfort horizontal plane is established by connecting a line from the uppermost border of the external auditory canal (porion) to the lowest point of the orbital rim (orbitale), making porion the correct answer. A) Nasion is incorrect because it serves as an endpoint for the sella-nasion plane, not the Frankfort horizontal. B) Pogonion is incorrect as it represents the most anterior point of the chin and is not involved in defining either major cephalometric reference plane. C) Point B is incorrect because it is located on the mandible and is used in angular measurements like SNB, not in establishing reference planes. E) Sella turcica is incorrect as it forms part of the sella-nasion plane along with nasion, not the Frankfort horizontal plane.

questions.question:
When comparing laser-assisted liposuction to conventional suction-assisted lipectomy, which of the following has been demonstrated to be reduced?
A) Surface irregularities
B) Bruising
C) Pain following surgery
D) Tissue death of skin
E) Post-procedural edema
questions.answer:
C)
The correct answer is C because a prospective, randomized, double-blind clinical trial demonstrated that laser-assisted lipoplasty resulted in significantly reduced postoperative pain compared to traditional suction-assisted lipoplasty. A is incorrect because no significant difference in cosmetic outcomes or contour irregularities was observed between the two techniques. B is incorrect because bruising (ecchymosis) showed no significant difference between laser-assisted and suction-assisted methods. D is incorrect because skin necrosis was not identified as a differentiating factor between the two approaches in the study. E is incorrect because edema levels were comparable between both surgical techniques with no significant reduction noted.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male seeks evaluation for surgical removal of a large abdominal skin fold. His mother has a documented history of malignant hyperthermia. Which of the following most accurately characterizes the hereditary transmission pattern of this disorder?
A) Autosomal dominant
B) Autosomal recessive
C) Mitochondrial
D) X-linked dominant
E) X-linked recessive
questions.answer:
A)
Malignant hyperthermia follows an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern, meaning that according to Mendelian genetics principles, when one parent carries a confirmed diagnosis, each biological offspring has a 50% probability of inheriting the affected gene. This life-threatening condition involves a hypermetabolic response to certain volatile anesthetic agents and succinylcholine in individuals with this inherited muscle disorder. B) is incorrect because autosomal recessive inheritance would require both parents to carry the gene for expression in offspring. C) is incorrect because mitochondrial inheritance is passed exclusively through the maternal line and affects all offspring. D) is incorrect because X-linked dominant inheritance would show different patterns between male and female offspring and is not the mechanism for malignant hyperthermia. E) is incorrect because X-linked recessive inheritance primarily affects males and follows a different transmission pattern than observed with malignant hyperthermia.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male presents following multiple gunshot injuries to his right lower extremity and thigh region. Radiographic imaging reveals no remaining projectiles and no bone fractures. Physical examination demonstrates a warm foot with detectable pulses at the ankle level. The patient can extend his toes, perform ankle dorsiflexion, and evert his ankle. However, he cannot flex his toes. Sensation remains intact over the top of his foot and the innermost portion of the arch as well as the outermost mid and rear foot areas. Which nerve is most likely damaged in this case?
A) Common peroneal nerve
B) Femoral nerve
C) Saphenous nerve
D) Sural nerve
E) Tibial nerve
questions.answer:
E)
The tibial nerve is most likely injured because the patient cannot flex his toes, which is the primary function of muscles innervated by this nerve in the deep posterior compartment. The preserved sensation in the described areas and the location of injury distal to the sural nerve branch are consistent with tibial nerve damage. A) Common peroneal nerve is incorrect because this nerve controls dorsiflexion and eversion (which are intact) and provides sensation to the dorsal foot. B) Femoral nerve is incorrect because it primarily innervates the quadriceps and provides thigh sensation, not toe flexion. C) Saphenous nerve is incorrect because it only provides sensation to the medial foot and has no motor function. D) Sural nerve is incorrect because it provides sensation to the lateral foot and some motor function to the gastrocnemius, but not toe flexion.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male patient with chemical burns covering 60% of his body surface area needs skin grafting to correct ectropion following 8 weeks of intensive care treatment. During anesthetic administration, which medication is most likely to cause harmful effects in this patient?
A) Atropine
B) Diazepam
C) Enflurane
D) Pentobarbital
E) Succinylcholine
questions.answer:
E)
Succinylcholine is the correct answer because it can cause life-threatening hyperkalemia in burn patients with prolonged hospitalizations. The upregulation of acetylcholine receptors leads to excessive potassium release from muscle cells when depolarizing neuromuscular blockers like succinylcholine are used, potentially causing fatal cardiac arrhythmias. A) Atropine is incorrect because belladonna alkaloids are safe in young, healthy burn patients and are commonly used to manage heart rate and prevent nausea. B) Diazepam is incorrect because benzodiazepines are well-tolerated anxiolytic agents in all patient types, including burn patients, with no increased risk of adverse effects. C) Enflurane is incorrect because while halothane can cause malignant hyperthermia, this is due to genetic predisposition rather than burn injury status. D) Pentobarbital is incorrect because although IV barbiturates cause respiratory depression and prolonged recovery, they remain safe in young patients including those with burns.

questions.question:
Which anatomical structures form a continuous connection with the superficial musculoaponeurotic system?
A) Parotidomasseteric fascia and deep cervical fascia
B) Superficial layer of deep temporal fascia and deep cervical fascia
C) Superficial layer of deep temporal fascia and platysma
D) Temporalis muscle and platysma
E) Temporal parietal fascia and platysma
questions.answer:
E)
The superficial musculoaponeurotic system maintains continuity with the temporoparietal fascia in the superior direction and the platysma muscle in the inferior direction. From superior to inferior, the superficial layer that connects with the superficial musculoaponeurotic system includes the galea, temporoparietal fascia, facial superficial musculoaponeurotic system, platysma, and superficial cervical fascia. A is incorrect because the parotidomasseteric fascia and deep cervical fascia are part of the deeper fascial layer, not continuous with the superficial musculoaponeurotic system. B is incorrect because while the superficial layer of deep temporal fascia is involved in facial anatomy, it does not directly connect with the superficial musculoaponeurotic system, and the deep cervical fascia belongs to the deeper layer. C is incorrect because the superficial layer of deep temporal fascia becomes the parotidomasseteric fascia and is not directly continuous with the superficial musculoaponeurotic system. D is incorrect because the temporalis muscle lies beneath the deep temporal fascia and is therefore positioned deep to the superficial musculoaponeurotic system, not continuous with it.

questions.question:
Among the following basal cell carcinoma variants, which one carries the smallest likelihood of local recurrence?
A) Sclerosing
B) Nodular
C) Infiltrating
D) Morpheaform
E) Micronodular
questions.answer:
B)

Nodular basal cell carcinoma represents the subtype with the lowest recurrence risk among the options listed. This variant typically has well-defined borders and grows in a more predictable pattern, making complete surgical excision more achievable and reducing the likelihood of residual tumor cells that could lead to recurrence.

A) Sclerosing subtype is incorrect because it is classified as a high-risk variant with aggressive growth patterns and poorly defined margins that increase recurrence potential. C) Infiltrating subtype is incorrect as it demonstrates invasive growth characteristics with irregular borders, making complete removal more challenging and recurrence more likely. D) Morpheaform subtype is incorrect because it exhibits aggressive behavior with strand-like growth patterns that extend beyond clinically apparent borders, significantly increasing recurrence risk. E) Micronodular subtype is incorrect as it shows aggressive features with small nodular aggregates that can extend beyond visible tumor margins, leading to higher recurrence rates.

questions.question:
In adolescence, which hormone is primarily responsible for glandular bud formation in breast tissue?
A) Estrogen
B) Follicle-stimulating hormone
C) Oxytocin
D) Progesterone
E) Prolactin
questions.answer:
D)
Progesterone is responsible for the development of glandular buds in breast tissue during adolescence. Estrogen is incorrect because it primarily controls mammary duct elongation and branching rather than glandular bud formation. Follicle-stimulating hormone is incorrect because it regulates ovarian function and follicle development, not direct breast glandular development. Oxytocin is incorrect because it functions in milk ejection during lactation, not in pubertal breast development. Prolactin is incorrect because it primarily stimulates milk production after childbirth rather than glandular bud development during puberty.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 3-year history of a raised, dark brown lesion on her back. The lesion is not painful and does not bleed. A photograph is shown. An excisional biopsy is performed. Pathologic examination shows proliferation of cells from the basal layer of the epidermis with cystic inclusions. The lesion exhibits hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and papillomatosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?


A) Basal cell carcinoma
B) Malignant melanoma
C) Nevus sebaceous
D) Seborrheic keratosis
E) Verrucous carcinoma
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


The lesion is a seborrheic keratosis, also known as verruca senilis or pigmented papilloma. Seborrheic keratoses are common benign lesions that may begin to appear during the fifth decade of life. They arise from the basal layer of the epidermis and are composed of well-differentiated basal cells. They often contain cystic ‚Äuinclusions‚Äu of keratinous material called ‚Äuhorn cysts.‚Äu Lesions exhibit hyperkeratosis (thickening of the stratum corneum), acanthosis (diffuse epidermal hyperplasia and thickening of the skin), and papillomatosis (skin surface elevation). The growth and depth of pigmentation vary directly with exposure to sunlight. If left untreated, they will enlarge gradually and increase in thickness. Seborrheic keratoses typically do not involute spontaneously. They may appear on the head, neck, and trunk after age 50 years and are often distinctly marked and have a waxy, stuck-on appearance. The surface is soft and oily to the touch. Sizes can range from 1 mm to 5 cm. No treatment is necessary, but these lesions are cosmetically unappealing, and for that reason alone, patients may request to have them removed. It is extremely rare for cutaneous malignancies to develop within seborrheic keratoses.


A verrucous carcinoma is a variant of squamous cell carcinoma. As such, it requires wide local excision with negative margins for treatment.


Nevus sebaceous (Jadassohn nevus) may be described as cerebriform, nodular, or verrucous. It is hairless and can appear on the scalp, face, or neck. When present at birth, it persists throughout life and tends to become more verrucous and nodular during the growth phase associated with puberty. Over time, these lesions are associated with a risk of basal cell carcinoma, which occurs in approximately 15 to 20%. Keratoacanthoma and squamous cell carcinoma may also develop, although with much less frequency than basal cell carcinoma. Because of the risk of malignant transformation, complete excision is generally recommended.


Melanoma results from malignant transformation of the melanocyte; the pigment-producing cell of the body can occur anywhere melanocytes are present, including skin, eye, and the mucous membranes of the upper digestive tract, sinuses, anus, and vagina. The incidence of cutaneous melanoma in the United States has increased steadily over the past 50 years and is now 15 per 100,000. Worldwide, the incidence of melanoma is generally reflective of variation in genetic, phenotypic, and ultraviolet (UV) exposure risk factors. Major risk factors include exposure to UV radiation and genetic predisposition. The exposure risk primarily involves intermittent, damaging exposure to the sun such that history of a severe sunburn (blistering or pain for more than 2 days), even in youth, confers an approximately twofold increase in risk. Patients who have fair skin, blue eyes, red hair, and are prone to freckling are at increased risk for melanoma. Mutations in two genes are associated with hereditary melanoma predisposition.


References
1. Saltz R, Ohana BMB. Dermatology for Plastic Surgeons I ‚Äi Skin care and Benign Dermatologic Conditions. In: Thorne CH, Chung KC, Gosain AK, et al, eds. Grabb and Smith‚Äos Plastic Surgery. 7th ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2014:105-114.
2. Zbar RI. Skin Tumors I: Basal and Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Selected Readings, Volume 10, Number 3, Part I, 2004.
3. Ceradini DJ, Blechman KM. Dermatology for Plastic Surgeons II ‚Äi Cutaneous Malignancies. In: Thorne CH, Chung KC, Gosain AK, et al, eds. Grabb and Smith‚Äos Plastic Surgery. 7th ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2014:115-126.

questions.question:
A 57-year-old male patient requires reconstruction following excision of a malignant tumor that involves the mandible. The patient is a non-smoker. Which of the following reconstructive options is most suitable for addressing the mandibular defect extending from ramus to ramus?
A) Allograft bone with scapular free flap
B) Free fibula flap
C) Anterolateral thigh flap with rib graft
D) Pectoralis major myocutaneous flap with reconstruction plate
E) Radial forearm osteocutaneous free flap
questions.answer:
B)
The free fibula flap is the optimal choice for reconstructing an extensive ramus-to-ramus mandibular defect. This flap provides a substantial length of vascularized bone along with a skin paddle for comprehensive reconstruction. B is correct because the fibular flap offers the longest segment of vascularized bone available for mandibular reconstruction, making it ideal for large defects. A is incorrect because scapular flaps require patient repositioning and cannot provide sufficient vascularized bone for such extensive defects. C is incorrect because the anterolateral thigh flap lacks vascularized bone, and non-vascularized rib grafts are inadequate for large mandibular reconstructions. D is incorrect because pectoralis major flaps are historically used but have high failure rates over reconstruction plates and are inferior to vascularized bone flaps. E is incorrect because radial forearm osteocutaneous flaps provide limited bone stock insufficient for ramus-to-ramus defects.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old female patient experiences trauma to her right thigh. Following wound debridement, she develops a 15 × 25-cm defect on the anterior thigh two days post-injury, with exposed adipose tissue and muscle visible. What is the most suitable treatment approach for achieving wound closure?
A) Free latissimus dorsi muscle flap
B) Full-thickness skin graft
C) Local fasciocutaneous flap
D) Negative pressure wound therapy
E) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
E)
Split-thickness skin grafts are the optimal choice for covering extensive wound areas. These grafts, typically harvested at 8/1000th to 14/1000th inch thickness using a mechanical dermatome, can be meshed at ratios of 1:1.5, 1:2, or 1:3 to maximize coverage area per harvested unit. Success requires a viable, infection-free wound bed and proper graft immobilization through negative pressure therapy or tie-over bolster dressing. The thigh's abundant soft tissue makes skin grafting sufficient rather than requiring flap reconstruction. A) Free latissimus dorsi flap is unnecessarily complex when viable tissue exists at the wound base without exposed vital structures. B) Full-thickness skin graft is impractical for such a large defect due to limited donor site availability and the significant secondary defect it would create. C) Local fasciocutaneous flap would require extensive tissue mobilization and create a large donor defect requiring grafting. D) Negative pressure wound therapy alone would result in prolonged healing by secondary intention with significant scarring rather than definitive closure.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old female presents to the emergency room with dyspnea and right chest pain occurring 2 days following an uncomplicated tummy tuck procedure. Vital signs reveal pulse 100 bpm, respirations 20/min, BP 110/60 mmHg, and O2 saturation 92% on ambient air. Chest radiograph demonstrates no abnormal findings. Laboratory results show serum creatinine level of 2.5 mg/dL. What represents the most suitable initial management approach?
A) CT pulmonary angiogram
B) Urgent cardiac catheterization
C) Enoxaparin administration
D) Bilateral leg venous ultrasound
E) V/Q lung scan
questions.answer:
E)
The most suitable initial management approach is obtaining a V/Q lung scan. This patient exhibits classic signs of pulmonary embolism following major surgery. The normal chest radiograph excludes obvious pulmonary pathology such as pneumonia or pneumothorax. While CT pulmonary angiogram would typically be preferred, the elevated creatinine level (2.5 mg/dL) indicates renal impairment, making contrast administration risky. V/Q scanning is ideal for patients with kidney dysfunction since the perfusion component uses radioactive tracers rather than nephrotoxic contrast agents, allowing safe evaluation of PE probability. A is incorrect because CT angiography requires contrast dye which could worsen existing renal insufficiency. B is incorrect because this presentation suggests venous thromboembolism rather than acute coronary syndrome. C is incorrect because enoxaparin is contraindicated in renal insufficiency due to impaired clearance and bleeding risk. D is incorrect because while lower extremity Doppler may eventually be needed, it doesn't diagnose PE and isn't the priority first step.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old male patient has undergone surgical repair of an extensor tendon laceration affecting his middle finger on the dorsal aspect of his left hand. He desires the fastest possible restoration of hand function. What is the optimal splinting immobilization approach?
A) Static extension splinting for 4 weeks
B) Static extension splinting for 6 weeks
C) Dynamic extension splinting for 6 weeks
D) Relative motion extension splinting for 6 weeks
E) No splinting required
questions.answer:
D)
The optimal treatment approach is relative motion extension splinting for 6 weeks. This technique permits immediate controlled active movement by positioning the injured tendon in 15-20 degrees less extension compared to adjacent tendons, which significantly reduces mechanical stress on the repair. The splint maintains the repaired middle finger extensor tendon in 15-20 degrees greater metacarpophalangeal extension than neighboring extensor tendons while allowing complete interphalangeal joint mobility. A wrist component accompanies the finger splint for the initial 3 weeks, followed by finger splinting alone for an additional 3 weeks. This protocol enables earlier motion recovery and faster return to activities. A) is incorrect because static extension splinting for 4 weeks provides inadequate protection duration and prevents beneficial early motion. B) is incorrect because while 6 weeks of static extension splinting offers appropriate protection time, it causes unnecessary stiffness from prolonged immobilization. C) is incorrect because dynamic extension splinting is primarily indicated for extensor pollicis longus injuries or cases involving all six finger extensors, not single finger extensor repairs. E) is incorrect because absence of immobilization significantly increases rupture risk and repair failure.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a motorcycle accident with trauma to his right upper limb. Initial examination reveals a paralyzed and numb right arm, while radiographic imaging demonstrates no fractures. Nerve conduction testing performed one month later demonstrates intact sensory nerve action potentials but shows fibrillation potentials and denervation changes in motor responses from paraspinal muscles, biceps, triceps, and deltoid. Where is the nerve lesion most likely situated?
A) Anterior division
B) C5 and C6 trunk
C) Lateral cord
D) Preganglionic root
E) Subscapular nerve
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is preganglionic root injury. In preganglionic (supraganglionic) lesions, the nerve root is torn away from the spinal cord proximal to the dorsal root ganglion. This disrupts motor fibers from anterior horn cells while leaving sensory cell bodies at the dorsal root ganglion intact, resulting in preserved sensory nerve action potentials but absent motor responses with denervation changes in paraspinal and limb muscles. A is incorrect because anterior division injuries would affect both motor and sensory potentials. B is incorrect because C5-C6 trunk lesions would spare triceps function and show different electrophysiologic patterns. C is incorrect because lateral cord injuries would not involve paraspinal muscles and would show different sensory/motor patterns. E is incorrect because subscapular nerve injury would only affect specific muscles innervated by this nerve, not the widespread pattern described.

questions.question:
A healthy 38-year-old female smoker is contemplating implant-based breast reconstruction after mastectomy. She has received counseling regarding the probable use of acellular dermal matrix during tissue expander placement and seeks additional information about why this matrix will be utilized. This patient should be informed that acellular dermal matrix usage is linked to a reduced risk of which of the following?
A) Malignancy recurrence
B) Capsular contracture
C) Seroma formation
D) Skin flap necrosis
E) Tobacco-related complications
questions.answer:
B)
Acellular dermal matrix (ADM) utilization has been growing in frequency with tissue expander or implant-based breast reconstruction after mastectomies. Various potential benefits and drawbacks have been investigated, with some conflicting data. Nevertheless, the literature consensus demonstrates that ADMs are linked to reduced capsular contracture rates. Studies suggest that seroma formation rates are elevated or unchanged, not reduced, with ADM use, making C incorrect. ADMs have not been demonstrated to reduce inherent patient risk factors for complications like smoking or decrease malignancy recurrence rates, making A and E incorrect. ADMs also do not seem to enhance vascular supply to overlying tissues when initially implanted, making D incorrect.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old female patient comes to the clinic with persistent, small ulcerations on her right index and middle finger tips that fail to heal. Her past medical history is significant for limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis diagnosed 5 years prior, ongoing pain, and finger color alterations when exposed to cold. Her symptoms have shown no improvement despite treatment with nifedipine. Vascular imaging reveals widespread arterial constriction without discrete stenotic areas. What is the most suitable treatment approach for managing her pain and promoting ulcer healing?
A) Cervical sympathetic nerve ablation
B) Prolonged brachial plexus nerve block
D) Onabotulinum toxin A injection
C) Digital artery bypass surgery
E) Stellate ganglion nerve block
questions.answer:
D)
Onabotulinum toxin A is the most appropriate intervention because it has demonstrated efficacy in improving digital blood flow via laser Doppler studies, reducing pain symptoms, and facilitating ulcer healing in scleroderma-associated Raynaud's phenomenon. Clinical studies show that 50-100 units of onabotulinum toxin A results in complete ulcer healing within 60 days in all treated patients, with rapid pain relief occurring within 5-10 minutes and minimal complications. Patients with limited scleroderma and shorter disease duration respond best to this treatment. A is incorrect because cervical sympathectomy is not the standard approach and carries higher surgical risks. B is incorrect because continuous brachial plexus blockade provides only temporary perfusion improvement and is primarily used during microvascular procedures, not for chronic management. C is incorrect because digital bypass is not indicated when distal target vessels are small and have inadequate flow, as shown by the diffuse narrowing on angiography. E is incorrect because stellate ganglion blocks provide only inconsistent and short-term relief without promoting ulcer healing, and may not interrupt all sympathetic innervation to the hand.

questions.question:
A 3-year-old patient presents with funnel chest deformity and is being considered for surgical repair of the chest wall abnormality. The patient has been experiencing minor breathing difficulties. What represents the most appropriate timing for intervention in this case?
A) Operative repair during ages 2 to 5 years
B) Operative repair during ages 6 to 12 years
C) Operative repair during ages 13 to 17 years
D) Operative repair after complete skeletal development
questions.answer:
B)
The most appropriate timing for pectus excavatum repair is during mid-childhood, typically between 6 and 12 years of age. This timing allows for optimal chest wall remodeling while the cartilage remains flexible, and provides the best long-term outcomes with modern minimally invasive techniques like the Nuss procedure. Option A is incorrect because repair before age 6 may result in recurrence as the chest wall continues rapid growth. Option C is incorrect because adolescent repair, while possible, may be more challenging due to increased chest wall rigidity and higher complication rates. Option D is incorrect because waiting until skeletal maturity makes repair significantly more difficult due to calcified cartilage and reduced remodeling potential.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old male patient has undergone decompressive craniectomy following traumatic brain injury and has now fully recovered. The overlying soft tissue at the skull defect site is in good condition with no connection to the paranasal sinuses. Reconstruction using an alloplastic cranioplasty material is being considered. A material with excellent osteoconductive characteristics is preferred. Which of the following represents the best option?
A) Hydroxyapatite
B) Polyetheretherketone
C) Polymethylmethacrylate
D) Porous polyethylene
E) Titanium
questions.answer:
A)
Hydroxyapatite is the optimal choice due to its superior osteoconductive properties among available alloplastic materials. As a calcium phosphate compound with bone-like chemical composition, it promotes bone integration and growth. It can be molded during surgery or fabricated as custom ceramic implants, though its brittleness may require titanium mesh reinforcement for structural support. B) is incorrect because PEEK, while strong and radiolucent, lacks osteoconductive properties. C) is incorrect because PMMA, despite being commonly used and mechanically strong, does not possess osteoconductive capabilities. D) is incorrect because porous polyethylene, although allowing tissue ingrowth and having good biocompatibility, does not have osteoconductive properties. E) is incorrect because titanium, while biocompatible and strong with low infection rates, does not provide osteoconductive benefits.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old male smoker experiences a degloving trauma to his left foot following a motorcycle accident. The heel was torn away from the calcaneus through a deep posterior wound but maintains adequate capillary refill. While no tissue loss occurred, the injury is severely contaminated and the calcaneus shows abrasions with embedded debris. Following operative irrigation and debridement, what represents the most suitable subsequent management approach for this injury?
A) Free gracilis muscle flap reconstruction
B) Secondary intention healing
C) Primary layered repair with drainage
D) Vacuum-assisted closure therapy followed by skin grafting
E) Staged debridement with delayed primary closure
questions.answer:
E)
Staged debridement with delayed primary closure is the optimal management strategy. Given the extensive contamination of both soft tissue and bone, immediate layered repair following initial debridement carries a high risk of infection, particularly in this smoking patient. A is incorrect because free tissue transfer should not be performed in heavily contaminated wounds, and there is no tissue loss or ischemia requiring flap coverage. B is incorrect because while secondary healing is possible, staged debridement with delayed closure offers faster healing, reduced pain, and prevents heel scar contracture. C is incorrect because primary closure in a contaminated wound significantly increases infection risk. D is incorrect because negative pressure therapy with skin grafting is inappropriate for deep wounds with bone exposure when viable local tissue remains available for closure - this approach is better suited for superficial wounds with skin defects.

questions.question:
A 2-month-old girl is presented to the clinic for assessment of a vascular lesion on her right mid-cheek that has been growing steadily since she was 3 weeks old. Clinical examination reveals a raised, 1-cm diameter lesion measuring 1 cm in height. What is the most suitable approach to management at this point?
A) Intralesional corticosteroid injection
B) Surgical excision
C) Systemic sirolimus treatment
D) Systemic corticosteroid treatment
E) Watchful waiting
questions.answer:
E)
Watchful waiting is the most appropriate management for this small, asymptomatic infantile hemangioma. These vascular proliferative lesions typically appear in the first weeks of life, undergo a growth phase, and then spontaneously involute in most cases. Treatment is only indicated when complications arise such as ulceration, bleeding, visual impairment, or feeding difficulties. Since this lesion is small and causing no symptoms, observation with expectation of natural resolution is the best approach. A) Intralesional corticosteroid injection is incorrect because it's reserved for symptomatic or problematic hemangiomas, not small asymptomatic ones. B) Surgical excision is incorrect as it's typically used for residual tissue after involution or for urgent complications, not as first-line treatment for small lesions. C) Systemic sirolimus treatment is incorrect because sirolimus is used for complex lymphatic and vascular malformations, not infantile hemangiomas. D) Systemic corticosteroid treatment is incorrect because it's reserved for hemangiomas causing significant complications or functional impairment, not small asymptomatic lesions.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old male presents to the clinic with fever and worsening pain one week following partial ear amputation sustained from a bite injury during an altercation. The wound underwent irrigation and repair in the emergency room. His temperature is 100.4°F (38.0°C). Physical examination reveals redness and edema of the entire ear with a small dehiscent area containing purulent drainage along the posterior suture line. What is the most crucial management step?
A) Use of moist-to-dry wound dressings
B) Complete amputation while preserving cartilage in a distant subcutaneous pocket
C) Administration of intravenous antibiotics
D) Wound irrigation, debridement, and open packing
E) Treatment with oral antibiotics
questions.answer:
D)
This patient has auricular chondritis/perichondritis, a severe surgical infection requiring immediate operative intervention as the primary treatment in trauma cases. Surgical drainage through irrigation, debridement, and open packing is essential for treating infected cartilage. Culture specimens should be obtained to guide antibiotic selection for associated soft tissue infection. A) is incorrect because topical dressings alone without surgical opening and drainage of infected cartilage will be ineffective. B) is incorrect because completing amputation is overly aggressive when tissues remain viable; cartilage salvage would also be risky given the active infection. C) is incorrect because intravenous antibiotics alone, while important as adjunctive therapy, are insufficient without surgical drainage for localized suppurative chondritis. E) is incorrect because oral antibiotics alone are inadequate for treating this serious cartilage infection that requires surgical intervention.

questions.question:
A 49-year-old male presents to the clinic with a dull, throbbing discomfort on the top surface of his foot. Electrodiagnostic testing reveals normal findings for nerves surrounding the knee, but demonstrates chronic denervation changes in the extensor digitorum brevis muscle on the foot's dorsal aspect. Which nerve is most likely compressed?
A) Anterior tibial
B) Deep peroneal
C) Lesser saphenous
D) Medial plantar
E) Medial sural
questions.answer:
B)
The deep peroneal nerve travels from the anterior compartment muscles of the leg and passes under the ankle's extensor retinaculum. This nerve provides motor innervation to the extensor digitorum brevis muscle before ending in the first web space of the foot, coursing beneath the extensor hallucis brevis tendon. Compression of this nerve at the extensor retinaculum can cause pain, motor weakness, or sensory disturbances on the foot's dorsal surface. A) The anterior tibial nerve is not the correct terminology for this anatomical region. C) The lesser saphenous nerve provides sensation to the posterolateral lower leg, not motor function to dorsal foot muscles. D) The medial plantar nerve innervates plantar foot structures, not the extensor digitorum brevis on the dorsum. E) The medial sural nerve supplies sensation to the posterior-lateral lower leg area, not motor innervation to dorsal foot muscles.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male patient has surgical removal of an aggressive floor-of-mouth malignancy that includes excision of a mandibular segment containing teeth. Immediate reconstruction is completed using a fibular free flap. Dental rehabilitation with osseointegrated implants is being considered. Which of the following characteristics of the fibular flap will most likely provide optimal primary stability for the dental implants?
A) Trabecular (cancellous) bone density
B) Cortical bone density
C) Periosteal layer density
D) Overall bone density
E) Overall bone diameter
questions.answer:
B)
Cortical bone density is the most critical factor for achieving superior primary stability of dental implants. The fibula's thick cortex allows bicortical engagement, and when implants are inserted into dense cortical bone, enhanced initial fixation occurs at the implant-bone interface, minimizing micromotion during the osseointegration phase. Cortical density also correlates with higher insertion and removal torque values. A) Trabecular (cancellous) bone density is incorrect because, although cancellous bone contains osteogenic cells that contribute to biologic healing and later osseointegration, it does not provide the mechanical interlock that cortical bone offers at the time of placement. C) Periosteal layer density is incorrect because the periosteum contributes to flap vascularity and bone healing but does not directly influence implant primary stability. D) Overall bone density is incorrect because studies show no significant relationship between total (combined cortical plus cancellous) bone density and implant removal torque; the cortical component drives stability. E) Overall bone diameter is incorrect because bone width alone, without adequate cortical thickness and quality, does not determine primary stability.

questions.question:
A 77-year-old male patient has undergone extensive local resection of a melanoma located on his posterior shoulder region. A concurrent sentinel lymph node biopsy reveals metastatic disease. Subsequently, he receives complete axillary lymph node dissection followed by adjuvant radiotherapy to the axillary region. Systemic staging workup demonstrates no evidence of distant disease. Following surgery, the patient develops a persistent draining fluid collection and non-healing axillary wound. He is consulted for management of this radiation-induced wound after conservative local care has proven unsuccessful. Clinical examination reveals a 2-cm open axillary defect that extends 5 cm deep toward the apex, surrounded by significant scarring and inflammation. Which of the following treatment approaches is most likely to achieve complete wound healing?
A) Delivery of 30 sessions of hyperbaric oxygen therapy at 2.4 atmospheres absolute
B) Implementation of negative pressure wound therapy
C) Debridement of the wound cavity followed by full-thickness skin graft coverage
D) Debridement of wound margins with placement of acellular dermal matrix
E) Extensive resection of radiated tissues with reconstruction using a thoracodorsal artery perforator flap
questions.answer:
E)
