questions.answer:
D)

The primary benefit of ultrasound-assisted liposuction compared to suction-assisted liposuction is reduced operator exhaustion. In conventional SAL, fat removal requires repetitive manual movements to break up adipose tissue before suction aspiration. UAL uses ultrasonic energy to emulsify fat, eliminating the need for vigorous manual manipulation and significantly reducing physical strain on the surgeon. This technology is particularly helpful in fibrous regions or areas with scar tissue from previous procedures. A is incorrect because evidence-based studies show no consistent aesthetic advantages of UAL over SAL. B is incorrect because skin tightening results are not superior with UAL technology. C is incorrect because patient satisfaction rates are similar between techniques and depend more on surgical skill than technology choice. E is incorrect because complication rates are comparable between UAL and SAL when performed properly.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old woman is evaluated in the emergency department because of necrotizing fasciitis of the right upper extremity. BMI is 35 kg/m2. After adequate debridement, the entire extensor and flexor compartments are open with exposed tendon. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial method of reconstruction?


A) Anterolateral thigh free flap
B) Bilaminate neodermis
C) Full-thickness skin grafts
D) Pedicled abdominal flap
E) Split-thickness skin grafts
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


Although a bilaminate neodermis (Integra) artificial skin substitute has been traditionally used in the acute management of burns, there have been many successful reports incorporating its use in general reconstructive plastic surgery. Integra is a bioengineered dermal substitute consisting of a bilayer membrane system. The dermal replacement layer is composed of a cross-linked bovine tendon collagen-glycosaminoglycan (chondroitin-6-sulfate) matrix coated on one side with a synthetic polysiloxane polymer (silicone) layer. This layer functions as an epidermis to control moisture loss from the wound. The collagen matrix serves as a scaffold for ingrowth of fibroblasts, macrophages, lymphocytes, and capillaries and is ultimately replaced by host tissue. Integra "take" mirrors skin graft "take" and follows the sequence of 1) imbibition, 2) fibroblast migration, 3) neovascularization, and 4) maturation.


As the host tissue infiltrates the dermal layer, the collagen layer is biointegrated with the wound to form a vascular neodermis capable of accepting a split-thickness skin graft after a period of approximately 4 weeks. Proper patient selection and careful monitoring for infection or hematoma accumulation are crucial in this time period. After approximately 4 weeks, the silicone layer is removed and a thin (0.008- to 0.010-inch) skin graft can be applied.


Advantages of Integra use include improved cosmesis, diminished scar contracture or development of hypertrophic scar, off-the-shelf availability in large quantities, increased elasticity, and the ability to use thinner skin grafts with subsequent improvement in donor-site morbidity, scar, and time to heal. Other cited advantages include commensurate growth of the grafted tissue in children, potential avoidance of a microsurgical procedure, and placement over tendons with no significant reduction in tendon mobility. The disadvantages of Integra include its high cost, steep learning curve, need for at least two stages with subsequent increased time to final closure, potential for infection under the silicone layer, and lack of adnexal structures with patient concerns of skin dryness.






In this patient, use of Integra with delayed thin split-thickness skin grafts at 4 weeks will give the best outcome in terms of cosmesis and function. A photograph is shown. Split-thickness skin grafts are not a good option in this location because of the risk of graft loss with tendon exposure due to lack of viable paratenon and the risk of secondary contracture at the wrist and elbow. Full-thickness skin grafts would diminish the risk of secondary contracture but harvesting enough tissue to cover the entire arm would be impossible using the inguinal region as a donor site. Full-thickness grafts also require a healthier wound bed for optimal graft "take" and are not likely to heal over exposed tendons.


Free tissue transfer is an excellent technique for resurfacing the forearm, but in this patient, the thigh donor site would be difficult secondary to tissue thickness and the need for an extremely large flap. A better choice could be the scapular or parascapular donor site, perhaps in combination with a preliminary tissue expansion of that location. Obtaining enough tissue would be difficult. Banking the forearm in the abdomen would be less desirable as well, given her obesity and the need for a large surface area.


References
1. Jones I, Currie L, Martin R. A guide to biological skin substitutes. Br J Plast Surg. 2002 Apr;55(3):185-193.
2. Stanton RA, Billmire DA. Skin resurfacing for the burned patient. Clin Plast Surg. 2002 Jan;29(1):29-51.
3. Dantzer E, Braye FM. Reconstructive surgery using an artificial dermis (Integra): results with 39 grafts. Br J Plast Surg. 2001 Dec;54(8):659-664.
4. Moiemen NS, Vlachou E, Staiano JJ, et al. Reconstructive surgery with Integra dermal regeneration template: histologic study, clinical evaluation, and current practice. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2006 Jun;117(7 Suppl):160S-174S.

questions.question:
After central slip damage, ventral displacement of the lateral bands results in which deformity?
A) Boutonnière
B) Lumbrical plus
C) Mallet
D) Quadriga
E) Swan-neck
questions.answer:
A)

Boutonnière deformity results from ventral displacement of the lateral bands following central slip injury. The triangular ligament normally maintains the lateral bands in their dorsal position, preventing their ventral migration below the PIP joint's axis of rotation. When this stabilization fails, the lateral bands slip ventrally, creating the characteristic boutonnière deformity with PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension. B is incorrect because lumbrical plus deformity involves paradoxical extension of the IP joint during grip, unrelated to lateral band displacement. C is incorrect because mallet deformity results from terminal extensor tendon rupture at the DIP joint, not lateral band subluxation. D is incorrect because quadriga effect involves restriction of one finger affecting adjacent finger motion due to shared flexor digitorum profundus muscle belly. E is incorrect because swan-neck deformity occurs when lateral bands sublux dorsally above the PIP joint axis, opposite to the ventral subluxation described.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old carpenter experiences a dominant left thumb injury involving loss of less than 2 cm of distal pulp with bone exposure from a woodworking tool. Which reconstructive technique will most likely restore normal sensation to the thumb's volar pulp?
A) Cross-finger flap from the middle finger
B) Islandized Moberg flap
C) Flag flap
D) Thenar flap
E) Venous flow-through flap
questions.answer:
B)

The islandized Moberg flap (O'Brien modification) is the only option that preserves normal thumb pulp sensation. This technique advances the volar thumb tissue on its intact neurovascular bundles, maintaining the original sensory innervation. The islandized version involves making a transverse incision at the thumb base and dissecting the neurovascular pedicles to allow greater distal advancement, with skin grafting of the proximal donor site. A is incorrect because cross-finger flaps provide coverage but lack sensory innervation from the thumb's original nerve supply. C is incorrect because flag flaps are random pattern flaps without specific sensory nerve inclusion. D is incorrect because thenar flaps are primarily used for pediatric finger pulp reconstruction, not thumb reconstruction, and don't maintain original sensation. E is incorrect because venous flow-through flaps are designed for dorsal defects with adequate vessel size for anastomosis, which wouldn't be available in a volar thumb pulp defect.

questions.question:
A surgeon plans a prospective research study to examine potential causation between breast implants and breast implant illness (BII). The study will compare women with implants to those without implants to assess BII development. What type of study design does this represent?
A) Case series study
B) Case-control study
C) Comparative cohort study
D) Cross-sectional study
E) Randomized controlled trial
questions.answer:
C)

This describes a comparative cohort study, which follows groups with different exposures (implants vs. no implants) prospectively to determine disease development (BII). Cohort studies begin with exposure status and follow participants forward in time to observe outcomes. The comparative aspect involves comparing exposed and unexposed groups. A is incorrect because case series studies only follow participants with a specific exposure without a comparison group. B is incorrect because case-control studies work retrospectively, starting with disease status (cases with BII vs. controls without BII) and looking backward at exposure history. D is incorrect because cross-sectional studies examine both exposure and outcome at a single time point rather than following participants prospectively. E is incorrect because randomized controlled trials involve random assignment to interventions, which would be unethical when studying potential harmful exposures like implant-related illness.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old African American female presents with multiple draining sinuses and nodular abscesses in bilateral inframammary regions, groins, and axillae. She has not responded to topical and oral antibiotics. Her history includes type 2 diabetes, obesity, and keloid formation. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
A) Adalimumab therapy
B) Incision and drainage
C) Radiotherapy
D) Skin-tissue-saving excision with electrosurgical peeling (STEEP) procedure
E) Wide excision and skin grafting
questions.answer:
A)

Adalimumab therapy is most appropriate for this patient with moderate hidradenitis suppurativa (Hurley stage II) who has failed conventional antibiotic treatment. Adalimumab is an anti-TNF monoclonal antibody FDA-approved for moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa, particularly effective for patients requiring long-term antibiotics or experiencing rapid flares when antibiotics are discontinued. Given her keloid history, medical management is preferable to surgical intervention. B is incorrect because incision and drainage only helps fluctuant abscesses with fluid collections, not inflamed nodules, and doesn't address the underlying inflammatory process. C is incorrect because radiotherapy lacks randomized trial evidence, carries cancer risk, and is not considered first-line therapy for this systemic inflammatory condition. D is incorrect because STEEP procedures have significant morbidity, higher recurrence rates, and substantial scarring risk, particularly problematic given this patient's keloid tendency. E is incorrect because wide excision, while having lower recurrence rates, involves high morbidity and should be reserved for severe refractory disease after medical options are exhausted, especially in keloid-prone patients.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old man is evaluated because of a congenital deficiency of the upper extremity. A photograph is shown. This patient‚Äos developmental abnormality most likely occurred during which of the following periods of gestation?


A) 0‚Äi4 weeks
B) 5‚Äi8 weeks
C) 9‚Äi13 weeks
D) 14‚Äi18 weeks
E) 19‚Äi23 weeks
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


The most likely period of time during gestation for this abnormality is 31 to 45 days.


This patient presents with transverse deficiency of the upper limb (phocomelia). This can result from abnormal development of the limb with an interruption in longitudinal growth.


The limb develops with formation of a limb bud at 26 days after gestation, which rapidly enlarges with growth of the embryo until approximately 47 days. At around 52 to 53 days after gestation, the fingers are separate. Embryogenesis is complete by 8 weeks, and all limb structures are present.


Limb development is controlled by signaling pathways that are located within three different signaling centers. These control the proximal-distal, anterior-posterior, and dorsal-ventral axes of limb development.


The limb develops in a proximal-distal direction, from shoulder to wrist, which is controlled by the apical ectodermal ridge (AER), a thickened layer of ectoderm over the limb bud. Fibroblast growth factors secreted within the AER signal the underlying mesoderm to differentiate. Disruption of the AER results in truncation of the limb.


Growth in the anterior-posterior (radioulnar) axis is determined by the zone of polarizing activity (ZPA). This is located in the posterior margin of the limb bud. The sonic hedgehog protein acts to signal development of the limb into radial and ulnar aspects. Alterations in this pathway can result in mirror duplication.


Dorsal-ventral limb development is signaled by the Wnt signaling pathway, which produces a transcription factor, LMX1 that induces the development of dorsal structures. In the ventral portion of the limb, the EN1 gene product blocks the Wnt pathway, leading to ventralization.


A variety of other transcription factors encoded by Hox and T-Box genes also govern limb and organ development, and alterations in these can give rise to various developmental differences.


Most limb abnormalities occur during the period of 4 to 8 weeks. In this case, the transverse deficiency likely occurred earlier in the process of limb outgrowth, while abnormalities of the digit would have taken place towards the end of this period.


References
1. Kozin S. Embryology of the upper extremity. In: Wolfe SW, Pedersen WC, Hotchkiss RN, Kozin SH, eds. Green‚Äos Operative Hand Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Churchill Livingstone; 2011:1295-1301.
2. Netscher DT, Baumholtz MA. Treatment of congenital upper extremity problems. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2007 Apr 15;119(5):101e-129e.
3. Oberg KC, Feenstra JM, Manske PR, Tonkin MA. Developmental biology and classification of congenital anomalies of the hand and upper extremity. J Hand Surg Am. 2010 Dec;35(12):2066-2076.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old female patient presents requesting tummy tuck surgery. Her medical history reveals frequent bruising and four first-trimester pregnancy losses, plus one successful delivery. Her newborn weighed 10 lb 8 oz (4.5 kg) at birth. The patient's BMI is 28 kg/m2. Physical examination reveals a 6-cm separation of abdominal muscles, excess abdominal skin, and a healed cesarean section scar. Which of the following specialist referrals is most appropriate before surgical intervention?
A) Cardiologist
B) Endocrinologist
C) General surgeon
D) Hematologist
E) Nutritionist
questions.answer:
D)

The correct answer is D) Hematologist. This patient's history of multiple spontaneous first-trimester abortions strongly suggests a hypercoagulable disorder that requires evaluation before abdominoplasty, which carries significant thromboembolism risk. Common genetic thrombophilic conditions include Factor V Leiden mutation, prothrombin variant 20210A, and protein C/S deficiencies. Hematologic assessment can identify these high-risk patients and guide appropriate anticoagulation protocols. A) Cardiologist is incorrect because there are no cardiac symptoms or risk factors mentioned. B) Endocrinologist is incorrect because while the large birth weight might suggest gestational diabetes, this doesn't require preoperative consultation for abdominoplasty. C) General surgeon is incorrect because a plastic surgeon can distinguish diastasis recti from true hernias in routine cases. E) Nutritionist is incorrect because while BMI >30 increases complications, this patient's BMI of 28 doesn't require nutritional consultation.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old male patient seeks hair restoration treatment for scalp baldness. He experienced a childhood scalp burn that was treated with split-thickness skin grafting. Hair transplantation using micrograft technique is being considered to reconstruct his hairline. What is the most likely percentage of micrograft survival and eventual hair growth expected in this patient?
A) 10%
B) 25%
C) 50%
D) 85%
E) 95%
questions.answer:
D)

The correct answer is D) 85%. Micrografts have lower metabolic demands due to their small size, allowing them to survive in compromised tissue including burn scars, fibrotic areas, and over skin grafts. In these challenging conditions, survival rates are approximately 85% compared to 95% in normal, unscarred tissue. A) 10% is incorrect because this survival rate is far too low for micrograft transplantation in any clinical scenario. B) 25% is incorrect as this would represent poor graft survival that wouldn't justify the procedure. C) 50% is incorrect because micrograft survival rates in scarred tissue are significantly higher than this. E) 95% is incorrect because this represents the survival rate in healthy, unscarred tissue, not in burn scar areas.

questions.question:
Under HIPAA regulations, which of the following constitutes individually identifiable personal health information?
A) Age
B) Date of birth
C) Gender
D) Race
E) State of residence
questions.answer:
B)

The correct answer is B) Date of birth. According to HIPAA Privacy Rules, individually identifiable health information includes specific identifiers that can reasonably be used to identify an individual, and date of birth is explicitly listed as one of these common identifiers along with name, address, and social security number. A) Age is incorrect because general age ranges are not specific enough to identify individuals and can be used in de-identified datasets. C) Gender is incorrect because it represents broad demographic categories that alone cannot identify specific individuals. D) Race is incorrect because racial categories are general demographic information that cannot uniquely identify individuals. E) State of residence is incorrect because state-level geographic information is too broad to serve as an individual identifier under HIPAA.

questions.question:
Which of the following anatomical structures forms part of the boundaries that define the internal nasal valve?
A) Anterior edge of the vomer
B) Anterior middle turbinate
C) Caudal border of the upper lateral cartilage
D) Cephalic border of the lower lateral cartilage
E) Foot plate of the medial crus
questions.answer:
C)

The correct answer is C) Caudal border of the upper lateral cartilage. The internal nasal valve represents the narrowest portion of the upper respiratory tract, with its boundaries defined by the caudal border of the upper lateral cartilage superiorly, the anterior inferior turbinate posteriorly, the caudal septum medially, the nasal floor inferiorly, and the pyriform margin laterally. A) Anterior edge of the vomer is incorrect because the vomer forms part of the nasal septum but not specifically the internal valve boundary. B) Anterior middle turbinate is incorrect because the internal valve is bounded by the inferior turbinate, not the middle turbinate. D) Cephalic border of the lower lateral cartilage is incorrect because this structure is part of the external nasal valve anatomy, not the internal valve. E) Foot plate of the medial crus is incorrect because this is part of the lower lateral cartilage complex and doesn't contribute to internal valve boundaries.

questions.question:
A plastic surgeon flies home after taking her oral American Board of Plastic Surgeons (ABPS) examination. She is excited to finally start advertising to the public in order to grow her practice. She enlists an endorsement from one of her satisfied patients who underwent augmentation mammaplasty. The patient provides a quote and allows her photograph to be used. The plastic surgeon also wants to highlight her additional fellowship training in breast surgery. She is an American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) candidate member. Inclusion of which of the following items in her advertisement would be a breach of the ASPS Code of Ethics?


A) ASPS logo
B) Assertion of advanced skills in breast surgery as a result of her breast fellowship
C) A list of her plastic surgery training programs
D) Testimonial of the patient stating that this is the best plastic surgeon she knows
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


The plastic surgeon described is board eligible, not board certified, and a Candidate Member of the ASPS. She cannot use the logo until she is a member of the ASPS, and she must first be board-certified. She cannot assume she has passed her oral board examination until the board contacts her to let her know this. Using the ASPS logo in advertising is a breach of the ASPS Code of Ethics without board certification and full membership in the ASPS.


Claims highlighting the fact that she is a female plastic surgeon to attract female patients do not represent a breach of the Code of Ethics, nor is sharing her educational history. She has enlisted her patient‚Äos endorsement, and use of a direct quotation as a testimonial from the patient is fine if it is clearly a quote from the patient. The plastic surgeon needs to be careful, because other plastic surgeons in her area may think she is breaching the Code of Ethics with claims of superiority, as stated in Section 2IG: The member, either personally or through a partner or associate or any physician or other affiliated health care provider, uses or participates in the use of any form of public or private communication (including computer imaging and electronic communications) containing a false, fraudulent, deceptive, or misleading statement or claim.


References
1. American Society of Plastic Surgeons Ethics Committee. Code of Ethics of The American Society of Plastic Surgeons. Available at: http://www.plasticsurgery.org/Documents/ByLaws/Code_of_Ethics_Oct09.pdf. Updated October 16, 2009.
2. Verheyden CN. A 5-year review of ethics complaints to the American Society of Plastic Surgeons. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2012 Feb;129(2):531-6.
3. Fox D. Pearls of Practice: A Brand Apart. Arlington Heights, IL: American Society of Plastic Surgeons; 2008.

questions.question:
A full-term male infant is being assessed for Blauth Type IV (pouce flottant) thumb underdevelopment. Physical examination reveals no additional anomalies. Index finger pollicization is being considered. At what age is it most optimal to perform this reconstructive procedure?
A) 1 Month
B) 1 Year
C) 5 Year
D) 10 Year
E) 15 Year
questions.answer:
B)

The correct answer is B) 1 Year. Pollicization for severe thumb hypoplasia (Types IIIB and IV) and aplasia is most successful when performed between 6-12 months of age, allowing natural integration and adaptation as the child develops manual skills. This timing optimizes neuroplasticity for cortical reorganization of the index finger as a thumb. A) 1 Month is incorrect because infants under 3 months may have incomplete cardiopulmonary maturation, and the procedure offers no advantage at this early age despite increased technical difficulty. C) 5 Years is incorrect because children develop established pinch and prehension patterns by age 3, making adaptation to the new thumb configuration more difficult. D) 10 Years is incorrect because cortical reorganization becomes slower and less complete in older children, reducing functional outcomes. E) 15 Years is incorrect because adolescents have fully established hand function patterns, making successful adaptation to pollicization extremely challenging.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old female patient is having an elective tummy tuck procedure at an ambulatory surgical facility under general anesthesia. After 30 minutes of surgery, the anesthesia provider notices elevated end-tidal carbon dioxide levels and rapid heart rate. What should be the initial management step?
A) Give dantrolene medication
B) Stop all inhalational anesthetic gases
C) Start lipid emulsion therapy
D) Convert to completely intravenous anesthesia
E) Manage cardiac rhythm disturbances
questions.answer:
B)

This clinical presentation suggests malignant hyperthermia, a life-threatening anesthetic emergency caused by excessive calcium release from muscle cells. The immediate priority is to eliminate the triggering agent by discontinuing all volatile anesthetic agents. A is incorrect because dantrolene administration, while essential, comes after stopping the triggering agents. C is incorrect because lipid emulsion is used for local anesthetic toxicity, not malignant hyperthermia. D is incorrect because switching to IV anesthesia is a subsequent step after discontinuing volatiles. E is incorrect because treating arrhythmias is supportive care that follows the primary intervention of stopping the causative agents.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female patient has been sent by her cancer doctor for evaluation of a longstanding abdominal wall hernia. During the consultation for hernia correction, she expresses interest in having a tummy tuck performed simultaneously. She inquires whether insurance coverage could apply to this procedure or a related operation like removal of excess abdominal tissue. What is the best approach to handle this patient's inquiry?
A) Have the patient pay out-of-pocket for the cosmetic surgery portion
B) Complete both the hernia repair and tummy tuck and submit claims to insurance for both
C) Decline the case since combining cosmetic and reconstructive procedures is unethical
D) Label the surgery as excess tissue removal, perform the tummy tuck, and bill insurance accordingly
questions.answer:
A)

When combining reconstructive and cosmetic procedures, the patient must pay separately for the elective cosmetic component and related costs, as insurance does not cover aesthetic procedures. B is incorrect because insurance will not reimburse for cosmetic procedures, making this inappropriate billing. C is incorrect because performing both reconstructive and cosmetic procedures together is ethically acceptable with proper disclosure and billing practices. D is incorrect because billing for a different procedure than what was performed constitutes insurance fraud and is never acceptable.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male patient presents for assessment of a non-healing wound on his foot. He has had type 1 diabetes for a decade. Examination reveals a deep, 4-cm ulceration on the bottom of his foot at the base of the big toe. What is the most probable underlying cause of this wound?
A) Hardening of the arteries
B) Blocked lymphatic vessels
C) Loss of nerve sensation
D) Inadequate personal cleanliness
E) Poor venous circulation
questions.answer:
C)

Diabetic peripheral neuropathy causes loss of protective sensation, leading to unnoticed trauma and pressure points that develop into ulcers, particularly at weight-bearing areas like the metatarsal heads. A is incorrect because while diabetics can have vascular disease, large vessel atherosclerosis is not the primary cause of neuropathic ulcers at pressure points. B is incorrect because lymphatic obstruction typically causes swelling rather than ulceration at specific pressure points. D is incorrect because poor hygiene alone does not cause deep plantar ulcers at characteristic locations. E is incorrect because venous stasis ulcers typically occur around the ankles, not on plantar surfaces.

questions.question:
Which embryological structure is responsible for developing into the lower jaw bone and its vertical portion?
A) First pharyngeal arch
B) First pharyngeal groove
C) Second pharyngeal arch
D) Second pharyngeal groove
questions.answer:
A)

The first pharyngeal arch gives rise to the mandible (lower jaw), including both the body and ramus, as well as parts of the ear like the tragus and anterior helix. B is incorrect because the first pharyngeal groove develops into the external ear canal, not bone structures. C is incorrect because the second pharyngeal arch forms most of the external ear structures (antihelix, antitragus, etc.) but not the mandible. D is incorrect because the second pharyngeal groove normally disappears during development and may only persist as cysts, not forming any normal anatomical structures.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male presents with a hand injury sustained from striking a wall with his fist. Radiographic imaging demonstrates a break in the neck of the fifth finger bone in his hand. Which clinical finding would most strongly indicate the need for operative treatment?
A) Angular deformity
B) Bone healing response
C) Bone fragment overlap
D) Rotational malalignment
E) Bone length loss
questions.answer:
D)

Rotational malalignment causes the affected finger to overlap with adjacent fingers during flexion (scissoring), significantly impairing hand function and requiring surgical correction. A is incorrect because angular deformity can often be tolerated, especially in the fourth and fifth metacarpals which have greater mobility at their base joints. B is incorrect because callus formation indicates normal healing and does not require surgery. C is incorrect because impaction, while potentially causing deformity, is generally well-tolerated unless severe. E is incorrect because shortening is typically well-tolerated as long as finger extension is not compromised.

questions.question:
A 44-year-old woman presents with a histologically confirmed basal cell carcinoma on her cheek. Which of the following represents an appropriate indication for standard surgical excision rather than Mohs micrographic surgery?
A) Lesion diameter of 1.2 cm
B) Position adjacent to the nasal alar rim
C) Morpheaform histologic pattern
D) Surrounding burn scar tissue
E) Previously treated tumor
questions.answer:
A)
A 1.2 cm diameter basal cell carcinoma on the cheek is appropriately managed with conventional excision as it can be removed with adequate margins and reconstructed using local tissue rearrangements like rhomboid or slide-swing flaps. B is incorrect because locations near critical anatomic structures like the alar rim require tissue preservation best achieved with Mohs surgery. C is incorrect because aggressive subtypes like morpheaform patterns are indications for Mohs surgery. D is incorrect because preexisting scars are indications for Mohs surgery due to altered tissue planes. E is incorrect because recurrent tumors require the precise margin control provided by Mohs surgery.

questions.question:
A recent plastic surgery residency graduate has established her private practice, obtained hospital privileges, state licensing, and malpractice coverage, and begun treating patients while promoting her services. Regarding promotional activities, which statement is consistent with ABPS guidelines and principles?
A) The ABPS has not established promotional guidelines
B) Board certification candidates with the ABPS bear responsibility for all promotional content, including third-party employers or physician review platforms
C) Practice websites may be activated before residency completion
D) Alcoholic beverages may be served at promotional events where injectable treatments, procedures, or surgeries are demonstrated
E) Candidates may promote themselves as board eligible for a 10-year period
questions.answer:
B)
Candidates for ABPS board certification are held accountable for all promotional materials and content, including those created by third-party employers or physician rating platforms, as outlined in the ABPS Booklet of Information. A is incorrect because the ABPS has established specific advertising guidelines. C is incorrect because practice websites cannot be activated prior to residency graduation. D is incorrect because alcoholic beverages are not permitted at marketing events involving medical procedures. E is incorrect because the board eligible designation cannot be used for 10 years.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old right-handed male presents with a 1-month history of inability to extend his right thumb interphalangeal joint. He sustained a thumb injury in a stair fall 15 months prior, which was managed with 6 weeks of cast treatment. Examination reveals 45-degree IP joint flexion with absent active extension. Radiographs demonstrate a healed, non-displaced distal radius fracture. What is the optimal treatment approach?
A) Thumb IP joint fusion
B) Bone spur removal and thumb IP joint fusion
C) Distal radius plate fixation with extensor indicis proprius tendon transfer
D) Direct extensor pollicis longus tendon repair
E) Extensor indicis proprius to extensor pollicis longus tendon transfer
questions.answer:
E)
Extensor pollicis longus tendon rupture following distal radius fracture is optimally treated with extensor indicis proprius to EPL tendon transfer, which restores active thumb extension while preserving joint mobility. A is incorrect because joint fusion eliminates motion and is not preferred in active individuals. B is incorrect because bone spur excision alone will not address the ruptured tendon, and fusion is unnecessarily limiting. C is incorrect because the healed radius fracture requires no additional treatment. D is incorrect because delayed primary EPL repair is rarely feasible due to tendon retraction and degeneration.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old woman presents 2 months following repair of volar lacerations to her dominant ring and middle fingers in Zone III of both digits. Examination reveals complete absence of active finger flexion, with preserved passive range of motion and intact fingertip sensation. Surgical exploration demonstrates complete tendon division at both locations with 2-cm tendon defects, but no tendon sheath adhesions. What is the most appropriate treatment?
A) Single-stage tendon grafting
B) Direct tendon repair
C) Direct tendon repair with z-plasty lengthening
D) Flexor digitorum superficialis to profundus transfer
E) Two-stage tendon grafting
questions.answer:
A)
Single-stage tendon grafting is appropriate for this Boyes grade 1 injury, which meets the criteria of good passive motion, well-healed wound with minimal scarring, and intact neurovascular structures. B is incorrect because the 2-cm tendon gap precludes direct repair without excessive tension. C is incorrect because z-lengthening cannot bridge a 2-cm defect. D is incorrect because tendon transfer is not indicated when grafting can restore normal anatomy and function. E is incorrect because two-stage grafting is reserved for higher-grade injuries with poor tissue conditions or limited passive motion.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old male presents with a 2-week history of right wrist pain following a fall onto his extended hand. Radiographic studies are provided. If this condition remains untreated, which joint articulation will most likely develop degenerative changes initially?
A) Capitolunate
B) Lunotriquetral
C) Radiolunate
D) Radioscaphoid
E) Scaphocapitate
questions.answer:
D)
The radioscaphoid joint develops arthritis first in untreated scapholunate ligament injuries, as demonstrated by the widened scapholunate interval and increased scapholunate angle on imaging. This follows the predictable SLAC (scapholunate advanced collapse) degenerative pattern. A is incorrect because capitolunate arthritis occurs later in the SLAC sequence. B is incorrect because the lunotriquetral joint remains unaffected in SLAC wrist as this ligament stays intact. C is incorrect because the radiolunate joint is typically preserved until advanced disease stages. E is incorrect because scaphocapitate arthritis develops after radioscaphoid involvement in the SLAC progression.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old child with a previous cleft palate reconstruction presents to the clinic for assessment of velopharyngeal dysfunction. Following speech assessment, which of the following represents the most suitable primary diagnostic tool for evaluating and managing this patient's condition?
A) Dynamic MRI imaging
B) Computed tomography
C) Examination under general anesthesia
D) Acoustic rhinometry
E) Flexible nasal endoscopy
questions.answer:
E)
Flexible nasal endoscopy is the most appropriate initial diagnostic tool. This technique has become the standard approach in most comprehensive cleft centers because it provides direct visualization of velopharyngeal closure patterns and function without radiation exposure, can typically be performed comfortably in the office setting, and offers valuable information for surgical planning. Dynamic MRI imaging is emerging technology but not first-line for diagnosis. Computed tomography involves unnecessary radiation exposure. Examination under general anesthesia is usually not required when office-based endoscopy can be performed. Acoustic rhinometry measures nasal airflow objectively but is not routinely used for surgical decision-making in velopharyngeal insufficiency.

questions.question:
In patients with velopharyngeal dysfunction, which of the following muscles is utilized to create a sphincter pharyngoplasty?
A) Levator veli palatini
B) Musculus uvulae
C) Palatoglossus
D) Palatopharyngeus
E) Tensor veli palatini
questions.answer:
D)
Palatopharyngeus is the correct muscle used in sphincter pharyngoplasty. This secondary speech procedure involves rotating the posterior tonsillar pillars as superiorly based flaps to narrow the velopharyngeal opening, and these pillars contain the palatopharyngeus muscles. Levator veli palatini is incorrect because it functions to elevate the soft palate rather than being used in sphincter creation. Palatoglossus is wrong as it runs through the anterior tonsillar pillar and serves to depress the palate. Musculus uvulae is incorrect because it is the muscle of the uvula itself. Tensor veli palatini is wrong as it primarily functions in eustachian tube pressure regulation.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female presents to the emergency room following traumatic right orbital and zygomatic fractures from a car accident. Clinical examination reveals focal swelling. Which of the following findings would most likely require urgent ophthalmologic evaluation?
A) Corneal surface injury
B) Double vision
C) Drooping eyelid
D) Blood in anterior eye chamber
E) Conjunctival bleeding
questions.answer:
D)
Blood in the anterior eye chamber (hyphema) requires immediate ophthalmologic consultation because blood clotting can obstruct fluid drainage from the anterior chamber, potentially causing glaucoma and vision loss. This condition necessitates urgent intraocular pressure measurement and slit-lamp examination. Corneal surface injury is incorrect because while it requires evaluation, it can be managed with urgent but not emergent consultation. Double vision is wrong as it may occur after facial trauma but doesn't warrant emergency consultation. Drooping eyelid is incorrect because traumatic ptosis, while concerning, doesn't require immediate specialist evaluation. Conjunctival bleeding is wrong as subconjunctival hemorrhage, though dramatic in appearance, is typically benign and doesn't require emergency ophthalmologic care.

questions.question:
A 61-year-old female is assessed 7 hours following bilateral lower eyelid surgery with fat repositioning. She complains of ocular pain and decreased vision in her right eye. Examination reveals increased right-sided swelling compared to the left and painful forward displacement of the right eye. Which of the following represents the most suitable management?
A) Prescribing stronger analgesics
B) Elevation of head and cold compresses
C) Diuretic therapy and monitoring
D) Emergency orbital decompression
E) Eyelid suturing
questions.answer:
D)
Emergency orbital decompression is the most appropriate treatment for retrobulbar hematoma. The patient's symptoms of pain, vision loss, and proptosis indicate orbital compartment syndrome requiring immediate surgical decompression to prevent permanent vision loss from optic nerve compression. Prescribing stronger analgesics is incorrect because it would mask symptoms and delay necessary treatment. Elevation of head and cold compresses is wrong as these measures are insufficient for treating orbital compartment syndrome, though appropriate for routine postoperative swelling. Diuretic therapy and monitoring is incorrect because while diuretics may be adjunctive treatment, they are inadequate as standalone therapy for this emergency. Eyelid suturing is wrong as tarsorrhaphy is used for lagophthalmos or ectropion, not for acute orbital compartment syndrome.

questions.question:
An otherwise healthy 62-year-old female presents with mild swelling, some iron deposits in the skin, and a clean, shallow, painful 2-cm ulcer located above the left inner ankle bone. Her history includes a left ankle fracture 15 years prior. She is a non-smoker with an occupation requiring 8-hour standing periods. Foot pulses are palpable and ankle-brachial index measures 0.94. Which of the following represents the most appropriate initial treatment?
A) Clean the wound and apply a skin graft
B) Elevate the leg and apply compression bandaging
C) Administer hyperbaric oxygen treatment
D) Prepare the wound with dermal substitute material
E) Remove the saphenous vein and close perforating veins
questions.answer:
B)
Elevating the leg and applying compression bandaging (such as an Unna boot) is the most appropriate initial management for venous ulcers. Compression therapy combined with wound care represents the primary and mainstay treatment for healing venous insufficiency ulcers, addressing the underlying venous hypertension while maintaining wound cleanliness. Cleaning the wound and applying a skin graft is incorrect as surgical closure should only be considered after a trial of compression therapy and wound optimization. Administering hyperbaric oxygen treatment is wrong because HBOT is not indicated for venous ulcers. Preparing the wound with dermal substitute material is incorrect as this advanced treatment is premature before attempting standard compression therapy. Removing the saphenous vein and closing perforating veins is wrong because while vein procedures may reduce ulcer recurrence, studies show they don't accelerate healing of existing ulcers compared to compression therapy alone.

questions.question:
A 44-year-old woman visits the clinic with a 2-year history of a non-tender mass on the palm side of her forearm that has been slowly growing. She denies any history of skin abnormalities or neurological symptoms. On examination, there is a 1.5-cm mass that moves freely from side to side. Gentle percussion over the mass causes tingling in the index and middle fingers. MRI reveals a well-defined enlarged area within the median nerve that appears bright on T2-weighted imaging. What is the most appropriate treatment?
A) Complete resection with nerve grafting
B) Tumor removal with nerve preservation
C) Partial biopsy through incision
D) Needle biopsy through skin
E) Partial nerve removal with direct repair
questions.answer:
B)

The most appropriate treatment is tumor removal with microsurgical nerve preservation. This patient has a neurilemoma (schwannoma), the most common benign nerve tumor of the upper extremity, arising from Schwann cell proliferation. These tumors typically present as painless masses on the flexor surface that are mobile transversely but not longitudinally, with characteristic MRI findings of T2 hyperintensity. Neurilemomas usually shell out easily from surrounding nerve tissue with careful microsurgical dissection, allowing complete removal with minimal risk of neurologic deficit and low recurrence rates. A) is incorrect because en bloc resection with grafting is unnecessarily aggressive for these well-circumscribed tumors that can be dissected from nerve fascicles. C) is incorrect because incisional biopsy creates scarring that complicates subsequent definitive resection and is unnecessary when complete excision can be performed safely. D) is incorrect because percutaneous needle biopsy rarely changes management, can cause nerve scarring and neurologic deficits, and makes subsequent resection more difficult. E) is incorrect because segmental resection is not needed for neurilemomas that separate easily from nerve tissue, unlike neurofibromas that are intimately intertwined with fascicles.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old man comes to the emergency department with jaw pain and bite misalignment. His teeth are normal. CT imaging reveals an isolated, simple left mandibular angle fracture without bone fragments. Which treatment approach is most likely to result in the fewest complications?
A) Non-surgical treatment with wire fixation
B) Surgical repair through mouth opening with single small plate
C) Surgical repair through mouth opening with two small plates
D) Surgical repair through neck incision with large reconstruction plate
questions.answer:
B)

Surgical repair through an intraoral approach with a single miniplate has been shown in comparative studies and meta-analyses to have the lowest complication rates for isolated, noncomminuted mandibular angle fractures. This technique provides adequate stability while minimizing tissue trauma and infection risk. A) is incorrect because closed reduction with intermaxillary fixation alone has approximately 17% risk of infection or malunion due to inadequate stabilization of the proximal segment in angle fractures. C) is incorrect because using two plates increases soft tissue complications and infection rates due to greater periosteal stripping and devascularization of bone segments. D) is incorrect because extraoral approach with reconstruction plating, while having comparable outcomes, creates a visible scar, increases facial nerve injury risk, and is unnecessarily complex for simple fractures in patients with intact dentition.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old woman has a malignant melanoma of the right ankle requiring resection that will expose bone. Her thighs are unsuitable as donor sites for coverage of the ankle. A free scapular fasciocutaneous flap is planned. The vascular pedicle of this flap passes through which of the following anatomic spaces?
A) Anterior triangle of the neck
B) Posterior triangle of the neck
C) Quadrangular (quadrilateral) space
D) Subclavian (omoclavicular) triangle
E) Triangular space
questions.answer:
E)

The scapular (and parascapular) fasciocutaneous flap is supplied by the circumflex scapular artery, a branch of the subscapular artery, which passes through the triangular space before emerging onto the posterior chest wall. The triangular space is bounded by the long head of the triceps laterally, teres minor superiorly, and teres major inferiorly.

A) The anterior triangle of the neck is bounded by the mandible, the sternocleidomastoid, and the midline of the neck; it contains the carotid sheath structures and cranial nerves, not the scapular flap pedicle.

B) The posterior triangle of the neck is bounded by the trapezius, the sternocleidomastoid, and the clavicle; it contains the brachial plexus and subclavian vessels, not the circumflex scapular artery.

C) The quadrangular space transmits the posterior circumflex humeral vessels and the axillary nerve; it is bounded by teres minor superiorly, teres major inferiorly, the long head of the triceps medially, and the surgical neck of the humerus laterally.

D) The subclavian (omoclavicular/supraclavicular) triangle is a subdivision of the posterior triangle, bounded by the sternocleidomastoid, the inferior belly of the omohyoid, and the clavicle; it contains the third part of the subclavian artery, not the flap pedicle.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old man arrives at the emergency department 6 hours following a bicycle crash with an open lower leg bone fracture. He was riding at 10 mph when the accident occurred. The wound measures 5 cm long with moderate debris contamination. The fracture is located mid-shaft of the tibia with moderate bone fragmentation and an associated closed fibula fracture. What is the most appropriate Gustilo classification for this injury?
A) I
B) II
C) IIIA
D) IIIB
E) IIIC
questions.answer:
B)

This injury meets the criteria for Gustilo Type II classification based on the wound length of 5 cm, moderate contamination, and moderate comminution of a mid-shaft tibial fracture. Type II fractures are characterized by wounds 1-10 cm in length with moderate soft tissue damage and contamination, without extensive soft tissue loss or major complications. A) is incorrect because Type I fractures have wounds less than 1 cm with minimal contamination and soft tissue damage. C) is incorrect because Type IIIA fractures have wounds greater than 10 cm or high-energy mechanisms with extensive soft tissue damage but adequate coverage of bone. D) is incorrect because Type IIIB fractures involve extensive soft tissue loss with exposed bone requiring flap coverage. E) is incorrect because Type IIIC fractures have associated vascular injury requiring repair.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old boy with a Gustilo Type IIIB open lower leg fracture received wound coverage using an anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap that included muscle tissue. What is the most likely muscle-related complication in this patient?
A) Reduced ability to straighten the knee
B) Reduced ability to bend the knee
C) Reduced ability to move thigh away from body
D) Reduced ability to move thigh toward body
E) Reduced ability to lift thigh upward
questions.answer:
A)

The most likely muscular complication is weakness of knee extension. The ALT flap perforators frequently pass through the vastus lateralis muscle, which may require dissection or harvesting during flap elevation. The vastus lateralis is a major component of the quadriceps muscle group responsible for knee extension, so injury or removal can result in knee extension weakness. B) is incorrect because knee flexion is primarily performed by the hamstring muscles (semitendinosus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris), which are not involved in ALT flap harvest. C) is incorrect because thigh abduction is accomplished by the tensor fascia lata and sartorius muscles, not the vastus lateralis. D) is incorrect because thigh adduction is performed by the pectineus, adductor longus, adductor brevis, gracilis, and adductor magnus muscles. E) is incorrect because thigh flexion is achieved by the pectineus, adductor brevis, and adductor magnus muscles.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old male patient seeks both aesthetic and functional nasal enhancement. He is scheduled for an open approach rhinoplasty, septal submucous resection, spreader graft placement, and inferior turbinate submucous reduction. Which of the following agents can be combined with local anesthetic to most effectively reduce operative bleeding during the rhinoplasty procedure?
A) Aprotinin
B) Hyaluronic acid
C) Ketorolac
D) Tissue plasminogen activator
E) Tranexamic acid
questions.answer:
E)
Tranexamic acid blocks fibrinolysis, thereby strengthening blood clots and reducing hemorrhage. This agent has demonstrated efficacy in minimizing bleeding across numerous plastic surgery procedures including rhinoplasty, facelift surgery, liposuction, breast reduction, and tummy tuck operations. Administration methods include intravenous, oral, topical application, and local tissue infiltration. Research has not demonstrated increased thromboembolic complications. The therapeutic effects persist for approximately 17 hours. When combined with local anesthetic, typical concentrations range from 1 to 2 mg/mL. While increasingly utilized in plastic surgery, tranexamic acid remains an off-label application. A) Aprotinin is incorrect because although it also inhibits fibrinolysis, it was withdrawn from the US market due to associated increased mortality risk. B) Hyaluronic acid is incorrect because it has not been proven to reduce surgical bleeding. C) Ketorolac is incorrect because this NSAID impairs platelet function, potentially increasing bleeding risk. D) Tissue plasminogen activator is incorrect because it promotes plasminogen conversion to plasmin, which dissolves clots and can worsen bleeding.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old male patient with type 2 diabetes presents with a diabetic foot ulcer on the right plantar surface. Reconstruction using a medial plantar artery flap is being considered. The arterial perforator is positioned adjacent to which of the following muscles?
A) Adductor hallucis
B) Flexor hallucis
C) Lumbrical
D) Plantar interosseous
E) Quadratus plantae
questions.answer:
B)
The medial plantar artery flap is raised beginning from the plantar surface, beneath the muscle fascia. The perforating vessel is located in the space between the flexor hallucis and abductor hallucis muscles. The perforator is then carefully dissected back to its source from the medial plantar artery within this intermuscular plane. A) Adductor hallucis is incorrect because the perforator is not located against this muscle. C) Lumbrical is incorrect because this muscle is not adjacent to the perforator location. D) Plantar interosseous is incorrect because these muscles are not in the correct anatomical position relative to the perforator. E) Quadratus plantae is incorrect because this muscle is located deeper and not adjacent to the perforator site.

questions.question:
A 6-month-old female child presents with uvular bifurcation, hard palate notching, and zona pellucida. The child demonstrates adequate feeding without respiratory compromise. What represents the most suitable next management step?
A) Beginning speech therapy
B) Nasoendoscopy
C) Palatal elevator
D) Palate repair at 1 year of age
E) Cleft team reassessment in 1 year
questions.answer:
E)
This patient demonstrates the three characteristic findings of submucous cleft palate. The prevalence of overt submucous cleft palate is extremely low (0.02 to 0.08%). While surgical timing remains debated, most patients achieve satisfactory speech outcomes without surgical intervention. Velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) that fails to respond to speech therapy represents the primary indication for surgical correction. Speech evaluation cannot be reliably performed before 2.5 years of age, and speech therapy cannot begin prior to this developmental stage. Standard management involves VPI diagnosis followed by 6 to 12 months of speech therapy, with surgical intervention reserved for therapy-resistant cases. At 6 months of age, surgical consideration is premature, and cleft team monitoring is most appropriate. A) Speech therapy is incorrect because it cannot be initiated before 2.5 years of age when speech can be properly assessed. B) Nasoendoscopy is incorrect because it is used for preoperative surgical planning, not initial management. C) Palatal elevator is incorrect because it has no role in submucous cleft palate management. D) Palate repair at 1 year is incorrect because surgery is only indicated for VPI that fails speech therapy, which cannot be determined at this age.

questions.question:
Which statement accurately describes cleft lip with or without cleft palate compared to isolated cleft palate?
A) Cleft lip/palate does not involve nasal deformity
B) Cleft lip/palate occurs less frequently than isolated cleft palate
C) Cleft lip/palate shows slight female predominance
D) Cleft lip/palate occurrence is uniform across ethnicities
E) Cleft lip/palate demonstrates lower syndromic association
questions.answer:
E)
Cleft lip with or without palate (CLP) exhibits distinct epidemiological patterns and clinical features compared to isolated cleft palate only (CPO). CLP demonstrates higher birth prevalence (1 in 700 versus 1 in 1500), male predominance (M:F ratio 2:1 versus F:M ratio 3:2), ethnic variation (Asian:Caucasian:African ratio 4:2:1 versus no ethnic differences), and reduced syndromic association (15% versus 50%). Cleft lip invariably involves some degree of nasal deformity, while CPO does not affect the nose. Therefore, cleft lip/palate has lower likelihood of syndromic association. A) This is incorrect because cleft lip always involves some degree of nasal deformity. B) This is incorrect because CLP has higher incidence than CPO (1 in 700 versus 1 in 1500). C) This is incorrect because CLP shows male predominance (2:1 M:F ratio). D) This is incorrect because CLP incidence varies significantly by ethnicity with highest rates in Asians.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female patient reports episodic severe left ring finger nail pain that has progressively worsened over recent years. Finger radiographs reveal no abnormalities. Which physical examination finding supports a glomus tumor diagnosis in this patient?
A) Pain decreases from pinpoint pressure on the nail
B) Pain decreases with inflation of a blood pressure cuff
C) Pain increases in warm temperatures
D) Pain increases only at night
questions.answer:
B)
A glomus tumor represents a small benign neoplasm composed of glomus apparatus cells. The majority (75%) occur in the hand, with most of these (65%) located in the fingertip. These tumors cause intermittent but severe pain. The characteristic symptom triad for fingertip glomus tumors includes: 1) cold sensitivity, 2) paroxysmal pain (occurring day or night), and 3) pinpoint tenderness (Love's sign). When a blood pressure cuff is inflated proximally, fingertip pain diminishes (Hildreth's sign). MRI typically confirms the diagnosis, and surgical excision provides treatment. Recurrence rates may reach 20%. A) This is incorrect because pinpoint pressure typically increases pain (Love's sign), not decreases it. C) This is incorrect because glomus tumors characteristically cause increased pain in cold temperatures, not warm. D) This is incorrect because the pain is paroxysmal and can occur during both day and night, not exclusively at night.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient with bilateral breast implants from cosmetic surgery presents following a car crash involving airbag deployment. Clinical evaluation reveals localized chest pain and a characteristic "seatbelt mark" across the left breast. Initial implant assessment demonstrates no rupture. After 6 months, she develops left breast deformity with implant distortion and groove formation. What is the most suitable next diagnostic approach to evaluate implant condition?
A) Plain chest radiography
B) Contrast-enhanced CT imaging
C) Breast mammography
D) Magnetic resonance imaging
E) Ultrasonography
questions.answer:
D)
MRI is the optimal imaging modality for evaluating implant integrity in this delayed presentation of seatbelt injury syndrome. This condition can manifest as breast deformity or masses months after trauma, and MRI provides the most comprehensive assessment to exclude implant rupture, intracapsular seroma formation, and rule out invasive ductal carcinoma along the contracture line. A) Plain chest radiography is incorrect because it's primarily useful for immediate assessment of chest wall bone injuries, not implant evaluation. B) Contrast-enhanced CT is incorrect as it's mainly indicated for acute settings to detect arterial bleeding or pneumothorax, not for detailed implant assessment. C) Mammography is incorrect because while useful for initial mass evaluation, it cannot definitively assess implant rupture. E) Ultrasonography is incorrect because although it can detect some implant issues, MRI remains the gold standard for definitive implant integrity evaluation.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents for abdominal contouring surgery consultation. Clinical findings include rectus muscle separation and surplus skin and adipose tissue below the navel. The surgical plan involves tummy tuck with upper abdominal tissue elevation and muscle repair. Which anatomical region is most likely to experience persistent sensory loss beyond 3 years following surgery?
A) Upper abdominal region
B) Below-umbilical area
C) Side abdominal region
D) Below-breastbone area
E) Above-pubic region
questions.answer:
B)
The infraumbilical (below-umbilical) region experiences the most persistent sensory deficits lasting beyond 3 years postoperatively. This area shows prolonged loss of superficial touch, pain, temperature, and vibration sensation due to division of intercostal nerve branches during surgical undermining. A) The epigastric (upper abdominal) region is incorrect because sensation typically recovers within 3 years for most modalities except temperature. C) The lateral abdominal region is incorrect as it shows less severe and more temporary sensory changes compared to the infraumbilical area. D) The subxiphoid (below-breastbone) region is incorrect because it experiences less significant long-term sensory loss. E) The suprapubic (above-pubic) region is incorrect as it primarily shows temperature sensation deficits while other sensory modalities recover relatively quickly.

questions.question:
What is the primary distinction between the Nagata and Brent approaches for surgical ear reconstruction in congenital ear deformity?
A) Nagata is done at age 5, while Brent requires waiting until age 12
B) Nagata requires two surgical phases, while Brent needs three or more
C) Nagata employs microvascular tissue transfer, while Brent uses only adjacent tissue
D) Nagata utilizes synthetic implant material, while Brent uses patient's own cartilage
E) Nagata uses nearby tissue for framework, while Brent uses patient's cartilage and hip bone
questions.answer:
B)
The Nagata technique's main advantage is requiring fewer surgical stages compared to the Brent method. The key difference lies in lobule and tragus reconstruction timing - Nagata performs these simultaneously with framework placement, while Brent separates lobule creation/elevation and tragal reconstruction into distinct stages. A) Age requirements are incorrect as both techniques can be performed at similar ages when adequate rib cartilage is available. C) Microvascular techniques are incorrect as both methods primarily use autologous rib cartilage, with microvascular procedures only used as salvage options. D) Framework materials are incorrect because both Nagata and Brent techniques use the patient's own rib cartilage, not synthetic materials like porous polyethylene (which is used in the Reinisch technique). E) Tissue sources are incorrect as neither technique routinely incorporates iliac crest bone, and both rely on autologous costal cartilage for framework construction.

questions.question:
A 51-year-old female patient receives bilateral breast reconstruction using free abdominal tissue flaps. For postoperative pain management, she receives bilateral injections of 10 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine into the transversus abdominis plane block region. What anatomical boundaries should guide proper needle placement for this procedure?
A) Latissimus dorsi muscle, external oblique muscle, and iliac crest
B) Lateral rectus border, inferior epigastric vessels, and inguinal ligament
C) Quadratus lumborum muscle, internal oblique muscle, and 12th rib
D) Teres major, teres minor, and triceps long head
questions.answer:
A)
The TAP block utilizes the anatomical landmarks of Petit's triangle (inferior lumbar triangle): latissimus dorsi muscle (posterior border), external oblique muscle (anterior border), and iliac crest (inferior border). This technique blocks sensory nerves (T6-L1) supplying the anterior abdominal wall by injecting anesthetic between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles. B) These landmarks define Hesselbach's triangle is incorrect because this describes the area where direct inguinal hernias occur, not the TAP block injection site. C) These structures form Grynfeltt's triangle (superior lumbar triangle) is incorrect as this is a site of lumbar herniation, not the TAP block location. D) These muscle boundaries define the triangular space is incorrect because this anatomical region is relevant for scapular flap harvest and circumflex scapular artery identification, not abdominal wall anesthesia.

questions.question:
A 76-year-old male patient receives extensive oral cavity tumor removal and reconstruction using free tissue transfer. What represents a definitive contraindication for using the microvascular arterial coupling device?
A) Patient's advanced age
B) Vessel calcification from atherosclerosis
C) Prior radiation treatment history
D) Discrepancy in vessel diameters
questions.answer:
B)
Atherosclerotic calcification creating rigid, non-compliant vessels is an absolute contraindication for coupler use. The ring-pin coupling technique requires flexible vessels that can be everted over the pins; calcified vessels cannot accommodate this manipulation, resulting in technical failure and poor anastomotic outcomes. A) Advanced age alone is incorrect because age by itself is not a contraindication to microvascular surgery or coupler use, provided the patient is medically suitable for surgery. C) Radiation therapy history is incorrect as it's not an absolute contraindication, though vessels should be inspected for radiation-induced changes; if vessels remain pliable, coupler use is acceptable. D) Vessel size mismatch is incorrect because the coupler system is actually designed to accommodate size discrepancies, particularly in venous anastomoses, making this a relative advantage rather than a contraindication.

questions.question:
Which drug category is most likely to amplify the therapeutic effects of botulinum toxin type A?
A) Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors
B) Adrenergic beta-receptor antagonists
C) Voltage-gated calcium channel antagonists
D) Thiazide and loop diuretics
E) Organic nitrate compounds
questions.answer:
C)

Voltage-gated calcium channel antagonists are recognized for their ability to amplify botulinum toxin effects. Since botulinum toxin functions by preventing acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, calcium channel antagonists can strengthen this neuromuscular blockade. Additional medications that amplify botulinum toxin include aminoglycoside antibiotics, penicillamine, and quinine derivatives. A) Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors primarily target the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and do not influence neuromuscular transmission. B) Adrenergic beta-receptor antagonists target sympathetic receptors and do not amplify botulinum toxin effects. D) Thiazide and loop diuretics influence electrolyte balance and fluid homeostasis but do not strengthen neuromuscular blockade. E) Organic nitrate compounds function as vasodilators and do not interfere with botulinum toxin's neuromuscular mechanism.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old man with a seizure disorder presents with mandibular discomfort and dental occlusion problems 12 hours after sustaining facial injuries during a physical altercation. Radiographic studies demonstrate a displaced fracture of the left mandibular angle and a right parasymphyseal fracture. He smokes one pack of cigarettes daily. Open reduction and internal fixation is planned. Which element most substantially elevates his risk for postoperative infection?
A) History of seizure disorder
B) Cigarette smoking habit
C) Patient age
D) Male sex
E) 5-day delay before surgery
questions.answer:
B)

Cigarette smoking substantially elevates postoperative infection risk, with research demonstrating a six-fold increase in surgical site infections among smokers versus non-smokers. Tobacco use compromises wound healing through arterial constriction, decreased tissue oxygenation, and impaired immune response. A) A history of seizure disorder does not directly increase infection rates following mandibular fracture surgery. C) Although patient age can influence healing capacity, it is not the most significant risk factor in this scenario. D) Male sex by itself does not substantially increase infection risk. E) A surgical delay of several days has not been shown to directly correlate with higher infection rates in multiple research studies.

questions.question:
A 57-year-old female patient requests evaluation for cosmetic body sculpting surgery. Her sole medication consists of daily garlic supplement capsules. This botanical supplement primarily elevates her risk for which surgical complication?
A) Excessive bleeding
B) Elevated blood pressure
C) Nausea and vomiting
D) Prolonged anesthetic recovery
E) Increased heart rate
questions.answer:
A)

Garlic supplementation elevates bleeding risk through its antiplatelet properties and enhancement of fibrinolytic processes. It prevents platelet aggregation and can increase hemorrhage during and following surgical procedures, necessitating discontinuation one week prior to surgery. B) Garlic generally exhibits blood pressure-lowering properties rather than causing hypertension. C) Gastrointestinal upset is not a well-established perioperative effect of garlic supplementation. D) Garlic does not meaningfully extend anesthetic effects or delay recovery from anesthesia. E) Cardiac rhythm acceleration is not a recognized surgical complication associated with garlic supplementation.

questions.question:
Which tissue plane is included when constructing a posterior pharyngeal flap?
A) Investing layer of the deep cervical fascia
B) Palatopharyngeus muscle fibers
C) Prevertebral fascial plane
D) Superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle
questions.answer:
D)

The posterior pharyngeal flap incorporates the superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle together with the overlying mucosa and buccopharyngeal fascia. This flap is raised with a superior pedicle at the junction between the nasopharynx and oropharynx to address velopharyngeal insufficiency. The superior constrictor contributes both bulk and vascular supply to the flap. A) The investing layer of deep cervical fascia is more superficial and encompasses the platysma muscle, which is not part of pharyngeal flap procedures. B) The palatopharyngeus muscle is utilized in sphincter pharyngoplasty techniques rather than pharyngeal flap construction. C) The prevertebral fascia represents the deepest fascial layer and is preserved during flap elevation, functioning as the posterior limit of the dissection.

questions.question:
A healthy 26-year-old man with receding frontal hairline requests hair restoration therapy. Which feature best characterizes the underlying disease process of his condition?
A) Depletion of fine vellus hairs
B) Accelerated telogen phase
C) Eosinophil-mediated follicular inflammation
D) Prolonged anagen phase
E) Progressive hair follicle shrinkage
questions.answer:
E)

Androgenetic alopecia is defined by progressive hair follicle shrinkage, whereby thick terminal hairs are systematically converted to thinner vellus-type hairs until follicles ultimately cease functioning. This transformation results from genetic susceptibility and hormonal sensitivity to androgens. A) Fine vellus hairs actually proliferate rather than disappear, as terminal hairs transform into vellus-like hairs during the shrinkage process. B) The telogen phase becomes extended rather than accelerated, disrupting the normal growth cycle balance. C) The inflammatory response is predominantly lymphohistiocytic with T-lymphocyte infiltration rather than eosinophilic. D) The anagen phase becomes increasingly abbreviated rather than prolonged, producing progressively shorter and finer hairs with each growth cycle.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old female presents with concerns about her bite and facial aesthetics related to her left-sided cleft lip and palate. Examination reveals underdeveloped midface and Class III bite pattern. Oral examination shows 6 mm reverse overjet and an absent left upper lateral incisor with preserved space. Radiographic imaging shows 5 mm of bone height at the cleft site. What is the optimal treatment approach for this patient?
A) Bone transport distraction of the alveolus
B) Wait and monitor until growth completion
C) Fixed dental bridge reconstruction
D) Mandibular bilateral split with dental implants
E) Segmented Le Fort I advancement with alveolar gap closure
questions.answer:
E)
The optimal treatment is a segmented Le Fort I advancement with alveolar gap closure. This patient presents with typical cleft-related maxillary growth restriction causing Class III malocclusion and missing lateral incisor. The two-piece Le Fort I procedure with canine substitution addresses both the skeletal deficiency and missing tooth by advancing the maxilla and repositioning the canine to replace the lateral incisor, which can then be reshaped prosthetically. At 17 years old, skeletal maturity is likely achieved. A is incorrect because alveolar transport distraction alone won't correct the malocclusion. B is incorrect as the patient is likely skeletally mature and has functional complaints requiring intervention. C is incorrect because a fixed bridge doesn't address the underlying skeletal malocclusion. D is incorrect because mandibular surgery alone doesn't correct midface deficiency, and insufficient bone stock (5mm vs required 10-15mm) precludes standard implant placement.

questions.question:
A 78-year-old female presents with a 6.5-cm right cheek defect below the lower eyelid following complete excision of lentigo maligna melanoma with clear margins. What is the optimal reconstructive approach?
A) Cervicofacial advancement flap
B) Complete-thickness skin graft
C) Natural wound healing
D) Internal mammary perforator flap
E) Direct wound closure
questions.answer:
A)
The cervicofacial advancement flap provides the best reconstruction for large cheek defects by utilizing adjacent cheek and neck tissue with optimal color and texture matching. This inferiorly-based flap transfers substantial soft tissue from the preauricular and cervical regions, with incisions following natural facial contours and allowing primary donor site closure. Proper anchoring to the zygoma prevents lower lid complications. B is incorrect because full-thickness grafts create poor contour with shiny, patch-like appearance and potential contracture. C is incorrect as secondary healing would cause prolonged recovery, significant scarring, and likely ectropion with facial distortion. D is incorrect because while the IMAP flap can provide good color match, it requires microvascular surgery, may cause breast deformity, and doesn't offer superior results to local tissue. E is incorrect because primary closure of such a large defect would create excessive tension and severe distortion of surrounding facial structures.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old female presents with 4 months of numbness affecting the thumb, index, middle finger, and palm on the right hand's palm side. She has no significant medical history. Examination reveals weak thumb opposition and thumb tip bending weakness. Wrist tapping and sustained wrist bending do not trigger symptoms. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Anterior interosseous nerve compression
B) Carpal tunnel syndrome
C) Cubital tunnel syndrome
D) Posterior interosseous nerve compression
E) Pronator syndrome
questions.answer:
E)
Pronator syndrome involves median nerve compression in the upper forearm, characterized by palm numbness (via palmar cutaneous branch) and thumb flexor weakness, distinguishing it from carpal tunnel syndrome where palm sensation is preserved. The combination of palmar numbness and flexor pollicis longus weakness is diagnostic. A is incorrect because anterior interosseous syndrome causes only motor symptoms without sensory loss. B is incorrect because carpal tunnel syndrome typically spares palm sensation since the palmar cutaneous branch originates proximal to the carpal tunnel, and provocative tests would be positive. C is incorrect because cubital tunnel syndrome affects the ring and small fingers with ulnar nerve distribution. D is incorrect because posterior interosseous syndrome affects forearm extensors and has no sensory component matching this presentation.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female with symptomatic breast enlargement is planned for Wise-pattern breast reduction surgery. Which postoperative complication is most probable?
A) Impaired wound healing
B) Fat tissue death
C) Blood collection
D) Raised scarring
E) Nipple-areola distortion
questions.answer:
A)
Impaired wound healing is the most frequent complication following breast reduction, occurring in 21.6% of patients according to large prospective studies. This complication correlates with larger preoperative breast size, greater tissue removal weight, smoking history, and younger patient age. The overall complication rate for reduction mammaplasty is approximately 43%. B is incorrect because fat necrosis occurs in only 1.8% of cases. C is incorrect because hematoma develops in 3.7% of patients. D is incorrect because hypertrophic scarring affects 2.5% of patients. E is incorrect because nipple-areola complex deformities are less common than wound healing issues and weren't specifically quantified as a leading complication in major studies.

questions.question:
A 39-year-old male presents 3 months after a 10-foot fall with ongoing thumb-side wrist pain, swelling, reduced grip strength, and painful clicking during moderate activity. Examination shows widespread radial wrist tenderness and a painful 'clunk' when pressing the scaphoid during wrist deviation toward the thumb. Initial and recent standard radiographs show no fractures or bone malalignment. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A) de Quervain's tendon inflammation
B) Dynamic scapholunate joint instability
C) Flexor carpi radialis tendon inflammation
D) Kienböck disease
E) Hidden scaphoid fracture
questions.answer:
B)
Dynamic scapholunate instability presents with these exact findings: radial wrist pain, clicking, and a painful clunk during scaphoid palpation with radial deviation, despite normal static radiographs. This occurs when the scapholunate interosseous ligament is disrupted but secondary stabilizers remain intact, preventing static radiographic changes while causing symptoms with mechanical loading. Stress radiographs or MRI may be needed for confirmation. A is incorrect because de Quervain's tenosynovitis affects the first dorsal compartment tendons with positive Finkelstein test, not carpal bone instability. C is incorrect because FCR tendinitis presents with flexion crease tenderness and crepitus, not carpal instability. D is incorrect because Kienböck disease involves lunate collapse with more global wrist pain and dorsal tenderness over the lunate. E is incorrect because any occult scaphoid fracture would be visible on radiographs by 12 weeks due to bone resorption at the fracture site.

questions.question:
A healthy 76-year-old woman experiences a deep partial-thickness burn to her face from hot liquid. No immediate treatment is provided, and she returns to clinic 6 weeks later. She reports right eye discomfort and excessive tearing. Eye examination reveals 4 mm lagophthalmos, conjunctival redness, and thick scarring on the upper eyelid with limited movement. The adjacent cheek and forehead skin appears red and thickened. What is the most suitable treatment approach for this patient?
A) Scar release with forehead flap reconstruction
B) Scar release with full-thickness skin graft
C) Scar release with allograft placement
D) Scar release with split-thickness skin graft
E) Scar manipulation and eyelid taping
