questions.answer:
B)

Periorbital burn injuries require prompt management to ensure patient comfort and preserve vision. The patient's persistent lagophthalmos and symptoms necessitate surgical intervention given the severity of her complaints. Scar release combined with full-thickness skin grafting is the optimal treatment because full-thickness grafts minimize post-operative contracture formation compared to split-thickness grafts. A is incorrect because forehead flap reconstruction is not appropriate when the donor site may be compromised by burn injury, as in this patient's case. C is incorrect because allograft placement is not indicated following contracture release when adequate recipient tissue is available. D is incorrect because split-thickness skin grafts have higher contracture rates than full-thickness grafts in this location. E is incorrect because conservative measures are insufficient given the degree of functional impairment and symptoms.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old man presents with a 6-month history of left temporomandibular joint clicking and movement-related pain. Examination reveals 20 mm interincisal opening and repeated open-position locking; no infection or ankylosis is present. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Botulinum toxin type A injection
B) Intracapsular disc repositioning with articular eminence reduction
C) Disc removal with interpositional temporalis fascia flap
D) Total temporomandibular joint replacement
E) Conservative observation
questions.answer:
B)

Surgical articular eminence reduction is the appropriate treatment for patients experiencing symptomatic open mandibular locking. This procedure addresses the mechanical cause of the open locking by reducing the height of the articular eminence that prevents jaw closure. A is incorrect because botulinum toxin injection is not an established treatment for this specific condition. C is incorrect because discectomy with interpositional flap is typically reserved as a salvage procedure for more severe cases. D is incorrect because total joint replacement is rarely indicated unless there is infection, malignancy, or severe ankylosis, none of which are present. E is incorrect because conservative management is only appropriate when there are no significant functional limitations, but this patient has symptomatic locking.

questions.question:
The lower limb malformation called mirror foot is most commonly associated with which embryologic developmental abnormality?
A) Apical ectodermal ridge duplication
B) Zone of polarizing activity duplication
C) Apical ectodermal ridge absence
D) Ventral ectoderm signal loss
E) Zone of polarizing activity absence
questions.answer:
B)

The zone of polarizing activity (ZPA) controls anteroposterior axis differentiation through sonic hedgehog and Hox b-8 protein regulation. ZPA duplication results in mirror hand and mirror foot anomalies by creating symmetrical digit patterns. A is incorrect because apical ectodermal ridge duplication does not cause mirror deformities but affects proximal-distal growth patterns. C is incorrect because loss of the apical ectodermal ridge leads to arrested limb development rather than mirror patterns. D is incorrect because ventral ectoderm signal disruption affects dorsal-ventral patterning and proximal-distal growth but not mirror duplication. E is incorrect because ZPA absence results in missing posterior limb elements rather than mirror duplication patterns.

questions.question:
What is the most frequent complication following rotation-advancement repair of unilateral cleft lip?
A) Cupid's bow flattening
B) Lip lengthening
C) Lip shortening
D) Triangular philtral scar
E) Philtral widening
questions.answer:
C)

Insufficient rotation during the rotation-advancement technique commonly results in a shortened upper lip (reduced white lip height), making this the most frequent stigma of this repair method. A is incorrect because Cupid's bow flattening is more characteristic of straight-line repair techniques rather than rotation-advancement repairs. B is incorrect because lip lengthening typically occurs with Tennison triangular flap repairs, not rotation-advancement techniques. D is incorrect because triangular scars across the philtrum are associated with Tennison flap repairs, while rotation-advancement places scars along the philtral ridge. E is incorrect because excessive philtral width is a stigma specifically associated with bilateral cleft lip repairs, not unilateral repairs.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old woman has biopsy-confirmed basal cell carcinoma on her left mid-cheek and seeks surgical consultation. Physical examination shows a 0.6 cm lesion with poorly defined margins. Which factor most strongly indicates the need for Mohs micrographic surgery in this case?
A) Tumor location
B) Basal cell carcinoma diagnosis
C) Poorly defined margins
D) Patient's age
E) Tumor dimensions
questions.answer:
C)

Poorly defined or indistinct tumor borders represent the strongest indication for Mohs micrographic surgery in this case, as this technique allows for complete margin assessment and tissue-sparing excision of ill-defined lesions. A is incorrect because while facial location can be an indication, the mid-cheek is not considered a high-risk anatomical zone that would mandate Mohs surgery. B is incorrect because basal cell carcinoma diagnosis alone does not require Mohs surgery unless other high-risk features are present. D is incorrect because patient age is not a determining factor for Mohs surgery selection. E is incorrect because this tumor size (0.6 cm) is relatively small and does not meet the typical size criteria (>2 cm) that might indicate Mohs surgery.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female with diabetes type 2 presents to the emergency room with intense pain and discharge from her right buttock 36 hours following bilateral buttock enhancement using autologous fat from her thighs. Vital signs show temperature 102.0°F (38.9°C), pulse 105 bpm, respirations 16/min, and blood pressure 90/60 mmHg. Examination reveals dusky redness and cloudy fluid draining from an injection site on the right buttock. The patient experiences significant buttock tenderness, while her abdomen is soft. Laboratory values include WBC 18.5 × 10⁹/L and creatinine 1.5 mg/dL. Following stabilization, what is the most appropriate next management step?
A) Abdominal and pelvic CT imaging
B) Hospital admission for IV antibiotics
C) Discharge with oral antibiotics
D) Operative wound exploration
E) Buttock ultrasound examination
questions.answer:
D)
Operative wound exploration is the most appropriate next step. This clinical presentation suggests severe rapidly advancing infection, potentially necrotizing fasciitis, which requires immediate surgical intervention for diagnosis and treatment. The combination of systemic toxicity, local tissue changes, and rapid progression following cosmetic surgery demands urgent operative exploration and debridement to prevent fatal outcomes. A) is incorrect because imaging will delay necessary treatment and won't change management. B) is incorrect because antibiotics alone are insufficient for necrotizing fasciitis without surgical debridement. C) is incorrect because this severe infection with systemic signs requires immediate inpatient surgical care, not outpatient treatment. E) is incorrect because ultrasound will not provide definitive diagnosis or treatment for this surgical emergency.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female has liposuction performed on her abdomen, flanks, and thighs. The procedure uses 4 L of tumescent solution, with each liter containing 50 mL of 2% lidocaine without epinephrine and 1 mL of 1:1000 epinephrine. When would blood lidocaine levels be anticipated to reach their maximum in this patient?
A) Right after injection
B) 1 hour post-procedure
C) 2 to 4 hours post-procedure
D) 8 to 18 hours post-procedure
E) 24 to 48 hours post-procedure
questions.answer:
D)
Blood lidocaine concentrations reach their peak 8 to 18 hours following infiltration during liposuction procedures. This delayed peak occurs because lidocaine is slowly absorbed from the tumescent solution in the subcutaneous tissues. This timing is clinically significant since patients are often discharged home when peak levels occur, requiring careful dosage calculations. A) is incorrect because immediate absorption is minimal with tumescent technique. B) is incorrect because one hour is too early for peak absorption from subcutaneous tissues. C) is incorrect because 2-4 hours is still too early for maximum blood levels. E) is incorrect because 24-48 hours is beyond the typical peak absorption timeframe.

questions.question:
A 67-year-old female with a large ventral hernia following previous exploratory surgery for trauma is scheduled for complex abdominal wall reconstruction using posterior component separation with mesh placement. This surgical approach requires division of which muscle at which anatomical location?
A) External oblique lateral to the semilunar line
B) External oblique medial to the semilunar line
C) Internal oblique lateral to the semilunar line
D) Transversus abdominis lateral to the semilunar line
E) Transversus abdominis medial to the semilunar line
questions.answer:
E)
Posterior component separation involves releasing the transversus abdominis muscle medial to the semilunar line. This technique allows medialization of the posterior rectus sheath-transversalis fascia complex through retro-rectus dissection, creating a posterior closure layer with mesh placement between the posterior and anterior fascial layers. A) is incorrect because lateral external oblique release is used in anterior component separation, not posterior. B) is incorrect because external oblique is not released medially in either technique. C) is incorrect because internal oblique is not the primary muscle released in posterior component separation. D) is incorrect because transversus abdominis is released medially, not laterally, in posterior component separation.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female seeks abdominoplasty and liposuction of her flanks and mid-back. She is a non-smoker, can ascend two flights of stairs without dyspnea or chest discomfort, and takes thyroid medication for well-managed hypothyroidism. Her measurements are height 5 ft 6 in (167 cm), weight 260 lbs (118 kg), with BMI 42 kg/m². She has no other medical issues. Based on her clinical profile, what is her appropriate American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status classification?
A) ASA I
B) ASA II
C) ASA III
D) ASA IV
E) ASA V
questions.answer:
C)
This patient qualifies as ASA III due to her BMI exceeding 40 kg/m², which represents severe obesity with significant systemic disease. This classification may restrict her surgical options, as many office-based facilities only accept ASA I or II patients. The well-controlled hypothyroidism alone would not elevate her classification, but the morbid obesity does. A) is incorrect because ASA I requires no systemic disease, but BMI >40 constitutes significant pathology. B) is incorrect because ASA II covers mild systemic disease, but BMI >40 represents severe systemic disease. D) is incorrect because ASA IV indicates severe systemic disease with constant life threat, which doesn't apply here. E) is incorrect because ASA V is reserved for moribund patients not expected to survive without surgery.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old male presents to the clinic following a right ring finger injury during football. Physical examination reveals inability to bend the fingertip, with a hollow appearance along the palm side of the finger and tenderness in the palm when pressed. Radiographs are normal. What is the maximum timeframe for performing primary repair?
A) 1 day
B) 1 week
C) 1 month
D) 2 months
E) 3 months
questions.answer:
B)
This presentation describes jersey finger (flexor digitorum profundus rupture), which requires primary repair within 1 week for optimal outcomes. The injury involves tendon avulsion from the distal phalanx, and delayed repair beyond 7 days risks tendon necrosis due to compromised blood supply from vincular disruption. Early surgical intervention is crucial to prevent permanent contracture and restore function. A) is incorrect because while earlier repair is beneficial, 1 week is the accepted maximum timeframe, not 1 day. C) is incorrect because 1 month exceeds the safe window for primary repair of most jersey finger injuries. D) is incorrect because 2 months is too late for primary repair except in specific Type III injuries with large bone fragments. E) is incorrect because 3 months far exceeds the timeframe for primary repair and would require tendon reconstruction rather than primary repair.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient presents for evaluation of a 2.5-cm surgical wound on the nasal dorsum following Mohs micrographic excision of morpheaform basal cell carcinoma. Physical examination reveals a defect that spans from the nasal dorsum to the right nasal sidewall and extends to the superior nasal alar margins. The wound involves complete skin thickness, underlying subcutaneous tissue, and nasal musculature. The perichondrium overlying both the lower lateral and upper lateral cartilages has been removed. What reconstructive approach would be most suitable for this case?
A) Acellular dermal matrix with overlying thin split-thickness skin graft
B) Bilobed flap technique
C) Full-thickness skin graft placement
D) Paramedian forehead flap reconstruction
E) Superiorly based nasolabial flap
questions.answer:
D)
The paramedian forehead flap is the optimal reconstructive choice for this large, full-thickness nasal defect. For defects exceeding 1.5 cm, local flaps become inadequate and forehead flaps provide superior aesthetic outcomes with excellent skin color matching. A) Acellular dermal matrix with skin grafting is inappropriate for such a large, full-thickness defect requiring structural support. B) Bilobed flaps are best suited for smaller defects (1-1.5 cm) confined to the nose. C) Full-thickness skin grafts work well for smaller defects (5-10 mm) but would provide poor aesthetic results for this large defect. E) Superiorly based nasolabial flaps are typically reserved for alar defects up to 2 cm and would not adequately address this extensive dorsal defect.

questions.question:
A 10-year-old male patient with a history of cleft palate repair presents for assessment of velopharyngeal insufficiency characterized by limited palatal mobility and coronal closure pattern. Which muscle should be the primary target for the most suitable surgical intervention?
A) Hyoglossus
B) Levator veli palatini
C) Palatopharyngeus
D) Pharyngeal constrictor
E) Stylohyoid
questions.answer:
C)
The palatopharyngeus muscle is the appropriate target for sphincter pharyngoplasty in this clinical scenario. This muscle forms one of the tonsillar pillars and elevates the pharynx during swallowing to separate the nasopharynx from oropharynx. Bilateral transposition of these muscles creates an enhanced barrier to reduce velopharyngeal insufficiency. A) The hyoglossus is an extrinsic tongue muscle not typically used for VPI correction. B) The levator veli palatini is important in primary cleft repair but not effective in secondary cases with non-functional muscle. D) Pharyngeal constrictors are utilized in pharyngeal flaps, primarily for sagittal closure patterns rather than coronal patterns. E) The stylohyoid muscle attaches to the hyoid bone and is not commonly employed for VPI treatment.

questions.question:
An otherwise healthy 28-year-old woman comes to the physician requesting removal of bilateral axillary masses. She states that the masses fluctuate in size and tenderness with her menstrual cycle. She reports that the masses have not had discharge or drainage. Physical examination shows smooth, spongy masses in both axillae. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management of this patient?


A) Excise the bilateral axillary masses and skin
B) Obtain bilateral mammograms of the axillary masses
C) Order an MRI of the chest
D) Perform a core biopsy of both axillary masses
E) Perform liposuction
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


This patient presents with ectopic breast tissue. In utero, the milk line (galactic band) forms at 5 weeks of gestation. This bilateral structure courses from the axillae to the groin, and normal breasts form in the prepectoral region after there has been regression of the rest of the galactic band. When there is failure of this regression, breast tissue remains in locations outside of the normal breast. The most common location for ectopic breast tissue is in the axillae, although it can be found anywhere along the milk line from the axillae to the groin. Ectopic breast tissue outside of the milk line has been described and is termed aberrant breast tissue.


The tissue found in these ectopic locations is breast tissue with the same characteristics and propensity for disease as normally located breast tissue, and breast cancer has been described in these tissues. In the absence of pathologic findings such as a mass, pain, and skin changes that are associated with breast cancer, there is no strong oncologic indication for excision. If there are findings concerning for a neoplasm, then work-up should be initiated and might include further imaging, core biopsy, and surgery. However, most cases present without pathologic findings and are excised to achieve a more reasonable appearance for the patient, the ability to don clothing more comfortably, and for the obvious social advantages.


In this case, the patient is young, has no complaints, and has no physical findings to suggest a neoplasm. Excision should be offered.


Obtaining bilateral mammograms is incorrect because there is no indication for imaging in this patient based on her age, history, and physical examination. In addition, mammograms of axillary breast tissue are technically unfeasible.


Performing a core biopsy is incorrect as there is no concern for malignancy in this case. In the case of a mass noted within the ectopic axillary breast tissue, then an oncologic workup should be initiated which might include a core biopsy.


An MRI of the chest is incorrect because there is no indication for imaging in this patient based on her age, history, and physical examination.


Reassuring the patient with no further action is not the most appropriate management, as it will not address the patient‚Äos concerns and desires. In the patient who does not request excision or is not an appropriate surgical candidate, then reassurance and surveillance are appropriate.


As this is a young female with axillary breast tissue, liposuction will not improve the excess breast tissue or skin.


References
Francone E, Nathan MJ, Murelli F, et al. Ectopic breast cancer: case report and review of the literature. Aesthetic Plast Surg. 2013 Aug;37(4):746-9. Epub 2013 Apr 26.
Visconti G, Eltahir Y, Van Ginkel RJ, et al. Approach and management of primary ectopic breast carcinoma in the axilla: where are we? A comprehensive historical literature review. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2011 Jan;64(1):e1-11. Epub 2010 Oct 12.

questions.question:
What patient positioning strategy is most effective for preventing perioperative peripheral nerve injuries?
A) Positioning arms at 100-degree abduction in supine patients
B) Placing forearms in pronated position when arms are tucked in supine patients
C) Maintaining arms in dorsal extension in supine patients
D) Keeping neck in extended position for prone patients
E) Utilizing leg holders with heel support during lithotomy positioning
questions.answer:
E)
Leg holders incorporating heel support during lithotomy positioning effectively prevent peroneal nerve compression injuries by avoiding direct pressure on vulnerable nerve locations. A) Arm abduction should be limited to 90 degrees maximum to prevent brachial plexus injury, making 100 degrees excessive. B) When arms are tucked, forearms should be in neutral position, not pronated, to prevent ulnar nerve compression. C) Dorsal extension should be avoided as it can cause brachial plexus stretching and injury. D) The neck should be maintained in neutral position during prone positioning to prevent vertebral artery complications, not extended.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old African American female patient returns 6 months following Wise pattern breast reduction surgery. Physical examination reveals bilateral raised, itchy medial inframammary scars that remain within the original surgical boundaries. Intralesional triamcinolone (TAC) therapy is being considered. Which medication, when combined with TAC, would enhance long-term treatment outcomes?
A) 5-Fluorouracil
B) Diphenhydramine
C) Methotrexate
D) Tamoxifen
E) Verapamil
questions.answer:
A)
Combining 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) with triamcinolone has demonstrated superior efficacy compared to triamcinolone alone in randomized controlled trials for hypertrophic scar treatment. The typical protocol involves 4 mg TAC with 45 mg 5-FU administered weekly for 8 weeks, showing significant improvements in scar assessment scores. B) Diphenhydramine has theoretical interest but lacks clinical evidence for scar treatment efficacy. C) Methotrexate shows promise for keloid recurrence prevention but lacks definitive randomized data for hypertrophic scars. D) Tamoxifen has mechanistic interest but no current clinical data supporting its use. E) Verapamil has been shown inferior to intralesional TAC in randomized trials.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old male patient presents with a large congenital nevus on his calf. His medical history includes successfully treated lymphoma and his BMI is 28 kg/m². Tissue expander placement followed by staged excision and advancement flap reconstruction is planned. Which factor places this patient at greatest risk for expander-related complications?
A) Age
B) Elevated BMI
C) Expander location
D) History of malignancy
E) Male sex
questions.answer:
C)
Expander placement in extremity locations carries the highest complication risk according to multiple large-scale studies, with scalp and extremity sites showing significantly elevated complication rates compared to other anatomical locations. A) While younger age can be a risk factor in some studies, this teenager's age is not the primary concern. B) A BMI of 28 kg/m² is not a significant risk factor, and some studies suggest low BMI may actually increase risk. D) Successfully treated malignancy history does not indicate current immunocompromise or increased risk. E) Male sex is not generally considered a risk factor, and some studies suggest female sex may carry higher risk.

questions.question:
A 1-year-old boy presents to the clinic because his mother is worried about his mouth's appearance (shown). This patient's condition most likely resulted from failed fusion of which of the following structures?
A) Anterior and posterior hillocks
B) Frontonasal and maxillary prominences
C) Mandibular and maxillary prominences
D) Maxillary prominence and medial nasal process
E) Second and third pharyngeal arches
questions.answer:
C)
This patient exhibits a lateral facial cleft (macrostomia), which occurs due to failed fusion of the mandibular and maxillary prominences from the first pharyngeal arch. This orofacial anomaly, classified as a Tessier No. 7 cleft, ranges from minor lateral oral commissure displacement to extensive defects affecting lateral mouth, cheek skin and muscle, zygomatic arch, and occasionally temporal areas. A is incorrect because anterior and posterior auricular hillocks from the first and second pharyngeal arches form the external ear, not facial structures. B is incorrect because frontonasal and maxillary prominence fusion failures result in Tessier No. 2, 3, or 4 clefts, not lateral facial clefts. D is incorrect because maxillary prominence and medial nasal process fusion failure causes cleft lip, not lateral facial clefts. E is incorrect because second and third pharyngeal arch confluence occurs in the upper neck region, not the facial area.

questions.question:
A 1-year-old male child presents to the clinic with congenital drooping of the left eyelid. Physical examination reveals the eyelid margin obscures 4 mm of the upper corneal border, and levator movement measures 4 mm. Which of the following represents the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Fasanella-Servat procedure
B) Frontalis suspension with sling
C) Levator advancement
D) Müller muscle resection
E) Observation
questions.answer:
B)
With the eyelid margin covering more than 4 mm of the upper corneal border, this represents severe ptosis, and with levator function measuring 4 mm, this indicates poor levator function. Frontalis suspension is the appropriate surgical intervention for severe ptosis with poor levator function, providing excellent symmetry and durable outcomes. A is incorrect because Fasanella-Servat procedure is reserved for mild ptosis with good levator function. C is incorrect because levator advancement is used for moderate ptosis with fair levator function. D is incorrect because Müller muscle resection is indicated for mild ptosis with fair to good levator function. E is incorrect because observation is not appropriate for severe ptosis that significantly impairs vision and function.

questions.question:
A healthy 52-year-old woman without smoking history is scheduled for bilateral breast reconstruction using abdominal perforator flaps. Which of the following represents the most suitable antibiotic prophylaxis protocol?
A) Preoperative antibiotics
B) Preoperative chlorhexidine bath
C) Preoperative and intraoperative antibiotics
D) Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative antibiotics for 7 days
E) Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative antibiotics until all drains are removed
questions.answer:
C)
For a healthy patient undergoing prolonged autologous breast reconstruction, the optimal antibiotic prophylaxis includes preoperative intravenous antibiotics and intraoperative dosing to maintain therapeutic levels throughout the lengthy procedure. This approach prevents surgical site infections while avoiding unnecessary antibiotic exposure. A is incorrect because a single preoperative dose is insufficient for lengthy surgical procedures requiring sustained therapeutic antibiotic levels. B is incorrect because preoperative chlorhexidine bathing alone, while beneficial, is significantly less effective than antibiotic prophylaxis for infection prevention. D is incorrect because extended 7-day postoperative antibiotic courses have not demonstrated reduced infection rates and promote antibiotic resistance. E is incorrect because continuing antibiotics until drain removal lacks evidence for improved outcomes and increases risks of resistance and adverse reactions.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old woman presents for assessment 7 weeks following Zone II flexor tendon repair of the left middle finger. She describes hearing a "pop" at home and now cannot bend the finger at either interphalangeal joint. Current examination reveals finger swelling with moderate stiffness. Flexor tendon rupture is suspected. Surgical exploration confirms ruptures of both flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) and flexor digitorum profundus tendons, with a 1.5-cm profundus tendon gap and A2 pulley scarring. Which of the following represents the most appropriate management approach?
A) Excision of the flexor tendons with implantation of a passive silicone rod prosthesis
B) Fractional lengthening of the tendon in the forearm and revision of primary repair
C) Single-stage reconstruction with implantation of an active silicone rod prosthesis
D) Single-stage tendon reconstruction with palmaris graft
E) Tendon transfer from the ring finger FDS
questions.answer:
A)
This patient requires staged flexor tendon reconstruction due to significant scarring, poor passive motion, and a large tendon gap precluding primary repair. The first stage involves excising damaged tendons and implanting a passive silicone rod to create a pseudosheath, followed by tendon grafting once soft tissues heal and passive motion improves. B is incorrect because fractional lengthening cannot address the 1.5-cm gap and extensive scarring present 7 weeks post-repair. C is incorrect because active silicone rods require meeting single-stage reconstruction criteria, which this patient does not meet due to scarring and poor passive motion. D is incorrect because single-stage reconstruction requires adequate passive motion, minimal scarring, and functional pulley systems, none of which are present. E is incorrect because FDS transfers require single-stage reconstruction criteria and would be inappropriate given the extensive scarring and poor tissue quality.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old man with spinal cord injury has a right sacral pressure ulcer present for 12 months. He has no smoking or diabetes history. Osteomyelitis is controlled with oral antibiotics and nutrition is optimized. Physical examination demonstrates a 6 × 5 × 4-cm wound over the sacrum. Which of the following represents the most suitable reconstructive option for wound coverage?
A) Biceps femoris V-Y musculocutaneous advancement flap
B) Gluteal V-Y musculocutaneous advancement flap
C) Pedicled lumbosacral perforator flap
D) Pedicled tensor fascia lata flap
questions.answer:
B)
Gluteal V-Y musculocutaneous advancement flaps are the optimal choice for deep sacral pressure ulcer reconstruction, providing reliable coverage with the advantage of re-advancement capability for recurrent wounds or dehiscence. These flaps can be used unilaterally or bilaterally depending on wound size and are specifically designed for sacral region reconstruction. A is incorrect because biceps femoris V-Y flaps are designed for ischial pressure ulcers and cannot reach the sacral region as pedicled flaps. C is incorrect because pedicled lumbosacral perforator flaps are too small for deep sacral ulcers and are only suitable for small or superficial wounds. D is incorrect because pedicled tensor fascia lata flaps cannot reach sacral wounds and are primarily used for trochanteric pressure ulcer reconstruction.

questions.question:
A plastic surgeon is consulted in the neonatal intensive care unit to assess a newborn with a myelomeningocele. The infant has an unruptured 4 × 4-cm sac in the lumbosacral region with minimal fluid leakage from the site. Prompt surgical repair is recommended primarily for which of the following reasons?
A) To reduce the likelihood of cerebrospinal fluid shunt requirement
B) To reduce the need for folic acid supplementation
C) To enhance motor function recovery
D) To prevent bacterial meningitis
E) To prevent cerebrospinal fluid leakage
questions.answer:
D)
The primary indication for early myelomeningocele repair in the newborn period is to prevent infection and bacterial meningitis. The sac must be kept sterile and moist. Additional cardiac, orthopedic, and urologic evaluations are often required, along with assessment for hydrocephalus. While early repair has not been demonstrated to improve motor function recovery, it does improve neurogenic bladder outcomes. Cerebrospinal fluid leakage frequently occurs regardless of repair timing. Although folic acid supplementation reduces neural tube defects and myelomeningocele formation, postnatal supplementation has not proven effective. A is incorrect because while prenatal repair may reduce shunt needs, postnatal repair timing doesn't significantly affect this outcome. B is incorrect because postnatal folic acid supplementation doesn't benefit already formed neural tube defects. C is incorrect because early repair hasn't been shown to improve motor function return in postnatal cases. E is incorrect because CSF leakage commonly occurs regardless of surgical timing.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 2-year history of lower extremity lymphedema. She has been unable to achieve weight loss despite dietary efforts. Her BMI is 32 kg/m². Physical examination reveals asymmetry of the left lower extremity with increased circumference of both the thigh and calf. Which of the following represents the most appropriate management for this patient's lymphedema?
A) Administration of a benzopyrene
B) Administration of a diuretic
C) Application of Unna boots
D) Caloric restriction
E) Intermittent pneumatic pump compression therapy
questions.answer:
E)
Intermittent pneumatic pump compression therapy is the most appropriate treatment and should be initiated on an outpatient or home basis. The primary treatment approach is conservative medical management, including careful hygiene and regular examination, weight loss encouragement, trauma avoidance, avoiding restrictive clothing, and elevation of the affected limb. A is incorrect because benzopyrenes like flavonoids and coumarin, while useful adjuvants in other countries, are not clinically available in the United States. B is incorrect because diuretics have no therapeutic role in lymphedema management. C is incorrect because Unna boots are specifically used for venous stasis ulcers of the lower extremity, not lymphedema. D is incorrect because this patient has already failed dietary weight loss attempts, making caloric restriction likely ineffective.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old girl with a history of repaired complete cleft lip and palate as an infant comes for treatment of her alveolar cleft. During the preoperative consultation, management options for the bony defect are reviewed. Which of the following represents the main disadvantage of secondary bone grafting using iliac crest cancellous bone compared to demineralized bone matrix?
A) Cost
B) Donor site morbidity
C) Failure rate
D) Impact on mid face growth
E) Surgical procedure duration
questions.answer:
B)
The main disadvantage of iliac crest bone grafting is postoperative donor site pain, while demineralized bone matrix (DBM) has no donor site morbidity. A is incorrect because the increased operating room time costs for iliac crest bone graft are offset by the higher material costs of DBM. C is incorrect because failure rates are equivalent between DBM and iliac crest bone grafting for alveolar defects. D is incorrect because primary bone grafting (not secondary) negatively impacts mid-face growth, and this effect occurs regardless of the graft material used. E is incorrect because while iliac crest bone graft does increase operative time, this duration increase is not significant enough to cause meaningful morbidity.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old left-hand dominant man comes to the emergency department with right thumb pain following a hiking fall. Radiographic images are provided. Physical examination reveals thumb swelling, bruising, and tenderness to touch. The metacarpophalangeal joint shows 40 degrees of laxity with a solid endpoint during valgus stress testing. To assess whether conservative treatment is feasible, which of the following additional diagnostic tests should be obtained?
A) Arthrography
B) CT scan
C) Electrodiagnostic studies
D) Triple-phase bone scan
E) Ultrasonography
questions.answer:
E)
Ultrasonography is the most effective method to diagnose a Stener lesion, which would require surgical treatment for this patient. Stener lesions are specific ulnar collateral ligament injuries where the dorsal adductor aponeurosis becomes trapped between the torn ligament end and its insertion site at the proximal phalanx, preventing healing and requiring surgical repair. Ultrasonography is cost-effective, dynamic, readily available, and has a positive predictive value of 87-100% for identifying Stener lesions. A is incorrect because arthrography can identify capsular injury but cannot accurately detect collateral ligament displacement. B is incorrect because CT scan cannot clearly resolve ligament positioning. C is incorrect because electrodiagnostic studies evaluate nerve function, not ligament integrity. D is incorrect because triple-phase bone scan assesses bone metabolism and blood flow, not soft tissue ligament injuries.

questions.question:
A 6-year-old boy is evaluated for ongoing hypernasal speech. His medical history includes cardiac abnormalities and developmental delays. Physical examination demonstrates a wide nose, flattened cheekbones, epicanthal folds, small jaw, and excessive vertical maxillary height. Oral examination reveals a split uvula and a palpable notch in the posterior nasal spine. Which of the following imaging studies is most appropriate before surgical treatment?
A) Carotid angiography
B) MRA of the head and neck
C) PET scan of the brain
D) Renal ultrasonography
questions.answer:
B)
The patient exhibits features consistent with velocardiofacial syndrome, an autosomal dominant disorder resulting from chromosome 22q11 deletion. This syndrome includes cleft palate, velopharyngeal insufficiency, and cardiac defects. Characteristic facial features include a prominent wide nose, flattened cheekbones, epicanthal folds, small jaw, and increased vertical maxillary height. MRA is the preferred diagnostic method for detecting carotid vascular abnormalities, particularly medialization, which can complicate palatal or pharyngeal surgery. A is incorrect because while carotid angiography would provide similar information, it is unnecessarily invasive compared to MRA. C is incorrect because PET brain scanning does not address the vascular anatomy concerns relevant to surgical planning. D is incorrect because renal ultrasonography does not evaluate the carotid vascular anatomy that must be assessed before pharyngeal surgery.

questions.question:
Poly-L-lactic acid (Sculptra) therapy is most effective for addressing soft-tissue facial volume loss associated with which of the following conditions?
A) Discoid lupus erythematosus
B) Parry-Romberg syndrome
C) Systemic sclerosis
D) Antiretroviral therapy complications
questions.answer:
D)
Poly-L-lactic acid (Sculptra) is most effective for treating facial lipoatrophy caused by antiretroviral therapy complications in HIV patients. This injectable has been successfully used since 1999 for HIV medication-induced volume loss and represents its primary indication. The treatment works well for gradual volume restoration in cases of drug-related fat loss. A is incorrect because discoid lupus-related lipoatrophy responds better to autologous fat grafting rather than synthetic fillers. B is incorrect because Parry-Romberg syndrome involves severe progressive tissue loss that typically requires more substantial reconstruction with free flaps or fat grafting rather than injectable treatments. C is incorrect because systemic sclerosis causes skin tightening and fibrosis rather than the type of volume loss that responds well to poly-L-lactic acid injections.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department following a devastating hand injury from a car accident. Physical examination reveals the hand cannot be salvaged. Wrist disarticulation is being considered. What is the primary advantage of wrist disarticulation compared to transradial amputation?
A) Enhanced myoelectric prosthetic accommodation
B) Preserved forearm rotation capability
C) Reduced neuroma development risk
D) Lower prosthetic abandonment rates
E) Enhanced soft-tissue coverage stability
questions.answer:
B)
Wrist disarticulation preserves the distal radioulnar joint, which maintains forearm pronation and supination capabilities that are lost with transradial amputation. This preservation of rotational movement is the key functional advantage of the wrist-level approach. A is incorrect because the additional length from wrist disarticulation can actually create fitting challenges for myoelectric devices and may cause limb length discrepancies. C is incorrect because neuroma formation risk is not significantly different between these amputation levels. D is incorrect because wrist disarticulation patients actually have higher prosthetic abandonment rates compared to transradial amputees. E is incorrect because the bony prominences of the preserved radius and ulna can create pressure-related soft tissue problems with prosthetic wear.

questions.question:
What represents the most appropriate first-line treatment for lower limb lymphedema?
A) Charles procedure
B) Compression therapy
C) Suction-assisted lipectomy
D) Vascularized lymph node transplantation
E) Lymphaticovenous anastomosis
questions.answer:
B)
Compression therapy is the cornerstone of initial lymphedema management and should be the first treatment approach. Conservative management including compression garments, complete decongestive therapy, lifestyle modifications, and therapeutic exercise consistently demonstrates effectiveness in reducing limb volume and should be attempted before considering surgical interventions. A is incorrect because the Charles procedure is a radical surgical debulking technique reserved for end-stage cases that have failed all other treatments. C is incorrect because liposuction is a surgical intervention that should only be considered after conservative management has been unsuccessful. D is incorrect because vascularized lymph node transfer is an advanced microsurgical procedure reserved for patients who have failed conservative therapy. E is incorrect because lymphaticovenous anastomosis is a complex microsurgical technique that should only be performed after conservative measures have been exhausted.

questions.question:
In the mixed dentition phase, which permanent tooth emerges first?
A) Lower canine tooth
B) Lower first molar tooth
C) Lower first bicuspid tooth
D) Upper central incisor tooth
E) Upper lateral incisor tooth
questions.answer:
B)
The lower first molar is the initial permanent tooth to emerge during mixed dentition, typically appearing between ages 6-7 years posterior to the primary second molar. This tooth marks the beginning of the mixed dentition period when both primary and permanent teeth coexist in the mouth. A is incorrect because the mandibular canine erupts later in the sequence, typically between ages 9-10 years. C is incorrect because the mandibular first premolar erupts between ages 10-12 years, well after the first molar. D is incorrect because the maxillary central incisor erupts after the first molar, typically between ages 7-8 years. E is incorrect because the maxillary lateral incisor erupts even later, typically between ages 8-9 years, making it one of the later teeth in the mixed dentition sequence.

questions.question:
A healthy 17-year-old male arrives at the emergency department with a laceration on his distal middle toe that is actively bleeding. Which local anesthetic is most suitable for injection at the injury site prior to suturing?
A) 0.5% Lidocaine solution
B) 1% Lidocaine solution
C) 1% Lidocaine with sodium bicarbonate buffer
D) 1% Lidocaine with 1:200,000 epinephrine
E) 2% Lidocaine solution
questions.answer:
D)
1% Lidocaine with 1:200,000 epinephrine is the optimal choice for digital laceration repair. The epinephrine provides vasoconstriction that reduces bleeding, improves visualization, and facilitates repair while extending the anesthetic duration and allowing for lower lidocaine doses. Contrary to outdated beliefs, epinephrine is safe in digits as the vasoconstriction lasts only 60-90 minutes, far shorter than the time needed to cause tissue necrosis. A is incorrect because 0.5% lidocaine provides inadequate anesthesia for laceration repair and lacks hemostatic benefits. B is incorrect because plain lidocaine without epinephrine does not control bleeding, making the repair more difficult and providing shorter pain relief. C is incorrect because while bicarbonate reduces injection pain, it does not provide the hemostatic advantages crucial for digital repairs. E is incorrect because 2% lidocaine increases toxicity risk without providing additional benefits, and lacks the bleeding control that epinephrine provides.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old woman with Scandinavian ancestry seeks laser hair removal for fine facial hair on her upper lip. She presents with Fitzpatrick Type I skin characteristics, being extremely pale with platinum blonde hair and blue eyes. What is the most suitable hair removal approach for this patient?
A) Alexandrite laser (755 nm)
B) Electrolysis
C) Intense pulsed-light
D) Long-pulse ruby laser (694 nm)
E) Nd:YAG laser (1064 nm)
questions.answer:
B)
Electrolysis is the correct choice. Laser hair removal relies on targeting melanin pigment within hair follicles, making it ineffective for patients with light-colored hair that contains minimal melanin. While all the listed laser devices can be used for hair reduction, only electrolysis would provide effective results in this fair-haired patient. A is incorrect because alexandrite lasers require adequate melanin in hair for effectiveness. C is incorrect because intense pulsed-light also depends on melanin targeting. D is incorrect because ruby lasers similarly require melanin presence for hair destruction. E is incorrect because Nd:YAG lasers, despite deeper penetration, still rely on melanin absorption for hair removal.

questions.question: A 65-year-old man comes to the office with a 2-cm basal cell carcinoma involving the left nasal ala extending across the nasofacial junction onto the cheek. A photograph is shown. Medical history includes previous melanoma. Which of the following is an indication for Mohs micrographic surgery over conventional excision in this patient?A) Cancer sizeB) Diagnosis of basal cell carcinomaC) History of previous melanomaD) Location of the lesionE) Patient age
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Mohs micrographic surgical technique has demonstrated cure rates of 99% for primary basal cell carcinomas and up to 95% for recurrent basal cell carcinomas. In this particular patient, the strongest indication for use of the Mohs technique is the anatomical location. The nose is considered a high-risk location in the classically described ‚ÄuH-zone.‚Äu This patient underwent Mohs excision with multi-stage forehead flap reconstruction, as shown in the photographs. Patient age, history of previous melanoma, and tumor size 2 cm or less are not standard indications for Mohs excision. Other indications for Mohs technique include the following: Recurrent basal cell/squamous cell carcinomas, Locations prone to recurrence- ‚ÄuH-zone‚Äu of the face: periorbital, periauricular, temple, upper lip, nose/nasolabial fold, and chin, Tumors involving critical structures such as the eyelid or lip, Functionally important areas such as the genitals, perianal location, hands, and feet, Tumors arising in sites of previous irradiation therapy, Large tumors (> 2 cm) Lesions with ill-defined tumor margins, Histologic aggressive subtype (morpheaform, basosquamous, perineural, and invasive/poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma) Tumors arising in immunosuppressed patients such as transplant recipients or patients with genetic predisposition (basal cell nevus syndrome, xeroderma pigmentosum)ReferencesDenkler K, Kivett WF. Management of Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer. In: Mathes SJ, ed. Plastic Surgery. 2nd ed. Philadelphia, PA: Saunders-Elsevier; 2006;5: 391-464.Connolly KL, Nehal KS, Disa JJ. Evidence-Based Medicine: Cutaneous Facial Malignancies: Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2017 Jan;139(1):181e-190e.Netscher DT, Spira M. Basal Cell Carcinoma: An Overview of Tumor Biology and Treatment. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2004;113(5):74e-94e.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old woman develops complications following a facelift with SMAS resection. After drain removal on postoperative day 2, she presents with a persistent fluid collection on the right side. The aspirated fluid appears clear and shows markedly elevated amylase levels. The parotid duct remains undamaged. A bland diet and scopolamine patch have been initiated. What additional intervention would most likely benefit this patient's condition?
A) Anti-inflammatory medication
B) Botulinum toxin type A injections
C) Direct surgical repair of the injury
D) Nerve grafting of the injury
E) Surgical evacuation of the fluid
questions.answer:
B)
Botulinum toxin type A injections are the most appropriate additional treatment. This patient has developed a salivary leak from parotid gland injury during surgery. The goal is to minimize salivary production while allowing spontaneous healing. Botulinum toxin injections directly into the gland effectively reduce salivary secretions and have shown success in managing these complications. A is incorrect because anti-inflammatory medications do not address the underlying salivary production issue. C is incorrect because surgical repair may cause additional damage and worsen the condition. D is incorrect because nerve grafting is not indicated for this type of glandular injury. E is incorrect because surgical evacuation alone does not prevent continued fluid accumulation and may cause further trauma.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old woman undergoes tissue expander replacement with permanent implant and fat transfer 3 months following complete expansion. During surgery, total capsulectomy is performed due to capsular thickness and positioning. What is the appropriate CPT coding for this procedure?
A) 11970 and 20926
B) 19342 and 20926
C) 19371 and 11970
D) 19328, 19342, and 20926
E) 19371, 11970, and 20926
questions.answer:
E)
The correct coding includes 19371 (capsulectomy), 11970 (tissue expander removal and replacement), and 20926 (fat grafting). CPT code 11970 covers the capsulotomy approach but not the complete capsulectomy, which requires separate reporting with 19371. Fat grafting is reported separately with 20926. A is incorrect because it omits the capsulectomy code. B is incorrect because using 19342 with 20926 would be unbundling since 19342 includes fat grafting. C is incorrect because it omits the fat grafting code. D is incorrect because using 19342 with additional codes 19328 and 20926 constitutes inappropriate unbundling.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old woman comes to the office for evaluation of a poor outcome after liposuction of the arms. She says she is dissatisfied with the marked laxity of the skin of her arms. A photograph is shown. History includes gastric bypass surgery followed by a 100-lb (45.3-kg) weight loss. BMI is 28 kg/m2. Which of the following procedures is most appropriate to improve contour of the arm in this patient?


A) Laser-assisted liposuction
B) Lipobrachioplasty
C) Radiofrequency treatment (Thermage)
D) T-incision brachioplasty
E) Ultrasound-assisted liposuction
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Traditional brachioplasty comprises a T-shaped scar along the length of the arm and the axilla. This patient has excess skin on her arm, which dictates the necessity for an excisional procedure. Further liposuction of any modality will exaggerate her presentation further, including Vaser liposuction, a form of ultrasound-assisted liposuction, and laser-assisted liposuction, both of which are reported to tighten skin through heating its undersurface. There is no evidence to support Thermage as an effective treatment for lax skin. Lipobrachioplasty is a technique which safely combines liposuction with excisional surgery, performing liposuction on the proposed area to be excised. In a thinned arm, potential risks of neuropathy and seroma that accompany liposuction are unnecessary in a patient with lax skin that requires excision to improve contour. 


Limited incision brachioplasty with excision limited to an ellipse in the axilla, with or without liposuction, provides very limited results with regard to improving overall arm contour, particularly with moderate-to-severe skin redundancy.


References
1. Aly A, Soliman S, Cram A. Brachioplasty in the massive weight loss patient. Clin Plast Surg. 2008 Jan;35(1):141-147.
2. Nguyen AT, Rohrich RJ. Liposuction-assisted posterior brachioplasty: technical refinements in upper arm contouring. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Oct;126(4):1365-1369.
3. Shermak MA. Traditional brachioplasty. In: Shermak MA, ed. Body Contouring. New York: McGraw-Hill Professional; 2011:42-47.
4. Iverson RE, Pao VS. MOC-PS(SM) CME article: liposuction. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008 Apr;121(4 Suppl):1-11.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old woman presents for evaluation one day following glabellar injection of 0.8 mL hyaluronic acid filler. She reports intense pain since the procedure. Examination reveals significant edema and purple-blue skin discoloration over the glabella. Massage and heat application provide minimal relief. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Antibiotic therapy
B) Aspiration of injected material
C) Conservative operative debridement
D) Hyperbaric oxygen therapy
E) Injection of hyaluronidase
questions.answer:
E)
Hyaluronidase injection is the most appropriate immediate treatment. The patient's severe pain, swelling, and violaceous discoloration suggest vascular compromise, likely venous congestion from excessive filler volume. Hyaluronidase rapidly breaks down hyaluronic acid, reducing tissue volume and pressure, making it essential for treating filler-related vascular complications. A is incorrect because antibiotics don't address the underlying vascular compromise from filler volume. B is incorrect because aspiration is rarely feasible 1-2 days post-injection when venous compromise typically manifests. C is incorrect because surgical debridement is premature and may cause additional tissue damage. D is incorrect because hyperbaric oxygen is reserved for cases where skin necrosis appears imminent, not as first-line treatment.

questions.question:
Which acid is included in the formulation of Jessner solution?
A) Ascorbic acid
B) Glycolic acid
C) Kojic acid
D) Malic acid
E) Salicylic acid
questions.answer:
E)
Salicylic acid is a key component of Jessner solution. This chemical peel preparation contains three acids at 14% concentration each: salicylic acid USP, lactic acid USP, and resorcinol USP, dissolved in ethanol USP. It serves as a light peel or preparation for deeper TCA peels. A is incorrect because ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is not part of Jessner solution formulation. B is incorrect because glycolic acid is used in other chemical peels but not in Jessner solution. C is incorrect because kojic acid is a separate skin lightening agent that inhibits tyrosinase, not a Jessner component. D is incorrect because malic acid is found in other peel formulations but not in Jessner solution.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male patient undergoes preoperative radiotherapy for a large skull osteosarcoma requiring a 9-cm² cranial bone removal. What is the most suitable reconstructive material for this defect?
A) Bone graft from donor with bone morphogenic protein (BMP)
B) Calcium phosphate cement
C) Polyether ether ketone (PEEK) prosthesis
D) Titanium mesh plate
questions.answer:
C)
PEEK implants are the optimal choice because they are radiolucent, allowing clear surveillance imaging without artifacts, and can be custom-made for the planned resection size. Bone allograft with BMP is contraindicated in malignancy cases since BMP promotes bone growth and may contribute to tumor development. Calcium phosphate is suitable only for smaller defects and carries high infection risk, especially contraindicated after preoperative radiation. Titanium mesh creates significant imaging artifacts that interfere with cancer surveillance monitoring.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old male patient presents with an open ankle fracture exposing internal hardware. A sural artery flap reconstruction is being considered. Which vein must be included during flap harvest?
A) Anterior tibial vein
B) Lesser saphenous vein
C) Peroneal vein
D) Popliteal vein
E) Posterior tibial vein
questions.answer:
B)
The lesser saphenous vein must be harvested with the sural artery flap as it provides the venous drainage for this posterior leg cutaneous flap, along with the sural nerve that accompanies it. The anterior tibial vein is not part of this flap's vascular supply. The peroneal vein does not contribute to the sural flap anatomy. The popliteal vein is not involved in the sural flap's venous drainage system. The posterior tibial vein is separate from the sural flap's vascular network.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male with 35% total body surface area burns sustained 24 hours prior is being managed in the burn intensive care unit. Following Parkland formula resuscitation with adequate urine output, gastric feeding was initiated based on admission weight. Which clinical finding most strongly indicates the need to reduce feeding to minimal trophic levels?
A) Scheduled operative debridement beginning in 8 hours
B) Low blood pressure requiring vasopressin therapy
C) Slight abdominal swelling that remains soft on examination
D) Gastric tube drainage of 100 mL over 24 hours
E) Requirement for escharotomy procedure
questions.answer:
B)
Hypotension requiring vasopressor support indicates compromised systemic perfusion, which can lead to inadequate intestinal blood flow and potential gut ischemia when combined with the metabolic demands of full enteral feeding. Scheduled operative debridement requires NPO status for 8 hours but doesn't necessitate trophic feeds. Mild soft abdominal distension is not concerning compared to firm, obvious distension. Gastric output of 100 mL/24 hours is below the 200 mL threshold that would indicate feeding intolerance. Escharotomy increases fluid requirements but doesn't alter nutritional metabolic needs.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male is assessed 2 weeks following open reduction and internal fixation of a distal tibial extra-articular fracture due to wound breakdown. Examination reveals exposed metalwork and a 5×3-cm open defect above the medial malleolus. Following complete debridement, hardware extraction, and external fixation placement, closure is performed using a perforator propeller flap from a posterior tibial artery perforator. During elevation and positioning, the flap develops progressive edema and cyanosis with rapid capillary return throughout. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Topical nitropaste application
B) Free tissue transfer salvage
C) Postoperative medicinal leech treatment
D) Proximal perforator exploration to source artery
E) Conservative observation
questions.answer:
D)
Proximal perforator dissection to the source vessel is essential to release fascial constrictions and prevent venous kinking, which is the primary cause of congestion in propeller flaps during 180-degree rotation. Nitropaste is inappropriate for acute venous insufficiency management. Free flap reconstruction would only be considered after complete flap failure, not as initial congestion management. Leech therapy is reserved for postoperative venous congestion when surgical options are exhausted, not as a primary intraoperative intervention. Observation is inappropriate for progressive congestion noted during surgery affecting the entire flap length.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old female is being evaluated for fluid collection six weeks following a lower body lift after significant weight reduction. The procedure was uncomplicated with drain removal completed. Multiple fluid aspirations have been unsuccessful. The surgeon is contemplating sclerosant injection into the fluid cavity. Which medication is most commonly employed for this purpose?
A) Doxorubicin
B) Doxycycline
C) Erythromycin
D) Gentamycin
questions.answer:
B)
Doxycycline is the most frequently used sclerosant agent for seroma treatment, along with bleomycin, due to its proven efficacy in obliterating fluid collections. Doxorubicin is a chemotherapy agent not used for sclerotherapy of seromas. Erythromycin is an antibiotic without sclerosing properties for fluid collection management. Gentamycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic that lacks the sclerosing characteristics needed for seroma treatment.

questions.question:
A 41-year-old male presents to the emergency room after being unable to shut his mouth following a yawn. He experiences jaw discomfort. What is the most suitable first-line treatment?
A) Joint reconstruction surgery
B) Manual reduction under sedation
C) Surgical removal of bony prominence
D) Botulinum toxin A administration
E) Joint injection with sclerosing agents
questions.answer:
B)
This patient presents with acute anterior temporomandibular joint dislocation. Manual reduction under sedation is the appropriate initial treatment as it helps relax the spastic muscles (masseter, temporalis, and pterygoid) that prevent the condyle from returning to its normal position in the glenoid fossa. The reduction technique involves downward and backward movement of the jaw. A is incorrect because arthroplasty is a surgical procedure reserved for chronic recurrent dislocations, not acute cases. C is incorrect because eminectomy is also used for preventing chronic recurrent dislocations, not as initial treatment for acute dislocation. D is incorrect because botulinum toxin injection is an alternative treatment for recurrent cases, not the standard first-line approach for acute dislocation. E is incorrect because intra-articular sclerosing injections are outdated treatments for chronic cases and have poor long-term efficacy.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old commercial driver is brought to the emergency room after a car accident. He is unconscious, intubated, and immobilized. Physical findings include facial bruising, left jaw swelling, and visible pulsing of the left eyeball. Which fracture location poses the greatest risk?
A) Lower jaw body
B) Central maxillary support
C) Nasal fracture
D) Upper eye socket
E) Cheekbone complex
questions.answer:
D)
Fractures of the orbital roof are most concerning because they can extend into the middle cranial fossa, potentially creating communication between the cavernous sinus and carotid artery, leading to a carotid-cavernous fistula. The pulsating globe (pulsatile exophthalmos) is a key clinical sign of this serious complication. A is incorrect because mandibular body fractures, while significant, do not typically cause life-threatening vascular complications. B is incorrect because medial maxillary buttress fractures are important structurally but don't pose the same vascular risk as orbital roof fractures. C is incorrect because nasal bone fractures are relatively minor injuries that don't threaten vital structures. E is incorrect because zygomatic-malar complex fractures, though important for facial function and aesthetics, don't carry the same risk of carotid-cavernous fistula formation.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old male visits the clinic due to chin swelling. A panoramic radiograph is provided. What type of cyst is most probable?
A) Follicular
B) Gum-related
C) Root tip
D) Developmental
E) Remaining
questions.answer:
A)
This radiographic appearance is most characteristic of a dentigerous (follicular) cyst, which is the second most frequent odontogenic cyst. These cysts develop around the crown of an impacted tooth, typically showing a radiolucent area attached at an acute angle to the unerupted tooth. Third molars are most commonly affected. B is incorrect because gingival cysts are superficial lesions in the gum tissue and wouldn't present with this deep radiographic appearance. C is incorrect because periapical cysts occur at the root tip of infected teeth and would show lucency at the tooth apex, not around the crown. D is incorrect because primordial cysts develop in place of a tooth rather than around an existing unerupted tooth. E is incorrect because residual cysts are remnants of periapical cysts that remain after tooth extraction, which doesn't match this clinical scenario.

questions.question:
Targeted muscle reinnervation enhances which form of prosthetic control for patients with above-elbow amputation?
A) Mechanical cable
B) Muscle signal detection
C) Non-functional
D) Manual activation
questions.answer:
B)
Targeted muscle reinnervation (TMR) enhances electromyographic (muscle signal detection) control by using nerve transfers to create additional distinct muscle signals that can be detected by EMG sensors. This technique increases the number of independent control sites available for prosthetic operation, allowing for more sophisticated prosthetic function in above-elbow amputees who have limited residual muscle groups. A is incorrect because cable control relies on body movement through harnesses and cables, not on the enhanced muscle signals that TMR provides. C is incorrect because passive prosthetics are non-functional devices used primarily for cosmetic purposes and don't utilize the enhanced muscle signals from TMR. D is incorrect because switch control uses simple on/off mechanisms rather than the amplified and multiplied muscle signals that TMR creates.

questions.question:
A healthy 45-year-old woman has bilateral breast reconstruction using free abdominal perforator flaps. Only the deep inferior epigastric vein was connected to the internal mammary vein with a 3.5-mm coupler. Her right reconstructed breast shows progressive congestion. Doppler examination reveals strong signals, and the vascular connections appear patent without compression or bleeding. What is the best next management step?
A) Connect the lateral deep epigastric vein
B) Connect the superficial inferior epigastric vein
C) Redo the arterial connection
D) Redo both connections
E) Redo the venous connection
questions.answer:
B)
The most appropriate management is to perform an additional anastomosis of the superficial inferior epigastric vein. This clinical scenario represents persistent superficial venous system dominance, where venous blood cannot adequately drain from the superficial system into the deep system (which is the only system currently anastomosed). This occurs due to either anatomical dominance of the superficial venous system or insufficient perforator connections between the two systems. A is incorrect because the lateral deep epigastric vein wouldn't address the superficial system drainage problem that's causing the congestion. C is incorrect because the arterial anastomosis is functioning well as evidenced by strong Doppler signals, so revision isn't needed. D is incorrect because both anastomoses are patent and functioning; the issue is inadequate venous drainage from the superficial system. E is incorrect because the deep venous anastomosis is working properly; the problem is that it's the only drainage route while the superficial system needs its own egress.

questions.question:
A 22-month-old female infant presents with a large mixed micro- and macrocystic lymphatic malformation of the right lower extremity. A photograph is shown. Medical history includes two rounds of sclerotherapy for the macrocystic component at 6 and 12 months of age and repeated infections, requiring a long hospital stay for intravenous antibiotic therapy 4 months ago. Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy for this patient?


A) Amputation
B) Embolization
C) Power-assisted liposuction
D) Repeated sclerotherapy
E) Surgical debulking
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


This 22-month-old female has undergone treatment of the macro cystic component of the lymphatic malformation and continues to present with complication secondary to the disease. In addition to difficulty of mobilization, fitting of regular clothes, nutrition problems due to repeated infections, there is also significant life threatening risk of severe infection. Even though compression garment and repeated sclerotherapy are potential options, there will be no control of the disease. The best next step is surgical debulking. Embolization is not appropriate for a lymphatic malformation, and amputation is not indicated at this time. Power-assisted liposuction would be indicated for lymphedema, not for a lymphatic malformation.


ReferencesDefnet AM, Bagrodia N, Hernandez SL, et al. Pediatric lymphatic malformations: evolving understanding and therapeutic options. J Pediatr Surg Int. 2016 May;32(5):425-33. doi: 10.1007/s00383-016-3867-4. Epub 2016 Jan 27.Kanth AM, Krevalin M, Adetayo OA, Patel A. Surgical Management of Pediatric Lymphedema: A Systematic Review. J Reconstr Microsurg. 2019 Feb 27. doi: 10.1055/s-0039-1681068.

questions.question:
A male neonate is presented to a specialized multidisciplinary referral facility for assessment of anorectal abnormality, tracheoesophageal fistula and missing right thumb. Which of the following VACTERL-related conditions is the strongest predictor of hospital mortality?
A) Aniridia with brainstem underdevelopment
B) Spinal or vertebral defects
C) Heart defects
D) Kidney or urinary tract abnormalities
E) Tracheal narrowing with noisy breathing
questions.answer:
C)
Heart defects represent the most significant predictor of mortality in VACTERL association patients. Multiple studies have consistently demonstrated that congenital cardiac anomalies, particularly those requiring surgical intervention, are associated with the highest mortality risk among all VACTERL components. A) is incorrect because aniridia and brainstem hypoplasia are not characteristic features of VACTERL association. B) is incorrect because while vertebral anomalies are part of VACTERL, they are not the strongest mortality predictor compared to cardiac disease. D) is incorrect because renal abnormalities, though common in VACTERL, carry lower mortality risk than cardiac defects. E) is incorrect because tracheal stenosis is not a primary component of VACTERL association.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female presents for evaluation due to dissatisfaction with uneven skin texture 1 year following power-assisted liposuction performed with the super-wet method. Examination reveals skin surface irregularities arranged in a radial pattern around a single 1-cm scar. Which of the following factors most likely contributed to this complication?
A) Incorrect power settings
B) Multiple entry points
C) Inadequate postoperative compression
D) Suctioning in the superficial fat layer
E) Utilization of small-diameter cannulas
questions.answer:
D)
Suctioning in the superficial fat layer is the most likely cause of the described surface irregularities. When liposuction is performed too close to the skin surface, it creates visible contour deformities and irregularities that can be seen and felt through the skin. A) is incorrect because power source settings do not directly cause surface contour problems. B) is incorrect because multiple access sites actually help prevent irregularities by allowing cross-tunneling from different angles. C) is incorrect because poor compression leads to prolonged swelling but not permanent surface irregularities. E) is incorrect because fine cannulas are actually preferred to minimize surface irregularities when used in the appropriate deep fat plane.

questions.question:
Which of the following conditions is most frequently linked with Pierre Robin sequence?
A) Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
B) Hemifacial microsomia
C) Stickler syndrome
D) Treacher Collins syndrome
E) DiGeorge syndrome
questions.answer:
C)
Stickler syndrome is the most common syndromic association with Pierre Robin sequence, accounting for over 40% of syndromic cases. This collagen disorder, most commonly caused by COL2A1 mutations, presents with ocular abnormalities, hearing loss, joint problems, and craniofacial features including the mandibular underdevelopment seen in Pierre Robin sequence. A) is incorrect because Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, while potentially associated, is much less common than Stickler syndrome in Pierre Robin patients. B) is incorrect because hemifacial microsomia has a significantly lower association rate with Pierre Robin sequence. D) is incorrect because Treacher Collins syndrome, though it can present with mandibular hypoplasia, is not the most common syndromic association. E) is incorrect because DiGeorge (velocardiofacial) syndrome has a much lower frequency of association with Pierre Robin sequence compared to Stickler syndrome.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old female seeks consultation regarding asymmetric breast appearance. Examination demonstrates the right nipple-areolar complex positioned more superiorly with reduced breast volume. The right anterior axillary fold is absent. Which of the following additional examination findings is most probable?
A) Supernumerary nipple
B) Ear malformation
C) Right foot deformity
D) Evidence of repaired cleft lip
E) Underdeveloped right-hand fingers
questions.answer:
E)
Underdeveloped right-hand fingers are most likely to be found in this patient with Poland syndrome. The described chest findings (absent pectoralis major muscle, breast asymmetry, missing anterior axillary fold) are classic for Poland syndrome, which commonly includes ipsilateral hand abnormalities such as shortened or absent digits, particularly affecting the middle fingers. A) is incorrect because supernumerary nipples are not characteristic features of Poland syndrome. B) is incorrect because ear malformations are not typically associated with Poland syndrome. C) is incorrect because foot deformities are not part of the Poland syndrome spectrum. D) is incorrect because cleft lip is not associated with Poland syndrome.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old female with a history of breast augmentation using textured silicone implants has confirmed breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) on tissue analysis. Imaging studies including MRI and PET reveal no masses, with abnormal activity confined to the periprosthetic fluid collection. What is the most appropriate management approach?
A) Front capsule removal with bilateral implant extraction
B) Total capsule removal with implant extraction on the involved side
C) Partial capsule removal with implant replacement
D) Textured implant removal and smooth implant substitution
E) Fibrin glue application to seal the fluid cavity
questions.answer:
B)
Total capsule removal with implant extraction on the involved side represents the standard treatment for localized BIA-ALCL according to NCCN guidelines. Complete capsulectomy ensures removal of all potentially affected tissue, while implant removal eliminates the source of the lymphoma. A) is incorrect because bilateral treatment is not mandatory for unilateral disease, though it may be considered. C) is incorrect because partial capsulectomy is inadequate treatment that may leave residual lymphoma cells. D) is incorrect because implant replacement of any type is not appropriate in the acute treatment phase of BIA-ALCL. E) is incorrect because sealing the cavity does not address the underlying lymphoma and is not a recognized treatment approach.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old female presents to the clinic with a raised scar following abdominoplasty performed 3 months prior. A comprehensive treatment plan for scar improvement is being considered. Which of the following treatment options has the strongest evidence base for this patient?
A) Onion extract (Allium cepa)
B) Autologous fat grafting
C) Percutaneous collagen induction
D) Silicone-based gel therapy
E) Topical vitamin E
questions.answer:
D)
Silicone-based gel therapy has shown effectiveness in treating hypertrophic scars through multiple clinical studies and is backed by level I evidence. A) Onion extract has limited high-quality evidence supporting its use in scar treatment. B) Autologous fat grafting lacks robust clinical evidence for hypertrophic scar improvement. C) Percutaneous collagen induction has only lower-level evidence for scar management. E) Topical vitamin E is not supported by strong clinical evidence for hypertrophic scar treatment.

questions.question:
A 59-year-old female develops an infected sternal wound dehiscence following coronary bypass surgery 4 weeks earlier. Following wound debridement, five sternal fixation plates and bilateral pectoralis muscle flaps are utilized for reconstruction. Post-procedure, the patient develops low blood pressure, rapid heart rate, and altered mental status. Neck vein distension is observed. Blood oxygen levels remain normal on supplemental oxygen. What is the most appropriate first intervention?
A) Cardiac auscultation
B) Chest radiograph
C) Electrocardiogram
D) Echocardiography
E) Immediate surgical re-exploration
questions.answer:
A)
Cardiac auscultation will reveal muffled heart tones and pericardial friction rub, guiding immediate recognition and treatment of cardiac tamponade. The patient exhibits Beck's triad with risk factors for tamponade. B) Chest radiograph could help exclude pneumothorax but normal oxygenation makes this less likely, and other steps are more appropriate initially. C) Electrocardiogram may support pericardial effusion diagnosis but is not definitive and serves only as supplementary information. D) Echocardiography can confirm pericardial effusion and guide drainage but should follow initial auscultation. E) Immediate surgical re-exploration is premature without proper initial assessment.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old male presents for evaluation of painless right facial swelling that developed 2 months following a knife assault resulting in a mid-facial laceration. The wound was primarily closed in the emergency department. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Collection drainage combined with anti-salivary medications
B) Surgical debridement followed by skin grafting
C) Operative exploration with duct re-connection
D) Complete parotidectomy preserving facial nerve function
E) Image-guided needle drainage alone
questions.answer:
A)
Collection drainage with anti-salivary medications effectively manages late-presenting salivary collections (sialoceles) that commonly develop after parotid duct injury. B) Surgical debridement with skin grafting is not indicated for salivary collections. C) Operative exploration with duct re-connection is technically challenging and typically unsuccessful when performed late after injury. D) Complete parotidectomy is reserved for cases that fail conservative management. E) Image-guided needle drainage alone without anti-salivary therapy is insufficient treatment.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old commercial fisherman seeks treatment for a 3-week history of index finger swelling. The finger remains in a bent position, with difficult but painless straightening. Operative examination reveals clear fluid within the tendon covering. Which organism is most likely to be identified on fluid culture?
A) Eikenella corrodens
B) Mycobacterium marinum
C) Sporothrix schenckii
D) Staphylococcus aureus
E) Vibrio vulnificus
questions.answer:
B)
Mycobacterium marinum is the most frequent atypical mycobacterium causing hand infections in individuals exposed to marine environments, typically presenting as chronic, painless flexor tenosynovitis. A) Eikenella corrodens is associated with human bite injuries and typically causes painful infections. C) Sporothrix schenckii is found in soil and plants, causing lymphatic chain lesions rather than isolated tenosynovitis. D) Staphylococcus aureus causes painful suppurative tenosynovitis with classic inflammatory signs. E) Vibrio vulnificus causes rapidly progressive, painful cellulitis with hemorrhagic bullae and systemic symptoms.
