A 1-year-old boy is brought to the office by his parents for evaluation and correction of the findings shown in the photograph. The patient is otherwise healthy. Which of the following techniques is most appropriate to reconstruct the apex of the web space in this patient?


A) Bilobed flap from the dorsal hand
B) Cross-finger flap
C) Full-thickness skin grafting
D) Proximally based dorsal rectangular flap
E) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Full-thickness skin grafts are usually used to close the resultant defects of the fingers after release of congenital syndactyly.


Several local dorsal flaps have been described to reconstruct the web space with differing shapes to avoid the use of skin grafts, including rectangular, a V-Y island, a dorsal flap interdigitated with a small palmar V and a dorsal V-shape. 


A bilobed flap has been described for treating web creep in adults, but would not routinely be used.


References
Hsu VM, Smartt JM, Chang B. The modified V-Y dorsal metacarpal flap for repair of syndactyly without skin graft. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Jan;125(1):225-32.
Matsumine H, Yoshinaga Y, Fujiwara O, et al. Improved "bell-bottom" flap surgical technique for syndactyly without skin graft. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2011 Nov;128(5):504e-509e.
Miyamoto J, Nagasao T and Miyamoto S. Biomechanical analysis of surgical correction of syndactyly. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Mar;125(3):963-8.
Sahin C, Ergun O, Kulahci Y, et al. Bilobe flap for web reconstruction in adult syndactyly release: a new technique which can avoid the use of skin graft. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2014 Jun;67(6):815-21.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female presents with enophthalmos secondary to left orbital trauma that occurred 6 months previously. What is the minimal orbital volume increase that can cause post-traumatic enophthalmos?
A) 1%
B) 5%
C) 10%
D) 25%
E) 50%
questions.answer:
B)
A 5% increase in orbital volume is the minimum threshold that can result in clinically apparent post-traumatic enophthalmos. This occurs when bony orbital anatomy is inadequately restored following fracture displacement, commonly affecting the orbital floor or medial wall. A is incorrect because a 1% volume increase is too small to produce noticeable enophthalmos. C is incorrect because 10% represents a more significant volume change that would cause obvious enophthalmos, but the threshold is lower. D is incorrect because 25% volume increase would result in severe enophthalmos, far exceeding the minimum threshold. E is incorrect because 50% volume increase would cause dramatic enophthalmos, much greater than the minimum required.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female experiences significant tenderness at the residual index finger tip 8 weeks following fingertip amputation. Physical examination demonstrates marked stump sensitivity. Which therapeutic modality is most appropriate for desensitizing the amputation stump?
A) Functional electrical stimulation
B) Splint immobilization
C) Kinesiology taping
D) Semmes-Weinstein monofilament testing
E) Vibratory stimulation
questions.answer:
E)
Vibratory stimulation is the most appropriate desensitization technique for amputation stump neuromas. Treatment involves applying vibration peripherally around the sensitive area and gradually progressing toward the center. Additional therapeutic methods include massage and transcutaneous nerve stimulation. A is incorrect because functional electrical stimulation is not a recognized desensitization modality for neuromas. B is incorrect because immobilization would not address the hypersensitivity and may worsen stiffness. C is incorrect because kinesiology tape is used for edema control and support, not desensitization of amputated stumps. D is incorrect because Semmes-Weinstein monofilaments are assessment tools for measuring sensation, not therapeutic desensitization devices.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female patient is sent to your clinic by her dental provider due to a 6-week duration of visible intraoral bone exposure. She is currently on zoledronic acid therapy for osteoporosis management. Clinical examination reveals a 1-cm gingival ulcer with visible necrotic bone tissue near the right premolar tooth. There are no signs of active infection or fistula formation present. Along with thorough oral hygiene practices, which of the following represents the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Prescribing preventive oral antibiotic therapy
B) Performing curettage with bone graft placement
C) Extracting the affected tooth
D) Conducting segmental bone resection
E) Monitoring without intervention
questions.answer:
E)
Monitoring without intervention is the most suitable approach. This clinical scenario represents Stage I bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ), where patients typically remain asymptomatic except for bone exposure and/or necrosis. A is incorrect because prophylactic antibiotics are not indicated unless infection develops (Stage II or III BRONJ). B is incorrect because curettage and bone grafting are not appropriate interventions for Stage I BRONJ. C is incorrect because tooth extraction carries significant risk and may worsen the condition; when severe dental pathology exists, endodontic treatment with crown amputation is preferred. D is incorrect because segmental resection is reserved for Stage III BRONJ, which involves more severe complications like pathologic fractures or extraoral fistulas.

questions.question:
A 51-year-old female patient presents to your clinic with unilateral breast enlargement occurring 1 year following subglandular silicone breast augmentation. The patient denies recent injury, fever, or muscle aches. Clinical examination demonstrates fluid accumulation around the prosthesis without signs of redness or swelling. Which of the following represents the most suitable initial management approach?
A) Performing needle drainage with Gram stain and bacterial culture
B) Prescribing oral antibiotics with complete blood cell analysis
C) Recommending activity restriction and supportive brassiere use
D) Conducting ultrasound-guided aspiration with cytological examination
questions.answer:
D)
Ultrasound-guided aspiration with cytological examination is most appropriate because the primary concern is ruling out anaplastic large T-cell lymphoma (ALCL), a rare lymphoma associated with breast implants that requires cytological diagnosis with CD30 expression and cytokeratin negativity testing. A is incorrect because needle aspiration risks implant damage and doesn't provide the necessary cytological analysis for ALCL detection. B is incorrect because antibiotics and blood work are not warranted when infection is unlikely based on history and examination findings. C is incorrect because activity restriction and supportive measures are appropriate for early postoperative edema but not for late-onset fluid collections that require ALCL evaluation.

questions.question:
An otherwise healthy 3-month-old female infant is admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit because of progressive difficulty breathing for the past 3 weeks. Examination shows mild stridor. Cultures are negative for acute viral or pulmonary illness. A photograph is shown. Administration of which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?


A) Imiquimod
B) Interferon alfa-2a
C) Propranolol
D) Vincristine
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


In the absence of other pulmonary disease, the stridor is most likely being caused by the hemangioma which is present in the beard distribution. Hemangiomas can be present in the airway as well as the surrounding soft tissue.


In some centers, propranolol has supplanted corticosteroids as the first-line medical therapy for complicated hemangiomas. Currently, there is no universally accepted protocol for propranolol administration. Propranolol is initially given intravenously and then converted to oral dosing. Blood pressure and heart rate monitoring must be done on an outpatient basis, generally by a pediatric cardiologist. Treatment is typically 2 to 6 months.


Systemic corticosteroids are still considered effective therapy. Corticosteroids generally require prolonged therapy to prevent rebound effect. It can take upwards of 2 years for treated patients to catch up in growth after prolonged corticosteroid therapy in infancy. Treatment is typically upwards of 9 to 12 months.


Vincristine is a first-line treatment for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma. It has supplanted interferon alfa-2a, which is avoided due to the risk of spastic diplegia.


Topical imiquimod is still considered an experimental therapy.


References
1. Hogeling M, Adams S, Wargon O. A randomized controlled trial of propranolol for infantile hemangiomas. Pediatrics. 2011 Aug;128(2):e259-266. Epub 2011 Jul 25.
2. Schiestl C, Neuhaus K, Zoller S, et al. Efficacy and safety of propranolol as first-line treatment for infantile hemangiomas. Eur J Pediatr. 2011 Apr;170(4):493-501. Epub 2010 Oct 9.
3. Arneja JS, Pappas PN, Shwayder TA, et al. Management of complicated facial hemangiomas with beta-blocker (propranolol) therapy. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Sep;126(3):889-895.

questions.question:
A 19-year-old man sustains a partial amputation fight-bite injury to the ear. The wound has been revised and a photograph of the residual defect is shown. The patient wants the ear to have a normal appearance. Which of the following is the best option to restore normal aesthetics to the ear?


A) Addition of a silicone framework
B) Composite cartilage grafting
C) Reconstruction with a temporoparietal fascia flap with skin grafting
D) Serial fat injections
E) Staged autologous reconstruction with costal cartilage
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


This patient has sustained a three-dimensional and sizable defect of the ear. He is missing a portion of the helical rim, the scaphoid fossa to the antihelix. This is a difficult reconstructive challenge. The anatomic components that are missing are skin and underlying cartilage. The best option for obtaining a normal-appearing ear would be reconstruction with a cartilage framework carved to replace the cartilage and to support the overlying skin to retain the form of the ear. This could be done as a stage procedure.


Fat injection would not be adequate to replace the missing components or to give adequate shape to the ear.


A silicone framework within a scarred bed would be prone to complication, most notably infection and/or extrusion. The defect is too large to be replaced by a composite cartilage graft.


Although a temporoparietal fascia flap could potentially be used to cover a cartilage framework, used alone it would not give adequate form to reconstruct this defect.


References
Gault D. Post traumatic ear reconstruction. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2008;61 Suppl 1:S5-12.
Firmin F, Bulstrode NW. Ear reconstruction. In: Bulstrode NW, Cugno S, Farhadieh RD. Plastic and reconstructive surgery: Approaches and techniques. Wiley-Blackwell, Chichester, UK: 2015.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old mobile male patient presents to your office with a Stage IV pressure ulcer located over the left ischial tuberosity. He has no prior history of pressure ulcers, maintains proper nutrition, and is a non-smoker. He demonstrates strong motivation to prevent future occurrences. The most suitable treatment approach involves debridement followed by reconstruction using which of the following options?
A) Gluteal fasciocutaneous flap
B) Gracilis muscle flap
C) Posterior thigh musculocutaneous flap
D) Split-thickness skin graft
E) Tensor fascia lata flap
questions.answer:
A)
The gluteal fasciocutaneous flap is most appropriate because it preserves muscle function in this ambulatory patient while providing adequate blood supply and durable coverage that closely restores normal anatomy over bony prominences. B is incorrect because the gracilis muscle flap would sacrifice muscle function unnecessarily in an ambulatory patient. C is incorrect because the posterior thigh musculocutaneous flap would also sacrifice muscle function when a fasciocutaneous option is available. D is incorrect because skin grafting has only a 30% success rate in this scenario and provides unstable coverage over pressure points. E is incorrect because the tensor fascia lata flap is primarily indicated for trochanteric pressure sores and typically provides insufficient padding for ischial coverage.

questions.question:
A 9-year-old female patient with unilateral cleft lip and palate receives alveolar bone grafting using cancellous iliac bone graft material. Which of the following represents the most probable healing mechanism for the bone graft in this patient?
A) Endochondral ossification
B) Osteoconduction
C) Osteogenesis
D) Osteoinduction
E) Progenitor cell recruitment
questions.answer:
C)
Osteogenesis is the most probable healing mechanism for cancellous bone grafts because they undergo rapid revascularization, allowing transplanted osteoblasts to survive and directly produce new bone at the recipient site. A is incorrect because endochondral ossification is an embryologic process for appendicular skeleton development, while the maxilla develops through membranous ossification. B is incorrect because osteoconduction (creeping substitution) is the primary mechanism for cortical bone graft healing, not cancellous grafts. D is incorrect because osteoinduction involves stimulating mesenchymal cells to differentiate into bone-producing cells, which is characteristic of demineralized bone matrix and bone morphogenic proteins. E is incorrect because while progenitor cells may be recruited to the grafting site, this is not the primary healing mechanism for cancellous bone grafts.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male patient is being assessed for Le Fort I maxillary advancement and lengthening surgery. His medical background includes repair of bilateral cleft lip and palate during infancy. Following the surgical procedure, which of the following facial modifications is most probable in this patient?
A) Reduced nasolabial angle
B) Reduced tooth visibility at rest
C) Widened alar base
D) Deeper nasolabial folds
E) Lengthened upper lip
questions.answer:
C)
Widened alar base is the most probable outcome because Le Fort I advancement moves the bony platform of the lower piriform region forward, causing the nasal base to widen and the tip to rotate upward. A is incorrect because the nasolabial angle typically increases rather than decreases due to tip rotation. B is incorrect because tooth show in repose and smile typically increases rather than decreases following maxillary advancement. D is incorrect because nasolabial folds typically become shallower rather than deeper due to increased midfacial projection. E is incorrect because upper lip height typically decreases rather than increases following this procedure.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old female patient is scheduled for office-based breast augmentation surgery under general anesthesia. Her medical history is significant for previous episodes of postoperative nausea and vomiting, as well as motion sickness. Along with ondansetron 4 mg given intravenously, which of the following medications administered before anesthesia induction would most likely provide optimal antiemetic prophylaxis for this patient?
A) Aprepitant 40 mg orally
B) Diphenhydramine 25 mg intravenously
C) Droperidol 1.25 mg intravenously
D) Metoclopramide 25 mg intravenously
E) Promethazine 25 mg orally
questions.answer:
A)
Aprepitant 40 mg is the most effective choice for preoperative antiemetic prophylaxis in this high-risk patient. As a neurokinin-1 receptor antagonist with a long half-life, aprepitant works by blocking substance P binding at neurokinin-1 receptors in the brainstem vomiting center and GI tract. Its extended duration of action and specific mechanism make it ideal for prophylactic use when given 1-3 hours before anesthesia induction in patients at high risk for postoperative nausea and vomiting. B is incorrect because diphenhydramine has a short duration and is less effective for prophylaxis in high-risk patients. C is incorrect because droperidol, while effective, has a shorter duration and is typically used postoperatively rather than for preoperative prophylaxis. D is incorrect because metoclopramide has a brief duration of action and is more commonly used for postoperative treatment. E is incorrect because promethazine also has a short duration and is better suited for postoperative rather than prophylactic use.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female patient who had a right mastectomy 6 months prior presents for consultation regarding delayed autologous breast reconstruction using free tissue transfer. If she is currently taking any of the following medications on a regular basis, which one should be stopped before the surgical procedure?
A) Diltiazem
B) Fluoxetine
C) Metoprolol
D) Multivitamin
E) Tamoxifen
questions.answer:
E)
Tamoxifen should be discontinued preoperatively because it significantly increases the risk of thromboembolic complications. Research from MD Anderson Cancer Center demonstrated that patients taking tamoxifen close to their surgical procedure experienced substantially higher complication rates. Current recommendations advise stopping tamoxifen at least 28 days prior to surgery to minimize thrombotic risk. A is incorrect because diltiazem, a calcium channel blocker, does not significantly affect thrombotic complications in microsurgical procedures. B is incorrect because fluoxetine, an SSRI antidepressant, does not have direct effects on thrombotic risk relevant to free tissue transfer. C is incorrect because metoprolol, a beta-blocker, does not increase thrombotic complications in reconstructive surgery. D is incorrect because multivitamins do not pose thrombotic risks and generally do not require discontinuation before surgery.

questions.question:
Which type of craniosynostosis responds most reliably to endoscopic suture release combined with postoperative helmet therapy?
A) Coronal
B) Lambdoidal
C) Metopic
D) Sagittal
E) Squamosal
questions.answer:
D)
Sagittal craniosynostosis is most successfully treated with endoscopic suturectomy and postoperative orthotic molding. This minimally invasive approach involves removing the fused suture and additional bone, creating microfractures in the parietal bones, and using postoperative helmet therapy to achieve normal head shape and cephalic index. The procedure must be performed early, ideally between 2-4 months of age, and does not require internal fixation. A is incorrect because coronal synostosis typically requires open surgical correction for optimal results, as endoscopic treatment has shown variable and less predictable outcomes. B is incorrect because lambdoidal synostosis is most effectively managed with traditional open surgical approaches rather than endoscopic techniques. C is incorrect because metopic synostosis generally requires open surgical correction for reliable results. E is incorrect because squamosal synostosis usually does not require any surgical intervention at all.

questions.question:
A 4-month-old child presents for assessment of a unilateral hand anomaly featuring seven digits with a central index finger surrounded by long, ring, and little fingers on both sides, and absence of the thumb. Abnormal activity of which developmental signaling molecule most likely caused this congenital malformation?
A) Bone morphogenetic protein
B) Fibroblast growth factor
C) Sonic hedgehog protein
D) Wingless protein
questions.answer:
C)
Sonic hedgehog protein (SHH) abnormal expression is responsible for this mirror hand deformity. SHH is normally produced in the zone of polarizing activity (ZPA) on the ulnar side of the developing limb bud and controls anteroposterior (radioulnar) axis development. Ectopic SHH expression, such as duplication of the ZPA on the radial side, causes duplication of ulnar-sided structures, resulting in the mirror hand pattern described. Normal SHH signaling creates ulnar structures directly and radial structures through diffusion gradients, while its absence allows thumb development. A is incorrect because bone morphogenetic proteins primarily control digital separation and are involved in preventing syndactyly, not anteroposterior axis patterning. B is incorrect because fibroblast growth factors control proximodistal limb development through the apical ectodermal ridge, not the radioulnar axis. D is incorrect because wingless proteins primarily regulate dorsoventral axis development and maintain SHH expression, but are not the primary controllers of anteroposterior limb patterning.

questions.question:
A 59-year-old female patient presents with a 7-month history of radial-sided wrist pain that worsens with strong gripping activities. She reports no history of wrist trauma. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the anatomic snuffbox and thenar eminence on the right side. Basal joint loading and manipulation do not produce grinding sensations or pain. Resisted thumb extension at the metacarpophalangeal joint is painless. Based on the radiographic findings shown, what is the most appropriate surgical treatment?
A) Arthrodesis of the scaphotrapeziotrapezoid joint
B) Arthrodesis of the trapeziometacarpal joint
C) Hemi-resection of the distal trapezium and tendon interposition
D) Release of the first dorsal compartment
E) Release of the second dorsal compartment
questions.answer:
A)
Scaphotrapeziotrapezoid (STT) joint arthrodesis is the most appropriate treatment for this patient's STT arthritis. The clinical presentation of tenderness proximal to the basal joint, absence of pain with grinding maneuvers, and radiographic evidence of STT joint degeneration while sparing the trapeziometacarpal joint confirms this diagnosis. STT arthrodesis effectively addresses both the scapho-trapezial and scapho-trapezoid articulations and provides reliable symptom relief. B is incorrect because the trapeziometacarpal joint appears preserved on imaging and the clinical examination does not support basal joint arthritis. C is incorrect because hemi-resection with tendon interposition is designed for basal joint arthritis, which is not present in this case. D is incorrect because first dorsal compartment release treats de Quervain's tenosynovitis, but this patient lacks the characteristic pain with resisted thumb extension that would indicate this condition. E is incorrect because second dorsal compartment release addresses intersection syndrome, which typically causes more proximal forearm pain rather than the STT region tenderness seen in this patient.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old healthy woman presents to the clinic seeking advice about laser treatment for fine wrinkles around her mouth. She has light brown skin and mentions she seldom experiences sunburn (Fitzpatrick Type IV). Physical examination reveals wrinkles around the mouth, forehead, and outer corners of the eyes. In comparison to a patient with fairer skin (Fitzpatrick Type I-III), what complication is this patient more likely to experience following perioral laser resurfacing?
A) Freckles
B) Herpetic lesions
C) Hypertrophic scars
D) Post-treatment hyperemia
E) Postinflammatory hyperpigmentation
questions.answer:
E)
Postinflammatory hyperpigmentation is the primary concern for patients with darker skin types (Fitzpatrick Type IV) following laser resurfacing procedures. The Fitzpatrick Scale helps assess skin tone and predict complications, particularly pigmentation changes after treatment. Patients with darker skin are at significantly higher risk for developing postinflammatory hyperpigmentation due to increased melanocyte activity following tissue injury. A) is incorrect because laser therapy is actually used to treat freckles rather than cause them. B) is incorrect because herpetic lesions can occur in patients of any skin type following laser treatment. C) is incorrect because laser therapy is used to treat hypertrophic scars, not cause them. D) is incorrect because while hyperemia can occur in any patient after laser resurfacing, it is not specifically increased in darker skin types.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old man with eyeglasses experienced severe trauma to the left facial region, resulting in globe rupture and complete loss of both upper and lower eyelids. What is the optimal aesthetic recommendation for this patient?
A) Eye patch
B) Hemifacial prosthesis
C) Ocular prosthesis
D) Orbital prosthesis
questions.answer:
D)
An orbital prosthesis is the most appropriate choice for this patient who has lost both the globe and eyelids due to severe trauma. Reconstructing functional eyelids is extremely difficult, and eyelids are necessary to support an ocular prosthesis. An orbital prosthesis can provide both comfort and acceptable aesthetics, with the patient's glasses helping to camouflage the prosthetic margins. A) is incorrect because an eye patch would not provide reconstruction or improve facial symmetry. B) is incorrect because a hemifacial prosthesis is unnecessarily extensive for this localized defect and would create unnatural seam lines. C) is incorrect because an ocular prosthesis requires intact eyelids for support, which this patient lacks.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old wheelchair-dependent woman presents with a stage IV pressure ulcer over the ischium. Her medical history includes systemic lupus erythematosus and multiple sclerosis. Current medications are prednisone and gabapentin. Her BMI is 21 kg/m² and has remained constant over the past year. Laboratory values show WBC 10.5 × 10⁹/L, hematocrit 30%, and serum albumin 3.6 mg/dL. Following debridement of necrotic tissue and initiation of wound care, which supplement would most effectively enhance wound healing?
A) Echinacea
B) Ferrous gluconate
C) Glutamine
D) Lipid emulsion
E) Vitamin A
questions.answer:
E)
Vitamin A supplementation is most beneficial for this patient because it enhances epithelialization and collagen synthesis, and is specifically recommended for patients on chronic corticosteroid therapy like prednisone. A daily dose of 20,000 IU can help counteract the wound healing suppression caused by corticosteroids. A) is incorrect because echinacea can have immunosuppressive effects despite being marketed as an immunostimulant. B) is incorrect because while the patient has mild anemia, iron deficiency is not the primary impediment to wound healing in this case. C) is incorrect because the patient has adequate protein status as evidenced by normal albumin levels and stable BMI. D) is incorrect because lipid emulsion is indicated for severely malnourished patients, but this patient has a stable normal BMI.

questions.question:
A 14-year-old girl presents with a 1-month history of a painful, enlarging hard palate lesion that causes "electric-shock sensations" when touched. Incisional biopsy reveals adenoid cystic carcinoma of minor salivary glands. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Chemotherapy
B) CT scan and MRI
C) Excision with 1-cm margins
D) Excision with 2-cm margins
E) Radiation therapy
questions.answer:
B)
CT scan and MRI are essential initial steps because the patient's symptoms of paresthesias suggest perineural invasion, a characteristic feature of adenoid cystic carcinoma. MRI is particularly valuable for detecting perineural spread and planning the extent of surgical intervention. Minor salivary gland tumors in pediatric patients have a high malignancy rate (approximately 50%), and palatal location increases the likelihood of advanced disease. Imaging will guide appropriate surgical planning. A) is incorrect because chemotherapy is not a primary treatment for adenoid cystic carcinoma. C) and D) are incorrect because surgical planning requires imaging first to determine the extent of disease and perineural involvement. E) is incorrect because radiation therapy alone is not standard treatment, though it may be used as adjuvant therapy after surgery.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old woman seeks evaluation for excessive perspiration and body odor. She describes a longstanding history of profuse sweating, particularly in the underarm and groin regions. Which type of gland is responsible for her malodorous excessive sweating?
A) Apocrine
B) Eccrine
C) Holocrine
D) Merocrine
E) Sebaceous
questions.answer:
A)
Apocrine glands are responsible for malodorous sweating, particularly in hair-bearing areas like the axilla and groin. These glands secrete protein-rich fluid that, when combined with bacterial breakdown (especially Corynebacterium), produces the characteristic body odor. This condition is called osmidrosis or bromhidrosis. B) is incorrect because eccrine glands produce primarily water and salt throughout the body and are associated with hyperhidrosis but not malodor. C) is incorrect because holocrine glands (like sebaceous glands) secrete via cell destruction and are not primarily involved in sweating. D) is incorrect because merocrine is a type of secretion method (which includes eccrine glands) but doesn't specifically cause malodorous sweating. E) is incorrect because sebaceous glands produce oil, not sweat, and are not the primary source of body odor from excessive sweating.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old white male presents to the clinic with a painful growing lesion at the tongue base. He is a non-smoker. The mass measures 4.5 cm in diameter. Tissue biopsy reveals p16-positive, non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. Additional imaging and evaluation show a single ipsilateral lymph node measuring 2.3 cm. No distant metastases are detected. What stage best characterizes this patient's disease?
A) Stage 1
B) Stage 2
C) Stage 3
D) Stage 4
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is Stage 2. Under the revised AJCC staging system for p16-positive squamous cell carcinomas, this patient's disease is classified as Stage 2, whereas it would have previously been Stage 3. The AJCC updated its staging criteria for p16-positive squamous cell cancers because these HPV-related tumors demonstrate less aggressive behavior than their HPV-negative counterparts. Research showed that 5-year survival rates for Stage 4 disease differ significantly between HPV-negative patients (<50%) and HPV-positive patients (>70%), leading to the staging revision that took effect January 1, 2017. HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancers typically respond better to radiation and chemoradiation therapy and carry an improved overall prognosis. These tumors commonly affect younger, male, Caucasian patients and now constitute the majority of newly diagnosed oropharyngeal cancers in the United States. A is incorrect because the tumor size and nodal involvement exceed Stage 1 criteria. C is incorrect because the revised staging system for p16-positive tumors downgrades this presentation from the previous Stage 3 classification. D is incorrect because there is no evidence of distant metastatic disease or multiple nodal involvement that would warrant Stage 4 classification.

questions.question:
What complication is more frequently associated with internal ultrasound-assisted liposuction compared to conventional suction-assisted lipectomy?
A) Contour irregularities
B) Infection
C) Seroma
D) Skin laxity
E) Surgeon fatigue
questions.answer:
C)
The correct answer is seroma formation. Internal ultrasound-assisted lipoplasty (UAL) carries a higher risk of seroma development compared to traditional suction-assisted lipectomy. UAL also increases the likelihood of tissue damage, thermal injury, and nerve dysfunction. The technique uses ultrasonic energy delivered through a cannula or solid probe to disrupt fat cells, creating 'liquefied' fat that is then removed by suction. To prevent thermal skin injury, adequate solution infiltration and continuous probe movement are essential. A is incorrect because contour irregularities depend more on surgical technique and operator skill rather than the specific method used. B is incorrect because infection rates are comparable between UAL and traditional suction-assisted lipectomy. D is incorrect because some studies suggest UAL may actually reduce skin laxity compared to conventional techniques. E is incorrect because UAL may actually decrease surgeon fatigue in some cases compared to traditional methods.

questions.question:
A 6-month-old male infant has bilateral radial longitudinal deficiency with hypoplastic thumbs noted on examination and confirmed by plain films. Which of the following tests is most appropriate to exclude Fanconi anemia in this patient?
A) Bone marrow biopsy
B) Chromosomal breakage testing
C) Complete blood count with differential
D) Peripheral blood smear
E) Renal ultrasonography
questions.answer:
B) Chromosomal breakage testing

Chromosomal breakage testing (diepoxybutane or mitomycin C-induced breakage assay on peripheral lymphocytes) is the definitive screening study for Fanconi anemia and should be obtained in every child with radial longitudinal deficiency (RLD), regardless of age or hematologic status. Children with Fanconi anemia usually do not manifest marrow failure until a median age of approximately 7 years, so an infant with normal blood counts is not excluded. Early diagnosis is critical because it permits hematologic surveillance, family/donor screening, and timely hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and it alters chemotherapy/radiation risk profiles.

All children with RLD warrant a broader syndromic evaluation, including cardiac echocardiography (Holt-Oram syndrome), renal ultrasonography and spine imaging (VACTERL association), and platelet count (thrombocytopenia-absent radius syndrome, in which the thumbs are characteristically present).

A is incorrect: bone marrow biopsy is invasive and will typically be normal in an infant with Fanconi anemia; it is used to evaluate established cytopenias or suspected myelodysplasia, not for initial exclusion of the diagnosis.
C is incorrect: the complete blood count with differential is usually normal in young children with Fanconi anemia and therefore cannot exclude the disease.
D is incorrect: the peripheral smear does not detect the DNA cross-link repair defect that defines Fanconi anemia.
E is incorrect: renal ultrasonography screens for the genitourinary anomalies of VACTERL association (and may show renal anomalies in Fanconi anemia) but is not diagnostic for Fanconi anemia.

questions.question:
A 9-month-old girl with severe metopic craniosynostosis needs bifrontal craniotomy with fronto-orbital advancement. The anesthesiologist is worried about operative blood loss and transfusion requirements. Which intravenous medication given during cranial reconstruction would most effectively decrease both operative and postoperative bleeding?
A) Aprotinin
B) Erythropoietin
C) Fibrinogen
D) Protamine
E) Tranexamic acid
questions.answer:
E)
The correct answer is tranexamic acid (TXA). TXA is a synthetic lysine analog that prevents the conversion of plasminogen to plasmin when given intravenously. By inhibiting plasmin's proteolytic activity, TXA blocks fibrinolysis and has been proven in numerous studies to reduce both intraoperative and postoperative blood loss in craniosynostosis surgery. A is incorrect because aprotinin was removed from the US market in 2007 due to increased complications and mortality, though it has been reapproved in some other countries. B is incorrect because erythropoietin stimulates red blood cell production when given preoperatively but does not reduce acute blood loss during surgery. C is incorrect because fibrinogen is not administered intravenously in this context; fibrin glue may be used topically but not systemically. D is incorrect because protamine is used to reverse heparin effects and has no role in this clinical situation.

questions.question:
Prompt reimplantation of an avulsed tooth is essential for maximizing its long-term survival because it prevents additional injury to which structure?
A) Cementum
B) Dentin
C) Enamel
D) Periodontal ligament
E) Pulp
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is the periodontal ligament. When a permanent tooth is completely avulsed, the exposed periodontal ligament can undergo desiccation and cellular death within one hour of injury. Teeth with dry times exceeding 60 minutes have poor long-term prognosis. If immediate replantation is not possible, the tooth should be preserved in an appropriate medium such as milk, saliva, or Hanks balanced storage solution. A is incorrect because cementum forms part of the tooth's hard outer surface at the root and is relatively resistant to avulsion damage. B is incorrect because dentin, the thick layer beneath the enamel/cementum that comprises most of the tooth structure, is typically not damaged in clean avulsions. C is incorrect because enamel, the hard outer covering of the crown, is generally resistant to avulsion injury. E is incorrect because while the pulp will become non-viable after complete avulsion and require root canal treatment, the tooth can survive after pulp removal with appropriate management.

questions.question:
A healthy 35-year-old male presents with a 15-year history of bilateral Grade III gynecomastia. He measures 5 ft 10 in (178 cm) tall and weighs 187 lb (85 kg) with a BMI of 27 kg/m2. Examination reveals breast enlargement with excess skin and palpable glandular and fatty tissue. Ultrasound-assisted liposuction is planned as the patient wants to avoid visible scarring. Which of the following techniques is most likely to reduce the need for skin excision?
A) Disruption of the inframammary fold
B) High energy setting
C) Peripheral feathering with standard liposuction
D) Treatment of the intermediate fat layer
E) Tumescent infiltration with a 3:1 ratio
questions.answer:
A)
Disrupting the inframammary fold is crucial because it allows the skin to drape more naturally onto the abdomen, creating the typical male breast contour and improving skin retraction to minimize the need for subsequent skin removal procedures. B) is incorrect because high energy settings should be avoided as they increase the risk of burns and dermal injuries. C) is incorrect because peripheral feathering improves contour transitions but does not specifically address skin excess. D) is incorrect because treating the intermediate fat layer alone does not optimize skin retraction. E) is incorrect because while tumescent infiltration is important for preventing burns, the ratio does not specifically influence skin retraction.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female is dissatisfied with her "boxy facial appearance," particularly the lower jaw "near the angles," and desires permanent smoothing of her mandibular contour. Which of the following represents the most suitable treatment option?
A) Alloplastic implant
B) Autologous fat grafting
C) Hyaluronic acid dermal filler
D) Mandible angle and body contouring
E) Suction lipectomy
questions.answer:
D)
Mandible angle and body contouring is the appropriate surgical procedure to reduce the angular contours of a "square face" by gracefully contouring or resecting both the mandible angle and body to achieve an aesthetically pleasing, rounder facial appearance. A) is incorrect because alloplastic implants would add volume rather than reduce the square appearance. B) is incorrect because fat grafting would increase facial fullness rather than reduce angular contours. C) is incorrect because hyaluronic acid fillers are temporary and would not address the underlying bony structure. E) is incorrect because liposuction would not be effective for addressing the bony prominence of a square jaw.

questions.question:
A 3-year-old male child suffers a crush injury to his right index fingertip from a door. Examination reveals a stellate nail bed laceration with intact eponychial fold and proximal nail bed. What is the most accurate information to provide the parents regarding fingertip trauma and nail regrowth expectations?
A) Nail growth will average about 0.1 mm a week
B) Nail regrowth will take approximately 3 months
C) Scarring of the sterile matrix will lead to absence of nail growth
D) The sterile matrix produces about 90% of nail growth
questions.answer:
B)
Nail regrowth takes approximately 3 months (about 100 days) for normal appearance to return after injury, as nails grow at approximately 0.1 mm per day. A) is incorrect because nail growth averages 0.1 mm per day, not per week. C) is incorrect because scarring of the sterile matrix leads to nail deformity, while scarring of the germinal matrix leads to absence of nail growth. D) is incorrect because the germinal matrix, not the sterile matrix, produces about 90% of nail growth.

questions.question:
In Grade II breast ptosis, which of the following most accurately describes the nipple location?
A) At the apex of the breast mound
B) At the lowest contour of the breast
C) At the transposed inframammary fold
D) Between the inframammary fold and the lowest contour of the breast
E) On the posterior aspect of the breast as it rests on the chest wall
questions.answer:
D)
In Grade II ptosis, the nipple is positioned between the inframammary fold level and the lowest contour of the breast according to the Regnault classification system. A) is incorrect because this describes normal breast position without ptosis. B) is incorrect because this describes Grade III ptosis where the nipple is at the lowest breast contour. C) is incorrect because this describes Grade I ptosis where the nipple is at the inframammary fold level. E) is incorrect because this does not correspond to any standard ptosis classification.

questions.question:
Negative pressure wound therapy using sponge dressing is CONTRAINDICATED in which of the following situations?
A) An abdominal wound with an enteric fistula
B) A dorsal hand wound with an exposed tendon
C) A lower extremity wound with acute osteomyelitis
D) Over a closed surgical incision
E) A radiated scalp wound with exposed bone
questions.answer:
C)
Negative pressure therapy is contraindicated in wounds with active infection, including acute osteomyelitis, because it converts an open, draining wound into a closed system, potentially leading to abscess formation and sepsis. A) is incorrect because enteric fistulas are not an absolute contraindication for negative pressure therapy. B) is incorrect because exposed tendons can benefit from negative pressure therapy as a temporary measure. D) is incorrect because recent studies show negative pressure therapy over closed incisions may reduce dehiscence and infection risks. E) is incorrect because exposed bone in radiated tissue can be managed with negative pressure therapy as a temporary measure before definitive treatment.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male patient receives radial forearm free flap reconstruction following complete laryngectomy and partial pharyngectomy for T4 N3 M0 squamous cell carcinoma of the laryngopharynx. After surgery, the patient experiences numbness and tingling around the mouth. What electrolyte imbalance is most probable in this case?
A) Elevated calcium levels
B) Elevated potassium levels
C) Elevated sodium levels
D) Decreased calcium levels
E) Decreased sodium levels
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is decreased calcium levels because laryngopharyngectomy procedures frequently involve thyroid gland removal, which can inadvertently damage or remove parathyroid glands or compromise their blood supply. Since parathyroid glands control calcium regulation, their dysfunction initially presents as perioral tingling and numbness before progressing to more serious symptoms like tetany. A) Elevated calcium levels is wrong because symptomatic hypercalcemia typically causes gastrointestinal symptoms like vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and muscle pain. B) Elevated potassium levels is incorrect as it primarily affects cardiac rhythm on EKG and is unrelated to parathyroid gland function. C) Elevated sodium levels is wrong because when symptomatic, it produces nausea, vomiting, and confusion. E) Decreased sodium levels is incorrect because symptomatic hyponatremia causes nausea, vomiting, lethargy, and confusion.

questions.question:
What genetic alteration is most commonly associated with a patient presenting with facial clefting and webbing behind the knee?
A) Enhanced function mutation in FGFR2
B) Enhanced function mutation in NF1
C) Enhanced function mutation in PIK3CA
D) Reduced function mutation in IRF6
E) Reduced function mutation in TCOF1
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is reduced function mutation in IRF6 because loss-of-function IRF6 mutations are documented in both Van der Woude syndrome (which can include popliteal pterygium) and isolated orofacial clefting. A) Enhanced function mutation in FGFR2 is incorrect as these are linked to syndromic craniosynostosis conditions like Apert and Crouzon syndromes. B) Enhanced function mutation in NF1 is wrong because NF1 mutations lead to elevated RAS/MAPK signaling and neurofibromatosis type 1. C) Enhanced function mutation in PIK3CA is incorrect as these are associated with venous and lymphatic malformations. E) Reduced function mutation in TCOF1 is wrong because TCOF1 mutations cause Treacher Collins syndrome, where patients may have cleft palate but lack lip pits.

questions.question:
An otherwise healthy 10-year-old girl is brought for evaluation because of a chronic ulcer of the right leg. The ulcer first appeared 6 months ago when she scraped her leg on a boat dock at her family‚Äos lake house. The wound has increased in size despite treatment with a course of oral antibiotic therapy prescribed by her primary care physician. A photograph is shown. On evaluation today, the patient is afebrile and has no systemic signs of infection. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of these findings?


A) Candida tropicalis
B) Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus
C) Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
D) Mycobacterium marinum
E) Vibrio vulnificus
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


The history and presentation are classic for an atypical mycobacterial infection. Unlike bacterial infections, atypical mycobacteria rarely produce systemic signs of infection and often manifest as a nonhealing (sometimes progressive) wound. Given the history of injury on a boat dock, the most likely causative organism is Mycobacterium marinum, an acid-fast bacillus that lives in water environments. This pathogen results in localized granulomas such as the one seen in this patient. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common source of skin infections but typically results in a more pronounced and acute immune reaction with localized redness and purulence. These findings are not present in this patient. Cutaneous infections with Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus and Vibrio vulnificus tend to increase rapidly and are often accompanied by severe systemic response (i.e., necrotizing fasciitis). Candida tropicalis is a fungus that is often part of normal skin flora. It is related to Candida albicans and can produce opportunistic internal infections in susceptible individuals.


References
1. Gunther SF, Levy CS. Mycobacterial infections. Hand Clin. 1989 Nov;5(4):591-598.
2. Bhatty MA, Turner DP, Chamberlain ST. Mycobacterium marinum hand infection: case reports and review of literature. Br J Plast Surg. 2000 Mar;53(2):161-165.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with asymmetric breast development, showing underdevelopment of the right breast. Examination reveals right breast hypoplasia, missing sternal portion of the pectoralis major muscle, and a congenital hand anomaly on the right side. What classification best characterizes this patient's hand abnormality?
A) Amniotic band syndrome
B) Polydactyly
C) Differentiation failure
D) Formation failure
E) Macrodactyly
questions.answer:
C)
The correct answer is differentiation failure because the patient has Poland sequence (indicated by absent sternal pectoralis major head), which is associated with symbrachydactyly of the same-side hand. Symbrachydactyly represents inadequate separation of parts and falls under Type II (failure of differentiation) in the ASSH/IFSSH classification system. A) Amniotic band syndrome is incorrect as it involves constriction rings that may cause amputation at various levels (Type VI). B) Polydactyly is wrong because it represents duplication abnormalities (Type III), not differentiation problems. D) Formation failure is incorrect as it involves lack of formation such as longitudinal or transverse arrest (Type I). E) Macrodactyly is wrong because it represents overgrowth disorders (Type IV).

questions.question:
A 3-year-old patient with funnel chest deformity is being assessed for surgical repair of the chest wall abnormality. The patient has experienced some breathing difficulties. What is the best timing for surgical intervention in this case?
A) Operative repair between ages 2 and 5
B) Operative repair between ages 6 and 12
C) Operative repair between ages 13 and 17
D) Operative repair after growth completion
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is operative repair between ages 6 and 12 because this represents the ideal timing for pectus excavatum correction, typically during mid-adolescence when the chest wall has adequate development but remains malleable for remodeling. Modern minimally invasive techniques like the Nuss procedure and MIRPE utilize thoracoscopy and retrosternal bars to gradually remodel the chest over 2-4 years, working best during this age range. A) Operative repair between ages 2 and 5 is incorrect as the chest wall is too immature and flexible at this early age. C) Operative repair between ages 13 and 17 is wrong because the chest wall becomes increasingly rigid during late adolescence, making correction more difficult. D) Operative repair after growth completion is incorrect as the chest wall becomes too rigid for optimal results with minimally invasive techniques.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient seeks consultation for face lift surgery. Physical examination reveals more than 2 inches of redundant neck skin when pinched on both sides. The illustration displays incision options (A to D) that all start at the temporal pre-hairline area, continue to the tragal margin, then curve around the earlobe to the post-auricular groove. Which incision design would best address this patient's neck excess?
A) Superior horizontal extension into the posterior scalp
B) Posterior scalp pre-hairline with a lower extension into hair-bearing scalp
C) Inferior horizontal placement in the non-hair-bearing neck area
D) Termination at the lower post-auricular groove
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is posterior scalp pre-hairline with a lower extension into hair-bearing scalp because this design allows removal of significant neck skin excess while maintaining natural hairline appearance and hiding scars. The pre-hairline component prevents pulling non-hair-bearing skin into the scalp, while the final scalp extension provides better scar camouflage. A) Superior horizontal extension into the posterior scalp is incorrect for severe neck laxity as it would pull non-hair-bearing neck skin into the scalp area, creating unnatural hairline distortion. C) Inferior horizontal placement in the non-hair-bearing neck area is wrong because while it removes excess skin effectively, it creates a highly visible scar. D) Termination at the lower post-auricular groove is incorrect as this short-scar technique only addresses minor neck laxity and risks skin bunching at the earlobe with potential draping deformities.

questions.question:
What is the optimal surgical approach for repairing this patient's abdominal wall hernia?
A) Mobilization of vertical rectus abdominis muscle-skin flaps
B) Division and mobilization of external oblique muscle layers
C) Division and mobilization of rectus, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis muscle layers
D) Transfer of anterolateral thigh tissue flaps
E) Transfer of transverse rectus abdominis muscle-skin flaps
questions.answer:
C)
The optimal approach is division and mobilization of rectus, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis muscle layers through component separation technique. This method enables tension-free primary repair of large central abdominal wall defects by releasing the external oblique aponeurosis lateral to the linea semilunaris and advancing the rectus muscle medially with the internal oblique and transversus muscles while preserving their neurovascular supply for maintained function. A is incorrect because vertical rectus flaps are used for soft tissue reconstruction rather than functional wall repair. B is incorrect because releasing only the external oblique provides insufficient mobilization for large defects. D is incorrect because anterolateral thigh flaps are for soft tissue coverage, not functional wall reconstruction. E is incorrect because transverse rectus flaps are primarily reconstructive rather than providing functional abdominal wall repair.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old woman presents with foot drop following right leg vein stripping and lesser saphenous vein ligation performed 4 weeks prior. Examination reveals loss of ankle dorsiflexion and eversion. Based on the electromyography results shown, what is the most probable location of nerve damage?
A) Common peroneal nerve at the knee level
B) Superficial peroneal nerve at the knee level
C) Sural nerve at the knee level
D) Tibial nerve at the knee level
E) Tibial nerve at the mid-calf level
questions.answer:
A)
The most probable injury site is the common peroneal nerve at the knee level. This nerve is frequently damaged in both traumatic and surgical procedures, causing foot drop and numbness in the first web space. The electromyography showing absent recruitment in both lateral compartment muscles (peroneals) and anterior compartment muscles (tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus) indicates common peroneal nerve involvement. B is incorrect because isolated superficial peroneal injury would preserve anterior compartment function. C is incorrect because the sural nerve is purely sensory and causes no motor deficits. D and E are incorrect because tibial nerve injuries would affect different muscle groups, and the presence of biceps femoris and tibialis posterior recruitment excludes tibial involvement.

questions.question:
Skin melanomas originate from which epidermal layer?
A) Stratum basale
B) Stratum corneum
C) Stratum granulosum
D) Stratum lucidum
E) Stratum spinosum
questions.answer:
A)
Melanomas develop from melanocytes located in the stratum basale, the deepest epidermal layer containing stem cells that differentiate into keratinocytes. This basal layer also houses Merkel cells and serves as the origin for basal cell carcinomas. B is incorrect because the stratum corneum is the outermost layer of dead, keratinized cells that provide barrier function. C is incorrect because the stratum granulosum contains keratinocytes with keratohyalin granules but not melanocytes. D is incorrect because the stratum lucidum exists only in thick skin and lacks melanocytes. E is incorrect because the stratum spinosum contains keratinocytes connected by desmosomes and Langerhans cells, but melanocytes reside deeper in the basal layer.

questions.question:
A 6-year-old girl with cerebral palsy requires surgical management for excessive drooling after failed medical therapy. Which salivary gland produces the largest portion of resting saliva?
A) Lacrimal
B) Minor salivary
C) Parotid
D) Sublingual
E) Submandibular
questions.answer:
E)
The submandibular glands produce approximately 60% of resting salivary output, making them the primary contributors to basal saliva production in the daily 500-2000 mL volume. Excessive drooling in cerebral palsy patients results from impaired swallowing rather than overproduction. A is incorrect because lacrimal glands produce tears, not saliva. B is incorrect because minor salivary glands contribute only about 10% of basal production. C is incorrect because parotid glands contribute approximately 20% of basal saliva. D is incorrect because sublingual glands contribute only about 10% of resting salivary flow.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old male presents with displaced left parasymphyseal and right mandibular body fractures from a motor vehicle accident. Biodegradable plate fixation is being considered. What outcome is associated with resorbable plates compared to titanium implants for mandibular fracture repair?
A) Reduced postoperative pain
B) Lower malunion rates
C) Higher total treatment cost
D) Greater infection risk
E) Thinner hardware profile
questions.answer:
C)
Bioresorbable fixation systems have significantly higher total treatment costs compared to titanium implants, which is the only consistent difference demonstrated in comparative studies. Multiple investigations have shown no statistical differences in complication rates, healing outcomes, or clinical performance between the two systems for mandibular fractures, with some studies suggesting a trend toward increased complications with resorbable plates. A is incorrect because postoperative pain levels are equivalent between systems. B is incorrect because malunion rates show no significant difference. D is incorrect because infection rates are comparable or potentially higher with resorbable systems. E is incorrect because resorbable plates typically have similar or bulkier profiles than titanium plates.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male arrives at the emergency room with severe left wrist pain following a 10-foot fall from a ladder. Radiographic imaging of the left wrist is provided. Following unsuccessful closed reduction, the patient experiences tingling that advances to progressive and persistent numbness in the left index and middle fingers during a 6-hour period. Which of the following emergency procedures is most indicated?
A) Joint aspiration of the wrist
B) Surgical carpal tunnel decompression
C) Magnetic resonance imaging of the wrist
D) Surgical reduction of the scaphoid bone
E) Additional attempt at closed reduction
questions.answer:
B)

This patient presents with a type IV perilunate dislocation (true lunate dislocation), representing complete disruption of ligamentous structures surrounding the lunate. The progression of median nerve symptoms despite reduction attempts indicates acute carpal tunnel syndrome requiring immediate surgical decompression. The lunate has displaced volarly into the carpal tunnel, compressing the median nerve and causing the progressive numbness in the median nerve distribution. Carpal tunnel release is urgently needed to decompress the nerve and prevent permanent damage. A is incorrect because wrist aspiration will not address the underlying nerve compression from the displaced lunate. C is incorrect because MRI is not urgently needed and delays necessary treatment. D is incorrect because there is no scaphoid fracture present, and this would not address the acute nerve compression. E is incorrect because repeat closed reduction is likely to fail and may worsen swelling without resolving the carpal tunnel symptoms.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old male develops foot drop and loss of sensation in the left foot after reconstruction of a soft tissue defect from a Gustilo Type IIIB proximal tibial fracture. Which of the following muscle flaps was most likely utilized for the reconstruction?
A) Gracilis muscle
B) Lateral head of gastrocnemius
C) Reverse sural artery flap
D) Sartorius muscle
E) Soleus muscle
questions.answer:
B)

The lateral gastrocnemius muscle flap is commonly used for proximal tibial reconstruction and carries a 7.7% risk of common peroneal nerve injury during harvest, which would cause the described foot drop and numbness. The nerve runs in close proximity to the lateral head of the gastrocnemius during dissection. This complication explains the patient's symptoms of foot drop (inability to dorsiflex) and sensory loss in the lateral foot. A is incorrect because gracilis harvest does not typically cause foot drop or involve the common peroneal nerve. C is incorrect because the reversed sural artery flap dissection does not endanger the common peroneal nerve. D is incorrect because sartorius muscle harvest does not affect the common peroneal nerve. E is incorrect because soleus harvest typically causes edema rather than nerve injury and does not commonly affect the common peroneal nerve.

questions.question:
A healthy 30-year-old female receives a diagnosis of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) on her upper back. Following wide local excision and local flap reconstruction, follow-up computed tomography reveals multiple lung metastases. What is the most suitable next treatment approach?
A) Systemic chemotherapy
B) Hormonal treatment
C) Immunological therapy
D) Radiation treatment
E) Surgical resection
questions.answer:
A)

Systemic chemotherapy with imatinib (a tyrosine kinase inhibitor) is the most appropriate treatment for metastatic DFSP. Imatinib specifically targets the platelet-derived growth factor receptor, which is overexpressed in DFSP due to chromosomal rearrangements. This targeted therapy blocks the autocrine growth stimulation that drives DFSP progression and has shown efficacy in inoperable, recurrent, or metastatic disease. B is incorrect because hormonal therapy has no established role in DFSP treatment. C is incorrect because immunotherapy is not a standard treatment for metastatic DFSP. D is incorrect because radiation therapy is used for local control but has no described benefit for pulmonary metastases in DFSP. E is incorrect because surgical resection of multiple pulmonary metastases is not recommended for metastatic DFSP.

questions.question:
Among the following permanent tooth types, which one typically emerges last during the transition from primary to permanent dentition?
A) Upper canine tooth
B) Upper central incisor tooth
C) Upper first molar tooth
D) Upper first premolar tooth
E) Upper lateral incisor tooth
questions.answer:
A)

The maxillary (upper) canine teeth are typically the last to erupt among the listed options, usually emerging around 11-12 years of age (excluding third molars/wisdom teeth). This late eruption timing is clinically significant for procedures like alveolar bone grafting in cleft patients, which must be completed well before canine eruption to provide adequate bone support for the tooth. B is incorrect because central incisors erupt much earlier, around 7-8 years of age. C is incorrect because first molars are among the earliest permanent teeth to erupt, around 6-7 years of age. D is incorrect because first premolars typically erupt around 10-11 years of age, before the canines. E is incorrect because lateral incisors erupt around 8-9 years of age, well before the canines.

questions.question:
When performing revision open rhinoplasty using a pre-existing transcolumellar incision, injury to which of the following vessels is most likely to compromise blood flow to the nasal tip?
A) Anterior ethmoidal artery
B) Columellar artery
C) Dorsal nasal artery
D) External nasal artery
E) Lateral nasal artery
questions.answer:
E)

The lateral nasal artery is the most critical vessel for nasal tip perfusion and is present in 100% of individuals. It arises from the facial artery and provides the dominant blood supply to the nasal tip. Injury to this vessel during transcolumellar dissection poses the greatest risk for tip ischemia. Safe dissection requires staying in a subperichondrial plane close to the lateral crura cartilage and limiting dissection above the alar groove level. A is incorrect because the anterior ethmoidal artery contributes to tip blood supply but is not the dominant vessel and can be sacrificed without compromising tip viability. B is incorrect because the columellar artery is only present in 68% of individuals and is not the primary blood supply. C is incorrect because the dorsal nasal artery provides supplementary flow but is not essential for tip viability. D is incorrect because the external nasal artery contributes to but does not provide the dominant blood supply to the nasal tip.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old male presents to the emergency department following an evening fight where he sustained multiple injuries to his right hand. Physical examination reveals deep lacerations overlying the right index and middle finger metacarpophalangeal joints. No tendon or neurovascular damage is evident. The wound undergoes bedside debridement, is packed with moist gauze, and covered with sterile dressing. Before discharge, which microorganism should prophylactic antibiotic therapy target?
A) Eikenella
B) Flavobacterium
C) Mycobacterium
D) Pasteurella
E) Vibrio
questions.answer:
A)
Dorsal hand lacerations must be recognized as potential sites for severe infection, particularly when sustained during altercations where "fight bites" may have occurred. Patients sometimes hesitate to disclose the true source of injury, so physicians should exercise caution and prescribe prophylactic antibiotics. Eikenella is the predominant bacteria found in human bite wounds, making it the correct target for prophylaxis. B is incorrect because Flavobacterium is linked to freshwater fish bites. C is incorrect because Mycobacterium is associated with bear and ferret bites. D is incorrect because Pasteurella is typically found in dog, cat, or farm animal bite wounds. E is incorrect because Vibrio is connected to shark bites and other marine-related injuries.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old woman in her first pregnancy at 24 weeks' gestation has a history of Bell's palsy and currently experiences synkinesis and left eye squinting when smiling. She seeks treatment options but wants to avoid anything that might compromise her pregnancy or interfere with her plan to breastfeed for one year postpartum. What is the most suitable treatment approach for this patient?
A) Chemodenervation of the left orbicularis oculi
B) Chemodenervation of the left orbicularis oris
C) Facial neuromuscular retraining
D) Gold weight implantation in the left upper eyelid
E) Selective neurolysis of the facial nerve's temporal branch
questions.answer:
C)
Facial neuromuscular retraining is the most appropriate option for this pregnant patient who wishes to avoid treatments that could affect her pregnancy or breastfeeding goals. This approach involves physical therapy with facial re-education techniques, including mirror biofeedback and electromyography, along with strategies like wearing sunglasses to minimize squinting. A is incorrect because chemodenervation agents have unknown effects during pregnancy and nursing, with botulinum toxin type A classified as pregnancy category C. B is incorrect for the same safety concerns regarding chemodenervation during pregnancy. D is incorrect because gold weight insertion would not address the patient's squinting symptoms. E is incorrect because permanent surgical denervation carries surgical risks during pregnancy and could compromise eye protection mechanisms.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old woman with right lateral chest wall sarcoma has completed preoperative radiation therapy. Following surgical resection, she has a 6-cm diameter chest wall skeletal defect. Only soft-tissue reconstruction is planned. What factor justifies soft-tissue reconstruction alone?
A) Lateral defects require no skeletal reconstruction
B) Prior radiation contraindicates skeletal chest wall reconstruction
C) Radiation-induced chest wall stiffness allows tolerance of large skeletal defects
D) Reconstruction should be delayed pending final pathology margin results
E) Oncologic resections preclude skeletal reconstruction
questions.answer:
C)
Radiation fibrosis creates chest wall rigidity, enabling patients to tolerate larger skeletal defects without requiring skeletal reconstruction. The radiation-induced stiffness provides adequate structural support despite the significant defect size. A is incorrect because lateral defects typically require skeletal reconstruction when ≥5 cm or involving four or more ribs due to the lateral chest wall's mobility. B is incorrect because radiation is not a contraindication for skeletal reconstruction. D is incorrect because reconstruction is performed simultaneously with resection, not staged. E is incorrect because oncologic resections do not contraindicate skeletal reconstruction when indicated.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old woman who has received botulinum toxin type A injections for orbital spasms over 16 years has developed treatment resistance. Botulinum toxin type B is being considered as an alternative. Compared to botulinum toxin type A, what outcome is most likely with botulinum toxin type B treatment?
A) Increased injection discomfort
B) Reduced wrinkle improvement
C) Extended duration of effect
D) Delayed onset of action
E) Decreased diffusion radius
questions.answer:
A)
Botulinum toxin type B causes significantly more injection pain due to its acidic pH of 5.6, which is necessary for its liquid stability. This low pH is consistently noted by patients as causing greater discomfort during injection compared to botulinum toxin type A. B is incorrect because botulinum toxin type B produces similar wrinkle reduction effectiveness to type A. C is incorrect because type B actually has a shorter, not longer, duration of action. D is incorrect because type B has a quicker, not delayed, onset of action. E is incorrect because type B has a greater, not smaller, radius of diffusion than type A.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old woman presents with jaw pain and new anterior open bite malocclusion following a ladder fall 6 hours earlier. Radiographic imaging demonstrates comminuted bilateral intracapsular mandibular fractures. What represents the most appropriate management?
A) External fixation application
B) Bilateral temporomandibular joint replacement
C) Two-week maxillomandibular fixation
D) Open reduction with internal fixation
E) Conservative observation with soft diet
questions.answer:
C)
Maxillomandibular fixation for 2 weeks is the standard treatment for bilateral intracapsular mandibular condyle fractures. This closed reduction approach with immobilization restores proper occlusion, relieves pain, and reestablishes normal bone and soft-tissue relationships. A is incorrect because external fixation provides no advantage when normal dentition is present and there are no complex mandibular injury patterns with segmental loss. B is incorrect because TMJ replacement is not indicated in a young patient with this injury pattern. D is incorrect because the small, comminuted intracapsular fragments are too small for reliable hardware fixation. E is incorrect because observation alone without immobilization would not adequately restore preinjury occlusion and bone relationships.

questions.question:
A 3-year-old boy is brought to the office because of abnormal head shape since birth. Photographs are shown. The patient is developmentally appropriate and has no other medical problems. Which of the following is the most appropriate surgical procedure for correction of this deformity?


A) Bilateral fronto-orbital advancement
B) Endoscopic craniotomy and helmet therapy
C) Monobloc distraction
D) Spring-mediated cranioplasty
E) Total vault reconstruction
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


The patient in the photograph has the classic features of sagittal suture synostosis. The primary clinical features of scaphocephaly are lengthening of the cranial vault in the anterior-posterior dimension, an anteriorly displaced cranial vertex, bullet-shaped occiput, biparietal and/or temporal narrowing and frontal bossing. All of these features are present in this patient. Because of the patient's late clinical presentation for treatment, the most appropriate surgical procedure would be a total cranial vault reconstruction of which there are many variations and techniques.


Because of the patient's age, he is not a candidate for either endoscopic-assisted wide strip craniotomy or spring-mediated cranioplasty. Ideal candidates for either procedure are ideally under age 6 months and 9 months, respectively, for an adequate clinical result. The results of both techniques have been shown to be comparable to traditional open remodeling procedures and are generally less invasive surgical procedures.


Although the monobloc distraction may allow the opportunity to remodel the forehead, there is no clinical indication for midface distraction in the patient described. A monobloc distraction alone will not correct the other abnormal features of scaphocephaly. It is not an indicated procedure for the correction of isolated sagittal suture synostosis.


Bilateral fronto-orbital advancement may allow the opportunity to remodel the forehead, but it will not address the other cranial vault abnormalities. There is no indication for remodeling the supraorbital bar in this case.


References
1. Greensmith AL, Holmes AD, Lo P, et al. Complete correction of severe scaphocephaly: the Melbourne method of total vault remodeling. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008 Apr;121(4): 1300-1310.
2. Massimi L, Caldarelli M, Tamburrini G, et al. Isolated sagittal craniosynostosis: definition, classification, and surgical indications. Childs Nerv Syst. 2012 Sep;28(9):1311-1317. Epub 2012 Aug 8.
3. Cohen SR, Mittermiller PA, Meltzer HS, et al. Nonsyndromic craniosynostosis: current treatment options. In: Thaller SR, Bradley JP, Garri JI, eds. Craniofacial Surgery. New York, NY: Informa Healthcare; 2008: 83-102.

questions.question:
A 3-year-old child presents to the clinic with a congenital soft tissue defect affecting the lower outer eyelid. What is the most suitable Tessier classification for this craniofacial cleft anomaly?
A) Tessier No. 3
B) Tessier No. 4
C) Tessier No. 6
D) Tessier No. 10
questions.answer:
C)
Tessier No. 6 clefts affect the bone and soft tissue structures of the lower lateral orbital region and are commonly associated with lower eyelid colobomas, making this the correct classification for a congenital soft tissue notch of the lower lateral eyelid. A is incorrect because Tessier No. 3 clefts involve defects between lateral incisors and canine teeth, affecting the alar base and medial canthal area rather than the lower eyelid. B is incorrect because Tessier No. 4 clefts extend from the upper lip through the alar base and nasomaxillary junction to the medial orbital tissues, not the lower lateral eyelid. D is incorrect because Tessier No. 10 clefts involve the superior orbital rim and medial orbit extending into the frontal bone, which is the upper rather than lower eyelid region.

questions.question:
What condition represents a relative CONTRAINDICATION for using the flap depicted in the image to reconstruct an 8 x 10-cm wound on the front of the ankle?
A) Diabetes mellitus
B) Hypertension
C) Joint exposure with loss of the joint capsule
D) Occlusion of the peroneal artery
E) Underlying osteomyelitis
questions.answer:
D)
Occlusion of the peroneal artery is a relative contraindication because the reverse sural artery flap depends primarily on perforators from the peroneal artery for its blood supply, particularly those arising 4-7 cm proximal to the lateral malleolus. A is incorrect because diabetes mellitus alone does not prevent successful use of this flap, though preoperative vascular assessment is recommended. B is incorrect because hypertension does not preclude the use of fasciocutaneous flaps in the lower extremity. C is incorrect because joint exposure with capsule loss is actually an indication for vascularized flap coverage. E is incorrect because underlying osteomyelitis is an indication for vascularized flap reconstruction when combined with adequate debridement and antibiotic therapy.

questions.question:
A healthy 27-year-old male presents for treatment of asymptomatic breast enlargement that has remained stable since developing at age 14. He uses no medications or recreational substances. Examination reveals bilateral symmetrical firm, rubbery subareolar masses measuring 4.5 cm in diameter with minimal surrounding fat, no sagging, and 28 mm areolar diameter. What is the most suitable treatment approach for this patient's condition?
A) Circumferential periareolar resection with liposuction
B) Mastectomy via Wise pattern incision
C) Observation to allow for involution
D) Oral hormone-blocking medication
E) Subareolar tissue resection via pull-through excision technique
questions.answer:
E)
Subareolar tissue resection via pull-through excision technique is most appropriate for uncomplicated gynecomastia with primarily fibrous tissue and minimal fat, allowing for complete removal through a limited areolar incision with minimal scarring. A is incorrect because circumferential periareolar resection with liposuction is better suited for cases with more fatty tissue and some skin redundancy. B is incorrect because mastectomy via Wise pattern is reserved for severe cases with significant skin excess and ptosis. C is incorrect because observation is inappropriate since gynecomastia persisting after age 21 is unlikely to resolve spontaneously. D is incorrect because hormone-blocking medications have no role in treating persistent breast tissue in healthy individuals.

questions.question:
Which rhinoplasty technique has the highest likelihood of causing alar rim notching, retraction, or collapse?
A) Cephalic trim of the lower lateral cartilages
B) Failure to place a columellar strut graft
C) Failure to place spreader grafts
D) Inadequate transdomal sutures
E) Migration of a cartilage tip onlay graft
questions.answer:
A)
Cephalic trim of the lower lateral cartilages is most likely to cause alar rim deformities because excessive or improper resection weakens the structural support of the alar rims, leading to notching, retraction, or collapse. B is incorrect because failure to place a columellar strut graft primarily affects nasal tip projection and support rather than alar rim contour. C is incorrect because failure to place spreader grafts mainly affects the internal nasal valve and has minimal impact on external nasal appearance, particularly the alar rims. D is incorrect because inadequate transdomal sutures affect nasal tip shape and definition but not alar rim position. E is incorrect because migration of a cartilage tip onlay graft affects tip contour and projection rather than alar rim integrity.

questions.question:
A 14-year-old male is evaluated for recurring severe epistaxis requiring emergency care. Skin examination reveals no discoloration abnormalities. Neurological assessment is normal. Family history is positive for frequent nosebleeds. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasias (HHT) is suspected. Which gene mutation is most probable in this patient?
A) ENG
B) KRIT1
C) PIK3CA
D) PTEN
E) RASA1
questions.answer:
A)
ENG (endoglin gene) mutation is most commonly associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT), which presents with characteristic arteriovenous malformations in nasal/oral mucosa, lungs, GI tract, and CNS, causing recurrent nosebleeds and bleeding complications. B is incorrect because KRIT1 mutations cause cerebral cavernous malformations with hyperkeratotic cutaneous vascular lesions, not the mucosal telangiectasias seen in HHT.
