C is incorrect because PIK3CA mutations cause CLOVES syndrome, an overgrowth disorder with vascular malformations but different clinical presentation than HHT. D is incorrect because PTEN mutations cause Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome with macrocephaly and genital lentiginosis, not the mucosal bleeding pattern of HHT. E is incorrect because RASA1 mutations cause capillary malformations with oval port-wine stains on skin, not the mucosal arteriovenous shunting characteristic of HHT.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old female presents with painless swelling in the lumbar region following a lower body lift procedure after significant weight reduction. Physical examination reveals firm swelling with a positive fluid wave sign. Weekly percutaneous needle drainage has been performed, with persistent fluid accumulation after three separate aspirations of 150 mL each of clear, amber-colored fluid. What is the most appropriate subsequent management approach?
A) Compression therapy
B) Surgical incision and drainage
C) Insertion of a closed suction drainage system
D) Ipsilateral gluteus maximus muscle advancement flap coverage
questions.answer:
C)

Closed suction drain placement is the most appropriate next step for this persistent seroma. Seroma formation occurs in 35-50% of post-massive weight loss body contouring patients, and after multiple failed aspirations, ultrasound-guided percutaneous closed suction drain insertion is the recommended treatment. A) Compression alone is insufficient after failed aspirations and would not effectively eliminate the established seroma. B) Surgical incision and drainage is reserved for cases where closed drainage fails, after unsuccessful sclerosant therapy, or when infection is present. D) Muscle flap reconstruction is not indicated for seroma management in this clinical scenario.

questions.question:
A male newborn with a Tessier No. 3 orofacial cleft is being assessed in the neonatal intensive care unit. When this cleft involves the alveolar ridge, which anatomical location represents the most typical pathway?
A) Between the canine and first premolar
B) Between the central and lateral incisors
C) Between the central incisors
D) Between the lateral incisor and canine
E) Between the first premolar and first molar
questions.answer:
D)

Tessier No. 3 clefts most commonly traverse between the lateral incisor and canine when involving the alveolar ridge, then extend through the nasal floor, nasolacrimal system, orbital floor, and medial canthal area. A) The canine-premolar location is not the typical pathway for Tessier No. 3 clefts. B) The central-lateral incisor position does not represent the characteristic route of this cleft type. C) The midline location between central incisors is not associated with Tessier No. 3 clefts. E) The premolar-molar region is not involved in the typical Tessier No. 3 cleft pathway.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female is scheduled for fleur-de-lis abdominoplasty after successful bariatric surgery, having lost 94 pounds (43 kg) with a current BMI of 28 kg/m². To optimize wound healing outcomes, what is the recommended daily protein consumption for this patient postoperatively?
A) 20 to 30 g/day
B) 40 to 50 g/day
C) 60 to 70 g/day
D) 80 to 90 g/day
E) Greater than 100 g/day
questions.answer:
C)

Post-bariatric patients require 60-70 g/day of protein for optimal wound healing, starting 2-4 weeks preoperatively and continuing 1-2 months postoperatively. Adequate protein intake is crucial for successful healing in massive weight loss patients due to gastrointestinal anatomical changes that can worsen nutritional deficiencies. A) 20-30 g/day is insufficient to meet the increased protein demands for wound healing in post-bariatric patients. B) 40-50 g/day remains below the recommended threshold for optimal healing outcomes. D) 80-90 g/day exceeds the established guidelines for post-bariatric body contouring patients. E) More than 100 g/day is unnecessarily high and beyond current recommendations.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female presents for consultation following a breast cancer diagnosis affecting her right breast. She has chosen to proceed with mastectomy of the affected breast. Which of the following represents a relative CONTRAINDICATION for nipple-sparing mastectomy?
A) Comedo-pattern breast neoplasm
B) Invasive lobular carcinoma
C) Subareolar tumor location
D) Tumor positioned 3 cm from the nipple
E) Tumor measuring 2.5 cm in diameter
questions.answer:
C)

A centrally located or subareolar tumor is a relative contraindication to nipple-sparing mastectomy, as tumors within 2 cm of the nipple are generally not suitable candidates for this procedure due to oncologic safety concerns. A) Comedo-type ductal carcinoma in situ is an early-stage cancer confined to ducts and does not contraindicate nipple-sparing mastectomy when meeting other criteria. B) Invasive lobular carcinoma is acceptable for nipple-sparing mastectomy provided it meets size and distance requirements. D) A tumor 3 cm from the nipple meets the minimum 2 cm distance requirement for nipple-sparing mastectomy. E) A 2.5 cm tumor falls within the acceptable size criteria of 3 cm or less for nipple-sparing mastectomy.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old male presents with significant hypotension and bradycardia following multiple facial fractures sustained in a motor vehicle accident. No other injuries are identified. Surgical repair of which anatomical structure would most likely resolve the patient's cardiovascular symptoms?
A) Mandible
B) Mental nerve
C) Nasal bone
D) Orbital floor
E) Zygomatic arch
questions.answer:
D)

Orbital floor fractures commonly trigger the oculocardiac reflex, causing bradycardia and hypotension, particularly in young patients with maxillofacial trauma. Surgical repair of the orbital floor fracture will likely resolve these cardiovascular symptoms by eliminating the reflex trigger. A) Mandibular fractures do not typically cause oculocardiac reflex or associated cardiovascular instability. B) Mental nerve injury does not produce systemic cardiovascular effects or oculocardiac reflex. C) Nasal bone fractures are not associated with oculocardiac reflex or hemodynamic instability. E) Zygomatic arch fractures do not commonly trigger oculocardiac reflex or cause bradycardia and hypotension.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old healthcare professional experiences a needlestick injury from a patient positive for hepatitis C antibodies. Immediate anti-HCV antibody testing and HCV-RNA confirmatory assays are conducted. At what time interval should the initial follow-up testing after exposure be scheduled?
A) 1 week
B) 3 weeks
C) 6 weeks
D) 12 weeks
E) 24 weeks
questions.answer:
C)
The appropriate response is C. Guidelines recommend follow-up retesting at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months following confirmed HCV exposure. A is incorrect because testing at 1 week is too early and may result in false negative results due to the window period. B is incorrect because 3 weeks is still within the early window period where antibodies may not yet be detectable. D is incorrect because waiting 12 weeks unnecessarily delays detection when earlier testing at 6 weeks is adequate. E is incorrect because 24 weeks provides no benefit over the standard 6-week initial follow-up and delays appropriate monitoring.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old woman without family history of breast malignancy undergoes bilateral breast augmentation using 300 mL autologous fat per breast. Six months postoperatively, she develops right breast pain. Mammographic evaluation reveals linear clustered microcalcifications in the right breast's medial lower quadrant, bilateral small lipid cysts with scattered dystrophic rod-shaped calcifications in both upper lateral quadrants, and pectoral muscle heterogeneity. What is the most appropriate management approach?
A) Baseline mammography between ages 35 and 40 and yearly thereafter
B) Core needle biopsy of the bilateral upper outer quadrants
C) Core needle biopsy of the right lower inner quadrant
D) Repeat mammography at 6 months and 12 months
E) Repeat mammography in 1 year
questions.answer:
C)
The correct answer is C. The linear clustered microcalcifications in the right lower inner quadrant are suspicious and require tissue sampling via core needle biopsy to rule out malignancy. A is incorrect because routine screening mammography is inappropriate when there are suspicious findings requiring immediate evaluation. B is incorrect because the bilateral upper outer quadrant calcifications appear benign (dystrophic rod-like) and can be observed rather than biopsied. D is incorrect because short-interval follow-up mammography is inadequate for suspicious clustered microcalcifications that need histologic evaluation. E is incorrect because waiting one year to repeat imaging ignores the suspicious findings that require immediate tissue diagnosis.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department following electrical burn injuries. He experiences left hand numbness with decreased pulse and diminished tactile sensation. What is the most effective treatment to restore circulation to the left hand?
A) Anticoagulation
B) Embolectomy
C) Burn excision
D) Escharotomy
E) Fasciotomy
questions.answer:
E)
The correct answer is E. The patient has circumferential electrical burns causing compartment syndrome, requiring fasciotomy to relieve increased compartment pressure and restore perfusion. A is incorrect because anticoagulation does not address the underlying compartment pressure problem causing the vascular compromise. B is incorrect because embolectomy treats arterial occlusion from emboli, not compartment syndrome from external compression. C is incorrect because burn excision removes devitalized tissue but does not treat compartment syndrome or restore circulation. D is incorrect because escharotomy releases constriction from burn eschar but fasciotomy is needed to address the deeper compartment pressure affecting circulation.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old woman presents for assessment one year following vertical mastopexy performed without implants, concerned that her breasts appear to be drooping again. Which breast measurement has most likely increased since her previous examination?
A) Breast base diameter
B) Nipple to inframammary crease
C) Nipple-areola diameter
D) Suprasternal notch to inframammary crease
E) Suprasternal notch to nipple
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is B. The nipple-to-inframammary crease distance most commonly increases over time, causing pseudoptosis or "bottoming out" where breast tissue descends below the inframammary fold while the nipple maintains its position. A is incorrect because breast base diameter remains relatively stable when breast volume is constant, changing primarily with weight fluctuations. C is incorrect because nipple-areola diameter typically does not increase with vertical mastopexy, though it may occur with periareolar techniques. D is incorrect because the suprasternal notch-to-inframammary crease distance changes minimally compared to the nipple-to-inframammary crease measurement. E is incorrect because suprasternal notch-to-nipple distance shows little postoperative change unless implants are used.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old man receives microsurgical reattachment of a severed ear. Venous congestion develops and medicinal leeches are utilized. This patient has increased risk for infection from which microorganism?
A) Actinobacillus lignieresii
B) Aeromonas hydrophila
C) Eikenella corrodens
D) Pasteurella canis
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is B. Aeromonas hydrophila naturally inhabits the digestive system of Hirudo medicinalis (medicinal leeches) and can cause infection when leeches are used therapeutically, requiring antibiotic prophylaxis with fluoroquinolones, tetracycline, or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. A is incorrect because Actinobacillus lignieresii is associated with equine bite wounds, not leech therapy. C is incorrect because Eikenella corrodens is typically found in human bite infections, not leech-related infections. D is incorrect because Pasteurella canis is associated with canine bite wounds, not medicinal leech applications.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient requires evaluation for immediate bilateral breast reconstruction utilizing deep inferior epigastric artery perforator free flap coverage. Which of the following medical conditions is most commonly linked to a hypercoagulable state?
A) Celiac disease
B) Graves disease
C) Rheumatoid arthritis
D) Systemic lupus erythematosus
E) Type 1 diabetes mellitus
questions.answer:
D)
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is the correct answer because certain patients with SLE can develop antiplatelet membrane phospholipid antibodies, which enhance platelet adhesion and aggregation, creating a hypercoagulable condition. While not universal among SLE patients, this autoimmune condition warrants special consideration during free flap reconstruction planning. A) Celiac disease is incorrect as it is primarily a gastrointestinal autoimmune disorder without typical coagulation abnormalities. B) Graves disease is incorrect because this thyroid autoimmune condition does not commonly cause hypercoagulability. C) Rheumatoid arthritis is incorrect as this joint-focused autoimmune disease typically does not involve coagulation disorders. E) Type 1 diabetes mellitus is incorrect since this endocrine autoimmune condition does not typically present with hypercoagulable states.

questions.question:
A 19-year-old woman presents with a 2 √o 3-cm burn to the left dorsal thumb sustained from brief exposure to hot bacon grease. During the next 24 hours, the burned area becomes erythematous and several blisters containing clear fluid have formed and then ruptured. Examination shows no erythema extending proximally. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Dry dressing
B) Hydrogen peroxide soaks
C) Leave open to air
D) Topical antibiotic ointment
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Based on the information provided, this is likely a superficial partial-thickness burn. It is not deep enough or large enough to warrant transfer to a burn center. Local wound care should lead to full resolution, with appropriate follow-up to detect delays in healing. Partial-thickness wounds like this will heal fastest when a moist environment is maintained. Antibiotic ointment or other neutral moisturizing agents (e.g., petrolatum ointment) are appropriate for local wound care. Leaving the wound open to air or covering with a dry dressing will delay healing. Hydrogen peroxide is appropriate for cleansing dirty or infected wounds, but it is not necessary in the scenario presented. Furthermore, sustained use of hydrogen peroxide may delay healing in clean wounds.


ReferencesPan BS, Vu AT, Yakuboff KP. Management of the acutely burned hand. J Hand Surg Am. 2015;40(7):1477-1485.Richards WT, Vergara E, Dalaly DG, Coady-Fariborzian L, Mozingo DW. Acute surgical management of hand burns. J Hand Surg Am. 2014;39(10):2075-2085.e2.Winter GD. Formation of the scab and the rate of epithelization of superficial wounds in the skin of the young domestic pig. Nature. 1962;193:293-294.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old male patient presents with a painful unilateral facial eruption featuring vesicles, severe ear discomfort, and complete ipsilateral facial nerve palsy. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Cholesteatoma
B) Facial myokymia
C) Lyme disease
D) Möbius syndrome
E) Ramsay Hunt syndrome
questions.answer:
E)
Ramsay Hunt syndrome (herpes zoster oticus) is correct because this condition represents a herpes zoster variant that affects both sensory neurons and facial nerve motor fibers during viral reactivation, presenting with the classic triad of facial rash, ear pain, and facial paralysis. Treatment typically involves corticosteroids, analgesics, and antiviral therapy. A) Cholesteatoma is incorrect as this benign keratinous growth in the ear may cause facial nerve damage but does not present with vesicular rash and ear pain. B) Facial myokymia is incorrect because this condition, often associated with multiple sclerosis, causes rippling facial muscle movements without rash or severe pain. C) Lyme disease is incorrect as this bacterial infection does not typically present with vesicular rash and ear pain in this pattern. D) Möbius syndrome is incorrect because this is a congenital neurological disorder with facial paralysis present from birth, not acquired with rash and pain.

questions.question:
A 20-year-old man has purulent breakdown 5 months after sustaining a Gustilo type IIIB open fracture treated with intramedullary rod placement and skin grafting over a medial gastrocnemius flap. A postoperative x-ray study and current photograph are shown. The intramedullary rod is removed and an external fixator is placed. There is 1.5 cm of bone without periosteum surrounding the fracture exposed in the wound. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in wound reconstruction?


A) Full-thickness skin grafting with a bolster dressing
B) Reconstruction with an anterior tibial artery perforator flap
C) Reconstruction with a lateral gastrocnemius muscle flap and skin grafting
D) Reconstruction with a pedicled descending medial genicular artery flap
E) Split-thickness skin grafting with negative pressure wound therapy
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


Perforator flap reconstruction, whether free or pedicled, has become increasingly popular over the past decade. Perforator flap use allows for the creation of an axial pattern flap without the sacrifice of a major artery and can often be done for areas once considered to require free flaps for coverage. Prior transfer of a medial gastrocnemius flap might disrupt perforators from the posterior tibial artery to the medial leg skin, but would not have disturbed anterior tibial artery perforators through the skin of the anterolateral leg.





Skin grafting, whether split- or full-thickness, would not be successful on fractured bone without periosteum, regardless of the type of dressing used.


The lateral gastrocnemius muscle is smaller and cannot reach as far as the medial gastrocnemius. It would not be able to reach the mid-shaft tibia defect shown in this patient.


The descending medial genicular artery is the pedicle of the medial femoral condyle flap. It is normally used as a bone graft donor, although an overlying skin paddle can be harvested with it. When used in a pedicled fashion, it can be transposed proximally onto the thigh, but not distally onto the leg.


References
1. Hallock GG. A paradigm shift in flap selection protocols for zones of the lower extremity using perforator flaps. J Reconstr Microsurg. 2013 May;29(4):233-240. Epub 2013 Mar 5.
2. Iorio ML, Masden DL, Higgins JP. Cutaneous angiosome territory of the medial femoral condyle osteocutaneous flap. J Hand Surg Am. 2012 May;37(5):1033-1041. Epub 2012 Apr 5.
3. Kasabian AK, Karp NS. Lower extremity reconstruction. In: Grabb & Smith‚Äos Plastic Surgery. 7th ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2014: 941-954.

questions.question:
Which of the following variables is most likely to influence whether a patient receives breast reconstruction following mastectomy?
A) BRCA1/BRCA2 status
B) Insurance coverage through Medicaid
C) Living close to a reconstructive surgeon
D) Patient age
E) Residence in the southeastern United States
questions.answer:
C)
Proximity to a reconstructive surgeon is correct because multiple large population studies demonstrate that geographic distance from reconstruction providers is one of the two primary barriers to accessing breast reconstruction services. Patients living farther from qualified surgeons have significantly lower reconstruction rates compared to those with better geographic access. A) BRCA1/BRCA2 status is incorrect because while BRCA-positive patients may have higher bilateral reconstruction rates, genetic status is not the primary determinant of reconstruction access. B) Medicaid insurance coverage is incorrect as it represents a barrier rather than a facilitating factor for reconstruction access. D) Patient age is incorrect because while younger patients may have higher reconstruction rates, age alone is not the strongest predictor of reconstruction access. E) Southeastern US residence is incorrect as regional location alone does not determine reconstruction likelihood as strongly as provider proximity.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male patient has sustained an ulnar nerve injury at the elbow with an 8-cm nerve defect. The treatment plan includes distal nerve transfers at the wrist level (motor) and palm level (sensory) to restore intrinsic hand function and digital sensation. If the proximal nerve defect remains unrepaired, which of the following impairments will most likely remain?
A) Decreased elbow flexion strength
B) Decreased finger extension strength
C) Decreased sensation in the first web space
D) Decreased sensation on the dorsal hand
questions.answer:
D)
Decreased dorsal hand sensation is correct because the dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve originates approximately 7 cm proximal to the wrist crease, and distal nerve transfers at the wrist and palm levels cannot restore this proximal sensory branch function. Only repair of the proximal nerve gap would restore dorsal ulnar hand sensation. A) Decreased elbow flexion strength is incorrect because elbow flexion is primarily mediated by the biceps, brachialis, and brachioradialis muscles, which are not innervated by the ulnar nerve. B) Decreased finger extension strength is incorrect as finger extension is controlled by the posterior interosseous nerve (radial nerve branch), not the ulnar nerve. C) Decreased first web space sensation is incorrect because this area is innervated by the radial nerve, not the ulnar nerve, and would not be affected by ulnar nerve injury.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for assessment of pigmented bands affecting the left thumb and index finger nails. His history includes a minor crush injury to the thumb one year prior that required no intervention. Physical examination reveals 4-mm-wide pigmented bands in both digits extending from the nail fold to the nail tip. The patient notes progressive darkening of the pigmented regions over time. Which of the following clinical characteristics most strongly suggests a benign process?
A) Age greater than 50 years
B) Change in color over time
C) Involvement of more than one digit
D) Pigmentation involving the periungual skin
E) Width greater than 3 mm
questions.answer:
C)
Multiple digit involvement is correct because benign melanonychia commonly affects several digits simultaneously, whereas subungual melanoma typically presents as a solitary lesion affecting only one digit. This multi-digit presentation strongly favors a benign etiology. A) Age greater than 50 years is incorrect as this demographic factor actually increases suspicion for subungual melanoma, which commonly occurs in patients aged 50-70 years. B) Color change over time is incorrect because progressive darkening or size changes are concerning features that suggest possible malignant transformation. D) Periungual skin pigmentation is incorrect as this represents Hutchinson's sign, which is highly suspicious for subungual melanoma. E) Width greater than 3 mm is incorrect because pigmented bands wider than 3 mm are considered a warning sign for possible subungual melanoma.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old female presents for assessment of painless swelling in the left mandibular region. A panoramic radiograph (Panorex) is provided. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Cherubism
B) Dentigerous cyst
C) Desmoid tumor
D) Giant cell tumor
E) Tuberous sclerosis
questions.answer:
B)

The panoramic radiographic findings are most characteristic of a dentigerous cyst, also known as a follicular cyst. These are developmental cystic lesions, not neoplasms, that form when the dental follicle separates from an unerupted tooth crown. Dentigerous cysts are odontogenic in nature and develop when fluid collects between the reduced enamel epithelium and the crown of an impacted tooth. They typically occur around mandibular third molars in adolescents and young adults, presenting as painless bony expansion with a well-defined, unilocular radiolucent appearance on imaging, often surrounded by a sclerotic border. A) Cherubism is incorrect because it is a rare hereditary condition affecting children with bilateral jaw involvement and fibrous tissue replacement. C) Desmoid tumor is incorrect because it appears as a solid, erosive lesion rather than a cystic one. D) Giant cell tumor is incorrect because it presents as a solid, aggressive-appearing lesion with bone destruction. E) Tuberous sclerosis is incorrect because associated bone tumors are rare and appear solid, not cystic.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old Japanese boy is evaluated by his mother due to concerns about extreme sun sensitivity. His history reveals severe sunburns with minimal exposure and early freckling by age 2. His siblings are unaffected despite similar skin tones. Biopsy of an elevated facial lesion shows squamous cell carcinoma. What inheritance pattern best describes this child's likely condition?
A) Autosomal dominant
B) Autosomal recessive
C) Multifactorial
D) X-linked dominant
E) X-linked recessive
questions.answer:
B)

This child has xeroderma pigmentosum (XP), which follows an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. XP results from defective DNA repair mechanisms, making patients extremely susceptible to UV-induced DNA damage and early malignancies. The condition affects approximately 1 in 250,000 individuals and is more prevalent in Japanese populations. Patients develop severe photosensitivity, early freckling, and skin cancers at a young age, with dramatically increased risks for various malignancies compared to the general population. A) Autosomal dominant is incorrect because both parents must be carriers for the child to be affected, and siblings are typically unaffected. C) Multifactorial is incorrect because XP is caused by single gene defects, not multiple genetic and environmental factors. D) X-linked dominant is incorrect because the condition affects both sexes equally and follows autosomal inheritance. E) X-linked recessive is incorrect because XP is not located on the X chromosome and affects males and females equally.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old man is evaluated 10 days after sustaining a traumatic amputation of the tip of the right index finger. A photograph of the debridement is shown. X-ray study shows no fractures. After debridement of loose eschar, no bone or tendon was exposed. The wound is approximately 1 cm2. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment of the resulting defect?


A ) Coverage with bilateral V-Y flaps
B ) Coverage with volar advancement flap
C ) Dressing changes
D ) Periarterial sympathectomy
E ) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Although composite grafts will often survive in children and may be attempted in adults, aggressive defatting of the amputated segment and removal of bone fragments may still fail.


The photograph demonstrates an eschar resulting from necrosis following reattachment of an amputated fingertip pulp. In the absence of underlying exposed ?white? structures such as joints, or tendon denuded of tenosynovium, optimal healing and function will occur via secondary intention. In this case, removal of any sloughing eschar will facilitate local wound care during healing.


Skin grafting is useful for covering larger defects; however, sensation over the graft will be less satisfactory than over a fingertip wound that heals by secondary intention.


A variety of local flaps have been used for fingertip tissue loss, including bilateral V-Y (Kutler) and volar advancement (Atasoy/Tranquilli-Leali) flaps. V-Y flaps place a scar directly in the midline of the pulp and are limited in the degree to which they may be advanced. The longer volar advancement flaps may be useful in covering bone or supporting the nail bed in the setting of a palmar oblique amputation through the distal phalanx; however, these flaps carry an increased risk of flexion contracture at the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint.


Pulp necrosis can occur in the setting of digital ischemia due to Raynaud disease or thrombotic ulnar artery occlusion (hypothenar hammer syndrome). Periarterial sympathectomy can prevent tissue loss in some cases of vascular spasm or insufficiency. In this patient with an otherwise visibly well-perfused hand and discrete history of trauma, digital ischemia would be an unlikely cause of the necrosis.


References
1. Lemmon JA, Janis JE, Rohrich RJ. Soft-tissue injuries of the fingertip: methods of evaluation and treatment. An algorithmic approach. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008 Sep;122(3):105e-117e.
2. Chen SY, Wang CH, Fu JP, et al. Composite grafting for traumatic fingertip amputation in adults: technique reinforcement and experience in 31 digits. J Trauma. 2011 Jan;70(1):148-153.

questions.question:
A 10-year-old male with obstructive sleep apnea history and previous straight-line cleft palate repair presents with hypernasal speech causing social difficulties. No oronasal fistula is present, the velum shows vaulting but elevates appropriately during phonation. What is the optimal treatment for speech improvement?
A) Continued speech therapy
B) Furlow palatoplasty
C) Posterior pharyngeal flap
D) Tonsillectomy
E) Use of a palatal lift device
questions.answer:
B)

This patient is an ideal candidate for conversion Furlow palatoplasty. The presence of velar vaulting indicates anteriorly positioned levator veli palatini muscles, and the good palatal elevation demonstrates adequate muscle function. These factors make Furlow palatoplasty particularly effective for addressing hypernasality after failed straight-line repairs. This technique repositions the levator muscles more posteriorly and lengthens the palate. A) Continued speech therapy is incorrect because structural velopharyngeal insufficiency requires surgical correction, not just therapy. C) Posterior pharyngeal flap is incorrect because this patient has sleep apnea history and good palatal mobility; this procedure would be better for patients with poor velar motion. D) Tonsillectomy is incorrect because while it might help sleep apnea, it won't address the structural cause of hypernasality. E) Palatal lift device is incorrect because it's reserved for patients with poor palatal motion who cannot undergo surgery, not for those with good mobility.

questions.question:
What is the most frequent complication associated with using the Moberg volar advancement flap for thumb tip reconstruction?
A) Difficulty retraining sensory function
B) Extension deficit of the interphalangeal joint
C) Hook-nail deformity
D) Necrosis of the flap
E) Skin necrosis of the dorsal thumb
questions.answer:
B)

Extension deficit of the interphalangeal joint is the most common complication of the Moberg volar advancement flap. Studies show that when bony amputations are excluded, approximately 55% of patients develop extension deficits with at least 20 degrees of active range of motion loss. This occurs due to the advancement of volar skin and soft tissues, which can create tension and restrict joint extension. A) Difficulty retraining sensory function is incorrect because the Moberg flap preserves native innervation, eliminating the need for sensory retraining unlike other flaps. C) Hook-nail deformity is incorrect because this results from loss of distal nail bed support after injury, not from the flap procedure itself. D) Necrosis of the flap is incorrect because the Moberg flap includes the robust neurovascular bundles, making flap necrosis unlikely. E) Skin necrosis of the dorsal thumb is incorrect because the thumb has independent dorsal circulation, unlike other digits where this might be a concern.

questions.question:
According to CDC guidelines, which timeframe most accurately defines when surgical site infections can occur?
A) Within 3 days of surgery or within 30 days of prosthetic implant placement
B) Within 7 days of surgery or within 3 months of prosthetic implant placement
C) Within 14 days of surgery or within 6 months of prosthetic implant placement
D) Within 21 days of surgery or within 9 months of prosthetic implant placement
E) Within 30 days of surgery or within 1 year of prosthetic implant placement
questions.answer:
E)

The CDC defines surgical site infection as occurring within 30 days after surgery or within 1 year if a prosthetic implant is placed. This extended timeframe for implant-related infections recognizes that foreign materials can harbor bacteria and cause delayed infections. The infection must meet specific criteria including purulent drainage, positive cultures, wound dehiscence with signs of infection, abscess formation, or physician diagnosis. A) Within 3 days/30 days is incorrect because the standard timeframe is 30 days for non-implant surgery, not 3 days. B) Within 7 days/3 months is incorrect because both timeframes are shorter than CDC standards. C) Within 14 days/6 months is incorrect because the non-implant timeframe is too short and implant timeframe is too short. D) Within 21 days/9 months is incorrect because both timeframes differ from the established CDC definitions.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female patient with right breast carcinoma presents for consultation regarding right mastectomy with immediate implant-based reconstruction and a balancing procedure for the opposite breast. Clinical evaluation reveals bilateral Grade 3 breast ptosis with equivalent breast volumes. She currently uses a 34C bra and wishes to maintain her current breast size. Which of the following represents the most suitable procedure for the opposite breast?
A) Breast augmentation
B) Autologous fat grafting
C) Breast lift
D) Breast reduction
questions.answer:
C)
The most suitable procedure for the opposite breast in this scenario is a breast lift (mastopexy). Since the patient has equivalent breast volumes bilaterally and desires to maintain her current size, volume adjustment is not needed. The primary issue is the Grade 3 ptosis of the contralateral breast, which requires positional correction to achieve symmetry with the reconstructed breast. A) Breast augmentation is incorrect because the patient has adequate volume and doesn't want to increase size. B) Autologous fat grafting is incorrect because volume enhancement is not needed when volumes are already symmetric. D) Breast reduction is incorrect because the patient wants to maintain her current breast size, not reduce it.

questions.question:
A 7-month-old male infant is referred because of the lesion shown in the photograph. Ophthalmologic examination shows mild astigmatism, for which he was being treated with corrective lenses. No amblyopia is noted. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Administration of propranolol 2 mg/kg/day in divided doses
B) Magnetic resonance angiography of the brain
C) Pulsed-dye laser (595 nm) therapy
D) Surgical resection
E) Observation only
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


The patient described has focal hemangioma. Medical therapy is the first line of treatment in this case when there are minimal ophthalmologic findings. There is a subset of periorbital hemangiomas for which surgical resection is indicated: well-localized hemangioma amenable to resection, greater than 2 diopters of astigmatism, visual obstruction, or nonresponsive to medical therapy. In a study by Arneja and Mulliken, the best ophthalmologic improvement occurred when the hemangioma was resected at less than age 3 months.


Laser therapy can treat discoloration only and will not decrease the bulk of the lesion.


Surgical debulking is indicated if the hemangioma does not clinically respond (softer, lightening in color, no improvement in/worsening of astigmatism).


References
1. Chiller KG, Passaro D, Frieden IJ. Hemangiomas of infancy: clinical characteristics, morphologic subtypes, and their relationship to race, ethnicity, and sex. Arch Dermatol. 2002 Dec;138(12):1567-1576.
2. Metry D, Heyer G, Hess C, et al. Consensus Statement on Diagnostic Criteria for PHACE Syndrome. Pediatrics. 2009 Nov;124(5):1447-1456. Epub 2009 Oct 26.
3. Batta K, Goodyear HM, Moss C, et al. Randomised controlled study of early pulsed dye laser treatment of uncomplicated childhood haemangiomas: results of a 1-year analysis. Lancet. 2002 Aug 17;360(9332):521-527.
4. Arneja JS, Mulliken JB. Resection of amblyogenic periocular hemangiomas: indications and outcomes. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2010 Jan;125(1):274-281.

questions.question:
A 71-year-old female patient chooses surgical intervention for basilar thumb arthritis. Along with carpal tunnel syndrome and pathology at the scaphotrapeziotrapezoid (STT) joint, evaluation for which of the following additional concurrent conditions is most important during surgical planning for this patient?
A) Lunotriquetral instability
B) Radioscaphoid joint disease
C) Scapholunate instability
D) Thumb interphalangeal joint arthritis
E) Thumb metacarpophalangeal joint hyperextension
questions.answer:
E)
Thumb metacarpophalangeal joint hyperextension is the most important additional condition to evaluate during surgical planning for basilar thumb arthritis. Preoperative assessment must include evaluation of the MP joint for hyperextension deformity, especially during pinch activities. Failure to address MP hyperextension greater than 30 degrees can result in continued pain and progressive thumb collapse after basilar joint treatment. A) Lunotriquetral instability is incorrect because it is not commonly associated with basilar thumb arthritis or its surgical management. B) Radioscaphoid joint disease is incorrect because this condition is not typically related to basilar thumb pathology. C) Scapholunate instability is incorrect because it does not correlate with basilar thumb arthritis treatment outcomes. D) Thumb interphalangeal joint arthritis is incorrect because this joint is not commonly involved in the pathophysiology of basilar thumb arthritis.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female patient with a documented anaphylactic response to procaine seeks consultation for breast augmentation surgery. Local anesthetics containing which of the following components should be contraindicated in this patient?
A) Acetaldehyde
B) Epinephrine
C) Iodine
D) Methylparaben
E) Para-aminobenzoic acid
questions.answer:
E)
Para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) should be avoided in local anesthetics for this patient. Genuine allergic responses to local anesthetics are uncommon, but when they occur, PABA is the most probable allergen. This compound is a metabolite of ester-type local anesthetics like procaine and can trigger Type I hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis through IgE-mediated mechanisms. A) Acetaldehyde is incorrect because it is not a component found in local anesthetic formulations. B) Epinephrine is incorrect because while it can cause physiologic effects like vasoconstriction, it typically does not cause allergic reactions. C) Iodine is incorrect because it is not present in standard local anesthetic preparations. D) Methylparaben is incorrect because although preservatives can occasionally cause reactions, they are much less likely to cause allergic responses compared to PABA.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old male patient arrives at the emergency department following a laceration involving the index finger flexor digitorum profundus, flexor digitorum superficialis, and radial digital nerve of his non-dominant left hand. Emergency repair is planned using single-cuff Bier block anesthesia. Which of the following would provide the strongest rationale for choosing an axillary block instead?
A) Patient age
B) Patient gender
C) Patient occupation
D) Expected operative time
E) Emergency nature of procedure
questions.answer:
D)
Expected operative time is the strongest rationale for selecting an axillary block over Bier block anesthesia. Bier block is constrained by tourniquet tolerance, with tourniquet pain typically developing after 20-30 minutes, making it suitable only for brief upper extremity procedures. Complex repairs involving multiple structures (two flexor tendons and a digital nerve) require extended operative time that would exceed the comfortable duration of a Bier block. A) Patient age is incorrect because a 53-year-old patient falls within the acceptable age range for Bier block (contraindicated only in very young children and very elderly patients). B) Patient gender is incorrect because gender is not a contraindication for Bier block anesthesia. C) Patient occupation is incorrect because occupation does not influence the choice of anesthetic technique for this procedure. E) Emergency nature of procedure is incorrect because urgency is not a contraindication to Bier block anesthesia.

questions.question:
Following uncomplicated breast reconstruction using an abdominal flap, a healthy 45-year-old female patient receives ketorolac as part of her comprehensive pain management protocol. Suppression of which of the following represents the main mechanism responsible for the prolonged bleeding time associated with this medication?
A) Lipoxygenase
B) Nitric oxide
C) Prostacyclin
D) Prostaglandins
E) Thromboxane A2
questions.answer:
E)
Thromboxane A2 suppression is the main mechanism responsible for prolonged bleeding time with ketorolac use. Ketorolac, as an NSAID, inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) enzymes, thereby blocking thromboxane A2 synthesis. This creates a systemic bleeding tendency by disrupting thromboxane-dependent platelet aggregation, resulting in extended bleeding time. A) Lipoxygenase is incorrect because its inhibition is not the primary mechanism for NSAID-related bleeding complications. B) Nitric oxide is incorrect because nitric oxide suppression is not the main pathway for NSAID-induced platelet dysfunction. C) Prostacyclin is incorrect because while NSAIDs affect prostacyclin production, this is not the primary mechanism for increased bleeding time. D) Prostaglandins is incorrect because although NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandin synthesis, this primarily contributes to anti-inflammatory effects rather than bleeding complications.

questions.question:
For a solo physician practice, which of the following characterizations of a Privacy Official aligns with US Department of Health & Human Services (HHS) standards as outlined in the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)?
A) A committee of staff members serving as a privacy committee
B) A person who serves as both the privacy official and practice manager
C) An external advisor with specialized knowledge in HIPAA privacy regulations
D) A trainee who works exclusively as the privacy official
questions.answer:
B)
The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), enacted in 1996, establishes guidelines for protecting private health information. The law includes scalability provisions that allow smaller practices flexibility in implementation. According to HHS guidance, in a small physician practice, the privacy official may be the office manager with additional non-privacy duties, making option B correct. Option A is incorrect because a privacy board is not required for small practices and doesn't designate a single responsible individual. Option C is incorrect because while consultants can provide expertise, the practice must have a designated internal privacy official. Option D is incorrect because a student intern lacks the authority and permanence needed for this role, and having privacy as the sole responsibility is unnecessary in a small practice setting.

questions.question:
For patients with thumb basilar joint arthritis, what outcome is most likely when comparing simple trapeziectomy versus trapeziectomy combined with ligament reconstruction and tendon interposition?
A) Lower complication rates
B) Higher likelihood of persistent pain
C) Extended rehabilitation period
D) Inferior functional results
questions.answer:
A)
Meta-analyses demonstrate that simple trapeziectomy provides equivalent pain relief and functional outcomes compared to trapeziectomy with ligament reconstruction and tendon interposition, but with fewer complications, making option A correct. Option B is incorrect because studies show no difference in pain outcomes between the two approaches. Option C is incorrect because simple trapeziectomy typically has a shorter, not longer, recovery time due to its less complex nature. Option D is incorrect because functional outcomes are equivalent between the two procedures, with no demonstrated superiority of the more complex reconstruction technique.

questions.question:
From which epidermal layer does cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma originate?
A) Stratum basale
B) Stratum corneum
C) Stratum granulosum
D) Stratum lucidum
E) Stratum spinosum
questions.answer:
A)
Squamous cell carcinoma develops from keratinocytes located in the stratum basale, the deepest epidermal layer containing stem cells that differentiate into keratinocytes, making option A correct. Option B is incorrect because the stratum corneum consists of dead, keratinized cells that form the skin's outer barrier and cannot give rise to carcinomas. Option C is incorrect because the stratum granulosum contains keratinocytes with keratohyalin granules that are in a transitional state, not the origin of malignancy. Option D is incorrect because the stratum lucidum is only present in thick skin and consists of translucent cells, not the source of squamous cell carcinoma. Option E is incorrect because while the stratum spinosum contains keratinocytes, the malignant transformation originates from the basal stem cells in the stratum basale.

questions.question:
A 19-year-old male presents with ongoing left wrist pain following an ATV crash 4 months prior. History includes cast immobilization for a wrist fracture. Radiographs reveal a proximal pole scaphoid fracture without degenerative changes or structural collapse. What imaging modality is most suitable for evaluating bone fragment vascularity in this case?
A) Angiography
B) CT scan
C) MRI
D) Triple phase bone scan
E) Ultrasonography
questions.answer:
C)
MRI, particularly with gadolinium enhancement, is the optimal imaging method for assessing scaphoid vascularity and detecting avascular necrosis in proximal pole fractures, which are at high risk due to retrograde blood supply, making option C correct. Option A is incorrect because angiography shows blood flow patterns but lacks the anatomical detail needed for fracture assessment. Option B is incorrect because CT provides excellent anatomical detail but is less sensitive than MRI for detecting avascular necrosis. Option D is incorrect because bone scans show inflammatory activity but have poor resolution and cannot reliably determine avascular necrosis. Option E is incorrect because ultrasonography can diagnose acute fractures but cannot assess bone vascularity.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old child with congenital right facial paralysis is evaluated for potential facial reanimation. MRI demonstrates absent right facial nerve trunk. A two-stage cross-facial nerve grafting approach is proposed, utilizing a sural nerve graft connected to a buccal branch of the facial nerve with 10-0 nylon sutures. Which factor will most significantly impact the success of this procedure?
A) Patient's advanced age
B) Donor nerve axon count
C) Length of paralysis
D) Obturator nerve pedicle length
E) Nerve repair technique
questions.answer:
B)
Recent studies demonstrate that donor nerve axonal density is the most critical factor determining outcomes in cross-facial nerve grafting procedures, making option B correct. Option A is incorrect because while age affects outcomes in adults, there is no evidence that age significantly impacts results in children under 10 years. Option C is incorrect because in congenital facial nerve agenesis, paralysis duration is irrelevant since the facial muscles are absent or fibrotic from birth, unlike acquired injuries. Option D is incorrect because obturator nerve pedicle length does not influence the nerve grafting outcome. Option E is incorrect because the method of nerve coaptation, while important for technical success, does not have the greatest influence on functional outcomes compared to axonal density.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female patient comes to the office following Mohs micrographic surgery for a basal cell carcinoma located on the mid-cheek. The resulting defect measures 4 cm and extends to the left eyelid-cheek junction. Which of the following represents the best approach for closing this defect?
A) Cheek neck rotation flap
B) Lateral thigh flap
C) Radial forearm free flap
D) Split-thickness skin grafting
E) Xenografting
questions.answer:
A)
The cheek neck rotation flap is the optimal choice for this reconstruction. Mohs surgery typically creates margin-free defects that require careful reconstruction, often by plastic surgeons after dermatologist referral. Large cheek defects near the lower eyelid pose significant risk for ectropion development. The rotation flap technique, extending through the lateral canthus into preauricular and cervical regions, provides excellent tissue mobilization for closing substantial defects while maintaining proper eyelid position. B) is incorrect because lateral thigh flaps provide suboptimal color matching and excessive bulk for facial reconstruction. C) is incorrect because radial forearm free flaps, while useful in head and neck reconstruction, offer poor color match and unnecessary complexity for this defect. D) is incorrect because split-thickness skin grafts have high contracture risk leading to ectropion in this location. E) is incorrect because xenografts carry unacceptable risks of rejection and cicatricial ectropion.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old female patient arrives at the emergency department following a bicycle accident involving a motor vehicle, resulting in a 6-8 cm soft-tissue defect overlying the tibial tuberosity. Clinical examination reveals bone exposure in the proximal third of the lower leg. Which of the following muscle flaps would be most suitable for this patient?
A) Lateral gastrocnemius
B) Lateral soleus
C) Medial gastrocnemius
D) Medial soleus
E) Sartorius
questions.answer:
C)
The medial gastrocnemius flap is the most appropriate choice for covering proximal third tibial defects with bone exposure. This muscle originates from the medial femoral condyle and has longer muscular fibers extending more inferiorly than its lateral counterpart. It can be harvested while preserving plantar flexion function if the soleus remains intact, making it ideal for coverage of the tibial tuberosity region. A) is incorrect because the lateral gastrocnemius head is shorter and carries risk of footdrop when used alone. B) and D) are incorrect because soleus flaps are better suited for middle and distal third tibial defects rather than proximal coverage. E) is incorrect because the sartorius has limited arc of rotation due to its Type IV segmental blood supply and is primarily indicated for femoral vessel coverage.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old male patient arrives at the emergency department following a canine bite injury to his face. Clinical examination reveals near-complete loss of the nose and glabella region. A multi-stage reconstruction using a forearm flap is planned, beginning with flap elevation, cartilage graft placement, and nostril formation. The second stage involves flap thinning, refinement, and additional cartilage grafting. The third stage consists of microsurgical flap transfer for nasal reconstruction. Which of the following best characterizes this type of flap?
A) Delayed
B) Freestyle
C) Prefabricated
D) Prelaminated
E) Tubularized
questions.answer:
D)
This describes a prelaminated flap, which is an axial flap that undergoes modification through addition of various tissue grafts (skin, mucosa, cartilage, or bone) to recreate the missing anatomical structures at the donor site before transfer. The staged approach with cartilage grafting and structural modification prior to final transfer is characteristic of prelamination. A) is incorrect because delayed flaps involve vascular compromise procedures to enhance circulation, not structural modification. B) is incorrect because freestyle flaps are harvested based on Doppler-identified perforators without predetermined anatomy. C) is incorrect because prefabricated flaps involve transferring a vascular pedicle into tissue to induce neovascularization. E) is incorrect because tubularized flaps are formed into conduits for reconstruction of hollow structures like the pharynx or esophagus.

questions.question:
Which of the following represents the most probable long-term consequence of radiation therapy following mastectomy?
A) Desquamation
B) Dyspigmentation
C) Edema
D) Erythema
E) Ulceration
questions.answer:
B)
Dyspigmentation is the most characteristic chronic effect of post-mastectomy radiation therapy. Radiation-induced tissue damage manifests in two phases: acute and chronic. Chronic changes include skin atrophy, dryness, telangiectasia, dyspigmentation, and dyschromia, along with progressive fibrosis of skin and subcutaneous tissues that can develop over months to years. This fibrosis can result in pain and arm movement restriction. A) is incorrect because desquamation is an acute radiation effect occurring during treatment. C) is incorrect because edema is typically an acute manifestation rather than a chronic consequence. D) is incorrect because erythema represents acute radiation dermatitis seen in over 85% of patients during treatment. E) is incorrect because ulceration is an acute severe reaction, not a typical chronic effect.

questions.question:
Which of the following muscles is utilized to create the sphincter mechanism in sphincter pharyngoplasty for treating velopharyngeal insufficiency?
A) Levator veli palatini
B) Musculus uvulae
C) Palatopharyngeus
D) Superior constrictor
E) Tensor veli palatini
questions.answer:
C)
The palatopharyngeus muscle, contained within the posterior tonsillar pillar, is the muscle used to construct the sphincter in sphincter pharyngoplasty. The surgical technique involves elevating the posterior tonsillar pillar from inferior to superior, rotating it 90 degrees medially while maintaining superior pedicle blood supply, and suturing it into a horizontal incision on the posterior pharyngeal wall at the adenoid pad level. A) is incorrect because the levator veli palatini functions as the primary velar elevator, positioned horizontally within the soft palate for velopharyngeal closure. B) is incorrect because the musculi uvulae provide velar stiffness modification as paired midline structures ending in the uvula. D) is incorrect because the superior constrictor is used in posterior pharyngeal flap procedures, not sphincter pharyngoplasty. E) is incorrect because the tensor veli palatini forms the tensor aponeurosis connecting the soft palate to hard palate via the hamulus.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a canine bite injury to his nasal tip. His medical history is significant for high blood pressure. Examination reveals a 3-cm tissue loss affecting 80% of the nasal tip area. Besides removing the remaining nasal tip tissue, which reconstructive approach would most likely yield the best cosmetic result?
A) Partial-thickness skin graft
B) Complete-thickness skin graft
C) Dorsal nasal flap
D) Nasolabial flap
E) Forehead flap
questions.answer:
E)
The forehead flap represents the optimal reconstructive choice for this extensive nasal tip defect. According to aesthetic reconstruction principles established by Burget and colleagues, when more than 50% of a nasal subunit is damaged, complete subunit removal and reconstruction provides superior aesthetic outcomes by avoiding conspicuous scars directly on the nasal tip. A) Partial-thickness skin grafts are incorrect because they contract significantly and create color/texture mismatches. B) Complete-thickness skin grafts are incorrect as they still result in visible color and quality differences compared to native nasal skin. C) Dorsal nasal flaps are incorrect because they are limited to defects of 1.5-2 cm maximum. D) Nasolabial flaps are incorrect as they typically cannot reach across the midline for central tip reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old male arrives at the emergency department 3 hours following complete amputation of his right forearm at the mid-level during an industrial accident at a paper facility. A tourniquet was applied at the accident site. His vital signs are stable with no other injuries present. What is the most appropriate handling of the severed limb until blood vessel reconnections are finished?
A) Clamp the distal blood vessels
B) Cool the severed extremity
C) Flush the artery with clot-dissolving agents
D) Submerge in saline solution
E) Create fasciotomy incisions
questions.answer:
B)
Cooling the amputated limb until vascular reconnection is the correct management approach. Hypothermia extends the safe ischemia time from 6 hours (warm) to 10-12 hours (cold), which is crucial for successful replantation. A) Clamping distal vessels is incorrect because it damages the vessels needed for microsurgical anastomoses. C) Flushing with thrombolytics is incorrect as this is not routinely done unless thrombi are present. D) Simple saline immersion is incorrect as it doesn't provide the necessary cooling or appropriate solution composition. E) Fasciotomies are incorrect as they should not delay reperfusion and are performed after vascular anastomoses to prevent compartment syndrome.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old girl is evaluated 2 months after a failed scalp replantation because of an avulsion injury. Skin grafting is planned, followed by staged tissue expansion. Photographs are shown. Between which of the following layers of the scalp is the most appropriate anatomic plane for tissue expander placement?


A) Skin and galea
B) Galea and temporalis muscle
C) Temporalis muscle and pericranium
D) Pericranium and cranium
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.




Layers of the scalp can be easily remembered using the mnemonic SCALP: S (skin), C (subcutaneous), A (galea aponeurotica), L (loose areolar), and P (pericranium). The skin is quite thick and densely adherent to the subcutaneous layer, which contains the vessels and nerves that travel just above the galea. The galea aponeurotica is continuous with extensions of the superficial muscular aponeurotic system: the frontalis anteriorly, the occipitalis posteriorly, and the temporoparietal fascia (superficial temporal fascia) laterally. The loose areolar plane is quite mobile and dissects very easily. As a result, most avulsions occur within this plane. The pericranium is densely attached to the skull and is contiguous laterally with the deep temporal fascia. The temporalis muscle lies below this layer and attaches directly to the temporal bone.


Tissue expanders should be placed under the galea/superficial muscular aponeurotic system layer to provide maximal tissue coverage and to protect and optimize the blood supply to the expanded skin. Placement in the subcutaneous plane would require a difficult, tedious dissection and would result in a thin, poorly perfused flap. Conversely, placement of the expander under the pericranium is unnecessary and would result in a painful, difficult, and unpredictable expansion. There is no clinical indication to place a tissue expander under the temporalis muscle.


References
Leedy JE, Janis JE, Rohrich RJ. Reconstruction of Acquired Scalp Defects: An Algorithmic Approach. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2005;116(4):54e-72e.
Argenta LC, Marks MW. Principles of Tissue Expansion. In: Mathes SJ, ed. Plastic Surgery. 2nd Edition. Philadelphia, PA: Saunders/Elsevier; 2006;1:548-551.
Wei FC, Dayan JH. Scalp, Skull, Orbit, and Maxilla Reconstruction and Hair Transplantation. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2013;131(3):411e-424e.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old male is scheduled for surgical treatment of severe grade IV gynecomastia. Physical examination shows the nipple-to-sternal notch distance measures 25 cm, and the inframammary fold sits 4 cm below the lower pectoral margin. The surgical plan includes mastectomy with free nipple transplantation. What represents the optimal shape and positioning for the reconstructed nipple-areolar complex?
A) Elliptical; positioned at the fourth-to-fifth rib space junction
B) Elliptical; positioned 20 cm from the midclavicle
C) Elliptical; positioned 25 cm from the sternal notch
D) Circular; positioned 25 cm from the sternal notch
E) Circular; positioned at the fourth-to-fifth rib space junction
questions.answer:
A)
The optimal configuration is an elliptical nipple-areolar complex positioned at the fourth-to-fifth intercostal space. Studies of normal male anatomy show that 91% of men have oval-shaped nipple-areolar complexes, and 75% have their centers located at the fourth intercostal space. This creates the most natural masculine appearance. B) The 20 cm measurement from midclavicle is incorrect as this doesn't correspond to proper anatomical landmarks for nipple positioning. C) Positioning 25 cm from the sternal notch is incorrect as this would place the nipple too low. D) A circular shape is incorrect because only 9% of normal males have round nipple-areolar complexes, making it less natural appearing. E) While the intercostal positioning is correct, the circular shape remains inappropriate for masculine chest reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female presents for consultation regarding upper eyelid surgery and facelift procedures. She reports asymmetrical eyelid folds, with her right upper fold positioned higher than her left. She experiences visual obstruction from her right eye during fatigue. These symptoms have gradually worsened over 5 years. Her levator muscle function measures 11 mm with the brow and forehead muscles in resting position. This patient most likely demonstrates which category of eyelid drooping?
A) Age-related
B) Weight-induced
C) Muscle-related
D) Nerve-related
E) Injury-related
questions.answer:
A)
This patient exhibits age-related (involutional) ptosis, the most common form of eyelid drooping. The characteristic features include progressive onset over years, high eyelid crease (>7 mm), adequate levator function (>10 mm), and symptoms worsening with fatigue. B) Weight-induced (mechanical) ptosis is incorrect as there's no mention of masses, tumors, or edema causing the drooping. C) Muscle-related (myogenic) ptosis is incorrect because conditions like myasthenia gravis would typically present with poorer levator function and different clinical features. D) Nerve-related (neurogenic) ptosis is incorrect as there are no signs of oculomotor nerve palsy, Horner syndrome, or other neurological conditions. E) Injury-related (traumatic) ptosis is incorrect since there's no history of trauma or birth injury mentioned.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female with enlarged masseter muscles on both sides seeks treatment because she desires a more heart-shaped facial contour. Her bite alignment is otherwise normal. Which treatment approach would be most appropriate as the initial intervention for this patient?
A) Botulinum toxin type A injection of 30 to 50 units into the masseter muscle bulk
B) Surgical reduction of the deep masseter muscles through the mouth
C) Mandibular bone cutting with backward repositioning
D) Targeted nerve cutting to the masseter muscles
E) Orthodontic appliance therapy to reposition the teeth
questions.answer:
A)
Botulinum toxin type A injection represents the most appropriate initial treatment for masseter hypertrophy when seeking facial feminization. This non-surgical approach effectively reduces muscle bulk, narrows the lower face width, and creates the desired heart-shaped feminine facial contour with minimal risk and downtime. B) Surgical masseter reduction is incorrect as it carries significant surgical risks and should be reserved for cases where non-surgical treatment fails. C) Mandibular osteotomy is incorrect as it's an extensive procedure with major morbidity that's not indicated for isolated masseter hypertrophy. D) Selective denervation is incorrect because it's a more invasive procedure with potential complications that's not first-line treatment. E) Orthodontic treatment is incorrect since the patient has normal occlusion and the issue is muscle hypertrophy, not dental alignment.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male presents 72 hours following an assault with a nondisplaced, minimally angulated right mandibular angle fracture that is not comminuted. The plastic surgeon intends to proceed with open reduction and internal fixation. Which of the following variables most significantly increases this patient's risk for postoperative complications?
A) Perioperative ampicillin-sulbactam therapy
B) Use of two mini-plates for fixation
C) Postoperative intermaxillary fixation
D) Patient gender
E) Delay to surgical treatment
questions.answer:
B)
Multiple research studies have demonstrated that single plate fixation along either the oblique ridge or lateral cortex results in the lowest complication rates for this fracture pattern. The use of two mini-plates has been specifically linked to higher postoperative complication rates. A is incorrect because perioperative ampicillin-sulbactam has been proven to reduce complications in this patient group. C is incorrect because postoperative intermaxillary fixation does not affect complication rates. D is incorrect because patient gender has not been shown to influence complication rates. E is incorrect because timing of surgical intervention has not been demonstrated to increase complications.

questions.question:
From which cellular origin do lactiferous ducts develop during human embryonic development?
A) Endodermal cells
B) Epithelial cells
C) Mesenchymal cells
D) Neural crest cells
E) Pluripotent cells
questions.answer:
B)
By 6 weeks of gestation, specific regions of epithelial cell proliferation appear on the ventral chest wall. These regions develop into buds that subsequently hollow out and form secondary buds, which eventually become the lactiferous duct system. A is incorrect because endodermal cells form the digestive tract lining and contribute to liver and pancreatic development, not breast tissue. C is incorrect because mesenchymal cells, derived from mesoderm, surround the ducts and form the breast stroma including smooth muscle, capillary endothelium, and fat cells. D is incorrect because neural crest cells produce pigment cells and other structures but do not participate in breast embryogenesis. E is incorrect because pluripotent cells do not form either the parenchymal or stromal components of the developing breast.

questions.question:
A 69-year-old male arrives at the emergency department with sudden onset of severe left forearm pain and a cold, pale, pulseless left hand. His medical history is significant for atrial fibrillation and steroid-dependent chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Physical examination and Doppler ultrasound findings are consistent with acute occlusion of the left ulnar artery. Besides aspirin, which of the following treatments should be initiated immediately while evaluating the patient's surgical candidacy?
A) Apixaban
B) Clopidogrel
C) Heparin
D) Recombinant tPA
E) Verapamil
questions.answer:
C)
Heparin should be administered immediately along with aspirin to prevent further clot propagation and arterial occlusion while the patient is being evaluated. This represents the standard first-line approach to prevent additional tissue damage. A is incorrect because apixaban is an oral anticoagulant that would not provide immediate anticoagulation in this acute setting. B is incorrect because clopidogrel is an antiplatelet agent that would not provide adequate immediate anticoagulation. D is incorrect because while tPA may be used for thrombolysis, it carries higher risks of bleeding and distal embolization compared to initial anticoagulation. E is incorrect because verapamil is a calcium channel blocker that has not been proven beneficial for tissue salvage in acute arterial occlusion.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old female presents with a 12-mm firm nodule on her right cheek that has been slowly enlarging over 2 months. The lesion is mildly painful, has a slight blue tint, and shows no erythema, ulceration, or visible pore opening. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Hemangioma
B) Keratinous cyst
C) Pilomatricoma
D) Sebaceous nevus
E) Spitz nevus
questions.answer:
C)
Pilomatricoma (pilomatrixoma or calcifying epithelioma of Malherbe) is a benign calcifying tumor of hair follicle structures that predominantly affects individuals under 20 years of age. It commonly occurs in the head and neck region and presents as described. The absence of a punctum distinguishes it from cystic lesions. A is incorrect because hemangiomas are bright red or purple vascular proliferations that are typically present at birth and more superficial. B is incorrect because keratinous cysts have a discrete capsule and often a visible punctum, which this lesion lacks. D is incorrect because sebaceous nevi present as waxy patches often present at birth, typically on the scalp. E is incorrect because Spitz nevi are melanocytic lesions that appear as dark brown or black macules on the skin surface.

questions.question:
For which cosmetic application have both onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox Cosmetic) and abobotulinumtoxinA (Dysport) received US Food and Drug Administration approval?
A) Cervical dystonia
B) Forehead wrinkles
C) Glabellar wrinkles
D) Vertical lip lines
questions.answer:
C)
Both onabotulinumtoxinA and abobotulinumtoxinA have received FDA approval specifically for the temporary improvement of moderate to severe glabellar lines as their sole cosmetic indication. All other cosmetic applications are considered off-label uses. A is incorrect because cervical dystonia is a medical, not cosmetic, indication and rimabotulinumtoxinB is the only botulinum toxin approved specifically for this condition. B is incorrect because forehead wrinkles do not have FDA approval for either product as a cosmetic indication. D is incorrect because vertical lip lines are not an FDA-approved cosmetic indication for these products.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old female patient presents for surgical correction of congenital unilateral left upper eyelid drooping. Examination reveals moderate left levator muscle function measuring 8 mm. Which of the following surgical approaches is most suitable for treating this child's ptosis?
A) Fasanella-Servat technique involving excision of tarsal plate, conjunctiva, and Müller muscle
B) Frontalis muscle flap transfer
C) Frontalis suspension using autologous fascia lata
D) Müller muscle-conjunctival excision
E) Levator aponeurosis resection and advancement
questions.answer:
E)
Levator aponeurosis resection and advancement is the most suitable surgical approach for this child's congenital ptosis. This technique is indicated for patients with levator function exceeding 5 mm, and this child demonstrates 8 mm of levator function, making her an ideal candidate for this procedure. A) is incorrect because the Fasanella-Servat technique is designed for minimal ptosis correction and can adversely affect eyelid contour. B) is incorrect because frontalis muscle flap procedures are reserved for severe ptosis cases with levator function below 4 mm. C) is incorrect because frontalis suspension procedures are typically used for patients with poor levator function or congenital Marcus Gunn jaw-winking syndrome. D) is incorrect because Müller muscle-conjunctival resection is recommended for patients with good levator function but doesn't allow intraoperative adjustment of eyelid height, which is crucial for achieving symmetry in unilateral cases.

questions.question:
A 49-year-old female patient is planning to have breast augmentation surgery with silicone implants placed beneath the breast tissue. During preoperative counseling, she inquires about potential complications comparing silicone versus saline implants. Which of the following represents a drawback of silicone implants for this patient?
A) Rupture causes an immediate visible reduction in breast volume
B) Increased risk of developing invasive breast malignancy
C) Interference with breast tissue visualization during mammographic screening
D) Greater tendency toward visible rippling effects
questions.answer:
C)
Silicone implants can interfere with breast tissue visualization during mammographic screening because they are radiopaque on mammography. When positioned beneath the breast tissue (subglandular), they may obscure a small portion of breast tissue during imaging. A) is incorrect because silicone implant ruptures often remain contained within the capsule and may not cause obvious size changes, unlike saline implants which are absorbed by the body causing visible deflation. B) is incorrect because silicone implants have not been shown to increase the likelihood of developing breast cancer. D) is incorrect because silicone implants actually demonstrate less superior pole rippling compared to saline implants.

questions.question:
Which of the following embryological structures is responsible for forming the tragus?
A) First pharyngeal arch
B) First pharyngeal cleft
C) Second pharyngeal arch
D) Second pharyngeal cleft
questions.answer:
A)
The first pharyngeal arch is responsible for forming the tragus and the anterior portion of the helix. B) is incorrect because the first pharyngeal cleft develops into the external auditory canal, not the tragus. C) is incorrect because the second pharyngeal arch forms the majority of the external ear structures including the antitragus, remaining helix, antihelix, and crura. D) is incorrect because the second pharyngeal cleft normally disappears during development, though it may occasionally persist as a second branchial cleft cyst.

questions.question:
A doctor is evaluating various settings for performing a particular medical intervention. Based on Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services guidelines, performing this intervention in which of the following locations would yield the highest relative value units?
A) Ambulatory surgery center
B) Community mental health facility
C) Hospital inpatient setting
D) Hospital outpatient department
E) Private physician office
questions.answer:
E)
A private physician office setting yields the highest relative value units (RVUs) for a given medical intervention according to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services fee schedules. This occurs because office-based services receive higher Practice Expense RVUs compared to facility-based settings, as the physician's practice bears the costs of clinical staff, equipment, and supplies. A) is incorrect because ambulatory surgery centers are considered facility settings with lower Practice Expense RVUs. B) is incorrect because community mental health facilities are facility settings that receive reduced Practice Expense RVUs. C) is incorrect because hospital inpatient settings are facilities where the hospital, not the physician's practice, incurs the overhead costs. D) is incorrect because hospital outpatient departments are facility-based settings that receive lower Practice Expense RVU allocations.

questions.question:
A plastic surgery trainee is conducting research involving retrospective analysis of breast cancer patients who received immediate tissue expander reconstruction over the previous decade and later underwent radiotherapy. When gathering this information under Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) regulations, which of the following patient identifiers may be collected without obtaining patient authorization?
A) Patient age
B) Electronic mail address
C) Hospital record number
D) Patient full name
E) Contact phone number
questions.answer:
A)
Patient age (excluding birth date) may be collected without patient authorization under HIPAA regulations as it is not considered a protected health identifier when used alone for retrospective research purposes. B) is incorrect because electronic mail addresses are specifically listed as protected identifiers that must be removed for de-identification. C) is incorrect because hospital record numbers are protected identifiers that require removal or patient consent for research use. D) is incorrect because patient names are primary protected identifiers that must be stripped from records or require authorization. E) is incorrect because telephone numbers are explicitly listed as protected identifiers under HIPAA de-identification requirements.

questions.question:
For patients who maintain their posterior vertical height, what is the most suitable duration of maxillomandibular fixation (MMF) when treating minimally displaced bilateral subcondylar mandibular fractures?
A) 1 week
B) 4 weeks
C) 8 weeks
D) None; use gunning splint to stabilize mandible for 8 weeks
E) None; manage patient with soft diet only
questions.answer:
B)

The appropriate treatment duration is 4 weeks of MMF for minimally displaced bilateral subcondylar fractures in patients without loss of posterior vertical height. For nondisplaced or minimally displaced fractures with functional occlusion, 4 to 6 weeks of MMF followed by 2 to 3 weeks of guiding elastics provides optimal fracture union without increasing ankylosis risk. A) 1 week is insufficient time for adequate bone healing and union. C) 8 weeks is excessive and may lead to masseter muscle shortening and joint stiffness from prolonged immobilization. D) Gunning splints are primarily used for edentulous patients and do not provide functional MMF. E) Soft diet alone would be inadequate for bilateral instability and could result in malocclusion due to the unstable fracture pattern.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old woman underwent delayed microsurgical breast reconstruction. Two hours postoperatively, she develops breast swelling and increased drainage. Bedside examination reveals a purple-colored flap with 1-second capillary refill. Vital signs show heart rate 70 bpm, blood pressure 110/60 mmHg, and hematocrit 28%. Handheld Doppler detects an arterial signal in the skin paddle. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Apply nitroglycerin paste
B) Return to operating room for exploration
C) Perform flap pinprick test
D) Apply medicinal leeches
E) Administer streptokinase therapy
questions.answer:
B)

Immediate operative reexploration is indicated for this patient with venous insufficiency following microsurgery. The purple discoloration, rapid capillary refill, swelling, and increased drainage with preserved arterial flow are classic signs of venous thrombosis.
