Early reexploration significantly improves flap salvage rates, with most microvascular complications occurring within 48 hours and being primarily venous in nature. A) Nitroglycerin paste may help pedicled flaps but does not replace the need for microsurgical reexploration. C) Pinprick testing and suture release are temporizing measures that don't address the underlying vascular compromise. D) Leeches are a salvage option used when intraoperative interventions fail. E) Streptokinase should only be considered during reexploration if clots are identified within the vascular system.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male with unrepaired submucous cleft palate underwent Le Fort I surgery 3 months ago. His parents note speech clarity problems since surgery. Nasometry confirms hypernasal speech patterns. Which finding would indicate the need for a pharyngeal flap rather than Furlow palatoplasty or sphincter pharyngoplasty?
A) 10 mm Le Fort I advancement
B) Reduced lateral wall movement on nasopharyngoscopy
C) 25 mm postoperative nasopharyngeal depth
D) 32 mm preoperative soft palate length
E) 12 mm velopharyngeal gap during maximum phonation
questions.answer:
E)

A velopharyngeal gap exceeding 5 mm during maximum phonation requires pharyngeal flap reconstruction, as gaps larger than this cannot be adequately addressed with Furlow palatoplasty or sphincter pharyngoplasty. The 12 mm gap described is significantly beyond the threshold for these alternative procedures. A) Le Fort I advancement distance does not directly correlate with specific procedure selection. B) Poor lateral wall motion would actually favor sphincter pharyngoplasty over pharyngeal flap. C) A 25 mm nasopharyngeal depth is within normal range for a 17-year-old (normal is 24 mm). D) A 32 mm soft palate length represents normal dimensions for this age group.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old woman seeks body contouring after gastric bypass surgery 2 years prior. She has redundant skin on arms, thighs, breasts, and abdomen. Plans include circumferential body lift and mastopexy with barbed sutures for dermal closure. What advantage do running barbed sutures offer over conventional interrupted suture methods in this case?
A) Reduced major postoperative complications
B) Shortened operative time
C) Enhanced scar appearance
D) Superior scar tensile strength
questions.answer:
B)

Barbed sutures provide the primary advantage of reduced operative time compared to traditional interrupted suture techniques. Multiple studies demonstrate decreased surgical duration and improved surgeon satisfaction with barbed suture use. While the suture material itself costs more, overall cost savings result from shorter operative times. A) Major complication rates are similar between techniques, though barbed sutures may have slightly higher rates of suture extrusion and minor wound healing issues. C) Studies show equivalent scar aesthetics between barbed and traditional sutures. D) No significant differences in scar tensile strength have been demonstrated between the two techniques.

questions.question:
What characteristic do cancellous bone grafts exhibit when compared to cortical bone grafts?
A) Superior osteogenic capacity
B) Greater density with delayed resorption
C) Enhanced structural stability
D) Minimal osteoblast and osteocyte concentrations
E) Limited osteoinductive properties
questions.answer:
A)

Cancellous bone grafts demonstrate superior osteogenic capacity compared to cortical bone grafts due to their high concentrations of osteoblasts and osteocytes. This cellular richness makes cancellous bone the most commonly used autologous graft and gives it excellent healing properties. B) Cortical bone is denser with slower resorption, while cancellous bone is less dense and resorbs more quickly. C) Cortical bone provides greater structural support due to its dense, organized structure. D) Cancellous bone contains high concentrations of osteoblasts and osteocytes, not low concentrations. E) Cancellous bone has excellent osteoinductive potential, not poor potential.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male presents to the clinic with a 6 to 8-cm open forearm wound. The wound displays healthy granulation tissue without signs of infection. What is a benefit of using split-thickness skin grafts compared to full-thickness skin grafts for this patient?
A) Reduced metabolic requirements from the recipient bed
B) Decreased secondary contracture from elastin components
C) Increased primary contracture from myofibroblast cells
D) Inosculation occurring prior to plasmatic imbibition
E) Intact skin appendages present within the graft
questions.answer:
A)
Split-thickness skin grafts have reduced metabolic requirements from the recipient bed compared to full-thickness skin grafts. When the wound bed cannot provide sufficient nutrient diffusion through the graft, full-thickness grafts may develop superficial epidermolysis. B is incorrect because split-thickness grafts actually have more secondary contraction, not less. C is incorrect because primary contracture comes from elastin fibers, not myofibroblasts, and split-thickness grafts have less primary contraction. D is incorrect because plasmatic imbibition occurs before inosculation in the normal healing sequence. E is incorrect because split-thickness grafts do not contain intact skin appendages, whereas full-thickness grafts do.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female visits the office seeking eyebrow reconstruction consultation. She describes compulsively plucking her eyebrows multiple times daily due to perceived asymmetry, resulting in complete eyebrow loss. She demands hair transplantation and reports feeling depressed about her missing eyebrows. What is the most probable DSM-5 diagnosis?
A) Body dysmorphic disorder
B) Borderline personality disorder
C) Excoriation (skin-picking) disorder
D) Major depressive disorder
E) Trichotillomania
questions.answer:
A)
Body dysmorphic disorder is classified as an obsessive-compulsive and related disorder in DSM-5, characterized by preoccupation with perceived appearance defects, repetitive behaviors related to this preoccupation, and significant distress. The underlying motivation is appearance-based symmetry concerns, distinguishing it from other conditions. B is incorrect because borderline personality disorder involves unstable emotional responses and relationships, not appearance preoccupation. C is incorrect because excoriation disorder involves skin picking without the appearance-based motivation. D is incorrect because while depression may coexist, it lacks the appearance preoccupation criterion. E is incorrect because trichotillomania involves hair pulling but often includes pleasurable sensations rather than appearance-based concerns.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old woman undergoes abdominoperineal resection secondary to aggressive rectal cancer. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy have been performed. Surgical examination shows defect of the anus, rectum, and posterior vaginal wall. An intraoperative photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate reconstructive option in this patient?


A) Bilateral Singapore (pudendal thigh) flaps
B) Gracilis muscle flap
C) Omental flap
D) Rectus femoris flap
E) Vertical rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


As the treatment of anorectal cancers has shifted to more sphincter-preserving surgeries and radiochemotherapy, the need for abdominoperineal resection (APR) has decreased. However, in cases of locally persistent disease, involvement of nearby structures (vagina), or recurrent disease, there is an increased rate of survival and improved quality of life with pelvic extirpation. These cases typically result in problematic wounds secondary to previous radiation therapy, with complication rates as increased as 60%. Complications include delayed wound healing, infection, internal hernia, chronic sinus formation, and the psychological and physical concerns associated with vaginal resection in the female patient. In an effort to minimize these complications and restore sexual function in the female patient, musculocutaneous flap reconstruction is recommended.


In the patient described, the most appropriate option for reconstruction is the vertical rectus abdominis musculocutaneous (VRAM) flap.





The advantages of the rectus flap include an excellent and safe pedicle (Mathes/Nahai Type III flap), rapid technique, abundant well-vascularized tissue, wide arc of rotation, acceptable donor-site morbidity, and ease of access in relation to the APR procedure. The well-vascularized bulky tissue is effective in obliterating the pelvic dead space, minimizes the risk of internal herniation of the abdominal contents, and provides healthy tissue in the event of suture line dehiscence allowing more rapid healing by secondary intention if necessary. The disadvantages of the VRAM include lack of sensation in the vagina/perineum, loss of secretory function that may result in dyspareunia, abdominal weakness/hernia, and unsightly bulk in the perineum that may require a secondary debulking procedure for aesthetic improvement. In the patient described, the decision was made to close the perineal skin over the de-epithelialized flap. Another patient is shown below with a perineal skin paddle.






Primary closure is inappropriate secondary to the increased rate of complications and poor sexual function without reconstruction as noted above. Bilateral pudendal thigh (Singapore) flaps are a great option for vaginal or labial reconstruction in the congenital or ablative setting when there is not a need for a large volume of tissue. In this case, the flaps are not an option because of the need for bulky tissue, previous radiation therapy administered to the base of the flaps, and transection of the flap‚Äos blood supply (posterior labial artery). The extended groin flap is inappropriate for the same reason.


A skin graft is not likely to be successful, given the patient's radiation history and violation of the rectum.


References
1. Pusic AL, Mehrara BJ. Vaginal reconstruction: an algorithm approach to defect classification and flap reconstruction. J Surg Oncol. 2006 Nov 1;94:515-521.
2. Bell SW, Dehni N, Chaouat M, et al. Primary rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap for repair of perineal and vaginal defects after extended abdominoperineal resection. Br J Surg. 2005 Apr;92(4):482-486.
3. Buchel EW, Finical S, Johnson C. Pelvic reconstruction using vertical rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flaps. Ann Plast Surg. 2004 Jan;52(1):22-26.
4. Tei TM, Stolzenburg T, Buntzen S, et al. Use of transpelvic rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap for anal cancer salvage surgery. Br J Surg. 2003 May;90(5):575-580.
5. Wee JTK, Joseph VT. A new technique of vaginal reconstruction using neurovascular pudendal-thigh flaps: a preliminary report. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1989 Apr;83(4):701-709.
6. Cordeiro PG, Pusic AL, Disa JJ. A classification system and reconstructive algorithm for acquired vaginal defects. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2002 Sep 15;110(4):1058-1065.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female undergoes evaluation for central abdominal lipodystrophy with loose skin. She seeks volume reduction and skin laxity improvement. Superficial abdominal liposuction is planned. What postoperative complication is most probable for this patient?
A) Contour irregularities
B) Hyperpigmentation
C) Infection
D) Seroma
E) Skin necrosis
questions.answer:
A)
Contour irregularities are the most frequent complication following superficial liposuction. This occurs because superficial liposuction targets the dense, compact superficial adipose layer located 1-2 mm below the dermis, disrupting extensive septations. B is incorrect because hyperpigmentation is a less common complication. C is incorrect because infection occurs less frequently than contour irregularities. D is incorrect because seroma formation is less common than contour problems. E is incorrect because skin necrosis is among the less frequent complications of superficial liposuction.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old female seeks consultation for facial rejuvenation including eyelid and perioral areas. Her history and examination reveal dry eyes, dry mouth, and joint issues. What test should be performed next to confirm her diagnosis?
A) Hand radiographic imaging
B) Lip biopsy
C) Schirmer test
D) Serum antibody marker
E) Stimulated salivary flow rates
questions.answer:
D)
Serum antibody markers (anti-SSA/Ro and anti-SSB/La) are present in 60-80% of Sjögren syndrome patients and are considered diagnostic when present, making this the most appropriate next step. A is incorrect because hand x-rays show nonspecific arthritis changes that don't establish the diagnosis. B is incorrect because while lip biopsy is diagnostic, it's more invasive and not the appropriate next step. C is incorrect because Schirmer tests are less reliable in elderly patients due to age-related decreased tear production. E is incorrect because salivary flow rates also decline with age and are less predictable for diagnosis.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old male seeks consultation for a 1.5-cm lower lip and commissure squamous cell carcinoma without regional or distant spread. He selects radiation therapy with 5000 cGy delivered over six weeks. What percentage best describes the likelihood of achieving a disease-free outcome with this treatment?
A) 35%
B) 50%
C) 65%
D) 80%
E) 95%
questions.answer:
E)
Radiation therapy for lip cancer up to 2 cm achieves cure rates of 90-95%, comparable to surgical excision success rates. This high effectiveness makes radiation an excellent treatment option for appropriately sized lesions. A is incorrect because 35% represents cure rates for much larger T3-T4 lesions with nodal involvement. B is incorrect because 50% is too low for small lip cancers treated with radiation. C is incorrect because 65% underestimates the effectiveness for this tumor size. D is incorrect because 80% represents cure rates for larger T2 lesions, not the smaller lesion described.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old male patient presents with digital clubbing affecting all fingers on both hands. His medical background includes cyanotic congenital cardiac disease. What is the most probable etiology of the abnormal nail appearance in this case?
A) Enlargement of the terminal phalanx
B) Excessive nail keratin growth
C) Proliferation of vascular connective tissue
D) Decreased collagen in the fingertip
E) Tendon sheath enlargement
questions.answer:
C)
Digital clubbing results from proliferation of vascular connective tissue in the fingertips. This condition has been documented since ancient times and occurs with various systemic diseases including cardiac, pulmonary, malignant, thyroid, and gastrointestinal disorders. The pathophysiology involves increased vascular connective tissue causing the characteristic appearance, including the profile sign where the nail angle exceeds 180 degrees. A is incorrect because the distal phalanx bone structure remains unchanged in clubbing. B is incorrect because nail keratin deposition is not responsible for the altered nail shape. D is incorrect because collagen actually increases with chronic clubbing rather than decreases. E is incorrect because tenosynovial tissue is not involved in the clubbing process.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old male visits the clinic due to dissatisfaction with his ear appearance. Examination reveals bilateral loss of antihelical folds, enlarged conchal bowls, and marked protrusion of the earlobes. Otoplasty is completed using a posterior approach with permanent sutures placed from the scaphal and helical sulcus cartilage to the mastoid fascia. Post-operatively, the patient is pleased with the upper and middle ear appearance but continues to have protruding earlobes. What is the most probable explanation?
A) Insufficient antitragus reduction
B) Insufficient cavum conchae reduction
C) Excessive tightening of scapha-mastoid sutures
D) Suturing triangular fossa to temporal fascia
questions.answer:
B)
Insufficient reduction of the cavum conchae is the most likely cause of persistent earlobe prominence. When the cartilage angle between the cavum conchae and antitragus remains too acute due to inadequate cavum conchae reduction, the hypertrophied cavum conchae continues to project the lower ear third, pushing the lobule outward. A is incorrect because the antitragus is not directly excised in standard otoplasty procedures. C is incorrect because overtightening scapha-mastoid sutures would create a 'pinned-back' appearance rather than lobule prominence. D is incorrect because suturing the triangular fossa to temporal fascia addresses upper ear prominence, not lobule issues.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old female child is brought for evaluation of a gradually expanding wrist mass. Her past medical history includes congenital cardiac disease requiring prolonged hospitalization as a newborn. Examination demonstrates a painless 3 × 3-cm mass on the radial-volar aspect. The overlying skin appears thin, and a palpable thrill is detected. What represents the most suitable management approach?
A) Corticosteroid injection into the lesion
B) Radial artery ligation
C) Interventional radiology referral for vascular ablation
D) Surgical excision with vein graft reconstruction
E) Conservative monitoring with annual evaluations
questions.answer:
D)
Surgical excision with vein graft reconstruction is the most appropriate management for this arteriovenous fistula. The clinical presentation (palpable thrill, thin overlying skin, history of prolonged hospitalization suggesting IV access complications) indicates an established arteriovenous fistula requiring surgical repair with vascular reconstruction. A is incorrect because this is not a hemangioma and corticosteroids would be inappropriate. B is incorrect because simple ligation would result in revascularization through collateral circulation. C is incorrect because vascular ablation is not suitable for this type of established fistula. E is incorrect because observation is inappropriate given the progressive growth and unstable overlying skin.

questions.question:
A 72-year-old male presents with a 2-cm, painless, fast-growing, purple-colored intradermal nodule on his cheek. His current medications include tacrolimus following kidney transplantation. Tissue biopsy reveals small, round, blue cells with enlarged prominent nuclei that are positive for cytokeratin 20 staining. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Non-pigmented melanoma
B) Basal cell carcinoma
C) Keratoacanthoma
D) Merkel cell carcinoma
E) Squamous cell carcinoma
questions.answer:
D)
Merkel cell carcinoma is the most likely diagnosis based on the clinical presentation and histologic findings. This aggressive cutaneous malignancy typically presents as rapidly growing, painless, violaceous nodules in sun-exposed areas of immunosuppressed or elderly patients. The characteristic small, round, blue cells with prominent nuclei that stain positive for cytokeratin 20 are pathognomonic for Merkel cell carcinoma. A is incorrect because melanoma cells stain positive for S100 and HMB-45, not cytokeratin 20. B is incorrect because basal cell carcinomas stain positive for Ber-EP4. C is incorrect because keratoacanthomas have different histologic characteristics and growth patterns. E is incorrect because squamous cell carcinomas stain positive for AE1/AE3.

questions.question:
A patient with complete traumatic brachial plexus root avulsion is scheduled for functioning free muscle transfer to restore both elbow flexion and finger flexion simultaneously, along with additional reconstructive procedures. Which muscle is most suitable for this application?
A) Gracilis
B) Pectoralis major
C) Rectus abdominis
D) Serratus anterior
E) Trapezius
questions.answer:
A)
The gracilis muscle is the most appropriate choice for free functioning muscle transfer in upper extremity reconstruction following brachial plexus injury. It is the most frequently used muscle for these reconstructions due to its favorable characteristics including good excursion, appropriate size, and adequate length, making it ideal for restoring both elbow and finger flexion. B is incorrect because while pectoralis major was historically described for this purpose, it is not commonly used in current practice. C is incorrect because rectus abdominis has not been established as a viable option for free functioning muscle transfer in upper extremity reconstruction. D is incorrect because serratus anterior is not described for this specific application. E is incorrect because trapezius is not used for free functioning muscle transfers in upper extremity reconstruction.

questions.question:
Which bone is most frequently involved in isolated orbital fractures?
A) Ethmoid
B) Frontal
C) Lacrimal
D) Maxillary
E) Zygomatic
questions.answer:
D)

The maxillary bone is most commonly affected in isolated orbital fractures because most of these injuries involve the orbital floor, which is predominantly composed of maxillary bone. This bone is particularly thin posterior to the infraorbital rim and is weakened by the infraorbital canal containing the infraorbital nerve. The majority of pure blowout fractures affect the orbital floor. A) Ethmoid is incorrect because while it contributes to the medial orbital wall, it is less commonly involved in isolated fractures. B) Frontal is incorrect as it forms the superior orbital rim and roof, which are stronger structures less prone to isolated fractures. C) Lacrimal is incorrect because it only forms a small portion of the medial orbital wall. E) Zygomatic is incorrect as it typically involves the lateral orbital wall and is more commonly fractured as part of complex facial injuries rather than isolated orbital fractures.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old man presents to the emergency department following a motor vehicle accident. Examination reveals a traumatic degloving injury to the dorsal right hand with exposed but intact extensor tendons. A fascial free flap with full-thickness skin grafting is planned for reconstruction. Which artery provides the blood supply to the most suitable flap choice?
A) Posterior auricular
B) Superficial temporal
C) Superior thyroid
D) Supratrochlear
E) Transverse facial
questions.answer:
B)

The superficial temporal artery provides blood supply to the temporoparietal fascial flap, which is the optimal choice for this reconstruction. This thin fascial free flap is ideal for reconstructing traumatic injuries where skin grafting alone is insufficient, particularly when covering exposed tendons or joints where gliding surfaces need to be restored. A) Posterior auricular is incorrect because this external carotid artery branch supplies the posterior ear region, not the temporoparietal fascia. C) Superior thyroid is incorrect as this external carotid branch supplies the thyroid gland and has no role in fascial flap reconstruction. D) Supratrochlear is incorrect because it supplies the forehead and scalp, not fascial flaps used for hand reconstruction. E) Transverse facial is incorrect as this superficial temporal artery branch supplies the parotid gland and is not the primary vessel for the temporoparietal fascial flap.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old man with bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome presents for elective surgery on his dominant right hand. This will be the surgeon's tenth case of the day. The surgeon prefers open technique and has completed 150 carpal tunnel procedures since completing hand fellowship 3 years ago. Which factor most significantly increases the risk of wrong-site surgery?
A) The elective nature of the procedure
B) Only one surgeon is involved in the operation
C) The procedure will be performed using an open technique
D) The surgeon has a high volume of cases scheduled for the same day
E) The surgeon has only been practicing independently for 3 years
questions.answer:
D)

High surgical case volume on the same day significantly increases wrong-site surgery risk due to time pressures and fatigue that can lead to system failures and communication breakdowns. Studies show a direct correlation between increasing surgical volumes and wrong-site surgery rates, with hand surgeons having four times higher rates than other specialties. A) Elective nature is incorrect because emergency cases actually increase wrong-site surgery risk, not elective procedures. B) Single surgeon involvement is incorrect as multiple surgeons involved in a case actually increases risk, not decreases it. C) Open technique is incorrect because surgical technique type does not significantly impact wrong-site surgery risk compared to volume pressures. E) Three years of independent practice is incorrect because studies show wrong-site surgery rates actually increase with surgeon age and experience, not decrease.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old woman undergoes hyaluronic acid gel filler injection for nasolabial fold enhancement. That evening, she contacts the surgeon reporting skin irritation on the left nasal side with discoloration, swelling, and numbness that developed hours after injection. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Evaluate the patient in person
B) Initiate treatment with an oral antihistamine
C) Initiate treatment with an oral benzodiazepine
D) Tell the patient to immediately apply ice
E) Reassurance
questions.answer:
A)

Immediate in-person evaluation is essential because these symptoms suggest impending tissue necrosis, the most serious early complication of soft-tissue fillers. This occurs from vascular compromise through direct vessel injury, compression, or obstruction by filler material. Early recognition and intervention are critical to minimize tissue death and deformity, requiring immediate assessment and potential treatments like warm compresses, nitroglycerin paste, and hyaluronidase injection. B) Oral antihistamine is incorrect because antihistamines do not address the underlying vascular compromise causing tissue ischemia. C) Oral benzodiazepine is incorrect as benzodiazepines do not treat the tissue ischemia that is causing the symptoms. D) Ice application is incorrect because cold would further compromise the already impaired blood flow to the affected area. E) Reassurance is incorrect because these symptoms indicate a potentially serious complication requiring immediate intervention, not reassurance.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old woman returns for follow-up 2 weeks after facelift surgery. Examination shows a 2 × 3-cm area of ischemic skin changes with central eschar formation in the right preauricular region. What is the most appropriate initial management?
A) Debridement of the eschar
B) Full-thickness skin grafting
C) Local wound care
D) Re-advancement of the flap
E) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
C)

Local wound care is the most appropriate initial management for post-rhytidectomy skin necrosis and wound healing complications. Conservative management often results in healing without adverse outcomes, with only some cases requiring corticosteroid injection or scar revision later. The eschar should be left intact as it functions as a natural biological dressing. A) Debridement is incorrect because removing the eschar eliminates its protective function as a biological dressing during the healing process. B) Full-thickness skin grafting is incorrect as it would only be considered for very extensive areas of full-thickness necrosis, not for initial management. D) Re-advancement of the flap is incorrect because it would create excessive tension on the closure at this early stage, though it might be considered later during scar revision once healing is complete. E) Split-thickness skin grafting is incorrect as conservative management should be attempted first, with grafting reserved for cases that fail to heal adequately.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male patient with spinal cord injury and chronic ischial pressure ulcer receives preoperative optimization including pressure relief and nutritional support. His medical background includes type 2 diabetes and chronic ischial osteomyelitis. Following comprehensive wound debridement and myocutaneous flap coverage with appropriate IV antibiotic treatment, he returns to clinic four months postoperatively with a new ulcer in the same area as the prior reconstruction. Which of the following factors most likely contributed to the recurrence of this ischial pressure ulcer?
A) Hemoglobin A1c exceeding 6%
B) Osteomyelitis
C) Patient's age
D) Prealbumin below 20 mg/dL
questions.answer:
A)
Poor diabetes control, demonstrated by Hemoglobin A1c above 6%, is a significant predictor of pressure ulcer recurrence. Inadequate glycemic management impairs wound healing and increases the risk of wound breakdown and early surgical revision. B is incorrect because osteomyelitis presence during surgery does not appear to influence recurrence rates. C is incorrect because younger age (under 45) actually predicts recurrence, while older age appears protective. D is incorrect because low prealbumin levels do not significantly contribute to recurrence in multivariate analysis models.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient presents for botulinum toxin type A treatment of glabellar lines. Twenty units total are administered, with 10 units injected into each corrugator muscle region. The patient returns 10 days later with left upper eyelid drooping. To help reduce this eyelid ptosis, alpha-adrenergic agonist eye drops can be administered to stimulate which of the following muscles?
A) Dilator pupillae
B) Frontalis
C) Levator palpebrae superioris
D) Müller
E) Orbicularis oculi
questions.answer:
D)
Alpha-adrenergic eye drops like apraclonidine or phenylephrine stimulate Müller muscle, an accessory eyelid elevator located beneath the levator palpebrae superioris. This sympathetically innervated smooth muscle can partially compensate for levator weakness caused by botulinum toxin, providing some improvement in ptosis until the toxin effect resolves. A is incorrect because dilator pupillae affects pupil size, not eyelid position. B is incorrect because frontalis muscle is not affected by these eye drops. C is incorrect because the levator palpebrae superioris is weakened by the botulinum toxin and cannot be stimulated by these drops. E is incorrect because orbicularis oculi is not responsive to alpha-adrenergic stimulation.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old female patient undergoes liposuction of the hips, abdomen, and lateral thighs using super-wet technique. Three liters of aspirate are removed. What is the most accurate estimate of the percentage of infiltrated fluid that remains in the patient's body following the procedure?
A) 10%
B) 30%
C) 50%
D) 70%
E) 90%
questions.answer:
D)
Approximately 70% of infiltrated fluid remains in the patient's body after liposuction and is absorbed systemically over time. This retained fluid becomes intravascular and must be considered in fluid management calculations to prevent complications like pulmonary edema. Understanding this retention is crucial for proper perioperative fluid management. A is incorrect because only 10% retention would mean nearly all infiltrate is removed, which is not accurate. B is incorrect because 30% retention significantly underestimates the actual amount. C is incorrect because 50% retention is still an underestimate of the true percentage. E is incorrect because 90% retention would be excessive and represents an overestimate.

questions.question:
A 14-year-old male patient suffers a distal forearm laceration. Clinical examination and wound exploration reveal involvement of the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon and ulnar nerve. The patient undergoes immediate microsurgical nerve repair using nerve grafting. Which of the following factors most likely predicts a favorable outcome in this patient?
A) Age
B) Gender
C) Immediate repair
D) Ulnar nerve involvement
E) Use of nerve graft
questions.answer:
A)
Younger age, particularly under 16 years old, is the strongest predictor of satisfactory motor function recovery following median and ulnar nerve repair after transection injuries. Pediatric patients have superior regenerative capacity and neuroplasticity compared to adults. B is incorrect because patient gender does not significantly influence nerve repair outcomes. C is incorrect because immediate repair may actually result in worse outcomes compared to slightly delayed repair. D is incorrect because ulnar nerve injuries typically have poorer recovery rates than median nerve injuries. E is incorrect because nerve graft use does not significantly predict improved motor recovery in these injuries.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male patient arrives at the burn center following injuries from a residential fire. Vital signs show heart rate 112 bpm, respiratory rate 10/min, blood pressure 113/63 mmHg, and room air oxygen saturation 98%. Physical examination reveals facial charring, singed eyebrows, and coarse inspiratory breath sounds. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Face mask oxygen delivery at 40%
B) Bilevel positive airway pressure
C) Hyperbaric oxygen therapy
D) Intubation with 100% oxygen administration
E) Nasal cannula oxygen at 6 L
questions.answer:
D)
Immediate intubation with 100% oxygen is essential due to high risk of carbon monoxide poisoning and impending airway compromise. The patient shows signs of inhalation injury with potential airway edema, and the normal oxygen saturation is falsely elevated due to carboxyhemoglobin. High-flow oxygen helps dissociate carbon monoxide from hemoglobin. A is incorrect because 40% oxygen is insufficient for carbon monoxide treatment and doesn't protect the airway. B is incorrect because BiPAP doesn't provide airway protection in patients at risk for airway collapse. C is incorrect because hyperbaric oxygen is controversial and inappropriate during acute burn resuscitation. E is incorrect because nasal cannula provides inadequate oxygen concentration and no airway protection.

questions.question:
A 59-year-old male patient is seen in consultation with a confirmed diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. Following esophagectomy, the surgical team decides to perform a supercharged pedicled jejunal flap for total esophageal reconstruction. Which of the following represents the most probable recipient site complication?
A) Chylothorax
B) Fistula
C) Flap failure
D) Hematoma
E) Isolated neck cellulitis
questions.answer:
B)
Fistula formation is the most frequent recipient site complication following esophageal reconstruction with jejunal flaps, occurring in up to 14% of cases according to multiple surgical series. A) Chylothorax is incorrect because it occurs in only 1% of cases, making it much less common than fistula formation. C) Flap failure is incorrect as it has the lowest complication rate at only 1% of cases. D) Hematoma is incorrect because it occurs in only 4% of cases, significantly lower than fistula rates. E) Isolated neck cellulitis is incorrect as it occurs in only 5% of cases, well below the fistula complication rate.

questions.question:
A 2-week-old male newborn is brought to the office for evaluation of median craniofacial dysraphia. His parents say that aside from the deformity, the child is thriving. Physical examination shows Tessier No. 0 and 14 clefts. A clinical photograph and a three-dimensional CT scan are shown. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?


A) Choanal atresia
B) Contact between the dura and ectoderm through the anterior fontanelle
C) Failure of closure of the foramen cecum
D) Heterotopic glial tissue
E) Rathke pouch cyst
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


OThe classification scheme by Tessier is perhaps the most accepted and basic approach to describe these rare craniofacial clefts. As it only provides an anatomical description, others have further developed description schemes. Some have an embryonic emphasis to further characterize these disorders. These severe clefts can be associated with encephalocele, which if not repaired can be life-threatening. 


Nasal dermoids arise from contact between dura and ectoderm through the foramen cecum. These can be dangerous if there is intracranial extension. 


Heterotopic glial tissue is equivalent to the term glioma because these are generally not connected to the intracranial space and are treated as benign lesions. 


The Rathke pouch occurs during development when the stomodeum ectoderm invaginates toward the hypophysis and remnants are usually located in the nasopharynx as a cyst. 


An encephalocele is similar to a glioma but contains meninges and/or brain (encephalomeningocele) and can communicate with the ventricle (encephalomeningocystocele). Fifteen percent of these are intranasal. Resection of these without knowing about their intracranial communication can be disastrous. Left untreated, these lesions can significantly increase the risk of meningitis and be life-threatening.


References
1. Allam KA, Wan DC, Kawamoto HK, et al. The spectrum of median craniofacial dysplasia. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2011 Feb;127(2):812-821.
2. Fearon JA. Rare craniofacial clefts: a surgical classification. J Craniofac Surg. 2008 Jan;19(1):110-112.
3. Rahbar R, Shah P, Mulliken JB, et al. The presentation and management of nasal dermoid: a 30-year experience. Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2003 Apr;129(4):464-471.
4. Woodworth BA, Schlosser RJ, Faust RA, et al. Evolutions in the management of congenital intranasal skull base defects. Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2004 Nov;130(11):1283-1288.

questions.question:
A newborn girl is assessed following an uncomplicated birth due to left ear microtia. Her facial features appear symmetrical otherwise. Which of the following diagnostic studies is most appropriate to order?
A) CT scan to rule out tethered cord
B) Echocardiography to rule out ventricular septal defect
C) Extremity x-ray studies to rule out limb-length discrepancies
D) Magnetic resonance angiography of the brain to rule out ipsilateral cerebral artery anomalies
E) Ultrasonography of the kidney to screen for structural anomalies
questions.answer:
E)
Renal ultrasonography is the most appropriate screening study because syndromic ear malformations are associated with increased risk of kidney abnormalities in conditions like brachio-oto-renal syndrome and Townes-Brocks syndrome. A) CT scan for tethered cord is incorrect because spinal cord tethering is not associated with ear anomalies but rather with myelomeningoceles and spina bifida. B) Echocardiography is incorrect because cardiac abnormalities are not linked to isolated microtia, only to extended spectrum hemifacial microsomia. C) Extremity x-rays are incorrect because limb-length discrepancies have no association with microtia. D) Brain MRA is incorrect because cerebral artery anomalies are evaluated in PHACE syndrome when large segmental hemangiomas are present, not with isolated ear malformations.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female patient receives breast augmentation surgery in an office-based surgical suite. She receives intravenous midazolam and fentanyl along with lidocaine local anesthetic blocks. One hour postoperatively in recovery, she develops confusion, muscle twitching, and dizziness. Which of the following medications represents the most appropriate immediate treatment?
A) Dantrolene
B) Fat emulsion
C) Flumazenil
D) Naloxone
E) Propofol
questions.answer:
B)
Fat emulsion (Intralipid) is the correct treatment for lidocaine toxicity, which presents with the described symptoms of confusion, muscle twitching, and dizziness occurring within 60 minutes of injection. A) Dantrolene is incorrect because it is specifically used to treat malignant hyperthermia, not local anesthetic toxicity. C) Flumazenil is incorrect as it reverses benzodiazepine effects, not lidocaine toxicity. D) Naloxone is incorrect because it counteracts opioid overdose, not local anesthetic poisoning. E) Propofol is incorrect as it is an anesthetic induction agent that would worsen the patient's neurological depression rather than treat lidocaine toxicity.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old male patient receives open reduction and internal fixation for an open proximal right tibial fracture. The injury shows minimal tissue loss and limited wound contamination. The wound is closed with 2-cm elevated flaps. Popliteal artery reconstruction is necessary. Which of the following Gustilo fracture classifications most likely applies to this patient?
A) I
B) II
C) IIIA
D) IIIB
E) IIIC
questions.answer:
E)
This fracture is classified as Gustilo Type IIIC because it involves major vascular injury requiring arterial repair for limb salvage, which is the defining criterion for this classification regardless of other factors. A) Type I is incorrect because it involves clean wounds less than 1 cm with minimal bone comminution, and this case has vascular injury. B) Type II is incorrect as it involves contaminated wounds greater than 1 cm with moderate comminution but no vascular injury. C) Type IIIA is incorrect because while it involves highly contaminated wounds with severe comminution, it does not include vascular injury requiring repair. D) Type IIIB is incorrect as it involves highly contaminated wounds greater than 10 cm with severe comminution but lacks the vascular injury component that defines Type IIIC.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female patient is examined following Mohs micrographic surgery for basal cell carcinoma removal from her lower eyelid 2 days prior. Physical examination reveals a 65% lower eyelid defect affecting both anterior and posterior lamellae. The canthi remain uninvolved. Which of the following represents the most suitable reconstructive approach for this patient?
A) Hughes tarsoconjunctival flap and Tripier lid switch flap
B) Local cheek V-Y advancement flap and buccal mucosal graft
C) Mustardé flap and hard palate mucosal graft
D) Tenzel semicircular flap and periosteal flap
E) Upper eyelid Cutler-Beard flap and buccal mucosal graft
questions.answer:
A)
The Hughes tarsoconjunctival flap combined with Tripier lid switch flap is the optimal choice for reconstructing a 65% full-thickness lower eyelid defect, providing appropriate anterior and posterior lamellar reconstruction with high-quality tissues. B) Local cheek V-Y advancement flap and buccal mucosal graft is incorrect because the V-Y flap would create poor cosmetic contour for such a large defect, and buccal mucosa lacks the structural support needed to prevent ectropion. C) Mustardé flap and hard palate mucosal graft is incorrect because hard palate mucosa contains keratinized epithelium that can cause corneal irritation, making it less desirable than conjunctiva. D) Tenzel semicircular flap and periosteal flap is incorrect because Tenzel flaps are appropriate for defects 50% or smaller, not 65% defects. E) Upper eyelid Cutler-Beard flap and buccal mucosal graft is incorrect because the Cutler-Beard flap already provides both lamellae, making the buccal mucosal graft redundant and unnecessary.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old child is brought to the clinic with progressive downward and outward displacement of the left globe and diplopia that has worsened over 18 months. Medical history is notable for open reduction and internal fixation of a left frontal bone fracture at age 2 years after a fall. On examination there is a soft, pulsatile fullness over the left superolateral orbital rim with palpable bony separation, hypoglobus, and lateral displacement of the left eye; extraocular movements are limited in upgaze. Which of the following factors during the initial surgical repair most likely led to this deformity?
A) Inadequate frontal sinus obliteration
B) Unrecognized dural tear and deficiency
C) Incomplete repair of periorbital tissue tears
D) Improper bone fragment alignment during fixation
E) Application of resorbable fixation plates
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is B. An unrecognized dural tear beneath a pediatric skull fracture allows herniation of arachnoid and brain tissue with transmitted cerebrospinal fluid pulsations, which prevents bony healing and produces progressive diastasis of the fracture edges — a growing skull fracture (leptomeningeal cyst). When the fracture involves the orbital roof/superolateral rim, the enlarging defect causes progressive hypoglobus, lateral globe displacement, pulsatile proptosis, and diplopia, exactly as seen here. Recognition and watertight repair of the dural defect (with duraplasty and cranioplasty as needed) at the time of the original injury prevents this complication. A is incorrect because the frontal sinus is essentially not pneumatized in a 2-year-old, so sinus obliteration would not have been relevant. C is incorrect because repair of periorbital soft-tissue lacerations has no bearing on the development of a growing skull fracture. D is incorrect because malalignment of bone fragments may cause a static contour irregularity but does not produce progressive bony separation over years in the absence of a dural defect. E is incorrect because resorbable fixation is standard in young children and is not associated with growing skull fractures; the underlying dural deficiency, not the plate material, drives the progressive deformity.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old adolescent who had successful Le Fort III osteotomy with bone grafting at age 10 for significant jaw disproportion returns with severe bite misalignment. Clinical evaluation reveals Angle class III malocclusion and marked midface underdevelopment. What is the most probable cause for the return of this patient's original problem?
A) Patient's age at the time of initial operation
B) Differential growth patterns between the surgically treated midface and mandible
C) Insufficient bone healing during the first year after surgery
D) Inadequate postoperative monitoring
E) Suboptimal surgical technique during the original procedure
questions.answer:
B)
The correct answer is B because research demonstrates that children who undergo Le Fort III advancement experience recurrence due to restricted midface sagittal growth while mandibular growth continues normally, creating progressive jaw disproportion despite initial surgical success. A is incorrect because studies show the average age of Le Fort III procedures (around 6 years) is not an independent risk factor for recurrence. C is incorrect because studies demonstrate good bony stability in the first postoperative year, with problems developing later due to growth discrepancies. D is incorrect because inadequate follow-up doesn't cause the underlying growth pattern differences that lead to recurrence. E is incorrect because the recurrence occurs despite technically successful initial surgery due to inherent growth biology rather than surgical technique.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old child with left femoral sarcoma undergoes tumor removal with limb-sparing surgery including intercalary bone allograft reconstruction. For extensive segmental bone defects in the femur and tibia, allografts are chosen over cancellous bone grafts primarily because of which characteristic?
A) Superior structural integrity
B) Enhanced bone conduction properties
C) Better graft incorporation rates
D) Reduced financial expense
questions.answer:
A)
The correct answer is A because allografts provide superior structural integrity and load-bearing capacity essential for reconstructing large weight-bearing bone segments in the femur and tibia, where mechanical strength is critical for function. B is incorrect because cancellous bone grafts actually have better osteoconductive properties than allografts due to their porous structure and cellular content. C is incorrect because cancellous autografts demonstrate superior incorporation and healing compared to allografts, which have limited cellular viability. D is incorrect because cost is not a primary clinical consideration when selecting reconstruction methods for complex oncologic defects, and allografts may actually be more expensive due to processing and storage requirements.

questions.question:
Two hours after a fall, a 23-year-old male experiences worsening numbness and pain in his left thumb and index finger. Radiographic images of the left wrist are provided. Reduction attempts are unsuccessful. What is the most appropriate immediate management for this patient?
A) Closed reduction with percutaneous wire fixation
B) Surgical exploration with wrist fusion
C) Application of external fixation device
D) Open surgical reduction with internal fixation
E) Removal of proximal carpal row
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is D because this patient has a Mayfield III greater arc perilunate injury with failed closed reduction and progressive median nerve symptoms, requiring urgent open reduction and internal fixation to address both the bony injury and potential carpal tunnel syndrome. A is incorrect because closed reduction has already failed, and percutaneous pinning wouldn't address the carpal tunnel compression or achieve adequate reduction. B is incorrect because wrist arthrodesis is reserved for chronic cases with painful instability, not acute injuries in young patients. C is incorrect because external fixation is used for staged reconstruction in chronic cases, not acute injuries where immediate definitive repair is possible. E is incorrect because proximal row carpectomy is a salvage procedure for missed chronic injuries with arthritis, not appropriate for acute trauma.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old male presents 8 weeks following fingertip amputation of his index finger that healed without surgical closure, resulting in a curved nail deformity. Examination reveals the remaining nail plate growing downward over the fingertip. What is the most probable underlying cause of this patient's nail deformity?
A) Loss of dorsal tissue with damage to the cuticle area
B) Loss of dorsal tissue with destruction of nail-producing cells
C) Loss of lateral tissue with ingrown nail border
D) Loss of fingertip pad tissue causing nail bed to curve over the remaining tip
E) Loss of fingertip pad tissue with cuticle overgrowth covering the nail bed
questions.answer:
D)
The correct answer is D because hook nail deformity results from loss of volar fingertip support tissue, causing the nail bed to fold over the shortened fingertip due to inadequate bony support and scar contracture at the nail-pulp junction. A is incorrect because dorsal tissue loss with eponychial fold damage doesn't cause the characteristic downward curving seen in hook nail. B is incorrect because loss of germinal matrix would prevent nail growth rather than cause abnormal curvature. C is incorrect because lateral tissue loss causes ingrown nail problems, not the hook-shaped deformity described. E is incorrect because eponychial fold overgrowth would cover the nail rather than cause the nail to curve over the fingertip.

questions.question:
A 6-year-old child with a history of cleft palate repair performed 5 years prior presents for evaluation. The child demonstrates hypernasality. Nasoendoscopic examination reveals adequate lateral pharyngeal wall movement and a sagittal closure pattern. Cephalometric measurements demonstrate a 10 mm posterior gap. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Intravelar veloplasty
B) Obturator
C) Palatal lift
D) Pharyngeal flap
E) Sphincter pharyngoplasty
questions.answer:
D)
The pharyngeal flap is the optimal treatment for patients with adequate lateral pharyngeal wall movement and sagittal or circular velopharyngeal closure patterns. A) Intravelar veloplasty is incorrect because it is reserved for unrepaired clefts or submucous clefts with minimal posterior gaps. B) An obturator is incorrect because it is used when there is insufficient palatal tissue for closure. C) A palatal lift is incorrect because it is indicated for patients with adequate tissue but poor muscular control or coordination. E) Sphincter pharyngoplasty is incorrect because it is used for large posterior gaps with coronal, circular, or bowtie closure patterns combined with good velar elevation but inadequate lateral wall movement.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old male patient who had laparoscopic gastric bypass 2 years ago presents for belt lipectomy consultation following massive weight reduction of 150 lb (68 kg). His weight has been stable for more than 6 months. His current BMI is 30 kg/m2. Which factor poses the greatest risk for hematoma formation in this patient?
A) Age
B) Gender
C) Location of incision
D) Postoperative BMI
questions.answer:
B)
Male gender represents an independent risk factor for hematoma and seroma formation in body contouring procedures, regardless of hypertension status. A) Age is incorrect because it has not been demonstrated to increase hematoma risk in body contouring patients. C) Location of incision is incorrect because incision site has not been shown to correlate with increased hematoma risk. D) Postoperative BMI is incorrect because it has not been established as a risk factor for hematoma formation.

questions.question:
What is the main benefit of using 2-octyl cyanoacrylate versus sutures for nail bed laceration repair?
A) Better cosmetic outcome
B) Better functionality
C) Less pain
D) Shorter repair time
questions.answer:
D)
The primary advantage of 2-octyl cyanoacrylate is significantly reduced repair time compared to suturing techniques. A) Better cosmetic outcome is incorrect because cosmetic results are equivalent between the two methods. B) Better functionality is incorrect because functional outcomes are comparable for both techniques. C) Less pain is incorrect because pain levels are not significantly different between the two repair methods.

questions.question:
Which congenital hand anomaly is caused by failure of differentiation?
A) Complex syndactyly
B) Congenital preaxial polydactyly
C) Long finger macrodactyly
D) Type 4 (pouce flottant variant) thumb hypoplasia
E) Unilateral below-the-elbow congenital amputation
questions.answer:
A)
Complex syndactyly belongs to the failure of differentiation category, where all necessary anatomical components are present but incompletely separated. B) Congenital preaxial polydactyly is incorrect because it represents a duplication anomaly, not a differentiation failure. C) Long finger macrodactyly is incorrect because it is classified as an overgrowth anomaly. D) Type 4 thumb hypoplasia is incorrect because it falls under the undergrowth classification. E) Unilateral below-the-elbow congenital amputation is incorrect because it represents a failure of formation anomaly.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old male presents for consultation regarding unsatisfactory results from rhinoplasty performed 2 years earlier. He experiences nasal opening collapse during deep inspiration and nasal tip deformity. Examination demonstrates external nasal valve collapse on deep inspiration and bilateral asymmetric alar rim collapse with 1-2 mm alar retraction. Revision rhinoplasty is being considered. Which graft would be most suitable for addressing these issues?
A) Columella strut
B) Composite alar rim
C) Lateral crural strut
D) Spreader
E) Subdomal
questions.answer:
C)
The lateral crural strut graft, made from septal cartilage and sutured to the undersurface of the lower lateral cartilage, provides enhanced support and positional control, effectively addressing alar retraction and external valve collapse. A) Columella strut is incorrect because it is primarily used for tip projection and support, not for alar retraction or valve collapse. B) Composite alar rim graft is incorrect because it is reserved for severe alar retraction with soft tissue deficiency. D) Spreader grafts are incorrect because they address internal nasal valve issues and dorsal septal deviation. E) Subdomal graft is incorrect because it is used for tip asymmetry correction and pinched tip improvement.

questions.question:
Which anatomical location listed below is known to house apocrine sweat glands?
A) Areola
B) Glans penis
C) Labia minora
D) Palms of the hands
E) Vermilion border of the lips
questions.answer:
A)

The areola is correct because it is one of the specific anatomical sites where apocrine sweat glands are naturally found, along with the axilla, labia majora, scrotum, prepuce, periumbilical, and perianal regions. These glands discharge their secretions into hair follicles and become active during puberty. B is incorrect because the glans penis lacks eccrine sweat glands entirely and does not contain apocrine glands. C is incorrect because the labia minora, like the glans penis, is devoid of eccrine sweat glands and does not have apocrine glands. D is incorrect because the palms contain the highest concentration of eccrine sweat glands in the body, not apocrine glands. E is incorrect because the vermilion border of the lips is one of the few body areas that lacks both eccrine and apocrine sweat glands.

questions.question:
The Froment sign results from compensatory activity of which muscle listed below?
A) Adductor pollicis
B) Extensor pollicis brevis
C) Extensor pollicis longus
D) Flexor pollicis brevis
E) Flexor pollicis longus
questions.answer:
E)

The flexor pollicis longus is correct because it produces the compensatory thumb interphalangeal joint flexion seen in Froment sign when the ulnar nerve-innervated adductor pollicis cannot function properly during pinch attempts. This median nerve-innervated muscle creates the characteristic thumb flexion posture. A is incorrect because the adductor pollicis is the muscle that fails to function due to ulnar nerve injury, not the compensating muscle. B is incorrect because the extensor pollicis brevis does not contribute to the interphalangeal joint flexion that characterizes Froment sign. C is incorrect because the extensor pollicis longus extends rather than flexes the thumb and is not involved in producing this compensatory sign. D is incorrect because the flexor pollicis brevis does not create the interphalangeal joint flexion that defines Froment sign.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old male patient who is intubated and sedated in the ICU following trauma has immediate extravasation of concentrated calcium solution from his peripheral IV access. What represents the most appropriate initial treatment for this injury?
A) Intravenous administration of dexrazoxane
B) Local injection of hyaluronidase
C) Phentolamine infiltration
D) Topical application of dimethyl sulfoxide
E) Topical application of heat
questions.answer:
B)

Local hyaluronidase injection is correct because this enzyme degrades hyaluronic acid in the extracellular matrix, reducing tissue viscosity and promoting rapid dispersion and absorption of the extravasated calcium solution when administered within one hour of the incident. A is incorrect because dexrazoxane is specifically indicated for anthracycline extravasation (like doxorubicin) and has no role in calcium extravasation management. C is incorrect because phentolamine is an alpha-blocker used specifically for extravasation of vasoconstrictive agents like norepinephrine or dopamine, not calcium solutions. D is incorrect because dimethyl sulfoxide is primarily used for doxorubicin extravasation as a free radical scavenger, not for calcium-related injuries. E is incorrect because heat application is recommended for vinca alkaloid extravasation to enhance circulation, but is not the appropriate treatment for calcium extravasation.

questions.question:
A healthy 55-year-old woman with Fitzpatrick Type II skin is scheduled for facial rejuvenation including phenol-croton oil (Hetter) peel combined with extended SMAS facelift and transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty. Which anatomical region carries the highest risk for healing complications following this combined procedure?
A) Forehead
B) Lateral cheek
C) Lower eyelid
D) Nasal dorsum
E) Perioral
questions.answer:
B)

The lateral cheek is correct because this area requires skin undermining during the facelift procedure, creating thin flaps that are at high risk for delayed healing and scarring when combined with chemical peeling. Peeling undermined tissue significantly increases complication rates. A is incorrect because the forehead is part of the 'T-zone' of non-undermined skin that can be safely peeled during facelift surgery. C is incorrect because studies have demonstrated that croton oil peeling can be safely performed with lower eyelid surgery, including transconjunctival approaches, since the peel is not applied to undermined areas. D is incorrect because the nasal dorsum is also part of the safe 'T-zone' where peeling does not involve undermined tissue. E is incorrect because the perioral region represents non-undermined skin in the 'T-zone' that can be safely treated with concurrent peeling and facelift procedures.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old Hispanic male presents with progressive enlargement of his lower abdomen occurring 8 months after receiving two cryolipolysis treatments with large applicators at another facility. His weight remains stable and recovery was initially unremarkable. Examination reveals a well-defined area of increased adiposity in the treatment zone. Which factor below is most likely NOT associated with his risk for developing this complication?
A) Abdomen as the site of treatment
B) Age less than 35 years
C) Hispanic background
D) Male sex
E) Use of a large applicator
questions.answer:
B)

Age less than 35 years is correct because patient age has not been identified as a risk factor for developing paradoxical adipose hyperplasia (PAH) following cryolipolysis in current literature. A is incorrect because abdominal treatment location is a well-established risk factor for PAH development. C is incorrect because Hispanic ethnicity has been identified as a significant risk factor for this complication. D is incorrect because male sex is a documented risk factor, with men having higher rates of PAH compared to women. E is incorrect because the use of large applicators has been specifically associated with increased risk of developing PAH after cryolipolysis procedures.

questions.question:
Following laser treatment of a complex multicolored tattoo, a patient presents with remaining green pigment. What is the most suitable treatment approach for this persistent ink?
A) CO2 laser
B) Intense pulsed light therapy
C) Long-pulsed Nd:YAG (1064-nm) laser
D) Q-switched alexandrite (755-nm) laser
E) 70% TCA chemical peel
questions.answer:
D)
The Q-switched alexandrite laser at 755-nm wavelength is optimal for treating green tattoo pigment. This wavelength specifically targets green ink effectively, with picosecond-domain alexandrite lasers achieving up to 75% clearance in just 1-2 sessions for fair-skinned individuals. Ruby lasers at 694-nm can also be used as an alternative. A) CO2 laser is incorrect because it cannot selectively target tattoo pigments. B) IPL is incorrect because it lacks the short pulse duration necessary for effective tattoo removal, leading to incomplete clearance and potential scarring. C) Long-pulsed Nd:YAG is incorrect because while the 1064-nm wavelength works well for dark colors, it is less effective on green pigment and is designed for hair removal/vascular treatments rather than tattoo removal. E) TCA peel is incorrect because it is non-selective, can cause severe scarring and burns, and is not recommended for tattoo removal.

questions.question:
A 78-year-old male with newly diagnosed low rectal cancer comes for consultation. His daughter completes his paperwork. Past medical history includes hypertension, osteoarthritis, and bilateral knee replacements from 20 years ago. Vital signs are normal, BMI is 21.5 kg/m2, and he uses a walker for mobility. Physical exam is unremarkable. An abdominoperineal resection with perineal reconstruction is planned. What assessment tool would be most valuable for evaluating his perioperative complication risk?
A) APACHE II scoring system
B) FEV1/FVC measurement
C) Frailty assessment
D) Hepatic function panel
E) SOFA scoring system
questions.answer:
C)
A frailty assessment is most appropriate for evaluating perioperative risk in this elderly patient with mobility limitations and potential cognitive concerns who will undergo major colorectal surgery with reconstruction. Frailty represents functional decline in elderly patients with reduced physiological reserve and increased vulnerability to adverse perioperative outcomes. Various frailty scoring tools assess physical characteristics, medical history, and laboratory values, with higher scores correlating with increased complications, longer stays, and poorer outcomes. A) APACHE II is incorrect because it's designed for critically ill ICU patients to predict outcomes, not for preoperative risk assessment. B) FEV1/FVC ratio is incorrect because it's used for monitoring asthma patients and assessing airway flow, not general surgical risk. D) Liver function tests are incorrect because this patient has no signs or history of liver disease or bleeding disorders. E) SOFA score is incorrect because it's used to assess organ failure severity in ICU patients, not for preoperative evaluation.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old male is scheduled for septorhinoplasty after sustaining a nasal fracture 3 years prior. He has mild von Willebrand disease. On the day of surgery, the surgeon gives 0.3 μg/kg of desmopressin (1-deamino-8-D-arginine-vasopressin) before and after the procedure to reduce postoperative bleeding. What is the primary mechanism by which this medication promotes hemostasis in this patient?
A) Stimulating Factor V Leiden activation in the coagulation pathway
B) Converting fibrinogen to fibrin
C) Triggering von Willebrand factor release from endothelial cell storage sites
D) Permanently blocking platelet thromboxane A2 production
E) Facilitating tissue factor complex formation to generate thrombin for fibrin plug formation
questions.answer:
C)
Desmopressin primarily works by triggering the release of von Willebrand factor (VWF) from its storage sites within endothelial cells. In von Willebrand disease, patients have deficient or abnormal VWF, which is essential for platelet adhesion and Factor VIII stabilization. By releasing additional VWF from endothelial stores, desmopressin improves hemostatic function in patients with mild VWD. A) Factor V Leiden activation is incorrect because this refers to a hypercoagulable mutation, and desmopressin doesn't directly interact with this molecule. B) Converting fibrinogen to fibrin is incorrect because this is the function of thrombin, not desmopressin. D) Blocking thromboxane A2 is incorrect because this describes aspirin's mechanism, which inhibits rather than promotes hemostasis. E) Tissue factor complex formation is incorrect because this describes Factor VII activity in hemophilia treatment, not desmopressin's mechanism.

questions.question:
During a Le Fort I osteotomy procedure, which vessel has the highest risk of injury?
A) Descending palatine artery
B) External carotid artery
C) Greater palatine artery
D) Internal carotid artery
E) Internal maxillary artery
questions.answer:
A)
The descending palatine artery is most vulnerable during Le Fort I osteotomy because it's directly in the path of the pterygoid osteotomy and down fracture. This vessel becomes clearly visible after down fracture and mobilization of the Le Fort I segment, and injury typically occurs during the osteotomy before it divides into the greater and lesser palatine branches. B) External carotid artery is incorrect because it's located in the neck region and gives rise to facial branches that terminate as the sphenopalatine artery. C) Greater palatine artery is incorrect because both greater and lesser palatine arteries are positioned below the pterygoid osteotomy level, making the more proximal descending palatine artery at higher risk. D) Internal carotid artery is incorrect because it's not in the surgical field of a Le Fort I osteotomy. E) Internal maxillary artery is incorrect because it's the larger parent vessel that branches into smaller arteries including the descending palatine, and it's not directly in the osteotomy path.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male has a sarcoma excised from his leg, creating a 6 x 5 cm defect. The wound is left open pending final pathology results before reconstruction. Due to expected heavy drainage from limb edema, a highly absorbent dressing is needed. What is the optimal wound management approach?
A) Foam dressing
B) Hydrocolloid dressing
C) Hydrofiber dressing
D) Hydrogel dressing
questions.answer:
C)
Hydrofiber dressing is optimal for this high-exudate wound. Composed of hydroxymethyl cellulose fibers, hydrofibers have superior absorptive capacity and transform into gel upon contact with moisture, maintaining an ideal wound environment. They can remain in place for several days, reducing dressing change frequency, and are specifically designed for moderate-to-heavy exudate wounds. A) Foam dressing is incorrect because while it provides some absorption, its capacity depends on foam thickness and is generally suitable for mild-to-moderate exudate, not heavy drainage. B) Hydrocolloid dressing is incorrect because although it absorbs exudate and forms gel, its absorptive capacity is significantly less than hydrofibers and is better suited for mild-to-moderate exudate. D) Hydrogel dressing is incorrect because it has 90% water content and doesn't absorb exudate; instead, it's designed for dry or minimally exudative wounds to provide moisture.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female presents to the clinic for removal of a skin lesion under local anesthesia. Her medical history is significant for numerous food and medication allergies. Soon after beginning the procedure, she complains of itching eyes and nasal discharge and becomes highly anxious. Over the following 5 minutes, she develops widespread skin redness and breathing difficulty, which advances to respiratory stridor. No intravenous line has been established. Which of the following medications given intramuscularly represents the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Diphenhydramine
B) Epinephrine
C) Ketamine
D) Midazolam
E) Triamcinolone
questions.answer:
B)

Epinephrine is the primary treatment for anaphylaxis and must be given intramuscularly (preferably in the anterolateral thigh) immediately upon diagnosis. The recommended dose is 0.01 mg/kg (up to 0.5 mg maximum), administered intramuscularly every 5-15 minutes as needed to manage symptoms. Early epinephrine administration is crucial since studies show the average time from medication-induced anaphylaxis to cardiac or respiratory arrest in hospitals is only 5 minutes, with merely 14% of patients receiving epinephrine before arrest. A) Diphenhydramine is incorrect because antihistamines are second-line therapy for anaphylaxis, not first-line treatment. C) Ketamine is incorrect because it has no role in anaphylaxis management. D) Midazolam is incorrect because benzodiazepines are not indicated for treating anaphylaxis. E) Triamcinolone is incorrect because while corticosteroids may be used as adjunctive therapy, they are not first-line treatment and work too slowly for acute anaphylaxis.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old woman presents with significant capsular contracture and deformity of her left reconstructed breast 3 years after undergoing bilateral mastectomy, left-sided radiation therapy, and subsequent two-stage implant reconstruction. A photograph is shown. She has a history of abdominoplasty. Which of the following is the most reliable way to achieve an acceptable reconstruction in this patient?


A) Conversion to prepectoral plane with acellular dermal allograft
B) Deep inferior epigastric perforator flap
C) Implant exchange with capsulectomy and acellular dermal allograft
D) Implant exchange with capsulotomy
E) Latissimus dorsi flap with expander
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


In this patient with a history of left-sided radiation and a severely contracted and deformed implant, the most reliable way to achieve an acceptable reconstruction would be to convert to some form of autologous reconstruction. Given her prior history of abdominoplasty, a deep inferior epigastric perforator flap is not feasible. A latissimus dorsi flap with an expander is a reliable option. Implant exchange with capsulotomy would have an extremely high risk for recurrence of capsular contracture and deformity. Capsulectomy with acellular dermal allograft replacement would have a fairly high risk for complications due to adding yet more foreign body to a radiated tissue bed, and there would still be a high risk for recurrent capsular contracture. Conversion to a prepectoral plane with acellular dermal allograft would have a potentially higher risk for complications because even more foreign body is required to fully wrap the implant.


ReferencesFischer JP, Basta MN, Shubinets V, et al. A systematic meta-analysis of prosthetic-based breast reconstruction in irradiated fields with or without autologous muscle flap coverage. Ann Plast Surg. 2016;77(1):129-134.Lee KT, Mun GH. Prosthetic breast reconstruction in previously irradiated breasts: a meta-analysis. J Surg Oncol. 2015;112(5):468-475.Nelson JA, Disa JJ. Breast reconstruction and radiation therapy: an update. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2017;140(5S Advances in Breast Reconstruction):60S-68S.

questions.question:
A 2-year-old male child receives treatment for congenital constriction band affecting the left upper limb with distal swelling. The patient undergoes removal of 50% of the circumferential constriction band with primary closure. This surgical intervention will most likely result in which of the following outcomes regarding the distal limb swelling?
A) Progressive improvement throughout childhood growth
B) Progressive deterioration throughout childhood growth
C) Marked improvement within several weeks following surgery
D) Marked deterioration throughout childhood growth
E) No change
questions.answer:
C)

Congenital constriction band syndrome affects 1:1200 to 1:15,000 live births with a preference for upper extremities and distal limbs. For complete circumferential bands, a staged approach is recommended where half the circumference is excised initially, with the remainder removed after 3-6 months to prevent compromising already vulnerable distal circulation. When edema is present, it shows significant improvement within a few weeks of the initial surgery. A) Progressive improvement during childhood is incorrect because the improvement occurs rapidly within weeks, not gradually over years. B) Progressive deterioration during childhood is incorrect because surgical treatment improves rather than worsens the condition. D) Marked deterioration during childhood is incorrect because proper surgical treatment leads to improvement, not worsening. E) No change is incorrect because surgical excision of constriction bands relieves the obstruction causing the edema, leading to rapid improvement.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old female patient who had periareolar mastopexy 13 years previously presents to the clinic requesting revision surgery for her current DD-cup breasts. She desires enhanced breast appearance with increased projection and reduction to B-cup size. Breast examination reveals flattened nipple-areolar complexes measuring 72 mm in diameter with surrounding circumferential hypertrophic surgical scars. The breasts appear wide and bottomed-out with a 14-cm measurement from the lower areolar border to the inframammary fold. Which surgical approach would be most suitable to accomplish her goals?
A) Breast liposuction with autologous fat grafting to the retroareolar area
B) Breast liposuction with breast implant placement
C) Lower pole breast liposuction with hypertrophic areolar scar excision
D) Periareolar mastopexy with open breast tissue excision
E) Wise pattern mastopexy with open breast tissue reduction
questions.answer:
E)

A secondary Wise pattern mastopexy with open reduction of excess breast tissue is most appropriate to achieve improved breast appearance with increased projection and significant cup size reduction (DD to B cup). This technique allows areolar diameter reduction, enhanced breast projection, and decreased risk of recurrent widened hypertrophic periareolar scarring. A) Breast liposuction with fat grafting is incorrect because while it may increase central projection and decrease cup size, it doesn't address the hypertrophic areolar scarring or abnormal lower pole dimensions. B) Breast liposuction with implants is incorrect because implants would not provide the desired three cup size reduction and wouldn't improve periareolar scars or bottoming out. C) Lower pole liposuction with scar excision is incorrect because it would only modestly decrease volume and cannot adequately improve breast shape, projection, or areolar dimensions. D) Periareolar mastopexy with tissue excision is incorrect because it won't increase central projection or adequately address the excessive inferior areolar to inframammary crease distance.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old attorney presents to the office with a 1-year history of restricted extension at the proximal interphalangeal joint of the right middle finger, with normal flexion, following a finger injury during basketball. Radiographic examination demonstrates normal joint surfaces without fracture or foreign material. What is the most probable etiology of this patient's condition?
A) Dorsal collateral ligament contracture
B) Dorsal edema
C) Dupuytren contracture
D) Extensor adhesions
E) Flexor adhesions
questions.answer:
E)

Flexor adhesions are the most likely cause of this patient's isolated extension limitation following trauma. Previous flexor tendon or canal injuries can cause scar formation between the tendon and adjacent structures, restricting extension while preserving flexion. Other causes of limited extension include volar plate contracture, collateral ligament contracture, volar skin scarring, and joint irregularities. A) Dorsal collateral ligament contracture is incorrect because this would limit flexion, not extension, of the PIP joint. B) Dorsal edema is incorrect because it commonly occurs after PIP joint injuries but limits flexion rather than extension. C) Dupuytren contracture is incorrect because it rarely affects the PIP joint in a 25-year-old patient, typically occurs spontaneously in older individuals, and usually involves the MCP joint first. D) Extensor adhesions is incorrect because these occur after dorsal finger injuries and cause limitation in flexion, not extension.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old Caucasian male presents to the office with a dark, pigmented lesion on his thumb that he first observed 3 months ago. He denies any history of digit trauma. Physical examination reveals a variegated lesion with irregular borders located in the germinal matrix of the right thumb nail bed. What represents the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Amputation to the next joint
B) Radiation therapy
C) Shave biopsy
D) Wide excision
E) Observation
questions.answer:
C)

A shave biopsy is the most appropriate first step for evaluating this suspicious pigmented nail bed lesion.
