C) Indium scintigraphy
D) Plain radiographs
E) Wound swab culture
questions.answer:
A)
Bone biopsy represents the gold standard for diagnosing osteomyelitis in pressure ulcer patients. Histopathologic examination of bone tissue provides the most accurate diagnosis, with core needle bone biopsy demonstrating 73% sensitivity and 96% specificity for osteomyelitis detection. This definitive diagnostic approach is crucial for determining appropriate treatment and predicting surgical outcomes, as patients with confirmed osteomyelitis face higher risks of postoperative complications following flap reconstruction. B is incorrect because CT scanning, while useful for assessing bone involvement extent, has lower diagnostic accuracy with only 50% sensitivity and 88% specificity compared to biopsy. C is incorrect because indium scanning with radiolabeled leukocytes has high sensitivity (100%) but poor specificity (50%), leading to many false positive results due to inflammation. D is incorrect because plain radiographs have limited diagnostic value with 88% sensitivity but only 32% specificity, often missing early osteomyelitis. E is incorrect because swab cultures are unreliable and discouraged as they typically reflect surface contamination rather than deep bone infection.

questions.question:
A 2-month-old female infant is evaluated for the ear anomaly shown in the photograph. Which of the following most accurately describes the anomaly?


A) Anotia
B) Crumple ear
C) Cryptotia
D) Lop ear
E) Stahl ear
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


This is cryptotia, a deformity of the ear in which the superior helical rim is buried beneath the skin of the scalp. Some studies report successful treatment with early ear molding, but this often requires elevation of the helical rim and application of a skin graft or regional flap to line the posterior aspect.

Anotia refers to complete absence of the ear structures, while lop ear is an ear that is typically constricted and has an overhang or hooding of the superior helical rim. Crumple ear is a form of constricted ear with variable cartilage abnormalities that give it an irregular appearance. Lastly, Stahl ear refers to an otherwise normal-sized ear with a third crus, usually accompanied by an evagination of the helical rim.


ReferencesJanz BA, Cole P, Hollier LH Jr, Stal S. Treatment of prominent and constricted ear anomalies. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009;124(suppl 1):27e-37e.Schultz K, Guillen D, Maricevich RS. Newborn ear deformities: early recognition and novel nonoperative techniques. Semin Plast Surg. 2017;31(3):141-145.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male undergoes abdominal wall reconstruction using component separation technique. Following bilateral external oblique muscle release, what best accounts for maintained trunk flexion capability?
A) Nerve preservation between anterior rectus fascia and pyramidalis muscle
B) Nerve preservation between external oblique and internal oblique muscles
C) Nerve preservation between internal oblique and transversalis muscles
D) Nerve preservation between transversus abdominis and peritoneum
questions.answer:
C)
Trunk flexion is preserved because the segmental nerves supplying the rectus abdominis muscle travel in the plane between the internal oblique and transversalis muscles. The rectus muscle serves as the primary trunk flexor, and its nerve supply enters the rectus sheath laterally through this specific anatomical plane. In component separation, only the external oblique aponeurosis is divided, leaving the internal oblique layer intact to protect the underlying neural supply to the rectus muscle, thus maintaining functional abdominal wall strength and flexion capability. A is incorrect because nerves don't travel between the anterior rectus fascia and pyramidalis muscle - this isn't the location of the main nerve supply to the rectus. B is incorrect because while the plane between external and internal oblique contains some neural structures, this isn't where the primary rectus muscle innervation travels. D is incorrect because the space between transversus abdominis and peritoneum doesn't contain the segmental nerves that supply the rectus abdominis muscle.

questions.question:
A 67-year-old female patient requires bilateral levator muscle reattachment due to drooping eyelids 6 months following cataract extraction. During this surgical procedure, the levator aponeurosis is reconnected to which of the following anatomical structures?
A) Lockwood ligament
B) Müller muscle
C) Orbital septum
D) Tarsal plate
E) Whitnall ligament
questions.answer:
D)

The tarsal plate is the correct attachment site for the levator aponeurosis during ptosis repair procedures. In age-related ptosis, the levator aponeurosis becomes detached or weakened from its normal insertion on the tarsal plate, requiring surgical reattachment. A) Lockwood ligament is incorrect because it is located in the lower eyelid and forms a supportive structure for the inferior rectus and oblique muscles, not related to upper eyelid elevation. B) Müller muscle is incorrect as it serves as a secondary elevator muscle but is not the primary attachment site for the levator aponeurosis. C) Orbital septum is incorrect because it lies in front of the fat compartments and levator aponeurosis, serving as a barrier rather than an attachment point. E) Whitnall ligament is incorrect as it represents a thickening of the levator muscle sheath in its anterior superior portion, not the insertion point for the aponeurosis.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old female patient with fair skin (Fitzpatrick Type II) seeks treatment for persistent melasma that has not responded to hydroquinone treatment. Tissue sampling confirms mixed-type melasma penetrating into the upper reticular dermis. Which of the following treatments would be most suitable for this condition?
A) Glycolic acid 50 to 70%
B) Jessner solution
C) Salicylic acid 20 to 30%
D) Tretinoin
E) Trichloroacetic acid 35 to 50%
questions.answer:
E)

Trichloroacetic acid 35 to 50% provides the appropriate medium-depth penetration needed to reach the upper reticular dermis where this mixed melasma extends, making it the most effective treatment option. Medium-depth peels penetrate approximately 200 μm through the epidermis and papillary dermis to the upper reticular dermis, which matches the depth of this patient's pigmentation. A) Glycolic acid 50 to 70% is incorrect because it only achieves superficial-light depth penetration of about 100 μm, insufficient for dermal pigment. B) Jessner solution is incorrect as it also provides only superficial-light penetration to 100 μm depth. C) Salicylic acid 20 to 30% is incorrect because it creates very superficial injury less than 100 μm deep, affecting only the stratum corneum and possibly stratum granulosum. D) Tretinoin is incorrect as it promotes cellular turnover and prevents collagen degradation but is not indicated for melasma treatment.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old male patient has a persistent wound on the bottom surface of his foot. His medical background includes type 2 diabetes. Which of the following findings would most strongly suggest that hyperbaric oxygen treatment could benefit this patient?
A) Ankle brachial index greater than 1
B) Exposed bone
C) Failed total contact casting
D) Hemoglobin A1c greater than 7.0%
E) Peripheral neuropathy
questions.answer:
B)

Exposed bone indicates a Wagner grade 3 diabetic foot ulcer with bone involvement, which represents the primary indication for hyperbaric oxygen therapy in diabetic foot wounds. Research demonstrates that HBOT is beneficial for deep ulcers (Wagner grades 3 and 4) to enhance healing and reduce amputation risk, but not for superficial soft tissue ulcers (Wagner grades 1 and 2). A) Ankle brachial index greater than 1 is incorrect because while this can occur in diabetic patients due to vessel calcification, it does not indicate HBOT candidacy. C) Failed total contact casting is incorrect as this represents a treatment failure for pressure off-loading, but HBOT is only indicated for deep ulcers regardless of previous treatment attempts. D) Hemoglobin A1c greater than 7.0% is incorrect because while this indicates poor glycemic control over 2-3 months, it is not a specific indication for HBOT. E) Peripheral neuropathy is incorrect as this is a common diabetic complication that contributes to ulcer development but does not determine HBOT indication.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male patient arrives at the emergency room 6 hours after suffering an open wrist fracture with soft tissue loss during agricultural work. His medical history includes diabetes. Physical examination reveals intact distal circulation and sensation. Surgical debridement and fixation are scheduled. Which of the following factors creates the highest risk for postoperative infection in this patient?
A) Gustilo fracture classification
B) History of diabetes mellitus
C) Method of fracture fixation
D) Period of time from injury to initial debridement
E) Type of contamination
questions.answer:
E)

The type of contamination represents the strongest predictor of postoperative infection risk in distal radius fractures, particularly in agricultural injuries which typically involve heavy bacterial contamination. Recent research by Glueck and Swanson has demonstrated that contamination type correlates more strongly with infection rates than other factors in distal radius fractures. A) Gustilo fracture classification is incorrect because while it has some correlation with infection rates, this relationship is weaker in distal radius fractures compared to lower extremity long bone fractures. B) History of diabetes mellitus is incorrect as systemic conditions like diabetes show only modest correlation with postoperative infections in distal radius fractures, often without statistical significance. C) Method of fracture fixation is incorrect because the fixation technique has minimal correlation with infection rates in distal radius fractures. D) Period of time from injury to initial debridement is incorrect since timing within the first 24 hours does not significantly impact infection rates, unlike the contamination severity.

questions.question:
A 57-year-old female patient presents with burning pain and stiffness in her right hand 8 weeks following non-surgical treatment of a wrist fracture. She reports sleep difficulties and ongoing discomfort despite narcotic medication. Physical examination reveals a shiny, swollen, warm hand with limited finger movement and hypersensitivity to gentle touch. Radiographs demonstrate proper fracture alignment. Nerve conduction studies are normal. Bone scintigraphy reveals increased uptake around joints. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A) Complex regional pain syndrome
B) Factitious disorder
C) Midpalmar space abscess
D) Opioid addiction
E) Pain catastrophizing
questions.answer:
A)

Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) type I, formerly known as reflex sympathetic dystrophy, is the most appropriate diagnosis based on the constellation of symptoms including disproportionate pain, autonomic changes (temperature and color alterations), sudomotor dysfunction (swelling), and trophic skin changes (shiny appearance). The increased periarticular uptake on bone scan in multiple joints supports this diagnosis, as triple-phase bone scans commonly show this pattern in CRPS. B) Factitious disorder is incorrect because the patient exhibits genuine physiological symptoms and autonomic changes that cannot be voluntarily produced. C) Midpalmar space abscess is incorrect as it would be extremely unlikely following a closed wrist fracture and would not cause the widespread trophic changes or bone scan abnormalities seen in this case. D) Opioid addiction is incorrect because while patients may seek additional narcotics, the objective physical findings and diagnostic test results indicate genuine pathophysiology rather than drug-seeking behavior. E) Pain catastrophizing is incorrect as this represents a maladaptive psychological response to pain but does not explain the physical examination findings or positive bone scan results.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old man who is a biathlete comes to the office because of weakness and pain when gripping or pinching with the left hand. Medical history includes a sprain to the left thumb with forced radial abduction 1 year ago. Physical examination shows a difference in stability of the right thumb and the left thumb during stress testing. Photographs are shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this patient's metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint injury?


A) Direct repair of the collateral ligament
B) Graft reconstruction of the collateral ligament
C) Occupational therapy for strengthening of the adductor muscle
D) Placement of a short opponens splint for 6 weeks
E) Transfer of the extensor indicis proprius tendon to the adductor insertion
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.





Injuries to the ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint (skier's thumb Injury) can be successfully treated with 4 weeks of immobilization provided that the injury results in either no instability, or limited (<30 to 35-degree laxity under load, or <10 to 15-degree difference from the contralateral UCL under load) instability. The photographs provided show 40 to 45 degrees of laxity, which differs substantially from the contralateral (<10 degrees) thumb. Treatment of this injury requires operative intervention. Incomplete injuries, or injuries with only mild symptomatic laxity, may benefit from occupational therapy. The adductor muscle provides a stabilizing force across the metacarpophalangeal joint and has been a target for treating mild injuries that result in some degree of instability. This would be insufficient for treating this complete rupture. In a similar fashion to strengthening the adductor muscle, addition of another force directed at providing ulnar adduction at the metacarpophalangeal joint has been proposed. As in the case of adductor strengthening, however, this would be inadequate to treat the complete rupture apparent in the clinical photos. When encountered acutely, unstable, complete ruptures of the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint are optimally treated with operative repair. Four to six weeks following the injury, direct repair may be difficult if not impossible. In this patient, the presentation for treatment occurs one year after the initial injury, making repair of the UCL extremely unlikely. On operative exploration in this patient, only a shortened stump of UCL remained attached to the metacarpal head. Chronic unstable injuries of the thumb metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) may be symptomatic via weakened grip and pinch as well as pain. Treatment in this setting will be dictated by patient needs and by the status of the joint. Patients requiring mobility and lacking arthritic degeneration at the MCP joint are candidates for UCL reconstruction. Reconstruction will typically be accomplished by use of a tendon graft, either palmaris or plantaris, placed through bone tunnels and secured through one of multiple methods (interference screws, periosteal sutures, bone anchors). Given this patient's presentation one year out from the initial injury, reconstruction is the best option.


References
Carlson MG, Warner KK, Meyers KN. Mechanics of an anatomical reconstruction for the thumb metacarpophalangeal collateral ligaments. J Hand Surg Am. 2013 Jan;38(1):117-23.
Tang P. Collateral ligament injuries of the thumb metacarpophalangeal joint. J Am Acad Orthop Surg. 2011 May;19(5):287-96.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male presents to the clinic following a brachial plexus injury from a motorcycle crash. A nerve transfer to the biceps muscle is being considered to restore elbow flexion function. Which of the following fascicles or nerves represents the most suitable donor for this transfer procedure?
A) Distal spinal accessory nerve
B) Flexor carpi ulnaris fascicle of the ulnar nerve
C) Medial pectoral nerve
D) Palmaris longus fascicle of the median nerve
E) Thoracodorsal nerve
questions.answer:
B)
The flexor carpi ulnaris (FCU) fascicle of the ulnar nerve represents the optimal donor choice for biceps nerve transfer. This technique, initially described by Oberlin and colleagues in 1994, utilizes the donor nerve with the largest diameter and highest motor axon count for elbow flexion restoration. The FCU fascicle provides superior outcomes compared to other options. MacKinnon has recommended combining FCU fascicle transfer to biceps with FCR fascicle of median nerve to brachialis for optimal elbow flexion recovery. A is incorrect because the distal spinal accessory nerve has fewer motor axons and smaller caliber than the FCU fascicle. C is incorrect because the medial pectoral nerve provides less optimal motor axon count for biceps reinnervation. D is incorrect because the palmaris longus fascicle has inferior axon count compared to the FCU fascicle. E is incorrect because the thoracodorsal nerve, while viable, is not as effective as the FCU fascicle for biceps transfer.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male arrives at the emergency department following a chest gunshot injury. He exhibits breathing difficulties and diminished breath sounds on the right side. Right chest needle decompression is performed followed by chest tube placement. The patient's condition stabilizes. Which of the following initial clinical findings would most likely be present in this patient?
A) Cardiac murmur
B) Decreased urine output
C) Hyperresonance of the left chest
D) Hypertension
E) Tracheal deviation to the left
questions.answer:
E)
Tension pneumothorax causes tracheal deviation away from the affected side due to increasing intrapleural pressure that shifts mediastinal structures. In this case with right-sided injury, the trachea deviates to the left (contralateral side). This occurs alongside other classic findings including tachypnea, dyspnea, jugular venous distention, decreased air entry, and hyperresonance on the affected side. A is incorrect because cardiac murmurs are not characteristic features of tension pneumothorax. B is incorrect because decreased urine output is not a primary manifestation of tension pneumothorax. C is incorrect because hyperresonance occurs on the affected (right) side, not the left side. D is incorrect because tension pneumothorax typically causes hypotension, not hypertension, due to decreased venous return.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old female with excessive vertical maxillary height is planned for LeFort I osteotomy with impaction. During this surgical procedure, which of the following arterial pairs is most likely to be interrupted?
A) Ascending pharyngeal and ascending palatine
B) Greater palatine and facial
C) Maxillary and lesser palatine
D) Nasopalatine and descending palatine
E) Sphenopalatine and pterygopalatine
questions.answer:
D)
The nasopalatine and descending palatine arteries are routinely disrupted during LeFort I osteotomy procedures. These vessels provide significant blood supply to the palatal and alveolar regions that are mobilized during the osteotomy. Following downfracture of the maxillary segment, the ascending palatine and ascending pharyngeal arteries become the primary vascular supply to the mobilized segment. Understanding this vascular anatomy is essential for successful LeFort I procedures. A is incorrect because these arteries become the dominant supply after downfracture rather than being disrupted. B is incorrect because the greater palatine and facial arteries are not the primary vessels interrupted during this procedure. C is incorrect because the maxillary and lesser palatine arteries are not the main vessels affected during LeFort I osteotomy. E is incorrect because the sphenopalatine and pterygopalatine vessels are not the primary arteries disrupted in this procedure.

questions.question:
A 39-year-old female seeks consultation for abdominoplasty. She reports a family history of blood clots. Her sole current medication is oral contraceptive pills. Her BMI measures 26 kg/m². Which of the following factors contributes most significantly to this patient's deep venous thrombosis risk?
A) Abdominoplasty
B) Age
C) BMI
D) Family history of thrombosis
E) Oral contraceptive use
questions.answer:
D)
According to the 2005 Caprini risk assessment scale, family history of thrombosis carries the highest point value (3 points) among the listed factors, making it the most significant contributor to DVT risk. This scoring system is recommended for plastic surgeons to evaluate thrombosis risk in surgical patients. The family history represents an inherited predisposition that substantially elevates baseline risk. A is incorrect because abdominoplasty, while considered major surgery, contributes only 2 points to the Caprini score. B is incorrect because the patient's age contributes only 1 point to the risk assessment. C is incorrect because a BMI of 26 kg/m² contributes only 1 point to the Caprini scale. E is incorrect because oral contraceptive use contributes only 1 point to the overall risk score.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male with mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the left parotid gland undergoes parotidectomy. Which of the following complications is most likely to occur in this patient?
A) Gustatory sweating
B) Hyperacusis
C) Loss of taste
D) Tardive dyskinesia
E) Tearing while eating
questions.answer:
A)
Gustatory sweating (Frey syndrome) is the most common complication following parotidectomy, occurring due to aberrant reinnervation of cutaneous sweat glands in the cheek skin overlying the parotid bed. This results in sweating and flushing during eating when parasympathetic fibers intended for salivary glands inappropriately innervate sweat glands. This complication is directly related to the surgical disruption of normal nerve anatomy during parotidectomy. B is incorrect because hyperacusis occurs with intracranial facial nerve injury before the stylomastoid foramen, not with parotidectomy. C is incorrect because taste loss involves chorda tympani injury in the tympanic cavity, not facial nerve injury within the parotid gland. D is incorrect because tardive dyskinesia results from antipsychotic medication side effects, not facial nerve dysfunction. E is incorrect because crocodile tear syndrome occurs after Bell's palsy with aberrant regeneration to lacrimal glands, not typically after parotidectomy.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient has undergone surgical removal of a malignant tumor in her left parotid gland. During the procedure, the facial nerve was excised along with the tumor, creating a 5- to 7-cm defect between the proximal nerve stump and the distal nerve branches. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Cable nerve grafting
B) Cross-facial nerve grafting
C) Hypoglossal nerve to facial nerve transfer
D) Innervated gracilis muscle free flap reconstruction
E) Nerve repair with a conduit
questions.answer:
A)
Cable nerve grafting is the optimal choice when there is a significant gap between facial nerve stumps following resection. This technique provides the best functional recovery outcomes when direct repair is not feasible due to the distance between nerve ends. B) Cross-facial nerve grafting is reserved for cases where the nerve has been resected very proximally near the intracranial portion, which is not the case here. C) Hypoglossal nerve transfer provides facial tone and symmetry but is typically used when direct repair or cable grafting is not possible. D) Innervated gracilis muscle free flap is indicated when nerve repair options are not feasible or after motor endplate degeneration has occurred. E) Nerve conduits are limited to gaps less than 3 cm for optimal recovery, making them unsuitable for this 5-7 cm defect.

questions.question:
A 2-week-old male infant presents with a wide unilateral cleft lip and palate for assessment and surgical planning. His parents are considering nasoalveolar molding versus lip adhesion to align the alveolar segments, reduce cleft width, and enhance nasal contour. What is the main benefit of lip adhesion compared to nasoalveolar molding?
A) Decreased cost
B) Decreased scar tissue
C) Fewer treatment complications
D) Improved clinical outcome
E) Increased compliance
questions.answer:
E)
Increased compliance is the primary advantage of lip adhesion over nasoalveolar molding because it reduces the burden on the family by eliminating the need for continuous appliance management. A) Decreased cost is incorrect because lip adhesion actually costs more than nasoalveolar molding. B) Decreased scar tissue is incorrect as lip adhesion can potentially create more scarring. C) Fewer treatment complications is incorrect since lip adhesion has a higher complication rate including scarring and wound dehiscence. D) Improved clinical outcome is incorrect as there is no proven clinical advantage, and some argue nasoalveolar molding may be superior since it also addresses nasal contour.

questions.question:
A 10-month-old boy is brought to the office because of the ocular defect shown in the photograph. Which of the following is the correct term for this anomaly?


A) Anophthalmia
B) Coloboma
C) Congenital cataract
D) Palpebral fissure
E) Tessier No. 6 cleft
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


Coloboma is a congenital ocular defect of the eyelid, iris, retina, choroid, or optic disk. The defects can range in size from a small notch to a large structural cleft. Palpebral colobomas are thought to arise from a localized growth disturbance, while colobomas of the iris, retina, and optic disk arise from defective closure of the optic fissure. Upper eyelid coloboma rarely affects vision; large defects of the lower eyelid can lead to corneal ulceration.


Anophthalmia is total absence of the eye. A congenital cataract is a lens opacity that is present in 1:4000 to 1:10,000 newborns. The size and location determine the effect on vision. The palpebral fissure is the natural opening between the upper and lower eyelids. A Tessier No. 6 cleft involves the inferolateral aspect of the lower eyelid, inferior orbital rim, and the zygoma. This cleft often has an associated lower eyelid coloboma and is related to Treacher Collins syndrome.


References
Levin AV. Congenital eye anomalies. Pediatr Clin North Am. 2003 Feb;50(1):55-76.
Guercio JR, Martyn LJ. Congenital malformations of the eye and orbit. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2007 Feb;40(1):113-140, vii.

questions.question:
A 4-month-old male infant is brought to the office for evaluation of an abnormal head shape that has been present since birth. The patient is developmentally appropriate and has no other abnormalites. A photograph is shown. At which of the following ages does the involved suture normally fuse?


A) 2 weeks
B) 8 months
C) 3 years
D) 10 years
E) 22 years
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


The patient in the photograph has metopic craniosynostosis. The primary clinical features of trigonocephaly are a palpable metopic ridge, bossing with thickened bone at the glabella, bifrontal narrowing, recession of the superior orbital rims, temporal narrowing, and hypotelorism. Trigonocephaly is also known as a keel-shaped deformity.


The metopic suture is the first cranial suture to fuse and this usually occurs at approximately 8 months of age. The other cranial sutures generally fuse in adulthood.


Treatment depends on the age of presentation and extent of deformity. Options for management are varied and range from no intervention for minimal deformity, burring of the metopic ridge only, endoscopic synostectomy with helmet therapy, and bilateral fronto-orbital advancement.


References
1. Shin JH, Persing JA. Nonsyndromic Craniosynostosis and Deformational Plagiocephaly. In: Thorne CH, Bartlett SP, Beasley RW, et al, eds. Grabb & Smith's Plastic Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2006:229-230.
2. Vu HL, Panchal J, Parker EE, et al. The timing of physiologic closure of the metopic suture: a review of 159 patients using reconstructed 3D CT scans of the craniofacial region. J Craniofac Surg. 2001 Nov;12(6):527-532.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old male patient with schizophrenia is evaluated 1 hour following self-amputation of his penis at the shaft base using a cleaver. The severed penis has been recovered and microvascular replantation is planned. Which arterial repair is most critical for successful outcomes?
A) Bulbourethral
B) Deep cavernosal
C) Dorsal penile
D) Helicine
E) Internal pudendal
questions.answer:
C)
Dorsal penile artery repair is most critical for successful penile replantation outcomes, as meta-analysis demonstrates it best predicts combined sexual function, urinary function, and sensation recovery. A) Bulbourethral artery supplies the penile bulb and urethra but is not the primary determinant of overall functional success. B) Deep cavernosal artery repair does not correlate with improved outcomes despite its role in erection and shaft supply. D) Helicine artery is a terminal branch of the dorsal penile artery located distal to the amputation site. E) Internal pudendal artery supplies the penis but is located proximal to the amputation site.

questions.question:
A healthy 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with a soft-tissue sarcoma in his mid-anterior leg. Following neoadjuvant radiation and wide local excision, a superficial circumflex iliac perforator-based flap is being considered for reconstructing the 10 × 5-cm defect. What is the primary benefit of this flap compared to a radial forearm flap?
A) Ability to neurotize the flap
B) Ease of flap harvest
C) Length of pedicle
D) Lower donor site morbidity
E) Thickness of flap
questions.answer:
D)
Lower donor site morbidity is the primary advantage of the SCIP flap over the radial forearm flap, as the SCIP flap can usually be closed primarily while most radial forearm flap donor sites require skin grafting, and the groin location is more concealed. A) Ability to neurotize is incorrect as both flaps can be neurotized using different nerve sources. B) Ease of flap harvest is incorrect since the SCIP flap is actually more technically challenging to raise. C) Length of pedicle is incorrect as the SCIP flap has a shorter pedicle length. E) Thickness of flap is incorrect as both flaps are known for being thin and have similar thickness characteristics.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old female patient is being assessed for left nipple reconstruction following mastectomy. She has scarring on the left breast from a prior biopsy and the mastectomy procedure. The nipple reconstruction must be planned to accommodate these scars. In single-pedicle nipple reconstruction techniques, what provides the blood supply to the pedicle?
A) Internal mammary artery perforators
B) Posterior intercostal arteries
C) Subdermal plexus
D) Superior intercostal artery
E) Thoracoacromial artery perforators
questions.answer:
C)
The subdermal plexus provides blood supply to single-pedicle nipple reconstructions including skate flap, star flap, C-V flap, and opposing tab flaps, which create nipples from remaining mastectomy skin through local tissue transfer. A) Internal mammary artery perforators supply the breast and nipple-areola complex but not the reconstruction pedicle. B) Posterior intercostal arteries supply the intercostal spaces, not the nipple reconstruction. D) Superior intercostal artery arises from the costocervical trunk and supplies intercostal spaces. E) Thoracoacromial artery perforators supply the pectoralis muscle and breast tissue, not the nipple reconstruction pedicle.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient experiences insufficient tear production due to malfunctioning lacrimal gland function. Which component of her tear film is most likely to be compromised?
A) Lipid content of the tear film
B) Mucin content of the tear film
C) Antibacterial properties of the tear film
D) Rate of tear film evaporation
E) Tear film distribution
questions.answer:
C)
The lacrimal gland produces the middle aqueous layer of the three-layered tear film, which contains water and proteins responsible for osmotic balance and antimicrobial defense. When this gland malfunctions, the antibacterial properties are most significantly affected, leading to dryness and increased infection risk. A is incorrect because lipids are produced by meibomian glands, not the lacrimal gland. B is incorrect because mucin is secreted by conjunctival goblet cells. D is incorrect because evaporation is primarily controlled by the lipid layer from meibomian glands. E is incorrect because tear distribution is mainly facilitated by the mucin layer from goblet cells.

questions.question:
In complete laryngopharyngeal reconstruction, what benefit does jejunal free flap offer compared to anterolateral thigh free flap?
A) Superior voice quality with tracheoesophageal puncture prosthesis
B) Higher rate of feeding tube independence
C) Reduced donor site complications
D) Decreased flap failure rates
E) Simpler surgical placement
questions.answer:
E)
The jejunal free flap, being a pre-formed tubular structure, offers simpler surgical placement requiring only superior and inferior anastomoses, while the ALT flap must be shaped into a tube with additional suture lines. A is incorrect because ALT flaps provide superior voice quality with TEP prostheses, as jejunal speech tends to be wet and difficult to understand. B is incorrect because ALT flaps have higher feeding tube independence rates. C is incorrect because jejunal harvest has greater donor site morbidity. D is incorrect because ALT flaps have equivalent or lower failure rates compared to jejunal flaps.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old woman is evaluated because of a new 2 √o 2-cm open area near her left axillary fold. Medical history is significant for left breast cancer previously treated with bilateral mastectomies, left axillary node dissection, and adjuvant chemoradiation 10 years ago. A photograph is shown. She has been compliant with postoperative oncologic surveillance and has had no recent trauma. Which of the following underlying conditions is most likely responsible for her current presentation?


A) Empyema with spontaneous drainage
B) Lymphedema drainage tract
C) Osteoradionecrosis of the underlying rib(s)
D) Recurrent breast cancer
E) Skin ulceration from intertriginous shearing forces
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


The effects of ionizing radiation are permanent and may present either acutely or in delayed fashion, even years after the original radiation insult. The mechanism of injury from this radiation is through free radical production which, in turn, directly damages the DNA. In the acute period, the effects of radiation may manifest themselves as erythema and edema of the skin, vasodilation with endothelial edema, and lymphatic obliteration. This eventually leads to capillary thrombosis and subsequent inadequate tissue oxygenation. Over time, nonhealing ulcers can spontaneously develop, sometimes years later.


Although recurrent cancer is always a concern in patients with a personal history of cancer, proper, regular, and thorough surveillance can often detect recurrences early, especially in compliant patients. Most recurrences occur within the first 5 years.


Abscesses usually present initially with pain, erythema, and localized fluctuance, and often with associated fever and/or malaise. Spontaneous necessitation to the skin would also result in purulent drainage.


Lymphedema can be a chronic condition after mastectomy and axillary node dissection, and is usually manifested as generalized edema of the ipsilateral upper extremity. Sinus tract formation is rare.


Intertriginous shearing would most often present as superficial epidermal loss with possible superinfection with yeast due to moisture.


References
Janis JE, Harrison B. Wound Healing Part I ‚Äi Basic Science. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2014 Feb;133(2):199e-207e.
Tibbs MK. Wound healing following radiation therapy: A review. Radiother Oncol. 1997;42:99‚Äi106.
Drake DB, Oishi SN. Wound healing considerations in chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Clin Plast Surg. 1995 Jan;22(1):31-7.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old male seeks treatment for prominent nasolabial creases and desires durable results with minimal work absence. Which treatment option will most likely require the longest healing period?
A) Calcium hydroxylapatite (Radiesse)
B) Collagen (Zyderm)
C) Autologous fat transfer
D) Hyaluronic acid (Restylane or Juvéderm)
E) Poly-L-lactic acid (Sculptra)
questions.answer:
C)
Autologous fat transfer requires the longest recovery time due to deeper placement with large-bore needles, resulting in more substantial bruising and swelling compared to other fillers. A is incorrect because Radiesse provides long-lasting results with rapid recovery. B is incorrect because collagen products have minimal downtime. D is incorrect because hyaluronic acid fillers offer quick recovery times. E is incorrect because Sculptra, while used for volume enhancement similar to fat transfer, has less associated downtime than fat grafting procedures.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old female develops acute lateral elbow pain after lifting a trash bag from a container at her workplace. Which muscle is most likely responsible for her symptoms?
A) Anconeus
B) Brachioradialis
C) Extensor carpi radialis brevis
D) Extensor carpi radialis longus
E) Extensor carpi ulnaris
questions.answer:
C)
The extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB) is the primary muscle involved in lateral epicondylitis, as it originates from the lateral epicondyle via the common extensor tendon and is most commonly affected in this condition. A is incorrect because the anconeus is a small elbow extensor that rarely causes lateral epicondylitis symptoms. B is incorrect because the brachioradialis is an elbow flexor originating from the lateral supracondylar ridge, not involved in lateral epicondylitis. D is incorrect because the extensor carpi radialis longus originates from the supracondylar ridge rather than the lateral epicondyle. E is incorrect because while the extensor carpi ulnaris can contribute to lateral elbow pain, ECRB is the most commonly implicated muscle.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female presents with incomplete right eye closure one week after bilateral upper lid blepharoplasty with levator advancement. Examination reveals 2 mm overcorrection of the right eyelid with normal slit lamp findings. What is the most appropriate initial management?
A) Apply downward massage to the right eyelid
B) Conduct an edrophonium (Tensilon) test
C) Perform skin grafting to the right eyelid
D) Remove the skin and levator sutures
E) Revise the left eyelid for symmetry
questions.answer:
A)
Downward massage is the appropriate conservative first-line treatment for early postoperative eyelid overcorrection, combined with aggressive lubrication to protect the cornea. B is incorrect because the Tensilon test is used to diagnose myasthenia gravis, not relevant to surgical overcorrection. C is incorrect because there is no skin deficiency requiring grafting. D is incorrect because removing levator sutures could cause ptosis recurrence without addressing the overcorrection. E is incorrect because revising the contralateral eyelid would create bilateral dry eye symptoms and poor aesthetic outcomes.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old man has clawing of all four fingers of the right hand 2 years after repair of a forearm laceration that injured the median and ulnar nerves. Photographs are shown. Both nerves were repaired shortly after the injury. All fingers have full passive range of motion. An extensor carpi radialis longus transfer is planned to correct the clawing of all four fingers. Which of the following donor sites is most likely to provide sufficient tendon graft for this procedure?


A) Abductor digiti quinti
B) Extensor digitorum longus
C) Flexor digitorum superficialis of the long finger
D) Palmaris brevis
E) Pronator teres
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


The Brand transfer uses the extensor carpi radialis longus or brevis as a donor motor to correct clawing of the fingers. It can be used to correct ulnar (ring and small finger) clawing or clawing of all four fingers. In either case, a tendon graft is needed to bridge the gap between the native distal limit of the extensor carpi radialis longus or brevis (on the index or long finger metacarpal base, respectively) to the transfer insertion on the lateral band at the proximal phalanx level. The transfer can be passed through the interosseous membrane in the forearm and then through the carpal tunnel or the intermetacarpal spaces in the hand. The transfer must pass volar to the deep transverse metacarpal ligament to have the correct vector of pull.






The extensor digitorum longus provides four tendon slips distally, each with its own paratenon, but has one tendon coming off the muscle proximally. A photograph is shown. There is minimal donor site morbidity in the foot due to the retained function of the extensor digitorum brevis.


Palmaris brevus has no tendon and cannot be used as a graft donor.


Abductor digiti quinti can be used as a donor muscle for thumb opposition transfer, most commonly in children. It has a very short tendon and cannot be used for anti-claw transfers. In addition, due to this patient's injury, the abductor digiti quinti is likely denervated and would not be functional for a transfer.


Flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) of the long finger can be used for anti-claw transfers. The tendon can be split along the plane of Camper's chiasm to create two distal slips for insertion. It is well suited as an anti-claw transfer in patients with isolated ulnar nerve palsy. The FDS tendon cannot be split into four slips for insertion, as would be needed in this patient, and the power of one FDS muscle is insufficient to correct clawing in four fingers. In addition, the FDS resides superficial to the median nerve. In a patient who sustained a forearm laceration with injury to the median nerve, the overlying FDS is also likely to have been injured.


Pronator teres is the most common donor motor to restore wrist extension in patients with radial nerve palsy. It has a very short tendon and is not used for anti-claw transfers.


References
1. Alagoz MS, Uysal AC, Tuccar E, et al. Morphologic assessment of the tendon graft donor sites: palmaris longus, plantaris, tensor fascia lata. J Craniofac Surg. 2008 Jan;19(1):246-250.
2. Davis TRC. Median and ulnar nerve palsy. In: Wolfe SW, Pederson WC, Hotchkiss RN, et al, eds. Green's Operative Hand Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia: Churchill Livingstone; 2011:1093-1137.
3. Wehb√© MA. Tendon graft donor sites. J Hand Surg Am. 1992 Nov;17(6):1130-1132.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old female patient presents to the emergency room for assessment of jaw fractures 12 hours following a horse kick to the face. Clinical examination reveals an anterior open bite with bilateral crossbites. CT imaging is provided. What is the most suitable treatment approach at this time?
A) Closed reduction of all jaw fractures with intermaxillary fixation
B) Open reduction and internal fixation of all jaw fractures
C) Open reduction and internal fixation of parasymphyseal and condylar fractures, closed reduction of ramus fracture, with intermaxillary fixation
D) Open reduction and internal fixation of parasymphyseal fracture, closed reduction of condylar and ramus fractures, with intermaxillary fixation
E) Conservative observation only
questions.answer:
D)
Pediatric mandibular fractures require more conservative treatment compared to adult fractures due to mixed dentition, skeletal elasticity, and bone remodeling potential during growth. Surgical intervention must consider potential growth disturbances. The displaced parasymphyseal fracture requires open reduction and internal fixation for stability, while the condylar and ramus fractures can be managed with closed reduction and intermaxillary fixation. A is incorrect because closed reduction alone won't provide adequate stability for the displaced parasymphyseal fracture. B is incorrect because the condylar fracture fragments are too small for internal fixation due to their intracapsular location. C is incorrect because the condylar fracture cannot be internally fixated due to fragment size limitations. E is incorrect because the extent and displacement of fractures necessitate active treatment rather than observation alone.

questions.question:
A healthy 22-lb (10-kg), 2-year-old male patient is undergoing removal of a 5 × 5-cm facial arteriovenous malformation. To minimize operative bleeding, which solution should be infiltrated around the lesion?
A) 20 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine with 1:100,000 epinephrine
B) 20 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine with 1:200,000 epinephrine
C) 20 mL of 1.0% lidocaine with 1:100,000 epinephrine
D) 20 mL of 1.0% lidocaine with 1:200,000 epinephrine
E) 20 mL of 1:200,000 epinephrine
questions.answer:
E)
For hemostasis during vascular lesion removal, 20 mL of 1:200,000 epinephrine solution is most appropriate. The safe epinephrine dose for this 10-kg child is approximately 30 mL (3 mL/kg) every 10 minutes, making this volume acceptable. A is incorrect because 20 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine (50 mg total) exceeds the maximum safe dose of 3 mg/kg (30 mg) for this child. B is incorrect for the same reason regarding bupivacaine dosage limits. C is incorrect because 20 mL of 1% lidocaine (200 mg total) far exceeds the maximum safe dose of 7 mg/kg (70 mg) for this patient. D is incorrect because it still contains excessive lidocaine despite the lower epinephrine concentration.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old female patient with abdominal and waist lipodystrophy is scheduled for suction-assisted lipectomy under general anesthesia. The anesthesiologist needs information about wetting solution volumes for fluid management planning. The surgeon expects to remove 1.5 L of lipoaspirate. Using the superwet technique, what volume of subcutaneous infiltration fluid is appropriate?
A) 0 mL
B) 375 mL
C) 750 mL
D) 1500 mL
E) 3000 mL
questions.answer:
D)
The superwet technique uses a 1:1 ratio of infiltration solution to expected lipoaspirate volume. With anticipated removal of 1.5 L of lipoaspirate, 1500 mL of wetting solution should be infiltrated. This technique provides excellent hemostasis and pain control while maintaining appropriate fluid balance. A is incorrect because this represents the dry technique with no wetting solution. B is incorrect because this volume represents the wet technique, which uses a standard 200-300 mL regardless of aspirate volume. C is incorrect because 750 mL doesn't correspond to any established wetting technique ratio. E is incorrect because 3000 mL represents the tumescent technique with a 2:1 or 3:1 ratio of solution to aspirate.

questions.question:
A 62-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with mandibular osteosarcoma. Microsurgical reconstruction using a free osseocutaneous iliac bone flap is planned. What is the vascular supply for this flap?
A) Deep circumflex iliac vessels
B) Deep inferior epigastric vessels
C) Superficial circumflex iliac vessels
D) Superficial femoral vessels
E) Superficial inferior epigastric vessels
questions.answer:
A)
The deep circumflex iliac artery (DCIA) provides the vascular pedicle for the iliac bone flap. This vessel originates from the external iliac artery's lateral aspect and travels toward the anterior superior iliac spine, giving off an ascending branch before coursing along the iliac crest's inner lip to supply the bone. B is incorrect because the deep inferior epigastric vessels supply TRAM and DIEP flaps from the abdomen. C is incorrect because the superficial circumflex iliac vessels supply the groin flap, not the bone-containing iliac flap. D is incorrect because superficial femoral vessels supply muscle flaps like the sartorius. E is incorrect because superficial inferior epigastric vessels supply the SIEA flap, which contains only skin and subcutaneous tissue.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male patient has a clean cheek laceration with complete facial nerve transection. What is the latest time point after which primary repair is unlikely to restore facial nerve function?
A) 3 weeks
B) 6 weeks
C) 6 months
D) 12 months
E) 24 months
questions.answer:
D)
Facial nerve injuries in young patients can tolerate delayed repair up to 12 months post-injury while still achieving functional recovery with tension-free primary repair. This extended timeframe distinguishes facial nerve repair from other peripheral nerve repairs. A is incorrect because 3 weeks is too early and primary repair would still be highly successful. B is incorrect because 6 weeks is well within the optimal repair window. C is incorrect because 6 months is still within the acceptable timeframe for facial nerve repair. E is incorrect because by 24 months, significant muscle degeneration from denervation has occurred, making primary nerve repair ineffective and requiring consideration of muscle transfer procedures instead.

questions.question:
What percentage of individuals with isolated cleft palate are most prone to developing middle ear fluid accumulation?
A) 10%
B) 30%
C) 50%
D) 70%
E) 90%
questions.answer:
E)
Over 90% of individuals develop chronic middle ear fluid accumulation before surgical repair. This high prevalence occurs due to eustachian tube dysfunction associated with cleft palate. All cleft palate patients require hearing assessment and middle ear evaluation. A is incorrect because 10% significantly underestimates the actual prevalence. B is incorrect because 30% is far below the documented rates. C is incorrect because 50% still underrepresents the true frequency. D is incorrect because even 70% falls short of the actual documented prevalence of over 90%.

questions.question:
A 64-year-old left-handed male has Dupuytren contracture affecting his hand. Examination reveals contractures at the small finger MCP joint (35°) and PIP joint (30°), plus ring finger MCP joint (30°) and PIP joint (15°). Needle aponeurotomy is being considered. Which disease-related factor best predicts the need for repeat intervention after this treatment?
A) Dominant hand involvement
B) MCP contracture severity
C) Older age
D) PIP contracture severity
E) Presence of a natatory cord
questions.answer:
D)
The severity of PIP joint contracture is the strongest disease-related predictor of requiring repeat intervention. Research involving 848 interventions demonstrated that PIP contracture degree and younger patient age were the primary predictors of re-intervention. A is incorrect because dominant versus non-dominant hand involvement showed no difference in re-intervention rates. B is incorrect because MCP contracture severity was not an independent predictor of repeat procedures. C is incorrect because older age actually reduces the likelihood of re-intervention, while younger age increases it. E is incorrect because natatory cords cause web space contractures but don't independently predict MCP or PIP joint re-intervention.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old walking patient with S2-level spina bifida requires closure of a stage IV ischial pressure ulcer. A rotational flap is planned for reconstruction. Which flap option best balances wound coverage with preservation of walking ability?
A) Gluteal thigh
B) Gluteus muscle
C) Hamstring
D) Reverse latissimus dorsi
E) Vastus lateralis
questions.answer:
A)
The gluteal thigh flap, based on the descending gluteal artery, is typically a fasciocutaneous flap that minimally impacts ambulation or lower extremity function. This patient retains complete upper extremity, thoracic, hip, and knee muscle function with S2 paraplegia. B is incorrect because gluteus muscle sacrifice could affect hip stability and function. C is incorrect because hamstring muscles are primary knee flexors, and their loss would severely compromise this ambulatory patient's walking ability. D is incorrect because reverse latissimus dorsi cannot reach the ischial region adequately. E is incorrect because vastus lateralis is a major knee extensor, and its sacrifice would weaken quadriceps function despite compensation from other quadriceps muscles.

questions.question:
Which method provides the best objective, dynamic assessment of nasal airway patency and respiratory function?
A) Anterior rhinoscopy
B) Cottle maneuver
C) Nasal endoscopy
D) Rhinomanometry
E) Sound wave analysis
questions.answer:
D)
Rhinomanometry provides objective, dynamic evaluation of nasal airway patency by measuring transnasal pressure and airflow to determine nasal resistance. This quantifies the difficulty of airflow through the nose during active breathing. A is incorrect because anterior rhinoscopy, while objective for visualization, relies on subjective examiner assessment of obstruction. B is incorrect because the Cottle maneuver is a subjective test performed by the patient. C is incorrect because nasal endoscopy provides static anatomical visualization but doesn't measure dynamic airflow function. E is incorrect because acoustic rhinometry using sound waves provides static geometric measurements of nasal cavity cross-sections and volumes, not dynamic airflow assessment.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old woman seeks consultation about breast reconstruction revision after mastectomy for breast cancer. She mentions taking adjuvant medication that blocks her body's natural breast development mechanisms but cannot recall the drug name. Which medication is she most likely receiving?
A) Alkylating agent (cyclophosphamide)
B) Anthracycline (doxorubicin)
C) Aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole)
D) Platinum agent (cisplatin)
E) Taxane (paclitaxel)
questions.answer:
C)
Aromatase inhibitors like anastrozole block the conversion of androgens to estrogens, thereby interfering with estrogen-mediated breast tissue growth mechanisms. Estrogens naturally promote breast development and also fuel many breast cancers. A is incorrect because cyclophosphamide is a chemotherapy agent that doesn't specifically target hormonal breast growth pathways. B is incorrect because doxorubicin is a chemotherapy drug that doesn't interfere with natural breast development hormones. D is incorrect because cisplatin is a chemotherapy agent without specific anti-hormonal effects on breast growth. E is incorrect because paclitaxel is a chemotherapy drug that doesn't target the hormonal mechanisms of breast development.

questions.question:
A 69-year-old female patient presents for consultation regarding lower eyelid cosmetic surgery. Physical examination reveals a downward canthal tilt. Lower eyelid snap-back assessment demonstrates 8 mm of distraction. Transcutaneous lower blepharoplasty with fat repositioning is scheduled. Which of the following surgical interventions is most appropriate to prevent postoperative lower eyelid malposition?
A) Horizontal wedge resection
B) Lateral canthoplasty
C) Orbicularis muscle repositioning
D) Posterior lamellar grafting
E) Tarsorrhaphy
questions.answer:
B)
Lateral canthal reinforcement addresses preexisting lower eyelid laxity and helps prevent post-blepharoplasty lower eyelid malposition. The treatment selection depends on the degree of eyelid laxity. For significant lower eyelid laxity (exceeding 6 mm of eyelid distraction), lateral canthoplasty with lateral cantholysis provides enhanced superior mobility and accurate positioning of the lower canthal tendon within the orbital rim. A) is incorrect because horizontal wedge resection addresses horizontal laxity but is not recommended for patients with negative canthal tilt who require lateral eyelid resuspension. C) is incorrect because orbicularis repositioning is only suitable for mild eyelid laxity (1-2 mm distraction). D) is incorrect because posterior lamellar grafting is not appropriate for this condition. E) is incorrect because tarsorrhaphy is only used for minimal laxity cases as temporary external support.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female with hypertension presents to the emergency department 1.5 hours following burn injuries from a residential fire. Initial assessment reveals deep partial-thickness burns covering 35% of the torso, non-circumferential full-thickness burns affecting 5% of the left forearm, and superficial burns on 2% of the head. Besides time since injury, which of the following shared components of burn assessment should be utilized in both the Parkland and Brooke formulas for calculating fluid resuscitation in this patient?
A) Total body surface area (including superficial, partial-thickness, and full-thickness burns), gender, weight
B) Total body surface area (including superficial, partial-thickness, and full-thickness burns), weight
C) Total body surface area (including partial-thickness and full-thickness burns), age, weight
D) Total body surface area (including partial-thickness and full-thickness burns), gender, weight
E) Total body surface area (including partial-thickness and full-thickness burns), weight
questions.answer:
E)
Both the Brooke and Parkland resuscitation formulas calculate fluid requirements by multiplying a specific fluid amount by the total body surface area (determined by partial-thickness and full-thickness burns only) and the patient's weight in kilograms. The fluid is administered based on time from injury, with half given in the first 8 hours and half in the subsequent 16 hours. This serves as a guideline that can be modified based on physiologic parameters like urine output. A) and B) are incorrect because superficial burns are not included in TBSA calculations. C) and D) are incorrect because age and gender are not factors in these formulas.

questions.question:
What mechanism triggers epithelial cell movement across an acute skin wound?
A) Myofibroblast contraction
B) Collagen deposition in the wound
C) Fibrin-fibronectin clot formation
D) Loss of contact inhibition
E) Anti-inflammatory mediator release
questions.answer:
D)
Epithelial cell movement begins with the loss of contact inhibition and proceeds from the wound edges and adnexal structures. Cell proliferation occurs within 48-72 hours, creating a thin epithelial bridge across the wound. Epidermal growth factors play a crucial role in this process. A) is incorrect because myofibroblasts are responsible for wound contraction, not epithelialization. B) is incorrect because collagen deposition occurs during the remodeling phase of healing. C) is incorrect because fibronectin serves as an adhesion molecule but doesn't initiate epithelial migration. E) is incorrect because cytokine release from platelets is important for the initial hemostatic phase, not epithelial migration.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old female seeks consultation for primary breast augmentation and is choosing between form-stable shaped implants and less cohesive round silicone gel implants. She asks about the advantages of each implant type. Compared to smooth round silicone gel implants, highly cohesive form-stable gel implants demonstrate reduced rates of which of the following complications?
A) Capsular contracture
B) Implant malposition
C) Infection
D) Seroma
questions.answer:
A)
Form-stable silicone gel implants are fifth-generation, anatomically shaped, textured implants with enhanced molecular cross-linking. They maintain their form and reduce folding and rippling incidence, resulting in significantly lower capsular contracture rates compared to other implant types. B) is incorrect because shaped implants actually have higher malposition rates since maintaining proper orientation is crucial. D) is incorrect because form-stable implants are more susceptible to seroma formation, possibly due to their textured surface. C) is incorrect because infection rates remain comparable between implant types.

questions.question:
A patient with breast cancer history undergoes nipple-sparing mastectomy of the right breast with immediate implant reconstruction. Ten months postoperatively, the patient begins experiencing nipple sensation recovery. Which nerve is most likely responsible for providing sensation to the nipple-areola complex in this patient?
A) Anterior branch of the fourth intercostal nerve
B) Anterior branch of the second intercostal nerve
C) Lateral branch of the fifth intercostal nerve
D) Lateral branch of the fourth intercostal nerve
E) Lateral branch of the second intercostal nerve
F) Lateral branch of the third intercostal nerve
questions.answer:
A)
The nipple and areola receive innervation from both anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of the third, fourth, or fifth intercostal nerves. The second and sixth intercostal nerve branches only supply breast skin. While the fourth intercostal nerve's lateral branch supplies nipples in 93% of cases, it penetrates deep fascia and travels through glandular tissue, making it vulnerable during mastectomy. The anterior cutaneous branches follow a superficial path in subcutaneous tissue, reaching the nipple laterally, making the anterior branch of the fourth intercostal nerve most likely to provide sensation after nipple-sparing mastectomy. B) and E) are incorrect because second intercostal branches only innervate breast skin. C), D), and F) are incorrect because while these lateral branches may contribute to nipple innervation, they are more likely to be disrupted during mastectomy due to their deeper course.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old electrical worker arrives at the emergency room following accidental contact with a high-voltage electrical line. Which anatomical site would most likely sustain the most severe damage?
A) Thoracic wall
B) Cervical region
C) Shoulder region
D) Upper extremity
E) Wrist area
questions.answer:
E)
The wrist area sustains the most severe electrical injury due to its smaller cross-sectional area, which concentrates current density and increases tissue damage. Injury severity is inversely related to tissue cross-sectional area, making distal extremities like wrists and ankles most vulnerable. A is incorrect because the chest wall has a larger cross-sectional area that distributes current more widely. B is incorrect because the neck, while narrow, is not typically the primary contact point in electrical injuries. C is incorrect because the shoulder has greater tissue mass to distribute electrical current. D is incorrect because the upper arm has more tissue volume than the wrist to carry current.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old female patient with cleft lip and palate history requires secondary alveolar bone reconstruction. Harvesting from the iliac crest is being considered. What advantage does iliac crest bone grafting offer compared to bone morphogenetic protein for this patient?
A) Increased graft volume availability
B) Scaffold properties for bone formation
C) Growth-promoting factors
D) Shorter surgical duration
E) Faster patient recovery
questions.answer:
B)
Iliac crest bone graft provides osteoconductive properties, serving as a natural scaffold for new bone formation, while bone morphogenetic protein requires an additional carrier material for osteoconduction. The autologous bone graft contains both the structural framework and cellular components necessary for bone regeneration. A is incorrect because bone morphogenetic protein can provide greater volume than what may be harvested from small children. C is incorrect because bone morphogenetic protein provides superior osteoinductive properties compared to autologous bone. D is incorrect because bone morphogenetic protein reduces operative time by eliminating the need for graft harvest. E is incorrect because bone morphogenetic protein offers faster recovery by avoiding donor site morbidity.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old female patient has bilateral breast reduction surgery with 800 grams removed from each breast and submitted for histopathologic examination. Which pathology finding would most warrant consultation with an oncologic breast specialist?
A) Apocrine cell changes
B) Abnormal lobular cell proliferation
C) Benign breast tumor
D) Ductal papillary lesions
E) Fibrous tissue proliferation
questions.answer:
B)
Atypical lobular hyperplasia represents abnormal cell proliferation that significantly increases breast cancer risk, requiring oncologic evaluation for potential chemoprevention and enhanced surveillance strategies. This high-risk lesion necessitates multidisciplinary management planning. A is incorrect because apocrine metaplasia is a benign finding with no increased cancer risk. C is incorrect because fibroadenoma is a common benign tumor requiring no additional intervention. D is incorrect because papillomatosis, while requiring monitoring, does not carry the same cancer risk as atypical hyperplasia. E is incorrect because sclerosing adenosis is a benign proliferative condition with minimal cancer risk elevation.

questions.question:
A patient returns 6 months following bilateral vertical breast lift surgery expressing dissatisfaction with her results. She measures 5 ft 5 in tall. Examination reveals nipple-to-sternal notch distance of 16 cm and nipple-to-inframammary fold distance of 14 cm on both sides. What is the most appropriate management approach?
A) Free nipple-areolar complex transfer
B) Dual-plane breast implant insertion
C) Subglandular implant placement
D) Lower pole skin excision at inframammary fold
E) Conservative management with massage therapy
questions.answer:
D)
The excessive nipple-to-inframammary fold distance of 14 cm indicates superior nipple malposition requiring lower pole skin resection to relocate the nipple to proper position, creating a T-shaped scar pattern. This corrects the technical error from the initial surgery. A is incorrect because free nipple grafts would create poor aesthetic scarring and are unnecessary for this positional problem. B is incorrect because dual-plane implants will not address the fundamental nipple positioning issue. C is incorrect because subglandular implants similarly fail to correct nipple malposition. E is incorrect because at 6 months post-surgery, significant positional changes are unlikely to occur with conservative measures alone.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old female patient presents seeking breast surgery due to cosmetic concerns. Physical examination reveals narrow breast base, enlarged areolar diameter, and areolar tissue protrusion. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Absent nipple development
B) Underdeveloped breast tissue
C) Chest wall developmental anomaly
D) Incomplete breast maturation
E) Constricted breast deformity
questions.answer:
E)
The clinical triad of constricted base width, enlarged areola, and areolar herniation is pathognomonic for tuberous breast deformity, a congenital condition affecting breast shape and development. These specific anatomical features distinguish this condition from other breast developmental abnormalities. A is incorrect because athelia refers to complete nipple absence, not the described findings. B is incorrect because hypomastia involves small breast volume without the specific structural abnormalities described. C is incorrect because Poland syndrome typically involves chest wall and pectoralis muscle defects, not isolated breast base constriction. D is incorrect because pubertal arrest would not produce the characteristic base constriction seen in tuberous breasts.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old male patient is scheduled for elective surgical correction of a large, recurring ventral hernia. Due to loss of abdominal domain, plastic surgery consultation is obtained. The surgical plan includes posterior component separation with biologic mesh placement. Superior to the arcuate line, which of the following anatomical structures combine to create the posterior rectus sheath?
A) Aponeurosis of external oblique and aponeurosis of internal oblique
B) Aponeuroses of external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis
C) Aponeurosis of internal oblique and aponeurosis of transversus abdominis
D) Transversalis fascia and peritoneal membrane
questions.answer:
C)

Thorough knowledge of anterior abdominal wall anatomy is essential for successful posterior component separation procedures. Superior to the arcuate line, the anterior rectus sheath forms from the external oblique aponeurosis and the anterior portion of the internal oblique aponeurosis. The posterior rectus sheath forms from the posterior portion of the internal oblique aponeurosis combined with the transversus abdominis aponeurosis. The rectus abdominis muscle lies between these anterior and posterior sheaths above the arcuate line. Inferior to the arcuate line, all three muscle aponeuroses (external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis) contribute to the anterior rectus sheath, while no posterior rectus sheath exists at this level. Below the arcuate line, only transversalis fascia and peritoneum separate the rectus muscle from abdominal contents. Option A is incorrect because it describes only part of the posterior sheath formation. Option B is incorrect because it describes the anterior sheath composition below the arcuate line. Option D is incorrect because these structures are found below the arcuate line where no posterior rectus sheath exists.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old female patient undergoes conjunctival and Müller muscle excision for ptosis correction. Which of the following anatomical structures lies directly anterior to the Müller muscle?
A) Capsulopalpebral fascia
B) Central fat compartment
C) Levator palpebrae superioris muscle
D) Lockwood ligament
E) Retro-orbicularis oculi fat
questions.answer:
C)

The upper eyelid anatomy consists of sequential layers from superficial to deep: skin, orbicularis oculi muscle, retro-orbicularis oculi fat, orbital septum, orbital fat pads (central and medial in the upper lid), levator palpebrae superioris muscle with its aponeurosis, Müller muscle, and conjunctiva. During a Fasanella-Servat ptosis correction procedure, the conjunctiva and Müller muscle are clamped and excised above the tarsal plate margin. Following this resection, the levator muscle is exposed at the wound base, confirming its position immediately anterior to the Müller muscle. Options A and D are incorrect because capsulopalpebral fascia and Lockwood ligament are lower eyelid structures - the capsulopalpebral fascia attaches to the inferior tarsal border and forms part of the lower lid retractors, while Lockwood ligament provides globe support and surrounds the inferior rectus and oblique muscles. Option B is incorrect because the central fat pad is located more superficially, anterior to the levator muscle. Option E is incorrect because retro-orbicularis oculi fat lies much more superficially, just deep to the orbicularis muscle.

questions.question:
A 6-month-old male infant with a birth-related brachial plexus injury presents for assessment. Physical examination reveals the left elbow maintained in extension with the arm positioned in internal rotation. Active finger and wrist flexion is present. Finger and wrist extension demonstrates weakness; anti-gravity elbow extension testing shows weakness. No active elbow flexion or shoulder abduction is observed; Horner's sign is not present. Which of the following anatomical structures is most likely affected?
A) C7 nerve roots
B) C8-T1 nerve roots
C) Lateral cord
D) Posterior cord
E) Upper trunk
questions.answer:
E)

This infant demonstrates typical features of upper trunk (C5-6) or Erb's palsy, characterized by absent or weak elbow flexion, shoulder abduction and external rotation, with relatively preserved elbow extension and distal hand/wrist flexion. The characteristic "waiter's tip" positioning indicates that lower nerve root (C8-T1) function remains relatively intact. Option A is incorrect because isolated C7 root injury is rare and would primarily affect radial nerve-innervated muscles including wrist/finger extensors and forearm pronators, not the biceps or deltoid muscles seen in this case. Option B is incorrect because C8-T1 root injury would cause weakness in intrinsic hand muscles and finger flexors, which are preserved in this patient. Option C is incorrect because lateral cord injury would affect biceps and pectoral muscle function but would not impair deltoid or periscapular muscle activity as observed. Option D is incorrect because posterior cord injury would primarily affect radial nerve-innervated muscles and would not alter biceps or deltoid function as demonstrated in this patient.

questions.question:
A 10-year-old male child presents for evaluation of a 6-month history of a slowly enlarging left cheek mass that is soft, mobile, and measures 4 cm in diameter. No associated lymphadenopathy is present. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy confirms pleomorphic adenoma located anterior to and outside the parotid gland. Following complete surgical excision, the parents should be informed that the recurrence rate is most likely which of the following?
A) 1%
B) 10%
C) 20%
D) 40%
questions.answer:
B)

Pleomorphic adenoma represents an uncommon tumor that typically arises in the parotid gland but can occur in submandibular, sublingual, and other minor salivary gland sites in decreasing frequency. Despite being a benign tumor, pleomorphic adenoma carries a recurrence rate of 6 to 15% following excision. Complete excision with wide margins is optimal for this location, though careful attention must be paid to preserve facial nerve branches during dissection. Option A is incorrect because a 1% recurrence rate is unrealistically low for pleomorphic adenoma, which has a well-documented higher recurrence potential. Option C is incorrect because a 20% recurrence rate exceeds the typical range reported in the literature for properly excised pleomorphic adenomas. Option D is incorrect because a 40% recurrence rate is significantly higher than expected and would suggest inadequate surgical technique or incomplete excision.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents for evaluation of a 2.5-cm, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the left oral floor. Radiographic studies demonstrate cortical mandibular invasion without enlarged cervical lymph nodes or distant metastases. Tracheostomy has been performed and immediate reconstruction is planned. Which of the following represents the most appropriate surgical management for this malignancy?
A) Wide local excision only
B) Wide local excision with marginal mandibulectomy
C) Wide local excision with neck dissection
D) Wide local excision, marginal mandibulectomy, and neck dissection
E) Wide local excision, segmental mandibulectomy, and neck dissection
questions.answer:
E)

This represents a T4aN0M0 oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma based on radiographic evidence of cortical mandibular invasion. According to AJCC staging criteria, cortical bone invasion classifies the tumor as T4a. When cortical mandibular invasion is present, segmental mandibulectomy is required, involving full-thickness removal of the affected mandible with disease-free margins achieved through osteotomies. Although the neck appears clinically and radiographically negative (N0), surgical neck dissection is typically performed due to the significant risk of occult nodal metastases (20% or higher in some studies) and to expose recipient vessels for potential microvascular reconstruction. Option A is incorrect because wide excision alone is inadequate for T4a disease with bone invasion. Option B is incorrect because marginal mandibulectomy is only appropriate when tumors abut the mandible or invade periosteum without cortical invasion. Option C is incorrect because it fails to address the documented cortical bone invasion. Option D is incorrect because marginal mandibulectomy is insufficient for cortical bone invasion, which requires segmental resection.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old male seeks consultation due to dissatisfaction with his fingernail appearance following a hand burn injury. Upon nail removal, examination reveals involvement of greater than one-third of the nail bed. Which of the following interventions is most likely to enhance nail appearance?
A) Nail bed debridement with full-thickness skin grafting
B) Nail bed dermabrasion with silicone rubber stent placement
C) Scar tissue excision, eponychial flap reconstruction, and toe nail bed grafting
D) Cross-finger flap reconstruction to distal pad with distal phalanx bone grafting
E) Scar resection, nail bed elevation for advancement, and primary nail bed repair
questions.answer:
C)
The optimal approach is scar tissue excision, eponychial flap reconstruction, and toe nail bed grafting. This patient presents with nail bed synechia at the lateral eponychial fold area. The problem involves two components: contracted eponychial fold adherent to the nail bed, and scarred nail bed tissue. Option A is incorrect because full-thickness skin grafting will not address the patient's cosmetic concerns. Option B is incorrect because dermabrasion and stenting cannot resolve the nail bed scarring or improve the deformity. Option D is incorrect because cross-finger flap with bone graft is suitable for hook nail deformity, not scarred nail bed conditions. Option E is incorrect because advancement and primary closure is limited to defects of 1mm or less and would likely fail in this extensive scenario. Given these limitations, scar resection with grafting from adjacent finger or toe combined with eponychial fold flap procedure offers the best chance for correcting the deformity.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female patient presents with the dental configuration illustrated in the provided diagram. Which of the following most accurately characterizes this dental relationship?
A) Angle class I
B) Angle class II
C) Angle class III
D) Negative overjet
E) Overbite
questions.answer:
B)
The images demonstrate an Angle class II relationship. The Angle classification describes the positional relationship between the maxillary first molar's mesial buccal cusp and the mandibular first molar's buccal groove. In class II, the maxillary mesiobuccal cusp sits anterior to the mandibular buccal groove. Option A is incorrect because class I involves alignment of the mesiobuccal cusp with the buccal groove. Option C is incorrect because class III occurs when the maxillary mesiobuccal cusp lies posterior to the mandibular buccal groove. Option D is incorrect because negative overjet refers to a specific horizontal discrepancy, not the molar relationship shown. Option E is incorrect because overbite describes vertical overlap between central incisor incisal surfaces, not the molar relationship demonstrated in this case.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old female is evaluated for rapid breast enlargement. She reports significant back pain and postural issues. Her parents note her bra size progressed from 34B to 34E at age 13, with no further growth over the past 12 months. She measures 5 ft 5 in (165 cm) tall and weighs 140 lb (63 kg). Which of the following represents the most appropriate treatment?
A) Antiestrogen hormonal treatment
B) Diet and exercise regimen to achieve 15 lb (6.8 kg) weight loss
C) Reduction mammaplasty
D) Six-month testosterone injection series
