E) Observation until patient reaches 18 years of age
questions.answer:
C)
Reduction mammaplasty is the appropriate treatment for this case of juvenile hypertrophy. When bilateral breast enlargement occurs disproportionately at menarche and stabilizes for approximately one year, surgical intervention is indicated. Option A is incorrect because antiestrogen therapy has only anecdotal evidence supporting its use. Option B is incorrect because diet and exercise would provide minimal size reduction, whereas typical resections involve 1800g or more of tissue. Option D is incorrect because testosterone injections are not indicated for juvenile hypertrophy. Option E is incorrect because while initial observation is appropriate to allow full manifestation of the process, continued observation after one year of stability is not warranted when surgical intervention can address the patient's symptoms and concerns.

questions.question:
A 12-month-old male infant is evaluated for complete right thumb absence. Physical examination reveals no additional limb abnormalities. Radiographic imaging confirms absent thumb metacarpal. Which of the following represents the optimal reconstructive approach?
A) Great toe-to-thumb transfer
B) Huber transfer
C) Index finger pollicization
D) Osteoplastic procedure
E) Prosthesis
questions.answer:
C)
Index finger pollicization is the most appropriate reconstruction for Type V thumb deformity. This procedure involves neurovascular pedicle transfer of the index finger, often with its metacarpal, and is the only satisfactory method for basal joint reconstruction. Option A is incorrect because great toe-to-thumb transfer requires presence of most of the first metacarpal and cannot reconstruct an adequate basilar joint when the CMC joint is absent. Option B is incorrect because Huber transfer is used for Type IIIA deformities to create opposition when absent, not for complete thumb absence. Option D is incorrect because osteoplastic reconstruction results in a stiff, broad, insensate thumb requiring multiple stages and is rarely performed today. Option E is incorrect because prostheses lack sensation, provide only a stable post, and are more of an encumbrance than benefit in congenital thumb reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old male with T12 paraplegia presents with a Stage IV sacral pressure ulcer. The chronic, persistent wound exposes bone structures. Multiple bedside debridements have maintained a clean, healthy-appearing wound bed. Upon admission, the patient demonstrates elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Before definitive wound coverage, which of the following represents the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Bone biopsy and culture
B) CT scan with IV contrast
C) Gadolinium-enhanced MRI
D) Tagged white blood cell scan
E) Triple phase bone scan
questions.answer:
A)
Bone biopsy and culture is the most appropriate next step for this patient with chronic Stage IV pressure ulcer and elevated ESR. Patients with chronic exposed Stage III or IV wounds have very high risk of pelvic osteomyelitis, which requires IV antibiotic treatment and bony debridement before coverage. Bone biopsy provides definitive diagnosis and guides antibiotic therapy by sampling deeper pelvic bone rather than just superficially exposed bone. Option B is incorrect because CT with IV contrast is less sensitive for localized inflammation and is a last-line diagnostic test. Option C is incorrect because while gadolinium-enhanced MRI can assess for osteomyelitis, it is used when bone biopsy is unavailable. Option D is incorrect because tagged white blood cell scan is also a second-line test when biopsy is not feasible. Option E is incorrect because bone scans have high false-positive rates in patients with open wounds, making them unreliable for diagnosis in this setting.

questions.question:
A 9-year-old girl is evaluated because of an 8-month history of alopecia of the scalp caused by a skin graft over the periosteum. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate method to correct this patient‚Äos alopecia?


A) Coverage with a latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous free flap
B) Follicular hair transplantation
C) Full-thickness skin grafting from hair-bearing scalp
D) Serial excision of the skin graft
E) Tissue expansion
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


Tissue expansion effectively expands hair-bearing scalp that can then be rotated, advanced, and/or transposed over the area of alopecia to correct the deformity. A latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous free flap does not contain hair, and thus, would cause a similar area of alopecia. Follicular hair transplantation would not be efficacious for a large area of alopecia, and the split-thickness graft over periosteum would be insufficient tissue to accept the grafts. Serial excision of the skin graft is not possible because of the large defect and absence of normal scalp tissue on either side of the defect. A full-thickness graft from the hair-bearing scalp would cause a similar area of donor site alopecia.


References
1. Seitz IA, Gottlieb LJ. Reconstruction of scalp and forehead defects. Clin Plast Surg. 2009 Jul;36(3):355-377.
2. Leedy JE, Janis JE, Rohrich RJ. Reconstruction of acquired scalp defects: an algorithmic approach. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2005 Sep 15;116(4):54e-72e.
3. Ridgway EB, Cowan JB, Donelan MB, et al. Pediatric burn-related scalp alopecia treated with tissue expansion and the incidence of associated facial burn injuries. J Burn Care Res. 2010 May-June;31(3):409-413.

questions.question:
A 39-year-old female patient has just completed successful immediate bilateral breast reconstruction using free deep inferior epigastric artery perforator flaps. Postoperative monitoring of the flaps is being planned. During which of the following postoperative time frames is vascular compromise most likely to develop?
A) 0-1 days
B) 2-3 days
C) 4-5 days
D) 6-7 days
E) 8-9 days
questions.answer:
A)
Vascular compromise in free flaps most commonly occurs within the first 24 hours postoperatively. This early period represents the highest risk time for perfusion issues, making intensive monitoring crucial during this window to enable timely intervention and maximize salvage potential. B is incorrect because while complications can occur at 2-3 days, they are less frequent than in the immediate postoperative period. C is incorrect because vascular events at 4-5 days are uncommon and more difficult to salvage successfully. D is incorrect because complications at 6-7 days are rare and typically have poor salvage outcomes. E is incorrect because vascular compromise at 8-9 days is very uncommon and usually not salvageable.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient returns for evaluation 6 days following bilateral upper eyelid blepharoplasty with right levator aponeurosis repair. Before surgery, she had bilateral levator function of 13 mm and right eyelid ptosis of 4 mm, with no left eyelid drooping. Current examination reveals 2 mm of left upper eyelid ptosis, while the right eyelid position is appropriate. What best accounts for these findings?
A) Hering law
B) Horner syndrome
C) Müller maneuver
D) Todd paresis
E) von Graefe sign
questions.answer:
A)
Hering law explains the equal neural stimulation sent to both levator muscles regardless of individual eyelid requirements. Initially, the significant right ptosis required strong neural signals to both eyelids. After correcting the right ptosis, the neural drive decreased, revealing the previously masked mild left ptosis. B is incorrect because Horner syndrome involves sympathetic denervation causing ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis, which doesn't match this scenario. C is incorrect because the Müller maneuver is a respiratory technique used to assess airway patency, not related to eyelid function. D is incorrect because Todd paresis refers to temporary weakness following seizures, which is not applicable here. E is incorrect because von Graefe sign describes lid lag in downgaze associated with thyroid eye disease.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old male patient with a smoking history needs extensive mandibular reconstruction using a free vascularized fibula flap. When harvesting the flap via an anterior approach, which muscle should the surgeon expect to encounter immediately before incising the interosseous septum?
A) Extensor hallucis longus
B) Flexor hallucis longus
C) Soleus
D) Tibialis anterior
E) Tibialis posterior
questions.answer:
A)
The extensor hallucis longus is positioned directly anterior to the interosseous septum within the anterior compartment of the leg, making it the muscle encountered just before septum incision during fibula flap harvest. B is incorrect because the flexor hallucis longus resides in the deep posterior compartment, not adjacent to the interosseous septum anteriorly. C is incorrect because the soleus is located in the superficial posterior compartment, away from the anterior dissection plane. D is incorrect because the tibialis anterior lies medial to the typical fibula flap dissection pathway. E is incorrect because the tibialis posterior is found in the deep posterior compartment, not in the anterior approach area.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old construction worker has a 6-month history of ring finger tip ulceration with rest pain. His digital brachial index measures 0.45, and imaging shows ulnar artery occlusion. After 3 months of unsuccessful treatment with calcium channel blockers and aspirin, what is the most appropriate next step?
A) Fingertip amputation
B) Chemical sympathectomy
C) Ulnar artery reconstruction
D) Stellate ganglion block
E) Surgical sympathectomy
questions.answer:
C)
With a digital brachial index of 0.45 indicating critical ischemia, failed conservative management, and tissue ulceration, ulnar artery reconstruction is warranted to restore adequate perfusion and prevent tissue loss. A is incorrect because amputation should be reserved for cases where reconstruction is not feasible or has failed, not as initial surgical treatment. B is incorrect because chemical sympathectomy is a conservative measure that would be insufficient for this degree of ischemia with tissue breakdown. D is incorrect because stellate ganglion blocks are part of conservative management, which has already failed in this patient. E is incorrect because surgical sympathectomy alone would not address the critical ischemia indicated by the low digital brachial index.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male presents with persistent right hand pain 5 days after punching a wall. Examination reveals fifth carpometacarpal joint tenderness. Standard posteroanterior, oblique, and lateral radiographs from urgent care were interpreted as normal. Which additional radiographic view would be most helpful in establishing the diagnosis?
A) Anteroposterior with 30 degrees of pronation from full supination
B) Carpal tunnel view with wrist in full extension
C) Clenched fist lateral in neutral forearm position
D) Lateral with 15 degrees of supination from neutral forearm position
E) Posteroanterior with 45 degrees of supination from full pronation
questions.answer:
A)
The anteroposterior view with 30 degrees of pronation from full supination optimally profiles the hamate-fifth metacarpal articulation, making subtle fifth carpometacarpal joint injuries more visible when standard views appear normal. B is incorrect because the carpal tunnel view is designed to evaluate the carpal tunnel and wouldn't improve visualization of the fifth carpometacarpal joint. C is incorrect because a clenched fist lateral view is used to assess scapholunate instability, not fifth carpometacarpal joint pathology. D is incorrect because 15 degrees of supination doesn't provide the optimal angle for visualizing fifth carpometacarpal joint injuries. E is incorrect because 45 degrees of supination moves away from the ideal positioning needed to profile the fifth carpometacarpal articulation.

questions.question:
A 39-year-old woman seeks consultation for tummy tuck surgery. She has a medical history of significant uterine fibroids, and her gynecologist is planning a complete abdominal hysterectomy (TAH). The patient desires to have both the tummy tuck and the TAH performed simultaneously. What is the most appropriate response to this patient's request?
A) The surgeries can be safely combined regardless of the TAH surgical approach
B) The gynecologist may perform TAH, but the tummy tuck flap must be elevated first
C) The patient's thromboembolic risk is reduced by having one large operation
D) TAH cannot be performed together with tummy tuck surgery
questions.answer:
A)
Combining tummy tuck surgery with total abdominal hysterectomy has been proven safe in multiple studies, regardless of whether the TAH is performed via open, laparoscopic, or robotic approach. The combination offers advantages including single recovery period, reduced costs, and fewer anesthetic exposures. However, thromboembolic prophylaxis is essential due to prolonged operative time. B is incorrect because while the abdominoplasty flap can be raised first, it's not required and may make laparoscopic ports less stable. C is incorrect because thromboembolic risk actually increases with longer combined procedures, not decreases. D is incorrect because numerous studies have demonstrated the safety of combining these procedures.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old boy with submucous cleft palate history presents with ongoing velopharyngeal insufficiency. His surgical history includes Furlow palatoplasty performed 3 years prior, followed by revision to a superiorly based pharyngeal flap for continued hypernasality 1 year ago. Despite the second surgery and speech therapy, he showed no improvement. Physical examination reveals an intact, high and wide pharyngeal flap. Nasoendoscopy demonstrates patent lateral oronasal ports and poor palatal and lateral pharyngeal wall movement. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient?
A) Creation of a custom palatal elevator prosthesis
B) Revision of pharyngeal flap ports
C) Posterior wall enhancement with fat injection
D) Additional speech therapy with retraining
E) Sphincter pharyngoplasty procedure
questions.answer:
A)
The most appropriate treatment is fabrication of a custom palatal elevator prosthesis. This child's persistent hypernasality is most likely due to hypotonia of the speech muscles, which is neurogenic in nature and difficult to correct surgically. A palatal elevator prosthesis can mechanically close off the nasal cavity during speech by elevating the posterior soft palate. B is incorrect because port revision won't address the underlying muscle hypotonia. C is incorrect because posterior wall augmentation alone won't provide adequate closure without proper muscle function. D is incorrect because the child has already failed speech therapy, and additional therapy is unlikely to help with the neurologic component. E is incorrect because sphincter pharyngoplasty is not viable after pharyngeal flap surgery and would fail without adequate muscle function.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old woman presents to the clinic following humerus fracture fixation 17 months ago. Physical examination reveals inability to extend the wrist, fingers, and thumb. This deficit has been present since the injury occurred, with no functional recovery. Tendon transfers are being planned. Which muscle transfer is most appropriate for restoring wrist extension?
A) Brachioradialis
B) Flexor carpi ulnaris
C) Flexor digitorum profundus
D) Palmaris longus
E) Pronator teres
questions.answer:
E)
The pronator teres is the most appropriate muscle for wrist extension restoration. It is innervated by the median nerve (unaffected in radial nerve palsy), has adequate strength and excursion, and provides synergistic action that facilitates patient retraining. It is typically transferred to the extensor carpi radialis brevis for centrally oriented wrist extension. A is incorrect because the brachioradialis is radial nerve-innervated and non-functional in high radial nerve palsy. B is incorrect because flexor carpi ulnaris, while having adequate power, is not synergistic (wrist flexor powering wrist extension is counterintuitive). C is incorrect because flexor digitorum profundus lacks independent muscle bellies and would sacrifice important finger flexion. D is incorrect because palmaris longus lacks sufficient power for wrist extension, though it can be used for thumb extension.

questions.question:
A healthy 27-year-old woman is assessed 16 weeks following bilateral breast reduction using an inferior pedicle approach. Pathological analysis of removed tissue revealed no cancer. She reports a painful mass in the right breast first noticed 8 weeks post-operatively. She is concerned because her mother developed breast cancer at age 34. Physical examination of the affected breast reveals a palpable, mildly tender, discrete, firm 2-cm subcutaneous mass below the upper areolar margin. There is no skin puckering, nipple inversion, redness, or swelling. What is the most appropriate next management step?
A) Perform needle aspiration of the mass
B) Inject triamcinolone acetonide suspension 20 mg into the mass
C) Proceed with surgical excision of the mass
D) Refer the patient for oncology evaluation
E) Order ultrasonography and mammography of the affected breast
questions.answer:
E)
The most appropriate next step is to schedule ultrasonography and mammography of the affected breast. Post-surgical breast changes after reduction mammaplasty can include fat necrosis, oil cysts, fibrosis, organizing hematoma, and calcifications. Combined imaging helps differentiate benign post-surgical changes from malignancy before proceeding with any intervention. A is incorrect because aspiration should not be performed before imaging evaluation to characterize the mass. B is incorrect because injection of any substance into an undiagnosed breast mass is contraindicated. C is incorrect because surgical removal without proper imaging workup is premature and may be unnecessary. D is incorrect because oncology referral would be premature at this stage and would cause unnecessary patient anxiety before completing the diagnostic workup.

questions.question:
A newborn is found to have an underdeveloped thumb and an anorectal malformation. These clinical findings are most likely associated with which of the following conditions?
A) Fanconi anemia
B) Fetal alcohol syndrome
C) Holt-Oram syndrome
D) Thrombocytopenia-absent radius syndrome
E) VACTERL association
questions.answer:
E)
VACTERL association is most likely associated with these findings. VACTERL is a sporadic collection of anomalies including vertebral deformity, anal atresia, cardiac anomalies, tracheoesophageal fistula, renal agenesis, and limb deformities. The combination of hypoplastic thumb and anorectal malformation fits this pattern. A is incorrect because Fanconi anemia typically presents after age 3 with aplastic anemia, not anorectal malformations. B is incorrect because fetal alcohol syndrome primarily causes brain damage and growth problems, not thumb hypoplasia or anorectal malformations. C is incorrect because Holt-Oram syndrome involves radial deficiency with cardiac anomalies, not anorectal malformations. D is incorrect because thrombocytopenia-absent radius syndrome involves thrombocytopenia and radial deficiency, but not anorectal malformations.

questions.question:
A 14-year-old female presents for evaluation of a canine bite wound to her left nasal alar margin that occurred 6 months prior. Clinical examination reveals complete loss of the left alar and soft triangle nasal subunits. Which of the following reconstructive approaches most comprehensively addresses all absent components?
A) Composite helical root graft
B) Conchal cartilage graft and bilobed flap for coverage
C) Forehead flap and skin graft for lining with septal cartilage graft
D) Forehead flap with nasolabial flap for lining
E) Nasolabial flap with full-thickness skin graft for lining
questions.answer:
C)
Complete nasal alar defects require reconstruction of all absent layers including internal lining, structural support, and external coverage, as well as restoration of all missing subunits. While numerous reconstructive techniques exist with individual advantages and limitations, only approaches that provide lining, support, and coverage will adequately address this type of defect. Among the listed options, only the forehead flap with skin graft lining and septal cartilage support reconstructs all missing layers. A is incorrect because although composite helical root grafts contain all three nasal layers, they lack sufficient size to reconstruct both the alar and soft triangle subunits. B is incorrect because it lacks internal lining. D is incorrect because it provides no structural support. E is incorrect because it lacks both structural support and adequate coverage for the defect size.

questions.question:
A 31-year-old female with underdeveloped breasts presents for consultation regarding bilateral breast augmentation. Which of the following surgical approaches will most effectively reduce the risk of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma?
A) Highly cohesive silicone gel
B) Nipple shields
C) Saline implants
D) Smooth wall implants
E) Subpectoral pocket
questions.answer:
D)
Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) is exceptionally rare, if ever documented, in cases involving only smooth-surfaced implants. When BIA-ALCL occurs with smooth implants, patient histories typically reveal previous exposure to textured devices (when adequate records are available). Aggressive surface texturing (macrotexturing) correlates with increased BIA-ALCL risk, potentially due to greater surface area promoting bacterial colonization. The typical presentation involves late seroma formation (usually beyond one year), requiring aspiration with cytologic analysis and flow cytometry for CD30 T-cell markers. A is incorrect because gel cohesiveness does not significantly influence BIA-ALCL incidence. B is incorrect because while nipple shields may reduce bacterial contamination, their impact on BIA-ALCL prevention remains unproven. C is incorrect because saline fill material does not significantly affect BIA-ALCL risk. E is incorrect because implant pocket location does not substantially impact BIA-ALCL development.

questions.question:
A healthy 48-year-old non-smoking female presents to an accredited facility for facelift, neck lift, and facial laser resurfacing under general anesthesia. The surgical duration is 4 hours and 15 minutes, which falls within state regulations for office-based procedures. Which of the following adverse events is most probable?
A) Cardiac arrest
B) Hospitalization
C) Postoperative nausea and vomiting
D) Reintubation
E) Reoperation
questions.answer:
C)
Office-based cosmetic procedures are increasingly common, with ASPS Task Force guidelines recommending procedures under 6 hours starting early morning to minimize complications. A comprehensive review of 2595 consecutive office-based cosmetic surgery patients under general anesthesia using propofol/remifentanil with airway protection showed no increase in major complications including deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, reintubation, reoperation, hospitalization, cardiac events, or death. However, procedures exceeding 4 hours showed statistically significant increases only in urinary retention and postoperative nausea and vomiting. A is incorrect because cardiac arrest rates do not increase significantly with procedure duration in this setting. B is incorrect because hospitalization rates remain unchanged for procedures over 4 hours. D is incorrect because reintubation risk does not increase significantly with extended procedure time. E is incorrect because reoperation rates do not correlate with procedure duration in office-based settings.

questions.question:
What is the optimal approach for managing maxillary width deficiency in a patient with completed skeletal growth?
A) Mandibular setback (bilateral sagittal split osteotomy)
B) Maxillary advancement (Le Fort I advancement)
C) Orthopedic and orthodontic expansion
D) Reverse-pull headgear
E) Surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion
questions.answer:
E)
Maxillary width deficiency in skeletally mature patients is optimally managed with surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion (SARPE). After suture fusion, surgical intervention is necessary because orthopedic and orthodontic forces alone cannot achieve adequate expansion in mature patients. SARPE provides controlled, predictable widening of the maxilla while maintaining dental and periodontal health. A is incorrect because bilateral sagittal split osteotomy addresses anteroposterior mandibular discrepancies, not maxillary width deficiency. B is incorrect because Le Fort I advancement corrects anteroposterior maxillary deficiency, not transverse problems. C is incorrect because orthopedic and orthodontic expansion is only effective before skeletal maturity when sutures remain open. D is incorrect because reverse-pull headgear cannot achieve expansion in skeletally mature patients and primarily addresses anteroposterior growth.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male presents to the emergency department following a power saw accident to his thumb. Examination reveals a 3 × 2-cm soft tissue loss extending from the interphalangeal crease to the right thumb tip with visible bone and tendon. What represents the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Amputation at the interphalangeal joint
B) First dorsal metacarpal artery flap coverage
C) Free great toe pulp transfer
D) Split-thickness skin grafting
E) Spontaneous healing
questions.answer:
B)
Thumb tip preservation is crucial for opposition and grip function, requiring restoration of sensation and durable padding. With exposed bone and tendon, flap coverage is mandatory. While small thumb tip defects (1-1.5 cm) can utilize Moberg volar advancement flaps, larger defects require alternative flaps like the first dorsal metacarpal artery (FDMA) flap or Little flap. The FDMA flap offers superior coverage area compared to the Little flap, can be harvested with dual venous drainage systems for enhanced reliability, and poses less donor site morbidity risk. Both provide innervated, sensate coverage requiring cortical reorientation over approximately one year. A is incorrect because amputation sacrifices valuable thumb length and function unnecessarily. C is incorrect because free toe pulp transfer represents excessive intervention for this injury magnitude. D is incorrect because skin grafting cannot provide adequate coverage over exposed bone and tendon. E is incorrect because spontaneous healing is inadequate for defects with bone and tendon exposure.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male comes to the clinic with pain and swelling at the base of his right thumb (dominant hand) following a bicycle accident 3 days ago. Radiographic imaging reveals a Bennett fracture. Surgical intervention is planned. Along with longitudinal traction and volar-directed pressure to the dorsal radial aspect of the metacarpal base, which of the following most accurately describes the proper reduction technique for this fracture?
A) Thumb abduction and pronation
B) Thumb abduction and supination
C) Thumb adduction and flexion
D) Thumb adduction and pronation
E) Thumb adduction and supination
questions.answer:
A)
A Bennett fracture represents an intra-articular fracture-dislocation at the thumb's carpometacarpal joint caused by axial loading through a partially flexed metacarpal. A small volar ulnar fragment of the metacarpal base stays attached to the trapezium via the anterior oblique ligament, while the larger remaining fragment displaces proximally, radially, and dorsally due to forces from the abductor pollicis longus and thumb extensors. The adductor pollicis also causes metacarpal adduction and supination. To counteract these deforming forces, reduction requires axial traction on the extended thumb combined with palmar abduction and pronation while applying pressure over the metacarpal base for K-wire placement. B is incorrect because supination would worsen the deformity rather than correct it. C is incorrect because flexion and adduction would not address the radial and dorsal displacement. D is incorrect because pronation alone without abduction would be insufficient. E is incorrect because both adduction and supination would worsen the existing deformity.

questions.question:
Based on the panoramic radiograph (Panorex) provided, what is the most probable diagnosis for these bilateral expansile lesions?
A) Ameloblastoma
B) Central giant cell granulomas (CGCG)
C) Neurofibromas
D) Odontogenic keratocysts
E) Osteosarcoma
questions.answer:
C)
Bilateral expansile lesions involving the inferior alveolar nerve canal are characteristic of neurofibroma. These lesions demonstrate expansion without local bone destruction, which is typical for neurofibromas. A is incorrect because ameloblastomas typically show locally destructive bone changes. B is incorrect because central giant cell granulomas usually present as multilocular lesions with cortical rupture and root resorption. D is incorrect because odontogenic keratocysts commonly cause local bone destruction. E is incorrect because osteosarcoma invariably demonstrates cortical destruction and aggressive bone changes.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old female presents with a 6-year history of hand weakness and numbness on the left side. Clinical examination reveals diminished sensation in the thumb, index, middle, and ring fingers, with no additional sensory deficits noted. Testing which of the following muscles would most likely establish the diagnosis?
A) Abductor pollicis brevis
B) Adductor pollicis
C) First dorsal interosseous
D) Flexor digiti minimi
E) Flexor pollicis brevis
questions.answer:
A)
The clinical presentation indicates median nerve injury or compression neuropathy. The abductor pollicis brevis is the only intrinsic hand muscle exclusively innervated by the median nerve (via its recurrent branch) that can be reliably tested independently from ulnar-innervated muscles, making it the key diagnostic muscle for median nerve function. B is incorrect because the adductor pollicis receives complete ulnar nerve innervation. C is incorrect because the first dorsal interosseous is entirely supplied by the ulnar nerve. D is incorrect because the flexor digiti minimi is completely innervated by the ulnar nerve. E is incorrect because the flexor pollicis brevis has dual innervation from both ulnar (deep head) and median (superficial head) nerves, making isolated testing unreliable.

questions.question:
A healthy 5-year-old girl presents with a yellow cystic lesion on the left sclera, a left preauricular branchial cleft remnant, elevation of the left corner of the mouth, and left facial soft tissue deficiency. Which of the following diagnostic tests should be prioritized to evaluate for important associated conditions?
A) Echocardiography
B) Fluorescence in situ hybridization of the branchial cleft remnant
C) Funduscopic examination
D) MRI of the brain
E) Plain x-ray studies of the hands
questions.answer:
C)
This patient exhibits features consistent with Goldenhar syndrome, a severe variant of hemifacial microsomia characterized by ear abnormalities, mandibular underdevelopment causing occlusal cant and oral commissure asymmetry, and affected-side soft tissue deficiency. Ocular abnormalities occur in approximately 50% of cases and include epibulbar dermoids (as described), microphthalmia, and eyelid or optic nerve colobomas. Colobomas may cause visual field defects or amblyopia, requiring early detection to implement contralateral eye patching for optimal visual development of the affected eye. A is incorrect because cardiac abnormalities are not typically associated with Goldenhar syndrome. B is incorrect because genetic testing of the branchial remnant is not indicated for this condition. D is incorrect because brain imaging is not routinely needed in Goldenhar syndrome. E is incorrect because hand abnormalities are not characteristic features of this syndrome.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female is sent by her dermatologist for assessment and management of a painful lesion on her lateral cheek. Physical examination reveals a 5-mm elevated skin lesion with a blue coloration. Complete excision with 1-mm margins is performed. Histopathological examination demonstrates a well-defined dermal tumor with dense basophilic cellular proliferation, eosinophilic hyaline material, and lymphocytic infiltration. The pathological diagnosis is spiradenoma. What is the most appropriate subsequent management for this lesion?
A) Chemotherapy targeting lymphocytes
B) Radiation therapy
C) Re-excision with 1-cm margins
D) Sentinel lymph node biopsy
E) Reassurance and observation
questions.answer:
E)
Following complete excision of a spiradenoma, reassurance and observation represent the most appropriate management. Spiradenomas are benign, well-differentiated dermal tumors of controversial origin (possibly sweat gland or hair follicle). They typically affect patients aged 15-35 years, presenting as small, solitary, painful nodules that may enlarge to several centimeters with characteristic bluish coloration, commonly on the head, neck, and trunk. Complete excision is curative for these benign lesions. A is incorrect because chemotherapy is not indicated for benign tumors and the lymphocytic infiltrate is reactive, not neoplastic. B is incorrect because radiation therapy is unnecessary for completely excised benign lesions. C is incorrect because wider re-excision is not required after complete removal of a benign tumor. D is incorrect because sentinel lymph node biopsy is not indicated for benign skin tumors.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old factory worker requires flexor tendon repair of the index finger following an occupational accident. What is the primary reason for implementing early mobilization exercises following surgical reconstruction?
A) Reduce scar tissue formation
B) Minimize postoperative discomfort
C) Enhance repair durability
D) Promote synovial fluid circulation
E) Avoid tendon rupture
questions.answer:
A)
The primary reason for implementing early mobilization exercises is to reduce scar tissue formation. In the initial stages of tendon recovery, substantial collagen deposition occurs, creating early fibrous tissue. While this fibrous tissue is essential for healing the reconstructed tendon, it also develops within the tendon sheath and can result in digital stiffness if left unchecked. Early passive and active movement protocols help disrupt early fibrous adhesions between the tendon and surrounding sheath. B is incorrect because early motion typically increases rather than decreases postoperative discomfort. C is incorrect because early motion does not enhance the final strength of the repair. D is incorrect because while synovial fluid circulation may increase with tendon movement, this does not improve clinical outcomes. E is incorrect because early motion actually increases the risk of tendon rupture rather than preventing it.

questions.question:
A 66-year-old male patient presents for assessment of drooping left upper eyelid. He experiences visual impairment in the left eye that persists during daily activities. Clinical examination reveals moderate left upper eyelid drooping with raised left upper eyelid fold. Eyebrow positioning and movement, along with pupil dimensions, appear normal on both sides. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Congenital eyelid drooping
B) Facial nerve damage
C) Horner's syndrome
D) Myasthenia gravis
E) Age-related eyelid drooping
questions.answer:
E)
Age-related eyelid drooping is characterized by separation of the levator muscle attachment, representing the most frequent cause of eyelid drooping in older adults. Raised upper eyelid fold is a characteristic finding. Levator muscle tightening or repositioning is necessary for surgical correction. A is incorrect because congenital eyelid drooping occurs in young patients with severe drooping, absent eyelid fold, and poor muscle function. B is incorrect because facial nerve damage causes eyebrow drooping but not upper eyelid drooping. C is incorrect because Horner's syndrome presents with drooping, small pupils, and decreased sweating, typically without affecting the eyelid fold. D is incorrect because myasthenia gravis causes drooping that worsens with fatigue and typically affects young women or elderly men, requiring specialized testing for diagnosis.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with gradual wrist swelling. Tendon rupture is being considered. In patients with rheumatoid arthritis, which tendon is most prone to rupture?
A) Common finger extensor
B) Hand digit extensor
C) Long thumb extensor
D) Deep finger flexor
E) Long thumb flexor
questions.answer:
A)
The common finger extensor is the most prone to rupture in rheumatoid arthritis patients. Tendon rupture occurs due to continuous friction over bone prominences causing wear, direct tendon invasion, or tissue death from inflammatory swelling. The ulnar-side extensors are most commonly affected, with rupture progressing toward the radial extensors. These ruptures are typically painless and occur with minimal tendon use. B is incorrect because this is not the standard anatomical term for the most commonly affected tendon. C is incorrect because the long thumb extensor is the second most common rupture, not the most common. D is incorrect because deep finger flexors are less commonly affected than extensors in rheumatoid arthritis. E is incorrect because while the long thumb flexor is the most commonly ruptured flexor tendon, it is still less common than extensor ruptures overall.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old male patient needs free tissue reconstruction for head and neck soft tissue defect repair. Which surgical technique is most likely to enhance flap viability?
A) Direct connection anastomosis
B) Multiple blood vessel branches
C) Muscle tissue only
D) Additional blood supply
E) Vein connecting device
questions.answer:
E)
The vein connecting device is most likely to enhance flap viability. Research involving 2296 head and neck free tissue reconstructions by Chang and colleagues showed that vein connecting devices significantly reduced complications compared to hand-sewn connections. The study found no significant improvement in survival with additional blood supply, multiple blood vessel branches, or connection orientation. Muscle-only flaps actually showed increased failure risk compared to skin-containing or bone-containing flaps. A is incorrect because direct connection showed no survival advantage over other connection orientations. B is incorrect because multiple blood vessel branches did not significantly improve outcomes. C is incorrect because muscle-only flaps actually had higher failure rates. D is incorrect because additional blood supply (supercharging) showed no significant benefit in flap survival rates.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient is planned for single-sided breast reconstruction using tissue expander. Her medical background includes cardiac stent placement 4 months prior. She currently takes aspirin and clopidogrel. The cancer surgeon prefers not to delay the mastectomy procedure. What is the optimal preoperative medication approach for this patient?
A) Maintain both aspirin and clopidogrel
B) Stop aspirin and maintain clopidogrel
C) Stop both aspirin and clopidogrel
D) Stop both aspirin and clopidogrel; begin preventive enoxaparin
E) Stop clopidogrel and maintain aspirin
questions.answer:
A)
Maintaining both aspirin and clopidogrel is the optimal approach. Patients with drug-eluting stents placed 4 months ago should continue dual antiplatelet therapy for at least 6 months, unless high bleeding risk procedures (brain or spine surgery) are planned. The aspirin and clopidogrel combination reduces cardiovascular events. Patients with coronary stents face an 8-10% risk of major cardiovascular events and stent clotting after non-cardiac surgery, which exceeds the 1-5% risk in patients without stents. B is incorrect because stopping aspirin while maintaining clopidogrel is not the recommended dual therapy approach. C is incorrect because stopping both medications increases the risk of stent thrombosis and cardiovascular events. D is incorrect because enoxaparin does not provide adequate antiplatelet protection for stent patients. E is incorrect because clopidogrel is essential for stent protection and should not be discontinued within 6 months of placement.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old woman comes to the office because of deep rhytides caused by photoaging. Topical application of 35% trichloroacetic acid in combination with Jessner solution is planned. Which of the following best describes the clinical endpoint during application of this chemical peel?


A) Dark firm eschar
B) Grey hue
C) Hypopigmentation
D) Transparent frost with a pink background
E) Uniform deep white frost
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


The deep white frost indicates the endpoint for the depth of skin penetration with a deep rhytid chemical peel such as the combination Jessner/35% trichloroacetic acid solution. This indicates that the peel has penetrated into the upper reticular dermis. There is no pink hue because at this level there is vasospasm of the capillaries in the papillary dermis. This depth of penetration is for moderate and deep rhytides. This is a transient phenomenon. Capillary refill should return within 20 to 40 minutes.


A transparent frost with a pink background is the endpoint for a superficial peel, such as that done with a trichloroacetic solution (<30%) alone. This frost is due to the coagulation of proteins in the dermis and epidermis. The pink hue emanates from blood vessels that remain intact in the papillary dermis.


A grey hue indicates a deeper penetration with destruction to the dermis. This level of penetration could lead to abnormal healing, scarring, pigmentation, and texturing changes. Hypopigmentation and superficial epidermolysis are potential complications of a chemical peel and not clinical endpoints to determine depth of penetration.


References
Fulton JE, Porumb S. Chemical peels: their place within the range of resurfacing techniques. Am J Clin Dermatol. 2004;5(3):179-87.
Herbig K, Trussler AP, Khosla RK, et al. Combination Jessner's solution and trichloroacetic acid chemical peel: technique and outcomes. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009 Sep;124(3):955-64.
Witheiler DD, Lawrence N, Cox SE, et al. Long-term efficacy and safety of Jessner's solution and 35% trichloroacetic keratoses. Dermatol acid vs 5% fluorouracil in the treatment of widespread facial actinic. Dermatol Surg. 1997 Mar;23(3):191-6.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old woman seeks consultation for breast reconstruction following modified radical mastectomy with adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy completed 18 months previously. Her final radiation session was 8 months ago. BMI is 29 kg/m2. Current examination reveals hyperpigmentation of the right chest wall without redundancy of the mastectomy skin flaps. Her opposite breast is D cup size with grade III ptosis. Which of the following approaches will achieve optimal symmetry for this patient?
A) Deep inferior epigastric perforator flap
B) Gel breast implant and acellular dermal matrix
C) Latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap
D) Tissue expander and acellular dermal matrix placement with planned staged exchange for permanent gel implant
E) Tissue expander placement alone with planned staged exchange for permanent gel implant
questions.answer:
A)
The deep inferior epigastric perforator flap provides the optimal reconstruction with autologous tissue that offers sufficient volume and skin coverage for this patient. In a previously irradiated patient with tight skin envelope, tissue expander/implant reconstruction (options D and E) would be challenging due to difficulty creating adequate skin expansion and increased risk of wound complications and capsular contracture. Option B (gel implant with acellular dermal matrix) faces similar challenges in the radiated field. Option C (latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap) provides autologous tissue but lacks sufficient volume to match the contralateral D cup breast and would require implant augmentation.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old woman with breast cancer undergoes right mastectomy and reconstruction using a free transverse rectus abdominis musculocutaneous (TRAM) flap. The surgery proceeds without complications. In the recovery area, the patient's spouse reveals that she has been smoking one pack of cigarettes daily until the day of surgery. Which of the following postoperative complications is most likely to develop?
A) Flap hematoma
B) Mastectomy skin loss
C) Microvascular thrombosis
D) Partial flap loss
E) Superficial infection
questions.answer:
B)
Mastectomy skin loss is the most likely complication in smoking patients undergoing free flap breast reconstruction. Smoking significantly increases the risk of mastectomy skin necrosis, along with donor site abdominal flap complications, umbilical necrosis, and hernias. Option A (flap hematoma) is not increased by smoking. Option C (microvascular thrombosis) does not show increased incidence in smokers undergoing microsurgical reconstruction. Option D (partial flap loss) and Option E (superficial infection) are not significantly elevated in smoking patients with free flap reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 6-week-old female infant is brought to the office for evaluation of a skull deformity shown in the photograph. Physical examination shows the absence of calvarial bone in multiple areas of the cranium. CT scan (also shown) confirms a kleeblattsch√§del skull deformity. Which of the following is the most likely indication for surgical intervention at this time?


A) Airway compromise
B) Hydrocephalus
C) Increased intracranial pressure
D) Loss of vision
E) Orbital exposure
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


The kleeblattsch√§del skull deformity occurs secondary to multiple suture synostoses. This results in a significant increase in intracranial pressure that causes the skull deformity shown in the CT scan. The increase in intracranial pressure produces a ?moth-eaten? appearance and is the reason for early surgical intervention. This skull deformity is not typically associated with hydrocephalus. Visual compromise sometimes occurs late in life secondary to increased intracranial pressure. Orbital exposure can be a reason for early surgical intervention in some types of syndromic craniosynostosis, such as Crouzon syndrome and Apert syndrome, but is not seen in the scenario described. Airway compromise would be an indication for urgent surgical intervention, but it is not typical for kleeblattsch√§del skull deformity.


References
Jarrahy R, Kawamoto HK, Keagle J, et al. Three tenets for staged correction of Kleeblattsch√§del or cloverleaf skull deformity. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009 Jan;123(1):310-318.
Bristol RE, Lekovic GP, Rekate HL. The effects of craniosynostosis on the brain with respect to intracranial pressure. Semin Pediatr Neurol. 2004 Dec;11(4):262-267.
Cohen MM Jr. Cloverleaf skulls: etiologic heterogeneity and pathogenetic variability. J Craniofac Surg. 2009 Mar;20 Suppl 1:652-656.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old woman presents to the clinic expressing dissatisfaction with her facial aging appearance. Physical examination demonstrates facial volume loss and moderate skin laxity. Autologous fat grafting is planned. Which of the following techniques is most appropriate to optimize the "take" of the fat graft?
A) Ensuring contact with other grafted fat with each successive pass
B) Injecting a small amount of fat per pass
C) Optimizing placement along the cortical facial bone
D) Rinsing the graft with Ringer's lactate
E) Using standard suction lipectomy to harvest the graft
questions.answer:
B)
Injecting small amounts of fat per pass maximizes the surface area contact between the graft and vascularized recipient bed, which is crucial for successful fat graft survival and integration. This technique allows better vascularization and reduces absorption rates. Option A is incorrect because avoiding contact between grafted fat parcels enhances integration with the recipient bed. Option C is incorrect because cortical bone provides poor vascularity for graft survival. Option D is incorrect because rinsing with Ringer's lactate does not improve graft take. Option E is incorrect because standard suction lipectomy reduces adipocyte viability compared to gentler harvest techniques.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old man suffers a Gustilo type IIIB open fracture of the distal left tibia in a boating accident. The wound shows severe contamination, and the patient undergoes multiple formal operative irrigations and debridements. No neurovascular compromise affects the extremity. External fixation stabilizes the limb. Which of the following represents the most appropriate next treatment step?
A) Coverage with a free tissue transfer
B) Negative pressure wound therapy until secondary healing is achieved
C) Pedicled gastrocnemius muscle and skin grafting
D) Primary bone allografting
E) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
A)
Free tissue transfer provides the optimal treatment by bringing healthy, well-vascularized tissue to cover the exposed bone and contaminated wound bed. Gustilo IIIB fractures involve extensive soft tissue loss with periosteal stripping requiring robust coverage. Option B is incorrect because secondary healing cannot close such extensive tissue defects. Option C is incorrect because a pedicled gastrocnemius flap cannot reach the distal tibia. Option D is incorrect because bone grafting in a contaminated field carries high infection risk and should be delayed until stable soft tissue coverage is achieved. Option E is incorrect because skin grafts cannot survive on exposed bone without periosteum and would be vulnerable to breakdown.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old woman presents to the office seeking facial rejuvenation due to premature aging and extensive cervicofacial skin laxity and excess. A congenital etiology for this patient's condition is suspected. This patient would be a candidate for elective surgery if her condition is determined to be which of the following disorders?
A) Cutis laxa
B) Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
C) Elastoderma
D) Progeria
E) Werner syndrome
questions.answer:
A)
Cutis laxa is the only condition listed where elective aesthetic surgery may be safely considered. This genetic disorder involves defective elastic fibers causing loose, excess skin, but normal wound healing remains intact, particularly in the autosomal dominant form which affects only the skin. Option B is incorrect because Ehlers-Danlos syndrome involves collagen defects causing poor wound healing, making surgery contraindicated. Option C is incorrect because elastoderma has unknown effects on wound healing, making elective surgery inadvisable. Option D is incorrect because progeria involves poor wound healing and premature death, contraindicating elective procedures. Option E is incorrect because Werner syndrome includes small vessel disease and poor wound healing, making surgery inappropriate.

questions.question:
A 5-day-old male infant is being assessed in the NICU due to underdeveloped thumb anatomy. His family is concerned and requests immediate treatment. Clinical examination reveals Buck-Gramcko Grade V thumb underdevelopment. At what age should reconstructive surgery ideally be performed?
A) 1 Month
B) 1 Year
C) 4 Years
D) 10 Years
E) 14 Years
questions.answer:
B)
The optimal timing for reconstruction is at 1 year of age. Buck-Gramcko Grade V thumb hypoplasia represents complete thumb absence, requiring pollicization surgery. This timing allows for proper cardiopulmonary maturation, development of bimanual grasp patterns, resolution of embryonic circulation, and adequate digital vessel development while preventing compensatory side-to-side pinch patterns that emerge after the first year. A) 1 month is too early as the infant's systems are not sufficiently developed for such complex surgery. C) 4 years is too late as abnormal compensatory grip patterns will have already formed. D) 10 years and E) 14 years are far too delayed, missing the critical developmental window for optimal functional outcomes.

questions.question:
A 3-year-old female child presents to the emergency room with a 6-hour onset of right facial muscle weakness. Clinical assessment reveals facial asymmetry when smiling and incomplete right eyelid closure. What is the most probable etiology of this condition?
A) Congenital
B) Idiopathic
C) Infection
D) Neoplastic
E) Trauma
questions.answer:
B)
Idiopathic facial nerve paralysis (Bell's palsy) is the most frequent cause of acute-onset facial weakness in pediatric patients. This diagnosis represents the majority of cases in large clinical reviews, making it the most statistically likely etiology. Early recognition is crucial as prompt treatment with antibiotics, antivirals, and sometimes surgical decompression improves long-term facial nerve recovery. A) Congenital causes would be present from birth, not acute onset. C) Infection and E) Trauma are less common than Bell's palsy in children. D) Neoplastic causes are rare in pediatric facial nerve paralysis compared to idiopathic etiology.

questions.question:
An infant presents with one-sided facial weakness. The rest of the clinical assessment is normal with no signs of delivery complications. Which diagnostic test will most likely identify the underlying cause of this facial nerve dysfunction?
A) CT scan of the head
B) Electromyography
C) Electroneurography
D) Stapedius (acoustic) reflex test
E) Ultrasonography
questions.answer:
A)
A CT scan of the head and temporal bones is the most appropriate study to identify temporal bone abnormalities, which are the most likely cause of isolated congenital facial nerve paralysis in an otherwise healthy newborn. This imaging modality can detect structural anomalies of the temporal bone that would explain the facial weakness. B) Electromyography assesses muscle function but doesn't reveal the underlying cause of nerve dysfunction. C) Electroneurography evaluates nerve conduction but cannot identify anatomical causes. D) Stapedius reflex testing can predict recovery but doesn't determine etiology. E) Ultrasonography is inadequate for imaging the skull base and temporal bone structures necessary for this diagnosis.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a tearing injury to the skin on the front portion of his left ear. Examination reveals a 2 × 2-cm tissue flap detached from the conchal area. Which blood vessel is most likely compromised?
A) Infraorbital
B) Occipital
C) Posterior auricular
D) Superficial temporal
E) Transverse facial
questions.answer:
C)
The posterior auricular artery provides the primary vascular supply to the anterior ear surface through perforating branches. This vessel is the main source of blood flow to the conchal bowl region where the injury occurred. A) The infraorbital artery supplies the orbital area, nasal dorsum, and upper lip, not the ear. B) The occipital artery contributes minimally only to the posterior ear aspect. D) The superficial temporal artery provides limited supply only to the superior helix area. E) The transverse facial artery supplies the parotid region and masseter muscle, not auricular structures.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old woman with no previous pregnancies seeks consultation for breast enhancement. Assessment shows bilateral underdeveloped breasts with narrow bases and protrusion of breast tissue through the areolar region. Tuberous breast anomaly is identified. Bilateral breast enhancement using smooth, round silicone implants through areolar incisions is proposed. Which technique will most effectively prevent a "double-bubble" appearance?
A) Decreasing the areolar diameter
B) Lowering of the inframammary fold
C) Parenchymal scoring
D) Periareolar incision
E) Subpectoral placement of the implant
questions.answer:
C)
Parenchymal scoring is the most effective technique to prevent double-bubble deformity by releasing constricting tissue bands and allowing lower pole breast tissue to properly drape over the implant while also releasing the abnormally elevated inframammary fold characteristic of tuberous breasts. This technique addresses the underlying anatomical problem causing the deformity. A) Areolar diameter reduction improves aesthetics but doesn't prevent double-bubble formation. B) Lowering the inframammary fold is a treatment goal but alone won't prevent the deformity. D) Periareolar incision allows areolar reduction but doesn't address the underlying tissue constriction. E) Subpectoral implant placement actually increases double-bubble risk, while subglandular or dual-plane approaches are preferred.

questions.question:
An infant presents with a midline defect on the lower spine featuring a protruding sac containing meninges, spinal fluid, and neural tissue. What is the main objective of surgical intervention?
A) Managing hydrocephalus
B) Enhancing lower limb motor function
C) Preventing infectious complications
D) Avoiding tethered cord development
E) Improving bowel and bladder control
questions.answer:
C)

The primary objective of meningomyelocele repair is preventing infectious complications. This neural tube defect involves herniation of meninges and spinal cord through vertebral defects, creating an exposed neural placode vulnerable to infection. Surgical closure within 24-48 hours of birth protects the neural elements, prevents infection, and avoids cerebrospinal fluid leakage through appropriate soft tissue coverage using muscle flaps, fasciocutaneous flaps, or combinations thereof. A) is incorrect because hydrocephalus, while common in these patients, is managed separately with CSF shunting when needed. B) and E) are incorrect because surgical repair cannot restore neurological functions that were absent at birth, such as motor abilities or bowel/bladder control. D) is incorrect because tethered cord syndrome may still develop in 20-50% of patients as they grow, despite initial repair, and is not prevented by the primary surgery.

questions.question:
A 10-year-old child presents with hand dysfunction following a supracondylar fracture treated 6 months prior. The fingers assume an intrinsic minus posture, suggesting Volkmann ischemic contracture. Which muscle would be LEAST affected by this condition?
A) Brachioradialis
B) Flexor digitorum profundus
C) Flexor digitorum superficialis
D) Flexor pollicis longus
E) Pronator teres
questions.answer:
A)

The brachioradialis is least likely to be affected by Volkmann ischemic contracture because it receives blood supply from the superficial radial artery circulation. Volkmann contracture results from muscle ischemia and subsequent fibrosis due to elevated compartment pressures, commonly following supracondylar fractures. The muscles most vulnerable are those supplied by the deep vascular pattern of the ulnar artery and its branches (common interosseous artery and its anterior/posterior divisions). B) is incorrect because the flexor digitorum profundus relies on deep circulation and is commonly affected. C) is incorrect because the flexor digitorum superficialis is also dependent on deep vascular supply and frequently involved. D) is incorrect because the flexor pollicis longus receives deep circulation and is typically affected. E) is incorrect because the pronator teres is supplied by deep vessels (ulnar artery passes deep to it) and is commonly involved in this ischemic process.

questions.question:
A 74-year-old patient seeks consultation for eyelid surgery. She has excess upper lid skin bilaterally and right upper lid drooping from levator muscle separation. She reports no dry eye symptoms and improved vision following recent laser eye surgery. What is the minimum waiting period after her laser eye surgery before proceeding with eyelid surgery?
A) 3 Months
B) 6 Months
C) 9 Months
D) 12 Months
E) Never; she cannot have eyelid surgery
questions.answer:
B)

The minimum recommended interval between laser vision correction and blepharoplasty is 6 months. This waiting period is essential because performing eyelid surgery too soon after corneal refractive procedures significantly increases the risk of severe dry eye syndrome and corneal complications. The corneal surface needs adequate time to stabilize and heal completely before any periorbital surgical intervention. A) is incorrect because 3 months is insufficient time for complete corneal healing and stabilization. C) and D) are incorrect because while longer waiting periods are safe, 6 months is the established minimum standard. E) is incorrect because the patient can undergo blepharoplasty after the appropriate waiting period, as she has no contraindications such as existing dry eye disease.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old healthy patient undergoes buttock fat transfer surgery. Following proper antibiotic prophylaxis, sterile preparation, tumescent liposuction, gravity fat processing, and injection of 350 mL per buttock, she develops localized tenderness, firmness, and mild redness. Drainage reveals oily, turbid fluid. What is the most probable cause of this complication?
A) Insufficient preoperative antibiotic coverage
B) Improper timing of tumescent infiltration before harvest
C) Missing postoperative antibiotic treatment
D) Fat injection technique
E) Gravity separation instead of centrifugation for fat processing
questions.answer:
D)

The most likely cause is improper fat injection technique, specifically delivering excessively large volumes of fat into inadequate recipient sites. This leads to poor revascularization and subsequent fat necrosis, manifesting as tenderness, firmness, and drainage of oily, cloudy fluid as described. Successful fat grafting requires injection of small aliquots into well-vascularized tissue to ensure graft survival. A) is incorrect because the patient received appropriate antibiotic prophylaxis for a clean elective procedure. B) is incorrect because the described tumescent technique with 3:1 fat-to-fluid ratio is standard and appropriate. C) is incorrect because postoperative antibiotics are not routinely required for clean cases, and any secondary infection would be due to the underlying necrotic tissue. E) is incorrect because gravity separation is an acceptable fat processing method and not the primary cause of this complication.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old patient presents with a 6-month history of a painless forearm mass. Examination reveals a well-defined 6-cm lesion. Imaging shows no additional masses in the chest, axilla, or forearm. Tissue sampling confirms epithelioid sarcoma. What is the most appropriate initial treatment approach?
A) Chemotherapy
B) Excisional biopsy
C) Forearm amputation
D) Radiation therapy
E) Wide local excision
questions.answer:
D)

Preoperative radiation therapy is the most appropriate initial management for epithelioid sarcoma. Radiation administered before surgery helps reduce tumor size and decreases local recurrence rates, improving surgical outcomes. This approach is standard for high-grade sarcomas like epithelioid sarcoma. A) is incorrect because chemotherapy is typically reserved for high-grade tumors >10 cm, those with lymph node involvement, or metastatic disease, and is usually given postoperatively when indicated. B) is incorrect because excisional biopsy is only appropriate for low-grade tumors, whereas epithelioid sarcomas are typically high-grade malignancies. C) is incorrect because amputation should only be considered when negative surgical margins cannot be achieved with limb-sparing procedures. E) is incorrect because while wide excision with negative margins is essential, preoperative radiation should be administered first to optimize surgical outcomes.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old female presents to the emergency room following a left thumb injury sustained during a basketball game. An unexpected finding is noted on the hand x-ray examination. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Enchondromatosis
B) Metachondromatosis
C) Osteochondroma
D) Solitary enchondroma
E) Synovial chondromatosis
questions.answer:
D)

The radiographic finding demonstrates characteristics typical of an enchondroma, displaying the pathognomonic ring-and-arc calcification pattern, central medullary location, and involvement of the proximal phalanx. These lesions may cause cortical endosteal scalloping due to expansion. Individual enchondromas represent the most prevalent benign bone tumors, with a particular affinity for the small bones of hands and feet. The proximal phalanx accounts for roughly 50% of cases, with metacarpals and middle phalanges following in frequency. These tumors comprise 12-14% of benign bone neoplasms and 3-10% of all bone tumors, affecting both sexes equally. Individual enchondromas typically present as incidental findings in patients aged 20-40 years. A) Enchondromatosis (Ollier disease) is incorrect because it typically manifests from birth to age 10 and involves multiple lesions. B) Metachondromatosis is incorrect as it's a rare hereditary condition featuring both multiple enchondromas and osteochondromas. C) Osteochondroma is incorrect because it appears as a cartilage-capped bony projection on the external bone surface, not within the medullary cavity. E) Synovial chondromatosis is incorrect as it involves cartilaginous loose bodies within joint synovium, not intraosseous lesions.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female seeks consultation for breathing difficulties and desires rhinoplasty. Clinical evaluation reveals a moderate dorsal hump. Nasal assessment demonstrates normal mucosa, septum, and turbinates, with an angle measuring less than 10 degrees between the septum and upper lateral cartilages. Which surgical technique would best address functional airway improvement in this case?
A) Avoidance of nasal bone infracture
B) Dorsal onlay graft
C) Septoplasty
D) Spreader grafts
E) Turbinate outfracture
questions.answer:
D)

This patient exhibits internal nasal valve narrowing with an angle below the normal 10-15 degree range, which is the probable source of her airway obstruction. Spreader grafts placed during rhinoplasty can widen this constricted area and provide symptomatic relief for her functional breathing problem. A) Avoiding nasal bone infracture is incorrect because it wouldn't address the internal nasal valve narrowing. B) Dorsal onlay grafting is incorrect as it serves cosmetic dorsal augmentation without functional benefit. C) Septoplasty is incorrect since the septum is described as normal and straight. E) Turbinate outfracture is incorrect because the turbinates are normal and don't require modification.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female seeks consultation regarding thigh contouring improvement. Her medical history includes gastric bypass surgery performed two years prior, resulting in a sustained 150-lb (68-kg) weight reduction. She presents with moderate horizontal skin redundancy and substantial vertical skin excess, prompting consideration of a full-length vertical thighplasty. Which complication poses the highest risk for this patient?
A) Hematoma
B) Infection
C) Labial spreading
D) Prolonged edema
E) Seroma
questions.answer:
D)

While all listed complications occur with significant frequency in thighplasty procedures among massive weight loss patients, prolonged edema represents the greatest risk specifically associated with full-length vertical thighplasty components. This increased risk stems from circumferential compression effects on the low-pressure lymphatic drainage system. A) Hematoma is incorrect as it's not the most common complication specific to vertical thighplasty. B) Infection is incorrect as it doesn't have the highest occurrence rate with this specific procedure. C) Labial spreading is incorrect because it's possible but unlikely with this technique. E) Seroma is incorrect as it's not the predominant complication associated with vertical thighplasty.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old male suffers a significant right orbital floor fracture during a physical assault. Repair using a pre-contoured orbital floor implant with intraoperative CT guidance is scheduled. Which aspect is most likely to benefit from this imaging technique during surgery?
A) Operative time
B) Plate positioning
C) Rate of corneal abrasion
D) Rate of plate extrusion
E) Risk for lid malposition
questions.answer:
B)

Intraoperative computed tomography utilization in maxillofacial trauma surgery is increasingly adopted, with documented advantages including reduced reoperation rates, enhanced implant positioning accuracy, and decreased postoperative enophthalmos. The primary benefit is optimizing precise plate placement during the procedure. A) Operative time is incorrect because intraoperative CT may actually increase surgical duration rather than optimize it. C) Rate of corneal abrasion is incorrect as this imaging modality has no impact on corneal injury rates. D) Rate of plate extrusion is incorrect since intraoperative CT doesn't affect implant extrusion rates. E) Risk for lid malposition is incorrect because this complication isn't influenced by intraoperative imaging.

questions.question:
A 77-year-old female undergoes basal cell carcinoma removal from the mid-cheek region. Clinical assessment reveals a 4 × 4-cm circular skin defect exposing subcutaneous tissue. Skin graft reconstruction is planned. Which grafting technique would best reduce long-term contracture?
A) Cultured epidermal autografting
B) Full-thickness skin grafting
C) Split-thickness skin grafting with meshing
D) Split-thickness skin grafting with no meshing
questions.answer:
B)

For this full-thickness skin defect with exposed subcutaneous fat, a full-thickness skin graft would minimize long-term (secondary) contracture. Full-thickness grafts include both epidermis and complete dermis, resulting in superior long-term outcomes with reduced contracture. Proper defatting is essential for optimal graft survival. A) Cultured epidermal autografting is incorrect as it's reserved for cases with limited donor sites (like extensive burns) and produces thin, fragile skin. C) Split-thickness grafting with meshing is incorrect because meshing increases contracture within the mesh interstices and split-thickness grafts have more secondary contracture. D) Split-thickness grafting without meshing is incorrect as split-thickness grafts contain incomplete dermis and exhibit greater long-term contracture compared to full-thickness grafts.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old female radiology technician arrives at the emergency department 1 hour following exposure of her right hand to approximately 5 Gy of ionizing radiation. Physical examination reveals no abnormal findings. What is the most probable clinical outcome?
A) Progressive skin necrosis
B) Widespread blister formation across the hand
C) Enhanced vulnerability to soft-tissue infections
D) Temporary skin redness, itching, and hair loss
E) No adverse effects
questions.answer:
D)
Temporary skin redness, itching, and hair loss is the expected outcome for low-dose radiation exposure under 10 Gy. The hand is frequently involved in occupational fluoroscopy incidents. Low-energy exposures typically cause transient erythema, pruritus, and alopecia. A is incorrect because delayed necrosis occurs with much higher doses (>20 Gy). B is incorrect because extensive blistering requires moderate to high doses (>10 Gy). C is incorrect because increased infection susceptibility is associated with severe exposures requiring amputation. E is incorrect because 5 Gy will produce mild but noticeable symptoms.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old female patient visits the clinic to discuss breast augmentation surgery. She prefers subglandular implant positioning and wants to review augmentation risks. Which complication is more frequent with smooth round silicone implants versus textured anatomic silicone implants?
A) Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
B) Capsular contracture
C) Double capsule formation
D) Late seroma development
E) Implant rotation
questions.answer:
B)
Capsular contracture occurs more frequently with smooth round silicone implants compared to textured implants. The textured surface is believed to provide protection against significant capsule formation. A is incorrect because anaplastic large cell lymphoma is more associated with textured implants. C is incorrect because double capsule is a complication more commonly seen with textured anatomic implants. D is incorrect because late seroma is an increased risk with textured implants. E is incorrect because malrotation can only occur with anatomic shaped implants, not symmetric round implants.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old male patient undergoes evaluation for a 1.6-cm pigmented lesion on his right shoulder. Excisional biopsy reveals superficial spreading malignant melanoma with 3 mm Breslow thickness. During staging workup, distant metastasis to which organ system indicates the worst prognosis?
A) Liver
B) Lung
C) Lymph nodes
D) Subcutaneous tissue
questions.answer:
A)
Liver metastases represent visceral involvement, which carries the worst prognosis according to AJCC melanoma staging. The staging system categorizes distant metastases into three prognostic groups: skin/soft-tissue (best), lung (intermediate), and other visceral organs like liver and brain (worst). B is incorrect because lung metastases have intermediate prognosis. C is incorrect because lymph node involvement represents regional rather than distant metastasis. D is incorrect because subcutaneous metastases fall into the best prognosis category for distant disease.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old Caucasian agricultural worker presents to the clinic with multiple pink scaly patches on his cheeks and nose. Biopsy of one lesion demonstrates atypical keratinocytes in the basal epidermis and hyperkeratosis, confirming actinic keratosis. Without treatment, what is the probability these lesions will undergo malignant transformation?
A) 0%
B) 10%
C) 30%
D) 50%
E) 70%
questions.answer:
B)
Actinic keratoses have approximately a 10% risk of malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma. These lesions result from chronic ultraviolet radiation exposure and are common in individuals with significant sun exposure. A is incorrect because there is a definite risk of malignant transformation. C is incorrect because 30% overestimates the transformation rate. D is incorrect because 50% significantly overestimates the risk. E is incorrect because 70% greatly overestimates the malignant potential.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old right-handed female with rheumatoid arthritis presents with progressive deformity of her left long finger, displaying proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint hyperextension and distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint flexion. Examination demonstrates restricted PIP joint flexion regardless of metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint position. What is the optimal treatment approach?
A) DIP joint fusion using a small cannulated screw
B) Figure-of-eight splinting for 6 to 8 weeks
C) PIP joint fusion and MCP joint intrinsic release
D) Terminal tendon division
E) Lateral band repositioning and dorsal PIP joint capsulectomy
questions.answer:
E)
This represents a Type III swan-neck deformity with limited PIP flexion in all MCP positions due to fixed dorsal lateral band positioning, requiring lateral band translocation and dorsal PIP capsulectomy. A is incorrect because DIP arthrodesis addresses mallet-related swan-neck deformity, not this presentation. B is incorrect because figure-of-eight splinting is appropriate for Type I flexible deformities. C is incorrect because this combination is used for Type IV deformities with joint destruction. D is incorrect because terminal tendon transection is not a standard treatment for swan-neck deformity.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old woman with no previous pregnancies presents to the clinic seeking breast augmentation surgery. She currently uses a 34B bra and desires to increase to a D cup size. She is an appropriate candidate for placing implants above the chest muscle. Which of the following complications is reduced when using textured silicone implants versus smooth silicone implants?
A) Capsular contracture
B) Hematoma
C) Implant displacement
D) Rippling
E) Symmastia
questions.answer:
A)
Textured implant surfaces have been demonstrated to reduce capsular contracture rates compared to smooth implants when placed in the subglandular position. This advantage may not exist when implants are positioned beneath the muscle. B is incorrect because hematoma occurrence is not affected by implant surface texture. C is incorrect because implant displacement relates to surgical pocket creation rather than implant surface characteristics. D is incorrect because some studies show increased rippling with textured implants compared to smooth ones, though this may relate more to gel consistency and shell fill volume. E is incorrect because symmastia results from pocket dissection extending too close to or across the sternum, not from implant surface type.

questions.question:
The 3-month-old infant shown has a bilateral cleft lip and palate. Which of the following is a goal of the nasoalveolar molding seen in the photograph?


A) Expansion of the alveolar cleft
B) Expansion of the soft tissue of the lip
C) Lengthening of the columella
D) Lengthening of the septum
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Nasoalveolar molding (NAM) is the fabrication and adjustment of a custom intraoral appliance that narrows the cleft, aligns the cleft segments, shapes existing nasal structures, and expands deficient nasal tissues. Bilateral cleft lip and palate is associated with a nasal deformity that is defined by a short columella. The premaxilla is typically protuberant if the cleft is complete. NAM allows alignment of the premaxilla with the lateral alveolar segments. Once this is accomplished, nasal stents are placed to lengthen the columella.


The alveolar clefts are aligned and narrowed. Generally the septum is in the midline and does not require any lengthening. The upper cleft lip does not require expansion; rather, it requires layered repair with good muscular approximation at the time of the primary lip and nasal repair.


References
Lee CT, Garfinkle JS, Warren SM, et al. Nasoalveolar molding improves appearance of children with bilateral cleft lip-cleft palate. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008 Oct;122(4):1131-1137.
Liou EJ, Subramanian M, Chen PK. Progressive changes of columella length and nasal growth after nasoalveolar molding in bilateral cleft patients: a 3-year follow-up study. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2007 Feb;119(2):642-648.
Cutting C, Grayson B, Brecht L, et al. Presurgical columellar elongation and primary retrograde nasal reconstruction in one-stage bilateral cleft lip and nose repair. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1998 Mar;101(3):630-639.

questions.question:
