A 42-year-old woman arrives for autologous fat transfer from her abdomen to her upper breast areas under IV sedation. Her medical history includes breast reconstruction with implants. She receives 1 gram of IV cefazolin in the pre-operative area. Within ten minutes, she develops widespread urticaria, facial flushing, and lip edema. She complains of breathing difficulty and has audible wheezing. What is the most appropriate route for epinephrine administration?
A) Intradermal injection
B) Intramuscular injection
C) Intravenous bolus
D) Intravenous infusion
E) Subcutaneous injection
questions.answer:
B)
This patient exhibits anaphylaxis with acute generalized urticaria, angioedema, and respiratory symptoms. Intramuscular epinephrine (0.3-0.5 mg) administered in the mid-lateral thigh is the first-line treatment for adults with anaphylaxis. A is incorrect because intradermal injection would result in slow absorption inadequate for anaphylaxis. C is incorrect because IV bolus epinephrine carries risks of dosing errors and overdose complications. D is incorrect because IV infusion is reserved for refractory cases, not initial treatment. E is incorrect because subcutaneous absorption is too slow to effectively reverse anaphylactic reactions.

questions.question:
A 16-year-old male is evaluated for managing maxillary underdevelopment and Class III bite misalignment. His history includes surgical repair of complete unilateral cleft lip and palate during infancy. Maxillary forward movement is planned once facial development is complete. Which method most accurately determines when facial growth has finished?
A) Patient's chronological age
B) Full eruption of second molars
C) Hand-wrist radiographic analysis
D) Sequential cephalometric radiographs
questions.answer:
D)
Sequential cephalometric radiographs provide the most reliable assessment of completed maxillofacial growth in adolescents by tracking growth velocity changes over time. When minimal or no growth velocity is observed, skeletal maturity is indicated. A is incorrect because chronological age varies widely among individuals regarding pubertal growth timing. B is incorrect because dental development markers do not reliably predict skeletal maturity stages. C is incorrect because while hand-wrist radiographs are standard for general skeletal development assessment, their validity for craniofacial growth evaluation has been questioned in recent studies.

questions.question:
A patient develops paradoxical adipose hyperplasia (PAH) following cryolipolysis treatment. What is the minimum waiting period required before surgical intervention for the PAH?
A) 1 Month
B) 3 Months
C) 6 Months
D) 1 Year
E) 2 Years
questions.answer:
C)
Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia is an uncommon cryolipolysis complication that may be more frequent than manufacturer reports suggest. Surgical intervention should be postponed until the affected tissue softens, typically occurring 6-9 months post-cryolipolysis. Power-assisted liposuction is the preferred treatment approach, though abdominoplasty may be required in certain cases. A is incorrect because one month is insufficient time for tissue softening. B is incorrect because three months typically does not allow adequate tissue softening. D and E are incorrect because waiting one to two years is unnecessarily prolonged beyond the typical 6-9 month softening period.

questions.question:
A 4-year-old male is scheduled for abdominal wall reconstruction using component separation. He received a living donor liver transplant as an infant, when the graft was oversized for his body. An intentional midline hernia was created to accommodate organ function post-transplant. Current examination reveals ventral herniation with significant domain loss. During component separation repair, the parallel aponeurotomy will most likely be performed immediately lateral to which anatomical landmark?
A) Arcuate line of Douglas
B) Inguinal ligament
C) Linea semilunaris
D) Midline
E) Tendinous inscription
questions.answer:
C)
Component separation involves medial advancement of the rectus abdominis muscle after dividing the external oblique aponeurosis. The incision is made lateral to the linea semilunaris, which marks the lateral border of the rectus sheath formed by the three muscle layer contributions. A is incorrect because the arcuate line represents where the posterior rectus sheath configuration changes, not the site for external oblique division. B is incorrect because the inguinal ligament should never be divided during component separation. D is incorrect because the midline contains the linea alba separating the rectus muscles, not the site for lateral release. E is incorrect because tendinous inscriptions are horizontal rectus muscle interruptions and are not divided in standard component separation.

questions.question: An otherwise healthy 23-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle-pedestrian collision causing compartment syndrome, myonecrosis, and need for radical resection of devitalized tissue of the right thigh. He is hemodynamically stable. A photograph taken two days after his first debridement is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?A) Bilaminate neodermal reconstructionB) Free contralateral anterolateral thigh flapC) Negative pressure wound therapyD) Skin graftingE) Surgical debridement
questions.answer: The correct response is Option E.Given the obvious devitalized tissue in the associated photograph, the most appropriate next step would be further debridement. This is an often overlooked, but still critical, cornerstone to reconstruction, because without it, complication rates from infection are significantly increased.Debridement involves the removal of nonviable or contaminated tissue that impedes normal tissue growth. It renews the wound and surrounding tissue to promote normal healing by removing infection, biofilm, and senescent cells.Different debridement options are available, including mechanical, biologic, technical, and surgical methods. In this acute scenario with an otherwise healthy patient and a large amount of devitalized tissue, surgical debridement is the most appropriate choice.All other modalities/choices are not appropriate until the wound bed is stabilized. Negative pressure wound therapy may be used in conjunction with debridement, but is not a replacement for it.ReferencesAnghel EL, DeFazio MV, Barker JC, et al. Current Concepts in Debridement: Science and Strategies. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2016 Sep;138(3 Suppl):82S-93S.Attinger CE, Janis JE, Steinberg J, et al. Clinical approach to wounds: d√©bridement and wound bed preparation including the use of dressings and wound-healing adjuvants. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2006 Jun;117(7 Suppl):72S-109S.

questions.question:
Which anatomical structure forms a component of the internal nasal valve?
A) Front section of the middle turbinate
B) Lower border of the upper lateral cartilage
C) Ethmoid cribriform plate
D) Maxillary sinus opening
E) Upper edge of the nasal bone
questions.answer:
B)
The internal nasal valve represents the narrowest portion of the nasal airway and consists of multiple anatomical boundaries. The lower border of the upper lateral cartilage forms the superior boundary of this critical structure, along with the nasal septum medially, the nasal vestibule floor inferiorly, the front portion of the inferior turbinate posteriorly, and the bony pyriform aperture rim laterally. This valve's dimensions directly influence nasal airflow during breathing. A is incorrect because the middle turbinate's anterior portion is not part of the internal valve anatomy. C is incorrect because the cribriform plate is located much higher in the nasal cavity and relates to olfaction, not the valve structure. D is incorrect because the maxillary sinus ostium opens into the middle meatus and is not a valve component. E is incorrect because the nasal bone's superior border is part of the external nasal framework, not the internal valve.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old woman presents with left breast discomfort. She had a benign core needle biopsy of a breast lesion two weeks prior. Her family history is negative for breast malignancy, and she is a non-smoker. Physical findings include left breast erythema, tenderness, and lateral skin retraction. A palpable cord-like structure extends longitudinally through the breast tissue. What is the most likely diagnosis and appropriate management?
A) Breast abscess, perform surgical drainage
B) Fibrocystic disease, obtain tissue biopsy
C) Mastalgia, prescribe 10-day antibiotic course
D) Intraductal papilloma, order diagnostic mammogram
E) Superficial thrombophlebitis, provide symptomatic care
questions.answer:
E)
This presentation is consistent with Mondor disease, which is superficial thrombophlebitis affecting breast and chest wall veins. It commonly occurs after surgical procedures, biopsies, radiation, or trauma. The characteristic cord-like thickened vein, pain, erythema, and skin retraction are typical findings. Treatment involves symptomatic management with analgesics, and the condition typically resolves within 4-6 weeks. A is incorrect because breast abscesses present with localized swelling and induration but lack the characteristic cord-like mass and skin retraction. B is incorrect because fibrocystic changes present as discrete masses that may fluctuate with menstrual cycles, not as linear cord-like structures. C is incorrect because while the patient has breast pain, the specific physical findings of cord-like mass and skin retraction indicate a more specific diagnosis than simple mastalgia. D is incorrect because papillomas typically present with bloody nipple discharge and would not cause the linear cord-like findings described.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old woman is being monitored in the recovery area within the first hour following microsurgical breast reconstruction using a free flap. Physical examination reveals a bluish skin paddle with brisk capillary refill and a strong arterial Doppler signal on the skin. What intervention would best optimize flap survival?
A) Give systemic heparin
B) Administer systemic tissue plasminogen activator
C) Use external warming device
D) Place medicinal leeches
E) Perform immediate surgical exploration
questions.answer:
E)
The clinical findings indicate venous congestion with intact arterial inflow, evidenced by the bluish discoloration, rapid capillary refill, and strong arterial Doppler signal. This represents venous thrombosis, which is more common than arterial compromise in free flap complications. Immediate surgical exploration is critical, as studies demonstrate that flaps re-explored within 5 hours have significantly higher salvage rates. Early recognition and prompt surgical intervention are the most important factors for successful flap salvage. A is incorrect because systemic heparin will not resolve an established venous thrombosis and may increase bleeding risk. B is incorrect because thrombolytics are not effective for this acute mechanical problem and carry significant bleeding risks. C is incorrect because external warming does not address the underlying venous obstruction and will not improve flap survival. D is incorrect because leeches may help with venous congestion but are not appropriate as first-line treatment when immediate surgical correction is possible and more effective.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old woman seeks consultation for a large abdominal pannus causing frequent rashes and skin breakdown. Her BMI is 41 kg/m2. While waiting, she reviews educational brochures about abdominoplasty and panniculectomy procedures. Based on National Institutes of Health and American Medical Association guidelines, patient educational materials should be written at or below which grade reading level?
A) Fourth grade
B) Sixth grade
C) Eighth grade
D) Tenth grade
E) High school graduate level
questions.answer:
B)
The NIH and AMA recommend that patient education materials be written at no higher than a sixth-grade reading level to ensure broad accessibility. Health literacy significantly impacts patient understanding, health outcomes, and healthcare utilization. While most adults read at eighth to ninth-grade levels, approximately 20% read at the lowest level (around fifth grade). Materials written above the sixth-grade level may contribute to patient confusion, such as misunderstanding the difference between reconstructive panniculectomy and cosmetic abdominoplasty. A is incorrect because fourth grade is below the recommended maximum, though not harmful. C is incorrect because eighth grade exceeds the recommended maximum despite being the average adult reading level. D is incorrect because tenth grade is significantly above recommendations and would exclude many patients from understanding the material. E is incorrect because high school graduate level is far above recommendations and would create barriers to comprehension for a substantial portion of patients.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old girl sustained burns covering 60% of her total body surface area. Examination reveals second- and third-degree burns affecting her face, neck, and torso. Following initial resuscitation, wound management, debridement, and skin grafting, she begins rehabilitation. Which medication would be most beneficial for enhancing bone mineral content in this patient?
A) Ascorbic acid
B) Glutamine
C) Insulin
D) Oxandrolone
E) Testosterone
questions.answer:
D)
Oxandrolone, a synthetic oral testosterone derivative, has been proven in randomized clinical trials to significantly improve bone mineral content, height, cardiac function, and muscle strength in severely burned children. It works by increasing insulin-like growth factor-1 secretion and, combined with exercise, substantially increases lean body mass and strength. The medication is most effective in children aged 7-18 years and has only 5% of testosterone's virilizing activity with low hepatotoxicity. Unlike testosterone, oxandrolone cannot be aromatized to estrogen, reducing the risk of bone-age advancement in growing children. A is incorrect because while ascorbic acid aids burn recovery as an antioxidant and supports wound healing, it does not significantly impact bone mineral density. B is incorrect because glutamine supplementation helps with wound healing and may reduce infection rates and hospital stay, but does not have the bone density benefits of oxandrolone. C is incorrect because insulin is primarily used for hyperglycemia management and has not been shown to increase bone mineral density in burn patients. E is incorrect because testosterone is not approved for burned children due to increased virilization risks in females and aromatization effects.

questions.question:
A 28-year-old female patient has septorhinoplasty surgery. If the septal L-strut is fractured, which of the following complications is most likely to occur?
A) Bossa formation
B) Open roof deformity
C) Pollybeak deformity
D) Rocker deformity
E) Saddle-nose deformity
questions.answer:
E)

The correct answer is E because the septal L-strut provides crucial structural support to the nasal framework. When fractured, it leads to loss of dorsal and caudal septal support, causing collapse of the middle third of the nose and resulting in a saddle-nose deformity. The keystone area where cartilaginous and bony structures meet becomes unstable, similar to removing the keystone from an arch. A) is incorrect because bossa formation results from cartilage irregularities and aggressive suturing techniques, not septal L-strut fractures. B) is incorrect because open roof deformity occurs after dorsal hump reduction when nasal sidewalls separate from the septum. C) is incorrect because pollybeak deformity involves supratip fullness from tip ptosis or inadequate dorsal septum resection. D) is incorrect because rocker deformity results from high nasal osteotomies above the canthal level, not septal cartilage fractures.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female patient presents with a 4.1-mm irregular dark lesion on her left leg. Her primary care doctor performed excisional biopsy with 1-mm margins. Pathology shows 1.8-mm thick ulcerated malignant melanoma. Wide local excision is being planned. What is the most appropriate excision margin for this tumor?
A) 0.5-cm margin
B) 1-cm margin
C) 2-cm margin
D) 3-cm margin
E) 5-cm margin
questions.answer:
C)

The correct answer is C because melanoma excision margins are determined by tumor thickness (Breslow depth), not diameter. This 1.8-mm thick melanoma falls into the intermediate thickness category (1-4 mm), which requires a 2-cm surgical margin based on established guidelines from landmark studies. A) is incorrect because 0.5-cm margins are only appropriate for melanoma in situ. B) is incorrect because 1-cm margins are used for thin melanomas less than 1 mm thick. D) is incorrect because 3-cm margins are only considered for very thick melanomas greater than 4 mm depth. E) is incorrect because 5-cm margins are excessive and not supported by current evidence-based guidelines for any melanoma thickness.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old male is assessed after being hit in the chin with a metal pipe during an altercation. Examination reveals a 6-mm displaced bicortical right parasymphyseal fracture and left nondisplaced subcondylar fracture with open crossbite. Complete trauma workup shows no cervical spine or brain injuries. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Liquid diet for 3 weeks, followed by mechanical soft diet for 3 weeks
B) Maxillomandibular fixation followed by open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) in 4 weeks
C) Maxillomandibular fixation alone for 4 to 6 weeks
D) ORIF of the parasymphyseal fracture followed by immediate maxillomandibular fixation
E) Maxillomandibular fixation followed by immediate ORIF of the parasymphyseal fracture
questions.answer:
E)

The correct answer is E because proper mandibular fracture repair requires establishing correct dental occlusion first through maxillomandibular fixation (MMF), then performing ORIF of the displaced parasymphyseal fracture. This sequence ensures anatomical reduction and prevents malocclusion complications. A) is incorrect because dietary modification alone will not provide adequate fracture stabilization and will lead to nonunion or malunion. B) is incorrect because delaying ORIF for 4 weeks risks fibrous nonunion or malunion, as facial fractures should be repaired within 10-14 days. C) is incorrect because MMF alone cannot adequately stabilize the displaced bicortical parasymphyseal fracture. D) is incorrect because performing ORIF before establishing proper occlusion through MMF can result in malocclusion, TMJ dysfunction, and abnormal mandibular forces.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old male with sickle cell disease presents to the emergency department following a Gustilo Type IIIB lower extremity fracture from an ATV accident. Soft-tissue coverage of exposed hardware and bone is being planned. Which factor is most likely to negatively impact perfusion to microsurgical reconstruction?
A) High sympathetic tone
B) Prostacyclines
C) Sludging
D) Young age of patient
questions.answer:
C)

The correct answer is C because sickle cell disease causes abnormal red blood cell morphology leading to increased blood viscosity and sludging within vessel lumens, which significantly compromises microvascular perfusion and flap viability. The altered rheologic properties create mechanical obstruction to blood flow in small vessels. A) is incorrect because high sympathetic tone was once thought to be problematic in pediatric microsurgery but has been proven false through multiple studies showing microsurgery is safe in children. B) is incorrect because prostacyclines (prostaglandin I2) are vasodilators that actually improve perfusion rather than compromise it. D) is incorrect because young age is not a risk factor for microsurgical complications and children actually have excellent outcomes with microvascular procedures.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old male is examined 7 months following an isolated left orbital blowout fracture that was managed non-operatively. Physical examination demonstrates normal extraocular movements. He describes gradual worsening episodes of double vision over the last 3 months. Which physical finding is most likely present with this condition?
A) Ectropion
B) Muscle entrapment
C) Exophthalmos
D) Vertical dystopia
E) Orbital proptosis
questions.answer:
D)

The correct answer is D because enophthalmos (posterior displacement of the globe) commonly develops months after orbital blowout fractures due to increased orbital volume from unrepaired floor defects. This altered globe position creates vertical dystopia where the affected eye sits at a different level than the unaffected eye, causing diplopia as the visual axes no longer align properly. A) is incorrect because ectropion (eyelid eversion) is not typically associated with isolated orbital floor fractures and rarely causes diplopia. B) is incorrect because muscle entrapment presents acutely with restricted eye movement, not months later with normal extraocular movements. C) is incorrect because exophthalmos (forward globe displacement) is opposite to what occurs with orbital floor fractures and is not associated with this injury pattern. E) is incorrect because orbital proptosis refers to forward displacement and is not characteristic of blowout fractures, which cause posterior globe displacement.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old female presents with two draining nodular lesions of axillary hidradenitis suppurativa. Each lesion measures approximately 10 mm in diameter. The surrounding axillary skin appears normal. Following a 6-week treatment course with oral doxycycline and topical mupirocin, the lesions have decreased drainage but persist. Which of the following represents the most appropriate next treatment for this patient?
A) Complete axillary excision with skin grafting
B) Surgical excision with primary closure
C) Incision and drainage procedure
D) Intravenous antibiotic therapy
E) Intralesional steroid injection
questions.answer:
B)

This adolescent patient presents with localized, limited disease that has not responded adequately to medical therapy. Surgical excision with primary closure is the most appropriate treatment for isolated, discrete lesions. This approach is less invasive than complete axillary excision, which is reserved for extensive disease involving a large portion of the axillary skin area. A) is incorrect because complete axillary excision is overly aggressive for this limited disease pattern. C) is incorrect because incision and drainage is appropriate for closed abscesses but would not address the underlying apocrine gland pathology in these draining lesions. D) is incorrect because after 6 weeks of oral antibiotics, further antibiotic therapy is unlikely to be beneficial. E) is incorrect because steroid injections have limited effectiveness in established lesions and can be quite painful.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old female is assessed for a 1.5-cm, slowly enlarging, solitary, firm subcutaneous nodule on the posterolateral aspect of her neck that has been present for one year. Excisional biopsy confirms the diagnosis of pilomatrixoma. The specimen will most likely demonstrate a mutation in which of the following genes?
A) CTNNB1
B) GLUT1
C) NF1
D) p57
questions.answer:
A)

Pilomatrixoma (calcifying epithelioma of Malherbe) is a benign, slowly progressive tumor originating from hair follicle cells. Mutations in the CTNNB1 gene are identified in approximately 75% of solitary pilomatrixomas. This gene regulates cellular growth and adhesion, and its mutation leads to beta-catenin/LEF pathway disruption, which is the primary mechanism of hair matrix cell tumor development in this condition. B) is incorrect because GLUT1 gene mutations are linked to infantile hemangiomas, not pilomatrixomas. C) is incorrect because NF1 gene mutations are associated with neurofibromatosis type 1. D) is incorrect because p57 gene mutations are related to Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome.

questions.question:
A 6-month-old female presents with facial asymmetry due to right cheek swelling. Imaging studies reveal an infantile hemangioma involving the parotid gland. There is no active bleeding, and the infant is feeding and developing appropriately. Which of the following represents the most appropriate immediate management for this patient?
A) Calcium channel blocking agents
B) Laser treatment
C) Percutaneous sclerotherapy
D) Surgical excision
E) Watchful waiting
questions.answer:
E)

Infantile hemangiomas are among the most frequent infant tumors. Parotid gland hemangiomas typically encircle the facial nerve, making complete surgical removal challenging. Fortunately, most parotid hemangiomas undergo spontaneous involution without requiring surgical intervention. E) is the correct approach for asymptomatic lesions. A) is incorrect because calcium channel blockers are not the standard treatment (beta-blockers like propranolol are used for symptomatic cases). B) is incorrect because laser therapy is ineffective for deep parotid lesions. C) is incorrect because sclerotherapy is used for venous malformations, not hemangiomas. D) is incorrect because surgical resection carries significant risk of facial nerve injury and is not indicated for asymptomatic lesions that typically resolve spontaneously.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male is planned for reconstruction of avascular necrosis affecting the proximal scaphoid pole using a free osteochondral bone flap. Which of the following vessels represents the most frequently utilized vascular pedicle for the medial femoral condyle free bone flap?
A) Anterior tibial recurrent artery
B) Descending genicular artery
C) Popliteal artery
D) Saphenous artery
E) Superficial femoral artery
questions.answer:
B)

The medial femoral condyle free bone flap represents an excellent reconstructive option for complex degenerative bone conditions of the wrist, especially scaphoid avascular necrosis. The descending genicular artery is the most commonly used vascular pedicle for this flap, providing reliable blood supply to the corticocancellous bone. When the descending genicular artery is inadequate, the medial superior genicular artery can serve as an alternative, though it typically offers a shorter pedicle length. A) is incorrect because the anterior tibial recurrent artery is located distally and laterally over the lateral tibial plateau, not supplying the medial femoral condyle. C) is incorrect because the popliteal artery is a larger regional vessel that gives rise to the medial superior genicular artery but is not the direct pedicle. D) is incorrect because the saphenous artery supplies only the overlying skin paddle, not the bone itself. E) is incorrect because the superficial femoral artery is the source vessel for the descending genicular artery but not the direct pedicle for the flap.

questions.question:
Which of the following represents the most probable outcome when liposuction is performed concurrently with brachioplasty?
A) Enhanced tissue dissection
B) Development of lymphedema
C) Tissue necrosis
D) Upper extremity numbness
E) Incisional separation
questions.answer:
A)

Liposuction is frequently combined with excisional brachioplasty to enhance soft tissue dissection, optimize contour, and reduce risks of nerve damage and lymphatic complications. Various techniques exist in the literature supporting this approach. Liposuction of tissues planned for excision facilitates creation of dissection planes and can be performed in the posterior upper arm to improve the contour of remaining tissues. This technique provides better protection for nerves and lymphatic structures compared to excisional debulking alone. B) is incorrect because liposuction actually reduces lymphedema risk by preserving lymphatic channels. C) is incorrect because liposuction does not increase skin necrosis rates when properly performed. D) is incorrect because liposuction helps protect nerves and reduces paresthesia risk compared to excision alone. E) is incorrect because liposuction does not increase wound dehiscence rates.

questions.question:
In the keystone region of the nose, which of the following best describes how the upper lateral cartilage is positioned relative to the nasal bones?
A) In front of the nasal bones
B) Below the nasal bones with a 1 to 2 mm fibrous separation
C) Adjacent to the nasal bones without any overlap
D) Behind the nasal bones
questions.answer:
D)

The correct answer is D because at the keystone region, the nasal bones consistently overlap the upper lateral cartilages posteriorly by 4 to 14 mm in all anatomical specimens. This overlapping relationship is crucial for understanding nasal anatomy and surgical planning. A is incorrect because the upper lateral cartilages are not positioned anterior to the nasal bones at this location. B is incorrect because there is no fibrous gap - instead there is direct bony overlap of the cartilages. C is incorrect because there is significant overlap rather than an edge-to-edge relationship without overlap.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old man presents with numbness and impaired movement of his ring and small fingers 5 months following a laceration to his upper arm from glass. Physical examination reveals inability to spread apart and bring together the ring and small fingers, with decreased light touch sensation. After surgical exploration and removal of a painful traumatic neuroma, a 5-cm defect in the ulnar nerve above the elbow is identified. Which of the following represents the best approach to restore intrinsic hand muscle function?
A) Cadaveric nerve allografting
B) Nerve transfer
C) Sural nerve grafting
D) Use of nerve conduit
E) Vascularized nerve grafting
questions.answer:
B)

Nerve transfer is the optimal choice because the high-level ulnar nerve injury with significant time delay (5 months) and distance to target muscles would result in reinnervation taking over 2 years with conventional repair methods, leading to poor intrinsic muscle recovery. Nerve transfer using the distal anterior interosseous nerve to the ulnar motor branch provides motor neurons closer to the target muscles, enabling reinnervation within the critical 12-18 month window. A is incorrect because cadaveric allografts are less effective than autografts and still require the same lengthy regeneration time. C is incorrect because sural nerve grafting would still require over 2 years for reinnervation due to the distance involved. D is incorrect because nerve conduits are typically used for shorter gaps (2-3 cm) and sensory nerves in non-critical areas. E is incorrect because vascularized grafts are used for severely scarred beds but don't address the fundamental timing issue in this case.

questions.question:
Which cranial nerve provides parasympathetic innervation to the parotid gland?
A) Trigeminal (V) nerve
B) Vestibulocochlear (VIII) nerve
C) Glossopharyngeal (IX) nerve
D) Vagus (X) nerve
E) Hypoglossal (XII) nerve
questions.answer:
C)

The glossopharyngeal nerve (cranial nerve IX) supplies parasympathetic innervation to the parotid gland and also carries taste sensation from the posterior third of the tongue. A is incorrect because the trigeminal nerve (specifically V2) provides sensory innervation to the midface but not parasympathetic fibers to the parotid gland. B is incorrect because the vestibulocochlear nerve is responsible for hearing and balance, not glandular innervation. D is incorrect because the vagus nerve's auricular branch (Arnold nerve) innervates the external acoustic meatus, not the parotid gland. E is incorrect because the hypoglossal nerve controls tongue muscle movement and does not provide parasympathetic innervation to salivary glands.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old man seeks consultation following Mohs micrographic surgery for a basal cell carcinoma of the right nasal sidewall. The resulting defect measures 1.2 × 1.4 cm and reaches but does not penetrate the underlying cartilage. The patient expresses significant concern regarding cosmetic appearance. Which of the following represents the optimal treatment approach?
A) Bilobed flap from the nose
B) Full-thickness skin graft
C) Paramedian forehead flap
D) Purse-string closure
E) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
A)

A bilobed flap is the most appropriate choice for this 1.2 × 1.4 cm nasal sidewall defect (approximately 12-14 mm), as it falls within the ideal size range of 10-15 mm for this single-stage technique. The bilobed flap recruits laxity from the upper nasal dorsum and sidewall and provides excellent color and texture matching for nasal sidewall reconstruction with superior cosmetic results. B is incorrect because full-thickness skin grafts often result in color and texture mismatch with a patch-like appearance and may contract, distorting nasal shape. C is incorrect because paramedian forehead flaps are reserved for larger defects (generally greater than 15 mm) or those involving multiple subunits, and would be excessive for a defect of this size, requiring a staged procedure with donor-site morbidity. D is incorrect because purse-string closure would create excessive tension and distortion, with risk of alar rim elevation for a defect of this size. E is incorrect because split-thickness skin grafts provide poor cosmetic results with significant color mismatch and contraction.

questions.question:
A 5-year-old girl is brought to the physician because her parents are interested in correction of the unilateral ear anomaly shown in the photographs. Which of the following materials is most likely to be used in the procedure to correct this anomaly?


A) Acellular dermal matrix
B) Autogenous rib cartilage
C) Porous polyethylene
D) Silicone
E) Skin
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.






This patient has cryptotia. The superior helical rim and scapha are not absent but lie buried under the supra-auricular skin. Although some authors have advocated expanding the superior helical framework, this is rarely indicated. In this patient with very mild auricular shortening, supplementing or reconstructing the cartilage framework with rib cartilage, polyethylene, or silicone is unnecessary. Instead, the ear framework simply released its posterior aspect and the resultant defect lined with full-thickness skin graft or any number of skin flaps raised from the postauricular region. The use of acellular dermal matrix is not an accepted method of correcting cryptotia.


References
Marsh D., Sabbagh W., Gault D. Cryptotia correction‚Äi the post-aruicular transposition flap. J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2011 Nov;64(11):1444-7.
Thorne C.H., Wilkes G. Ear deformities, otoplasty, and ear reconstruction. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2012 Apr;129(4):701e-16e

questions.question:
A healthy 55-year-old woman receives bilateral breast reconstruction using free deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flaps. Tissue oximetry-based flap monitoring is employed. What represents the primary benefit of this approach compared to handheld Doppler with clinical evaluation?
A) Direct blood flow measurement
B) Ease of use
C) Improved flap salvage rate
D) Less expensive modality
E) Operator must be bedside
questions.answer:
C)

The primary advantage is improved flap salvage rates, with studies showing an increase from 57.7% to 93.8% when using tissue oximetry monitoring. This improvement results from earlier detection of vascular compromise before clinical signs become apparent, allowing for timely intervention. The technology measures tissue oxygenation rather than flow, making it less susceptible to movement artifacts and providing continuous monitoring. A is incorrect because tissue oximetry measures oxygenation levels, not direct blood flow. B is incorrect because both methods are relatively easy to use, so this is not the main distinguishing advantage. D is incorrect because tissue oximetry systems require higher initial financial investment compared to handheld Doppler devices. E is incorrect because tissue oximetry allows remote monitoring without requiring the operator to be physically present at bedside.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old man comes to the office because he has ‚Äudrooping‚Äu of the right shoulder and inability to abduct it beyond 30 degrees. He underwent exploration and vascular repair 4 months ago after sustaining a stab wound to the right side of the neck. Photographs are shown. Which of the following surgical transfer techniques is most likely to restore deltoid function in this patient?


A) C5 to C6 nerve root
B) Intercostal to musculocutaneous nerve
C) Partial ulnar nerve to musculocutaneous nerve
D) Radial nerve fascicle to axillary nerve
E) Suprascapular to axillary nerve
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Of the nerve transfers listed, only the transfer of a triceps branch to the axillary nerve will restore innervation to the deltoid muscle and provide shoulder abduction. Although debate remains over whether nerve graft repair (if possible) or nerve transfer provides better outcomes for shoulder abduction, both techniques are frequently employed in the setting of upper trunk brachial plexus injury.


The location of the injury (based on scar and mechanism) makes the injury likely distal to the nerve roots; in addition, root to root transfers are not typically part of the brachial plexus reconstruction ladder.


The suprascapular nerve is often the recipient nerve for partial transfers from cranial nerve XI (spinal accessory nerve) in order to provide shoulder stability. In this pattern of injury and based on the photos demonstrating atrophy of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus, the suprascapular nerve could not act as a donor nerve.


Intercostal nerve and partial ulnar nerve transfers to the musculocutaneous nerve are both frequently used to restore elbow flexion in the setting of upper trunk injuries.


References
1. Garg R, Merrell GA, Hillstrom HJ, Wolfe SW. Comparison of nerve transfers and nerve grafting for traumatic upper plexus palsy: a systematic review and analysis. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2011 May 4;93(9):819-829.
2. Yang LJ, Chang KW, Chung KC. A systematic review of nerve transfer and nerve repair for the treatment of adult upper brachial plexus injury. Neurosurgery. 2012 Aug;71(2):417-429.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old male arrives with tender, erythematous swelling on the dorsal aspect of his right middle finger MCP joint, occurring 3 days following a punch to someone's face during an altercation. The patient describes reduced hand mobility and difficulty gripping items. He had visited the emergency room on the night of injury, where radiographs showed no fracture or retained foreign material. What is the most probable pathogenic microorganism?
A) Clostridium perfringens
B) Eikenella corrodens
C) Pasteurella multocida
D) Pseudomonas aeruginosa
E) Staphylococcus epidermidis
questions.answer:
B)
Eikenella corrodens is an anaerobic bacterium found in human oral microbiota and is commonly linked to human bite injuries. This patient likely sustained a "fight bite" injury from tooth penetration into the MCP joint when striking someone's mouth with a closed fist. These wounds can introduce oral bacteria into the joint space, leading to septic arthritis. A) Clostridium perfringens is incorrect because it causes gas gangrene with subcutaneous emphysema, not typical of fight bite infections. C) Pasteurella multocida is incorrect as it's primarily associated with cat bite wounds, not human bites. D) Pseudomonas aeruginosa is incorrect because it's more commonly seen in diabetic wound infections rather than human bite wounds. E) Staphylococcus epidermidis is incorrect as it's a skin commensal that typically causes implant-related infections, not fight bite wounds.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old female patient has undergone complete excision of an adnexal neoplasm from her upper lip with clear surgical margins. The resulting tissue loss involves a full-thickness defect encompassing 75% of the upper lip width. What represents the optimal reconstructive approach?
A) Abbe flap only
B) Bilateral Estlander flaps with an Abbe flap
C) Bilateral Karapandzic flaps with an Abbe flap
D) Radial forearm flap only
E) Radial forearm flap with a palmaris longus sling
questions.answer:
C)
Bilateral Karapandzic flaps combined with an Abbe flap provide optimal reconstruction for this extensive central upper lip defect. The Karapandzic flaps preserve muscle innervation while transferring remaining lip tissue, and the Abbe flap reconstructs the philtrum to maintain aesthetic appearance. A) Abbe flap alone is incorrect because it cannot adequately close a 75% defect. B) Bilateral Estlander flaps with Abbe flap is incorrect because Estlander flaps are designed for commissure reconstruction, not central defects. D) Radial forearm flap only is incorrect due to poor color match, lack of innervation, and absence of vermilion reconstruction. E) Radial forearm flap with palmaris longus sling is incorrect for the same reasons as option D, plus it doesn't address the specific functional and aesthetic needs of lip reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female patient is planned for debridement and repair of a Stage IV sacral decubitus ulcer. What constitutes the optimal reconstructive technique?
A) Free tissue transfer
B) Full-thickness skin grafting
C) Inferior gluteus maximus island flap
D) Split-thickness skin grafting
E) V-Y fasciocutaneous flap
questions.answer:
E)
V-Y fasciocutaneous advancement flaps are the preferred method for sacral pressure ulcer reconstruction. These flaps preserve the gluteus maximus muscle, maintain patient mobility, and provide durable coverage with high mechanical resistance to pressure and ischemia. A) Free tissue transfer is incorrect because it's reserved for cases with extensive radiation damage or poor local tissue options, which isn't indicated here. B) Full-thickness skin grafting is incorrect due to poor vascularity in the pressure ulcer zone and high failure rates under tension. C) Inferior gluteus maximus island flap is incorrect because muscle flaps are more sensitive to ischemia and pressure compared to fasciocutaneous flaps. D) Split-thickness skin grafting is incorrect for the same reasons as full-thickness grafts, with additional concerns about durability and pressure resistance.

questions.question:
A patient seeks consultation regarding nasal surgery. He expresses satisfaction with his nasal appearance at rest, but notes nasal distortion during laughing or speaking. Which muscle most likely accounts for this dynamic deformity?
A) Corrugator supercilii
B) Depressor septi nasi
C) Levator labii alaeque nasi
D) Orbicularis oris
E) Procerus
questions.answer:
B)
The depressor septi nasi muscle originates from the upper lip and inserts at the nasal base on the septum and alae. During facial animation, this muscle contracts and pulls the nasal tip downward, reduces the nasolabial angle, and can cause the described nasal distortion. A) Corrugator supercilii is incorrect because it's located at the medial supraorbital ridge and creates vertical glabellar wrinkles, not nasal tip depression. C) Levator labii alaeque nasi is incorrect as it functions to dilate nostrils and elevate the upper lip, not depress the nasal tip. D) Orbicularis oris is incorrect because it primarily affects lip function and doesn't directly influence nasal tip position during animation. E) Procerus is incorrect as it's positioned between the eyebrows and creates horizontal nasion wrinkles, not nasal tip movement.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old construction worker presents with a 3-month history of sensory loss in the median nerve distribution. Diagnostic workup reveals a mass within the medial cord of the brachial plexus. Histopathological examination confirms a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor. Which organ system is most commonly affected by metastatic spread?
A) Brain
B) Colon
C) Liver
D) Lung
E) Spine
questions.answer:
D)
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors metastasize in approximately 39% of cases, with the lungs being the most frequent site of distant spread. These sarcomas typically arise from major peripheral nerves and require wide surgical excision including the affected nerve, often combined with radiation therapy. A) Brain is incorrect as it's not the primary metastatic site for these tumors. B) Colon is incorrect because malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors don't commonly metastasize to gastrointestinal organs. C) Liver is incorrect as hepatic metastases are not the predominant pattern for these neural sarcomas. E) Spine is incorrect because while these tumors can involve spinal nerves primarily, spinal metastases are not the most common secondary site.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old man presents with the lower eyelid skin lesions shown in the photograph. The lesions have been slowly growing over the past 12 months. Which of the following treatment options is the most appropriate?


A) Excision of the mass and overlying skin
B) Excision with 1-mm tissue margins
C) Excision with 2-mm tissue margins
D) Excision with 4-mm tissue margins and sentinel lymph node biopsy
E) Mohs micrographic surgery
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


The patient presents with xanthelasmata, which are localized accumulation of lipid deposits on the eyelids. Multiple treatment modalities are available, including chemical peels, cryotherapy, and laser ablation. Traditionally, surgical excision has been used and yields excellent cosmetic outcomes. As the lesions are benign, there is no indication for Mohs micrographic surgery and no margins are required.


ReferencesLaftah Z, Al-Niaimi F. Xanthelasma: an update on treatment modalities. J Cutan Aesthet Surg. 2018;11(1):1-6.Lee HY, Jin US, Minn KW, et al. Outcomes of surgical management of xanthelasma palpebrarum. Arch Plast Surg. 2013;40(4):380-386.

questions.question:
A patient had open reduction and internal fixation for naso-orbital-ethmoid fractures 12 months prior, and excessive tearing was observed during follow-up. Following 6 months of monitoring with continuing excessive tearing, what is the most suitable next management approach for this patient's tear drainage system?
A) Conjunctivorhinostomy tube insertion
B) Further observation
C) Dacryocystorhinostomy
D) Jones testing
E) Lacrimal duct irrigation
questions.answer:
D)
Jones testing is the appropriate next step to evaluate lacrimal drainage function in this patient with persistent epiphora following NOE fracture repair. Naso-orbital-ethmoid fractures frequently affect the lacrimal drainage system either through direct trauma or surgical intervention with transcanthal wiring. Post-surgical epiphora occurs in approximately 50% of NOE fracture patients, with half resolving within 3-6 months and the remaining 25% requiring further evaluation. Jones tests help determine the level and nature of lacrimal obstruction before considering more invasive interventions. A is incorrect because conjunctivorhinostomy is a surgical procedure that would be premature without proper diagnostic evaluation. B is incorrect because 6 months of observation has already been completed and further waiting is not indicated with persistent symptoms. C is incorrect because dacryocystorhinostomy is a surgical treatment that should only be considered after diagnostic testing confirms the location and type of obstruction. E is incorrect because lacrimal irrigation is a diagnostic procedure that is less comprehensive than Jones testing for evaluating the entire drainage system.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old woman presents to the emergency department following a motor vehicle accident. She reports difficulty opening her mouth. Examination reveals bilateral facial swelling and decreased posterior facial height, along with an anterior open bite. What additional physical examination finding would most strongly indicate bilateral subcondylar fractures?
A) Bilateral facial numbness
B) Bilateral mastoid bruising
C) Blood in the ear canal
D) Clear fluid in the ear canal
E) Preauricular tenderness
questions.answer:
E)
Preauricular tenderness is the most characteristic additional finding for bilateral subcondylar fractures. These fractures disrupt the vertical buttress integrity, causing lateral pterygoid muscles to displace condylar necks medially and anteriorly while temporalis and masseter muscles shorten posterior facial height unopposed. The resulting premature posterior tooth contact creates an anterior open bite, bilateral swelling, and pain during mouth opening as movement displaces the fracture site. A is incorrect because bilateral facial numbness suggests mandibular ramus or body fractures where the inferior alveolar nerve travels, not subcondylar fractures. B is incorrect because bilateral mastoid ecchymosis indicates skull base fractures, which are more proximal injuries. C is incorrect because blood in the external auditory canal suggests fractures more proximal than the subcondylar region. D is incorrect because clear fluid in the ear canal also indicates skull base fractures rather than subcondylar injuries.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old woman presents with tissue breakdown 6 weeks following radiation treatment for breast cancer. She had a mastectomy 1 year earlier. Examination of the irradiated tissue would most likely demonstrate an elevation in which of the following?
A) Acute inflammatory response
B) Cytokines and growth factors
C) Neutrophil function
D) Tissue oxygenation
E) Vessel thrombosis
questions.answer:
E)
Vessel thrombosis is increased in irradiated tissue. Ionizing radiation causes direct DNA damage or injury through free radical formation. Acute radiation injury produces skin erythema and edema with fine vessel dilation, endothelial swelling, and lymphatic destruction. Despite apparently normal perfusion on fluorescein assessment, tissue oxygenation remains insufficient. Healing becomes impaired due to reduced fibroblast proliferation and compromised inflammatory responses, with fibroblast dysfunction being the primary issue in chronic radiation injury healing inhibition. A is incorrect because radiation actually impairs rather than increases the acute inflammatory response. B is incorrect because the irradiated tissue environment fails to provide adequate cytokines and growth factors needed for proper neutrophil activation. C is incorrect because neutrophil phagocytosis and bactericidal functions are impaired, not enhanced, by radiation effects. D is incorrect because tissue oxygenation is actually decreased despite seemingly normal perfusion, contributing to poor wound healing.

questions.question:
A 1-year-old girl presents with a 12 × 12-cm macrocystic lymphatic malformation on her posterior trunk that has been growing and causing recurrent infections over 6 months. The lesion extends through skin, subcutaneous tissue, and muscle. What is the most appropriate initial management?
A) Embolization
B) Prednisolone treatment
C) Propranolol treatment
D) Surgical resection
E) Sclerotherapy
questions.answer:
E)
Sclerotherapy is the primary treatment for large, symptomatic, macrocystic lymphatic malformations. This procedure involves injecting anti-inflammatory agents (such as doxycycline) into the lesion, causing endothelial injury, fibrosis, and malformation shrinkage. Sclerotherapy offers superior efficacy with reduced morbidity compared to surgical excision. A is incorrect because embolization is the first-line treatment for arteriovenous malformations, not lymphatic malformations. B is incorrect because prednisolone is used for problematic infantile hemangiomas but has no effectiveness against vascular malformations. C is incorrect because propranolol is also a hemangioma treatment without efficacy for vascular malformations. D is incorrect because surgical resection is second-line therapy for large macrocystic lymphatic malformations due to significant morbidity risks including bleeding, nerve damage, infection, and wound complications, plus high recurrence rates from incomplete removal.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old woman will undergo female-to-male gender confirmation surgery. A fasciocutaneous radial forearm flap will be used for phallus construction. This surgery involves connecting the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve to a terminal branch of which nerve?
A) Genitofemoral nerve
B) Iliohypogastric nerve
C) Ilioinguinal nerve
D) Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
E) Pudendal nerve
questions.answer:
E)
The pudendal nerve terminates as the dorsal nerve of the clitoris in females, providing primary erogenous sensation. Neurorrhaphy to this nerve produces optimal sensory outcomes in phalloplasty procedures. The dorsal clitoral nerve corresponds to the dorsal penile nerve used in penile reconstruction for amputation or congenital conditions. Other pudendal branches include inferior rectal and perineal nerves. A is incorrect because the genitofemoral nerve provides sensation to the labia majora and femoral triangle skin, not the primary erogenous zone. B is incorrect because the iliohypogastric nerve innervates skin above the pubis and gluteal areas, not genital sensation. C is incorrect because the ilioinguinal nerve supplies upper medial thigh skin and mons pubis/labia majora, not the clitoris. D is incorrect because the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve innervates posterior thigh skin and some perineal areas, not the clitoral region.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old male patient requires left hemimandibulectomy reconstruction. An osteocutaneous free flap from the same-side pelvis is being considered. Which artery serves as the vascular supply for this reconstructive flap?
A) Ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery
B) Deep circumflex iliac artery
C) Deep inferior epigastric artery
D) Descending branch of the geniculate artery
E) Peroneal artery
questions.answer:
B)
The deep circumflex iliac artery is the correct vascular supply for the iliac crest osteocutaneous flap. This vessel originates from the external iliac artery and provides blood flow to both bone-only and osteocutaneous variants of this flap. The iliac crest's natural contour makes it ideal for hemimandibular reconstruction, and the internal oblique muscle can be incorporated using the ascending branch of this same artery. A is incorrect because the ascending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery supplies the tensor fascia lata flap. C is incorrect because the deep inferior epigastric artery provides blood supply to the rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap. D is incorrect because the descending branch of the geniculate artery supplies the medial femoral condyle flap. E is incorrect because the peroneal artery is the vascular pedicle for the fibula flap.

questions.question:
A 4-week-old male infant presents with complete unilateral left cleft lip and palate. Genetic testing reveals an IRF6 gene mutation. What additional clinical feature is most commonly associated with this condition?
A) Agenesis of the corpus callosum
B) Glossoptosis
C) Hypodontia
D) Medialized internal carotid arteries
E) Preauricular accessory tag
questions.answer:
C)
Hypodontia is the most common additional finding in van der Woude syndrome, occurring in up to 86% of patients with IRF6 gene mutations on chromosome 1. This autosomal dominant condition with variable penetrance also presents with lip pits, high arched palate, syngnathia, and ankyloglossia. A is incorrect because agenesis of the corpus callosum is not associated with van der Woude syndrome. B is incorrect because glossoptosis is characteristic of Pierre Robin sequence, not van der Woude syndrome. D is incorrect because medialized internal carotid arteries are found in velocardiofacial syndrome. E is incorrect because preauricular skin tags are not features of van der Woude syndrome.

questions.question:
An 82-year-old male patient needs scalp reconstruction following Mohs surgery for aggressive squamous cell carcinoma. He requires immediate postoperative radiation therapy and has pulmonary fibrosis requiring supplemental oxygen. Examination reveals a 4 × 4 cm vertex defect with exposed calvarium. What is the optimal reconstructive approach?
A) Bilaminate neodermis
B) Delayed reconstruction
C) Local tissue rearrangement
D) Radial forearm free flap
E) Split-thickness skin graft
questions.answer:
C)
Local tissue rearrangement provides the best solution for this high-risk patient requiring immediate radiation therapy. Local scalp flaps offer excellent vascularization for rapid healing, can withstand radiation effects, and provide adequate coverage of exposed bone without subjecting the patient to prolonged anesthesia. A is incorrect because dermal matrices require well-vascularized beds, need additional procedures or prolonged healing, and are not optimal before radiation therapy. B is incorrect because delaying reconstruction until after radiation severely limits future reconstructive options and increases surgical complexity. D is incorrect because free flap surgery is too extensive and risky for this medically compromised patient with a relatively small defect. E is incorrect because skin grafts require well-vascularized recipient sites and may not tolerate subsequent radiation therapy effectively.

questions.question:
A 29-year-old male patient presents 12 weeks following extensive chemical burns affecting 30% total body surface area. Physical examination demonstrates thick hypertrophic scarring across the upper extremities and anterior chest. What treatment approach is most appropriate?
A) Injection of a corticosteroid
B) Scar band revision
C) Serial casting
D) Topical application of vitamin E
E) Use of pressure garments
questions.answer:
E)
Pressure garments are the most appropriate initial treatment for extensive hypertrophic burn scarring. Compression therapy reduces scar blood flow, decreases collagen production, and promotes balanced collagen synthesis and breakdown, resulting in flatter, softer, less vascular scars. Garments providing 24-28 mmHg pressure should be worn nearly 24 hours daily until scar maturation. A is incorrect because corticosteroid injections are limited to small, localized areas due to potential systemic effects and are impractical for extensive scarring. B is incorrect because surgical scar revision is reserved for cases where conservative management fails after appropriate rehabilitation. C is incorrect because serial casting is used during remodeling phase for contracture management, not initial hypertrophic scar treatment. D is incorrect because topical vitamin E lacks substantial evidence for efficacy and can cause delayed hypersensitivity reactions in 33% of patients.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female patient (G3P3) desires comprehensive body contouring including flank liposuction, extended abdominoplasty, arm lift, and breast augmentation. What is the approximate combined complication rate requiring reoperation or hospitalization for this surgical combination?
A) 3%
B) 12%
C) 25%
D) 35%
E) 50%
questions.answer:
B)
The combination of abdominoplasty with liposuction, breast procedure, and body contouring procedure carries approximately a 12% risk of complications requiring reoperation or hospitalization based on large multi-surgeon database studies. This represents a significant increase from abdominoplasty alone (3.1%) due to the additive risks of multiple simultaneous procedures. The most common complications include hematoma (31.5%), infection (27.2%), and venous thromboembolism (20.2%). A is incorrect because 3% represents the complication rate for abdominoplasty alone, not the combined procedures described. C is incorrect because 25% overestimates the actual documented complication rate for this combination. D is incorrect because 35% significantly exceeds the established complication rates for these combined procedures. E is incorrect because 50% greatly overestimates the risk and is not supported by current literature.

questions.question:
A 9-year-old child requires cranioplasty to address a 5 x 5-cm congenital cranial defect. Which of the following represents the optimal material for cranial reconstruction?
A) Costal cartilage transplant
B) Skull bone transplant
C) Fibular bone transplant
D) Pelvic bone transplant
E) Rib bone transplant
questions.answer:
B)
Skull bone transplant is the optimal choice for cranial reconstruction. Autologous bone grafts are preferred in pediatric cranioplasty because they integrate with existing bone and grow with the developing child. Cranial bone is the ideal donor site as it's accessible within the same surgical field, has minimal associated complications, and shows the least resorption. While cranial bone can be difficult to split in younger children due to underdeveloped diploic space, particulate cranial bone can be harvested at any age using specialized instruments. A) is incorrect because costal cartilage is not suitable for cranioplasty procedures. C) is incorrect because fibular bone is not used for cranial reconstruction. D) is incorrect because pelvic bone grafts carry significant donor site complications and higher resorption rates. E) is incorrect because rib bone grafts also have substantial donor site morbidity and increased resorption compared to cranial bone.

questions.question:
A newborn male infant presents with protruding ears during hospital evaluation. Non-operative correction using ear molding is suggested. To achieve the best results, treatment should begin at which of the following time points?
A) 3 days
B) 14 days
C) 1 month
D) 6 months
E) 1 year
questions.answer:
A)
Treatment should begin within 3 days of birth for optimal results. Ear molding can effectively and permanently correct certain congenital ear deformities when started in the first few days of life and continued until 6 months of age. Success depends on cartilage flexibility due to elevated maternal estrogen levels in the initial days after birth. Maternal estrogen peaks in the first 3 days and subsequently declines, making early intervention crucial for maintaining cartilage pliability. B) is incorrect because by 14 days, maternal estrogen levels have begun to decrease, reducing cartilage flexibility. C) is incorrect because at 1 month, estrogen levels are significantly lower, making molding less effective. D) is incorrect because 6 months is too late to initiate treatment, though it represents the endpoint of therapy. E) is incorrect because at 1 year, cartilage has become rigid and molding is ineffective.

questions.question:
A 59-year-old female with 35 years of rubber industry employment is evaluated for a firm, painless 1-cm ulcerated lesion on the hard palate located between the central teeth and incisive foramen. This presumed minor salivary gland neoplasm would most likely metastasize to which of the following lymph node regions?
A) Submandibular nodes
B) Parathyroid nodes
C) Parotid nodes
D) Posterior triangle nodes
E) Occipital nodes
questions.answer:
A)
Submandibular nodes are the primary drainage site for this location. The lips, gingiva, teeth, tongue, and anterior hard palate drain to the submental and submandibular regions (Level I lymph nodes). These are divided into Level IA (submental) and Level IB (submandibular) by the anterior belly of the digastric muscle. B) is incorrect because parathyroid nodes are not a recognized lymphatic drainage basin for oral cavity structures. C) is incorrect because parotid nodes primarily drain the parotid gland and surrounding tissues, not the anterior hard palate. D) is incorrect because posterior triangle nodes (Level V) drain the nasopharynx and oropharynx, not the anterior hard palate. E) is incorrect because occipital nodes drain the posterior scalp region, not oral cavity structures.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old male sustains a left ulnar nerve laceration at the mid-humeral level. Immediate exploration and direct nerve repair are completed. Which of the following treatments is most likely to optimize hand function recovery?
A) Anterior interosseous nerve transfer to the ulnar nerve
B) Dynamic splinting
C) Electrical stimulation of the ulnar nerve
D) Flexor digitorum superficialis tendon transfer to the A2 pulley
E) Wrist extensor tendon transfer to the lumbricals
questions.answer:
A)
Anterior interosseous nerve transfer to the ulnar nerve motor branch provides the best outcome for intrinsic hand function recovery. High ulnar nerve injuries typically have poor intrinsic muscle recovery even with optimal nerve repair. Transferring the anterior interosseous nerve motor branch to the ulnar nerve motor branch at the wrist level effectively restores intrinsic function and can serve as a 'babysitter' transfer to maintain motor endplates during primary nerve regeneration. B) is incorrect because dynamic splinting is primarily used for radial nerve palsies and joint contractures, not for improving denervated muscle function. C) is incorrect because electrical stimulation helps retrain already innervated muscles but cannot improve function in denervated intrinsic muscles. D) is incorrect because tendon transfers are reserved for cases where nerve repair is impossible or when reinnervation is unlikely due to time delays. E) is incorrect because while wrist extensor-to-lumbrical transfers can address clawing, they are secondary options when nerve reconstruction is not feasible.

questions.question:
A healthy 2-week-old male infant is evaluated due to parental concerns about his right ear appearance. Examination reveals a folded superior helix with all ear structures present. Gentle manual pressure restores normal ear contour. Which of the following represents the most appropriate initial treatment?
A) Application of a conforming splint
B) Burying of the helical cartilage in a retroauricular pocket
C) Rasping of the antihelical fold with an otoabrader
D) Resection of the superior auricular muscle
E) Surgical repair with cartilage grafts
questions.answer:
A)
A conforming splint is the appropriate initial treatment for this lop ear deformity. This condition represents an in-utero deformation rather than a true malformation, caused by maternal estrogens that soften cartilage and reduce its ability to support the upper helix. The pliable cartilage responds well to splinting that matches normal helical contour, applied for several weeks or longer. B) is incorrect because burying helical cartilage is used for soft-tissue avulsion injuries as preparation for reconstruction, not for deformational conditions. C) is incorrect because cartilage rasping with an otoabrader is used to create antihelical folds in older children with prominent ears, not for lop ear deformities. D) is incorrect because superior auricular muscle resection may worsen the superior auriculocephalic angle and helical malposition. E) is incorrect because surgical cartilage grafting is unnecessary for this deformational condition that responds to conservative splinting.

questions.question:
A 54-year-old woman develops ventricular fibrillation and profound hypotension 5 minutes following administration of 30 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine to her ankle for post-surgical pain management during foot reconstruction. Following the start of cardiopulmonary resuscitation, which of the following intravenous treatments represents the most suitable intervention?
A) Atropine
B) Dantrolene
C) Flumazenil
D) Lipid emulsion
E) Metoprolol
questions.answer:
D)

The most suitable treatment for acute bupivacaine toxicity is administration of a 20% lipid emulsion bolus followed by continuous infusion. All facilities using large doses of local anesthetics should maintain a clearly marked lipid rescue kit readily available for emergencies. While the exact mechanism remains incompletely understood, the additional lipid in circulation likely functions as a "sink," facilitating removal of lipophilic toxins from affected organs. Severe local anesthetic toxicity presents with symptoms including abrupt unconsciousness, generalized seizures, initial hypertension followed by progressive hypotension, rapid heart rate, ventricular fibrillation, slow heart rate, cardiac standstill, and cardiac arrest. Cardiac rhythm disturbances may resist standard treatment, and resuscitation efforts may extend beyond one hour. A) Atropine is incorrect because it is used for bradycardia/asystole in ACLS protocols but not specifically for local anesthetic toxicity. B) Dantrolene is incorrect because it is specifically indicated for malignant hyperthermia treatment, not local anesthetic toxicity. C) Flumazenil is incorrect because it reverses benzodiazepine effects, not local anesthetic toxicity. E) Metoprolol is incorrect because beta-blockers may worsen the myocardial depression phase of local anesthetic toxicity.

questions.question:
A 66-year-old man presents with a growth on the ulnar side of his index finger's proximal phalanx. The patient states that during the previous year, the growth has increased in size. Physical examination reveals the growth is now limiting finger flexion. Radiographic imaging demonstrates cortical bone erosion of the middle phalanx. Excisional biopsy reveals a tan-colored, multilobulated growth that has encircled the digital nerve and penetrated the bone cortex. What is the most probable diagnosis for this patient?
A) Chondrosarcoma
B) Epidermal inclusion cyst
C) Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
D) Retinacular cyst
E) Schwannoma
questions.answer:
C)

Giant cell tumors of the tendon sheath represent the second most frequent hand masses. These lesions grow slowly without pain and typically affect the palmar aspects of the index, middle, and ring fingers near the PIP or DIP joints. They characteristically appear tan or yellow, lobulated, and well-defined. Bone erosion from chronic pressure may be visible on radiographic studies. Treatment involves surgical removal, with recurrence rates varying from 0 to 44 percent. A) Chondrosarcoma is incorrect because while it can cause cortical breakthrough, it typically presents as a primary bone tumor rather than a soft tissue mass that secondarily erodes bone. B) Epidermal inclusion cyst is incorrect because these are keratin-filled cystic structures, not solid multilobulated masses that surround nerves. D) Retinacular cyst is incorrect because these are ganglion cysts arising from the A1 pulley, typically smaller and not associated with bone erosion or nerve involvement. E) Schwannoma is incorrect because while these can involve digital nerves, they are typically well-encapsulated and can be "shelled out" without the aggressive bone invasion described.

questions.question:
What is the correct Mathes and Nahai classification for the rectus abdominis muscle?
A) Type I
B) Type II
C) Type III
D) Type IV
E) Type V
questions.answer:
C)

The rectus abdominis muscle is classified as a Mathes and Nahai Type III muscle, characterized by having two dominant vascular pedicles. This classification system is fundamental in reconstructive surgery for understanding muscle vascular anatomy. Type III muscles, including the rectus abdominis, gluteus maximus, serratus anterior, and semimembranosus, possess dual dominant blood supplies that provide reliable perfusion for muscle flap procedures. A) Type I is incorrect because these muscles have only one vascular pedicle (examples: gastrocnemius, rectus femoris, tensor fascia lata). B) Type II is incorrect because these muscles have one dominant and one minor pedicle (examples: gracilis, sternocleidomastoid, trapezius). D) Type IV is incorrect because these muscles have multiple segmental pedicles (examples: sartorius, tibialis anterior). E) Type V is incorrect because these muscles have one dominant pedicle plus secondary segmental pedicles (examples: pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi).

questions.question:
A patient has a low-risk basal cell carcinoma lesion measuring 1.5 cm in diameter surgically removed. Based on established guidelines, what surgical margin is most suitable for excision?
A) 1 mm
B) 2 mm
C) 4 mm
D) 6 mm
E) 8 mm
questions.answer:
C)

For low-risk basal cell carcinoma lesions, a 4 mm surgical margin is recommended according to established guidelines. This recommendation is based on the research by Wolf and Zitelli and has been endorsed by numerous other authors and consensus panels. Basal cell carcinoma represents the most frequent cancer in the United States, affecting approximately 2 million Americans yearly, which surpasses the combined incidence of all other cancers. While mortality rates remain low, morbidity is significant due to the rapidly increasing incidence of this common malignancy. A) 1 mm is incorrect because this margin is insufficient for adequate tumor clearance in basal cell carcinoma. B) 2 mm is incorrect because this margin provides inadequate clearance for most basal cell carcinomas. D) 6 mm is incorrect because this exceeds the recommended margin for low-risk lesions and may result in unnecessary tissue removal. E) 8 mm is incorrect because this margin is excessive for low-risk basal cell carcinoma and would cause unnecessary morbidity.

questions.question:
A 7-month-old female infant is evaluated for a large neck mass on the left side. The parents state the mass has existed since birth and has grown proportionally with the child. It became more firm following a recent upper respiratory infection. Examination reveals an alert child without distress. The mass measures 3 × 2 cm at the left mandibular body and angle extending into the upper neck. It compresses easily, lacks pulsation, and is painless. What is the most suitable next step?
A) Hospital admission and propranolol treatment
B) Angiography with sclerosing agent injection
C) CT angiography
D) Fine-needle aspiration biopsy
E) MRI
questions.answer:
E)

MRI represents the most appropriate next step for this congenital neck mass. The clinical presentation suggests a vascular malformation, and MRI will help differentiate between lymphatic malformation and venous-lymphatic malformation while demonstrating involvement of deeper structures like the parotid gland and neck vessels. Given the non-urgent nature of this mass, further imaging is warranted before considering invasive interventions. MRI provides excellent soft tissue characterization without radiation exposure, which is particularly important in pediatric patients. A) Hospital admission and propranolol is incorrect because propranolol is used for hemangiomas, not vascular malformations, and there's no indication for urgent admission. B) Angiography with sclerosing agent injection is incorrect because this is a treatment modality that should only be considered after proper diagnosis is established. C) CT angiography is incorrect because while it could help identify arteriovenous malformations, the clinical examination makes this diagnosis less likely, and it involves radiation exposure. D) Fine-needle aspiration biopsy is incorrect because it's not indicated for suspected vascular malformations and could potentially cause complications.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old Korean woman expresses dissatisfaction with her "angular jawline appearance" and seeks a gentler facial contour through non-surgical means. Botulinum toxin type A therapy is suggested. Which of the following statements is accurate regarding botulinum toxin for masseter muscle enlargement?
A) The FDA has approved botulinum toxin type A injections for treating masseter muscle hypertrophy
B) Results are always temporary in duration
C) Headaches, though rarely reported, typically occur weeks following the injection
D) Muscle mass will not demonstrate meaningful volume decrease on CT imaging
E) Transient reduction in chewing strength is the most frequently observed side effect
questions.answer:
E)
Transient reduction in chewing strength is the most frequently observed side effect. Research by Peng et al showed that 30% of patients experienced temporary decrease in mastication force following botulinum injections. A is incorrect because botulinum toxin injection for masseter hypertrophy remains an off-label use, not FDA-approved for this indication. B is incorrect because studies by Shome et al demonstrated that masseter volume reduction can persist up to 4 years after treatment series. C is incorrect because headaches, when they occur, happen immediately after injection and resolve within 2-4 days, not weeks later. D is incorrect because Chang et al demonstrated significant reduction in masseter volume when measured before and after treatment on CT scans.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old woman received immediate tissue expander/implant-based breast reconstruction following right mastectomy. Post-surgical adjuvant chemotherapy or radiation are not indicated. Two months post-operatively, she has finished the expansion phase, is satisfied with her current breast volume, and wishes to proceed with permanent implant placement. Besides the primary code for expander-to-permanent implant exchange, which CPT modifier is required to ensure reimbursement for this second-stage procedure within her initial global period?
A) -22
B) -50
C) -57
D) -58
E) -62
questions.answer:
D)
Modifier -58 is required for staged procedures performed at the same surgical site within the standard 90-day global period to indicate the procedure was planned, anticipated, more extensive than the original, or needed for therapy related to the original procedure. A is incorrect because -22 denotes increased procedural services when surgery required significantly more effort than planned. B is incorrect because -50 indicates bilateral procedures, which doesn't apply here. C is incorrect because -57 is for urgent/emergent procedures performed the same day or next day after evaluation. E is incorrect because -62 denotes two surgeons working together as co-primary surgeons, which wasn't the case here.

questions.question:
A 37-year-old woman arrives in the operating room following a crush injury to her left upper arm from a rollover motor vehicle accident with prolonged vehicle extraction. During surgery, she underwent bypass grafting to repair the brachial artery after humeral fixation. Post-operatively, she reports escalating left forearm pain requiring increased analgesics. Doppler examination reveals intact radial and ulnar pulses. Which clinical assessment would most likely guide the treatment approach at this point?
A) Evaluation of fingertip capillary refill
B) Doppler study of digital arteries
C) Duplex ultrasound to verify graft patency
D) Forearm compartment pressure measurements
E) Digital pulse oximetry
questions.answer:
D)
Forearm compartment pressure measurements are most appropriate to rule out compartment syndrome given the crush injury, reperfusion state, and disproportionate pain despite adequate analgesia. Direct compartment pressure measurement is the only option that can definitively diagnose compartment syndrome. A is incorrect because capillary refill assessment would be a late finding when intervention may no longer be effective. B is incorrect because digital artery Doppler doesn't assess muscle compartment perfusion. C is incorrect because while graft patency is important, intact pulses suggest the graft is functioning, and this doesn't evaluate compartment syndrome.
