E is incorrect because digital pulse oximetry assesses skin perfusion, not muscle compartment pressure.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old woman is diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. Which element from this patient's medical history represents the most significant risk factor for developing this condition?
A) First pregnancy before age 30
B) Menarche before age 12
C) Menopause before age 55
D) History of multiple breastfeeding episodes
E) Previous oral contraceptive use
questions.answer:
B)
Menarche before age 12 represents the highest breast cancer risk factor among the listed options due to prolonged estrogen exposure. A is incorrect because early first pregnancy (before 30) is actually protective against breast cancer, while late first pregnancy increases risk. C is incorrect because early menopause (before 55) is protective due to reduced lifetime estrogen exposure, while late menopause increases risk. D is incorrect because multiple breastfeeding episodes are protective against breast cancer, while lack of breastfeeding increases risk. E is incorrect because remote oral contraceptive use carries lower risk compared to recent use, and early menarche remains a stronger risk factor.

questions.question:
Which technical aspect has the most beneficial effect on the final cosmetic outcome of a surgical scar?
A) Single-layer wound closure
B) Utilizing absorbable suture material
C) Application of topical cyanoacrylate
D) Placement of retention sutures
E) Creating wound-edge eversion
questions.answer:
E)
Creating wound-edge eversion has the greatest favorable impact on scar appearance by minimizing the natural tendency for scars to widen and reducing closure tension. A is incorrect because layered closure is often preferable to eliminate dead space and provide stronger closure, though not all layers require separate closure. B is incorrect because no specific suture type is inherently superior - the key is precise approximation without tension. C is incorrect because while topical adhesives can be useful in certain situations, they don't provide the same eversion benefit as properly placed sutures. D is incorrect because retention sutures tend to leave obvious cross-hatching marks if not removed early, making them less favorable for cosmetic outcomes.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old male patient is brought to the surgical intensive care unit (SICU) after undergoing ventral hernia repair surgery. His past medical history is significant for coronary artery disease. Soon after his arrival to the SICU, the accompanying 12-lead ECG is recorded. This electrocardiographic pattern is most suggestive of which of the following arrhythmias?
A) Atrial fibrillation
B) Atrial flutter
C) First-degree AV block
D) Multifocal atrial tachycardia
E) Second-degree AV block
questions.answer:
E)
Second-degree AV block is the correct diagnosis. This rhythm disturbance demonstrates progressive lengthening of the PR interval followed by a dropped QRS complex (Wenckebach pattern), which is characteristic of this type of conduction abnormality. A) Atrial fibrillation is incorrect because it presents with an irregularly irregular rhythm without discernible P waves, not the progressive PR prolongation seen here. B) Atrial flutter is incorrect as it shows characteristic sawtooth flutter waves at rates of 250-350 bpm with fixed AV conduction ratios, not the progressive conduction delay pattern observed. C) First-degree AV block is incorrect because it shows consistent PR prolongation without dropped beats, whereas this pattern shows intermittent conduction failure. D) Multifocal atrial tachycardia is incorrect as it demonstrates multiple different P wave morphologies with rates of 110-140 bpm, not the AV conduction abnormality pattern shown.

questions.question:
A healthy 65-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with a 3-cm ulcerative scalp lesion. Physical examination reveals no palpable lymphadenopathy in the regional nodes. Chest radiograph is unremarkable. Punch biopsy confirms the diagnosis of well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Wide local excision is being considered. What is the recommended minimum surgical margin for this patient?
A) 1 mm
B) 2 mm
C) 4 mm
D) 6 mm
E) 12 mm
questions.answer:
D)
A 6 mm margin is the appropriate recommendation for this high-risk cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. This lesion qualifies as high-risk due to its size (>2 cm) and location on the scalp, which requires wider margins of 6-10 mm to achieve adequate clearance and minimize recurrence risk. A) 1 mm is incorrect as this margin is insufficient for any squamous cell carcinoma and would result in high recurrence rates. B) 2 mm is incorrect as this margin is too narrow even for low-risk lesions, which require at least 4 mm margins. C) 4 mm is incorrect because while appropriate for low-risk lesions (<2 cm, well-differentiated, not on high-risk anatomic sites), this lesion's scalp location and size make it high-risk requiring wider margins. E) 12 mm is incorrect as this exceeds standard recommendations and would result in unnecessary tissue loss without proven benefit over 6-10 mm margins.

questions.question:
A 6-month-old female infant is brought by her pediatrician for evaluation of a scalp lesion on the right parietal area that has been present since birth. The lesion appears as a 2×1-cm hairless yellow plaque that has enlarged proportionally with the child's growth. The infant is otherwise healthy and developing normally. What is the most appropriate recommendation for the parents?
A) Biopsy to rule out malignancy
B) CO2 laser therapy prior to puberty
C) Excision due to high risk of malignant transformation
D) MRI to evaluate for brain abnormalities
E) Continued observation because of anesthetic risk
questions.answer:
E)
Continued observation is most appropriate due to anesthetic risks in young children. The FDA has warned about potential neurodevelopmental effects of anesthesia in children under 3 years, and since malignant transformation in nevus sebaceous is extremely rare in childhood (never reported under age 5), delaying surgery until the child is older is prudent. A) Biopsy is incorrect because the clinical features are classic for nevus sebaceous, malignant transformation is exceedingly rare at this age, and biopsy would still require anesthesia without changing management. B) CO2 laser therapy is incorrect as surface treatments may leave deeper nevus cells behind, potentially making future malignant detection more difficult while still requiring anesthesia. C) Excision is incorrect at this age because while definitive treatment, the malignant transformation risk is virtually zero in infancy, making the anesthetic risks outweigh benefits. D) MRI is incorrect because small isolated nevus sebaceous lesions without other systemic manifestations do not require neuroimaging evaluation.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old non-smoking female presents with a 1.4-cm squamous cell carcinoma involving the left anterior mandibular gingiva and an associated upper cervical lymph node. CT imaging demonstrates full-thickness cortical penetration of the tumor into the superior mandible along with a single enlarged cervical lymph node. Besides neck dissection, what is the most appropriate surgical approach?
A) Marginal mandibulectomy
B) Radiation therapy
C) Segmental mandibulectomy
D) Transoral laser surgery
E) Wide local excision with periosteal stripping
questions.answer:
C)
Segmental mandibulectomy is the appropriate treatment for full-thickness cortical invasion, requiring removal of a complete cross-sectional portion of the mandible to achieve adequate oncologic clearance. This advanced tumor with transcortical invasion necessitates aggressive surgical resection. A) Marginal mandibulectomy is incorrect because it is only appropriate when tumor involvement is limited to the periosteum or superficial cortex, not for full-thickness cortical penetration as described. B) Radiation therapy alone is incorrect as it provides inadequate treatment for this advanced-stage cancer with bone invasion; combined surgery and postoperative radiation is the standard approach. D) Transoral laser surgery is incorrect because it cannot adequately address the full-thickness mandibular invasion and would result in positive margins. E) Wide local excision with periosteal stripping is incorrect as it is insufficient for transcortical invasion and would leave residual tumor in the bone.

questions.question:
What is the most accurate term for the volume of air that moves in and out of the lungs during each normal, quiet respiratory cycle?
A) Dead-space volume
B) Functional capacity
C) Residual volume
D) Tidal volume
E) Vital capacity
questions.answer:
D)
Tidal volume correctly describes the amount of air inhaled and exhaled during normal quiet breathing at rest, typically measured through spirometry and used as a key parameter in mechanical ventilation settings. A) Dead-space volume is incorrect because it refers to inhaled air that doesn't participate in gas exchange, including air in conducting airways and non-perfused alveoli, not the total respiratory volume. B) Functional capacity is incorrect as it describes an individual's ability to perform daily activities, often measured in metabolic equivalents (METs) through exercise testing, not a lung volume measurement. C) Residual volume is incorrect because it represents the air remaining in the lungs after maximum exhalation, not the air moved during normal breathing. E) Vital capacity is incorrect as it measures the total air expelled after the deepest possible inspiration, which is much larger than normal breathing volumes.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old woman continues to require mechanical ventilation in the ICU following an extended surgical procedure. Blood gas analysis reveals respiratory acidosis. The medical team plans to increase respiratory minute ventilation. Minute ventilation is determined by multiplying respiratory rate by which of the following measurements?
A) Inspiratory capacity
B) Residual volume
C) Tidal volume
D) Total lung capacity
E) Vital capacity
questions.answer:
C)

Minute ventilation is determined by multiplying respiratory rate and tidal volume. Tidal volume represents the volume of air moved in and out of the lungs during normal, quiet breathing without additional inspiratory or expiratory effort. This calculation is fundamental in mechanical ventilation due to its inverse correlation with arterial carbon dioxide levels. However, not all ventilated air participates in gas exchange due to dead space in conducting airways and poorly perfused alveoli. A) Inspiratory capacity is incorrect because it represents the maximum air volume that can be inhaled starting from resting position, not the normal breathing volume used in minute ventilation calculations. B) Residual volume is incorrect because it refers to the air remaining in lungs after maximum expiration, which cannot be measured or used in minute ventilation. D) Total lung capacity is incorrect because it represents the sum of all lung volumes and is not involved in minute ventilation calculations. E) Vital capacity is incorrect because it represents the maximum air volume that can be expelled after maximum inspiration, not the regular breathing volume.

questions.question:
A healthy 50-year-old man is undergoing tumor removal and immediate reconstruction using an anterolateral thigh free flap for recurring squamous cell carcinoma of the mouth. His history includes previous tumor excision, primary wound closure, and radiotherapy. During surgery, he receives a low-dose phenylephrine infusion to maintain blood pressure. Which of the following approaches is most likely to reduce the risk of pedicle thrombosis in this patient?
A) Giving intravenous fluid boluses to discontinue phenylephrine
B) Performing anastomosis to non-irradiated recipient neck vessels
C) Using end-to-end anastomosis rather than end-to-side anastomosis
D) Administering intravenous heparin bolus 10 minutes prior to pedicle ligation
E) Creating venous anastomosis to internal jugular vein rather than external jugular vein
questions.answer:
B)

Performing anastomosis to non-irradiated recipient neck vessels significantly reduces flap failure rates compared to using radiated vessels in head and neck reconstruction. Radiation damages vessel walls and impairs healing, making non-radiated vessels the preferred choice when available. A) is incorrect because vasopressors do not increase pedicle thrombosis risk; recent meta-analyses actually show decreased thrombosis rates with perioperative vasopressor use due to improved hemodynamics and reduced fluid overload complications. C) is incorrect because meta-analyses demonstrate no difference in pedicle thrombosis rates between end-to-end and end-to-side anastomotic techniques for either arterial or venous connections. D) is incorrect because systemic heparin has not been proven to decrease pedicle thrombosis, though topical heparin irrigation may have some benefit based on animal studies. E) is incorrect because there is no proven difference in vessel patency rates between internal and external jugular vein systems for free flap reconstruction.

questions.question:
A 61-year-old man presents for assessment of a 3 x 3-cm heel defect with bone exposure. Reconstruction with a medial plantar flap is being considered. The main vascular supply to this flap originates from which of the following vessels?
A) Arcuate
B) Dorsalis pedis
C) Peroneal
D) Plantar arch
E) Posterior tibial
questions.answer:
E)

The medial plantar flap receives its primary vascular supply from the medial plantar artery, which is a terminal division of the posterior tibial artery. This reliable blood supply makes the medial plantar flap an excellent choice for heel reconstruction with good sensory innervation. A) is incorrect because the arcuate artery is a terminal branch of the anterior tibial artery on the dorsum of the foot and does not supply the medial plantar flap. B) is incorrect because the dorsalis pedis artery is the continuation of the anterior tibial artery and supplies the dorsal foot, not the medial plantar region. C) is incorrect because the peroneal artery is a proximal branch of the posterior tibial artery that runs in the deep posterior compartment and does not contribute to the medial plantar flap's blood supply. D) is incorrect because the plantar arch is formed by the confluence of the lateral plantar artery and deep plantar artery at the metatarsal level, which is distal to the medial plantar flap's vascular territory.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old woman seeks consultation regarding dissatisfaction with her nasal appearance. Clinical examination reveals a parenthesis tip deformity characterized by vertically positioned lower lateral cartilages. Which of the following grafts is most suitable for correcting this deformity?
A) Caudal septal extension
B) Crural turnover
C) Lateral crural strut
D) Spreader
E) Spring
questions.answer:
C)

A lateral crural strut graft is the most appropriate treatment for parenthesis tip deformity with vertically oriented lower lateral cartilages. This 3-4 mm wide cartilage strip is sutured to the deep surface of the lateral crura and can be buried or sutured to pyriform aperture soft tissue, allowing the native lower lateral cartilage to be rotated inferiorly and maintained in proper position. A) is incorrect because caudal septal extension grafts are used to control tip projection and lengthen shortened noses, not to correct lateral crural orientation. B) is incorrect because crural turnover grafts involve folding the cephalic portion of the upper lateral cartilage inferiorly to strengthen and support weakened lower lateral cartilages, but don't address vertical orientation. D) is incorrect because spreader grafts are placed at the dorsal septal edge to correct internal nasal valve collapse and support upper lateral cartilages, not lower lateral cartilage positioning. E) is incorrect because spring grafts widen the middle vault by spanning between upper lateral cartilages and don't address tip deformities.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman presents with a 2-year history of an asymptomatic mass in the thenar eminence. Physical examination demonstrates a soft, movable, painless mass that does not allow light transmission. Which of the following represents the most probable diagnosis?
A) Epidermal cyst
B) Ganglion
C) Giant cell tumor
D) Glomus tumor
E) Lipoma
questions.answer:
E)

Lipoma is the most likely diagnosis given the clinical presentation of a soft, mobile, non-tender mass in the thenar eminence in a middle-aged woman. Lipomas represent 10-20% of hand and wrist tumors, most commonly occur in the thenar eminence, have a 2:1 female predominance, and typically present in the third to sixth decades of life. A) is incorrect because epidermal cysts have a 2:1 male predominance, peak at age 39, and typically occur in distal phalanges, usually on the palmar aspect of index and long fingers. B) is incorrect because ganglions account for 50-70% of benign hand tumors with 3:1 female predominance, usually occur in second to fourth decades, and are typically located at dorsal carpal, volar carpal, or volar retinacular sites, with some showing transillumination. C) is incorrect because giant cell tumors show no sex preference, occur in fourth to sixth decades, and are typically located in digits, mostly on the volar aspect of index and long fingers. D) is incorrect because glomus tumors represent only 1-5% of hand tumors, have 2:1 female predominance, occur between ages 30-50, and are subungual 50% of the time.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male presents to the clinic with a 10-year history of progressive enlargement of the right facial region. Clinical examination reveals class I bite relationship, normal mouth opening capacity, and worn occlusal surfaces on the right posterior teeth. The right facial area becomes more prominent during jaw clenching. Imaging demonstrates a right masseter muscle that is double the size of the left, with outward bowing of the mandibular angle. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Condylar reduction
B) Masseter resection
C) Orthodontics
D) Radiation therapy
E) Sagittal split osteotomy
questions.answer:
B)

Masseter resection is the correct treatment for this case of benign masseteric hypertrophy. This condition typically results from chronic unilateral teeth clenching and causes enlargement of the masseter muscle, leading to facial asymmetry. Surgical removal of a portion of the masseter muscle, often combined with bone contouring, effectively addresses the cosmetic deformity and functional issues. A) Condylar reduction is used for condylar dislocation or hyperplasia, not masseteric hypertrophy. C) Orthodontics cannot correct muscle hypertrophy and is unnecessary given the normal class I occlusion. D) Radiation therapy is inappropriate for benign conditions and doesn't address the underlying muscle enlargement. E) Sagittal split osteotomy is indicated for malocclusion correction, not for treating muscle hypertrophy with normal occlusion.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old HIV-positive male presents to the emergency room with a one-month history of progressive enlargement and discomfort at the tip of his right index finger. Physical examination reveals marked swelling, redness, and small fluid-filled lesions on the fingertip and surrounding nail area. Several nodular, reddish-brown patches are observed on his chest and arms. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Administration of acyclovir
B) Administration of cefuroxime
C) Administration of ketoconazole cream
D) Excision of proximal nail plate
E) Incision and drainage
questions.answer:
A)

Acyclovir administration is correct for this herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection of the finger. The characteristic vesicular lesions on an erythematous base, prolonged duration (>3 weeks), and HIV-positive status strongly suggest HSV infection. The nodular lesions suggest possible Kaposi sarcoma, further supporting immunocompromise. Antiviral therapy with acyclovir is the appropriate treatment. B) Cefuroxime treats bacterial infections, but this presentation is viral, not bacterial. C) Ketoconazole cream treats fungal infections, which don't typically present with vesicles. D) Nail plate excision is unnecessary and inappropriate for viral infections. E) Incision and drainage should never be performed on herpetic infections as it can lead to secondary bacterial infection or viral encephalitis.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old female is planned for breast augmentation surgery using intravenous sedation and local infiltration of 1% lidocaine with 1:100,000 epinephrine. Her weight is 110 lb (50 kg). What is the maximum volume of lidocaine with epinephrine that can be safely administered to this patient?
A) 20 mL
B) 25 mL
C) 30 mL
D) 35 mL
E) 40 mL
questions.answer:
D)

The maximum safe dose of lidocaine with epinephrine for non-tumescent injection is 7 mg/kg. For this 50 kg patient, the maximum dose is 350 mg. Since 1% lidocaine contains 10 mg per mL, the maximum volume is 35 mL (350 mg ÷ 10 mg/mL = 35 mL). A) 20 mL would provide only 200 mg, which is unnecessarily restrictive. B) 25 mL would provide 250 mg, still below the safe maximum. C) 30 mL would provide 300 mg, which is safe but not the maximum allowable. E) 40 mL would provide 400 mg, exceeding the safe dose limit of 350 mg for this patient's weight.

questions.question:
An 80-year-old female seeks evaluation for inability to bend the tip of her little finger on her non-dominant hand, occurring 9 months after a knife injury. She did not receive treatment initially and reports no pain or functional limitations with daily activities. Examination shows a healed scar on the palm side of the middle finger segment. She has full movement at the knuckle and middle joint, but no bending at the fingertip joint. What is the most appropriate treatment?
A) Delayed primary flexor digitorum profundus repair
B) Flexor digitorum superficialis transfer
C) PIP joint arthrodesis
D) Staged flexor tendon reconstruction with placement of a silicone rod followed by tendon grafting
E) No intervention is indicated
questions.answer:
E)

No intervention is indicated for this elderly patient who reports no functional deficits from her injury. The intact flexor digitorum superficialis provides adequate function for most daily activities, and reconstruction through an intact FDS is typically reserved for younger patients (10-21 years) with high dexterity demands. Her age and lack of functional complaints make her a poor candidate for complex reconstruction. A) Delayed primary repair is impossible after 9 months. B) FDS transfer would sacrifice a functioning tendon unnecessarily. C) PIP joint arthrodesis is only indicated for joint instability, which is not present. D) Staged reconstruction would be the approach if surgery were indicated, but given her age, functional status, and lack of complaints, the risks outweigh potential benefits.

questions.question:
An active 73-year-old female presents with Eaton Stage IV arthritis affecting the thumb base joint of her dominant hand (complete joint destruction with subluxation). She experiences severe pain during gripping activities like opening doors or unscrewing jar lids. Which procedure offers the most reliable pain relief and functional improvement for this patient?
A) CMC fusion
B) Metacarpal osteotomy
C) Trapezial hemi-resection and tendon interposition
D) Trapezial resection and silicone implantation
E) Trapezial resection, ligament reconstruction, and tendon interposition
questions.answer:
E)

Trapezial resection with ligament reconstruction and tendon interposition (LRTI) is the gold standard treatment for Stage IV thumb basilar joint arthritis. This stage involves complete destruction of both the trapeziometacarpal and scaphotrapezial joints, making LRTI the most predictable procedure for pain relief and functional improvement. It provides excellent outcomes, especially in lower-demand patients. A) CMC fusion is better suited for younger, high-demand patients and has higher complication rates in elderly patients. B) Metacarpal osteotomy is only appropriate for early-stage arthritis, not Stage IV. C) Trapezial hemi-resection is insufficient for Stage IV disease with complete joint destruction. D) Silicone implantation has fallen out of favor due to high rates of instability, dislocation, implant failure, and chronic inflammation leading to bone resorption.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female patient receives upper and lower lid blepharoplasty using local anesthesia with IV sedation. Initially, the patient experiences no discomfort during the procedure; however, she develops significant pain when excision of the lower lateral fat compartment begins. Which of the following nerves is responsible for the pain experienced by this patient?
A) Facial nerve
B) Infraorbital nerve
C) Infratrochlear nerve
D) Lacrimal nerve
E) Zygomaticofacial nerve
questions.answer:
E)
The zygomaticofacial nerve is correct because it provides sensory innervation to the lateral fat compartment of the lower eyelid. A) The facial nerve is incorrect because it is a motor nerve controlling facial muscles, not providing sensory innervation. B) The infraorbital nerve is incorrect because while it supplies the lower eyelid, it does not specifically innervate the lateral fat pad. C) The infratrochlear nerve is incorrect because it provides sensation to the medial aspects of the upper and lower eyelids, not the lateral fat pad. D) The lacrimal nerve is incorrect because it supplies sensory innervation to the upper eyelid, not the lower lateral fat compartment.

questions.question:
An 8-year-old male child presents to the office for assessment of a congenital ear malformation featuring an absent antihelical fold. During embryonic development, which of the following structures failed to form properly?
A) First pharyngeal cleft
B) First pharyngeal pouch
C) Second pharyngeal arch
D) Third pharyngeal arch
E) Third pharyngeal pouch
questions.answer:
C)
The second pharyngeal arch is correct because ear formation begins during the third gestational month from six hillocks originating from the first and second pharyngeal arches, and malformations like unfolded antihelix result from improper development of these structures. A) The first pharyngeal cleft is incorrect because it develops into the external auditory canal, not the external ear structure. B) The first pharyngeal pouch is incorrect because it forms the eustachian tube and middle ear cavity, not external ear features. D) The third pharyngeal arch is incorrect because it contributes to hyoid bone formation, not ear development. E) The third pharyngeal pouch is incorrect because it develops into parathyroid glands and thymus, having no role in ear formation.

questions.question:
A patient with complete unilateral cleft lip and palate comes for consultation regarding alveolar bone grafting. The permanent lateral maxillary incisor is missing. Which of the following represents the most appropriate timing to perform alveolar bone grafting in this patient?
A) Prior to central incisor eruption
B) After permanent canine eruption
C) During infancy, concurrent with primary lip repair
D) During mixed dentition, prior to permanent canine eruption
questions.answer:
D)
During mixed dentition, prior to permanent canine eruption is correct because optimal bone graft success occurs when performed with the secondary canine root one-half to two-thirds developed, allowing the canine to erupt through the graft, typically between 8-12 years of age. A) Prior to central incisor eruption is incorrect because this timing is too early and does not optimize periodontal support for adjacent teeth. B) After permanent canine eruption is incorrect because studies show decreased success rates for bone grafts performed after canine eruption, as exposed tooth structures do not heal to bone graft. C) During infancy, concurrent with primary lip repair is incorrect because primary bone grafting has fallen out of favor due to diminished maxillary growth and poor arch relationships.

questions.question:
Based on the Malignant Hyperthermia Association of the United States recommendations, which of the following intravenous medications should be contraindicated during the acute management phase of malignant hyperthermia, after dantrolene has been given, when managing subsequent cardiac arrhythmias?
A) Dextrose 50% solution
B) Epinephrine
C) Lidocaine
D) Metoprolol
E) Verapamil
questions.answer:
E)
Verapamil is correct because calcium channel blockers like verapamil and diltiazem are contraindicated with dantrolene administration due to the risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia, since malignant hyperthermia involves calcium channel homeostasis disturbance. A) Dextrose 50% solution is incorrect because it can be safely used during advanced cardiovascular life support protocols or hyperkalemia treatment. B) Epinephrine is incorrect because it may be used as needed during resuscitation protocols without contraindication. C) Lidocaine is incorrect because it can be safely administered for arrhythmia management during malignant hyperthermia treatment. D) Metoprolol is incorrect because beta-blockers can be used safely during malignant hyperthermia management.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male patient comes to the office due to a 5-year history of excessive bilateral axillary sweating. He reports daily antiperspirant use, but still perspires through his clothing several times daily. He finds this condition embarrassing and disruptive to his professional life. Botulinum toxin type A injection into each axilla is being considered. Which of the following represents the most appropriate dose (per axilla) of this toxin for treatment?
A) 15 units
B) 25 units
C) 50 units
D) 100 units
E) 150 units
questions.answer:
C)
50 units is correct because this is the established appropriate dosing for axillary botulinum toxin type A treatment, which provides good improvement with 90% of patients experiencing relief for at least 3 months. A) 15 units is incorrect because this dose is insufficient for effective axillary hyperhidrosis treatment. B) 25 units is incorrect because this dose is below the therapeutic range needed for axillary sweating control. D) 100 units is incorrect because this dose is used for palmar injections, not axillary treatment. E) 150 units is incorrect because this higher dose is reserved for plantar injections, not axillary hyperhidrosis.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old female patient seeks enhancement of her rounded nasal tip. An open rhinoplasty with tip refinement is scheduled. During surgery, examination reveals that the rounded appearance results from broadly curved lower lateral cartilages that are thick and relatively rigid. The dome width exceeds 6 mm. The divergence angle is within normal limits. Which of the following surgical techniques is most appropriate to address this deformity?
A) Alar margin grafting
B) Cephalic reduction of the lower lateral cartilage
C) Intercrural spanning sutures
D) Lateral crural strut grafting
E) Subdomal spreader graft placement
questions.answer:
D)
A rounded/boxy nasal tip may result from curved lower lateral cartilages with excessive dome width (ideally less than 4 mm), increased divergence angle (ideally less than 30 degrees), or both factors combined. In this case, the problem is broadly curved lower lateral cartilages. The optimal treatment is lateral crural strut grafting. These grafts are typically obtained from septal cartilage and secured to the undersurface of the lower lateral cartilage. They provide structural support and can effectively reshape thick, inflexible lower lateral cartilages. A) Alar margin grafting is incorrect because it addresses rim buckling rather than cartilage convexity. B) Cephalic reduction is incorrect because it narrows but doesn't correct the convex shape. C) Intercrural spanning sutures are incorrect because they work only with flexible cartilages, not rigid ones as described. E) Subdomal spreader grafts are incorrect because they treat pinched tip deformities, not bulbous tips.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old female patient returns for follow-up 2 weeks following an endoscopic forehead lift and complains of loss of sensation in the middle forehead region. Which of the following nerves has most likely sustained injury?
A) Frontal division of the facial nerve
B) Infraorbital nerve
C) Supraorbital nerve
D) Zygomaticofacial nerve
E) Zygomaticotemporal nerve
questions.answer:
C)
Sensory loss in the middle forehead area typically results from traction damage to the supraorbital nerve, which is a branch of the ophthalmic division (V1) of the trigeminal nerve. The supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves provide sensation to the central forehead region. A) The frontal division of the facial nerve is incorrect because it provides motor innervation to the frontalis muscle, not sensory supply. B) The infraorbital nerve is incorrect because it innervates the mid-face and upper lip area. D) The zygomaticofacial nerve is incorrect because it supplies sensation to the lateral orbital and cheek regions. E) The zygomaticotemporal nerve is incorrect because it innervates the anterior temporal region.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male patient is brought to the emergency room due to severe bleeding from a stab wound to the neck located above the mandibular angle and anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Following airway management, surgical repair of a jugular vein laceration is completed. In which anatomical region is this injury situated?
A) Posterior triangle
B) Zone I
C) Zone II
D) Zone III
questions.answer:
D)
Zone III encompasses the upper neck region extending from above the mandibular angle to the skull base and contains structures including the pharynx, jugular veins, vertebral arteries, and distal internal carotid arteries. Since the injury is described as being above the mandibular angle, it falls within Zone III boundaries. A) The posterior triangle is incorrect because the injury is anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, placing it in the anterior triangle. B) Zone I is incorrect because it encompasses the lower neck from the sternal notch/clavicles to the cricoid cartilage. C) Zone II is incorrect because it extends from the cricoid cartilage to the mandibular angle, not above it.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old boy presents with a mass of the left forearm that has been enlarging over the past 3 months. A photograph is shown. Biopsy of the mass is consistent with spindle cell sarcoma. MRI shows a well-encapsulated mass that does not infiltrate neurovascular structures. CT scan of the chest shows no evidence of metastatic lesions. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Amputation at the midforearm
B) Chemotherapy only
C) Excision and chemotherapy
D) Excision and radiation therapy
E) Radiation therapy only
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Soft tissue sarcomas are rare malignant tumors representing less than 1% of all malignancies, with only 25% occurring in the upper extremity. The diagnostic workup generally includes a biopsy, magnetic resonance imaging scan to assess the extent of the tumor and its relationship to adjacent structures, and a computed tomography scan of the chest. This combination allows for appropriate clinical staging of the patient. The role of sentinel lymph node biopsy in the workup of soft tissue sarcomas is controversial. Treatment consists of wide excision, primary reconstruction, and radiation therapy (adjuvant or neoadjuvant). The tumor must be completely removed with a cuff of normal tissue (at least 1 cm); violation of the tumor decreases 5-year survival from 87 to 47%. More than 90% of extremity sarcomas can be managed with a limb-sparing resection.


Chemotherapy is rarely indicated and is never used as the only treatment for soft tissue sarcoma. Primary amputation is considered when the tumor infiltrates major neurovascular structures and resection would result in the sacrifice of more than one major peripheral nerve. Additional indications for amputation include involvement of the interosseous membrane, advanced disease with extensive loss of functional tissues, and severe comorbidities limiting reconstructive options.


ReferencesChao AH, Mayerson JL, Chandawarkar R, Scharschmidt TJ. Surgical management of soft tissue sarcomas: extremity sarcomas. J Surg Oncol. 2015 Apr;111(5):540-545.Megerle K, Sauerbier M. Reconstructive treatment of soft tissue sarcoma of the upper extremity. J Hand Surg Am. 2011 Jul;36(7):1241-1247.Popov P, Tukiainen E, Asko-Seljavaara S, et al. Soft-tissue sarcomas of the upper extremity: surgical treatment and outcome. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2004 Jan;113(1):222-230.Saint-Cyr M, Langstein HN. Reconstruction of the hand and upper extremity after tumor resection. J Surg Oncol. 2006 Nov 1;94(6):490-503.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old man is brought to emergency department because of a thumb avulsion injury measuring 3 √o 3 cm. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the best option for sensate, soft-tissue coverage?


A) Cross-finger flap
B) First dorsal metacarpal artery flap
C) Moberg flap
D) Pedicled groin flap
E) Skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.


There are several sensate options for thumb pulp deformities. These include neurovascular island flaps, Moberg flaps, free toe pulp flaps, and the first dorsal metacarpal artery flap (FDMA). Cross finger flaps, skin grafts, and pedicle groin flaps do not have innate innervation. The defect in the question involves the entire pulp of the thumb overlying the distal phalanx and is too large for a Moberg advancement flap.


The FDMA flap is supplied by its eponymous artery, which travels in the fascia overlying the index metacarpal and supplies the skin overlying the dorsum of the proximal phalanx. The vessel is accompanied superficially by a branch of the radial nerve that provides neural activation to the skin overlying the proximal phalanx of the index finger. The flap can be transposed to provide sensate coverage of the tip of the thumb, and can provide sufficient size to resurface relatively large defects.


Cortical reorientation is the fact that the brain recognizes a stimulus from the flap area as a stimulus from the thumb, and not from the index finger. This process takes some time, but is usually complete after 2 years. Average static two-point discrimination in these flaps utilized for thumb resurfacing is 10 to 11 mm.


Use of the FDMA flap for resurfacing of the thumb pulp has been compared to heterodigital island flaps in several studies. Both remain options to be considered, but the ease of elevation, limited dissection, and acceptable donor site morbidity make the FDMA flap a common primary option for thumb tip resurfacing.


References
Tr√§nkle M, Sauerbier M, Heitmann C, Germann G. Restoration of thumb sensibility with the innervated first dorsal metacarpal artery island flap. J Hand Surg Am. 2003; 28(5):758‚Äi766.
Muyldermans T, Hierner R. First dorsal metacarpal artery flap for thumb reconstruction: a retrospective clinical study. Strat Traum Limb Recon. 2009; 4:27.
Delikonstantinou IP, Gravvanis AI, Dimitriou V, Zogogiannis I, Douma A, Tsoutsos DA. Foucher first dorsal metacarpal artery flap versus Littler heterodigital neurovascular flap in resurfacing thumb pulp loss defects. Ann Plast Surg. 2011 Aug;67(2):119-22.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with a 10-mm mole on his right cheek. He reports concern because the lesion bleeds each time he shaves. Surgical removal of the mole is planned. Besides the standard CPT ICD-9-CM diagnostic code 216.3 (nevus), which of the following additional diagnostic codes is most suitable for billing this lesion?
A) 173.30 (skin neoplasm, primary)
B) 238.2 (skin neoplasm, uncertain behavior)
C) 459.0 (hemorrhage)
D) 782.9 (skin lesion changes)
E) No supplementary code required
questions.answer:
C)
Proper documentation of "complicating pathology" must be included in medical records and ICD-9-CM diagnostic coding for Medicare coverage of benign lesion excisions. Without a complicating pathology code, the procedure may be deemed "non-covered" or "cosmetic" by Medicare. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services recognize bleeding, intertrigo, pain, and itching as complicating pathologies justifying Medicare reimbursement. Since this lesion repeatedly bleeds during shaving, code 459.0 for hemorrhage is most appropriate. A) Code 173.30 is incorrect because it implies malignancy, which is not indicated. B) Code 238.2 is incorrect because it suggests uncertain malignant potential without evidence. D) Code 782.9 is incorrect because there's no history of the lesion changing or growing. E) An additional code is required to justify medical necessity.

questions.question:
Which of the following represents the strongest indication for considering lower limb replantation?
A) Bilateral clean amputation
B) Crush-type injury mechanism
C) Warm ischemia exceeding 8 hours
D) Multiple-level trauma
E) Patient age greater than 50 years
questions.answer:
A)
Lower extremity replantation indications are quite restrictive. The ideal candidate would be a young patient with bilateral leg amputations caused by a clean, sharp mechanism of injury. This scenario offers the best functional outcome potential and justifies the extensive surgical undertaking. B) Crush injury mechanism is incorrect because it represents a contraindication due to extensive tissue damage and poor healing potential. C) Ischemia time over 8 hours is incorrect because it represents a contraindication due to irreversible tissue damage. D) Multiple-level injury is incorrect because it represents a contraindication due to complexity and poor functional prognosis. E) Advanced age is incorrect because it represents a relative contraindication due to decreased healing capacity and functional demands.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient receives open reduction and internal fixation for a fracture shown in the radiographic image. At six weeks post-surgery, she develops widespread swelling, rigidity, and discomfort in her right upper limb. Her skin has a glossy appearance, and she exhibits altered hair growth and sweating patterns in the right upper extremity compared to the left. Prophylactic administration of which medication following the initial trauma would have been most effective in reducing the likelihood of this complication?
A) Amitriptyline
B) Ascorbic acid
C) Gabapentin
D) Prednisone
E) Pregabalin
questions.answer:
B)

Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) represents a chronic pain condition that continues despite the absence of active tissue damage, featuring autonomic dysfunction, trophic alterations, and functional impairment. The clinical presentation described - glossy skin, altered hair and sweat patterns, swelling, and pain - is characteristic of CRPS. Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) at 500 mg daily for 50 days has been proven in randomized controlled trials to significantly reduce CRPS incidence when used prophylactically after distal radius fractures. A is incorrect because amitriptyline is used for CRPS treatment, not prevention. C is incorrect because gabapentin treats established CRPS but doesn't prevent it. D is incorrect because prednisone may treat CRPS symptoms but lacks proven prophylactic efficacy. E is incorrect because pregabalin is therapeutic for existing CRPS, not preventive.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male patient is planned for extensive oncologic resection in the inguinal region. Reconstruction of the resulting tissue defect using a rectus femoris musculocutaneous flap is intended. What is the most probable functional consequence?
A) 15-Degree extensor lag of the knee
B) 20-Degree flexion contracture of the hip
C) Compromised ability to stand for extended periods
D) Inability to adduct the leg
E) No loss of function
questions.answer:
A)

The rectus femoris muscle is a component of the quadriceps group that extends the knee and inserts into the patella. When harvested as a flap, despite patellar tendon repair, patients typically experience approximately 15 degrees of knee extensor lag due to loss of this muscle's contribution to knee extension. This represents the most common and predictable functional deficit. B is incorrect because hip flexion contractures are not associated with rectus femoris harvest. C is incorrect because prolonged standing difficulties are not reported complications of this procedure. D is incorrect because leg adduction involves different muscle groups (adductors) that are not affected by rectus femoris harvest. E is incorrect because some functional loss, specifically knee extensor weakness, is expected and well-documented.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old transgender female (birth-assigned male) receives penile inversion vaginoplasty for gender dysphoria management. She desires the capability for penetrative sexual intercourse post-operatively. She received counseling regarding surgical risks including urethral damage, rectal perforation, and fistula development. Which anatomical plane should be utilized for neovaginal cavity dissection to minimize these complications while achieving sufficient depth for penetrative intercourse?
A) Anterior rectal fascia
B) Prostatic capsule
C) Rectoprostatic fascia (Denonvilliers' fascia)
D) Rectosacral fascia (Waldeyer's fascia)
E) Superficial perineal fascia (Colles' fascia)
questions.answer:
C)

Denonvilliers' fascia (rectoprostatic fascia) provides the optimal dissection plane for neovaginal cavity creation. This relatively avascular fascial plane separates the rectum from the prostate, allowing safe dissection to the peritoneal fold while achieving adequate depth for penetrative intercourse. A is incorrect because dissecting along the anterior rectal fascia exposes rectal muscle fibers, increasing risk of rectal injury during dissection and subsequent pressure necrosis. B is incorrect because prostatic capsule dissection risks inadvertent entry into the prostatic urethra, potentially causing urethrovaginal fistula and incontinence. D is incorrect because Waldeyer's fascia is presacral and not anatomically appropriate for neovaginal cavity creation. E is incorrect because Colles' fascia is superficial and dissection in this plane alone would not provide sufficient depth for penetrative intercourse.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old female patient is scheduled for facial rejuvenation using fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatment. This therapeutic modality functions by specifically targeting which component within skin tissue?
A) Collagen
B) Elastin
C) Hyaluronic acid
D) Melanin
E) Water
questions.answer:
E)

Fractionated carbon dioxide laser operates on the principle of selective photothermolysis, specifically targeting water as its chromophore. The CO2 laser emits at 10,600 nm wavelength with a water absorption coefficient of 800/cm. Since the epidermis contains approximately 90% water, the laser energy vaporizes tissue when temperatures exceed 100°C (212°F), creating controlled thermal injury for skin resurfacing. A is incorrect because while collagen may be secondarily affected by thermal changes, it is not the primary target chromophore. B is incorrect because elastin is not the specific chromophore targeted by CO2 lasers. C is incorrect because hyaluronic acid is not the primary chromophore for CO2 laser energy. D is incorrect because melanin is the target chromophore for different laser wavelengths used in pigment-specific treatments, not CO2 resurfacing lasers.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male adolescent receives a diagnosis of infected molar tooth and is scheduled for dental extraction. Prior to the surgical date, he presents to the emergency department with excessive salivation, tongue protrusion, bilateral firm swelling of the submandibular area, and neck tenderness. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Ludwig angina
B) Periapical abscess
C) Peritonsillar abscess
D) Primary mononucleosis
E) Reactive lymphadenopathy
questions.answer:
A)

Ludwig angina is a rapidly progressive cellulitis of the floor of the mouth characterized by the classic triad of drooling, protruding tongue, and bilateral woody (non-fluctuant) submandibular edema. This deep space infection commonly originates from infected mandibular molars where the thin bone allows spread to the sublingual and submylohyoid spaces. The condition requires immediate airway management and aggressive treatment. B is incorrect because periapical abscess remains localized to the tooth apex without causing bilateral submandibular woody edema. C is incorrect because peritonsillar abscess typically presents unilaterally with lateral pharyngeal involvement, not bilateral submandibular woody edema. D is incorrect because mononucleosis causes lymphadenopathy but not the characteristic woody edema of Ludwig angina. E is incorrect because reactive lymphadenopathy produces mobile, tender lymph nodes rather than the firm, woody tissue induration characteristic of Ludwig angina.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a motorcycle accident. Clinical assessment and radiographic imaging reveal an isolated left wrist trauma compatible with perilunate dislocation. In cases of perilunate dislocation, disruption of which structure represents the primary injury that subsequently causes lunate displacement?
A) Dorsal wrist ligaments
B) Lunocapitate articulation
C) Lunotriquetral ligaments
D) Scapholunate ligament
E) Triangular fibrocartilage complex
questions.answer:
D)
The scapholunate ligament disruption is the initial injury in the progressive perilunate instability sequence that ultimately leads to lunate dislocation. According to the Wagner-Mayfield classification, perilunate injuries follow a predictable pattern starting with scapholunate dissociation (Stage 1), progressing through midcarpal separation (Stage 2), lunotriquetral disruption (Stage 3), and finally complete lunate dislocation (Stage 4). A is incorrect because dorsal wrist ligaments are not the primary initiating injury in this sequence. B is incorrect because lunocapitate separation occurs later in the injury progression (Stage 2). C is incorrect because lunotriquetral ligament disruption occurs in Stage 3, after the initial scapholunate injury. E is incorrect because the triangular fibrocartilage complex is not involved in the perilunate injury sequence.

questions.question:
For patients with syndromic craniosynostosis, effective midface distraction osteogenesis is most likely to produce which of the following results?
A) Reduced ANB angle
B) Reduced exorbitism
C) Reduced upper airway volume
D) Enhanced negative overjet
E) Enhanced SNB angle
questions.answer:
B)
Successful midface distraction reduces exorbitism by increasing orbital volume, which allows the eyes to sit in a more normal position. The gradual advancement achieved through distraction osteogenesis can exceed 30mm, far greater than conventional single-stage procedures, leading to significant improvement in orbital projection. A is incorrect because midface advancement actually increases the ANB angle, not decreases it. C is incorrect because midface advancement increases upper airway volume, often improving obstructive sleep apnea. D is incorrect because the procedure decreases negative overjet by advancing the midface. E is incorrect because midface advancement decreases the SNB angle, not increases it.

questions.question:
For a rheumatoid arthritis patient experiencing painful, disabling deformity of the left wrist and hand, which intervention represents the most suitable initial approach for reconstruction?
A) Intercarpal arthrodesis combined with ulnar head replacement
B) Proximal interphalangeal joint fusion with terminal extensor tendon release
C) Silicone metacarpophalangeal joint replacement with sagittal band repair
D) Soft-tissue repair of extensor tendon rupture using tendon transfer
E) Complete wrist fusion with ulnar head resection
questions.answer:
E)
Total wrist arthrodesis with ulnar head excision is the most appropriate first step because rheumatoid reconstruction follows a proximal-to-distal sequence, and the wrist is the most commonly affected joint requiring stabilization first. With pancarpal arthritis present, complete wrist fusion provides the necessary stability for successful hand reconstruction, while ulnar head excision addresses the caput ulna syndrome common in rheumatoid disease. A is incorrect because intercarpal fusion alone would be insufficient for pancarpal arthritis. B is incorrect because PIP joint procedures should be performed after wrist stabilization, not before. C is incorrect because MCP joint arthroplasty should follow wrist reconstruction in the treatment sequence. D is incorrect because soft-tissue procedures alone do not address the underlying joint destruction and instability.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old male had squamous cell carcinoma excision and primary repair with extensive broad subcutaneous dissection of the leg one week ago. Assessment reveals positive margins, requiring re-excision that creates a defect with exposed tendon lacking peritenon. Which reconstructive approach is most suitable for this patient?
A) Bipedicled advancement flap
B) Keystone flap
C) Mustardé rotational flap
D) Split-thickness skin graft
E) V-Y advancement flap
questions.answer:
A)
The bipedicled advancement flap is most appropriate because it maintains dual blood supply connections, allowing for a 2:1 length-to-width ratio and better reliability after previous wide undermining. The prior extensive dissection would have created a delay phenomenon, potentially improving flap viability, and the bipedicled design provides redundant perfusion compared to single-pedicle flaps. B is incorrect because keystone flaps rely on perforators that were likely damaged during the extensive undermining. C is incorrect because Mustardé flaps are specifically designed for cheek reconstruction, not leg defects. D is incorrect because split-thickness skin grafts cannot survive on tendon without peritenon. E is incorrect because V-Y advancement flaps are typically islandized and would be compromised by the adjacent wide undermining that damaged local perforators.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old gardener with a 10-year history of inadequately managed type 2 diabetes presents to the emergency department with severe pain and swelling of the left forearm occurring 1 day after scraping his left arm on a rose bush. Physical examination reveals intense tenderness, swelling, and crepitus. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) CT imaging
B) Econazole therapy
C) Hyperbaric oxygen treatment
D) Urgent surgical debridement
questions.answer:
D)
Immediate surgical debridement is the most critical intervention for necrotizing fasciitis, which is strongly suggested by the clinical presentation of severe pain, rapid progression, crepitus, and high-risk patient factors (diabetes, penetrating injury). This life-threatening soft tissue infection requires emergent surgical removal of necrotic tissue combined with broad-spectrum antibiotics and intensive care monitoring. A is incorrect because imaging would delay necessary treatment and is not required for diagnosis when clinical signs are clear. B is incorrect because econazole is an antifungal medication inappropriate for bacterial necrotizing fasciitis. C is incorrect because while hyperbaric oxygen may be a useful adjunct, it should never delay immediate surgical debridement, which is the primary life-saving intervention.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old male patient presents for follow-up assessment one year following facial nerve reconstruction using free gracilis muscle transfer. Clinical examination reveals marked hyperkinesis on the unaffected side. Besides botulinum toxin type A injections, which of the following interventions has demonstrated efficacy in enhancing facial symmetry?
A) Facial muscle cryotherapy
B) Mirror-assisted biofeedback training
C) Oral beta-blocker medication
D) Radiofrequency tissue ablation
E) Selective contralateral facial nerve sectioning
questions.answer:
B)
Mirror-assisted biofeedback training has demonstrated significant improvement in facial symmetry when combined with botulinum toxin injections for treating facial hyperkinesis. Hyperkinesis refers to excessive activity on the unaffected, contralateral side. A is incorrect because facial muscle cryotherapy has not been established as an effective treatment for hyperkinesis. C is incorrect because oral beta-blocker medication is not indicated for post-reconstruction facial hyperkinesis. D is incorrect because radiofrequency tissue ablation is still investigational for synkinesis and not accepted for hyperkinesis treatment. E is incorrect because selective contralateral facial nerve sectioning is not typically recommended for hyperkinesis correction.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old carpenter seeks evaluation for a complete longitudinal ridge extending across the nail of his left index finger. He remembers striking it with a hammer 6 months prior and observed "blue discoloration beneath the nail" initially. He has delayed seeking treatment until now. Radiographic imaging reveals no abnormalities. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Conservative monitoring
B) Scar tissue removal and nail matrix ablation
C) Scar tissue removal and nail matrix reconstruction
D) Scar tissue removal and wrapped toe transfer
E) Nail plate trephination
questions.answer:
C)
Scar tissue removal and nail matrix reconstruction is the appropriate treatment for this nail deformity that developed after untreated trauma. The nail has completed a full growth cycle (3-4 months) since the 6-month-old injury, confirming the deformity is established. Surgical repair of both germinal and sterile matrices is needed after scar excision. A is incorrect because conservative monitoring will not correct an established post-traumatic nail deformity. B is incorrect because nail matrix ablation (matricectomy) is used for recurrent infections or painful conditions, not traumatic deformities. D is incorrect because wrapped toe procedures are for finger amputations requiring soft tissue replacement, not isolated nail matrix injuries. E is incorrect because nail plate trephination is only performed acutely to drain symptomatic hematomas.

questions.question:
A 13-year-old girl presents with an enlarging mass on the right hand. The patient's mother reports that the child has always had a bruised-appearing birthmark on the hand, but the region started enlarging in the last year. The patient reports aching pain mainly associated with exercise. On examination, the mass increases in size with dependence. A photograph, an x-ray study, and MRI images are shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?


A) Arteriovenous malformation
B) Hemangioma
C) Lymphatic malformation
D) Port-wine stain
E) Venous malformation
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


Vascular anomalies are divided into tumors and malformations. Hemangiomas are a classic example of a vascular tumor. Malformations are present at birth and grow with age. Vascular malformations don't regress with age. They may not be obvious at a young age and become more evident as the patient ages or goes through hormonal changes such as puberty and pregnancy (if female). Other reasons for enlargement include trauma, infection, and thrombosis. Vascular malformations are secondary to an error in the morphogenesis of blood vessels, and they don't enlarge secondary to cellular hyperplasia. There is a normal rate of endothelial cell turnover.


Vascular malformations are characterized by rate of flow and type of predominant tissue in the malformation. Slow-flow vascular malformations include capillary malformations, venous malformations (VMs), and lymphatic malformations (LMs). Fast-flow vascular malformations include arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) or fistulas. Combined vascular malformations aren't uncommon. Most vascular anomalies can be diagnosed by history and clinical examination. However, medical imaging has become an important component for diagnosis and treatment planning.


This patient presents with a vascular malformation based on history, examination, and MRI. The subtype for this patient is consistent with a venous malformation based on findings of phleboliths (blood clots that become hardened and calcified) on MRI and x-ray. VMs are the most common type of vascular malformation. These malformations may be present in all tissue planes but, when present at the subcutaneous level, give the skin a purplish hue that is accentuated with gravity position of the limb. VMs are traditionally compressible, and the purplish hue and fullness of the mass will frequently diminish with limb elevation against gravity. Painful clots and phleboliths are commonly identified and may be sources of pain causing acute presentation. Patients may report chronic aching pain, swelling, and stiffness that is worse in the morning. Phleboliths demonstrated on imaging are pathognomonic for VMs. VMs of the extremity can be associated with undergrowth or overgrowth.


Ultrasonography, MRI, and catheter angiography are frequently used imaging studies to delineate the rate of flow, identify features, and evaluate the extent of malformation. X-ray study or CT scan may be used to assess bony involvement/bony deformation and may show phleboliths appearing as rounded, lamellated calcifications. Ultrasonography with Doppler scan is frequently the first-line imaging study; it can assess the rate of flow (delineate fast/slow flow), depth of the mass, and any feeding vessels. Compressibility of the mass can also be assessed. An ultrasound of a VM usually shows a sponge-like collection of vessels and compression; then release will show inflow of blood into the cavity. Phleboliths, ectatic/dilated vessels, and thickened overlying tissue can all be shown on ultrasonography. MRI of VMs show multilocular, lobulated, septated masses. These are hypo/isointense on T1-weighted sequences and hyperintense on T2 sequences. VMs can be shown to involve nerves, tendons, muscles, joints, and adjacent organs. Phleboliths can also be appreciated on MRI as low-signal regions/flow voids.


The other options wouldn't be the most correct diagnosis for this patient. Hemangioma would be present at birth and grow rapidly (and regress for an involuting hemangioma). An AVM is a high-flow lesion and wouldn't have phleboliths on imaging. An LM is a low-flow lesion and similarly wouldn't demonstrate phleboliths. Neither an AVM nor an LM would appear to have increased size/congestion with dependence. Port-wine stain or capillary malformation is a flat macular cutaneous malformation and wouldn't be characterized by this patient's findings or imaging.


ReferencesArnold R, Chaudry G. Diagnostic imaging of vascular anomalies. Clin Plast Surg. 2011;38(1):21-29.Burns AJ, Navarro JA, Cooner RD. Classification of vascular anomalies and the comprehensive treatment of hemangiomas. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009;124(1 suppl):69e-81e.Jacobs BJ, Anzarut A, Guerra S, Gordillo G, Imbriglia JE. Vascular anomalies of the upper extremity. J Hand Surg Am. 2010;35(10):1703-1709.Taghinia AH, Upton J. Vascular anomalies. J Hand Surg Am. 2018;43(12):1113-1121.

questions.question:
An 87-year-old Caucasian male presents with numerous 5-6 mm lesions on his forehead. He reports extensive lifetime sun exposure. Physical examination reveals erythematous, rough, and scaly lesions. What is the most appropriate therapeutic approach?
A) Dexamethasone
B) Docosanol
C) Imiquimod
D) Isotretinoin
E) Watchful waiting with monthly follow-up
questions.answer:
C)
Imiquimod is the most appropriate treatment for these actinic keratoses, which are premalignant lesions commonly found in fair-skinned individuals with chronic sun exposure. Imiquimod works by stimulating local immune responses and apoptotic pathways, making it effective for multiple lesions. A is incorrect because dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used for inflammatory or autoimmune conditions, not premalignant lesions. B is incorrect because docosanol is an antiviral agent specifically for herpes simplex infections. D is incorrect because isotretinoin is indicated for severe cystic acne, not actinic keratoses. E is incorrect because observation alone is inappropriate given the malignant potential of actinic keratoses, which can progress to squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.question:
A healthy 25-year-old chef presents 2 hours after suffering scald injuries from accidentally spilling a large pot of soup. She immediately irrigated the area and applied silver sulfadiazine dressing. She remains alert and hemodynamically stable. Physical examination demonstrates partial-thickness burns affecting the lower abdomen, perineum, external genitalia, and anterior thighs, encompassing approximately 15% total body surface area. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
A) Oral antibiotic therapy
B) Outpatient treatment with silver sulfadiazine
C) Parkland formula fluid replacement
D) Transfer to inpatient burn unit
E) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
D)
Transfer to an inpatient burn unit is indicated because this patient meets American Burn Association criteria for burn center referral: partial-thickness burns >10% TBSA and involvement of the perineum/genitalia. Specialized burn centers provide optimal outcomes for complex burns. A is incorrect because prophylactic oral antibiotics are not routinely indicated for acute burn management. B is incorrect because outpatient care is inappropriate for burns meeting burn center referral criteria. C is incorrect because Parkland formula resuscitation is typically reserved for burns >20% TBSA, as the inflammatory response requiring high-volume resuscitation rarely occurs with burns <20% TBSA. E is incorrect because autografting is reserved for deep burns that fail to respond to initial optimal wound care, not as immediate management.

questions.question:
A 34-year-old male is transported to the emergency department 2 hours after injuring his right wrist by punching through a glass window. Surgical exploration reveals complete median nerve transection at the wrist level. A 1-cm gap exists between the proximal and distal nerve segments. Which treatment approach will most likely yield optimal functional recovery?
A) Multiple-strand nerve grafting
B) Nerve transfer procedure
C) Nerve transposition technique
D) Primary epineurial repair
E) Single-strand nerve grafting
questions.answer:
D)
Primary epineurial repair provides the best functional outcome for clean, sharp median nerve injuries with gaps <1 cm. Direct repair without tension is superior to grafting techniques for short gaps in major peripheral nerves. A is incorrect because multiple-strand nerve grafting produces inferior outcomes compared to primary repair and should be reserved for cases where primary repair would create tension. B is incorrect because nerve transfer is only considered when no viable proximal nerve segment exists for repair. C is incorrect because nerve transposition is specifically used for ulnar nerve lengthening at the elbow, not for median nerve repair at the wrist. E is incorrect because single-strand nerve grafting, while producing similar results to multistrand grafting, is still inferior to primary repair for short nerve gaps.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old otherwise healthy male presents to the clinic with sudden onset swelling on the back of his right dominant wrist. He reports that wrist motion causes pain. There is no history of antecedent injury. Which of the following represents the most sensitive diagnostic test for identifying septic arthritis of the wrist in this patient?
A) Radiographic evidence of carpal bone destruction
B) Gram stain of joint fluid
C) Erythrocyte sedimentation rate in serum
D) White blood cell count in serum
E) White blood cell count in synovial fluid
questions.answer:
E)

Synovial fluid white blood cell count is the most sensitive test for diagnosing septic wrist arthritis. Analysis of joint fluid provides the most valuable diagnostic information. While bacterial culture and Gram stain of synovial fluid are the most definitive tests, they are unfortunately not reliably positive in acute septic joints - culture results may be negative in approximately 50% of cases (particularly gonococcal infections), and Gram stain is positive even less frequently. Additionally, culture results require several days to obtain. When the white cell count threshold is lowered, sensitivity increases but specificity decreases. At a threshold of 50,000/mL (the traditional diagnostic cutoff), sensitivity is 61%. Lowering the threshold to 17,500/mL increases sensitivity to 83% but reduces specificity to 67%. A) Radiographic evidence of carpal bone destruction is incorrect because these changes occur late in the course of septic arthritis. B) Gram stain of joint fluid is incorrect because it has poor sensitivity, being positive less frequently than culture. C) Erythrocyte sedimentation rate in serum is incorrect because it provides little change to pretest probability of septic arthritis. D) White blood cell count in serum is incorrect because it similarly does not significantly alter pretest probability of joint infection.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old male presents to the clinic with locally recurrent rectal carcinoma occurring four years following low anterior resection with adjuvant radiation therapy. An open abdominoperineal resection is being considered. Which of the following wound closure techniques will most effectively minimize the risk of perineal wound complications?
A) Gracilis muscle flap reconstruction
B) Vacuum-assisted closure therapy
C) Direct primary wound closure
D) Rectus abdominis muscle flap reconstruction
E) Split-thickness skin graft application
questions.answer:
D)

Rectus abdominis myocutaneous flap reconstruction most reliably reduces perineal wound complications following abdominoperineal resection. Multiple retrospective studies and one randomized controlled trial have demonstrated that rectus abdominis flap closure significantly decreases wound healing complications compared to primary closure after APR procedures. This flap provides well-vascularized tissue coverage for the large perineal defect created during the procedure. A) Gracilis muscle flap reconstruction is incorrect because while it has been utilized for APR reconstruction, the supporting evidence is less robust compared to rectus abdominis flaps. B) Vacuum-assisted closure therapy is incorrect because it is inappropriate for APR reconstruction due to the large wound size and risk of evisceration. C) Direct primary wound closure is incorrect because it has higher complication rates compared to flap reconstruction, as demonstrated in comparative studies. E) Split-thickness skin graft application is incorrect because it is unsuitable for APR defects due to the wound size and evisceration risk.

questions.question:
A 3-month-old male infant is evaluated for a 10 × 10-cm violet-colored lesion on the right thigh that has been present since birth. The medical history is significant for epistaxis. Physical examination reveals ecchymoses on the torso. Laboratory studies show low platelet count. Which of the following represents the most probable diagnosis?
A) Arteriovenous malformation
B) Capillary malformation
C) Congenital hemangioma
D) Infantile hemangioma
E) Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
questions.answer:
E)

Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma is the most likely diagnosis in this case. This vascular tumor is typically present at birth and can cause Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, characterized by severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count <25,000/mm³) due to platelet sequestration within the tumor. This leads to spontaneous bleeding manifestations such as nosebleeds and bruising, as seen in this patient. Treatment options include vincristine or sirolimus (rapamycin). A) Arteriovenous malformation is incorrect because it does not cause Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon or associated coagulopathy. B) Capillary malformation is incorrect because it does not result in thrombocytopenia or bleeding complications. C) Congenital hemangioma is incorrect because it does not cause Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon or coagulation abnormalities. D) Infantile hemangioma is incorrect because it does not lead to platelet trapping or associated bleeding disorders.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old male child is seen with verrucous lesions on his digits. His parents state that these growths have remained despite using various over-the-counter topical medications. Which of the following viral pathogens is most likely responsible for this patient's clinical presentation?
A) H1N1
B) Hepatitis C
C) Herpes simplex
D) Human immunodeficiency
E) Human papilloma
questions.answer:
E)

Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the causative agent of cutaneous warts. Over 100 HPV subtypes exist, with types 2 and 4 being the most frequent causes of hand warts as seen in this patient. The virus is transmitted through direct contact or contaminated surfaces and enters through microscopic skin breaks, subsequently altering squamous epithelium to create characteristic cauliflower-like growths. Warts are typically painless, benign lesions that often resolve spontaneously - approximately 50% disappear within one year in children and 90% within five years. Treatment options range from topical salicylic acid and cryotherapy to more invasive procedures for resistant cases. A) H1N1 is incorrect because this influenza virus causes respiratory illness, not skin lesions on fingers. B) Hepatitis C is incorrect because this virus primarily affects the liver and does not cause digital lesions. C) Herpes simplex is incorrect because this virus typically causes oral or genital lesions, not finger warts. D) Human immunodeficiency virus is incorrect because HIV affects the immune system and does not directly cause finger lesions, though it may predispose to more severe wart infections.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old female has remained in the intensive care unit for two weeks following a motor vehicle collision. Her injuries included multiple facial fractures, severe traumatic brain injury with cerebral contusion, pelvic fractures, and numerous lower limb fractures. Emergency intubation was required and she has remained comatose since the accident. Current laboratory values show serum sodium of 148 mEq/L, with urinalysis revealing dilute urine and decreased osmolality. Central diabetes insipidus is being considered. A deficiency of which of the following hormones most likely accounts for this electrolyte abnormality?
A) Aldosterone
B) Angiotensin
C) Cortisol
D) Renin
E) Vasopressin
questions.answer:
E)

Vasopressin deficiency is the primary cause of central (neurogenic) diabetes insipidus following head trauma. Vasopressin, also called antidiuretic hormone (ADH), is synthesized in the hypothalamus but released by the posterior pituitary gland. This unique anatomical relationship makes it vulnerable to traumatic injury affecting the hypothalamus, pituitary stalk, or posterior pituitary. Vasopressin is essential for fluid homeostasis, promoting water reabsorption in the kidney's collecting ducts and distal convoluted tubules. Its deficiency results in the inability to concentrate urine, leading to hypernatremia and dilute urine with low osmolality as seen in this patient. A) Aldosterone is incorrect because this adrenal hormone regulates sodium and potassium balance through the renin-angiotensin system, not water retention, and its deficiency is not caused by head trauma. B) Angiotensin is incorrect because this peptide hormone causes vasoconstriction and is part of blood pressure regulation, not directly involved in water balance affected by neurogenic diabetes insipidus. C) Cortisol is incorrect because this adrenal hormone affects metabolism and has some role in fluid balance, but its deficiency is not the cause of neurogenic diabetes insipidus from head trauma. D) Renin is incorrect because this enzyme initiates the renin-angiotensin system for blood pressure control and is not affected by head trauma causing diabetes insipidus.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old woman presents with rigidity in her right index finger. Physical examination reveals that the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint moves from 0 to 45 degrees when the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint is extended (at 0 degrees). When the MCP joint is flexed (at 90 degrees), the PIP joint range of motion increases to 0 to 80 degrees. Which of the following conditions most likely explains these examination findings?
A) PIP joint capsular contracture
B) Extensor tendon contracture
C) Flexor tendon scarring
D) Intrinsic muscle tightness
E) Palmar fascial thickening
questions.answer:
D)
The examination findings are most consistent with intrinsic muscle tightness. The Bunnell test demonstrates that PIP joint flexion is restricted when the MCP joint is extended but improves when the MCP joint is flexed, which is pathognomonic for intrinsic tightness. The intrinsic muscles flex the MCP joints and extend the PIP joints, so when tight, they limit PIP flexion when the MCP is extended. Flexing the MCP joint relaxes the intrinsic muscles, allowing improved PIP motion. A is incorrect because PIP capsular contracture would cause equal limitation regardless of MCP position. B is incorrect because extensor tendon contracture would cause the opposite pattern - worse PIP flexion with MCP flexion due to increased extensor tension. C is incorrect because flexor tendon scarring would produce equal PIP limitations in all MCP positions. E is incorrect because palmar fascial thickening (Dupuytren's) primarily affects extension, not flexion as described.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old man suffered traumatic amputation of his non-dominant index finger 3 hours ago and is requesting replantation. Which of the following factors most significantly impacts the survival rate of the digit following replantation?
A) Type of injury mechanism
B) Quantity of vessels repaired
C) Patient's tobacco use
D) Duration from injury to surgery
E) Administration of anticoagulants
questions.answer:
A)
The type of injury mechanism is the most critical factor determining replantation success. Sharp, clean amputations with minimal tissue crushing have the highest survival rates because they preserve vessel integrity and minimize tissue damage. Crush or avulsion injuries cause extensive vessel trauma and tissue destruction, significantly reducing survival chances. B is incorrect because while adequate venous drainage is important, mechanism trumps vessel number in determining outcome. C is incorrect because although smoking affects circulation, it has not been proven to significantly impact replantation survival in studies. D is incorrect because digits lack muscle tissue (most ischemia-sensitive) and can tolerate extended ischemia times when properly preserved. E is incorrect because anticoagulant use has not been shown to improve replantation survival rates in clinical studies.
