A) Candida albicans
B) Eikenella corrodens
C) Listeria monocytogenes
D) Pasteurella multocida
E) Staphylococcus aureus
questions.answer:
E)
Staphylococcus aureus remains the most common causative organism in hand infections, particularly felons (fingertip pulp infections). Methicillin-resistant S. aureus community-acquired strains now account for approximately 60% of staphylococcal hand infections. A) is incorrect because Candida albicans typically causes chronic paronychia rather than acute felon infections. B) is incorrect because Eikenella corrodens is primarily associated with human bite wounds. C) is incorrect because Listeria monocytogenes is rare and typically seen in flexor tenosynovitis in immunocompromised patients. D) is incorrect because Pasteurella multocida is associated with animal bites, particularly cat bites, and there is no bite history in this case.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old male undergoes disc removal surgery for treatment of temporomandibular joint internal derangement. Which of the following long-term complications is most likely to occur in this patient?
A) Ankylosis
B) Condylar remodeling
C) Facial (VII) nerve injury
D) Frey syndrome
questions.answer:
B)
Condylar remodeling is the most frequent long-term complication following TMJ discectomy. The removal of the articular disc disrupts the normal biomechanics of the joint, leading to adaptive changes in the mandibular condyle over time. This remodeling process occurs as the condyle adapts to the altered joint environment without the protective disc. A) is incorrect because ankylosis, while possible, occurs less frequently than condylar remodeling after discectomy. C) is incorrect because facial nerve injury is an uncommon complication of TMJ discectomy due to the anatomical location of the procedure. D) is incorrect because Frey syndrome is rare following TMJ discectomy and is more commonly associated with parotid gland surgery.

questions.question:
In a patient with normal facial proportions, which of the following measurements most closely corresponds to the intercanthal distance?
A) Eyebrow length
B) Nasal bone width
C) Orbital fissure width
D) Stomion-to-menton distance
E) Subnasale-to-stomion distance
questions.answer:
C)
Orbital fissure width most accurately approximates intercanthal distance in normal facial anatomy. Both measurements represent approximately one-fifth of the total facial width when the face is divided into equal fifths for proportional analysis. The intercanthal distance typically ranges from 30-40mm in healthy individuals, which closely matches the orbital fissure width. A) is incorrect because eyebrow length extends beyond the lateral canthus, representing more than one-fifth of facial width. B) is incorrect because nasal bone width is narrower than the intercanthal distance. D) is incorrect because stomion-to-menton distance is a vertical facial height measurement, not a width measurement. E) is incorrect because subnasale-to-stomion distance is also a vertical measurement used for facial height analysis, not width proportions.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old woman presents with worsening painful ulceration of a prior healed surgical site of the left lower extremity after undergoing hidradenitis excisions 10 years ago. She reports no trauma and has had no fevers or chills. Examination shows some drainage at the wound site. She undergoes treatment with debridement, antibiotics, and multiple types of dressings without progress of wound healing. Photographs are shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?


A) Debridement and biopsy
B) Debridement and dermal allografting
C) Debridement and negative pressure dressing
D) Excision and coverage with a flap
E) Excision and skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.


Marjolin ulcers are malignancies (most commonly aggressive squamous cell carcinoma) that arise from areas of chronic irritation, injury, or unstable scar. These malignancies frequently occur over many years. This malignant degeneration is most commonly associated with burns; however, it can be associated with a multitude of other types of nonhealing wounds such as traumatic wounds, osteomyelitis, pressure sores, any type of ulcer, laceration, venous stasis ulcer, or fistulas. The rate of incidence is approximately 2% in burn scars, with a predilection for the extremities, especially in the lower limbs. There is often a delay in diagnosis, since the appearance of a nonhealing ulcer with heaped-up edges mimics other types of ulcerations. Marjolin ulcer should be ruled out in a chronic nonhealing ulcer in the setting of a long-term scar/injury/burn.


Diagnosis of Marjolin ulcer is typically made by tissue biopsy with pathologic evaluation. Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common type of histology seen in Marjolin ulcer, although basal cell carcinoma, malignant fibrous histiocytoma, malignant melanoma, liposarcoma, fibrosarcoma, eccrine syringofibroadenoma, Merkel cell carcinoma, and keratoacanthoma have all been described. For patients with squamous cell carcinoma (most common type), the degree of differentiation is important prognostically. The risk for metastasis is highly correlated with the degree of differentiation and grade of the tumor. There is early lymph node metastasis in 30% of patients.


Treatment is surgical with wide local excision with pursuit of negative margins. Sentinel lymph node biopsy is frequently pursued. Deeper ulcers involving bone may warrant amputation of the involved extremity.


Marjolin ulcer must be diagnosed and treated (or the diagnosis excluded) before considering any other treatments.


ReferencesBorghese L, Masellis A, Masellis M. Extremity burn reconstruction. In: Chang J, ed. Plastic Surgery: Lower Extremity, Trunk, and Burns. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018:424-444. Neligan PC, ed. Plastic Surgery; vol 4.Kerr-Valentic MA, Samimi K, Rohlen BH, Argawal JP, Rockwell WB. Marjolin's ulcer: modern analysis of an ancient problem. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2009;123(1):184-191.Pekarek B, Buck S, Osher L. A comprehensive review on Marjolin's ulcers: diagnosis and treatment. J Am Col Certif Wound Spec. 2011;3(3):60-64.

questions.question:
During genioglossus advancement surgery, which of the following nerves provides innervation to the targeted muscle?
A) Facial nerve
B) Glossopharyngeal nerve
C) Hypoglossal nerve
D) Lingual nerve
E) Vagus nerve
questions.answer:
C)
The hypoglossal nerve (cranial nerve XII) provides motor innervation to the genioglossus muscle. This muscle is crucial during genioglossus advancement procedures for obstructive sleep apnea treatment, as it helps advance the tongue and prevent posterior displacement of the mobilized chin segment. Understanding this innervation is essential for preserving muscle function during surgical manipulation. A) is incorrect because the facial nerve innervates muscles of facial expression, not tongue muscles. B) is incorrect because the glossopharyngeal nerve provides sensory innervation to the posterior tongue and some pharyngeal muscles, but not the genioglossus. D) is incorrect because the lingual nerve provides sensory innervation to the anterior tongue, not motor innervation to the genioglossus. E) is incorrect because the vagus nerve innervates various visceral structures but does not supply the genioglossus muscle.

questions.question:
Which of the following represents a risk factor for estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer?
A) Nursing an infant
B) Young maternal age at first birth
C) Premature menopause
D) Delayed onset of menstruation
E) Excess weight after menopause
questions.answer:
E)
Excess weight after menopause leads to increased estrogen production by fat tissue, elevating the risk for estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer. A is incorrect because nursing reduces lifetime estrogen exposure and lowers breast cancer risk. B is incorrect because younger age at first pregnancy provides protective benefits against hormone-sensitive breast cancers. C is incorrect because premature menopause reduces total menstrual cycles and decreases breast cancer risk. D is incorrect because delayed onset of menstruation means fewer lifetime menstrual cycles, which reduces breast cancer risk.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old woman presents for assessment of bilateral lower limb lymphatic swelling present for 15 years. She denies any precipitating injury. Examination reveals significant bilateral non-pitting swelling extending from hips to knees. Imaging studies demonstrate fat tissue enlargement and widespread soft tissue fluid accumulation. Which of the following represents the most suitable management for this patient?
A) Diuretic medication and compression treatment
B) Diuretic medication and surgical drain insertion
C) Maximum dose diuretic treatment
D) Surgical drain insertion
E) Liposuction procedure and compression clothing
questions.answer:
E)
Liposuction procedure and compression clothing is appropriate for severe primary lymphedema cases where conservative measures are insufficient. A is incorrect because diuretics are ineffective for lymphedema and compression alone is inadequate for severe cases. B is incorrect because diuretics don't treat lymphedema and drains are not standard treatment for this condition. C is incorrect because high-dose diuretics are ineffective for lymphatic disorders and can cause complications. D is incorrect because drain placement alone doesn't address the underlying lymphatic dysfunction or tissue changes.

questions.question:
A 23-year-old woman is evaluated for augmentation mammaplasty. Physical examination shows a flattened, depressed right anterior chest wall with a hypoplastic right breast and a superiorly displaced right nipple-areola complex. The right pectoralis major muscle, including its sternocostal head, is present and of normal bulk, and the sternum is midline and normally contoured. The upper extremities and hands are normal. Which of the following developmental abnormalities is most likely present?
A) Amastia
B) Chest wall hypoplasia
C) Pectus carinatum
D) Pectus excavatum
E) Poland syndrome
questions.answer:
B)
Isolated chest wall hypoplasia accounts for this constellation: unilateral depression/flattening of the anterior chest wall, breast hypoplasia with a superiorly displaced nipple-areola complex, an intact pectoralis major, and a normal sternum. Treatment typically involves staged expansion or implant-based reconstruction, often with autologous fat grafting to correct the soft-tissue contour deficiency.

A is incorrect because amastia denotes complete absence of both the breast parenchyma and the nipple-areola complex; this patient has a hypoplastic but present breast and nipple.

C is incorrect because pectus carinatum is an anterior protrusion of the sternum and costal cartilages, the opposite of the depression described.

D is incorrect because pectus excavatum is defined by posterior depression of the sternum and adjacent costal cartilages; here the sternum is midline and normally contoured.

E is incorrect because Poland syndrome requires absence or hypoplasia of the sternocostal head of the pectoralis major, frequently with rib and ipsilateral hand anomalies (e.g., symbrachydactyly); the pectoralis major is intact and the hands are normal in this patient.

questions.question:
A 3-month-old girl with Apert syndrome is brought for hand assessment. Which of the following clinical features is most likely to be observed?
A) Finger contracture
B) Fused digits with bone involvement
C) Rudimentary thumb attachment
D) Enlarged finger condition
E) Thumb deviation toward pinky side
questions.answer:
B)
Fused digits with bone involvement is characteristic of Apert syndrome, which involves complex fusion of fingers including bone, soft tissue, and nail structures. A is incorrect because finger contracture is not a primary feature of Apert syndrome but rather involves joint stiffness conditions. C is incorrect because rudimentary thumb attachment describes a specific type of thumb underdevelopment not associated with Apert syndrome. D is incorrect because enlarged finger condition involves overgrowth of individual digits, which is not part of Apert syndrome. E is incorrect because thumb deviation toward pinky side is not typical in Apert syndrome, where thumb deviation is usually toward the thumb side.

questions.question:
A 30-year-old man undergoes evaluation one year following forearm transplant surgery. Vascular imaging reveals 60% narrowing of one forearm artery and complete blockage of the other. The patient follows his anti-rejection medication regimen. Signs of long-term blood flow reduction are suspected. Which of the following mechanisms is most likely responsible?
A) Pre-existing antibody complex formation and immune system activation
B) IgA antibody-driven reaction
C) IgM and IgG antibody-antigen reaction
D) T-lymphocyte-driven immune reaction
questions.answer:
D)
T-lymphocyte-driven immune reaction describes Type 4 hypersensitivity, which causes chronic transplant rejection through delayed cellular immune responses leading to vascular damage. A is incorrect because pre-existing antibody complex formation describes Type 3 hypersensitivity, which causes acute rather than chronic vascular changes. B is incorrect because IgA antibody-driven reactions are not the primary mechanism in chronic transplant rejection. C is incorrect because IgM and IgG antibody-antigen reactions describe Type 2 hypersensitivity, which causes acute cytotoxic responses rather than the chronic vascular changes seen here.

questions.question:
A 22-year-old male presents after punching a concrete wall with both fists following alcohol consumption, resulting in multiple metacarpal fractures. Which of the following injuries will result in the greatest long-term functional disability of the hand?
A) Fifth metacarpal neck fracture with 40-degree angulation
B) Fourth metacarpal neck fracture with 35-degree angulation
C) Fourth metacarpal shaft fracture with 10-degree angulation
D) Third metacarpal neck fracture with 25-degree angulation
E) Third metacarpal shaft fracture with 0-degree angulation
questions.answer:
D)
The third metacarpal neck fracture with 25-degree angulation will cause the most significant long-term impairment. The index and middle finger metacarpals lack compensatory carpometacarpal joint mobility, making any angulation greater than 10-15 degrees functionally problematic. A is incorrect because the fifth metacarpal can tolerate up to 40-70 degrees of angulation without functional loss due to compensatory CMC joint motion. B is incorrect as the fourth metacarpal has some compensatory motion allowing tolerance of moderate angulation. C is incorrect because shaft fractures generally require less strict reduction criteria than neck fractures. E is incorrect as there is no angulation present to cause functional impairment.

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female presents to the clinic 2 years following bilateral breast augmentation using 350-cc smooth, round saline implants. She complains of persistent fatigue and joint discomfort. Physical examination reveals soft, symmetric, non-tender breasts without palpable masses or axillary lymphadenopathy. What is the most appropriate initial management?
A) Replace saline implants with cohesive gel implants
B) Order MRI
C) Perform en bloc removal of the implants
D) Perform stereotactic biopsy of capsule
E) Request autoimmune disease evaluation
questions.answer:
E)
Autoimmune disease evaluation is the most appropriate next step. The patient's symptoms are consistent with breast implant illness (BII), but these symptoms can also indicate underlying autoimmune conditions that should be ruled out before considering surgical intervention. A is incorrect because implant exchange would not address the underlying cause of her symptoms. B is incorrect as MRI is not indicated with normal physical examination findings and saline implants. C is incorrect because explantation should only be considered after medical evaluation and may not resolve symptoms, especially if an autoimmune disease is present. D is incorrect as stereotactic biopsy is used for mass evaluation, not for BII symptoms.

questions.question:
A 38-year-old woman, G2P2, is scheduled for reduction mammaplasty due to neck and shoulder discomfort. She wears a 44E bra size. Physical examination demonstrates pendulous breasts with a sternal notch-to-nipple measurement of 40 cm. Which muscle is most likely to show hypertrophy in this patient?
A) Latissimus dorsi
B) Levator scapulae
C) Pectoralis major
D) Rhomboid major
E) Trapezius
questions.answer:
E)
The trapezius muscle is most likely hypertrophied. In mammary hypertrophy, the weight of large breasts pulls the shoulders forward, requiring the trapezius to work harder to maintain proper shoulder positioning and posture, leading to muscle hypertrophy and associated pain. A is incorrect because the latissimus dorsi primarily functions in arm extension and adduction, not shoulder positioning. B is incorrect as the levator scapulae elevates the scapula but doesn't primarily counter the forward shoulder pull. C is incorrect because the pectoralis major would not hypertrophy to counter breast weight. D is incorrect as the rhomboid major retracts the scapula but is not the primary muscle affected by mammary hypertrophy.

questions.question:
A 61-year-old woman presents with a volar thumb tip soft-tissue injury sustained while preparing chicken. Physical examination reveals a 2 × 2.5-cm pulp defect with bone exposure. Radiographs show no fracture or dislocation. What is the optimal treatment approach?
A) Cross-finger flap
B) First dorsal metacarpal artery flap
C) Full-thickness skin grafting
D) Moberg volar advancement flap
E) Observation
questions.answer:
B)
The first dorsal metacarpal artery flap is the optimal choice for this defect. This island flap provides sensate, single-stage coverage for thumb defects with bone exposure and can adequately cover the described defect size. A is incorrect because cross-finger flaps require two stages, cause joint stiffness, and are better suited for younger patients. C is incorrect as skin grafts will not take on exposed bone and fail to restore pulp padding. D is incorrect because Moberg flaps are limited to defects up to 2 cm² and may cause IP joint contracture. E is incorrect as observation is only appropriate for defects under 1 cm² without bone exposure.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old man seeks treatment for under-eye puffiness and tear-trough deformity. The surgical plan includes transconjunctival lower lid blepharoplasty with tear trough ligament release and fat redistribution. Which anatomical structure indicates successful entry into the premaxillary space and tear-trough ligament release?
A) Levator labii superioris
B) Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
C) Orbicularis oculi
D) Zygomaticus major
E) Zygomaticus minor
questions.answer:
A)
Visualization of the levator labii superioris confirms entry into the premaxillary space and adequate tear-trough ligament release. During transconjunctival dissection, the plane transitions from preseptal to supraperiosteal over the orbital rim until this muscle is identified. B is incorrect as the levator labii superioris alaeque nasi is located more superficially and doesn't indicate proper depth. C is incorrect because the orbicularis oculi is the muscle being released, not the landmark for adequate release. D and E are incorrect as both zygomaticus muscles are superficial structures that don't indicate proper dissection depth or ligament release.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old woman presents to the clinic seeking breast augmentation surgery. Under which of the following circumstances would a preoperative mammogram be most strongly recommended?
A) Paternal grandmother with breast cancer diagnosis at 73 years old
B) Mother with breast cancer diagnosis at 45 years old
C) History of benign breast cysts
D) Previous fibroadenoma
E) Sister with ovarian cancer diagnosis
questions.answer:
B)

A mother diagnosed with breast cancer at 45 years old represents the strongest indication for preoperative mammography. Family history constitutes the most important risk factor for breast cancer development. First-degree relatives (mother, sister, daughter) with breast cancer significantly elevate risk, particularly when diagnosed before age 50, conferring a 2.3-fold increased risk compared to 1.8-fold when diagnosed after age 50. A) is incorrect because a grandmother represents a second-degree relative with less impact on risk, especially with diagnosis at advanced age. C) is incorrect because benign breast cysts do not substantially increase breast cancer risk. D) is incorrect because fibroadenomas are benign lesions that do not significantly elevate cancer risk. E) is incorrect because while ovarian cancer in a first-degree relative may suggest hereditary cancer syndromes, it is less directly indicative than early-onset breast cancer in a mother.

questions.question:
A 21-year-old male presents with left nasal breathing difficulties following a soccer injury to his nose one year prior. He experienced epistaxis initially but received no treatment. Examination reveals left nasal sidewall depression and septal deviation. He demonstrates increased breathing difficulty through the left nostril when the right is blocked, despite the nostril appearing open. The right nasal passage shows normal patency. Closed rhinoplasty with septoplasty is scheduled. Beyond submucous septal cartilage removal, which technique would best address the nasal airway obstruction?
A) Lateral osteotomies combined with right spreader graft placement
B) Left lateral osteotomy combined with columellar strut placement
C) Left lateral osteotomy combined with left spreader graft placement
D) Medial osteotomies combined with bilateral spreader graft placement
E) Right medial osteotomy combined with left alar batten graft placement
questions.answer:
C)

Left lateral osteotomy with left spreader graft placement is the optimal approach. The lateral osteotomy mobilizes the collapsed left nasal bone, allowing outward repositioning, while the left spreader graft maintains internal nasal valve patency and prevents recurrent collapse. A) is incorrect because the right side functions normally and doesn't require a spreader graft. B) is incorrect because columellar struts address tip support issues, not internal valve collapse, and aren't needed in closed rhinoplasty where the columella remains stable. D) is incorrect because bilateral spreader grafts would create excessive dorsal width when only the left side requires treatment. E) is incorrect because alar batten grafts treat external nasal valve collapse, not the internal valve collapse present in this case.

questions.question:
A 31-year-old woman (G2P2) seeks breast augmentation for enhanced volume with minimal scarring. She currently wears 34A and examination reveals pseudoptosis. Which submuscular augmentation approach would best achieve her objectives?
A) Intact pectoralis muscle without inframammary fold release
B) Pectoralis muscle release at inframammary fold plus periareolar mastopexy
C) Pectoralis muscle release at inframammary fold plus submammary dissection to lower areolar border
D) Pectoralis muscle release at inframammary fold plus vertical mastopexy
E) Pectoralis muscle release at inframammary fold alone
questions.answer:
C)

This patient requires a dual-plane type II augmentation with pectoralis muscle release at the inframammary fold and submammary dissection extending to the inferior areolar border. This technique addresses her moderately mobile breast parenchyma and moderate lower pole skin stretch while maximizing muscle coverage and allowing optimal lower pole expansion. A) is incorrect because maintaining muscle attachment would restrict lower pole expansion needed for her breast characteristics. B) is incorrect because periareolar mastopexy adds unwanted scarring and isn't necessary with proper dual-plane technique. D) is incorrect because vertical mastopexy creates additional scarring that contradicts her minimal scarring goal. E) is incorrect because type I dual-plane (muscle release only) is insufficient for her degree of parenchymal mobility and skin stretch.

questions.question:
A 47-year-old male receives split-thickness skin grafting for forearm burn treatment. Which donor site dressing approach would best promote optimal healing?
A) Alginate dressing with occlusive covering maintained for 7 days
B) Moist gauze with occlusive covering maintained for 7 days
C) Petrolatum gauze with occlusive covering for 2 days, then air exposure
D) Petrolatum gauze with air exposure
E) Xenograft with air exposure
questions.answer:
A)

Alginate dressing covered with occlusive material for 7 days provides optimal wound healing conditions. Moist wound environments consistently demonstrate superior healing compared to dry conditions. Alginate dressings offer ideal properties including adaptability, absorption capacity, non-adherence, antimicrobial effects, and sustained moisture maintenance throughout the reepithelialization period. B) is incorrect because conventional gauze adheres to wounds and causes tissue trauma during removal. C) is incorrect because early air exposure creates a dry environment that impairs healing. D) is incorrect because air exposure from the start prevents the moist environment necessary for optimal healing. E) is incorrect because xenografts with air exposure also fail to maintain the moist conditions required for optimal donor site healing.

questions.question:
When comparing activation criteria, which of the following typically warrants Rapid Response Team (RRT) activation rather than traditional code team response?
A) Complete cessation of breathing
B) Undetectable blood pressure
C) Absent pulse
D) Elevated heart rate
E) Complete loss of consciousness
questions.answer:
D)

Elevated heart rate (tachycardia) is a typical criterion for RRT activation. The RRT intervenes during early clinical deterioration to prevent catastrophic events, addressing conditions like tachycardia, hypotension, respiratory distress, and altered mental status before they progress to cardiac arrest. A) is incorrect because respiratory arrest requires immediate code team response for advanced life support. B) is incorrect because undetectable blood pressure typically indicates cardiovascular collapse requiring code team intervention. C) is incorrect because absent pulse represents cardiac arrest, which is a code team emergency. E) is incorrect because complete unresponsiveness often indicates severe compromise requiring code team response, though altered consciousness (not complete loss) would warrant RRT activation.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old male presents following a traumatic injury to his dominant right wrist sustained when he struck a window 4 weeks prior. He reports numbness and weakness consistent with median nerve distribution. Surgical exploration reveals complete median nerve transection with a 4-cm defect between nerve ends. What is the optimal approach for nerve reconstruction?
A) Placement of polyglycolic acid nerve conduit
B) Grafting with saphenous vein
C) Grafting with sural nerve
D) Median nerve mobilization with direct repair
questions.answer:
C)

Sural nerve grafting represents the optimal reconstruction method. Autologous sural nerve grafts are the gold standard for nerve defects measuring 3 cm or larger. Multiple cable grafts would likely be necessary to match the median nerve diameter and restore both sensory and motor function. A) is incorrect because polyglycolic acid conduits are only suitable for gaps under 3 cm and serve as scaffolds for regeneration. B) is incorrect because vein grafts are used for vascular rather than nerve reconstruction of this magnitude. D) is incorrect because the 4-cm gap is too large for tension-free direct repair, even with nerve mobilization.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old female presents to the emergency department following a fall onto her extended hand during tennis. Physical examination reveals wrist tenderness. Following the scaphoid, which carpal bone has the highest likelihood of fracture in this scenario?
A) Capitate
B) Hamate
C) Lunate
D) Pisiform
E) Triquetral
questions.answer:
E)

The triquetral bone ranks as the second most frequently fractured carpal bone. Triquetral fractures typically involve the dorsal ridge and present as avulsion injuries visible on lateral wrist radiographs. The frequency ranking of carpal fractures is: scaphoid (most common), triquetral, trapezium, lunate, and hamate. A) is incorrect because capitate fractures are less common than triquetral fractures. B) is incorrect because hamate fractures rank lower in frequency. C) is incorrect because lunate fractures occur less frequently than triquetral fractures. D) is incorrect because pisiform fractures are relatively uncommon compared to triquetral fractures.

questions.question:
A 27-year-old female arrives at the emergency department 2 hours following a degloving avulsion injury to her dominant right ring finger. Examination reveals complete soft tissue avulsion including both neurovascular bundles from the mid-proximal phalanx level. Emergency revascularization attempts have been unsuccessful. What represents the most cosmetically acceptable treatment approach?
A) Debridement with full-thickness skin graft coverage
B) Debridement with groin flap coverage
C) Ring finger ray amputation
D) Necrotic digit removal with toe-to-hand reconstruction
E) Mid-proximal phalanx revision amputation with primary closure
questions.answer:
C)

Ray amputation provides the most aesthetically pleasing outcome by removing the entire digit and metacarpal, eliminating the segmental defect and optimizing both function and appearance. This reconstructive approach restores hand functionality effectively. A) is incorrect because skin grafts over exposed bone and tendon typically fail. B) is incorrect because groin flaps require prolonged hand attachment to the groin, causing adjacent digit stiffness and requiring staged procedures. D) is incorrect because toe-to-hand transfer would create significant length discrepancy with adjacent digits, impairing overall function. E) is incorrect because amputation at the metacarpophalangeal level creates a large inter-digital gap, leading to functional problems like object dropping.

questions.question:
What mechanism best explains how botulinum toxin type A prevents muscle contraction?
A) Attaches to presynaptic acetylcholine and breaks it down
B) Attaches to postsynaptic acetylcholine and breaks it down
C) Attaches to postsynaptic acetylcholine, blocking nicotinic receptor interaction
D) Attaches to neuromuscular junction nicotinic receptors, preventing acetylcholine stimulation
E) Attaches to presynaptic nerve terminal receptors, preventing acetylcholine release
questions.answer:
E)

Botulinum toxin type A functions by attaching to receptor sites within presynaptic nerve terminals, thereby blocking acetylcholine release into the neuromuscular junction synapse. This prevents muscle contraction by eliminating the neurotransmitter signal. A) is incorrect because the toxin doesn't degrade acetylcholine but blocks its release. B) is incorrect because the toxin acts presynaptically, not postsynaptically, and doesn't degrade acetylcholine. C) is incorrect because the mechanism involves presynaptic action, not postsynaptic acetylcholine binding. D) is incorrect because the toxin doesn't bind to nicotinic receptors but to presynaptic nerve terminals.

questions.question:
A 44-year-old healthy female presents with a 2-week history of a painless left breast mass discovered during bathing. Her mother had fibrocystic breast changes. She denies alcohol use and smoking. Examination reveals a 5-cm mobile, painless mass in the left upper outer quadrant without nipple discharge, skin changes, or retraction. Biopsy reveals a phyllodes tumor requiring surgical removal. What factor is most critical for preventing local tumor recurrence?
A) Postoperative radiation therapy
B) Simultaneous axillary lymph node dissection
C) Postoperative systemic chemotherapy
D) Surgical margins of 0.5 cm or less
E) Extensive surgical margins
questions.answer:
E)

Extensive surgical margins (≥1 cm) are most crucial for preventing local recurrence, particularly in borderline and malignant phyllodes tumors. Wide local excision or mastectomy with adequate margins represents the preferred treatment approach. A) is incorrect because adjuvant radiotherapy's effectiveness for phyllodes tumors remains unclear and is infrequently used. B) is incorrect because axillary lymph node involvement is rare in phyllodes tumors. C) is incorrect because systemic chemotherapy has limited efficacy and is reserved for unresectable metastatic disease. D) is incorrect because narrow margins (≤0.5 cm) are associated with higher recurrence rates compared to wider margins.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female patient is contemplating breast augmentation surgery using silicone implants. She inquires about the potential risks of developing autoimmune connective tissue disorders. Which of the following represents the most accurate risk evaluation for this patient?
A) Elevated risk of extracapsular leakage exclusively
B) Elevated risk of both intracapsular and extracapsular leakage
C) Elevated risk only when silicone material spreads to lymphatic tissue
D) Elevated risk limited to pre-1990 implant models
E) No elevated risk
questions.answer:
E)
Numerous large-scale epidemiological studies conducted in Europe and North America since the 1990s have consistently failed to establish a causal relationship between silicone breast implants and connective tissue diseases. A is incorrect because extracapsular leak alone does not increase connective tissue disease risk. B is incorrect because neither type of leak correlates with increased connective tissue disease risk. C is incorrect because lymph node migration does not specifically increase connective tissue disease risk. D is incorrect because the timeframe of implant manufacture does not affect connective tissue disease risk.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman comes to the office requesting treatment of fine rhytides due to smoking and photoaging. Topical retinoid therapy is planned. Which of the following effects is most likely to occur with topical retinoid treatment?


A) Decreased collagen production
B) Decreased hyaluronic acid production
C) Thinning of the dermis
D) Thinning of the epidermis
E) Thinning of the stratum corneum
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


Tretinoin (all-trans-retinoic acid) is one of the best long-term topical therapies available for chronically photoaged skin. Long-term use of tretinoin is associated with improved skin texture, decreased sallowness, a reduction in fine rhytides and actinic keratoses, fading of pigmented macules, and an overall improvement in skin appearance. Histologic effects of tretinoin include the following: increased epidermal and dermal layer thickness, elimination of dysplasia, atypia, and microscopic actinic keratoses, uniform dispersion of melanin granules, increased collagen and glycosaminoglycan deposition in the papillary dermis, diminished dermal elastosis, angiogenesis, and compaction/thinning of the stratum corneum.


The mechanism of action of retinoids is regulated through specific nuclear receptors. Ultraviolet radiation activates a series of phosphokinases that stimulate c-Fos and c-Jun proto-oncogenes, and thereby activate activator protein 1 (AP-1) transcription factor. AP-1 causes activation of metalloproteases, such as collagenase, gelatinase, and stromelysin which then break down collagen. Tretinoin results in a 70% inhibition of AP-1 transcription factor binding to DNA and a significant reduction in protease activity.


Tretinoin side effects include erythema, photosensitivity, and desquamation. Patients are initially started on a low dose with nightly application until tolerance is achieved. Because tretinoin is a photosensitizer, sunscreen use is absolutely imperative. Topical retinoids should be used for a minimum of 3 to 4 months, with the greatest improvement after 1 year of use. Patients who use alpha-hydroxy acids concomitantly with topical retinoids will see a synergistic effect and this combination is tolerated well in most patients.


References
Hubbard BA, Unger JG, Rohrich RJ. Reversal of Skin Aging with Topical Retinoids. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2014;133(4):481e-490e.
Saltz R, Borba T. Skin Care and Dermatologic Treatments. In: Nahai F, ed. The Art of Aesthetic Surgery. St. Louis, Missouri: Quality Medical Publishing; 2005;1:170-193.
Bhawan J, Olsen E, Lufrano L, et al. Histologic evaluation of the long term effects of tretinoin on photodamaged skin. J Dermatol Sci. 1996;11:177-182.
Clark CP. Office-Based Skin Care and Superficial Peels: The Scientific Rationale. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1999;104(3):854-864.
Leyden JJ. Treatment of Photodamaged Skin with Topical Tretinoin: An Update. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1998;102(5):1667-1671.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female patient returns for evaluation one week following a SMAS facelift with neck lift procedure. Physical examination reveals facial asymmetry during smiling. She demonstrates normal whistling and lip pursing abilities, but shows lower lip asymmetry when attempting a broad smile. Which of the following findings is LEAST probable?
A) Botulinum toxin type A injection may help achieve symmetry during healing
B) The condition results from damage to a cervical facial nerve branch
C) Complete recovery typically occurs within 1 to 6 months without surgical intervention
D) The affected side shows increased lower tooth visibility during smiling
E) Mentalis muscle function remains intact
questions.answer:
D)
Cervical branch facial nerve injury causes impaired lower lip retraction on the affected side, resulting in less visible lower teeth during smiling, not more. A is correct because botulinum toxin can be injected into the unaffected side's depressor labii inferioris to improve symmetry. B is correct because this presentation is characteristic of cervical branch injury from subplatysmal dissection. C is correct because studies show 100% recovery rates within 3 weeks to 6 months. E is correct because preserved mentalis function helps differentiate this from marginal mandibular nerve injury.

questions.question:
When comparing liposuction-only breast reduction to traditional excisional breast reduction methods, which of the following represents a distinguishing feature of the liposuction-only approach?
A) Typically preserves lactation capability
B) More effectively addresses breast drooping
C) Creates greater risk to nipple-areolar blood circulation
D) Causes higher rates of nipple-areolar sensation loss
E) Produces minimal post-surgical edema
questions.answer:
A)
Liposuction-only breast reduction preserves major blood vessels and nerves, maintaining breast-feeding potential since no pedicle dissection or major tissue rearrangement occurs. B is incorrect because liposuction alone cannot effectively address significant ptosis. C is incorrect because liposuction preserves vascular structures, reducing rather than increasing blood supply risks. D is incorrect because nerve preservation during liposuction maintains sensation better than excisional techniques. E is incorrect because liposuction can cause significant swelling and bruising that may persist for weeks.

questions.question:
A 66-year-old male worker suffers complete traumatic amputation of his right ear. Emergency personnel retrieved the severed part, wrapped it in moist cloth, and stored it on ice. Microsurgical reattachment is attempted, but adequate venous drainage cannot be established. Which treatment strategy will most likely produce the optimal long-term cosmetic result?
A) Epidermal removal from the amputated segment, subcutaneous pocket placement, and staged reconstruction
B) Discarding the amputated tissue and performing delayed rib cartilage reconstruction
C) Microsurgical reattachment without venous connection combined with post-operative medicinal leech treatment
D) Skin removal from the amputated segment with temporoparietal fascial flap coverage
E) Simple reattachment without microsurgical connections followed by 3-week hyperbaric oxygen treatment
questions.answer:
C)
Recent systematic reviews demonstrate that microsurgical replantation achieves superior outcomes even without venous anastomosis, with no significant difference in survival rates between cases with and without venous repair when combined with leech therapy. A is incorrect because the Mladick technique produces inferior results compared to microsurgical approaches. B is incorrect because immediate replantation attempts yield better outcomes than delayed reconstruction. D is incorrect because this approach sacrifices the original skin unnecessarily when microsurgical options exist. E is incorrect because hyperbaric oxygen alone cannot substitute for proper microsurgical technique.

questions.question:
In hand transplantation, which tissue component is most prone to triggering IgM and IgG antibody responses that lead to cellular damage?
A) Bone marrow tissue
B) Vascular endothelium
C) Muscle tissue
D) Neural tissue
E) Cutaneous tissue
questions.answer:
E)
Cutaneous tissue contains numerous antigen-presenting cells including Langerhans cells, making it the most immunogenic component of composite tissue allografts and the primary target for type II hypersensitivity reactions involving IgG and IgM antibodies. A is incorrect because bone marrow is less immunogenic than skin in vascularized composite allografts. B is incorrect because endothelium, while immunogenic, is less reactive than skin tissue. C is incorrect because muscle tissue demonstrates lower immunogenicity compared to skin. D is incorrect because neural tissue is relatively immunoprivileged and less likely to trigger strong antibody responses than skin.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female presents to the clinic with a 5-year history of unchanging facial asymmetry. Clinical examination reveals prominence of the right mandibular angle; there is no facial pain, palpable masses, or lymph node enlargement. CT imaging of the maxillofacial region demonstrates hypertrophy of the right masseter muscle relative to the left side. What is the most suitable initial treatment approach for this condition?
A) Construction of an occlusal splint for bruxism management
B) Botulinum toxin type A injection into the hypertrophied right masseter muscle
C) Surgical partial excision of the right masseter muscle
D) Installation of a left mandibular angle implant
E) Oncology consultation to exclude systemic amyloidosis
questions.answer:
B)
The patient presents with benign masseter muscle hypertrophy, characterized by unilateral muscle enlargement causing facial asymmetry without symptoms. Botulinum toxin type A injection represents the optimal first-line therapy due to its minimally invasive nature, reversibility, and excellent safety profile without requiring general anesthesia. A) is incorrect because while bruxism can cause masseter hypertrophy, it typically presents bilaterally, and occlusal splints prevent dental damage but don't reduce existing muscle hypertrophy. C) is incorrect as surgical myectomy is more invasive and should be reserved for cases where conservative treatment fails. D) is incorrect because contralateral augmentation doesn't address the underlying hypertrophy and is typically considered after other treatments. E) is incorrect since systemic amyloidosis typically causes bilateral, painful masseter enlargement and progressive symptoms, unlike this stable unilateral presentation.

questions.question:
A healthy 30-year-old male presents with a slowly enlarging lesion on the palmar aspect at the base of his left ring finger. He denies any history of injury and reports the mass is painless. Physical examination reveals a 1.0-cm centrally located mass just beyond the metacarpophalangeal flexion crease. The lesion is solid, non-pulsatile, and does not allow light transmission. The mass remains stationary during finger movement. Radiographic imaging is unremarkable. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Digital lipoma
B) Fibrosarcoma
C) Ganglion cyst
D) Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
E) Neurilemmoma
questions.answer:
D)
This presentation is classic for a giant cell tumor of tendon sheath, given its midline location over the flexor tendon sheath and failure to transilluminate, indicating a solid mass rather than fluid-filled lesion. The location and characteristics strongly support this diagnosis. A) is incorrect because digital lipomas are extremely rare in this location. B) is incorrect as fibrosarcoma would be highly unusual and would not typically present as a spherical midline palmar mass. C) is incorrect because ganglion cysts would transilluminate due to their fluid content, unlike this solid mass. E) is incorrect since neurilemmomas arise from nerve sheaths and would present more laterally along the digital nerve pathway, not in the midline.

questions.question:
A healthy 64-year-old female undergoes facelift surgery with SMAS plication and neck muscle tightening. Prior to surgery, 150 mL of tumescent anesthetic is injected into the facial and neck tissues. In the post-anesthesia care unit, she develops weakness of the buccal branch on the right side. There is generalized facial edema, with the right side slightly more swollen than the left, but bruising appears symmetrical bilaterally. What is the most appropriate immediate management for the right facial weakness?
A) Corticosteroid injection
B) Needle aspiration
C) Return to operating room
D) Suture removal to free potential nerve compression
E) Watchful waiting
questions.answer:
E)
The most likely cause of immediate postoperative facial nerve weakness after facelift surgery is residual local anesthetic effect, which requires several hours to resolve completely. Observation with serial examinations is the most appropriate initial management. A) is incorrect because steroid injection is not indicated for anesthetic-related nerve weakness. B) is incorrect as aspiration is used for seromas that develop days after surgery, not immediate postoperative swelling. C) is incorrect since hematoma evacuation would be indicated for significant bleeding complications, but hematomas don't cause immediate nerve weakness. D) is incorrect because while suture entrapment is possible, it's much less likely than residual anesthetic effect in the immediate postoperative period.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male has a burn-related contracture affecting the third web space of his hand. A five-flap plasty (jumping man technique) is being planned for reconstruction. What method is used to achieve the final positioning of the central flap in this procedure?
A) 45-degree rotation
B) 60-degree rotation
C) 75-degree rotation
D) V-Y advancement
E) Y-V advancement
questions.answer:
E)
In the five-flap plasty (jumping man technique), the central flap is repositioned using Y-V advancement, where the pointed tip of the Y-shaped incision is advanced into an incision created in the opposing tissue to form a V configuration. This technique provides lengthening for contracture release. A) is incorrect because 45-degree rotation describes a z-plasty variation, not the central flap movement in jumping man plasty. B) is incorrect as 60-degree rotation refers to z-plasty angles used in the lateral components, not the central flap advancement. C) is incorrect since 75-degree rotation is another z-plasty variation that doesn't describe the central flap technique. D) is incorrect because V-Y advancement moves tissue in the opposite direction, advancing the base of a V into a defect to create a Y, which is the reverse of what occurs in jumping man plasty.

questions.question:
In adult patients, which bone is most frequently involved in isolated orbital floor fractures?
A) Ethmoid
B) Frontal
C) Lacrimal
D) Maxillary
E) Zygomatic
questions.answer:
D)
The maxillary bone forms the majority of the orbital floor and is most commonly fractured in isolated orbital floor injuries. This bone is particularly thin posterior to the infraorbital rim and is weakened by the infraorbital canal, making it susceptible to blow-out fractures from increased intraorbital pressure. A) is incorrect because the ethmoid bone primarily forms the medial orbital wall, not the floor. B) is incorrect as the frontal bone forms the superior orbital rim and roof, not the floor. C) is incorrect since the lacrimal bone is small and located in the medial orbital wall. E) is incorrect because while the zygomatic bone contributes to the lateral orbital floor, the maxillary bone comprises the larger portion that is most commonly fractured in isolated floor fractures.

questions.question:
A healthy 55-year-old female patient receives a diagnosis of vaginal squamous cell carcinoma. She undergoes subtotal vaginectomy, vulvectomy, and inguinal lymph node dissection. Bilateral sensate posterior thigh flaps are utilized for vaginal reconstruction. Which of the following nerves is required to be incorporated in this surgical procedure?
A) Iliohypogastric
B) Ilioinguinal
C) Inferior gluteal
D) Posterior femoral cutaneous
E) Pudendal
questions.answer:
D)
The posterior femoral cutaneous nerve (S1-S3) provides sensory innervation to the posterior thigh flap. This fasciocutaneous flap relies on the descending branch of the inferior gluteal artery and offers abundant, reliable soft tissue for transfer from the posterior thigh region. Due to its proximal vascular supply, this flap can easily extend high into the pelvic cavity and can be rotated to address both anterior and posterior vaginal defects. The flap can be harvested with relative technical simplicity in minimal time, and donor site closure typically doesn't require skin grafting. The posterior femoral cutaneous nerve (S1-S3) innervates the skin, enabling this flap to function as a sensate reconstruction when needed. A) Iliohypogastric nerve is incorrect because it provides sensation to the suprapubic region, not the posterior thigh. B) Ilioinguinal nerve is incorrect as it innervates the inguinal region and medial thigh, not the posterior thigh flap territory. C) Inferior gluteal nerve is incorrect because it provides motor innervation to the gluteus maximus muscle, not sensory innervation to the posterior thigh skin. E) Pudendal nerve is incorrect as it supplies sensation to the perineum and external genitalia, not the posterior thigh flap.

questions.question:
What is the primary function of meibomian gland secretions?
A) Forms the inner mucin layer covering the cornea
B) Provides lubrication to eyelid skin
C) Prevents evaporation of tear film
D) Controls infectious organisms
E) Facilitates tear film distribution
questions.answer:
C)
Meibomian glands produce the outer lipid layer of the tear film, which serves as a barrier to prevent evaporation of the underlying aqueous layer. This oil layer is essential for maintaining tear film stability and preventing dry eye symptoms. Meibomian gland dysfunction commonly leads to increased tear evaporation and dry eye syndrome. A) Forms the inner mucin layer is incorrect because this function is performed by conjunctival goblet cells, which secrete mucin to coat the corneal surface. B) Provides lubrication to eyelid skin is incorrect as meibomian glands specifically contribute to tear film composition, not direct skin lubrication. D) Controls infectious organisms is incorrect because this antimicrobial function is primarily carried out by proteins in the aqueous layer secreted by lacrimal glands. E) Facilitates tear film distribution is incorrect since this function is performed by the inner mucin layer from goblet cells, which helps spread the aqueous layer across the corneal surface.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old business professional presents with an 8-year history of cold sensitivity and fingertip ulcerations affecting the index and middle fingers on both hands. The patient does not smoke. Examination reveals slender fingers with glossy skin appearance. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Buerger disease
B) CREST syndrome
C) Hyperthyroidism
D) Hypothenar hammer syndrome
E) Sickle cell anemia
questions.answer:
B)
The clinical presentation is characteristic of CREST syndrome, a form of limited systemic sclerosis. CREST represents Calcinosis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysfunction, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasia. The combination of cold intolerance, bilateral fingertip ulcers, and shiny, tight skin (sclerodactyly) strongly suggests this connective tissue disorder. A) Buerger disease is incorrect because it typically occurs in heavy smokers and doesn't cause the characteristic skin changes seen in this patient. B) Hyperthyroidism is incorrect as it doesn't cause fingertip ulcers, cold intolerance, or skin tightening. D) Hypothenar hammer syndrome is incorrect because it usually affects only one hand following trauma or repetitive use, typically involving the ring and little fingers supplied by the ulnar artery. E) Sickle cell anemia is incorrect as it characteristically causes bone pain, abdominal pain, and leg ulcers, but fingertip ulceration is uncommon.

questions.question:
A 64-year-old postmenopausal woman inquires about why she hasn't been given hormone replacement therapy combining estrogen and progestin like her mother received. Combined hormone supplementation is linked to increased risk of which condition?
A) Coronary artery disease
B) Diabetes
C) Endometrial cancer
D) Invasive breast cancer
E) Osteoporosis
questions.answer:
D)
Combined estrogen and progestin hormone replacement therapy has been associated with an increased risk of invasive breast cancer, which is why its use has become more restricted. This increased breast cancer risk is one of the primary reasons why hormone replacement therapy has fallen out of widespread favor, as the risks are considered to outweigh the benefits for many patients. A) Coronary artery disease is incorrect because combined hormone therapy is not thought to significantly impact coronary artery disease risk. B) Diabetes is incorrect as hormone replacement therapy may actually decrease diabetes risk rather than increase it. C) Endometrial cancer is incorrect because the addition of progestin to estrogen therapy actually protects against endometrial cancer, unlike estrogen-only therapy. E) Osteoporosis is incorrect since hormone replacement therapy typically reduces osteoporosis risk by maintaining bone density.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old woman develops facial muscle weakness in the lower face following facelift surgery. Which finding would most strongly suggest cervical branch facial nerve injury rather than marginal mandibular nerve damage?
A) The patient can still purse her lips
B) The patient has lower lip depression weakness
C) The patient has lower lip numbness
D) The patient has mid-facial weakness
E) The patient has upper lip numbness
questions.answer:
A)
With cervical branch facial nerve injury, the patient retains the ability to purse lips because the mentalis muscle and orbicularis oris muscle innervation remains intact. The cervical branch primarily controls the platysma and lower lip depressor muscles, while lip pursing function is preserved through other facial nerve branches. This distinguishes it from marginal mandibular nerve injury, where lip pursing may be more significantly affected. B) Lower lip depression weakness is incorrect because both cervical branch and marginal mandibular nerve injuries can cause weakness in lower lip depression. C) Lower lip numbness is incorrect since neither the cervical branch nor marginal mandibular branch provides sensory innervation to the lip. D) Mid-facial weakness is incorrect as neither of these nerve branches supplies the mid-facial muscles. E) Upper lip numbness is incorrect because facial nerve branches do not provide sensory innervation to the lips.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old homeless male patient arrives at the emergency department via ambulance. His serum alcohol level measures 325 mg/dL. Physical examination of his right hand and forearm reveals no detectable pulses in the radial or ulnar arteries. The compartment pressure reads 55 mmHg. Which nerve is most susceptible to permanent damage in this clinical scenario?
A) Lateral antebrachial
B) Medial antebrachial
C) Median
D) Radial
E) Axillary
questions.answer:
C)
The median nerve is most vulnerable to irreversible injury in this compartment syndrome case. In Volkmann's contracture pathophysiology, damage progresses from deep central muscles (flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus) to middle layer muscles (flexor digitorum superficialis, pronator teres) and finally to wrist flexors and extensors. Nerve conduction decreases at 30 mmHg pressure and ceases at 50 mmHg, with permanent damage occurring after 8 hours. The median nerve suffers damage earlier than the ulnar nerve due to its anatomical location. A) Lateral antebrachial is incorrect because it runs superficially and is not in the deep compartment. B) Medial antebrachial is incorrect as it also travels superficially. D) Radial nerve is incorrect because it courses dorsally, outside the deep compartment. E) Axillary nerve is incorrect since it does not extend into the forearm region.

questions.question:
What advantage do myoelectric prosthetic devices provide compared to body-powered prosthetic systems?
A) Greater durability
B) Reduced cost
C) Less frequent adjustments needed
D) Capability for more sophisticated movements
E) Reduced training period required
questions.answer:
D)
Myoelectric prostheses excel in providing enhanced range of motion and the ability to perform sophisticated movements involving simultaneous multi-joint motion. While neither prosthetic type shows clear overall superiority, myoelectric systems specifically offer superior complex movement capabilities. Selection should be individualized based on patient needs, preferences, experience, and functional requirements. A) Greater durability is incorrect because body-powered prostheses actually demonstrate superior durability. B) Reduced cost is incorrect as myoelectric prostheses are typically more expensive than body-powered alternatives. C) Less frequent adjustments is incorrect since body-powered systems require fewer adjustments and less maintenance. E) Reduced training period is incorrect because body-powered prostheses generally require shorter training times.

questions.question:
A 2-month-old male infant is brought to the office because of mid face hypoplasia, craniosynostosis, and bilateral hand and foot anomalies. A photograph of the left foot is shown. This patient most likely has which of the following syndromes?


A) Apert
B) Crouzon
C) Goldenhar
D) Nager
E) Treacher Collins
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option A.






The patient described has Apert syndrome. This autosomal dominant syndrome is characterized by bicoronal craniosynostosis that leads to turribrachycephaly, mid face hypoplasia, and complex hand and feet syndactyly. 


Patients with Crouzon syndrome, an autosomal dominant disorder, typically have craniosynostosis involving the coronal, sagittal, and lambdoid sutures, as well as turribrachycephaly. Other findings include mid face hypoplasia, exorbitism, and proptosis. The extremities are normal.


Goldenhar syndrome, or oculoauriculovertebral dysplasia, involves asymmetry of the hard and soft tissues of the face. This condition is most commonly unilateral but may be seen bilaterally in some patients. Manifestations of this syndrome include hypoplasia involving the mandible and underlying soft tissues of the face, epibulbar dermoids, and varied degrees of microtia on the affected side. Most patients have associated vertebral abnormalities. 


Nager syndrome, or acrofacial dysostosis, is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by craniofacial and upper extremity abnormalities. Patients with Nager syndrome have hypoplasia of the orbits, zygoma, maxilla, mandible, and soft palate. Auricular defects may also be present. Hypoplasia or agenesis occurs in the radius, thumbs, and metacarpals. Some patients may have radioulnar synostosis and elbow joint deformities. 


Patients with Treacher Collins syndrome, or mandibular dysostosis, have hypoplasia of the zygoma, maxilla, and mandible, downward slanting of the palpebral fissures, colobomas of the lower eyelids, absence of eyelashes, and auricular defects.


References
Vander Kolk CA. Syndromic craniosynostosis. In: Achauer BM, Eriksson E, Guyuron B, et al, eds. Plastic Surgery: Indications, Operations, and Outcomes. Vol 2. St. Louis: Mosby; 2000:707-719.
McCarthy JG, Epstein FJ, Wood-Smith D. Craniosynostosis. In: McCarthy JG, ed. Plastic Surgery. Vol 4. Philadelphia: WB Saunders; 1990:3019-3025.
Bartlett SP, Mackay GJ. Craniosynostosis syndromes. In: Aston SJ, Beasley RW, Thorne CH, et al, eds. Grabb and Smith's Plastic Surgery. 5th ed. Philadelphia: Lippincott-Raven; 1997:295-304.

questions.question:
An 18-month-old patient presents for follow-up after fronto-orbital advancement surgery for metopic craniosynostosis. At what minimum age can radiographic imaging reliably demonstrate frontal sinus development?
A) 1 year
B) 2 years
C) 4 years
D) 6 years
E) 10 years
questions.answer:
D)
Frontal sinus development becomes radiographically visible at 6 years of age (72 months). The frontal sinuses are not present at birth and remain absent during early skull growth phases. They become detectable on imaging only when the first period of skull growth concludes, coinciding with when the endocranial table stops growing and adapts to brain morphology. A) 1 year is incorrect because frontal sinuses have not yet begun development at this age. B) 2 years is incorrect as the sinuses are still not radiographically apparent. C) 4 years is incorrect because although some early development may begin, the sinuses are not yet visible on standard radiographic studies. E) 10 years is incorrect as this significantly exceeds the age when frontal sinuses first become radiographically detectable.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old woman who has a 15-year history of rheumatoid arthritis comes for evaluation because of the inability to actively extend the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints of the right small and ring fingers. On examination today, she has near full passive motion of all fingers and is able to actively extend the thumb, index, and long fingers. Photographs are shown. She is unable to hold the ring and small fingers in extension when they are passively extended. X-ray studies show severe destructive arthropathy of the wrist, MCP, and proximal interphalangeal joints. There is ulnar drift and subtle volar subluxation of the MCP joint in all fingers; the ulnar head is prominent dorsally and is unstable. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her inability to actively extend the MCP joints of the ring and small fingers?


A) MCP joint contracture
B) Posterior interosseous nerve palsy associated with elbow synovitis
C) Rupture of the extensor tendons in zone VII
D) Rupture of the sagittal bands
E) Volar subluxation of the MCP joints
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


Extensor lag of the fingers is a common problem in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and severe wrist and finger arthropathy. Persistent synovial inflammation results in periarticular osseous destruction and weakening of the stabilizing ligaments. Any of the choices can potentially cause a restriction of finger extension at the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints, but only rupture of the extensor tendons would result in the constellation of findings observed here. This patient has severe wrist arthritis and dorsal prominence of the ulnar head (unstable). This can result in attritional ruptures of the extensor digiti minimi and ulnar-sided extensor digitorum communis tendons; treatment is resection of the ulnar head and tendon transfer to restore extensor function.


Posterior interosseous nerve palsy resulting from synovitis about the radiocapitellar joint is well described in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, but would affect extension of all fingers and the thumb. Rupture and subluxation of sagittal bands would lead to inability to actively extend the MCP but, in contrast to extensor tendon ruptures, full extension can be maintained after the fingers are passively extended. MCP joint contracture would limit active and passive finger motion.


References
1. Williamson SC, Feldon P. Extensor tendon ruptures in rheumatoid arthritis. Hand Clin. 1995 Aug;11(3):449-459.
2. Schindele SF, Herren DB, Simmen BR. Tendon reconstruction for the rheumatoid hand. Hand Clin. 2011 Feb;27(1):105-113.
3. Trieb K. Treatment of the wrist in rheumatoid arthritis. J Hand Surg Am. 2008 Jan;33(1):113-123.

questions.question:
A 154-lb (70-kg), 54-year-old male patient presents with decreased urine output and general malaise 48 hours following subtotal glossectomy with free radial forearm flap reconstruction. His medical history includes chronic kidney disease (baseline creatinine was 1.8 mg/dL, currently 3.3 mg/dL). Post-operative medications include aspirin 81 mg daily and dextran 40 infusion at 20 mL/hr. Vital signs: temperature 99.9°F (37.7°C), pulse 88 bpm, respirations 20/min, blood pressure 110/60 mmHg. The flap appears pink and pliable. Hourly urine output is 15 mL. What is the most appropriate intervention?
A) Give 500-mL lactated Ringer's bolus
B) Initiate diuretic therapy
C) Start dopamine infusion
D) Stop dextran administration
E) Perform urgent neck exploration
questions.answer:
D)
Discontinuing dextran is the most appropriate action. This patient exhibits dextran-induced acute kidney injury, a rare but serious complication caused by direct nephrotoxic effects or intraluminal hyperviscosity. Patients with pre-existing renal impairment are at increased risk. Studies show dextran increases systemic complications 3.9- to 7.2-fold compared to aspirin alone, with equivalent efficacy for flap protection. A) Lactated Ringer's bolus is incorrect because it contains potassium, which would worsen hyperkalemia in acute-on-chronic renal failure. B) Diuretic therapy is incorrect as there are no signs of fluid overload requiring diuresis. C) Dopamine infusion is incorrect because low-dose dopamine has not proven beneficial for preventing or treating acute renal failure in this clinical context. E) Neck exploration is incorrect since the flap appears healthy with no evidence of vascular compromise requiring surgical intervention.

questions.question:
What requirement must be met for accreditation of an outpatient surgical facility that serves plastic surgery patients?
A) Every staff member treating pediatric cases must possess Pediatric Advanced Life Support certification
B) Outpatient facilities undergo inspection every 5 years
C) Patients receiving general anesthesia in outpatient settings need supervised monitoring by a responsible adult for 1-2 hours post-discharge
D) Plastic surgeons practicing in outpatient facilities must hold American Board of Plastic Surgery certification
E) Surgeons must maintain unrestricted hospital privileges at an acute care facility within 30 minutes' drive time
questions.answer:
E)
Surgeons operating in ambulatory surgery centers must demonstrate unrestricted hospital privileges at an acute-care hospital within 30 minutes' driving distance of the facility. This requirement ensures rapid access to higher-level care if complications arise. The AAAASF mandates this standard for patient safety. A) Only one team member (not all) needs PALS certification when pediatric patients are treated. B) Facilities are inspected every 3 years, not 5 years. C) Patients require responsible adult supervision for 12-24 hours, not 1-2 hours after general anesthesia. D) Surgeons must be Board Certified or Board Eligible with any ABMS-recognized board, not specifically the American Board of Plastic Surgery.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old boy who is left-handed comes for evaluation of a scald injury to his right hand that occurred one year prior. Physical examination reveals a boutonniere deformity of the ring finger with extremely thin skin covering the dorsal aspect of the joint. Surgical repair of the joint deformity is being considered. Which of the following flaps would be most suitable for coverage in this patient?
A) Atasoy
B) Homodigital island
C) Moberg
D) Reverse cross finger
E) Thenar
questions.answer:
D)
The reverse cross finger flap is the only option among the choices that can adequately reach the dorsal proximal interphalangeal joint. This flap transfers a pedicled subdermal plexus to the defect while leaving thin skin at the donor site. The recipient area requires skin grafting to complete the coverage. The preferred donor locations are the dorsal surfaces of the middle and proximal phalanges of neighboring fingers. A is incorrect because the Atasoy V-Y advancement flap is designed for fingertip pulp defects, not dorsal joint coverage. B is incorrect because the homodigital island flap is specifically used for pulp reconstruction. C is incorrect because the Moberg flap is traditionally used for volar thumb amputation defects up to 2 cm and cannot cover the dorsal ring finger surface. E is incorrect because a thenar flap lacks sufficient reach to cover the dorsum of the ring finger PIP joint.

questions.question:
A healthy 154-lb (70-kg) woman is undergoing an elective facial cosmetic procedure with conscious sedation. The sedation protocol includes intravenous midazolam 0.25 mg/kg and fentanyl 12.5 mg/kg. During the middle of the procedure, two sequential non-invasive blood pressure measurements taken 5 minutes apart show a systolic pressure of 85 mmHg. What is the most appropriate initial management for this patient's hypotension?
A) Administer flumazenil
B) Administer naloxone
C) Administer a vasopressor intravenous bolus (ephedrine or phenylephrine)
D) Begin cardiopulmonary resuscitation
E) Increase intravenous fluids
questions.answer:
E)
Increasing intravenous fluids is the most appropriate first step because this scenario occurs in approximately 20% of patients undergoing similar conscious sedation procedures, and 100% of these patients respond appropriately to increased IV fluid administration. The medication doses used are within normal therapeutic ranges. A is incorrect because flumazenil reversal is not needed since the midazolam dose is appropriate and the patient shows no signs of benzodiazepine toxicity. B is incorrect because naloxone is unnecessary as the fentanyl dose is on the lower end of normal and there are no signs of opioid toxicity. C is incorrect because vasopressors should only be considered if fluid resuscitation fails, not as first-line treatment. D is incorrect because the patient has only mild hypotension without other concerning symptoms requiring CPR.

questions.question:
The parents of a healthy 3-day-old male infant seek consultation regarding their baby's bilateral lop ear deformities. What is the most appropriate initial management approach?
A) Await spontaneous correction
B) Fit the infant's head and ears for a helmet
C) Initiate ear molding devices immediately
D) Prescribe oral estrogen blocker therapy
E) Schedule bilateral otoplasty surgery at age 3 months
questions.answer:
C)
Immediate initiation of ear molding devices is most appropriate because maternal estrogen circulation causes decreased helical cartilage rigidity, allowing effective ear reshaping. Studies show 90% success rates when molding begins within the first week of life, but success drops to 50% when started even a few weeks later. A is incorrect because spontaneous correction of ear deformities is unlikely to occur as the child ages. B is incorrect because helmets are used for cranial reshaping, not ear deformity correction. D is incorrect because oral medications of any type are unlikely to influence ear shape. E is incorrect because surgical intervention is typically reserved for cases where molding fails and is usually performed closer to preschool age when the ear has reached most of its adult size.

questions.question:
Which of the following factors most significantly increases the risk of developing osteoradionecrosis following radiation therapy?
A) Dental caries
B) Edentulous mandible
C) Oral thrush
D) Osseointegrated implants
E) Radiation dose of 3500 cGy
questions.answer:
A)
Dental caries is the most significant risk factor because most reported cases of osteoradionecrosis have dental caries and extraction sites as precipitating factors. Periodontal disease also contributes to ORN development. B is incorrect because having an edentulous mandible does not increase ORN risk. C is incorrect because oral candidiasis (thrush) can develop after radiation but does not increase ORN risk. D is incorrect because osseointegrated implants do not increase the risk of osteoradionecrosis. E is incorrect because 3500 cGy is below the threshold where ORN risk significantly increases; most studies show increased risk occurs when radiation doses exceed 6500 cGy.

questions.question:
A 43-year-old woman presents for breast reduction consultation. She currently wears a DDD bra and desires reduction to a C cup. She takes oral contraceptives and does not smoke. Her height is 5 ft 5 in (167 cm), weight is 145 lb (65.7 kg), and BMI is 23.8 kg/m². Examination shows suprasternal notch to nipple distance of 29 cm and inframammary fold to nipple distance of 16 cm. Independent of surgical technique, which factor most increases her risk for postoperative fat necrosis?
A) Massive weight loss
B) Oral contraceptive use
C) Patient age
D) Suprasternal notch to nipple distance
E) Tissue resection weight
questions.answer:
E)
Tissue resection weight is the most significant risk factor for fat necrosis, with studies consistently showing increased rates with larger resection weights (both absolute and relative to preoperative breast size). Fat necrosis occurs in 2-10% of reduction mammaplasty cases regardless of technique. A is incorrect because massive weight loss is not associated with increased breast fat necrosis risk. B is incorrect because no studies link oral contraceptive use to increased fat necrosis; some evidence suggests hormone supplementation may decrease infectious complications. C is incorrect because while some studies suggest age correlation, they lack consensus and statistical significance when properly controlled. D is incorrect because while longer suprasternal notch to nipple distances (especially >37 cm) increase risk, this patient's 29 cm measurement is not in the high-risk range.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female patient presents with ductal carcinoma in situ positioned about 6 cm away from the nipple in the upper outer quadrant of her left breast. If she chooses to undergo breast-conserving surgery followed by radiotherapy, what is the required minimum surgical margin?
A) 1 mm
B) 2 mm
C) 5 mm
D) 1 cm
E) 2 cm
questions.answer:
B)

The correct answer is B because established clinical guidelines specify a minimum 2-mm margin for patients receiving breast-conserving treatment, as margins of this width significantly reduce the risk of local tumor recurrence compared to narrower margins. A is incorrect because 1-mm margins are associated with higher recurrence rates than the recommended 2-mm standard. C is incorrect because while 5-mm margins are adequate, they exceed the minimum requirement and are not necessary for optimal outcomes. D is incorrect because 1-cm margins are unnecessarily wide and provide no additional benefit over the 2-mm standard. E is incorrect because 2-cm margins are excessively wide and may compromise cosmetic results without improving oncologic outcomes.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old female patient experiences loss of sensation in her left ear lobule two weeks following a facelift procedure. Which nerve was most likely damaged during the surgery?
A) Auriculotemporal
B) Great auricular
C) Greater occipital
D) Lesser occipital
E) Vagus
questions.answer:
B)

The correct answer is B because the great auricular nerve, arising from cervical roots C2 and C3, travels superficially over the sternocleidomastoid muscle and specifically innervates the earlobe along with other parts of the ear's lower and posterior regions, making it vulnerable during facelift procedures. A is incorrect because the auriculotemporal nerve, a trigeminal nerve branch, primarily supplies the tragus and upper ear regions near the temporal area, not the earlobe. C is incorrect because the greater occipital nerve innervates the posterior scalp region, not ear structures. D is incorrect because the lesser occipital nerve supplies only the upper portion of the ear's medial surface, not the earlobe. E is incorrect because the vagus nerve's auricular branch (Arnold's nerve) innervates the ear canal and concha, not the earlobe.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female patient presents for evaluation of a ventral hernia that formed following a complex right colon resection performed 5 years prior. Her medical background includes high blood pressure, and her BMI is 34 kg/m2. She experiences dyspnea when scrubbing floors at her workplace but can ascend stairs or walk uphill without difficulty. She has no other pulmonary or cardiac complaints. Physical cardiac examination is normal, and recent ECG, CBC, and basic chemistry panel results are unremarkable. Component separation technique for hernia repair is under consideration. What is the most appropriate next action for preoperative cardiac evaluation?
A) Cardiac catheterization
B) Echocardiographic exercise stress testing
C) Echocardiography at rest
D) Nuclear cardiac pharmacologic stress testing
E) No further cardiac testing is needed
questions.answer:
E)

The correct answer is E because this patient undergoing elective intermediate-risk surgery has no active cardiac conditions, demonstrates adequate functional capacity (≥4 METs based on her ability to climb stairs), and lacks clinical risk factors requiring further evaluation according to ACC/AHA guidelines. A is incorrect because cardiac catheterization is an invasive procedure reserved for patients with active coronary syndromes or when revascularization is being considered, neither of which applies here. B is incorrect because exercise stress testing is not indicated in patients with good functional capacity who lack symptoms or clinical risk factors. C is incorrect because resting echocardiography has not been proven to predict perioperative cardiac events in asymptomatic patients with good functional capacity. D is incorrect because pharmacologic stress testing is unnecessary when patients demonstrate adequate exercise tolerance and have no clinical risk factors.

questions.question:
Which medical condition is linked to the greatest risk of failure in finger reattachment procedures?
A) Alcohol abuse
B) Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
C) Diabetes mellitus
D) Psychotic disorders
E) Tobacco use
questions.answer:
D)
