Angiography is not appropriate to evaluate or treat compartment syndrome. Ulnar nerve release will not treat the compartment syndrome.


ReferencesDonaldson J, Haddad B, Khan WS. The pathophysiology, diagnosis and current management of acute compartment syndrome. Open Orthop J. 2014;8:185-193.Gourgiotis S, Villias C, Germanos S, Foukas A, Ridolfini MP. Acute limb compartment syndrome: a review. J Surg Educ. 2007;64(3):178-186.Prasarn ML, Ouellette EA. Acute compartment syndrome of the upper extremity. J Am Acad Orthop Surg. 2011;19(1):49-58.Soong M, DaSilva M. Acute forearm compartment syndrome secondary to digit avulsion injury. A case report. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2009;91(2):435-437.

questions.question:
A 33-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of a 4-mm reddish discoloration underneath the left index fingernail. He reports significant tenderness to pressure directly on the discoloration, but not the surrounding tissue, along with pain in the area that is worse when going outside in the winter and reaching for items in the freezer. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most likely etiologic factor in the origin of this patient's mass?


A) Arthritis at the distal interphalangeal joint
B) Capillary malformation
C) Growth of myoarterial unit
D) Proliferation at the germinal matrix
E) Trauma to the nail bed
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


The most likely etiologic factor involved in the origin of this mass is growth of myoarterial unit.


This patient has evidence of a glomus tumor, which is a rare benign tumor that often presents in the subungual region. Glomus tumors arise from the glomus body, which is a myoarterial unit that functions in thermoregulation. Clinical findings include focal tenderness and cold intolerance.


Some tests for glomus tumor include the Love pin test, Hildreth test, and cold-sensitivity test. In the Love pin test, pressure is applied to the area with a pinhead and the area containing the glomus tumor becomes exquisitely painful. In the Hildreth test, pain in the area is relieved by the use of a tourniquet, due to the restricted blood supply. In the cold-sensitivity test, cold water or an ice cube elicits increased pain in the affected area.


Diagnosis of glomus tumor can be verified with MRI or ultrasonography. Management consists of surgical excision of the lesion, as shown in the photograph.


Arthritis at the distal interphalangeal joint can give rise to digital mucous cysts, which can demonstrate nail deformity but typically are not painful.


Capillary malformation can result in reddish-appearing vascular tumors, but these would not typically present the sensitivity and cold intolerance seen in glomus tumors.


Proliferation at the germinal matrix can give rise to nail abnormalities, but these typically manifest as abnormalities in the nail plate rather than in the subungual region (i.e., melanonychia, skin cancers).


Trauma to the nail bed can result in subungual hematoma, which can cause pain, but a hematoma typically will resolve and not persist for years.


ReferencesHufschmidt K, Foissac R, Camuzard O, Cardot-Leccia N, Chignon-Sicard B, Balaguer T. Glomus tumors of the upper limb: single-center retrospective study of clinical and functional outcomes. Hand Surg Rehabil. 2017;36(4):290-295.Kontogeorgakos VA, Jebson PJL. Soft tissue tumors. In: Weiss APC, Budoff JE, Calfee RP, et al, eds. Textbook of Hand and Upper Extremity Surgery. 2nd ed. American Society for Surgery of the Hand; 2019;79:1953-1968.Lee W, Kwon SB, Cho SH, Eo SR, Kwon C. Glomus tumor of the hand. Arch Plast Surg. 2015;42(3):295-301.Morey VM, Garg B, Kotwal PP. Glomus tumours of the hand: Review of literature. J Clin Orthop Trauma. 2016;7(4):286-291.Netscher DT, Aburto J, Koepplinger M. Subungual glomus tumor. J Hand Surg Am. 2012;37(4):821-823;quiz 824.

questions.question:
An 81-year-old male patient with peripheral arterial disease receives rectus femoris muscle flap coverage for an exposed vascular graft in the groin area. Two days after surgery, he experiences acute chest pain and becomes unconscious with no detectable pulse. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation begins immediately. The cardiac monitor displays ventricular fibrillation. What is the most appropriate immediate action following electrical defibrillation?
A) End-tidal CO2 monitoring
B) Two minutes of chest compressions
C) Airway intubation
D) Intravenous adenosine administration
E) Pulse and rhythm assessment
questions.answer:
B)
Current ACLS protocols require immediate resumption of CPR following defibrillation, without interrupting for pulse or rhythm evaluation. Chest compressions should begin immediately and continue for 2 minutes before reassessing rhythm and repeating the cycle if spontaneous circulation has not returned. A is incorrect because capnometry requires advanced airway placement first. C is incorrect because airway management should not delay chest compressions in witnessed VF arrest. D is incorrect because adenosine has no role in cardiac arrest management. E is incorrect because pulse checks should be delayed until after the 2-minute CPR cycle to maximize perfusion.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female presents with progressive facial edema around her jaw and mobile teeth. The swelling has gradually increased over time. Clinical examination reveals unilateral left facial swelling near the third molar area. Mandibular CT imaging demonstrates a radiolucent, multiloculated, single-chamber lesion at the left mandibular angle with evidence of root resorption. What treatment sequence is most appropriate for this patient?
A) Lesion curettage with cancellous bone grafting
B) Preoperative radiation, segmental mandibulectomy, and reconstruction
C) Segmental mandibulectomy with reconstruction
D) Segmental mandibulectomy, reconstruction, and postoperative chemotherapy
E) Segmental mandibulectomy, reconstruction, dental restoration, and sentinel lymph node sampling
questions.answer:
C)
This patient has an ameloblastoma, a benign odontogenic tumor requiring surgical excision. Segmental mandibulectomy with reconstruction is the standard treatment to prevent recurrence. A is incorrect because simple curettage has unacceptably high recurrence rates for ameloblastoma. B is incorrect because radiation therapy is not indicated for benign tumors and may cause complications. D is incorrect because chemotherapy has no role in treating benign ameloblastoma. E is incorrect because sentinel node biopsy is unnecessary for benign lesions that do not metastasize.

questions.question:
A 59-year-old female with 35 years of employment in rubber production is evaluated by her family doctor for a firm, painless, 1-cm ulcerated lesion on the hard palate located between the central incisors and incisive foramen. This presumed minor salivary gland neoplasm would most likely metastasize to which lymph node group?
A) Submandibular lymph nodes
B) Parathyroid lymph nodes
C) Parotid lymph nodes
D) Posterior cervical triangle nodes
E) Occipital lymph nodes
questions.answer:
A)
The anterior hard palate, lips, gingiva, teeth, and tongue drain primarily to Level I lymph nodes (submental and submandibular regions). B is incorrect because parathyroid nodes are not a recognized lymphatic drainage pattern for oral cavity lesions. C is incorrect because parotid nodes typically drain the lateral face and temporal region, not the anterior hard palate. D is incorrect because posterior triangle nodes (Level V) drain the nasopharynx and oropharynx, not the anterior oral cavity. E is incorrect because occipital nodes drain the posterior scalp, not oral cavity structures.

questions.question: A 50-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of a stab wound to the right forearm. A photograph is shown. She is taken to the operating room and general anesthesia is administered. Which of the following is the most appropriate examination, in this intubated patient, to assess for tendinous injuries to the fingers?A) Passively extend the fingersB) Passively extend the wristC) Passively flex the fingersD) Passively flex the wristE) Place hand in cold water
questions.answer: The correct response is Option D. This patient has sustained a dorsal mid forearm laceration. Common injuries within this location include injuries to the musculotendinous units of the extensors to the wrist, fingers, and thumb. Additionally, the radial sensory nerve and dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve could be injured depending on the location and vector of the object that caused the injury. Passive flexion as demonstrated in the photograph demonstrates the effect of tenodesis. With passive wrist flexion, intact digital extensors should be put under tension and bring the metacarpophalangeal joints into extension. However, in this patient the long and ring fingers do not extend with wrist flexion.In an uninjured hand, when the wrist is passively flexed the fingers and thumb will extend. With wrist extension, the fingers are brought into flexion and the thumb is brought toward the small finger.Bringing the wrist into extension would help with a volar wound as it would help establish injuries to digital flexors.Putting the hand in cold water is a better test for sensory nerve injury as loss of wrinkling will be demonstrated.Passive flexion or extension of the fingers will not reliably demonstrate which specific tendons are injured in this patient.ReferencesSeftchick JL, Detullio LM, Fedorczyk JM, Aulicino PL. Clinical examination of the hand. In Skirven TM, Osterman AL, Fedorczyk JM, Amadio PC, Eds. Rehabilitation of the Hand and Upper Extremity. Philadelphia, PA: Elsevier Mosby; 2011; 6:55-71.Cales L, Weber RA. Effect of water temperature on skin wrinkling. J Hand Surg. 1997; 22(4):747-749.Tay SC, Moran SL. Flexor tendon injuries in children. In Tang JB, Amadio PC, Guimberteau JC, Chang J, Eds. Tendon Surgery of the Hand. Philadelphia, PA: Elsevier Saunders; 2012; 15:179-185.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old male has recently obtained health insurance coverage through an Affordable Care Act marketplace plan. Which of the following services is NOT included as an essential health benefit for this patient?
A) Dental services
B) Mental health and addiction treatment
C) Pharmaceutical coverage
D) Preventive care services
E) Rehabilitative services
questions.answer:
A)
The ACA mandates ten Essential Health Benefits for all new insurance plans, but dental coverage is only required for pediatric patients, not adults. Since this patient is 50 years old, dental services are not guaranteed under his plan. B is incorrect because mental health and substance abuse treatment are required essential benefits. C is incorrect because prescription drug coverage is a mandated essential benefit. D is incorrect because preventive services and chronic disease management are required essential benefits. E is incorrect because rehabilitation services and devices are mandated essential benefits.

questions.question:
An 18-year-old male seeks surgical correction of a unilateral congenital Stahl ear malformation. Which of the following ear features would most likely be found during physical examination?
A) Additional third antihelical crus
B) Conchal protrusion due to mastoid prominence
C) Hypertrophied conchal cartilage
D) Superior antihelical crus overgrowth
E) Pointed cartilaginous thickening at the upper-middle helical junction
questions.answer:
A)
Stahl ear deformity is characterized by an abnormal third crus of the antihelix, often accompanied by helical flattening, rim unfurling, and posterosuperior helical projection. B is incorrect because conchal projection from mastoid prominence describes a different condition, not Stahl ear. C is incorrect because enlarged conchal cartilage is associated with prominent ear deformity, not Stahl ear. D is incorrect because Stahl ear typically involves absence or underdevelopment of the superior antihelical crus, not hyperplasia. E is incorrect because pointed thickening at the helical junction describes Darwin's tubercle, not Stahl ear deformity.

questions.question:
A 52-year-old male experiences traumatic amputation of his dominant right hand's index finger due to a table saw accident. Clinical assessment reveals a clean-cut amputation just beyond the flexor digitorum superficialis attachment site. The patient has no history of tobacco use. Which of the following represents the primary criterion for proceeding with replantation?
A) Hand dominance
B) Amputation of index digit
C) Anatomical location of injury
D) Absence of smoking history
E) Patient's age
questions.answer:
C)
The anatomical location of the injury is the primary criterion for replantation consideration. Amputations occurring beyond the flexor digitorum superficialis insertion are favorable for replantation because preserving additional digit length with an intact proximal interphalangeal joint significantly enhances functional outcomes. A is incorrect because hand dominance does not significantly influence replantation decisions. B is incorrect because single digit replantations at the proximal phalanx or PIP joint level in adults often yield poor functional results that may impair overall hand function. D is incorrect because smoking status is not a primary consideration for replantation candidacy. E is incorrect because adult age is not an indication for replantation, whereas pediatric amputations are typically replanted.

questions.question:
During surgical removal of a completely impacted lower third molar, adequate soft tissue protection around the mandible is essential to prevent damage to which nerve?
A) Facial nerve
B) Hypoglossal nerve
C) Inferior alveolar nerve
D) Infraorbital nerve
E) Lingual nerve
questions.answer:
E)
The lingual nerve requires protection during mandibular third molar extraction due to its intimate anatomical relationship with the lingual aspect of the mandible. This nerve is at high risk for iatrogenic injury if proper protective measures are not employed during the surgical procedure. A is incorrect because the facial nerve is located more superficially and is not at risk during intraoral third molar surgery. B is incorrect because the hypoglossal nerve runs deeper in the neck and is not endangered during routine third molar extraction. C is incorrect because the inferior alveolar nerve, while important, is typically protected by the bone during corticotomy procedures. D is incorrect because the infraorbital nerve is located in the maxilla and is not relevant to mandibular third molar surgery.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male arrives with severe closed head trauma. Intravenous fluid therapy is started due to ongoing nausea and decreased oral consumption. Head CT demonstrates widespread brain swelling. Which fluid choice is most suitable for this patient's management?
A) 5% dextrose in water
B) 3% hypertonic saline
C) 0.45% hypotonic saline
D) 0.9% normal saline
E) Lactated Ringer's solution
questions.answer:
B)
3% hypertonic saline is the optimal choice for managing elevated intracranial pressure and cerebral edema in traumatic brain injury. Hypertonic solutions effectively reduce brain swelling by creating an osmotic gradient that draws fluid from brain tissue, and studies demonstrate superior efficacy compared to mannitol in acute trauma settings. A is incorrect because hypotonic solutions like D5W can worsen cerebral edema by decreasing serum osmolality. C is incorrect because 0.45% saline is hypotonic and contraindicated in severe brain injury as it may exacerbate swelling. D is incorrect because normal saline, while isotonic, does not provide the osmotic benefit needed to reduce intracranial pressure. E is incorrect because lactated Ringer's solution lacks the hypertonic properties necessary to combat cerebral edema.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old right-handed male arrives at the emergency room following a stabbing incident at a tavern, resulting in a right arm injury. Examination reveals a 2×1 cm wound in the antecubital region. The patient cannot bend his thumb's interphalangeal joint or the index finger's proximal interphalangeal joint. Which nerve has most likely been damaged?
A) Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve
B) Median nerve
C) Musculocutaneous nerve
D) Radial nerve
E) Ulnar nerve
questions.answer:
B)
Median nerve injury is characterized by loss of thumb interphalangeal joint flexion and inability to flex the index finger at the proximal interphalangeal joint, along with impaired thumb opposition. These specific motor deficits are pathognomonic for median nerve damage. A is incorrect because the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve only provides sensation to the lateral forearm without motor function. C is incorrect because musculocutaneous nerve injury would affect elbow flexion and lateral forearm sensation, not finger flexion. D is incorrect because radial nerve palsy presents with wrist drop and inability to extend fingers and thumb, not flexion deficits. E is incorrect because ulnar nerve injury causes claw deformity of the ring and little fingers with hypothenar and interosseous muscle weakness, not the described pattern.

questions.question:
A 46-year-old female seeks consultation for neck aesthetic enhancement. Examination demonstrates neck fullness with poor jawline definition and a blunted neck-to-chin angle. What is the primary etiology of this blunted angle in this patient?
A) Forward-positioned mandible
B) Elevated hyoid bone placement
C) Excessive superficial neck fat
D) Retracted thyroid cartilage position
E) Sagging submandibular glands
questions.answer:
C)
Excessive preplatysmal fat accumulation is the predominant cause of an obtuse cervicomental angle, creating neck fullness and obscuring the mandibular border. This superficial fat layer can be addressed through direct excision or liposuction to restore proper neck contours. A is incorrect because an anteriorly positioned chin would actually improve the cervicomental angle, not worsen it. B is incorrect because a high hyoid position would create a more acute angle, while a low hyoid contributes to obtuseness. D is incorrect because thyroid cartilage position does not significantly influence the overall neck aesthetic contour. E is incorrect because submandibular gland ptosis affects lower neck fullness but is not the primary contributor to cervicomental angle obtuseness.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old woman comes to the office because of a split in the nail plate following a previous crush injury to the left index finger. The patient desires improvement in the appearance of the nail. A photograph is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?


A) Application of topical phenol
B) Excision/repair of the nail bed
C) Nail plate avulsion
D) Oral antifungal therapy
E) Split-thickness skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option B.






The most appropriate method of treatment is excision and repair of the nail bed.


The anatomy of the nail consists of a nail plate, nail fold, and a nail bed. The nail bed is the soft tissue beneath the nail plate, which is composed of the germinal matrix proximally and the sterile matrix distally. Most nail plate growth (90%) is provided by the germinal matrix. In cases of trauma, adherence between the nail fold dorsally and nail bed volarly can result in synechiae, interfering with nail growth and resulting in a longitudinal split in the nail. It is important to prevent adherence of dorsal and palmar elements by splinting the nail fold open during the healing phase. This can be accomplished by replacement of the nail plate if available, or using a piece of foil from the suture packet. This patient presents with a split nail deformity after previous trauma. There is scarring between the nail fold and the nail bed, resulting in a longitudinal split with inability to allow for growth of the nail plate in the central portion. Proper treatment consists of excision of the nail bed scar, with repair of the nail bed. Splinting of the nail fold during the healing period will prevent recurrent scarring of the dorsal fold to the palmar surface. In cases where there is significant scar tissue and inability to close the resultant defect after excision, grafting of the nail bed may be required. A split graft of the sterile matrix can be performed if the deficit is only present distally. If the germinal matrix is involved, a full-thickness graft is needed.


Avulsion of the nail plate alone will not eliminate the scarring at the proximal nail fold.


Oral antifungal therapy is useful in treatment of fungal onychomycosis.


Complete excision of the nail bed and split-thickness skin grafting can be used in nail ablation, but would result in absence of the nail and not yield a more cosmetic appearance.


Topical phenol application has been used for nail matricectomy, but can produce irregular tissue destruction and would result in loss of the nail.


References
Levin SL, Boyer MI, Bozentka DJ, et al, eds. Skin and Soft Tissue. In: Hammert W, Calfee RP, Bozentka DJ, et al, eds. ASSH Manual of Hand Surgery. 1st ed. Philadelphia, PA: Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2010;20:393-423.
Sommer NZ and Brown R, eds. The Perionychium. In: Wolfe SW, Hotchkiss RN, Pederson WC, et al, eds. Green‚Äos Operative Hand Surgery. 6th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Elsevier Churchill Livingstone; 2010;10: 333-53.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old male presents to the emergency room 2 hours following a punch to the left facial region. Clinical evaluation reveals left-sided facial edema. A panoramic radiograph (Panorex) was performed as shown. What is the most suitable treatment approach?
A) Remove all portions of the left mandibular third molar and apply maxillomandibular fixation (MMF) for 2 weeks
B) Remove all portions of the left mandibular third molar and apply MMF for 6 weeks
C) Remove all portions of the left mandibular third molar, apply MMF, and perform open reduction with internal fixation (ORIF)
D) Wire the left mandibular third molar to the neighboring tooth for stabilization, apply MMF, and perform ORIF
E) Maintain the third molar, apply MMF, and perform ORIF
questions.answer:
C)
The radiographic study demonstrates a root fracture, requiring complete tooth and root removal. Tooth extraction is indicated when the tooth lies within the fracture line and MMF is needed to restore proper occlusion. The left parasymphyseal and comminuted left angle fractures require management, with the parasymphyseal fracture specifically needing open reduction and internal fixation to prevent lateral displacement of the left mandibular body caused by masseter muscle pull. A is incorrect because 2 weeks of MMF is insufficient for proper healing. B is incorrect because MMF alone without ORIF would not adequately address the parasymphyseal fracture. D is incorrect because attempting to preserve a fractured tooth root through ligation is inappropriate. E is incorrect because keeping a tooth with a fractured root in the fracture line increases infection risk and complications.

questions.question:
A healthy 35-year-old male experiences exposure to freezing temperatures for 24 hours. Following initial hypothermia treatment and rapid hand rewarming, bilateral upper extremity cold injury is assessed. Clinical examination reveals extensive frostbite affecting both hands extending to the wrists. What represents the most suitable immediate management step?
A) Corticosteroid treatment
B) Heparin administration
C) Surgical tissue removal
D) Systemic antimicrobial therapy
E) Thrombolytic treatment
questions.answer:
E)
Intra-arterial thrombolytic therapy represents the most appropriate next intervention. Tissue damage in frostbite results from two phases: initial freezing with crystal formation (improved by rewarming) and subsequent local inflammation with coagulation causing microvascular thrombosis and progressive cell death. Thrombolytic agents like urokinase or tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) can reverse local microvascular thrombosis and restore perfusion before irreversible ischemia occurs. A is incorrect because systemic corticosteroids are not indicated in acute frostbite management. B is incorrect because heparin is used as an adjunct after thrombolytics are initiated, not as primary therapy. C is incorrect because surgical debridement is performed weeks to months later after tissue demarcation occurs. D is incorrect because systemic antibiotics are not indicated at this acute stage.

questions.question:
The tissue capsules obtained from patients diagnosed with breast implant-related anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (ALCL) demonstrate substantial colonization by which bacterial organism?
A) Escherichia coli
B) Ralstonia pickettii
C) Staphylococcus aureus
D) Pseudomonas aeruginosa
E) Serratia marcescens
questions.answer:
B)
Capsules from patients with breast implant-associated ALCL show significant presence of Gram-negative Ralstonia species bacteria compared to non-tumor capsules which typically contain Staphylococcus species. This finding supports the bacterial induction hypothesis for ALCL development, as bacterial biofilm is considered an inciting factor for both breast implant-related ALCL and capsule contractures. The condition is almost exclusively associated with textured implants and presents most commonly as late seroma. A is incorrect because E. coli is not the predominant organism found in ALCL capsules. C is incorrect because Staphylococcus aureus is more commonly found in non-tumor capsules rather than ALCL cases. D is incorrect because Pseudomonas aeruginosa is not the primary bacterial species associated with ALCL capsules. E is incorrect because Serratia marcescens is not the characteristic organism found in these cases.

questions.question:
A healthy 8-year-old female presents with a 15-cm congenital nevus located on the buttock and thigh region. What is the most suitable management recommendation for the parents?
A) Alexandrite laser therapy
B) Punch biopsy procedure
C) Sequential excision beginning at age 21 years
D) Tissue expansion with excision
E) Monitoring for 3 to 6 months
questions.answer:
D)
Tissue expansion followed by excision is the most appropriate treatment. This lesion qualifies as a giant congenital nevus (>6 cm on the body in children, estimated to reach >20 cm at maturity) with a significantly elevated melanoma risk of approximately 51%. Studies indicate that 50% of malignancies in large nevi occur by age 3 years and 70% by puberty, warranting early aggressive treatment starting around 6 months of age. Tissue expansion allows for adequate skin coverage after excision. A is incorrect because Alexandrite lasers are not recommended for nevus treatment and may cause hypertrophic scarring. B is incorrect because punch biopsy may not be representative of the entire large lesion and could yield false-negative results. C is incorrect because waiting until age 21 years significantly increases melanoma risk given the early transformation tendency. E is incorrect because observation alone is inappropriate for giant nevi due to high malignancy potential.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old male approaches his neighbor, who is a plastic surgeon, at a social gathering. He was evaluated in the emergency room yesterday for a fractured toe and received an ibuprofen prescription. He reports ongoing toe pain and requests a prescription for acetaminophen with codeine, which he has used previously. The plastic surgeon inquires about his medical background, and examination reveals buddy-taped toes with moderate bruising and swelling. The plastic surgeon provides the requested prescription. What represents the most essential subsequent action for the plastic surgeon?
A) Contact his primary physician
B) Obtain a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) authorization form
C) Request a follow-up x-ray examination
D) Direct the man to the emergency room
E) Document the medical encounter in writing
questions.answer:
E)
Writing a medical note documenting the encounter is most essential. Once a prescription is issued, a patient-physician relationship is established, creating legal obligations for documentation. Prescriptions are legal documents subject to local, state, and federal regulations. Most states require maintaining written records of all treatments and prescriptions, and federal law mandates a bona fide patient-physician relationship with written medical records for controlled substance prescriptions. Failure to comply can jeopardize medical licensure. A is incorrect because contacting the treating physician is unnecessary in this situation. B is incorrect because obtaining HIPAA consent is not the most critical immediate step after prescribing. C is incorrect because ordering repeat imaging is not necessary for this clinical scenario. D is incorrect because emergency department referral is not warranted for this stable condition.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old male presents to the emergency room 2 hours following a severe crushing injury to his right upper leg from a car accident. Clinical evaluation reveals an exposed femoral fracture; the lower leg and foot appear pale and cold. Popliteal, dorsalis pedis, and posterior tibialis pulses cannot be felt. Closed reduction fails to restore blood flow. What is the most appropriate next intervention?
A) Vascular reconstruction using a polytetrafluoroethylene graft
B) Vascular reconstruction using a reversed saphenous vein graft
C) CT angiography
D) Intramedullary stabilization of the femoral fracture
E) Insertion of a temporary vascular shunt
questions.answer:
E)
Gustilo Type IIIC fractures involve arterial damage requiring reconstruction regardless of soft tissue extent and often represent significant threats to limb viability. Prompt identification and treatment of lower limb vascular trauma is essential for limb preservation. CT angiography provides minimal value when hard signs of vascular compromise are present and may delay surgical treatment while increasing ischemic time. The combination of vascular and orthopedic trauma requiring reconstruction is uncommon, occurring in approximately 1.5% of cases. Evidence from military and civilian studies evaluating management sequences suggests that improved ischemic times and better limb salvage outcomes are achieved with temporary vascular reconstruction using shunts as the initial intervention to restore circulation, followed by debridement and fracture stabilization. Final vascular reconstruction should occur after debridement and fracture fixation. A) is incorrect because definitive repair should be delayed until after fracture fixation. B) is incorrect because permanent vascular reconstruction should follow temporary shunting and fracture stabilization. C) is incorrect because imaging delays treatment when hard signs of vascular injury are present. D) is incorrect because restoring perfusion takes priority over fracture fixation.

questions.question:
A 65-year-old male is sent for management of biopsy-confirmed subungual verrucous carcinomas affecting the index and middle fingers of his dominant right hand. Clinical examination reveals distorted, elevated nail beds. Radiographic imaging shows no bone involvement of the terminal phalanx. What is the most appropriate treatment approach?
A) Amputation at the distal interphalangeal joint level
B) Amputation at the proximal interphalangeal joint level
C) Mohs micrographic resection with graft reconstruction
D) Ray amputation
E) Topical 5-fluorouracil application
questions.answer:
C)
Verrucous squamous cell carcinoma of the fingernails typically involves the index, middle, and ring fingers. Research demonstrates that the cause is linked to human papillomavirus (HPV) strains. HPV presence in these lesions suggests possible genital-digital transmission as a tumor development mechanism. HPV-related digital squamous cell carcinoma has higher recurrence rates after surgical treatment than previously documented, exceeding rates for general cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas, possibly due to residual HPV after surgery. Mohs micrographic resection appears to enhance tumor-free excision rates compared to standard excision while preserving more healthy tissue. However, metastasis rates in verrucous squamous cell carcinoma remain low. Since bone involvement is absent, amputation is likely premature and would be considered for recurrent disease or persistent positive margins during Mohs resection. A) is incorrect because amputation is excessive when bone is uninvolved. B) is incorrect because more extensive amputation is unnecessary without bone involvement. D) is incorrect because ray amputation is overly aggressive for this presentation. E) is incorrect because topical 5-fluorouracil is inadequate treatment for this lesion type.

questions.question:
An otherwise healthy 37-year-old female is scheduled for delayed microsurgical breast reconstruction. Which of the following complications is linked to tamoxifen use?
A) Cardiovascular instability
B) Compromised wound healing
C) Enhanced bleeding risk
D) Seroma development
E) Thrombotic complications
questions.answer:
E)
Estrogen receptor-positive breast cancers may respond to adjuvant therapy with selective estrogen receptor modulators like tamoxifen, which can decrease recurrence and death rates. Tamoxifen is linked to thrombotic complications, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. This prothrombotic mechanism is thought to result from tamoxifen's effects on estrogen receptors that are plentiful in vascular endothelium. Studies demonstrate tamoxifen is associated with higher total flap failure rates and lower flap salvage rates when used within 28 days of microsurgical breast reconstruction, representing two half-lives of tamoxifen's active metabolite (N-desmethyl tamoxifen, half-life=14 days). Therefore, it is recommended that tamoxifen be discontinued for at least 28 days before microsurgical breast reconstruction, with some authors suggesting postoperative discontinuation as well. A) is incorrect because tamoxifen does not cause hemodynamic instability. B) is incorrect because tamoxifen is not associated with impaired wound healing. C) is incorrect because tamoxifen does not increase bleeding risk. D) is incorrect because tamoxifen is not linked to seroma formation.

questions.question:
The primary vascular supply to the rectus abdominis muscle arises from which of the following blood vessels?
A) Common femoral
B) External iliac
C) Internal iliac
D) Internal mammary
E) Superficial femoral
questions.answer:
B)
Component separation for large abdominal wall defect closure was initially described by Ramirez in 1990. The procedure aims to achieve abdominal wall closure using well-perfused, innervated muscle flaps. The main vascular supply to the rectus muscles consists of the deep inferior epigastric artery and vein, which branch from the external iliac vessels. The internal mammary vessels give rise to the superior epigastric arteries and veins, providing secondary, non-dominant vascular supply to the rectus muscles. The femoral vessels give rise to the superficial inferior epigastric artery and vein, which supply the skin and subcutaneous tissue of the lower lateral abdomen. A) is incorrect because the common femoral vessel does not directly supply the rectus muscle. C) is incorrect because the internal iliac vessel does not provide the dominant supply to the rectus muscle. D) is incorrect because the internal mammary vessel provides only secondary, non-dominant supply. E) is incorrect because the superficial femoral vessel does not supply the rectus muscle directly.

questions.question:
A 53-year-old male is having revision mandibular reconstruction. An iliac crest osteocutaneous free flap is being considered. What is the primary benefit of this flap compared to a free fibula osteocutaneous flap?
A) Bone length
B) Reduced donor site morbidity
C) Pedicle length
D) Dependability with multiple osteotomies
E) Vertical height
questions.answer:
E)
Multiple options exist for bone grafts, both vascularized and non-vascularized. In this clinical situation, a vascularized bone graft is clearly indicated due to the irradiated field, anterior location, and >6-cm defect. Vascularized bone graft options include free fibula, free iliac crest, free scapula, and free radius bone grafts. Each has individual advantages and disadvantages, though collectively, vascularized bone free flaps provide 40% greater strength, 56% increased stiffness, higher complete fusion rates, and superior functional results. The free fibula flap is typically the preferred choice for this scenario due to its long pedicle (6-10 cm), substantial usable bone (22-24 cm), minimal donor site morbidity, dental implant compatibility, and dependable skin flap (skin island survival rates near 100% due to enhanced anatomical knowledge and improved harvest techniques). However, its limitation is lacking the vertical height of the free iliac crest. A) is incorrect because the fibula provides greater bone length than the iliac crest. B) is incorrect because the fibula has less donor site morbidity than the iliac crest. C) is incorrect because the fibula has a longer pedicle than the iliac crest. D) is incorrect because the fibula is more reliable for multiple osteotomies than the iliac crest.

questions.question:
A 66-year-old woman weighing 132 pounds (60 kg) arrives at the emergency department with deep second-degree burns covering 20% of her total body surface area, plus a small surrounding area of first-degree burns. The injury occurred in an outdoor setting when she fell backward onto a fire pit. Her burns affect only her buttocks and back. She denies voice changes or breathing difficulties. During the first 24 hours, she receives 9600 mL of lactated Ringer's solution. Given her fluid management, what complication is she most at risk for developing?
A) Abdominal compartment syndrome
B) Burn depth progression to full-thickness
C) Deep vein thrombosis
D) Digital ischemia
E) Failed autologous skin graft take
questions.answer:
A)
The patient is at highest risk for abdominal compartment syndrome due to fluid over-resuscitation. Using the Parkland formula (4 × %TBSA × weight in kg), she should have received approximately 4800 mL in 24 hours, but received nearly double that amount (9600 mL). Over-resuscitation leads to complications including abdominal compartment syndrome, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and increased infection rates. B is incorrect because burn conversion to deeper injuries typically results from under-resuscitation, not over-resuscitation. C is incorrect as deep vein thrombosis has no established correlation with burn fluid resuscitation volumes. D is incorrect because digital ischemia is associated with inadequate resuscitation rather than excessive fluid administration. E is incorrect since there is no evidence that over-resuscitation impairs autologous skin graft engraftment.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old woman presents for evaluation of a biopsy-confirmed squamous cell carcinoma located in the right preauricular region, measuring 2.1 cm in diameter. She has no other medical conditions. What is the most appropriate next management step?
A) Electrodesiccation of the tumor
B) Surgical excision with intraoperative frozen section analysis
C) Surgical excision with 2-mm margins
D) Surgical excision with 4-mm margins
E) Topical 5% fluorouracil application
questions.answer:
B)
Surgical excision with intraoperative frozen section analysis is most appropriate for this high-risk squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is located in a high-risk anatomical site (preauricular area) and exceeds 2 cm in diameter, making it twice as likely to recur locally and three times more likely to metastasize. Frozen section margin evaluation is recommended for high-risk lesions to ensure complete excision before closure. A is incorrect because electrodesiccation is only suitable for small, low-risk squamous cell carcinomas. C is incorrect as 2-mm margins are inadequate for any squamous cell carcinoma. D is incorrect because while 4-mm margins might be appropriate for low-risk lesions, this high-risk tumor requires frozen section confirmation of clear margins. E is incorrect since topical fluorouracil is used for treating diffuse actinic keratoses, not established squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.question:
A 15-year-old girl presents to the clinic 2 months following failed scalp replantation after an avulsion injury. The resulting wound has been managed with negative pressure wound therapy. Examination reveals a clean, granulating defect involving approximately 50% of the total scalp area. What is the most appropriate reconstructive approach?
A) Bilateral temporo-parieto-occipital (Juri) flap coverage
B) Free latissimus dorsi muscle flap with immediate split-thickness skin grafting
C) Orticochea three-flap technique with skin grafting of donor sites
D) Sequential excision and primary closure
E) Split-thickness skin grafting followed by staged tissue expansion
questions.answer:
E)
Split-thickness skin grafting followed by staged tissue expansion provides the optimal reconstruction for this large scalp defect. Tissue expansion is the preferred method for defects approaching 50% of the scalp because it preserves hair-bearing tissue, maintains sensation, and provides the best aesthetic outcome. The expanded tissue should be approximately 20% larger than the defect to account for recoil. A is incorrect because Juri flaps are designed for frontal or frontoparietal defects, not vertex defects, and are unsuitable for defects exceeding 30% of the scalp. B is incorrect since free tissue transfer is reserved for total or near-total scalp defects, particularly in irradiated or oncologic cases. C is incorrect because the Orticochea procedure is intended for occipital defects up to 30% of scalp area and results in unnatural hair orientation. D is incorrect as serial excisions are only appropriate for smaller defects and would be impossible to achieve stable closure for a 50% scalp defect.

questions.question:
Which syndrome is most commonly associated with venous malformations?
A) Kasabach-Merritt syndrome
B) Maffucci syndrome
C) Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome
D) Parkes-Weber syndrome
E) Sturge-Weber syndrome
questions.answer:
B)
Maffucci syndrome is most commonly associated with venous malformations, characterized by the combination of venous malformations and multiple enchondromas. This syndrome carries risks for malignant chondrosarcoma transformation and intracranial tumors in 20% of patients. A is incorrect because Kasabach-Merritt syndrome is associated with hemangiomas or diffuse hemangiomatosis, presenting with severe thrombocytopenia and bleeding complications. C is incorrect as Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome (hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia) involves telangiectasias of the face, oral mucosa, and extremities, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. D is incorrect because Parkes-Weber syndrome is a variant of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome featuring arteriovenous fistulae with port-wine stains and limb hypertrophy. E is incorrect since Sturge-Weber syndrome involves facial capillary malformations (port-wine stains) in trigeminal distribution with associated leptomeningeal vascular malformations and seizure disorders.

questions.question:
A 35-year-old woman is scheduled for limited liposuction of the lower abdomen in an office-based facility. The plan includes intravenous sedation combined with local and tumescent anesthesia. According to the Guidelines for Office-Based Anesthesia, which equipment is mandatory in the operating suite?
A) Central line insertion kit
B) Electrocautery device
C) Airway management and intubation equipment
D) Tracheostomy instruments
E) Patient warming device
questions.answer:
C)
Airway management and intubation equipment is mandatory according to the Guidelines for Office-Based Anesthesia when administering any form of anesthesia in office settings. Required anesthesia equipment includes suction apparatus, appropriately sized airway devices, laryngoscope blades, positive-pressure ventilation capability, intravenous supplies, pharmacologic reversal agents, basic resuscitation medications, and defibrillator equipment for deep sedation cases. A is incorrect because central line kits, while potentially useful for certain cases, are not considered essential equipment for routine office-based procedures. B is incorrect as electrocautery units are procedure-specific equipment rather than mandatory anesthesia safety equipment. D is incorrect since tracheostomy sets are specialized equipment that may be desirable for certain patient populations but are not required for standard office-based anesthesia. E is incorrect because warming devices, though beneficial for patient comfort, are not classified as essential safety equipment under the guidelines.

questions.question:
A 25-year-old female presents to the clinic expressing dissatisfaction following breast augmentation surgery performed to address tuberous breast abnormalities. Clinical examination reveals two horizontal ridges running parallel across the inferior aspect of both breasts with downward displacement of the prosthesis. Which of the following most accurately characterizes the location of the native inframammary fold in this case?
A) Superior to both the upper and lower horizontal ridges
B) Located at the lower horizontal ridge
C) Located at the upper horizontal ridge
D) Inferior to both the upper and lower horizontal ridges
questions.answer:
C)
The upper horizontal ridge represents the original inframammary fold that was disrupted during surgery. In double-bubble deformity, the native fold becomes the superior transverse line, while the inferior line marks where the implant pocket was dissected or where the implant has settled. A is incorrect because the original fold is not above both ridges but forms one of them. B is incorrect because the lower ridge represents the new implant position, not the original anatomy. D is incorrect because the original fold is not below both ridges but is incorporated as the upper ridge.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old woman in good health with a prior history of breast cancer had bilateral mastectomies and reconstruction using tissue expanders, later exchanged for cohesive silicone gel implants 8 years previously with regular MRI monitoring. She presents with complaints of discomfort and firmness in her right breast that has progressively worsened over the past month. Vital signs show temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure 112/76 mmHg, and pulse 68 bpm. The right breast appears more voluminous than the left, though the implant position remains symmetric. The overlying skin appears normal without palpable tenderness. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) MRI of the right breast to evaluate implant integrity
B) Seven-day course of oral antibiotics with prednisone taper
C) Surgical exploration with culture and implant replacement
D) Consultation with medical and surgical oncology teams
E) Breast ultrasound with fine-needle aspiration of any collected fluid
questions.answer:
E)
When a patient presents with late seroma (typically >1 year post-surgery), evaluation for breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) is essential. The initial diagnostic approach involves ultrasound followed by fine-needle aspiration for immunohistochemistry testing, particularly CD30 staining. A is incorrect because MRI for implant integrity should not be the first step when BIA-ALCL must be excluded. B is incorrect because antibiotics and steroids are not indicated without evidence of infection or inflammation. C is incorrect because surgical exploration should not precede fluid analysis and immunohistochemistry evaluation. D is incorrect because oncology referral may be needed later but is not the immediate next step.

questions.question:
A 7-year-old male child is assessed for capillary malformations affecting his right leg and thigh that have been evident since birth. Physical examination demonstrates venous varicosities along the anterior leg and medial thigh regions. The circumference of the involved lower extremity exceeds that of the normal limb. Duplex ultrasonography reveals no evidence of arteriovenous connections. This patient has the highest risk of developing which of the following complications?
A) Chondrosarcoma
B) Disseminated intravascular coagulation
C) High-output cardiac failure
D) Limb-length discrepancy
E) Pathologic fracture
questions.answer:
D)
The combination of capillary malformations, varicosities, and limb overgrowth without arteriovenous fistulae is characteristic of Klippel-Trénaunay syndrome. Limb-length discrepancy occurs in up to 67% of these patients, typically with the affected limb being longer. A is incorrect because chondrosarcoma risk is associated with Maffucci syndrome, which typically presents in adolescence with enchondromas. B is incorrect because disseminated intravascular coagulation (Kasabach-Merritt syndrome) is more common with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma. C is incorrect because high-output cardiac failure occurs with arteriovenous fistulae, as seen in Parkes-Weber syndrome. E is incorrect because pathologic fractures occur through enchondromas in Maffucci syndrome, not Klippel-Trénaunay syndrome.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old female with hereditary breast cancer predisposition is planning bilateral prophylactic mastectomy. She has chosen immediate single-stage reconstruction with permanent silicone implants and acellular dermal matrix. Which of the following represents the most sensitive technique for detecting implant failure in this patient?
A) CT scan
B) Mammography
C) MRI
D) Physical examination
E) Ultrasonography
questions.answer:
C)
MRI remains the most sensitive imaging modality for detecting both intracapsular and extracapsular silicone implant ruptures, including silent ruptures that are asymptomatic. Current FDA recommendations suggest MRI screening 5-6 years after implantation, then every 2-3 years thereafter. A is incorrect because CT scans can detect intracapsular ruptures but have limited ability to identify extracapsular ruptures. B is incorrect because mammography can only detect extracapsular silicone leakage, missing intracapsular ruptures. D is incorrect because physical examination cannot reliably detect silent ruptures, which are often completely asymptomatic. E is incorrect because ultrasound accuracy depends heavily on operator skill and equipment, with limitations in detecting posterior wall ruptures.

questions.question:
A 36-year-old female seeks consultation for breast augmentation surgery. She currently wears a 34B bra and desires enhancement to a full C cup. Her height is 5 ft 6 in (168 cm) and weight is 126 lb (57 kg). While she considers her breast appearance acceptable, her estranged husband has encouraged her to pursue enhancement. After discussing surgical risks including potential loss of nipple-areola sensation and long-term prosthesis maintenance requirements, she decides to proceed. Subpectoral placement of 375-mL saline implants is performed via inframammary incisions. Which factor is most likely to result in postoperative patient dissatisfaction?
A) Ongoing marital separation from her husband
B) Deflation of the breast prostheses
C) Hypertrophic scarring of the breast incisions
D) Inability to breast-feed
E) Insufficient breast enlargement
questions.answer:
A)
Patient dissatisfaction in aesthetic surgery often stems from poor patient selection and unrealistic expectations rather than surgical complications. This patient's primary motivation appears to be saving her marriage, which is an unrealistic expectation that surgery cannot fulfill. Even with excellent surgical results, she will likely remain dissatisfied if her marital situation doesn't improve. B is incorrect because prosthesis deflation, while a potential complication, can be addressed surgically and patients are counseled about this risk preoperatively. C is incorrect because hypertrophic scarring is a known risk that can be managed and patients are informed of this possibility. D is incorrect because breastfeeding concerns are discussed preoperatively, allowing patients to make informed decisions. E is incorrect because inadequate size can often be addressed with revision surgery and proper preoperative planning helps set appropriate expectations.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old woman comes to the office for consultation about improving the appearance of her "saggy" breasts. She has lost 100 lb (45 kg) during the past 18 months by diet. Photographs are shown. Physical examination shows breast deflation and marked ptosis. A Wise pattern mastopexy with augmentation mammaplasty is planned. Which of the following arteries is most likely to provide circulation to the breast gland and nipple during submuscular augmentation in this patient?



A)Intercostal
B)Pectoral
C)Superior epigastric
D)Thoracoacromial
E)Thoracodorsal
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


The thoracoacromial artery and vein travel just deep to the pectoralis major muscle, supplying circulation to the overlying breast tissue and skin. Subglandular augmentation mammaplasty disrupts the connection between the thoracoacromial vessels and the overlying breast. This leads to a higher risk of wound-healing complications when placing the prosthesis in the subglandular plane. The submuscular plane of dissection maintains the connection between the thoracoacromial vessel and overlying breast and skin, allowing better potential healing.


Intercostal arteries are multiple and are not completely disconnected with either subglandular or subpectoral augmentation mammaplasty.


The superior epigastric artery provides circulation to the rectus abdominis muscle and abdomen. This artery would be injured with the mastopexy procedure.


The thoracodorsal artery supplies the latissimus dorsi muscle and not the chest.


References
1. Netter FH. Atlas of Human Anatomy. 5th edition. Philadelphia: Saunders; 2011.
2. Shermak MA. Female breast anatomy. In: Shermak MA, ed. Body Contouring. New York: McGraw-Hill Professional; 2011:60-61.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old male presents to the emergency room following rescue from an avalanche burial. His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes that is well-managed through dietary modifications. He has a 10-year history of smoking one pack of cigarettes per day. On examination, the right lower leg shows redness, swelling, and blister formation extending from the lower portion of the tibia down to the toe tips. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
A) Surgical debridement with negative pressure wound therapy
B) Hyperbaric oxygen treatment
C) Intravenous heparin administration
D) Immediate amputation
E) Warming in a 104°F (40°C) water bath
questions.answer:
E)
Rapid rewarming by immersing the affected area in a water bath maintained at 104-108°F (40-42°C) is the cornerstone of frostbite treatment. This approach addresses the formation of extracellular ice crystals that cause cellular damage and has remained the standard treatment for decades. The rewarming process typically requires 20-40 minutes until distal perfusion returns. A is incorrect because surgical debridement and negative pressure therapy are secondary treatments that haven't proven effective as initial management. B is incorrect because hyperbaric oxygen therapy lacks strong evidence from randomized controlled trials and is considered adjunctive at best. C is incorrect because anticoagulants like heparin should only be considered after rewarming has been completed. D is incorrect because primary amputation would unnecessarily commit the patient to significant disability when tissue viability cannot be determined initially.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old male has ventral hernia reconstruction using biological mesh with midline fascial repair. The surgical approach includes bilateral component separation involving division of the external oblique fascia and muscle lateral to the linea semilunaris, dissection between the external and internal oblique muscles, and mobilization of the rectus muscle from the posterior rectus sheath. At which anatomical location would you expect the minimal advancement of the medial fascial margins?
A) Between the umbilicus and pubic region
B) Between the umbilicus and lower rib margin
C) At the lower rib margin
D) Above the pubic area
E) At the umbilical level
questions.answer:
C)
The component separation technique provides the least fascial advancement in the subxiphoid and subcostal regions, making upper abdominal defects more challenging to close. At the umbilical level, this technique can achieve approximately 10 cm of unilateral advancement (20 cm bilateral), but advancement decreases significantly in the upper regions. A is incorrect because the area between umbilicus and pubis allows for reasonable advancement. B is incorrect because this mid-region typically provides moderate advancement capabilities. D is incorrect because the suprapubic area generally permits adequate fascial mobilization. E is incorrect because the umbilical level actually provides the maximum advancement of approximately 10 cm unilaterally.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old woman with chronic hidradenitis suppurativa of the bilateral axillae is referred for surgical management after 4 years of local wound care, multiple corticosteroid injections, and oral antibiotics failed to improve her symptoms. Physical examination shows multiple inflamed nodules and draining sinuses. Photographs are shown. Which of the following treatment options is most likely to provide long-term resolution of this patient‚Äos symptoms?


A) Axillary lymphadenectomy and coverage with a trapezius flap
B) Carbon dioxide laser and silver sulfadiazine
C) Fistulotomy and negative pressure wound therapy
D) Lesion excision and primary closure
E) Total axillary excision and skin grafting
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option E.


Hidradenitis is a chronic and often disabling skin condition of the apocrine glands. It results in abscesses, inflammatory nodules, and draining sinuses in the axillae, groin, perineum, and occasionally the submammary area. It affects approximately 1 in 300 people, and it is more common in women, people who smoke, and people who are overweight. The axillae are more commonly involved in women, and the perineum more commonly in men.


Early treatment centers around local wound care, oral antibiotics, corticosteroid injections, hygiene, weight loss, and smoking cessation. Decreased estrogen levels may also contribute, and disease often subsides with oral contraceptives and during pregnancy. Unresponsive or extensive disease requires surgical intervention for long-term resolution. Relapse rates are high, and healing is often slow. Although limited excision and closure of solitary lesions is an effective short-term treatment, new lesions are likely to develop. Fistulotomy alone has an unacceptably high recurrence rate.


A long-term resolution in this severely affected patient requires complete excision of the hair-bearing skin of the affected area. The large defect created needs broad skin coverage. The best options include split-thickness skin grafting or grafting with negative pressure wound therapy immobilization. Negative pressure wound therapy followed by healing by secondary intention or coverage with local flaps are additional options, though scar contractures and shoulder stiffness are risks.


Laser treatments are too superficial to treat the deeper apocrine structures. Lymphadenectomy is not necessary for a cure.


References
1. Buimer MG, Wobbes T, Klinkenbijl JH. Hidradenitis suppurativa. Br J Surg. 2009 Apr;96(4):350-360.
2. Pokala N, Kiran RP. Surgery for Hidradenitis Suppurativa. Medscape website. Available at: http://emedicine.medscape.com/article/190972. Accessed March 27, 2014.
3. Chen YE, Gerstle T, Verma K, et al. Management of hidradenitis suppurativa wounds with an internal vacuum-assisted closure device. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2014 Mar;133(3):370e-377e.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old female developed a postoperative infection and skin death following Achilles tendon reconstruction via a posterior midline approach 3 weeks prior. Examination reveals a 3 x 3-cm defect directly over the Achilles tendon without peritenon coverage. A fasciocutaneous propeller flap from the medial lower leg is planned for reconstruction. The septal perforating vessels supplying this flap course between which anatomical structures?
A) Flexor hallucis longus and gastrocnemius
B) Gastrocnemius and soleus
C) Peroneus longus and peroneus brevis
D) Soleus and flexor digitorum longus
E) Tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus
questions.answer:
D)
The posterior tibial artery perforator propeller flap receives its blood supply from vessels that emerge between the soleus and flexor digitorum longus muscles. Anatomical studies have identified three main perforator clusters at 4-9 cm, 13-18 cm, and 21-26 cm from the intermalleolar line. A is incorrect because these muscles don't form the anatomical corridor for posterior tibial perforators. B is incorrect because the space between gastrocnemius and soleus doesn't contain the relevant septal perforators for this flap. C is incorrect because peroneal muscles relate to peroneal artery perforators, not posterior tibial perforators. E is incorrect because this describes the location of anterior tibial artery perforators, not the posterior tibial perforators needed for this medial leg flap.

questions.question:
A 26-year-old female presents with burns to the back of her right hand. Following multiple debridement procedures, she has exposed extensor tendons, wrist joint capsule, and superficial radial nerve. Coverage with a pedicled groin flap is being considered. Which blood vessel most likely provides the primary arterial supply to this groin flap?
A) Deep circumflex iliac
B) Deep external pudendal
C) Lateral femoral circumflex
D) Superficial circumflex iliac
E) Superficial inferior epigastric
questions.answer:
D)
The superficial circumflex iliac artery (SCIA) serves as the primary vascular pedicle for both free and pedicled fasciocutaneous groin flaps. The flap is oriented along a line parallel to and 3 cm below the inguinal ligament, with a maximum dependable width of 10 cm. Harvest proceeds from lateral to medial, incorporating Scarpa's fascia laterally for improved reliability. A is incorrect because the deep circumflex iliac artery, while present in the region, is not the dominant supply for the standard groin flap. B is incorrect because the deep external pudendal artery supplies different anatomical territories. C is incorrect because the lateral femoral circumflex artery primarily supplies thigh-based flaps, not the groin flap. E is incorrect because the superficial inferior epigastric artery supplies lower abdominal wall flaps rather than the groin flap.

questions.question:
A 12-year-old male is assessed for a vertical groove near the facial midline extending from his hairline down to his eyebrows. All of the following clinical features may be observed in hemifacial atrophy EXCEPT:
A) Tongue wasting
B) Altered facial sensation
C) Underdeveloped cheekbone
D) Dental misalignment
E) Underdeveloped jaw
questions.answer:
B)
Hemifacial atrophy (morphea en coup de sabre/Parry-Romberg syndrome) preserves normal facial sensation, muscle function for facial expression, and chewing abilities. The condition primarily affects structural development rather than neurological function. A is incorrect because tongue atrophy commonly occurs on the affected side as part of the progressive tissue loss. C is incorrect because malar (cheekbone) underdevelopment is a characteristic finding due to the progressive atrophy affecting facial bones. D is incorrect because dental misalignment, particularly lateral open bite, frequently develops secondary to maxillary and mandibular hypoplasia. E is incorrect because mandibular underdevelopment is a typical feature of the condition, contributing to facial asymmetry and bite abnormalities.

questions.question:
An obese 47-year-old man comes to the office for pain and drainage in the perineal region. A photograph is shown. Medical history includes hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and diabetes. Which of the following is the most important factor in reducing the risk of recurrence after surgery?


A) Adjuvant radiation
B) Antibiotic therapy
C) Extent of resection
D) Intralesional corticosteroid injection
E) Method of closure
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option C.


This patient has hidradenitis suppurative (HS). There are various surgical treatments available to these patients with varying risk of recurrence. Surgical options include incision and drainage, surgical deroofing, local excision, and radical resection of all involved tissue. Reconstructive and closure techniques include secondary healing, primary closure, skin grafting and locoregional pedicled flaps. Numerous studies have looked at the outcomes with various closure techniques and they show that risk of recurrence is likely influenced more by the extent of disease rather than the method of definitive closure. Because of the recurrent nature of this disease, surgery has been considered as the only effective curative therapy for HS. Inadvertent compromise in the margin of resection may diminish the probability of successful healing. Radical resection of all hair-bearing skin with a 1- to 2-cm clear margin of normal tissue is the gold standard and the most important factor in reducing risk of recurrence. Recurrence rates tend to be higher after excision in regions where functional and aesthetic outcomes take priority, and often limit the extent of resection and compromise the ability to obtain clear margins (ie, axilla, perineum, breast). Historically, low-voltage radiation was used as a treatment modality for HS and it is thought to cause complete follicular destruction. Current studies on radiotherapy as treatment for HS are very limited because of concern regarding malignancies arising in radiation fields. Radiation should be reserved for individuals with severely recalcitrant disease and used with extreme caution in younger individuals. Bacterial burden may also diminish the probability of successful wound healing. Topical and systemic antibiotics are still the mainstay treatment for mild HS. Despite their widespread use, few studies have shown their efficacy. In addition, antibiotics do offer relief by reducing the burden of abscesses and pustules in some individuals, but recurrence in these people is frequent. Standard practice of managing acute flares with intra-lesional steroid injections lacks clinical evidence. It has been shown in a series of patients to reduce erythema, edema, size and pain, but no effect on recurrence of disease has been shown.


References
Falola RA, DeFazio MV, Anghel EL, et al. What Heals Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Surgery, Immunosuppression, or Both? Plast Reconstr Surg. 2016 Sep;138(3 Suppl):219S-29S.
Ellis, LZ. Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Surgical and Other Management Techniques. Dermatol Surg. 38:517-536, 2012.
Riis, PT et al. Intralesional triamcinolone for flares of hidradenitis suppurative: A case series. Journal of Amer Acad of Dermatol 75(6): 1151-1155, 2016 Dec.

questions.question:
A healthy 2-year-old girl is evaluated by her parents who are worried about her upper lip's appearance (shown). The parents report that her lip was mildly enlarged at birth and has been growing gradually. On examination, there is a soft, non-tender, bluish mass on the upper lip. What is the most probable diagnosis?
A) Congenital hemangioma
B) Infantile hemangioma
C) Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
D) Pyogenic granuloma
E) Venous malformation
questions.answer:
E)
The most probable diagnosis is venous malformation. This is a congenital abnormality that grows progressively over time. Management includes sclerotherapy or surgical removal. A) is incorrect because congenital hemangiomas are fully developed at birth and either rapidly involute (RICH) or remain stable (NICH), not enlarging at age 2. B) is incorrect because infantile hemangiomas typically appear around 2 weeks after birth, grow rapidly in the first months, then begin regressing by age 1 year. C) is incorrect because kaposiform hemangioendotheliomas are present at birth without size increase and often cause Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon with bleeding complications. D) is incorrect because pyogenic granulomas appear as rapidly growing red lesions in early childhood, are usually small, and frequently bleed.

questions.question:
A 40-year-old woman seeks consultation for the "collapsed" look of her buttocks (shown) following gastric bypass surgery and subsequent 100-lb (45-kg) weight reduction. Examination reveals loose skin and volume loss in the buttocks. Along with performing a lower body lift, what is the best approach to address the buttock deformity?
A) Application of external radiofrequency (Thermage)
B) Augmentation with gluteal artery perforator flap coverage
C) Fat grafting
D) Implantation of prostheses
E) Suction lipectomy
questions.answer:
B)
Gluteal artery perforator flap coverage is the most appropriate management. Massive weight loss patients require aggressive surgical approaches to restore volume and contour. Autologous gluteal augmentation flaps using superior and inferior gluteal artery perforators can reliably add volume and projection during lower body lifts. A) is incorrect because external radiofrequency provides only conservative skin tightening results insufficient for massive weight loss patients. C) is incorrect because these patients typically lack adequate donor fat (450-1100 mL per side needed) after massive weight loss. D) is incorrect because gluteal prostheses carry high risks of wound dehiscence, extrusion, infection, rotation, and displacement. E) is incorrect because suction lipectomy would worsen volume deficiency and provide minimal skin tightening.

questions.question:
A 50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus is scheduled for ligament reconstruction tendon interposition (LRTI) surgery to treat trapeziometacarpal joint arthritis. The operation is anticipated to take 90 minutes. What is the most suitable antibiotic prophylaxis for this patient?
A) Oral antibiotics for 3 days following surgery
B) Single dose intravenous antibiotic within 1 hour of surgery
C) Single dose intravenous antibiotic within 1 hour of surgery and oral antibiotics for 24 hours following surgery
D) Single dose intravenous antibiotic within 1 hour of surgery and oral antibiotics for 3 days following surgery
E) No antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated
questions.answer:
E)
No antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated. Level I evidence demonstrates that prophylactic antibiotics are unnecessary for clean hand surgery procedures lasting under 2 hours. Growing evidence shows prophylactic antibiotics are not needed for clean plastic surgery cases except breast procedures. Although diabetes was previously thought to increase infection risk, this has not been confirmed in larger multivariate studies. A) is incorrect because oral antibiotics post-operatively are not indicated for clean cases. B) is incorrect because even a single preoperative dose is unnecessary for clean hand surgery under 2 hours. C) is incorrect because neither preoperative IV nor postoperative oral antibiotics are needed. D) is incorrect because this represents antibiotic overuse without evidence-based support for clean procedures.

questions.question:
A 68-year-old woman has partial glossectomy, anterior floor of mouth resection, and bilateral modified radical neck dissection for squamous cell carcinoma of the ventral tongue and anterior floor of mouth. The defect is reconstructed using a 5 × 6-cm radial forearm free flap. The free flap is connected to the left facial artery and left internal jugular vein. The forearm donor site receives a split-thickness skin graft from the thigh. Besides Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code 15758 (free fascial flap with microvascular anastomosis), which of the following is most suitable?
A) 13152: Complex repair mouth 2.6–7.5 cm
B) 15100: Split thickness skin graft, arm; less than 100 cm²
C) 35761: Exploration of vessels without repair
D) 40840: Anterior vestibuloplasty
E) 69990: Use of operating microscope
questions.answer:
B)
Split thickness skin graft code 15100 is most appropriate. Free flap codes are comprehensive and include flap elevation, vessel isolation, transfer, microvascular anastomosis, inset, and primary donor site closure. When procedures exceed these global components, additional coding is warranted. Since the donor site required skin grafting beyond primary closure, this represents an additional procedure. A) is incorrect because complex repair is included in the global free flap procedure. C) is incorrect because vessel exploration is part of the global free flap code. D) is incorrect because vestibuloplasty is not described in this case. E) is incorrect because operating microscope use (69990) is included in free flap codes and should not be coded separately.

questions.question:
A 60-year-old woman is seen in the hospital for a pressure ulcer in the lumbar region. A photograph is shown. A sponge for negative pressure wound therapy is about to be applied directly to the wound. Which of the following is the most likely complication of this therapy in this patient?


A) Enterocutaneous fistula
B) Excessive bleeding
C) Excessive wound drainage
D) Infection
E) Retained sponge in wound
questions.answer:
The correct response is Option D.


Infection due to retained necrotic tissue would be the most likely complication in this patient. The vacuum-assisted negative pressure wound closure device should not be used in place of good wound care principles such as debridement.


Use of negative pressure wound therapy has been used for pressure ulcers, open abdomen, traumatic extremity wounds, chest wounds, burns, and skin grafts. Negative pressure wound therapy works through mechanisms that include fluid removal, drawing the wound together, microdeformation, and moist wound healing. Several randomized clinical trials support the use of negative pressure wound therapy in certain wound types. Serious complications include bleeding and infection.


Negative pressure wound therapy devices should be used with caution in infected wounds. They should not be used until the wounds are adequately debrided. This wound has not been adequately debrided and negative pressure wound therapy should not be used until necrotic tissue has been removed.


Bleeding is the next most common complication, but is usually seen in anticoagulated patients and after debridement. Use of a conventional gauze dressing for several hours after a debridement before placing a sponge-based negative-pressure wound therapy device may decrease the risk of excessive bleeding. Most significant bleeding has occurred secondary to disruption of major vessel grafts, cardiac bypass grafts, or the ventricle itself when sponges are placed directly on the structures. This wound is not near any major blood vessels.


Use of a single sponge or a long roll of gauze within any deep wounds is recommended to avoid retained foreign bodies.


Negative pressure wound therapy has been used to control wound drainage. Increased drainage would be caused by the lack of debridement and infection.
Even in clean wounds, a recent report on abdominal wound closure found the most likely complication to be infection rather than recurrent hernia or enterocutaneous fistula. This wound is on the back and would not be likely to have an enterocutaneous fistula. Although initially contraindicated for use with enterocutaneous fistula, recent reports have shown its use to be safe and effective in selected cases.


References
1. Argenta LC, Morykwas MJ, Marks MW, et al. Vacuum-assisted closure: state of clinic art. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2006 Jun;117(7 Suppl):127S-142S.
2. DeFranzo AJ, Pitzer K, Molnar JA, et al. Vacuum-assisted closure for defects of the abdominal wall. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2008 Mar;121(3):832-839.
3. Orgill DP, Bayer LR. Update on negative-pressure wound therapy. Plast Reconstr Surg. 2011 Jan;127 Suppl 1:105S-115S.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old woman has right breast swelling 10 years following bilateral mastectomy and reconstruction with bilateral submuscular textured implants and acellular dermal matrix sling. Examination reveals right-sided periprosthetic fluid accumulation. Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma is suspected. Fluid analysis will most likely demonstrate which of the following tumor markers?
A) Anaplastic lymphoma kinase
B) CD3
C) CD5
D) CD30
E) Human germinal center-associated lymphoma (HGAL)
questions.answer:
D)
CD30 will most likely be demonstrated. Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) neoplastic cells are strongly CD30-positive, making this the key diagnostic marker. BIA-ALCL is primarily associated with textured implants and presents as late-onset seroma, likely due to chronic inflammation from subclinical infection. A) is incorrect because anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is associated with systemic ALCL in 60% of cases but is characteristically negative in BIA-ALCL. B) is incorrect because BIA-ALCL neoplastic cells variably lose CD3 expression. C) is incorrect because BIA-ALCL cells variably lose CD5 expression. E) is incorrect because HGAL is associated with B-cell lymphoma, not BIA-ALCL.

questions.question:
Surgical removal of a regressed infantile hemangioma is being considered for remaining tissue distortion. Which of the following immunohistochemical stains is most characteristic for confirming this suspected condition?
A) D2-40
B) GLUT-1
C) HER2/neu
D) PROX-1
E) VEGFR-3
questions.answer:
B)

GLUT-1 immunostaining positivity serves as the characteristic marker for differentiating infantile hemangioma from other vascular lesions. This glucose transporter protein is consistently expressed in infantile hemangiomas and is considered the gold standard for diagnosis. A) D2-40 is incorrect because it marks lymphatic vessels and would not be broadly positive in infantile hemangiomas. C) HER2/neu is incorrect because it is primarily used as a prognostic marker in breast cancer, not vascular anomalies. D) PROX-1 is incorrect because it identifies lymphatic malformations and certain other vascular tumors like tufted angioma. E) VEGFR-3 is incorrect because it is associated with lymphatic malformations rather than infantile hemangiomas.

questions.question:
A 42-year-old male presents to the emergency room following a traumatic complete penile amputation at the proximal shaft level from domestic violence. Microsurgical repair of which of the following vessels is essential for successful penile reattachment?
A) Cavernous artery
B) Circumflex artery
C) Deep dorsal artery
D) Pudendal artery
E) Subtunical venous plexus
questions.answer:
C)

The deep dorsal artery is one of the three critical neurovascular structures that must be repaired for successful penile replantation, along with the dorsal nerves and dorsal veins. Modern microsurgical techniques have dramatically improved outcomes by allowing precise repair of these structures.
